The comparison is compatible with every arithmetic action preserving the cover. Thus a cusp-preserving isomorphism over $G_k$ preserves the point counts of every corresponding open cover over every finite constant extension.
notes: Working identifier A.CR2. Compactification and Frobenius are retained at the cusp prime. Proved.

statement: For a proper hyperbolic curve $C/k$ over a finite field of characteristic $p$, and $\Sigma=\mathrm{Primes}-\{p\}$, there is a finite set $E_C\subset C^{\cl}$ such that outside its inverse image a decomposition subgroup has a unique geometric point label, even up to commensurability, over every finite constant extension at once. The numbering of Definitions~1.3 and 1.5, Remark~1.2, and Proposition~1.8(vi) is the same in the attached arXiv text and the journal version of \cite{LA_ST2009}.
notes: Working identifier A.CR3. The exact uniform exceptional-set input. Known, with derivation.

statement: Let $C/L$ be smooth proper geometrically connected of genus at least two over a finite field, and let $\Sigma$ contain a prime $r\ne\operatorname{char}L$. If $D\subset\Pi_C^\Sigma$ is a continuous section subgroup mapping isomorphically onto $G_L$, then $N_{\Pi_C^\Sigma}(D)=D$.
notes: Working identifier A.CR4. A rational point section is self-normalizing. Proved.

statement: Under the hypotheses of AS-AG.40, a cusp-preserving isomorphism $\beta:G_P\simeq G_Q$ over $\mathrm{id}_{\Pi_C}$ carries every noncuspidal point section, after its finite residue-field extension, to an actual noncuspidal point section. Outside $E_C\cup\{P,Q\}$ the target point is the same point of $C$. This conclusion holds in the whole quotient, and not merely at a finite level.
notes: Working identifier A.CR5. Point recognition in the whole cuspidal quotient. Proved.

statement: Let $k$ be finite of characteristic $p$, $C/k$ smooth proper geometrically connected of genus at least two, $P,Q\in C(k)$, and $r\ne p$. Let $G_P,G_Q$ be the maximal cuspidally pro-$r$ quotients of the arithmetic geometrically prime-to-$p$ groups of $C-P,C-Q$, relative to their maps to the full proper group $\Pi_C$. If a continuous isomorphism $\beta:G_P\to G_Q$ over $\mathrm{id}_{\Pi_C}$ carries the cusp decomposition subgroup to a conjugate of the cusp decomposition subgroup, then $P=Q$.
notes: Working identifier A.CR6. The complete conditional cuspidal criterion. Proved.

statement: Let $\Sigma$ be any set of primes containing $r\ne p$. Use the full proper geometric pro-$\Sigma$ group in the preceding criterion. It suffices that the noncuspidal point transport induced by $\beta$ have unchanged labels outside $C(F)$, for one proper algebraic subfield $k\subset F\subsetneq\bar k$. In particular, an exceptional image supported over such an $F$ suffices, even if it is infinite. The annihilating integer for $[P-Q]$ need not be coprime to $r$.
notes: Working identifier A.CR7. Proper-field support suffices for the criterion. Proved.

statement: For a proper hyperbolic curve $C/k$ over a finite field of characteristic $p$, put \[ B_C=\{R\in C(\bar k):\exists S\ne R, [R-S]\in J_C(\bar k)[p^\infty]\}. \] There is a proper algebraic subfield $F\subsetneq\bar k$ containing $k$ for which $B_C\subset C(F)$. Hence the conditional criterion \statementref{A.19} admits a proof using \statementref{A.20} and this support field in place of the exceptional-set finiteness theorem.
notes: Working identifier A.CR8. An independent elementary support-field proof. Proved.

statement: For a proper hyperbolic $C/k$ over a finite field of characteristic $p$ and every prime set $\Sigma$ containing some $r\ne p$, $E_C^\Sigma=\varnothing$ is equivalent to injectivity of the geometric pro-$\Sigma$ point-section map after every finite constant extension of $k$.
notes: Working identifier A.CR9. Exceptional emptiness and all-extension point separation. Proved.

statement: Assume the cuspidal transport construction from equal point sections has been established for a prime set $\Sigma$ containing some $r\ne p$, allowing $p\in\Sigma$. Then $E_C^\Sigma=\varnothing$ whenever $\Sigma$ is $J_C$-large in the sense of \cite{LA_ST2017}; this includes every cofinite $\Sigma$. More generally, almost $\Sigma$-separation implies $E_C^\Sigma=\varnothing$, and a finite $E_C^\Sigma$ is necessarily empty. Thus the exceptional image is either empty or infinite. This dichotomy alone does not classify every prime set.
notes: Working identifier A.CR10. Large prime sets and the finite-or-infinite dichotomy. Proved.

statement: The elliptic curve $E/\mathbf F_2:y^2+xy=x^3+1$ has distinct rational points $O$ and $T=(0,1)$ whose sections collide in the entire geometrically prime-to-two arithmetic group. Its exceptional image is all of $E^{\cl}$. The finite-exception hypothesis used for proper hyperbolic curves fails here.
notes: Working identifier A.CR11. Genus-one negative control. Proved.

statement: The smooth proper genus-two curve $C/\mathbf F_2:y^2+x(x+1)y=x^5+1$ has distinct rational points $P=(0,1)$ and $Q=(1,0)$ with $[P-Q]$ of exact order two. They collide in the entire arithmetic extension by the geometric abelian prime-to-two quotient. Both the cusp-residue and the compactified-cover cohomology arguments cease to apply to that abelianized replacement.
notes: Working identifier A.CR12. The abelianized negative control in genus two. Proved.

statement: For every proper hyperbolic curve $C/k$ over a finite field and every prime $r$, including $r=\operatorname{char}k$, the exceptional image $E_C^{\{r\}}$ is infinite. Here the full arithmetic quotient $G_k$ is retained, and for $r=\operatorname{char}k$ we use the same definition by commensurable point decomposition groups. For $\Sigma=\varnothing$, the group is $\Pi_C^\varnothing=G_k$; all rational point sections are equal and every closed point is exceptional. Thus retaining at most one geometric prime does not separate points over every finite constant extension.
notes: Working identifier A.CR13. Empty and singleton prime sets have infinitely many exceptions. Proved.

statement: Let $L=\mathbf F_2[t]/(t^7+t+1)$ and $C/L:y^2+y=x^5$. The distinct $L$-points $P=(t,t^6)$ and $Q=(t^2,t^6+t^5)$ have conjugate sections in the entire arithmetic extension by the geometric pro-three group. The assertion is not merely a finite-quotient collision.
notes: Working identifier A.CR14. A completely specified pro-three collision. Proved.

statement: The assertions above prove emptiness for $J_C$-large sets (once the stated transport theorem is inserted), infiniteness for singletons, and a finite-or-infinite dichotomy. They do not decide the alternative for every arbitrary nonempty prime set that is neither a singleton nor $J_C$-large. That additional classification asked in A12 remains unproved in this audit.
notes: Working identifier A.CR15. The remaining arbitrary-prime-set classification. Open.

statement: Let $\Sigma$ contain two distinct primes $r,s$, and let $\Delta$ be the pro-$\Sigma$ completion of a surface group of genus at least two. Its Frattini quotient $\Delta/\Phi(\Delta)$ is infinite, where $\Phi$ is the intersection of the maximal open subgroups. In particular this applies to the geometric pro-$\Sigma$ group of a proper curve in characteristic outside $\Sigma$. For $\Sigma=\{2,3\}$ there is, moreover, an explicit two-generated group $G$ of order $576$, with $\Phi(G)=1$, and an automorphism of order seven acting trivially on $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$. Neither assertion is a counterexample to mixed-prime point separation. They show why the finite-Frattini and abelianization arguments used for a single prime do not extend by the same reasoning.
notes: Working identifier A.R6. Mixed-prime surface groups have infinite Frattini quotient. Proved. Exact obstruction to extending the single-prime finite-Frattini argument; no mixed-prime point-section counterexample asserted.

statement: Let $K$ be a field finitely generated over $\mathbf F_p$, and let $G/K$ be a semiabelian variety, an extension of an abelian variety by a torus. For the prime-to-$p$ Kummer map on rational points, the kernel is \[ \ker\left(G(K)\longrightarrow \prod_{\ell\ne p}H^1(G_K,T_\ell G)\right)=G(K)[p^\infty]. \] For a field finitely generated over $\mathbf Q$, the analogous map using every prime has zero kernel. No finite-generation assertion about $K^\times$ is needed or made.
notes: Working identifier A.R2. Prime-to-characteristic Kummer kernels. Proved. Exact semiabelian Kummer kernels; no false finite-generation claim for K^times.

statement: Let $C/k$ be as in \statementref{A.1}, and let $P,Q\in C(k)$. Their sections are geometrically conjugate if and only if the following condition holds. For every finite extension $L/k$ and every connected finite \emph{geometrically} prime-to-$p$ Galois cover $D\to C_L$ with a specified $P'\in D(L)$ over $P$, there is $Q'\in D(L)$ above $Q$ such that $[Q'-P']\in J_D(L)[p^\infty]$. When this condition holds, the lift $Q'$ is unique. This is the condition of cote 149, scan 36, with \emph{$p$-torsion} understood as $p$-primary torsion.
notes: Working identifier A.R3. The covering condition is equivalent to collision. Proved. Cover condition, whole-group compactness and unique compatible lifts.

statement: If proper hyperbolic curves over all finite fields of characteristic $p$ have injective geometrically prime-to-$p$ point-section maps, then so do proper hyperbolic curves over every field $K$ finitely generated over $\mathbf F_p$.
notes: Working identifier A.R4. Specialization from finite type to a finite field. Proved. Proper specialization with surjective arithmetic comparison.

statement: Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\mathbf F_p$, and let $X/K$ be a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve. Its map from $X(K)$ to geometric conjugacy classes of sections of its arithmetic geometrically prime-to-$p$ group is injective. For $K$ finitely generated over $\mathbf Q$, the same assertion holds for the full geometric fundamental group. The positive-characteristic assertion is equivalent to \statementref{A.1}.
notes: Working identifier A.R5. Every hyperbolic curve over a finitely generated field. Proved. All hyperbolic curves, affine genus0 and1, imperfect-field compactification accounted for.

statement: Mochizuki's original author Proposition~1.8(ii), equivalently Proposition~1.6(ii) in the separate LaTeX version, asserts the full prime-to-$p$ punctured-fibre identification when the ground field has characteristic $p$ and $\Sigma$ consists of all primes different from $p$. Consequently the noninjectivity established in the configuration audit contradicts this specialization of the assertion itself. The February 2014 Comments do not amend this assertion.
notes: Working identifier A.LIT1. A10, A14. Proved: the literal scope of the disputed assertion.

statement: Let $k$ be a perfect field, let $C/k$ be a proper smooth geometrically connected curve of genus at least two, and let $\Sigma^\dagger=\{r\in\Sigma:r\text{ is invertible in }k\}$ be nonempty. Thus $\Sigma^\dagger=\Sigma$ in characteristic zero and $\Sigma^\dagger=\Sigma\setminus\{p\}$ in characteristic $p>0$. Let $F\to E\to\Delta_2\to1$ be the geometric right-exact configuration sequence, let $F\twoheadrightarrow\Delta_1$ be the proper fibre quotient, and let $E\twoheadrightarrow\Delta_1\times\Delta_2$ be the proper product quotient. Write $K_F,K_E$ for their cuspidal kernels. Suppose the relative groups are formed from the \emph{tame} boundary groups, with Mochizuki's maximal cuspidally pro-$\Sigma^\dagger$ convention. The proper groups may retain $p$ in $\Sigma$. The relative cuspidally pro-$r$ fibre theorem of Part~A, including \statementref{A.13}, holds for every $r\in\Sigma^\dagger$. Then \[ K_F^{(r)}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E^{(r)}\quad(r\in\Sigma^\dagger), \qquad K_F^{\mathrm{ab}}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E^{\mathrm{ab}}. \] Consequently the configuration fibre sequence is left exact after cuspidal abelianization, as well as after the specified fixed-prime cuspidal completion. The one-puncture geometrically cuspidally central fibre identification also holds. For a $k$-rational point, the corresponding arithmetic inverse-image identifications hold over the unchanged quotient $G_k$.
depends_on: A.13 for every r in Sigma minus p, including labelled finite proper pullbacks and p in Sigma
notes: Working identifier A.LIT2. A10. Proved: a limited repair of the fibre input.

statement: Mochizuki--Tamagawa's configuration exactness theorem and Wakabayashi's configuration theorem do not assert the mixed prime-to-$p$ exactness refuted in Part~A.
notes: Working identifier A.LIT3. A10. Proved: the primary and total formation distinction.

statement: Fix a prime $l$ invertible in the two finite fields. Wakabayashi's Theorem~A, proved in the more general logarithmic form as Theorem~3.9, starts with a Frobenius-preserving isomorphism of the geometrically pro-$l$ groups of once-punctured curves, carrying the specified new cusp decomposition groups to one another. It extends this isomorphism to the two-point configuration groups, compatibly with the proper quotient and switching, up to the stated inner ambiguity. Corollary~3.10 transports punctures at other points with corresponding proper decomposition groups. Theorem~C, namely Theorem~4.4, reconstructs the higher configuration groups from the geometrically pro-$l$ curve group. These are reconstruction results in the singleton-prime category.
notes: Working identifier A.LIT4. A11. Proved: Wakabayashi's actual input and output.

statement: In Sa\"idi--Tamagawa 2017, Definition~2.6 calls $\Sigma$ $J_C$-large when the omitted-prime representation $\rho_{J_C,\Sigma'}:G_k\to\Aut(T_{\Sigma'}J_C)$ is noninjective. Definition~2.9 calls $C$ almost $\Sigma$-separated when its exceptional closed points are supported over some proper algebraic subfield $F\subsetneq\bar k$. Proposition~2.12 proves this latter conclusion under $J_C$-largeness. It does not in general assert that the exceptional set is finite.
notes: Working identifier A.LIT5. A10, A14. Proved: the exact later largeness conclusion.

statement: The separation argument extends from finite exceptional support to almost $\Sigma$-separation whenever $\Sigma\setminus\{p\}$ is nonempty, including $p\in\Sigma$. We use the relative fixed-$r$ fibre and transport statements of Part~A in that $\Sigma$-category, as extended by \statementref{A.13}. Consequently the $J_C$-large almost-separated cases of Sa\"idi--Tamagawa become separated.
depends_on: A.22 and A.23 generalized criterion;A.13 for any Sigma containing a non-p prime
notes: Working identifier A.LIT6. A10, A14. Proved with the relative criterion of Part A.

statement: The following comparison records exact predecessors and the additional work required in this audit. It is not a priority claim.
notes: Working identifier A.LIT7. A14. Proved: the recorded predecessor comparison.

statement: For the five papers specified in A10, the dependencies on the configuration fibre assertion are as listed below. At every listed central, abelian, or fixed-prime use, A.35 supplies the same quotient statement with its maps and boundary data. The literal mixed-prime fibre insertion and any argument requiring that full insertion are lost. This is a census of the disputed dependency, not a reproof of unrelated theorems in those papers.
depends_on: A.35 over perfect fields;A.13 fixed-prime relative exactness and boundary transport
notes: Working identifier A.LIT8. Which imported fibre arguments require replacement. Proved.

statement: Let $C/L$ be proper of genus at least two over a finite field of characteristic $p$, and let $D\to C$ be a nontrivial constant Galois \'etale $P$-split cover of degree $d$ prime to $p$. Put $B=(\ker(J_D\to J_C))^0$. Then \[ \frac{\#J_D(L)}{\#J_C(L)}=\#B(L)\in\mathbf Z_{>0}. \] If the group has a nonidentity element of odd order, the condition $B(L)[p]=0$ directly excludes a point-section collision at $P$. This includes every odd prime cyclic cover used in B1. The conclusion also holds for the remaining prime-to-$p$ groups by the independently proved A.1, but the odd-order stabilizer argument by itself does not prove that broader group assertion.
notes: Working identifier B.CL1. The relative class-number test, with its group hypothesis. Proved. Odd-order relative class-number criterion and its exact group scope

statement: Let $a:J_C(L)\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a nontrivial finite abelian quotient of order prime to $p$, and use the Abel map based at $P$ to pull back its constant Lang quotient. Put \[ \Theta_{C,P,A}=\sum_{d=0}^{g-1} \sum_{E\in\operatorname{Div}^{+}_d(C)(L)} [a([E-dP])]\quad\text{in }\mathbf F_p[A]. \] Its relative class number is prime to $p$ if and only if $\overline\psi(\Theta_{C,P,A})\ne0$ for every nontrivial character $\overline\psi:A\to\overline{\mathbf F}_p^\times$. For $A=\mathbf Z/\ell$ this is precisely B1's simultaneous test; it is not enough to check one reduced character unless all primitive characters form one Frobenius orbit.
notes: Working identifier B.CL2. Simultaneous character criterion in every genus. Proved. All-genus simultaneous effective-divisor character test

statement: For any quotient $A$ of $J_C(L)$ let $N=\#C(L)$ and let $N_b$ be the occupancies of the Abel-image points in its cosets. Then \[ \sum_bN_b(N_b-1) \le \frac{N^2}{|A|} +\frac{|A|-1}{|A|}(2g-2)^2q-N. \tag{B.CL.1} \] If all nonzero occupancies are multiples of $p$, the left side is at least $(p-1)(N-N_0)$. In genus two, if $p$ generates $(\mathbf Z/\ell)^\times$, a surjection with kernel $H\subset J_C(L)$ is a class-number witness whenever \[ N\ge2|H|,\qquad \ell>N. \tag{B.CL.2} \] Neither $p>(2g-2)^2$ nor these estimates alone proves universal existence of such a quotient. For $g>2$, occupancies of points alone are not the character test in B.2.
notes: Working identifier B.CL3. The corrected pair estimate and its precise limitation. Proved. Corrected pair estimate and the primitive-root genus-two sufficient conditions

statement: Fix $(C,P)/\mathbf F_q$ and an odd prime $\ell\ne p$. There is a finite procedure deciding whether B1 has an order-$\ell$ witness over \emph{any} constant extension. For each geometric nonzero character $\chi:\pi_1(C_{\overline k})\to\mathbf F_\ell$, let $m$ be its least Frobenius period. Construct its unique $P$-split constant cover over $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}$. It suffices to test these finitely many covers at these first fields. If $A_\chi$ is Frobenius on their new geometric $p$-torsion, the exact extension degrees preserving the witness are \[ n\ge1\quad\text{such that}\quad \det(1-A_\chi^n)\ne0. \tag{B.CL.3} \] A failed first-field test never becomes a witness at a later field. A successful one remains successful under all extensions of $p$-power degree.
notes: Working identifier B.CL4. A finite all-constant-extension decision for each fixed prime. Proved. Finite decision over all constant extensions for each fixed prime

statement: For every prescribed $(C,P)$ as in B1, prove or refute the existence of a prime $\ell$ for which at least one first-field test in B.4 succeeds. This remains undecided here, including the universal assertion for pairs $(p,g)$ with $p>(2g-2)^2$. B.3 gives the corrected numerical sufficient conditions; B.28--B.29 prove unpointed existence and quantify the prescribed-point obstruction. The R8 example has the explicit least-prime witness proved in B.26--B.27, and B.30 gives a plane-quartic instance. None of these removes the arbitrary-curve and prescribed-point quantifiers.
notes: Working identifier B.CL5. The remaining prescribed-point existence assertion. Open. Universal prescribed-point witness existence remains open

statement: There is a natural exact sequence of compact abelian pro-$p$ groups \[ 0\longrightarrow V\xrightarrow{F-1}V \xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M_P^F\longrightarrow0. \] For every $F$-stable normal level $H$, projection gives a continuous surjection \[ M_P^F\longrightarrow J_{D_H}(k)[p^\infty]. \] In particular $M_P^F$ need not vanish. The first term in the exact sequence is a Tate-module inverse limit; its Frobenius invariants vanish, whereas its Frobenius coinvariants need not vanish.
notes: Working identifier B.NM1. The integral description of the fixed norm module. Proved.

statement: Every $m\in M_P^F$ is the compatible $p$-adic abelianized difference of a continuous full étale arithmetic section from $s_P$. Its projection to the geometrically prime-to-$p$ quotient is exactly $s_P$. If $m\ne0$, the realizing section is not geometrically conjugate to a point section. This conclusion uses point separation proved by the cuspidal criterion and transport above; it does not assert free deck orbits for $m$.
notes: Working identifier B.NM2. All fixed classes have full arithmetic section realizations. Proved.

statement: For an $F$-stable open normal $H\triangleleft\Delta$, let $S_H$ be the finite set of $a\in J_{D_H}(k)[p^\infty]$ such that, for every normal $K\triangleleft\Delta$ containing $H$, the norm of $a$ to $D_K$ has trivial stabilizer in $\Delta/K$. The quotient $K/H$ and the curve $D_K$ need not be $F$-stable. Then the set of fixed norm-module vectors with free orbits at every normal level is naturally \[ \varprojlim_H S_H. \] It is nonempty if and only if every $S_H$ is nonempty. Any such vector is nonzero. Consequently, nonexistence of an all-level free vector has a finite certificate of this specific form: one stable pointed normal cover for which $S_H$ is empty.
notes: Working identifier B.NM3. An exact finite criterion for free orbits at every normal level. Proved.

statement: Suppose there are a finite extension $L/k$ and compatible pointed étale prime-to-$p$ covers $Z\to Y\to C_L$, both geometrically normal over $C$, such that $Z\to Y$ is nontrivial Galois and \[ p\nmid\frac{\#J_Z(L)}{\#J_Y(L)}. \] Then $M_P^F$ contains no vector with free deck orbit at every normal level. The geometric deck groups need not be constant over $L$. This is a sufficient condition, not a claimed equivalence with the existence of one cyclic witness over $C$.
notes: Working identifier B.NM4. A relative class-number witness obstructs free vectors. Proved.

statement: For the smooth proper model over $\F_2$ of \[ C:\quad y^2+y=x+\frac1x+\frac1{x+1}, \] one has $J_C(\F_2)\simeq(\Z/2)^2$. For every rational base point $P$, the group $M_P^F$ therefore has nonzero classes and these have non-point-theoretic full arithmetic section realizations. This assertion does not provide an all-level free vector.
notes: Working identifier B.NM5. Nonzero fixed classes on an explicit genus-two curve. Proved.

statement: The implication from a free vector in a finite coprime deck module to a free norm at every normal quotient is false, even for an abelian odd group acting on an $\F_2$-vector space.
notes: Working identifier B.NM6. Freeness at one normal level need not survive norm. Refuted.

statement: It remains undetermined here whether $M_P^F$ has no nonzero all-level free vector for every genus-two curve in characteristic two over every finite field of definition, and whether an all-level free vector exists for any proper hyperbolic curve in any characteristic. The general fixed classes and their full section realizations have been determined above, but these results do not decide nonemptiness of the inverse limit in \statementref{B.8} for all such curves.
notes: Working identifier B.NM7. The universal free-orbit assertion of B2. Open.

statement: Let $D\to C$ be a pointed geometrically connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover over $k=\mathbf F_q$, with abelian geometric Galois group $A$ of order prime to $p=\operatorname{char}k$. The chosen point of $D$ lies rationally above $P$. Let $F$ act on $A$ by the pointed arithmetic descent, and put \[ S_D(k)=\{a\in J_D(k)[p^\infty]: \operatorname{Nm}_{D/D_H}(a) \text{ has trivial stabilizer in }A/H \text{ for every }H\le A\}, \tag{B.AB.1} \] where $D_H=D_{\overline k}/H$, with its pointed descent whenever the subgroup is stable under a power of $F$. For each subgroup $H$ for which $A/H$ is a nontrivial cyclic prime-power group $\mathbf Z/\ell^a$, let $m_H$ be its orbit length under $F$, and let $H^+/H$ be the unique subgroup of order $\ell$ in $A/H$. Both quotient curves have their pointed models over $k_{m_H}=\mathbf F_{q^{m_H}}$. Then \[ S_D(k)\ne\varnothing \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p\mid \frac{\#J_{D_H}(k_{m_H})}{\#J_{D_{H^+}}(k_{m_H})} \quad\text{for every such }H. \tag{B.AB.2} \] Thus an empty set at a finite abelian normal level is equivalent to a relative class-number unit in one cyclic prime-power tower, at that quotient's first pointed field of definition. The step $D_H\to D_{H^+}$ has prime degree $\ell$; its lower curve need not be $C$.
notes: Working identifier B.AB1. Finite abelian norm obstructions, including nonconstant deck groups. Proved.

statement: If the group $A$ in \statementref{B.13} is constant, then all $m_H=1$. If in addition $A=(\mathbf Z/\ell)^d$, then $S_D(k)$ is nonempty exactly when every degree-$\ell$ quotient $D_H\to C$ has relative class number divisible by $p$. Thus at a constant elementary-abelian level, an obstruction is exactly a prime-degree class-number witness among those quotients. For higher-exponent abelian groups, the exact criterion also tests the primitive parts at cyclic prime-power quotients. These tests are strictly stronger as finite module conditions than testing only prime-degree quotients. This strictness does not assert that a particular curve has no prime-degree witness over all constant extensions.
notes: Working identifier B.AB2. The elementary-prime case and the stronger higher-power test. Proved.

statement: Let $G$ be a finite solvable group of order prime to $p$, acting on a finite abelian $p$-group $M$. Let $F$ be an automorphism of $M$, and let $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ satisfy $F(gm)=\sigma(g)F(m)$. For $K\triangleleft G$ put \[ e_K=|K|^{-1}\sum_{g\in K}g. \] There exists $a\in M^F$ with \[ \operatorname{Stab}_G(e_Ka)=K \quad(K\triangleleft G) \tag{B.SV.1} \] if and only if \[ \bigcap_{b\in M^F}\operatorname{Stab}_G(e_Kb)=K \quad(K\triangleleft G). \tag{B.SV.2} \] Neither $M^F$ nor an individual norm image is assumed to be $G$-stable. The order of $F$ or of $\sigma$ may be divisible by $p$.
notes: Working identifier B.SV1. Simultaneous norm freeness for solvable coprime actions. Proved.

statement: Let $D\to C$ be a constant pointed normal prime-to-$p$ cover over a finite field $k$, with solvable deck group $G$. The finite all-normal-quotient norm-free set $S_D(k)$ is empty if and only if there exist normal subgroups $K\subsetneq L\triangleleft G$ such that \[ p\nmid \frac{\#J_{D_K}(k)}{\#J_{D_L}(k)}. \tag{B.SV.7} \] In particular, for constant solvable deck groups, the relative class-number-unit sufficient criterion is also necessary at that finite level. The lower curve $D_L$ can differ from $C$, and the degree of the step is not required to be prime.
notes: Working identifier B.SV2. Constant solvable covers have exactly the relative-unit obstruction. Proved.

statement: For any proper hyperbolic pointed curve $(C,P)/k$ in characteristic two, $M_P^F$ has no all-level free vector if and only if there are a pointed $F$-stable normal cover $D\to C$, a normal subgroup $K$ of its geometric deck group $G$, and an element $g\in G\setminus K$ such that \[ g\,\operatorname{Nm}_{D/D_K}(a) =\operatorname{Nm}_{D/D_K}(a) \qquad\text{for every }a\in J_D(k)[2^\infty]. \tag{B.SV.8} \] The quotient $D_K$ need only be defined over its pointed finite constant extension. Thus in characteristic two a finite obstruction can always be witnessed by one quotient and one element fixing every candidate norm coordinate. It cannot require only a union of different stabilizers covering the candidates. This reformulation does not prove that such a finite certificate exists for every genus-two curve. That universal existence assertion in B2 remains open here.
notes: Working identifier B.SV3. A single-element finite certificate in characteristic two. Proved.

statement: The equivalence of \statementref{B.13} cannot be extended to arbitrary finite groups using only the vanishing of relative $p$-primary modules at normal quotient steps. There is a faithful action of a finite nonabelian simple $7'$-group $G$ on a nonzero finite $7$-group $M$ such that the set of vectors with free norm orbit at every normal quotient is empty, although the relative module at every nontrivial normal step is nonzero. This is an exact finite representation example, not a claimed realization by a Jacobian or a counterexample to universal B1.
notes: Working identifier B.NA1. A finite norm obstruction with no vanishing normal-step module. Proved.

statement: For every $C/k$ as in \statementref{A.1} and every $P\in C(k)$, there is a connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover $D\to C$ with geometrically Galois group of order prime to $p$, and a specified $P'\in D(k)$ over $P$, such that the image of $D(k)$ in $C(k)$ is exactly $\{P\}$. The geometric deck group need not be constant over $k$.
notes: Working identifier B.R1. A pointed cover isolating one rational point. Proved. Compactness yields a pointed cover isolating one rational point.

statement: Let $C/L$ be proper of genus at least two over a finite field of characteristic two, $P\in C(L)$, and let $D\to C$ be a connected constant cyclic odd-degree \emph{\'etale} cover with a point $P_D\in D(L)$ above $P$. Suppose $h(D)/h(C)$ is odd. Let $E\to D$ be the Lang cover associated with the maximal odd quotient of $J_D(L)$ and based at $P_D$. Then no point of $C(L)$ other than $P$ lifts rationally to $E$. Taking the geometric Galois closure and its $P$-pointed twist preserves this property and gives an odd geometric Galois cover of $C$.
notes: Working identifier B.R2. A constructive two-stage odd Lang criterion. Proved. Explicit two-stage odd Lang construction.

statement: Write $\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0$. The two conjugate curves \[ C_\alpha:\quad Y^2+(x^2+x+\alpha)Y =x^5+\alpha x^3+x+1 \] are the curves denoted by the pair of class labels $203/302$ in the supplied return. Each has seven $\mathbf F_4$-points. For every one of these fourteen pointed cases, the file \path{code/isolating_lang_covers.json} specifies a connected pointed cover over $\mathbf F_4$, with odd geometric Galois group, whose rational-point image is just the chosen point. The representation is an exact Lang-cover and geometric-core construction; it does not expand enormous affine equations.
notes: Working identifier B.R3. The two requested genus-two classes over $\mathbf F_4$. Proved by exact computation. Exact computation for all14requested pointed F4cases.

statement: For the curve and point $P=\infty$ specified in \statementref{B.23} below, put $m=2^{19}+1=524289$. The pullback of $[m]:J_C\to J_C$ by $i_P:C\to J_C$, $Q\mapsto[Q-P]$, is a connected \emph{\'etale} Galois cover of degree $m^4$ over $\mathbf F_{2^{38}}$. Its constant deck group is $(\mathbf Z/m)^4$, and its rational-point image in $C$ is exactly $\{P\}$.
notes: Working identifier B.R4. A direct isolating cover for the curve over $\mathbf F_{2^{38}}$. Proved. Exact multiplication-cover specification for R8.

statement: The assertion that every genus-two curve in characteristic two has a connected cyclic \emph{\'etale} cover of odd degree $n>1$ whose primitive Jacobian part has two-rank zero is false. A completely specified counterexample is the smooth proper model over $k=\mathbf F_2[t]/(M(t))$ of \[ \begin{split} M(Z)&=Z^{38}+Z^{14}+Z^{10}+Z^9+Z^8+Z^5+Z^2+Z+1,\\ d&=t^3+1,\qquad C:\ y^2+y=A(u)^3,\\ A(u)&=(u^2+t^2u+t)/d,\qquad B(u)=(tu^2+u+t^2)/d . \end{split} \] The polynomial $M$ is irreducible, and $C$ is supersingular of genus two with a unique rational point $P$ above infinity. For every such cover over $\bar k$, the primitive part has positive two-rank. This independently confirms the particular counterexample AS-A.86. It does not refute the version allowing degree one.
depends_on: Raynaud2000 theta criterion; exact division certificates
notes: Working identifier B.R5. Universal nontrivial primitive-zero cyclic covers. Refuted. All-conductor geometric primitive-zero counterexample; complete fresh certificates.

statement: For every proper curve of genus at least two over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$, does there exist a connected cyclic \emph{\'etale} cover of odd degree prime to $p$, allowing degree one, whose primitive part has $p$-rank zero, with the convention $P_1=J_C$?
notes: Working identifier B.R6. The literal degree-one-permitted primitive-cover assertion. Open. Literal odd-degree, degree-one-permitted universal question remains Open.

statement: Let $K=\mathbf F_{2^d}$, and let \[ C:\quad Y^2+hY=f(x),\qquad h\in K^\times, \quad f\text{ monic of degree five}, \] be smooth, with marked point $P=\infty$. Let $\ell$ be an odd prime such that $\mu_\ell\subset K$, and let $a\in J_C(K)$ have exact order $\ell$. Suppose every nonzero $ia$ has reduced Mumford representative $(u_i,v_i)$ of degree two. Write $j=2i\bmod\ell$ and \[ \begin{split} w_i&=(v_i^2+hv_i+f)/u_i,\\ V_i&=v_i+u_i\bigl((w_i/h)\bmod u_i\bigr),\\ c_i&=(V_i)_3\,(u_j)_1. \end{split} \] Here subscripts on polynomials indicate coefficients. Then the unique constant cyclic, $P$-split cover with character subgroup $\langle a\rangle$ has odd relative class number if and only if \[ A_i:=\prod_{s=0}^{d-1}c_{2^s i}^{\,2^{d-1-s}}\ne1 \qquad(1\le i<\ell). \] The index on each $c$ is reduced modulo $\ell$. The assertion includes the specified pointing; there is no unspecified constant twist.
notes: Working identifier B.W1. A normalized Cartier test in the case used here. Proved.

statement: For the curve and point $(C,P)$ of \statementref{B.23}, a constant cyclic $P$-split cover of degree $191$ with odd relative class number exists over $\mathbf F_{2^{380}}$. A second such cover, of degree $229$, exists over $\mathbf F_{2^{152}}$. Their genera are respectively $192$ and $230$, and their new Jacobian parts are ordinary of dimensions $190$ and $228$.
notes: Working identifier B.W2. Exact degree-191 and degree-229 rational witnesses. Proved.

statement: For the fixed marked curve $(C,P)$ of \statementref{B.23}, the least prime degree of a constant cyclic $P$-split cover satisfying the rational class-number criterion over any finite extension of $k=\mathbf F_{2^{38}}$ is exactly $191$. At degree $191$ the least possible constant extension degree is ten; at degree $229$ it is four, and each minimum is attained by \statementref{B.26}. The second assertion is a minimum for that specified prime, not a claimed minimum over all primes.
notes: Working identifier B.W3. The exact least prime and the two field minima. Proved.

statement: Let $C/K$ be smooth proper of genus $g\ge2$ over a finite field of characteristic $p$. Let $D\to C$ be a geometrically connected \emph{\'etale} cover with constant cyclic deck group of odd prime order $\ell\ne p$. Put $f=\operatorname{ord}_\ell(p)$. Among the $\ell$ constant twists of this cover, at most \[ \frac{(g-1)(\ell-1)}{f} \] have relative class number divisible by $p$. In particular, if $f\ge g-1$, at least one twist has $p$-unit relative class number. For genus two this last condition is automatic.
notes: Working identifier B.TW1. A uniform count of bad constant twists. Proved.

statement: For every smooth proper curve $C/k$ of genus $g\ge2$ over a finite field, there are a finite extension $K/k$, a point $P_K\in C(K)$, and a constant cyclic $P_K$-split cover of odd prime degree, different from the characteristic, with $p$-unit relative class number. The point $P_K$ is not prescribed in advance. More quantitatively, for a constant degree-$\ell$ cover as in \statementref{B.28}, put $B=(g-1)(\ell-1)/f$ and $g_D=1+\ell(g-1)$. If $f\ge g-1$, the number of $P\in C(K)$ for which its unique split twist is a class-number witness is at least \[ \frac{\ell-B}{\ell} \bigl(\#K+1-2g_D\sqrt{\#K}\bigr). \]
notes: Working identifier B.TW2. Existence with an unspecified base point. Proved.

statement: Let $C/\mathbf F_3$ be the smooth plane quartic \[ W^4=X^3Z-XZ^3,\qquad P=(1:0:0). \] There is a $P$-split constant cyclic degree-five cover over $\mathbf F_{3^8}$ whose relative class number is prime to three. Thus five is the least odd prime different from the characteristic which gives a witness for this pointed curve over some constant extension. Every constant degree-five cover of this curve requires a constant degree divisible by eight; the displayed field is therefore also the least one for a degree-five witness. The certificates give six such covers. For each of them the relative class number stays prime to three exactly under further constant extensions of odd degree.
notes: Working identifier B.Q1. A least-prime-five quartic witness over \(\mathbf F_{3^8}\). Proved. Least odd prime5 and least constant degree8 for the specified F3 plane quartic

statement: Let $C/\mathbf F_5$ have the same equation and point as in B.30. Pull its quadratic map to $E:y^2=x^3-x$ back along the duals of the four cyclic degree-three isogenies out of $E$, over $K=\mathbf F_{5^8}$. These four constant $P$-split covers have genus seven. Every one has relative class number divisible by five over $K$ and over every further constant extension. This assertion concerns these four covers; it does not exclude the other order-three characters of $J_C$ or other primes.
notes: Working identifier B.Q2. A four-cover all-extension negative test over \(\mathbf F_5\). Proved. Four actual degree3 F5 plane-quartic covers fail over all later constants

statement: The least witness over arbitrary constant extensions for \emph{every} smooth plane quartic over $\mathbf F_3$ and $\mathbf F_5$ remains undecided here. B.30 is an exact least-prime and first-field result for one pointed quartic; B.31 excludes four actual covers at all later fields. The independent program \path{code/pointed_quartic_tests.py} also computes the point counts and Weil polynomials of $X^4+Y^4+Z^4=0$ over $\mathbf F_3$, at $(1:1:1)$, and $X^4+Y^4-Z^4=0$ over $\mathbf F_5$, at $(1:0:1)$. Their base-field Jacobian orders are $64$ and $256$, respectively, so they have no base-field odd-prime Lang quotient. This is not an all-extension exclusion. The previous return's large base-field census programs were not attached and have not been rerun here. We do not treat their numerical tables as newly verified certificates. B.4 reduces each fixed-prime all-extension question to a finite calculation, but gives no terminating bound on the prime search. It also remains undecided whether some curve has a nonabelian witness of the stated type and has no class-number witness over any extension. Failure of finitely many characters, primes, or fields cannot prove that assertion.
notes: Working identifier B.Q3. The unbounded quartic classification in B6. Open. Every-quartic and unbounded-prime questions remain open

statement: Let \[ C/\mathbf F_5:\quad W^4=X^3Z-XZ^3,\qquad P=(1:0:0). \] Over $K=\mathbf F_{125}$ there is a constant cyclic, $P$-split, \emph{\'etale} cover $D\to C$ of degree thirteen with \[ g_D=27,\qquad \frac{\#J_D(K)}{\#J_C(K)}\equiv1\pmod5. \] Its new Jacobian part is ordinary of dimension twenty-four. Under an extension of $K$ of degree $n$, its relative class number stays prime to five if and only if $4\nmid n$.
notes: Working identifier B.QM1. A constant cyclic thirteen-cover over \(\mathbf F_{125}\). Proved.

statement: For the pointed quartic of \statementref{B.33}, the least constant extension degree over which an odd-prime constant cyclic $P$-split class-number witness exists is exactly three. At that first field, thirteen is the least possible prime, and \statementref{B.33} attains it. The same assertions hold for the pointed Fermat quartic \[ U^4+V^4=R^4\quad\text{over }\mathbf F_5, \qquad (U:V:R)=(1:0:1). \] This is a field-first minimum. The least prime when arbitrary constant extension degrees are allowed is not determined here.
notes: Working identifier B.QM2. The exact first-field minimum and the pointed Fermat identification. Proved.

statement: Let $E/\overline{\F}_p$ be an elliptic curve, let $\pi:E\to E/\{\pm1\}\simeq\mathbf P^1$ be its quotient map, and let $S\subset\mathbf P^1(\overline{\F}_p)$ be finite. There exists $\phi\in\mathrm{PGL}_2(\overline{\F}_p)$ such that every point of $\phi(S)$ is the image under $\pi$ of a prime-to-$p$ torsion point of $E$. The points of $\phi(S)$ may also be required to avoid the branch locus of $\pi$.
depends_on: Weil bounds for a geometrically connected fibre product;Tame/ordinary elliptic isogeny and branch-inertia normal generation
notes: Working identifier B.LIT1. B5. Proved: placing finitely many values over prime-to-$p$ torsion.

statement: Let $p$ be odd and let $C/\overline{\F}_p$ be hyperelliptic of genus at least two. For every hyperelliptic curve $H/\overline{\F}_p$ there is a connected finite \'etale cover $D\to C$ with prime-to-$p$ geometric Galois closure and a nonconstant map $D\to H$. In particular B5 holds for every such $C$, including characteristic three, with a supersingular target of genus at least two.
depends_on: B.35;Kummer ramification cancellation;Prime-to-p formation stability under wreath products
notes: Working identifier B.LIT2. B5. Proved: every odd-characteristic hyperelliptic source.

statement: Let $p=2$. Suppose a curve $C/\overline{\F}_2$ admits a finite separable map to $\mathbf P^1$ with three distinct fibres in which every ramification index is divisible by three. Then a connected finite \'etale cover of $C$ of degree one or three maps nonconstantly to a supersingular elliptic curve. In particular this applies to every cyclic degree-three cover of $\mathbf P^1$ of genus at least two.
depends_on: Three fibres with all ramification indices divisible by three
notes: Working identifier B.LIT3. B5. Proved: a characteristic-two ramification criterion.

statement: Suppose $p$ is odd, $C/\overline{\F}_p$ has genus at least two, and $G\subset\Aut(C)$ has order prime to $p$. Put $Y=C/G$ and suppose $g(Y)\le2$. If at least one of the following holds, then $C$ has a connected finite \'etale cover with prime-to-$p$ Galois closure mapping to a supersingular curve of genus at least two: \begin{enumerate} \item $g(Y)=1$ or $2$; \item $G$ is solvable; \item two distinct branch values of $C\to Y$ have ramification indices with a common prime factor. \end{enumerate} In particular this proves B5 for every tamely superelliptic curve in every odd characteristic, including characteristic three.
depends_on: Odd p;A finite prime-to-p Galois quotient of genus at most two;Poonen hypotheses (i), (ii), or (iii), or the stated strengthened modular hypothesis;B.36
notes: Working identifier B.LIT4. B5. Proved: the first three low-genus Galois cases.

statement: Let $C/\F_2$ be the smooth proper model \[ C:\quad Y^2+X^2Y=X^5+X, \qquad P=\infty. \] It has genus two, $2$-rank one, and no nonzero supersingular isogeny factor in its geometric Jacobian. Over $k=\F_{64}$ there is a connected $P$-pointed cyclic \'etale cover $D\to C_k$ of degree $13$, with zeta numerator \[ P_D(T)= (1-T-80T^2-64T^3+4096T^4) (1+12T+64T^2)^{12}. \tag{B.LIT.7} \] Its primitive degree-$13$ factor has Newton slopes $1/3$ and $2/3$, each with multiplicity $12$, and hence has $2$-rank zero. Its relative class number is \[ \frac{|J_D(k)|}{|J_C(k)|}=77^{12} =43439888521963583647921, \] which is odd. Nevertheless $D$ has no nonconstant map, even over $\overline{\F}_2$, to any supersingular curve of positive genus. Thus this is a B1 witness and a nontrivial positive-$2$-rank case of B4, but this particular cover does not supply the correspondence asked for in B5.
depends_on: Exact all-point Lang-character computation over F64;B.2 complete twisted L-polynomial formula
notes: Working identifier B.LIT7. An exact cyclic-thirteen distinction between B4 and B5. Proved.

statement: Let $C$ be a smooth hyperelliptic curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, of genus $g\in\{2,3\}$ and $2$-rank zero. For every connected cyclic \'etale cover $D\to C$ of degree three, the Prym variety is ordinary of dimension $2(g-1)$. In particular, $f_D=2(g-1)$. In genus three its genus-two reflection quotient is ordinary, so this cubic-reflection construction does not yield a supersingular target.
notes: Working identifier B.LIT8. Ordinary cubic Pryms in two small genera. Proved.

statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $f:C\to\mathbb P^1_k$ be finite separable, and assume that for every $t\in\mathbb P^1(k)$, \[ \gcd\{e_P(f):P\in f^{-1}(t)\}=1. \] Let $C'\to C$ be any finite \'etale cover and $h:\mathbb P^1\to\mathbb P^1$ any finite separable map. The composite $h\circ f\circ\pi$ cannot have three distinct fibres in each of which all ramification indices are divisible by three. It cannot have four distinct fibres in each of which they are all even. More generally, uniform fibre divisibilities $m_i$ at distinct values require \[ \sum_i(1-1/m_i)<2. \]
depends_on: Riemann-Hurwitz and multiplicativity of ramification indices
notes: Working identifier B.LIT9. A fixed simply branched function cannot supply the missing fibres. Proved.

statement: Let $C/\overline{\F}_p$ be a smooth proper curve admitting a finite separable map to $\mathbb P^1$ with three distinct fibres in which every ramification index is divisible by the same odd integer $r\ge3$. Suppose $r\mid p^a+1$ for some $a\ge1$. Then $C$ has a connected cyclic \'etale cover of degree dividing $r$ which dominates a supersingular curve of genus $(r-1)/2$. Its geometric Galois closure therefore has order prime to $p$. In characteristic two this applies to every cyclic prime-degree cover of $\mathbb P^1$ of genus at least two whose degree $\ell$ satisfies that $\operatorname{ord}_\ell(2)$ is even.
depends_on: Tame ramification cancellation;Explicit Hermitian point count
notes: Working identifier B.LIT10. Three uniformly divisible fibres with a supersingular Fermat quotient. Proved.

statement: Suppose \(\operatorname{trdeg}_{\Q}k<\infty\). For finite-type \(k\)-schemes, the functor to the preceding pro-systems is fully faithful after universal homeomorphisms are inverted, with pinned morphisms in \(\operatorname{Pro}(\mathsf T)_{/\mathcal B}\) as target morphisms. Equivalently, for absolutely weakly normal finite-type \(X,Y\), every such pinned ordinary pro-morphism is induced by a unique \(k\)-morphism \(X\to Y\). This includes all finite-transcendence-degree fields of B8, regardless of whether reconstruction from the single topos over \(k\) holds.
notes: Working identifier B.CF1. Ordinary pro-reconstruction for every field of finite transcendence degree. Proved.

statement: The mechanism in B.43 does not extend by the same argument to an arbitrary characteristic-zero field: transitions corresponding to transcendental field extensions need not preserve closed points. Specifically, for \(F\) of characteristic zero and \(u\) transcendental, the point \(T=u\) of \(\mathbb A^1_{F(u)}\) is closed, whereas its image in \(\mathbb A^1_F\) is generic. Consequently the full model system is not in general an object of the ordinary pro-category of pinned geometric morphisms. This is an obstruction to that categorical formulation, and is not a counterexample to reconstruction for pinned morphisms in \(\operatorname{Pro}(\mathsf T)_{/\mathcal B}\).
notes: Working identifier B.CF2. The remaining ordinary pro-category issue is an infinite-transcendence issue. Proved.

statement: For \(\operatorname{trdeg}_{\Q}k=\infty\), ordinary relative pro-reconstruction is proved by B.62--5 below, culminating in B.66. The shorter argument of B.43 alone does not prove it: a representative may have the form \(X_{E,\mathrm{et}}\to Y_{F,\mathrm{et}}\) with \(E/F\) transcendental. Pinnedness of the map on limits does not, by the argument of B.43, give pinnedness of a finite-stage representative. The coherent same-field result AS-FF.13 supplies neither that finite-stage assertion nor an equivalence with this ordinary pro-category. The new proof resolves the obstacle by deriving coherence from compactness, comparing whole Kummer systems after one finitely generated refinement, and reconstructing every étale slice over a fixed source field. It does not assert that those finite-stage transition morphisms preserve closed points.
uses: ANABELIAN_A1:B.43, ANABELIAN_A1:B.44, ANABELIAN_A1:B.62, ANABELIAN_A1:B.63, ANABELIAN_A1:B.64, ANABELIAN_A1:B.65, ANABELIAN_A1:B.66
notes: Working identifier B.CF3. The infinite-transcendence obstacle and its resolution. Proved.

statement: There exists \(u\in t\Q[[t]]\), transcendental over \(\Q(t)\), with the following property. Let \(\Omega\) be any complete rank-one valued extension of \(\Q((t))\), with the valuation trivial on \(\Q\), and let \(h\in\Omega\) satisfy \(v(h)=v(t)=1\). If both \(h\) and \(u(h)\) are algebraic over \(\Q(t,u(t))\), and \(h,u(h)\) are algebraically independent over \(\Q\), then \[ h=t. \tag{B.CF.3} \] The series \(u\) can be specified by a recursive sequence of rational finite jets; the proof gives a finite elimination certificate at every stage. The property holds simultaneously in all finite ramified extensions and their completions.
notes: Working identifier B.CF4. A formal arc with no nontrivial algebraic self-correspondence. Proved.

statement: Choose a series \(u\) as in B.46, and let \[ K=\Q(t,u(t))^h\subset\Q((t)) \tag{B.CF.7} \] be the henselization for the induced \(t\)-adic valuation. Then \(K\) is countable, has transcendence degree two over \(\Q\), value group \(\Z\), residue field \(\Q\), and completion \(\Q((t))\). For every finite extension \(E/K\), in a fixed algebraic closure \(\overline K\), one has \[ C_{\operatorname{Aut}(\overline K)}(G_E)=1. \tag{B.CF.8} \] Thus the centralizer hypothesis of B7 is attained among the residue-characteristic-zero fields with positive transcendence defect specified by B8.
notes: Working identifier B.CF5. Trivial centralizers at every finite extension of a transcendence-degree-two henselian field. Proved.

statement: Let \(R\) be a henselian discrete valuation ring of residue characteristic zero, with fraction field \(K\), uniformizer \(t\), and the unique extension \(v\) of its valuation to \(\overline K\). Put \(\lambda=1+t\), and define \[ F(a)= \begin{cases} \lambda a,&v(a)>0,\\ a,&v(a)\leq0, \end{cases} \qquad F(0)=0, \qquad F(\infty)=\infty. \tag{B.CF.12} \] For every finite \(G_K\)-stable set \(S\subset\mathbb P^1(\overline K)\) containing \(0,1,\infty\), the stable marked genus-zero models for \(S\) and \(F(S)\), over a finite Galois extension splitting their marks, have isomorphic logarithmic special fibres over the same standard log point. These isomorphisms preserve the labels and are compatible with forgetting marks, finite extensions of the field of definition, and the Galois descent data. At a mark \(a\), the induced comparison of the arithmetic cusp group preserves its inertia and induces the identity on its quotient \(G_{K(a)}\), with \(K(F(a))=K(a)\) as actual subfields of \(\overline K\).
notes: Working identifier B.CF6. Compatible logarithmic reduction under a supported infinitesimal scaling. Proved.

statement: For every field \(K\) admitting a nontrivial henselian discrete valuation with residue characteristic zero, closed-point-preserving reconstruction of finite-type \(K\)-schemes from their relative small étale topoi is false, even with universal homeomorphisms inverted. The supported scaling (B.CF.12) is the geometric-point function of a pinned autoequivalence \[ (\mathbb A^1_K)_{\mathrm{et}} \longrightarrow(\mathbb A^1_K)_{\mathrm{et}} \quad\hbox{over }BG_K \tag{B.CF.16} \] which is not induced by a morphism of \(K\)-schemes.
notes: Working identifier B.CF7. Reconstruction over an equicharacteristic-zero henselian discretely valued field. Refuted.

statement: There exists a characteristic-zero field \(K\), countable and of transcendence degree two over \(\Q\), such that \[ C_{\operatorname{Aut}(\overline K)}(G_E)=1 \quad\hbox{for every finite }E/K, \] but closed-point-preserving reconstruction of finite-type \(K\)-schemes from their relative étale topoi fails. One may take exactly the recursively specified field (B.CF.7). The obstruction is a compatible nonalgebraic permutation of points and their whole covering categories, not a centralizing field automorphism.
notes: Working identifier B.CF8. The centralizer condition in B7 is insufficient. Refuted.

statement: Let \[ u_*(t)=\sum_{n\geq1}t^{n!},\qquad K_* =\Q(t,u_*(t))^h\subset\Q((t)). \tag{B.CF.19} \] This field has transcendence degree two, residue field \(\Q\), value group \(\Z\), and positive transcendence defect one. It does not satisfy closed-point-preserving étale reconstruction. This settles the particular residue-characteristic-zero case left undecided in AS-FF.18, without claiming that its centralizers have the property proved for the different series in B.46.
notes: Working identifier B.CF9. The specified transcendence-defect field in AS-FF.18 does not reconstruct. Refuted.

statement: The universal quantifier in B8 is not fully settled. B.49--9, together with B.54--6, refute reconstruction for every field of finite transcendence degree admitting a nontrivial henselian valuation of residue characteristic zero. This includes all the residue-characteristic-zero transcendence-defect cases in AS-FF.18, the specified field \(K_*\), and fields with a mixed-characteristic valuation admitting such a nontrivial residue-characteristic-zero coarsening. The following mixed-characteristic cases remain from the original \texttt{agent\_F/F\_section.tex}. \begin{enumerate} \item General finite-transcendence-degree henselian fields of mixed residue characteristic outside the positive and negative classes already separated in AS-FF.16, AS-FF.22, and AS-FF.26--39. In particular, an unbounded wild ramification index is not by itself a negative criterion: the cyclotomic, maximal abelian, and each fixed bounded-nilpotency class in AS-FF.35, 37, 39 were already positive claims in the return. \item For every prime \(p\), the specified maximal metabelian field \[ K_p=\operatorname{Frac}(\Z_{(p)}^{sh}),\qquad I=G_{K_p},\qquad B_p=\overline\Q^{\,\overline{[I',I']}},\quad I'=\overline{[I,I]}, \] and general finite extensions of it. AS-FF.40 singles out this field; AS-FF.18 names \(B_2\) as the remaining degree-zero test. Neither its asserted centralizer condition nor the affine and selected-cover rigidity assertions AS-FF.44--50 prove reconstruction for arbitrary pinned morphisms or arbitrary covers. The negative residue-characteristic-zero argument here has no application to its mixed-characteristic valuation. \item AS-FF.39 explicitly makes no assertion about the union of the fixed nilpotency-class fields \(\bigcup_c\overline\Q^{\,\gamma_{c+1}(I)}\), or about a general solvable closure. The former union remains undecided here. If the latter phrase means the maximal solvable extension of this precise strict-local field \(K_p\), B.53 below identifies it with \(\overline\Q\) and refutes reconstruction. It does not identify the lower-central union with the derived-series union, and makes no assertion about solvable closures of arbitrary other base fields. B.57 determines the stable rational Kummer kernel at the lower-central union for \(p\geq5\), with explicit exceptions at \(p=2,3\), but its full reconstruction problem remains open. \end{enumerate}
notes: Working identifier B.CF10. Exact remaining scope of the henselian-field question B8. Open.

statement: Fix an embedding of the strict henselization \(A=\Z_{(p)}^{sh}\) in \(\overline\Q\), put \(K_p=\operatorname{Frac}(A)\), and write \(I=G_{K_p}\). Let \(I^{(0)}=I\) and \(I^{(d+1)}=\overline{[I^{(d)},I^{(d)}]}\) be the closed derived series. Then \[ K_p^{\mathrm{sol}} :=\bigcup_{d\geq 0}\overline\Q^{\,I^{(d)}} =\overline\Q. \tag{B.CF.20} \] Consequently this maximal solvable closure does not satisfy closed-point-preserving \(\acute etale\) reconstruction. The statement concerns the actual field in AS-FF.39, not a substitution of a completed local field. It leaves open the bounded derived-length field \(B_p=\overline\Q^{I^{(2)}}\), and the lower-central union \(\bigcup_c\overline\Q^{\gamma_{c+1}(I)}\).
notes: Working identifier B.CF11. The unbounded solvable closure of the strict-local field. Refuted.

statement: Let $R$ be a henselian rank-one valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field $\kappa$ of characteristic zero. Let $S\subset\mathbb P^1(K)$ be a finite set containing $0,1,\infty$, and let $\mathscr X/R$ be its stable marked genus-zero model. Endow $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the canonical valuative log structure $R\setminus\{0\}\to R$, and $\mathscr X$ with the log structure of its vertical boundary and its marked sections. Write $\mathscr X_s$ for its log closed fibre and $U=\mathbb P^1_K\setminus S$. Then restriction gives equivalences \[ \operatorname{FEt}(U) \ \longleftarrow\ \operatorname{KCov}(\mathscr X) \ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{KCov}(\mathscr X_s). \tag{B.LIT.1} \] Here $\operatorname{KCov}$ denotes all finite Kummer \'etale coverings in the saturated, not necessarily fs, sense of Achinger--H\"ubner--Lara--Stix. In that definition the underlying scheme map is integral and need not be finite. The equivalences are over the entire $BG_K$, and are compatible with finite valued extensions and with morphisms between stable models obtained by forgetting marks. Neither discreteness nor completeness is assumed.

statement: Every field $K$ admitting a nontrivial henselian rank-one valuation of residue characteristic zero fails closed-point-preserving reconstruction of finite-type $K$-schemes from their \'etale topoi over $BG_K$. In particular this holds for every field of finite transcendence degree over $\mathbb Q$ with a nontrivial henselian valuation of residue characteristic zero, regardless of its rank, discreteness, or transcendence defect.

statement: For a finite extension \(E/B_p\), let \(\kappa_E\) be the rational \(p\)-primary Kummer map. Put \[ W_p=\{a\in B_p^\times:a^m\in F_p^\times \text{ for some }m\geq1\}. \] Then \[ \ker\kappa_E=\bigcap_{n\geq1}(E^\times)^{p^n}=W_p, \qquad W_p\cap(1-W_p)=F_p\setminus\{0,1\}. \tag{B.MIX.2} \] In particular the supported scaling used in B.48--7 cannot be the point function of a pinned relative autoequivalence over \(B_p\). Precisely, for \(\lambda=1+p\), the bijection \[ f(a)=\begin{cases}\lambda a,&v(a)>0,\\a,&v(a)\leq0, \end{cases}\qquad f(0)=0 \tag{B.MIX.3} \] of \(\overline\Q\) is excluded by two one-puncture \(p\)-Kummer comparisons. This is an obstruction to this proposed counterexample, and not a proof of reconstruction over \(B_p\).

statement: Let \[ N=\bigcap_{c\geq1}\gamma_{c+1}(I),\qquad K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}=\overline\Q^N =\bigcup_{c\geq1}\overline\Q^{\gamma_{c+1}(I)}. \tag{B.MIX.4} \] For every \(p\geq5\) and every finite extension \(E/K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\), \[ \ker\!\left(E^\times\longrightarrow H^1(G_E,\Q_p(1))\right) =\bigcap_{n\geq1}(E^\times)^{p^n} =\mu_\infty. \tag{B.MIX.5} \] For \(p=2\) and \(p=3\), the corresponding kernel is already strictly larger than \(\mu_\infty\) over \(K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\) itself. Explicit nontorsion elements in it are \[ 2\quad(p=2),\qquad \frac{2+\sqrt{-3}}{2-\sqrt{-3}}\quad(p=3). \tag{B.MIX.6} \] These conclusions decide this exact Kummer input to AS-FF.39 at its unbounded union. They do not decide reconstruction at that union.

statement: Let \(p\geq5\), \(K=K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\), and let \(E/K\) be finite. If \(b\in E^\times\) and \(\alpha\in\Q_p\) satisfy \[ \kappa_E(b)=\alpha\kappa_E(p), \tag{B.MIX.11} \] then \(\alpha\in\Q\).

statement: Let \(p\geq5\), and let \(E\) be any finite extension of \(K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\). Every pinned autoequivalence of \(\mathbb A^1_{E,\mathrm{et}}\) over \(BG_E\), with its relative structural isomorphism retained, has actual geometric point function \[ a\longmapsto ua+v, \qquad u\in E^\times,\ v\in E. \tag{B.MIX.12} \] The coefficients are unique. This conclusion concerns the actual point function; it does not identify the remaining pointwise-trivial automorphism kernel on the full étale site, or assert existence for arbitrary noninvertible pinned maps.

statement: Let \(p\geq5\), let \(E/K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\) be finite, and let \(U\) be a smooth geometrically connected curve over \(E\), with smooth proper compactification \(\overline U\). Suppose \(\xi\in H^1(U,\Z_p(1))\) evaluates at every point \(x\in U(L)\), for every finite extension \(L/E\), to the Kummer class of an actual element of \(L^\times\). Every geometric boundary residue of \(\xi\) belongs to \(\Q\cap\Z_p\).

statement: Let \(p\geq5\), and let \(E\) be any finite extension of \(K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\). Every pinned geometric morphism \[ \mathbb A^1_{E,\mathrm{et}} \longrightarrow\mathbb A^1_{E,\mathrm{et}} \] over \(BG_E\) has actual geometric point function \(x\mapsto P(x)\) for a unique polynomial \(P\in E[T]\). Invertibility of the geometric morphism is not assumed. This does not identify the whole inverse-image functor with the functor induced by \(P\), and does not prove existence for an arbitrary source scheme.

statement: Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, let \(X,Y\) be finite-type \(k\)-schemes, and let \(\alpha:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) be an ordinary pro-morphism over \(\mathcal B\). There is a geometric morphism \[ \alpha_k:X_{\mathrm{et}}\longrightarrow Y_{\mathrm{et}} \tag{B.PRO.1} \] over \(BG_k\), compatible with the finite-level representatives of \(\alpha\). Its underlying-space map is the map on inverse limits defined by \(\alpha\), so it is pinned if \(\alpha\) is pinned. Moreover finite constant base change, precomposition by a scheme morphism, restriction to open subobjects, and slicing by a quasi-compact separated étale object preserve the class of maps obtained from ordinary pro-morphisms. For a slice defined at a particular target level, the source model can be taken to be its pullback by that level's chosen representative.
notes: Working identifier B.PRO1. Compact coherence for ordinary pro-morphisms. Proved.

statement: For every characteristic-zero \(k\), pinned ordinary pro-morphisms \(\mathcal B\to\mathcal Y\) over \(\mathcal B\) are precisely the \(k\)-rational points of \(Y\). This statement is compatible with finite extensions of \(k\). In particular, suppose a fixed representative of a pinned pro-morphism pulls the universal Kummer class back to \(\xi\in H^1(X_E,\widehat\Z(1))\). If \(x\in X_E(L)\), with \(L/E\) finite, and \(b\) is the value of its induced pro-point in \(\mathbb G_m\), then there is \emph{one} finitely generated field \(M\) containing \(L\) and \(b\) for which \[ \operatorname{res}_{M/L}(x^*\xi)=\kappa_M(b) \quad\hbox{in }\widehat{M^\times}. \tag{B.PRO.2} \] The field \(M\) works simultaneously for all Kummer levels.
notes: Working identifier B.PRO2. Pro-points and a single-stage Kummer comparison. Proved.

statement: Let \(A\subset B\) be finitely generated fields of characteristic zero. If \(\xi\in\widehat{A^\times}\), \(b\in B^\times\), and \[ \operatorname{res}_{B/A}\xi=\kappa_B(b), \tag{B.PRO.3} \] then \(b\in A^\times\) and \(\xi=\kappa_A(b)\).
notes: Working identifier B.PRO3. Intersection with a finitely generated field's Kummer completion. Proved.

statement: Let \(\alpha\) be a pinned ordinary pro-morphism and choose a relative representative \[ a:X_{E,\mathrm{et}}\longrightarrow Y_{F,\mathrm{et}} \tag{B.PRO.5} \] over \(BG_F\), with \(F\subset E\subset k\) finitely generated. If \(X_E\) is normal, then (B.PRO.5) is induced by a unique \(F\)-scheme morphism \(f_E:X_E\to Y_F\). Its lift to \(Y_E\), after extension to \(k\), realizes the point function of \(\alpha_k\). The same conclusion holds with the absolutely weak normalization of \(X_E\) as source.

statement: For every field \(k\) of characteristic zero, the functor from finite-type \(k\)-schemes localized at universal homeomorphisms to their model pro-systems is fully faithful, with pinned morphisms in the ordinary slice \(\operatorname{Pro}(\mathsf T)_{/\mathcal B}\) as defined above. In particular B9 is proved in arbitrary transcendence degree; no coherent-relative morphism condition has been added to its input.
notes: Working identifier B.PRO5. The ordinary pro-form for every characteristic-zero field. Proved.

statement: For every prime $p$ and every proper smooth connected curve $C/\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ of genus at least two, there exists a connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover $D\to C$ whose geometric Galois closure has order prime to $p$, and a nonconstant morphism $D\to H$ to a positive-genus supersingular curve $H$. This assertion remains undecided here for arbitrary $C$.
notes: Working identifier B.RQ1. The exact unsettled quantifier in B5. Open. Universal supersingular-target correspondence remains open; exact cases and failure of tame-Belyi reduction recorded.

statement: Over every field finitely generated over its prime field, the point-section map for a smooth hyperbolic curve is injective: use the full geometric group in characteristic zero, and its prime-to-$p$ quotient in characteristic $p$. For a proper curve of genus at least two over a finite field, the covering condition of scan 36 forces $P=Q$.

statement: The asserted characteristic-$p$ extension of cote 149, scan 32, Théorème 3, for every geometrically connected finite-type scheme embedded in a semiabelian variety, is false, already in dimension one. Over $\mathbf F_2$, take \[ E:\quad y^2+xy=x^3+1,\qquad O=\infty,\quad T=(0,1). \] The two points have identical prime-to-two section classes in the whole arithmetic extension. For an arbitrary semiabelian $G/K$ over a finitely generated characteristic-$p$ field, the exact replacement is \[ \ker\bigl(G(K)\to\hbox{prime-to-}p\hbox{ section classes}\bigr) =G(K)[p^\infty] \] after using the identity point to identify this section set with abelian Galois cohomology. A subscheme embedded in $G$ has injective point sections whenever no difference of distinct rational points lies in $G(K)[p^\infty]$.
notes: Working identifier C.R2. The characteristic-$p$ prime-to-$p$ extension of Théorème 3 in all dimensions. Refuted. All-dimensional prime-to-p Theorem3 refuted by elliptic p-torsion

statement: Point separation gives the isolating pointed cover of \statementref{B.19}; it gives no numerical value for the $p$-part of its relative class number. There is no universal assertion that every nontrivial pointed prime-to-$p$ cover has $p$-unit relative class number, or that every such cover has $p$-divisible relative class number. Both behaviours occur for the same curve, point, field, and prime degree in our computation. For $C_\alpha/\mathbf F_{64}$ of \statementref{B.21}, $\alpha$ with bit code $58$, and $P=\infty$, the degree-seven characters $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$ in the recorded basis give respectively \[ h(D_{(1,0)})/h(C)=46713473689,\qquad h(D_{(1,1)})/h(C)=55586549824. \] The first is odd and the second is even. Nevertheless the point-section map of $C$ is injective over this field and every constant extension.
notes: Working identifier C.R3. The precise class-number consequences and a sharp limitation. Proved. No universal relative-class-number parity follows from separation

statement: The characteristic-zero construction of a virtual puncture does not prove the surjectivity of the section map for the tripod over $\mathbf Q$, and does not construct a birational lift of an arbitrary section. The present finite-field injectivity theorem supplies no such assertion. Likewise a non-point-theoretic full section over a finite field obtained from a norm-module class in Part B is not a counterexample over a field finitely generated over $\mathbf Q$.

statement: Let $U,V$ be hyperbolic curves over finite fields, with an isomorphism of geometrically pro-$\Sigma$ tame groups. Assume, as in ST2017 Theorem~4.23, that there are corresponding open subgroups defining covers $U',V'$ whose smooth compactifications $X',Y'$ have genus at least two, with $\Sigma$ respectively $J_{X'}$-large and $J_{Y'}$-large. Then $E_U=E_V=\varnothing$, all closed-point decomposition labels are unique, and the unique scheme isomorphism with its pro-coverings in Theorem~4.23 has no exceptional-point restriction. The matched-open-subgroup hypothesis is part of this assertion.

statement: Let $U,V$ be hyperbolic curves over finite fields, and let $\Sigma_U^\dagger$ and $\Sigma_V^\dagger$ consist of every prime different from their respective characteristics. Every isomorphism of their geometrically pro-$\Sigma$ tame groups arises from a unique isomorphism of curves and corresponding pro-coverings. All their closed-point decomposition maps are injective, including after every constant extension and every open-subgroup covering. For proper $X,Y$, the restrictions to complements of exceptional sets in ST2009 Corollary~2.3, Theorem~3.6 and Proposition~3.8 can be replaced by all points.
notes: Working identifier C.LIT7. C2, C5. Proved: the prime-to-characteristic theorem and its simplified restrictions.

statement: For proper hyperbolic curves over finite fields and $\Sigma^\dagger=p'$, the $\Sigma$-separation assumption in Mochizuki's original Definition~1.18, Proposition~2.6(ii),(iii) and Corollary~3.11 is automatic. Thus a Frobenius-preserving isomorphism is point-theoretic, arbitrary finite corresponding marked sets are allowed in Theorem~2.5(i), the indicated proper and cuspidally abelian cusp decomposition groups are commensurably terminal, and the isomorphism is totally globally Green-compatible. The quotient repairs of A.35 are used at the fibre-identification inputs.
notes: Working identifier C.LIT8. C5. Proved: specific Mochizuki separation hypotheses become automatic.

statement: In the original Mochizuki 2007 text, the explicit separation or point-theoreticity conditions relevant to C5 are the loci in the following table. For finite fields with $\Sigma^\dagger=p'$, point-theoreticity and separation at these loci follow from \statementref{A.1} and its all-cover corollaries, as applied in C.7--8. Other hypotheses in the same statements remain. Wakabayashi 2016 and the two Sun preprints have no additional unproved finite-field prime-to-$p$ separation condition whose removal strengthens their stated theorems. The distinctions in the table are part of the conclusion.

statement: Let $k$ have characteristic zero, let $C/k$ be hyperbolic, and consider the projection $C^{(2)}=(C\times_k C)\setminus\Delta_C\to C$. Work in a specified quotient category in which there is an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow E\xrightarrow{q}\Pi_C \longrightarrow1. \] For every section $s:G_k\to\Pi_C$ the profinite pullback \[ \Pi_s=E\times_{\Pi_C,s}G_k \] is an extension $1\to F\to\Pi_s\to G_k\to1$. If $s=s_P$ is the section of $P\in C(k)$, the natural fibre map identifies $\Pi_s$ with the corresponding quotient of $\Pi_{C\setminus P}$, whenever the assumed exact fibration statement includes that fibre identification.
notes: Working identifier C.LIT1. C4. Proved: the exact pullback construction.

statement: Assume the chosen configuration quotient also retains a diagonal boundary decomposition group $D_\Delta$ mapping surjectively to $\Pi_C$, with kernel the surviving inertia $I_\Delta$. Then \[ D_s=D_\Delta\times_{\Pi_C,s}G_k\subset\Pi_s \] is the distinguished virtual cusp extension. The pair $(\Pi_s,D_s)$ depends only on the geometric conjugacy class of $s$, up to the corresponding inner ambiguity. For $s_P$ it is the actual punctured fibre group with its new cusp in the chosen quotient.
depends_on: Retained diagonal boundary decomposition with geometric lifting
notes: Working identifier C.LIT2. C4. Proved: retaining the distinguished cusp.

statement: The construction in C.10 is already Sun's virtual fundamental group. The two opened preprints do not assert that every virtual puncture is the puncture at a rational point.

statement: Suppose $k$ is finitely generated over $\Q$, $C/k$ is hyperbolic, and the base quotient retains the full arithmetic fundamental group, or at least the point-separating Kummer maps used below. A cusp-preserving isomorphism over the identity of this base quotient between the punctures at $P,Q\in C(k)$ forces $P=Q$. More generally, in the full base quotient, if the virtual puncture $(\Pi_s,D_s)$ is isomorphic over $\Pi_C$, preserving the distinguished cusp, to the actual puncture at $P$, then $s$ and $s_P$ are geometrically conjugate. Conversely a geometric section has that puncture by C.10.
notes: Working identifier C.LIT4. C4. Proved: the characteristic-zero recognition criterion.

statement: Let $C/k$ be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite field of characteristic $p$. The map \[ C(k)\longrightarrow \{s:G_k\to\Pi_C\mid \operatorname{pr}\circ s=\operatorname{id}\}/\Delta_C \] is injective. The same assertion holds for $C_L/L$ for every finite extension $L/k$. Thus AS-A.3 (AR.3), with precisely these hypotheses, is correct. This answers cote 149, scan 36, for proper hyperbolic curves.

statement: Let $1\to L\to H\to B_0\to1$ be an exact sequence of discrete groups, where $L$ is free of finite rank at least two. If conjugation by $H$ acts through an $r$-group on $L/[L,L]L^r$, the natural continuous map $L^{(r)}\to H^{(r)}$ is injective. Every prescribed finite $r$-quotient of $L$ is consequently dominated by the restriction of a finite $r$-quotient of $H$.
notes: No internal theorem dependency. Magnus and finite-r automorphism arguments are supplied. S1 blind proof and line comparison completed.

statement: Set $F=\Lambda^\Sigma$, $E=\Gamma^\Sigma$, and \[ \begin{split} K_F&=\ker(F\to\Delta),\qquad K_E=\ker(E\to\Delta\times\Delta),\\ F_{\crr}&=F/\ker(K_F\to K_F^{(r)}),\qquad E_{\crr}=E/\ker(K_E\to K_E^{(r)}). \end{split} \] The induced continuous sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow F_{\crr}\longrightarrow E_{\crr} \xrightarrow{\pr_2}\Delta\longrightarrow1 \] is exact. Every finite quotient of $F_{\crr}$ is dominated on the fibre by a finite quotient of $E_{\crr}$ which has a normal $r$-subgroup and a quotient $A\times A$, for a finite $\Sigma$-quotient $A$ of $\Delta$.
depends_on: A.2; external Bellingeri2004, Section 2.1 (discrete configuration fibre sequence)

statement: Let $C$ be smooth proper geometrically connected of genus at least two over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, and let $\Sigma$ be any set of primes not containing $p$, with $r\in\Sigma$. The preceding relative exact sequence holds for geometric etale groups. If $C/k$ is defined over a finite field and $P\in C(k)$, its arithmetic cuspidally pro-$r$ group is the inverse image of a chosen point section $s_P(G_k)$ under the second projection of the arithmetic configuration quotient. The comparison is over the identity of the whole $G_k$.
depends_on: A.3; external LA_SGA1 [source as cited; exact passage in source audit]; external LA_SGA1, III 7.3–7.4 and XIII 2.9–2.11 (lifted pair and prime-to-characteristic specialization)

statement: In the arithmetic situation of \statementref{A.4}, the image $\mathcal D$ of a fixed diagonal boundary component fits into a continuous exact sequence \[ 1\to\Z_r(1)\to\mathcal D\to\Pi_C\to1, \] and maps diagonally to $\Pi_C\times_{G_k}\Pi_C$. With paths chosen through this boundary, the actual cusp subgroup of $C-P$ is $\mathcal D\cap\pr_2^{-1}(s_P(G_k))$. Consequently, geometrically conjugate proper point sections give an isomorphism of their actual cuspidally pro-$r$ punctured groups over the identity of $\Pi_C$, carrying the cusp subgroup to a geometric conjugate of the other cusp.
depends_on: A.3;A.4; external LA_SGA1 [source as cited; exact passage in source audit]; external LA_SGA1, XIII 5.2 (tame boundary charts); finite étale descent

Thus actual direct deps are A3,A4. A48 supplies an independent stronger alternative, but is not silently substituted as this proof. External CF_SGA1 XIII5.2 gives local Kummer comparison.

statement: For genus two, $p=2$, $r=3$, and $A=(\Z/3)^4\times\Z/5$, there is a quotient of the fibre of order $1215$, with central cuspidal subgroup of order three and proper quotient $A$, which embeds in a quotient of the configuration group of order $492075$ with central kernel of order three over $A\times A$. The defining surface braid relations and the fibre injection have been checked by the retained program.

statement: Let $F_4=\langle a,b,c,d\rangle$ be the first fibre in the genus-two pure surface braid group $P_2$. Map $F_4$ onto the Heisenberg group $H=\operatorname{UT}_3(\F_3)$ by sending $a,b$ to its standard generators and $c,d$ to one. Let $K$ be the kernel and $N=[K,K]K^5$. Then the finite odd quotient $F_4/N$, of order $27\cdot5^{82}$, is not dominated on the fibre by any finite odd quotient of $P_2$. In particular $F_4^{(2')}\to P_2^{(2')}$ is not injective. The conclusion applies to the geometric groups of $y^2+y=x^5$ in characteristic two by specialization.
