statement: Suppose $C/\mathbb C$ has genus at least two and the full pro-$\Sigma$ fibre map for $(C\times C)-\operatorname{diag}$ is injective. For every connected finite Galois etale $\Sigma$-cover $C'\to C$, the analogous full fibre map for $C'$ is injective as well.
notes: As written it explicitly refers to the finite-quotient right-exactness argument in A3. This edge may be deleted if that already-stated universal-property argument is treated inline and the shorthand cross-reference is removed; no relative left-injectivity theorem is used.

statement: Let $C/\mathbb C$ have genus $h\geq2$, and let $r,\ell$ be distinct primes. There is a connected degree-$r^3$ cover of $C-P$, with $r$-group Galois group and cusp inertia of order $r$, whose compact homology modulo $\ell$ has a subspace of dimension $2h-2$ on which a subgroup of the configuration group preserving the cover acts onto $\operatorname{Sp}_{2h-2}(\F_\ell)$. Consequently, if $r,\ell\in\Sigma$ and the full pro-$\Sigma$ configuration fibre were injective, every prime divisor of $|\operatorname{Sp}_{2h-2}(\F_\ell)|$ would belong to $\Sigma$.
notes: Uses the normal-core topology argument supplied in A8, not its conclusion about passing to proper curve covers. All topological point-push and symplectic calculations are written in A9.

statement: For a smooth proper complex curve of genus at least two, the full pro-$\Sigma$ configuration fibre sequence is exact if and only if $\Sigma$ is empty, consists of one prime, or is the set of all primes. If $C$ instead has characteristic $p$ and $\Sigma\subseteq\{\ell:\ell\ne p\}$, it is exact if and only if $|\Sigma|\leq1$. In particular the full prime-to-$p$ fibre map is noninjective for every $p$ and every such curve, as claimed in R4. The relative cuspidally pro-$r$ sequence of \statementref{A.3} remains exact for every $r\in\Sigma$.
notes: A3 is needed for the final relative-repair assertion in the statement. External CF_MT2008 Proposition2.2 only for total formation. A4 transfers the full-fibre classification only for p excluded.

statement: Let $C_0,B/\mathbb C$ be smooth proper curves, with $B$ of genus at least one and $C_0$ of genus at least two, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_m:B\to C_0$ have pairwise disjoint graphs. For $Y=(C_0\times B)-\bigcup_i\operatorname{graph}(f_i)$, the relative cuspidally pro-$r$ fibre sequence over pro-$\Sigma$ proper groups is exact for every $r\in\Sigma$. The same assertion holds for simultaneously liftable smooth proper pairs in characteristic prime to every member of $\Sigma$ by the preceding specialization. In particular it applies to the diagonal families after finite proper covers used in cuspidally abelian reconstruction.
notes: This is the inherited simultaneously-liftable variant. The stronger direct constant-family proof follows from A45,A46 with the common-cover/core calculation repeated in A35; use those deps if replacing A11 by that stronger proof.

statement: For a genus-three curve, the full pro-$\{2,3\}$ configuration fibre map is noninjective. A particular obstructing fibre quotient has order $8\cdot3^{41}$; an exact computation of the preserving braid action on a four-dimensional homology subspace gives $\operatorname{Sp}_4(\F_3)$, of order $51840$, and an explicit acting element of order five.

statement: Let $F$ be profinite, $K\triangleleft F$ closed, $r$ prime, and $N=\ker(K\to K^{(r)})$. For every open $I\le F$ containing $N$, the continuous quotient map induces a natural isomorphism $I^{(r)}\simeq(I/N)^{(r)}$. No restriction on $[F:I]$ is imposed.

statement: Let $C/k$ be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $P\in C(k)$, and let $r\in\Sigma\setminus\{p\}$, with no other restriction on $\Sigma$. Put $U=C-P$, $F=\pi_1(U_{\bar k})^\Sigma$, $\Delta=\pi_1(C_{\bar k})^\Sigma$, $K=\ker(F\to\Delta)$, and $N=\ker(K\to K^{(r)})$. Let $G_P$ be the arithmetic relative cuspidally pro-$r$ quotient, with geometric kernel $F/N$ and full arithmetic quotient $G_k$. For every open geometric subgroup $I/N\le F/N$, let $V$ be its actual connected geometric cover of $U_{\bar k}$ and let $\bar V$ be its smooth compactification. If $T_I$ is the closed normal subgroup of $I/N$ generated by all its cusp inertia images, then the actual covering and compactification maps induce an isomorphism \[ ((I/N)/T_I)^{(r)}\simeq\pi_1(\bar V)^{(r)}. \] This isomorphism is compatible with every arithmetic outer action preserving the cover. Consequently, a cusp-preserving isomorphism of such arithmetic relative groups over $G_k$ preserves the integral Frobenius polynomial and the point counts of every pair of corresponding open covers, over every finite constant extension. In particular these assertions allow $p\in\Sigma$.

statement: Let $\Sigma$ contain a prime $r\ne p$, allowing $p\in\Sigma$. statement: Let $\Sigma$ contain two distinct primes $r,s$, and let $\Delta$ be the pro-$\Sigma$ completion of a surface group of genus at least two. Its Frattini quotient $\Delta/\Phi(\Delta)$ is infinite, where $\Phi$ is the intersection of the maximal open subgroups. In particular this applies to the geometric pro-$\Sigma$ group of a proper curve in characteristic outside $\Sigma$. For $\Sigma=\{2,3\}$ there is, moreover, an explicit two-generated group $G$ of order $576$, with $\Phi(G)=1$, and an automorphism of order seven acting trivially on $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$. Neither assertion is a counterexample to mixed-prime point separation. They show why the finite-Frattini and abelianization arguments used for a single prime do not extend by the same reasoning.

statement: Let $k$ be a perfect field, let $C/k$ be a proper smooth geometrically connected curve of genus at least two, and let $\Sigma^\dagger=\{r\in\Sigma:r\text{ is invertible in }k\}$ be nonempty. Thus $\Sigma^\dagger=\Sigma$ in characteristic zero and $\Sigma^\dagger=\Sigma\setminus\{p\}$ in characteristic $p>0$. Let $F\to E\to\Delta_2\to1$ be the geometric right-exact configuration sequence, let $F\twoheadrightarrow\Delta_1$ be the proper fibre quotient, and let $E\twoheadrightarrow\Delta_1\times\Delta_2$ be the proper product quotient. Write $K_F,K_E$ for their cuspidal kernels. Suppose the relative groups are formed from the \emph{tame} boundary groups, with Mochizuki's maximal cuspidally pro-$\Sigma^\dagger$ convention. The proper groups may retain $p$ in $\Sigma$. The relative cuspidally pro-$r$ fibre theorem of Part~A, including A.13, holds for every $r\in\Sigma^\dagger$. Then \[ K_F^{(r)}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E^{(r)}\quad(r\in\Sigma^\dagger), \qquad K_F^{\mathrm{ab}}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E^{\mathrm{ab}}. \] Consequently the configuration fibre sequence is left exact after cuspidal abelianization, as well as after the specified fixed-prime cuspidal completion. The one-puncture geometrically cuspidally central fibre identification also holds. For a $k$-rational point, the corresponding arithmetic inverse-image identifications hold over the unchanged quotient $G_k$.

statement: Suppose $P,Q\in C(k)$ and $\beta:G_P\xrightarrow{\sim}G_Q$ is a continuous isomorphism over $\operatorname{id}_{\Pi_C^\Sigma}$ preserving the cusp decomposition conjugacy class. Put $M=\mathbf Z_r(1)$, with its arithmetic cyclotomic action and its actual local inertia convention: $z^{1/r^a}\mapsto\zeta z^{1/r^a}$ represents $\zeta\in\mu_{r^a}$. The geometrically cuspidally central quotients fit into exact sequences \[ 1\to M\to E_A\to\Pi_C^\Sigma\to1\qquad(A=P,Q). \] The isomorphism induced by $\beta$ is the identity on $M$. On the arithmetic geometrically pro-$\Sigma$ group $\Gamma$ of $C-\{P,Q\}$ there is a continuous $M$-valued crossed homomorphism $\chi$ with residues $(1,-1)$ at $(P,Q)$. If $\operatorname{div}(f)=n(P-Q)$ for $f\in k(C)^\times$ and $n>0$, then there is $a\in k^\times$ such that \[ \kappa_r(f)-n[\chi]=\kappa_r(a) \quad\text{in }H^1(\Gamma,M). \tag{A.42.1} \] No assertion about exceptional points or transported point labels is used in this construction.

statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p\geq0$, let $r$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $C_0,S$ be smooth proper connected $k$-curves, with $g(S)\geq1$. Let $m\geq1$, and let $d_1,\ldots,d_m:S\to C_0\times S$ be pairwise disjoint sections. Put $X=C_0\times S$, $D=\coprod_i d_i(S)$, $U=X-D$, and $f:U\to S$. For a geometric point $s$ of $S$, every finite $r$-group quotient of $\pi_1(U_s)$ is dominated by the restriction of a finite $r$-group quotient of $\pi_1(U)$. Equivalently, $\pi_1(U_s)^{(r)}\to\pi_1(U)^{(r)}$ is injective. More precisely, every finite $r$-group torsor on $U_s$ extends to a torsor with the same group on $U\times_S S'$ for some connected finite \'etale cover $S'\to S$ whose Galois closure is an $r$-cover.

statement: Let $C/k$ be smooth proper geometrically connected of genus at least two over a finite field of characteristic $p$, and let $r\in\Sigma\setminus\{p\}$. Let $\Pi_C$ be the geometrically pro-$\Sigma$ arithmetic fundamental group, retaining the whole $G_k$. Let $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{cr}}$ be the arithmetic relative cuspidally pro-$r$ configuration group. statement: Let $a:J_C(L)\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a nontrivial finite abelian quotient of order prime to $p$, and use the Abel map based at $P$ to pull back its constant Lang quotient. Put \[ \Theta_{C,P,A}=\sum_{d=0}^{g-1} \sum_{E\in\operatorname{Div}^{+}_d(C)(L)} [a([E-dP])]\quad\text{in }\mathbf F_p[A]. \] Its relative class number is prime to $p$ if and only if $\overline\psi(\Theta_{C,P,A})\ne0$ for every nontrivial character $\overline\psi:A\to\overline{\mathbf F}_p^\times$. For $A=\mathbf Z/\ell$ this is precisely B1's simultaneous test; it is not enough to check one reduced character unless all primitive characters form one Frobenius orbit.
notes: Working identifier B.CL2. Simultaneous character criterion in every genus. Proved. All-genus simultaneous effective-divisor character test

statement: For any quotient $A$ of $J_C(L)$ let $N=\#C(L)$ and let $N_b$ be the occupancies of the Abel-image points in its cosets. Then \[ \sum_bN_b(N_b-1) \le \frac{N^2}{|A|} +\frac{|A|-1}{|A|}(2g-2)^2q-N. \tag{B.CL.1} \] If all nonzero occupancies are multiples of $p$, the left side is at least $(p-1)(N-N_0)$. In genus two, if $p$ generates $(\mathbf Z/\ell)^\times$, a surjection with kernel $H\subset J_C(L)$ is a class-number witness whenever \[ N\ge2|H|,\qquad \ell>N. \tag{B.CL.2} \] Neither $p>(2g-2)^2$ nor these estimates alone proves universal existence of such a quotient. For $g>2$, occupancies of points alone are not the character test in B.2.
notes: Working identifier B.CL3. The corrected pair estimate and its precise limitation. Proved. Corrected pair estimate and the primitive-root genus-two sufficient conditions

statement: Fix $(C,P)/\mathbf F_q$ and an odd prime $\ell\ne p$. There is a finite procedure deciding whether B1 has an order-$\ell$ witness over \emph{any} constant extension. For each geometric nonzero character $\chi:\pi_1(C_{\overline k})\to\mathbf F_\ell$, let $m$ be its least Frobenius period. Construct its unique $P$-split constant cover over $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}$. It suffices to test these finitely many covers at these first fields. If $A_\chi$ is Frobenius on their new geometric $p$-torsion, the exact extension degrees preserving the witness are \[ n\ge1\quad\text{such that}\quad \det(1-A_\chi^n)\ne0. \tag{B.CL.3} \] A failed first-field test never becomes a witness at a later field. A successful one remains successful under all extensions of $p$-power degree.
notes: Working identifier B.CL4. A finite all-constant-extension decision for each fixed prime. Proved. Finite decision over all constant extensions for each fixed prime

statement: For every prescribed $(C,P)$ as in B1, prove or refute the existence of a prime $\ell$ for which at least one first-field test in B.4 succeeds. This remains undecided here, including the universal assertion for pairs $(p,g)$ with $p>(2g-2)^2$. B.3 gives the corrected numerical sufficient conditions; B.28--B.29 prove unpointed existence and quantify the prescribed-point obstruction. The R8 example has the explicit least-prime witness proved in B.26--B.27, and B.30 gives a plane-quartic instance. None of these removes the arbitrary-curve and prescribed-point quantifiers.

statement: There is a natural exact sequence of compact abelian pro-$p$ groups \[ 0\longrightarrow V\xrightarrow{F-1}V \xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M_P^F\longrightarrow0. \] For every $F$-stable normal level $H$, projection gives a continuous surjection \[ M_P^F\longrightarrow J_{D_H}(k)[p^\infty]. \] In particular $M_P^F$ need not vanish. The first term in the exact sequence is a Tate-module inverse limit; its Frobenius invariants vanish, whereas its Frobenius coinvariants need not vanish.
notes: Working identifier B.NM1. The integral description of the fixed norm module. Proved.

statement: Every $m\in M_P^F$ is the compatible $p$-adic abelianized difference of a continuous full étale arithmetic section from $s_P$. Its projection to the geometrically prime-to-$p$ quotient is exactly $s_P$. If $m\ne0$, the realizing section is not geometrically conjugate to a point section. This conclusion uses point separation proved by the cuspidal criterion and transport above; it does not assert free deck orbits for $m$.
notes: Working identifier B.NM2. All fixed classes have full arithmetic section realizations. Proved.

statement: For an $F$-stable open normal $H\triangleleft\Delta$, let $S_H$ be the finite set of $a\in J_{D_H}(k)[p^\infty]$ such that, for every normal $K\triangleleft\Delta$ containing $H$, the norm of $a$ to $D_K$ has trivial stabilizer in $\Delta/K$. The quotient $K/H$ and the curve $D_K$ need not be $F$-stable. Then the set of fixed norm-module vectors with free orbits at every normal level is naturally \[ \varprojlim_H S_H. \] It is nonempty if and only if every $S_H$ is nonempty. Any such vector is nonzero. Consequently, nonexistence of an all-level free vector has a finite certificate of this specific form: one stable pointed normal cover for which $S_H$ is empty.
notes: Working identifier B.NM3. An exact finite criterion for free orbits at every normal level. Proved.

statement: Suppose there are a finite extension $L/k$ and compatible pointed étale prime-to-$p$ covers $Z\to Y\to C_L$, both geometrically normal over $C$, such that $Z\to Y$ is nontrivial Galois and \[ p\nmid\frac{\#J_Z(L)}{\#J_Y(L)}. \] Then $M_P^F$ contains no vector with free deck orbit at every normal level. The geometric deck groups need not be constant over $L$. This is a sufficient condition, not a claimed equivalence with the existence of one cyclic witness over $C$.
notes: Working identifier B.NM4. A relative class-number witness obstructs free vectors. Proved.

statement: For the smooth proper model over $\F_2$ of \[ C:\quad y^2+y=x+\frac1x+\frac1{x+1}, \] one has $J_C(\F_2)\simeq(\Z/2)^2$. For every rational base point $P$, the group $M_P^F$ therefore has nonzero classes and these have non-point-theoretic full arithmetic section realizations. This assertion does not provide an all-level free vector.
notes: Working identifier B.NM5. Nonzero fixed classes on an explicit genus-two curve. Proved.

statement: The implication from a free vector in a finite coprime deck module to a free norm at every normal quotient is false, even for an abelian odd group acting on an $\F_2$-vector space.
notes: Working identifier B.NM6. Freeness at one normal level need not survive norm. Refuted.

statement: It remains undetermined here whether $M_P^F$ has no nonzero all-level free vector for every genus-two curve in characteristic two over every finite field of definition, and whether an all-level free vector exists for any proper hyperbolic curve in any characteristic. The general fixed classes and their full section realizations have been determined above, but these results do not decide nonemptiness of the inverse limit in \statementref{B.8} for all such curves.

statement: Let $D\to C$ be a pointed geometrically connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover over $k=\mathbf F_q$, with abelian geometric Galois group $A$ of order prime to $p=\operatorname{char}k$. The chosen point of $D$ lies rationally above $P$. Let $F$ act on $A$ by the pointed arithmetic descent, and put \[ S_D(k)=\{a\in J_D(k)[p^\infty]: \operatorname{Nm}_{D/D_H}(a) \text{ has trivial stabilizer in }A/H \text{ for every }H\le A\}, \tag{B.AB.1} \] where $D_H=D_{\overline k}/H$, with its pointed descent whenever the subgroup is stable under a power of $F$. For each subgroup $H$ for which $A/H$ is a nontrivial cyclic prime-power group $\mathbf Z/\ell^a$, let $m_H$ be its orbit length under $F$, and let $H^+/H$ be the unique subgroup of order $\ell$ in $A/H$. Both quotient curves have their pointed models over $k_{m_H}=\mathbf F_{q^{m_H}}$. Then \[ S_D(k)\ne\varnothing \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p\mid \frac{\#J_{D_H}(k_{m_H})}{\#J_{D_{H^+}}(k_{m_H})} \quad\text{for every such }H. \tag{B.AB.2} \] Thus an empty set at a finite abelian normal level is equivalent to a relative class-number unit in one cyclic prime-power tower, at that quotient's first pointed field of definition. The step $D_H\to D_{H^+}$ has prime degree $\ell$; its lower curve need not be $C$.
notes: Working identifier B.AB1. Finite abelian norm obstructions, including nonconstant deck groups. Proved.

statement: If the group $A$ in \statementref{B.13} is constant, then all $m_H=1$. If in addition $A=(\mathbf Z/\ell)^d$, then $S_D(k)$ is nonempty exactly when every degree-$\ell$ quotient $D_H\to C$ has relative class number divisible by $p$. Thus at a constant elementary-abelian level, an obstruction is exactly a prime-degree class-number witness among those quotients. For higher-exponent abelian groups, the exact criterion also tests the primitive parts at cyclic prime-power quotients. These tests are strictly stronger as finite module conditions than testing only prime-degree quotients. This strictness does not assert that a particular curve has no prime-degree witness over all constant extensions.
notes: Working identifier B.AB2. The elementary-prime case and the stronger higher-power test. Proved.

statement: Let $G$ be a finite solvable group of order prime to $p$, acting on a finite abelian $p$-group $M$. Let $F$ be an automorphism of $M$, and let $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ satisfy $F(gm)=\sigma(g)F(m)$. For $K\triangleleft G$ put \[ e_K=|K|^{-1}\sum_{g\in K}g. \] There exists $a\in M^F$ with \[ \operatorname{Stab}_G(e_Ka)=K \quad(K\triangleleft G) \tag{B.SV.1} \] if and only if \[ \bigcap_{b\in M^F}\operatorname{Stab}_G(e_Kb)=K \quad(K\triangleleft G). \tag{B.SV.2} \] Neither $M^F$ nor an individual norm image is assumed to be $G$-stable. The order of $F$ or of $\sigma$ may be divisible by $p$.
notes: Working identifier B.SV1. Simultaneous norm freeness for solvable coprime actions. Proved.

statement: Let $D\to C$ be a constant pointed normal prime-to-$p$ cover over a finite field $k$, with solvable deck group $G$. The finite all-normal-quotient norm-free set $S_D(k)$ is empty if and only if there exist normal subgroups $K\subsetneq L\triangleleft G$ such that \[ p\nmid \frac{\#J_{D_K}(k)}{\#J_{D_L}(k)}. \tag{B.SV.7} \] In particular, for constant solvable deck groups, the relative class-number-unit sufficient criterion is also necessary at that finite level. The lower curve $D_L$ can differ from $C$, and the degree of the step is not required to be prime.
notes: Working identifier B.SV2. Constant solvable covers have exactly the relative-unit obstruction. Proved.

statement: For any proper hyperbolic pointed curve $(C,P)/k$ in characteristic two, $M_P^F$ has no all-level free vector if and only if there are a pointed $F$-stable normal cover $D\to C$, a normal subgroup $K$ of its geometric deck group $G$, and an element $g\in G\setminus K$ such that \[ g\,\operatorname{Nm}_{D/D_K}(a) =\operatorname{Nm}_{D/D_K}(a) \qquad\text{for every }a\in J_D(k)[2^\infty]. \tag{B.SV.8} \] The quotient $D_K$ need only be defined over its pointed finite constant extension. Thus in characteristic two a finite obstruction can always be witnessed by one quotient and one element fixing every candidate norm coordinate. It cannot require only a union of different stabilizers covering the candidates. This reformulation does not prove that such a finite certificate exists for every genus-two curve. That universal existence assertion in B2 remains open here.
depends_on: B.8;B.15; external FeitThompson1963 [Chapter~I, \S1, p.~775, unnumbered main theorem]
notes: Working identifier B.SV3. A single-element finite certificate in characteristic two. Proved.

statement: The equivalence of \statementref{B.13} cannot be extended to arbitrary finite groups using only the vanishing of relative $p$-primary modules at normal quotient steps. There is a faithful action of a finite nonabelian simple $7'$-group $G$ on a nonzero finite $7$-group $M$ such that the set of vectors with free norm orbit at every normal quotient is empty, although the relative module at every nontrivial normal step is nonzero. This is an exact finite representation example, not a claimed realization by a Jacobian or a counterexample to universal B1.

statement: For every $C/k$ as in \statementref{A.1} and every $P\in C(k)$, there is a connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover $D\to C$ with geometrically Galois group of order prime to $p$, and a specified $P'\in D(k)$ over $P$, such that the image of $D(k)$ in $C(k)$ is exactly $\{P\}$. The geometric deck group need not be constant over $k$.

statement: Let $C/L$ be proper of genus at least two over a finite field of characteristic two, $P\in C(L)$, and let $D\to C$ be a connected constant cyclic odd-degree \emph{\'etale} cover with a point $P_D\in D(L)$ above $P$. Suppose $h(D)/h(C)$ is odd. Let $E\to D$ be the Lang cover associated with the maximal odd quotient of $J_D(L)$ and based at $P_D$. Then no point of $C(L)$ other than $P$ lifts rationally to $E$. Taking the geometric Galois closure and its $P$-pointed twist preserves this property and gives an odd geometric Galois cover of $C$.

statement: Write $\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0$. The two conjugate curves \[ C_\alpha:\quad Y^2+(x^2+x+\alpha)Y =x^5+\alpha x^3+x+1 \] are the curves denoted by the pair of class labels $203/302$ in the supplied return. Each has seven $\mathbf F_4$-points. statement: The assertion that every genus-two curve in characteristic two has a connected cyclic \emph{\'etale} cover of odd degree $n>1$ whose primitive Jacobian part has two-rank zero is false. A completely specified counterexample is the smooth proper model over $k=\mathbf F_2[t]/(M(t))$ of \[ \begin{split} M(Z)&=Z^{38}+Z^{14}+Z^{10}+Z^9+Z^8+Z^5+Z^2+Z+1,\\ d&=t^3+1,\qquad C:\ y^2+y=A(u)^3,\\ A(u)&=(u^2+t^2u+t)/d,\qquad B(u)=(tu^2+u+t^2)/d . \end{split} \] The polynomial $M$ is irreducible, and $C$ is supersingular of genus two with a unique rational point $P$ above infinity. For every such cover over $\bar k$, the primitive part has positive two-rank. This independently confirms the particular counterexample AS-A.86. It does not refute the version allowing degree one.

statement: Let $K=\mathbf F_{2^d}$, and let \[ C:\quad Y^2+hY=f(x),\qquad h\in K^\times, \quad f\text{ monic of degree five}, \] be smooth, with marked point $P=\infty$. Let $\ell$ be an odd prime such that $\mu_\ell\subset K$, and let $a\in J_C(K)$ have exact order $\ell$. Suppose every nonzero $ia$ has reduced Mumford representative $(u_i,v_i)$ of degree two. Write $j=2i\bmod\ell$ and \[ \begin{split} w_i&=(v_i^2+hv_i+f)/u_i,\\ V_i&=v_i+u_i\bigl((w_i/h)\bmod u_i\bigr),\\ c_i&=(V_i)_3\,(u_j)_1. \end{split} \] Here subscripts on polynomials indicate coefficients. Then the unique constant cyclic, $P$-split cover with character subgroup $\langle a\rangle$ has odd relative class number if and only if \[ A_i:=\prod_{s=0}^{d-1}c_{2^s i}^{\,2^{d-1-s}}\ne1 \qquad(1\le i<\ell). \] The index on each $c$ is reduced modulo $\ell$. The assertion includes the specified pointing; there is no unspecified constant twist.

A second such cover, of degree $229$, exists over $\mathbf F_{2^{152}}$. Their genera are respectively $192$ and $230$, and their new Jacobian parts are ordinary of dimensions $190$ and $228$.

statement: Let $C/K$ be smooth proper of genus $g\ge2$ over a finite field of characteristic $p$. Let $D\to C$ be a geometrically connected \emph{\'etale} cover with constant cyclic deck group of odd prime order $\ell\ne p$. Put $f=\operatorname{ord}_\ell(p)$. Among the $\ell$ constant twists of this cover, at most \[ \frac{(g-1)(\ell-1)}{f} \] have relative class number divisible by $p$. In particular, if $f\ge g-1$, at least one twist has $p$-unit relative class number. For genus two this last condition is automatic.

statement: For every smooth proper curve $C/k$ of genus $g\ge2$ over a finite field, there are a finite extension $K/k$, a point $P_K\in C(K)$, and a constant cyclic $P_K$-split cover of odd prime degree, different from the characteristic, with $p$-unit relative class number. The point $P_K$ is not prescribed in advance. More quantitatively, for a constant degree-$\ell$ cover as in \statementref{B.28}, put $B=(g-1)(\ell-1)/f$ and $g_D=1+\ell(g-1)$. If $f\ge g-1$, the number of $P\in C(K)$ for which its unique split twist is a class-number witness is at least \[ \frac{\ell-B}{\ell} \bigl(\#K+1-2g_D\sqrt{\#K}\bigr). \]
notes: Working identifier B.TW2. Existence with an unspecified base point. Proved.

statement: Let $C/\mathbf F_3$ be the smooth plane quartic \[ W^4=X^3Z-XZ^3,\qquad P=(1:0:0). \] There is a $P$-split constant cyclic degree-five cover over $\mathbf F_{3^8}$ whose relative class number is prime to three. Thus five is the least odd prime different from the characteristic which gives a witness for this pointed curve over some constant extension. Every constant degree-five cover of this curve requires a constant degree divisible by eight; the displayed field is therefore also the least one for a degree-five witness. The certificates give six such covers. For each of them the relative class number stays prime to three exactly under further constant extensions of odd degree.

notes: Working identifier B.Q1. A least-prime-five quartic witness over \(\mathbf F_{3^8}\). Proved. Least odd prime5 and least constant degree8 for the specified F3 plane quartic

statement: Let $C/\mathbf F_5$ have the same equation and point as in B.30. Pull its quadratic map to $E:y^2=x^3-x$ back along the duals of the four cyclic degree-three isogenies out of $E$, over $K=\mathbf F_{5^8}$. These four constant $P$-split covers have genus seven. Every one has relative class number divisible by five over $K$ and over every further constant extension. This assertion concerns these four covers; it does not exclude the other order-three characters of $J_C$ or other primes.

B.30 is an exact least-prime and first-field result for one pointed quartic; B.31 excludes four actual covers at all later fields. The independent program \path{code/pointed_quartic_tests.py} also computes the point counts and Weil polynomials of $X^4+Y^4+Z^4=0$ over $\mathbf F_3$, at $(1:1:1)$, and $X^4+Y^4-Z^4=0$ over $\mathbf F_5$, at $(1:0:1)$. Their base-field Jacobian orders are $64$ and $256$, respectively, so they have no base-field odd-prime Lang quotient. This is not an all-extension exclusion. The previous return's large base-field census programs were not attached and have not been rerun here. We do not treat their numerical tables as newly verified certificates. It also remains undecided whether some curve has a nonabelian witness of the stated type and has no class-number witness over any extension. Failure of finitely many characters, primes, or fields cannot prove that assertion.

statement: Let \[ C/\mathbf F_5:\quad W^4=X^3Z-XZ^3,\qquad P=(1:0:0). \] Over $K=\mathbf F_{125}$ there is a constant cyclic, $P$-split, \emph{\'etale} cover $D\to C$ of degree thirteen with \[ g_D=27,\qquad \frac{\#J_D(K)}{\#J_C(K)}\equiv1\pmod5. \] Its new Jacobian part is ordinary of dimension twenty-four. At that first field, thirteen is the least possible prime, and \statementref{B.33} attains it. statement: Let $E/\overline{\F}_p$ be an elliptic curve, let $\pi:E\to E/\{\pm1\}\simeq\mathbf P^1$ be its quotient map, and let $S\subset\mathbf P^1(\overline{\F}_p)$ be finite. There exists $\phi\in\mathrm{PGL}_2(\overline{\F}_p)$ such that every point of $\phi(S)$ is the image under $\pi$ of a prime-to-$p$ torsion point of $E$. The points of $\phi(S)$ may also be required to avoid the branch locus of $\pi$.

statement: Let $p$ be odd and let $C/\overline{\F}_p$ be hyperelliptic of genus at least two. For every hyperelliptic curve $H/\overline{\F}_p$ there is a connected finite \'etale cover $D\to C$ with prime-to-$p$ geometric Galois closure and a nonconstant map $D\to H$. In particular B5 holds for every such $C$, including characteristic three, with a supersingular target of genus at least two.
notes: Working identifier B.LIT2. B5. Proved: every odd-characteristic hyperelliptic source.

statement: Let $p=2$. Suppose a curve $C/\overline{\F}_2$ admits a finite separable map to $\mathbf P^1$ with three distinct fibres in which every ramification index is divisible by three. Then a connected finite \'etale cover of $C$ of degree one or three maps nonconstantly to a supersingular elliptic curve. In particular this applies to every cyclic degree-three cover of $\mathbf P^1$ of genus at least two.

statement: Suppose $p$ is odd, $C/\overline{\F}_p$ has genus at least two, and $G\subset\Aut(C)$ has order prime to $p$. Put $Y=C/G$ and suppose $g(Y)\le2$. If at least one of the following holds, then $C$ has a connected finite \'etale cover with prime-to-$p$ Galois closure mapping to a supersingular curve of genus at least two: \begin{enumerate} \item $g(Y)=1$ or $2$; \item $G$ is solvable; \item two distinct branch values of $C\to Y$ have ramification indices with a common prime factor. \end{enumerate} In particular this proves B5 for every tamely superelliptic curve in every odd characteristic, including characteristic three.

statement: Let $C/\F_2$ be the smooth proper model \[ C:\quad Y^2+X^2Y=X^5+X, \qquad P=\infty. \] It has genus two, $2$-rank one, and no nonzero supersingular isogeny factor in its geometric Jacobian. Over $k=\F_{64}$ there is a connected $P$-pointed cyclic \'etale cover $D\to C_k$ of degree $13$, with zeta numerator \[ P_D(T)= (1-T-80T^2-64T^3+4096T^4) (1+12T+64T^2)^{12}. \tag{B.LIT.7} \] Its primitive degree-$13$ factor has Newton slopes $1/3$ and $2/3$, each with multiplicity $12$, and hence has $2$-rank zero. Its relative class number is \[ \frac{|J_D(k)|}{|J_C(k)|}=77^{12} =43439888521963583647921, \] which is odd. Nevertheless $D$ has no nonconstant map, even over $\overline{\F}_2$, to any supersingular curve of positive genus. Thus this is a B1 witness and a nontrivial positive-$2$-rank case of B4, but this particular cover does not supply the correspondence asked for in B5.
notes: Working identifier B.LIT7. An exact cyclic-thirteen distinction between B4 and B5. Proved.

statement: Let $C$ be a smooth hyperelliptic curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, of genus $g\in\{2,3\}$ and $2$-rank zero. For every connected cyclic \'etale cover $D\to C$ of degree three, the Prym variety is ordinary of dimension $2(g-1)$. In particular, $f_D=2(g-1)$. In genus three its genus-two reflection quotient is ordinary, so this cubic-reflection construction does not yield a supersingular target.

statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $f:C\to\mathbb P^1_k$ be finite separable, and assume that for every $t\in\mathbb P^1(k)$, \[ \gcd\{e_P(f):P\in f^{-1}(t)\}=1. \] Let $C'\to C$ be any finite \'etale cover and $h:\mathbb P^1\to\mathbb P^1$ any finite separable map. The composite $h\circ f\circ\pi$ cannot have three distinct fibres in each of which all ramification indices are divisible by three. It cannot have four distinct fibres in each of which they are all even. More generally, uniform fibre divisibilities $m_i$ at distinct values require \[ \sum_i(1-1/m_i)<2. \]
notes: Working identifier B.LIT9. A fixed simply branched function cannot supply the missing fibres. Proved.

statement: Let $C/\overline{\F}_p$ be a smooth proper curve admitting a finite separable map to $\mathbb P^1$ with three distinct fibres in which every ramification index is divisible by the same odd integer $r\ge3$. Suppose $r\mid p^a+1$ for some $a\ge1$. Then $C$ has a connected cyclic \'etale cover of degree dividing $r$ which dominates a supersingular curve of genus $(r-1)/2$. Its geometric Galois closure therefore has order prime to $p$. In characteristic two this applies to every cyclic prime-degree cover of $\mathbb P^1$ of genus at least two whose degree $\ell$ satisfies that $\operatorname{ord}_\ell(2)$ is even.

statement: Suppose \(\operatorname{trdeg}_{\Q}k<\infty\). For finite-type \(k\)-schemes, the functor to the preceding pro-systems is fully faithful after universal homeomorphisms are inverted, with pinned morphisms in \(\operatorname{Pro}(\mathsf T)_{/\mathcal B}\) as target morphisms. Equivalently, for absolutely weakly normal finite-type \(X,Y\), every such pinned ordinary pro-morphism is induced by a unique \(k\)-morphism \(X\to Y\). This includes all finite-transcendence-degree fields of B8, regardless of whether reconstruction from the single topos over \(k\) holds.

statement: The mechanism in B.43 does not extend by the same argument to an arbitrary characteristic-zero field: transitions corresponding to transcendental field extensions need not preserve closed points. Specifically, for \(F\) of characteristic zero and \(u\) transcendental, the point \(T=u\) of \(\mathbb A^1_{F(u)}\) is closed, whereas its image in \(\mathbb A^1_F\) is generic. Consequently the full model system is not in general an object of the ordinary pro-category of pinned geometric morphisms. This is an obstruction to that categorical formulation, and is not a counterexample to reconstruction for pinned morphisms in \(\operatorname{Pro}(\mathsf T)_{/\mathcal B}\).
notes: Working identifier B.CF2. The remaining ordinary pro-category issue is an infinite-transcendence issue. Proved.

statement: For \(\operatorname{trdeg}_{\Q}k=\infty\), ordinary relative pro-reconstruction is proved by B.62--B.66 below, culminating in B.66. The shorter argument of B.43 alone does not prove it: a representative may have the form \(X_{E,\mathrm{et}}\to Y_{F,\mathrm{et}}\) with \(E/F\) transcendental. Pinnedness of the map on limits does not, by the argument of B.43, give pinnedness of a finite-stage representative. The coherent same-field result AS-FF.13 supplies neither that finite-stage assertion nor an equivalence with this ordinary pro-category. The new proof resolves the obstacle by deriving coherence from compactness, comparing whole Kummer systems after one finitely generated refinement, and reconstructing every étale slice over a fixed source field. It does not assert that those finite-stage transition morphisms preserve closed points.

statement: There exists \(u\in t\Q[[t]]\), transcendental over \(\Q(t)\), with the following property. Let \(\Omega\) be any complete rank-one valued extension of \(\Q((t))\), with the valuation trivial on \(\Q\), and let \(h\in\Omega\) satisfy \(v(h)=v(t)=1\). If both \(h\) and \(u(h)\) are algebraic over \(\Q(t,u(t))\), and \(h,u(h)\) are algebraically independent over \(\Q\), then \[ h=t. \tag{B.CF.3} \] The series \(u\) can be specified by a recursive sequence of rational finite jets; the proof gives a finite elimination certificate at every stage. The property holds simultaneously in all finite ramified extensions and their completions.

statement: Choose a series \(u\) as in B.46, and let \[ K=\Q(t,u(t))^h\subset\Q((t)) \tag{B.CF.7} \] be the henselization for the induced \(t\)-adic valuation. Then \(K\) is countable, has transcendence degree two over \(\Q\), value group \(\Z\), residue field \(\Q\), and completion \(\Q((t))\). For every finite extension \(E/K\), in a fixed algebraic closure \(\overline K\), one has \[ C_{\operatorname{Aut}(\overline K)}(G_E)=1. \tag{B.CF.8} \] Thus the centralizer hypothesis of B7 is attained among the residue-characteristic-zero fields with positive transcendence defect specified by B8.

statement: Let \(R\) be a henselian discrete valuation ring of residue characteristic zero, with fraction field \(K\), uniformizer \(t\), and the unique extension \(v\) of its valuation to \(\overline K\). Put \(\lambda=1+t\), and define \[ F(a)= \begin{cases} \lambda a,&v(a)>0,\\ a,&v(a)\leq0, \end{cases} \qquad F(0)=0, \qquad F(\infty)=\infty. \tag{B.CF.12} \] For every finite \(G_K\)-stable set \(S\subset\mathbb P^1(\overline K)\) containing \(0,1,\infty\), the stable marked genus-zero models for \(S\) and \(F(S)\), over a finite Galois extension splitting their marks, have isomorphic logarithmic special fibres over the same standard log point. These isomorphisms preserve the labels and are compatible with forgetting marks, finite extensions of the field of definition, and the Galois descent data. At a mark \(a\), the induced comparison of the arithmetic cusp group preserves its inertia and induces the identity on its quotient \(G_{K(a)}\), with \(K(F(a))=K(a)\) as actual subfields of \(\overline K\).

statement: Let \[ u_*(t)=\sum_{n\geq1}t^{n!},\qquad K_* =\Q(t,u_*(t))^h\subset\Q((t)). \tag{B.CF.19} \] This field has transcendence degree two, residue field \(\Q\), value group \(\Z\), and positive transcendence defect one. It does not satisfy closed-point-preserving étale reconstruction. This settles the particular residue-characteristic-zero case left undecided in AS-FF.18, without claiming that its centralizers have the property proved for the different series in B.46.

statement: The classification demanded by B8 remains open for general finite-transcendence-degree fields over $\mathbb Q$ with a henselian mixed-characteristic valuation outside the following proved positive and negative classes. All positive assertions below concern full closed-point-preserving relative etale reconstruction of finite-type schemes, with the structural isomorphism retained and universal homeomorphisms inverted. They include every finite extension of the stated field. For every prime $p$, let $K_p=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb Z_{(p)}^{sh})$ and $I=G_{K_p}$. The fields \[ B_p=\overline{\mathbb Q}^{I''},\qquad K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}= \overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,\bigcap_{c\ge1}\gamma_{c+1}(I)} \] are positive by B.136 and B.138, respectively, including $p=2,3$. Every fixed bounded-nilpotency field is also covered by B.123. More generally, let $D\subset\overline{\mathbb Q}_p$ be finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, let $M$ be its finite local completion, and let $\Omega$ be its algebraic closure inside $\overline{\mathbb Q}_p$. B.139--B.140 prove the corresponding finite-derived and lower-central-union assertions in every finite transcendence degree. B.142--B.143 prove positivity for $\Omega^N$ for every nontrivial closed normal subgroup $N\triangleleft G_M$, and for every algebraic subfield over which such a positive field is algebraic. A nontrivial normal core of the field's absolute Galois subgroup in some open local Galois group is consequently a sufficient criterion, with the relative local base chosen as in B.139. No normal closure is substituted for that core. There is a further positive class with no finite-residue restriction. Let $D/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated with a discrete mixed-characteristic valuation whose residue field is finitely generated over $\mathbb F_p$. Let $M$ be its completion, let $\Omega$ be the algebraic closure of $D$ in $\overline M$, and let $I=I_M\subset G_D$. B.146--B.147 prove positivity for \[ \Omega^{I^{(r)}}\quad(r\ge0),\qquad \Omega^{\,\bigcap_{c\ge1}\gamma_{c+1}(I)}, \] and algebraic descent as above. The Gauss valuations on $\mathbb Q(t_1,\ldots,t_s)$ give strictly additional families with residue transcendence degree $s$ for every $s>0$. The all-proper-normal-subgroup conclusion of B.143 is not asserted for these more general complete bases. On the negative side, B.144 proves that positivity requires a slim absolute Galois group: every open subgroup must have trivial centre. It gives explicit henselian fields of every finite transcendence degree, and all their finite extensions, whose absolute Galois groups are wild procyclic $\mathbb Z_p$ groups. Their cores in every open finite-local Galois group are trivial. Reconstruction is also false for every field in the stated finite-transcendence-degree setting admitting a nontrivial henselian valuation of residue characteristic zero, by B.49 and B.54--B.55. This includes a mixed-characteristic valuation with such a henselian coarsening. An algebraically closed field is negative by B.53; in particular the union of all finite derived fields in the finite-local setting is distinguished from the positive lower-central union. Thus the remaining finite-local-subfield cases are slim and have trivial normal core in every open local group, apart from any further positive cases already covered by the stated criteria. Outside that setting, other algebraic Galois subgroups, residue-field configurations and nondiscrete valuations remain in the quantifier. Neither unbounded wild ramification nor a non-torsion Kummer kernel alone decides it.

statement: Fix an embedding of the strict henselization \(A=\Z_{(p)}^{sh}\) in \(\overline\Q\), put \(K_p=\operatorname{Frac}(A)\), and write \(I=G_{K_p}\). Let \(I^{(0)}=I\) and \(I^{(d+1)}=\overline{[I^{(d)},I^{(d)}]}\) be the closed derived series. Then \[ K_p^{\mathrm{sol}} :=\bigcup_{d\geq 0}\overline\Q^{\,I^{(d)}} =\overline\Q. \tag{B.CF.20} \] Consequently this maximal solvable closure does not satisfy closed-point-preserving \(\acute etale\) reconstruction. The statement concerns the actual field in AS-FF.39, not a substitution of a completed local field. The bounded derived-length field $B_p$ and the lower-central union are different fields; B.136 and B.138 respectively prove their reconstruction below.

statement: Let $R$ be a henselian rank-one valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field $\kappa$ of characteristic zero. Let $S\subset\mathbb P^1(K)$ be a finite set containing $0,1,\infty$, and let $\mathscr X/R$ be its stable marked genus-zero model. Endow $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the canonical valuative log structure $R\setminus\{0\}\to R$, and $\mathscr X$ with the log structure of its vertical boundary and its marked sections. Write $\mathscr X_s$ for its log closed fibre and $U=\mathbb P^1_K\setminus S$. Then restriction gives equivalences \[ \operatorname{FEt}(U) \ \longleftarrow\ \operatorname{KCov}(\mathscr X) \ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{KCov}(\mathscr X_s). \tag{B.LIT.1} \] Here $\operatorname{KCov}$ denotes all finite Kummer \'etale coverings in the saturated, not necessarily fs, sense of Achinger--H\"ubner--Lara--Stix. In that definition the underlying scheme map is integral and need not be finite. The equivalences are over the entire $BG_K$, and are compatible with finite valued extensions and with morphisms between stable models obtained by forgetting marks. Neither discreteness nor completeness is assumed.

statement: For a finite extension \(E/B_p\), let \(\kappa_E\) be the rational \(p\)-primary Kummer map. Put \[ W_p=\{a\in B_p^\times:a^m\in F_p^\times \text{ for some }m\geq1\}. \] Then \[ \ker\kappa_E=\bigcap_{n\geq1}(E^\times)^{p^n}=W_p, \qquad W_p\cap(1-W_p)=F_p\setminus\{0,1\}. \tag{B.MIX.2} \] In particular the supported scaling used in B.48--B.49 cannot be the point function of a pinned relative autoequivalence over \(B_p\). Precisely, for \(\lambda=1+p\), the bijection \[ f(a)=\begin{cases}\lambda a,&v(a)>0,\\a,&v(a)\leq0, \end{cases}\qquad f(0)=0 \tag{B.MIX.3} \] of \(\overline\Q\) is excluded by two one-puncture \(p\)-Kummer comparisons. This is an obstruction to this proposed counterexample, and not a proof of reconstruction over \(B_p\).

statement: Let \[ N=\bigcap_{c\geq1}\gamma_{c+1}(I),\qquad K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}=\overline\Q^N =\bigcup_{c\geq1}\overline\Q^{\gamma_{c+1}(I)}. \tag{B.MIX.4} \] For every \(p\geq5\) and every finite extension \(E/K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\), \[ \ker\!\left(E^\times\longrightarrow H^1(G_E,\Q_p(1))\right) =\bigcap_{n\geq1}(E^\times)^{p^n} =\mu_\infty. \tag{B.MIX.5} \] For \(p=2\) and \(p=3\), the corresponding kernel is already strictly larger than \(\mu_\infty\) over \(K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\) itself. Explicit nontorsion elements in it are \[ 2\quad(p=2),\qquad \frac{2+\sqrt{-3}}{2-\sqrt{-3}}\quad(p=3). \tag{B.MIX.6} \] These conclusions decide this exact Kummer input to AS-FF.39 at its unbounded union. B.138 below proves reconstruction at that union and every finite extension for every prime, including $2,3$; the kernel assertions here are retained unchanged.

statement: Let \(p\geq5\), \(K=K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\), and let \(E/K\) be finite. If \(b\in E^\times\) and \(\alpha\in\Q_p\) satisfy \[ \kappa_E(b)=\alpha\kappa_E(p), \tag{B.MIX.11} \] then \(\alpha\in\Q\).

statement: Let \(p\geq5\), and let \(E\) be any finite extension of \(K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\). Every pinned autoequivalence of \(\mathbb A^1_{E,\mathrm{et}}\) over \(BG_E\), with its relative structural isomorphism retained, has actual geometric point function \[ a\longmapsto ua+v, \qquad u\in E^\times,\ v\in E. \tag{B.MIX.12} \] The coefficients are unique. This conclusion concerns the actual point function; it does not identify the remaining pointwise-trivial automorphism kernel on the full étale site, or assert existence for arbitrary noninvertible pinned maps.

statement: Let \(p\geq5\), let \(E/K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\) be finite, and let \(U\) be a smooth geometrically connected curve over \(E\), with smooth proper compactification \(\overline U\). Suppose \(\xi\in H^1(U,\Z_p(1))\) evaluates at every point \(x\in U(L)\), for every finite extension \(L/E\), to the Kummer class of an actual element of \(L^\times\). Every geometric boundary residue of \(\xi\) belongs to \(\Q\cap\Z_p\).

statement: Let \(p\geq5\), and let \(E\) be any finite extension of \(K_{p,\mathrm{nil}}\). Every pinned geometric morphism \[ \mathbb A^1_{E,\mathrm{et}} \longrightarrow\mathbb A^1_{E,\mathrm{et}} \] over \(BG_E\) has actual geometric point function \(x\mapsto P(x)\) for a unique polynomial \(P\in E[T]\). Invertibility of the geometric morphism is not assumed. This does not identify the whole inverse-image functor with the functor induced by \(P\), and does not prove existence for an arbitrary source scheme.

statement: Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, let \(X,Y\) be finite-type \(k\)-schemes, and let \(\alpha:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) be an ordinary pro-morphism over \(\mathcal B\). There is a geometric morphism \[ \alpha_k:X_{\mathrm{et}}\longrightarrow Y_{\mathrm{et}} \tag{B.PRO.1} \] over \(BG_k\), compatible with the finite-level representatives of \(\alpha\). Its underlying-space map is the map on inverse limits defined by \(\alpha\), so it is pinned if \(\alpha\) is pinned. Moreover finite constant base change, precomposition by a scheme morphism, restriction to open subobjects, and slicing by a quasi-compact separated étale object preserve the class of maps obtained from ordinary pro-morphisms. For a slice defined at a particular target level, the source model can be taken to be its pullback by that level's chosen representative.

statement: For every characteristic-zero \(k\), pinned ordinary pro-morphisms \(\mathcal B\to\mathcal Y\) over \(\mathcal B\) are precisely the \(k\)-rational points of \(Y\). This statement is compatible with finite extensions of \(k\). In particular, suppose a fixed representative of a pinned pro-morphism pulls the universal Kummer class back to \(\xi\in H^1(X_E,\widehat\Z(1))\). If \(x\in X_E(L)\), with \(L/E\) finite, and \(b\) is the value of its induced pro-point in \(\mathbb G_m\), then there is \emph{one} finitely generated field \(M\) containing \(L\) and \(b\) for which \[ \operatorname{res}_{M/L}(x^*\xi)=\kappa_M(b) \quad\hbox{in }\widehat{M^\times}. \tag{B.PRO.2} \] The field \(M\) works simultaneously for all Kummer levels.

statement: Let \(\alpha\) be a pinned ordinary pro-morphism and choose a relative representative \[ a:X_{E,\mathrm{et}}\longrightarrow Y_{F,\mathrm{et}} \tag{B.PRO.5} \] over \(BG_F\), with \(F\subset E\subset k\) finitely generated. statement: For every prime $p$ and every proper smooth connected curve $C/\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ of genus at least two, there exists a connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover $D\to C$ whose geometric Galois closure has order prime to $p$, and a nonconstant morphism $D\to H$ to a positive-genus supersingular curve $H$. This assertion remains undecided here for arbitrary $C$.

statement: Let $K$ be any field, let $X/K$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve, and let $\mathfrak m$ be an effective divisor on $X$. Put $U=X-\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak m)$ and assume $b\in U(K)$. Let $J_{\mathfrak m}$ be the generalized Jacobian, with $J_0=J_X$, and let $j_b:U\to J_{\mathfrak m}$ send $x$ to the modulus class $[x-b]$. For every positive integer $n$ invertible in $K$, the sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow J_{\mathfrak m}[n]\longrightarrow J_{\mathfrak m}\xrightarrow{[n]}J_{\mathfrak m}\longrightarrow0 \] is exact as a sequence of fppf sheaves, and $[n]$ is finite \emph{\'etale}. The Abel map induces a $G_K$-equivariant isomorphism of finite abelian groups \[ \pi_1(U_{\overline K},\bar b)^{\mathrm{ab}}/n \ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ J_{\mathfrak m}[n](\overline K). \] For every $x\in U(K)$ the abelianized section-difference class is \[ [s_x-s_b]_n=\delta_n(j_b(x))\quad\hbox{in}\quad H^1(G_K,J_{\mathfrak m}[n](\overline K)). \tag{N1.1} \] Thus the sign is positive for $x-b$ and the stated difference convention. Changing the geometric path changes the cocycle by a coboundary; conjugacy throughout is conjugacy by the geometric kernel. Reversing the section difference gives $-\delta_n(j_b(x))$.
notes: Generalized-Jacobian Kummer compatibility with positive sign; characteristic-prime exclusions and modulus conventions stated explicitly.

statement: Let \[ C/\mathbf F _5:\quad W^4=X^3Z-XZ^3, \qquad P=(1:0:0),\qquad K=\mathbf F _{5^8}. \] Every nonzero geometric order-three character first becomes constant over $K$. There are $364$ connected constant cyclic degree-three $P$-split covers of $C_K$, up to inversion of the deck character. Exactly $96$ are class-number witnesses; the other $268$ fail the test over $K$ and every further constant extension. The successful ones remain witnesses over $\mathbf F _{5^{8n}}$ exactly when $3\nmid n$. Consequently the least admissible odd prime giving a witness for this pointed quartic over some extension is three, and the least field for an order-three witness is $\mathbf F _{5^8}$. More explicitly, the three elliptic quotients identify $J_C[3]$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_5$ with $E_0[3]\oplus E_1[3]\oplus E_2[3]$. A cover represented by $(T_0,T_1,T_2)$ is successful precisely when exactly two entries are nonzero. On its new coherent cohomology, the characteristic polynomial of the $K$-linear Cartier iterate is \[ \begin{cases} (T^2+T+1)^2,&\text{exactly two nonzero entries},\\ (T-1)^4,&\text{one or three nonzero entries}. \end{cases} \tag{B.80.1} \] The different optimization in B.34, minimizing the extension degree first among all primes, has degree three and least prime thirteen there. It is not the prime-first minimum asserted here.

statement: There are exactly $3001$ pointed smooth plane-quartic isomorphism classes over $\mathbf F _3$, and exactly $94283$ over $\mathbf F _5$. Here a point is part of the object and is rational over the stated base field; isomorphisms preserve it. Complete equations, point counts over the first three extensions, and Weil polynomials are retained for every class. For each such pointed curve let $m_\ell$ be the least positive integer $m$ for which a nonzero character $J_C(\mathbf F _{q^m})\twoheadrightarrow\mathbf Z/\ell$ exists. For the smallest admissible odd prime, namely $\ell=5$ when $q=3$ and $\ell=3$ when $q=5$, the exact distributions are \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrrrr} q=3:\ m_5&1&2&3&6&8&24\\ \hline \text{classes}&650&515&49&86&327&350\\[2pt] m_5&31&56&62&72&168&504\\ \hline \text{classes}&255&47&261&79&73&309 \end{array} \] and \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrrr} q=5:\ m_3&1&4&8&13&56\\ \hline \text{classes}&41623&5163&19699&14400&13398. \end{array} \] These are first fields of existence of a nonzero constant character, not first fields of a class-number witness.
notes: No A1 use. The new characteristic-polynomial tables do not test rational p-torsion on covering Jacobians. Quartics without a base-field point are outside this census.

statement: Let $H/\overline{\mathbf F}_2$ be a smooth proper connected curve with a cyclic degree-seven map to the projective line. Suppose its branch locus is contained in $\mathbf P^1(\mathbf F _8)$ and has at most seven points. Then $J_H$ has no positive-dimensional supersingular isogeny factor, even geometrically. Consequently $H$ has no nonconstant map to a supersingular curve of positive genus. For the normalized branch patterns with four through seven branch points, the exhaustive counts are respectively $620,2775,6666,6665$, and every one fails the supersingular-factor test. This settles precisely the finite search family, not B5.
check_types: new completeness proof and extended supp:2; independent finite certificate verificat:2
notes: No A1 use. This closes the specified finite family only; it does not prove or refute universal B5. Eight or nine rational branch points and larger branch fields remain outside the result.

statement: Let $H/\overline{\mathbf F}_2$ be smooth, proper and connected, with a cyclic degree-seven map to $\mathbf P^1$. If, after a projective change of coordinate, its branch locus is contained in $\mathbf P^1(\mathbf F _8)$, then $J_H$ has no positive-dimensional geometric supersingular isogeny factor. In particular $H$ has no nonconstant map to a positive-genus supersingular curve. For eight and nine branch points there are respectively $745$ and $511$ branch-exponent orbits under $\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbf F _8)$ and changes of cyclic generator. Their character polynomials all fail the complete supersingular-factor test. Together with B.82, these exhaust every possible rational branch pattern over $\mathbf F _8$.
check_types: new complete finite-family proof and exa:2; independent orbit and arithmetic verifie:2; targeted proof check:1
notes: Closes the entire F8-rational branch family. Larger branch fields and arbitrary prime-to-two correspondences remain open; no universal B5 conclusion is inferred. Direct computation agrees with, and replaces reliance on, the initial functional-equation reconstruction.

statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, and let $H/k$ be a smooth proper connected curve with a cyclic degree-seven map $H\to\mathbf P^1_k$ having at most four branch points. Then the Newton polygon of $J_H$ has no slope $1/2$. In particular $J_H$ has no positive-dimensional supersingular isogeny factor, and $H$ has no nonconstant map to a positive-genus supersingular curve. In the four-branch case, the only inertia multisets whose signatures could permit a supersingular Jacobian are opposite pairs $\{u,-u,v,-v\}$ in $(\mathbf Z/7)^\times$. Every such curve is ordinary. More explicitly, after normalization it has equation \[ y^7=x(x-1)^a(x-\lambda)^{7-a},\qquad a\in\{1,\ldots,6\},\quad \lambda\in k\setminus\{0,1\}, \tag{B.84.1} \] and the Cartier operator on its six regular differentials is bijective for every allowed $\lambda$.
check_types: targeted proof check:1; new universal proof:1; symbolic certificate:1; primary-source hypothesis check:1; new universal proof; symbolic certificat:1
notes: Uniform exclusion of the entire cyclic-seven four-branch construction. Does not settle B5 for arbitrary odd etale covers or correspondences. No A1 dependency.

statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic two, and let $C$ be the smooth proper model of \[ z^2+z=a x+\frac b x+\frac c{x+1},\qquad abc\ne0. \tag{B.85.1} \] This is an ordinary genus-two curve. It has a connected cyclic \'etale cover of degree three with primitive two-rank zero if and only if \[ (a+b+c)^3=abc. \tag{B.85.2} \] When (B.85.2) holds and $a,b,c$ are not all equal, exactly one of the forty geometric cyclic-three covers has primitive two-rank zero. When $a=b=c$, exactly two do. Every other cyclic-three cover has ordinary primitive part. Thus every curve in (B.85.2) satisfies B4 and B5, with an actual map from its cubic cover to a supersingular elliptic curve. Here are explicit defining functions. Choose $r\notin\{0,1\}$ and $\sigma$ with \[ b=a r^3,\qquad c=a(r+1)^3,\qquad \sigma^2+\sigma=a(r+1),\qquad h=x(x+1). \] Then the normalization of \[ w^3=\frac{b(z+\sigma)}h \tag{B.85.3} \] is one of the required covers. If the displayed coefficients and $\mu_3$ belong to a finite field $L$, each of the three points $W_0,W_1,W_\infty$ above $0,1,\infty$ splits over $L$. Its relative class number is odd over $L$ and every finite extension of $L$. In particular, for the S2 curve $y^2+x(x+1)y=x^5+1$, set \[ z=\frac{y+x+1}{x(x+1)},\qquad L=\mathbf F _2(\sigma),\quad \sigma^4+\sigma+1=0, \qquad r=\sigma^2+\sigma+1. \] The cubic cover (B.85.3), with $a=b=c=1$, is defined over $L=\mathbf F _{16}$, is split at both $P=(0,1)$ and $Q=(1,0)$, and has genus four. Its primitive zeta numerator is $(1-4T)^4$, so its exact relative class number is $81$. An explicit nonconstant map to the supersingular elliptic curve $E:Y^2+Y=T^3$ is \[ U=w+\frac{x+r}{x(x+1)w},\qquad T=\frac1{U+1},\qquad Y=\frac{xU^2+r}{(U+1)^2}. \tag{B.85.4} \] All these statements concern the smooth normalizations; the affine Kummer equation alone has singularities at its zero and poles.
check_types: new uniform proof and symbolic certifica:2; independent finite-field verification:2; complete second proof reading:2; targeted proof check:1
notes: Uniform positive locus and complete cubic classification only; universal B4/B5 remain unresolved. Nakajima1983 §6 identified as prior work but primary text not accessible, so no read or novelty claim.

statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic two and let $C$ be the smooth proper model of \[ z^2+z=x^3+a x+b/x,\qquad b\ne0. \tag{B.86.1} \] It has genus two and two-rank one. Every connected cyclic \'etale cubic cover of $C$ has ordinary primitive part. A connected cyclic \'etale quintic cover with primitive two-rank zero exists if and only if \[ b a^{16}=1. \tag{B.86.2} \] If (B.86.2) holds, there is exactly one such geometric cyclic-five cover; every other cyclic-five cover has ordinary primitive part. In particular the entire locus (B.86.2) satisfies B4 and B5. For an explicit cover, put $u=1/x$, $v=z u^2$, $r=a^4$, choose $d$ with $d^2+d=b a^4$, and use \[ v^2+u^2v=b u^5+a u^3+u,\qquad w^5=v+d u^2+a u+a^2. \tag{B.86.3} \] Its smooth normalization has genus six and a reflection quotient of genus two with supersingular Jacobian. For $a=b=1$, take $d=\rho$ with $\rho^2+\rho+1=0$. There is the following explicit map to a supersingular genus-two curve: \[ H:Y^2+Y=T^5+T^3+T+1,\qquad U=w+\frac{u+1}{w},\quad T=\frac1U,\quad Y=\frac{(U+1)u}{U^3}+\frac1{U^2}. \tag{B.86.4} \] Over $\mathbf F _{16}$ the quintic deck group is constant, both ramified points of $C\to\mathbf P^1$ split, and the exact relative class number is $194481=441^2$, an odd integer.
check_types: new uniform proof and symbolic certifica:2; independent finite-field verification:2; complete second proof reading:2; targeted proof check:1
notes: Uniform positive locus; classification only for cyclic degrees three and five. No extension to all odd degrees or all genus-two curves.

statement: For every finite set $\mathcal N$ of odd integers greater than one, there is an ordinary smooth proper genus-two curve $C/\overline{\mathbf F}_2$ such that every connected cyclic \'etale cover of $C$ of degree in $\mathcal N$ is ordinary. More precisely, if $M$ is any odd common multiple of $\mathcal N$, one can choose $C$ so that its maximal abelian \'etale cover of exponent dividing $M$, of degree $M^4$, is ordinary. All its intermediate covers are then ordinary. Consequently no bound depending only on $g=2,p=2$ for the degree of a B4 witness can hold for all ordinary curves, if every such curve has a witness at all. Degree one does not evade this conclusion, since $J_C$ has two-rank two. This is a finite-degree avoidance result, not a curve avoiding every odd degree, a counterexample to B4, or a resolution of any universal B4 or B5 gate.
check_types: new proof and exact primary-source check:2; complete second proof reading:2; targeted proof check:1
notes: Finite-degree avoidance only, not an all-prime counterexample or a strict reduction of the unresolved universal gate. The curve depends on the finite set.

statement: Let $C/\mathbf F_2$ and $P,Q$ be the curve and points of S2. Over $L=\mathbf F_{16}$, there is a specified connected finite \'etale cover $E\to C_L$ of degree $3^7=2187$ with an $L$-rational point over $P$ and no $L$-rational point over $Q$. Its geometric Galois closure is a $3$-group; indeed $E_{\bar L} \to C_{\bar L}$ is already Galois of degree $3^7$. Consequently the sections of $P$ and $Q$ are distinct in the geometrically pro-$3$ arithmetic quotient, over both $L$ and $\mathbf F_2$, and in every geometrically pro-$\Sigma$ quotient with $3\in\Sigma$. This does not assert separation of all points for the singleton prime set $\{3\}$. For the cover's complete definition, take the cubic cover $\pi:D\to C_L$ of B.85, choose any $P'\in D(L)$ above $P$, and put \[ J=J_D,\qquad A=J(L),\qquad H=A[2^\infty]. \] Factor the Lang isogeny as \[ F_{16}-1:J\longrightarrow J/H \mathop{\longrightarrow}^{\lambda}J. \] Then \[ E=D\times_{J,\,[R\mapsto R-P']} (J/H) \tag{B.88.1} \] with point $(P',0+H)$ is the required cover. Thus its definition uses an explicit smooth curve, a specified finite group scheme of rational translations and a specified isogeny; equations for a genus-$2188$ plane model are not required.

notes: This one pair separates already at prime3; no universal singleton separation assertion. The full E/C deck group is asserted geometrically and need not be constant over F16.

statement: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $g\ge2$, and a finite set $\mathcal S$ of odd primes different from $p$. There exist a finite field $k$ of characteristic $p$, an ordinary smooth proper geometrically connected genus-$g$ curve $C/k$, and $P\in C(k)$ such that, for every finite extension $L/k$, every $\ell\in\mathcal S$, and every nontrivial character $\chi:J_C(L)\to\mathbf Z/\ell$, one has \[ p^{(\ell-1)(g-1)} \ \bigm|\ \prod_{i=1}^{\ell-1} L_P(\chi^i,1). \tag{B.89.1} \] Thus none of those primes is a B1 witness over any constant extension. In particular no successful witness prime can be bounded in terms of $(p,g)$ alone, even within $p>(2g-2)^2$, if unrestricted B1 is true. This statement does not refute unrestricted B1, and does not decide its large-characteristic cases: the curve and field in the construction depend on the prescribed finite set of primes.

statement: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic zero and $X/k$ a hyperbolic curve. For the full geometric profinite group, the kernel of $G_k\to\operatorname{Out}(\pi_1(X_{\overline k}))$ is contained in the kernel of restriction $G_k\to G_{\mathbb Q}$, up to the usual choice of an embedding of $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ in $\overline k$. If $k$ is a number field, the outer action, and hence every nonempty marked-groupoid action, is faithful.
notes: Known opened theorem; not represented as a new proof of HM.

statement: Let $R$ be a henselian DVR of residue characteristic zero, with fraction field $F$. Let $\overline{\mathcal X}/R$ be a smooth proper curve and $\mathcal D\subset\overline{\mathcal X}$ a relative finite \'etale divisor. Put $\mathcal X=\overline{\mathcal X}\setminus\mathcal D$. Suppose every point of a finite set $I\subset\mathcal X_F(F)$ extends to an $R$-section of $\mathcal X$. Then the inertia subgroup $I_R$ of $G_F$ acts trivially on the full profinite groupoid $\widehat\Pi_1(\mathcal X_{\overline F},I)$.
notes: Actual fibre-functor groupoid, finite extending marks; not merely outer action.

statement: Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, with $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb Q}K>0$, and let $X/K$ be a smooth hyperbolic curve. For every nonempty finite set $I\subset X(K)$, the actual action of $G_K$ on $\widehat\Pi_1(X_{\overline K},I)$ is not faithful. In fact its kernel contains a subgroup isomorphic to $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)$.
notes: Spreading of finite marking; good codimension-one point; nonzero tame inertia.

statement: The uniqueness expectation of cote~142, scan~096 is false for finite markings, even when the field of definition is finite over the field of moduli. A counterexample is \[ K=\mathbb Q(t),\qquad X=\mathbb P^1_K\setminus\{0,1,t,\infty\},\qquad I=\{2\}. \] The inertia at $t=3$ is a nontrivial subgroup of the kernel of the actual marked action. The assertion becomes true for number fields, and for finite markings positive transcendence degree always prevents it, as specified in Claims~B.90 and B.92.
notes: Explicit Q(t), four punctures, marking 2, valuation t=3; moduli degree six; certificate attached.

statement: Let a marked curve as above spread to a smooth relative pair over a smooth integral characteristic-zero scheme $S$, with function field $K$. Let $N_S$ be the closed normal subgroup of $G_K$ generated by the inertia groups at all codimension-one points of $S$. Then \[ G_K/N_S\simeq\pi_1(S),\qquad \ker(\rho_I)/N_S=\ker(\rho_{S,I}), \] where $\rho_{S,I}:\pi_1(S)\to\operatorname{Aut} (\widehat\Pi_1(X_{\overline K},I))$ is the actual family monodromy. Thus uniqueness modulo $N_S$ is precisely injectivity of this family monodromy; it is not a consequence of the moduli-field condition alone.
notes: Galois quotient by good-divisor inertia equals pi1(S); no universal faithfulness asserted.

statement: For the curve and marking of Claim~B.93, put $S=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1,2,\infty\}$. Its actual family monodromy \[ \pi_1(S)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Aut}\bigl(\pi_1(X_{\overline{\mathbb Q(t)}},2)\bigr) \] is injective. Consequently the kernel of the $G_{\mathbb Q(t)}$-action is exactly $N_S$ in Claim~B.94.
notes: Configuration-space fibre exactness proved; two distinct cusp centralizers force geometric injectivity.

statement: For a constant hyperbolic curve $X_0/\mathbb Q$ with constant nonempty finite marking $I_0$, its base change to $K=\mathbb Q(t)$ has marked action factoring through $G_K\to G_{\mathbb Q}$; its kernel is exactly the kernel of that restriction. This explains the isotrivial obstruction, but Claims~B.92--B.93 show that eliminating isotriviality does not eliminate good-reduction inertia. The additional relations of Nakamura--Schneps (2000), Theorem~1.1 and Definition~1.1, define $\mathrm I\Gamma\subset\widehat{GT}$; Theorem~1.2 makes it a subgroup containing the Galois image. None of these statements identifies it with all of $\widehat{GT}$. Likewise Hoshi--Mochizuki--Tsujimura (2025), Definition~3.3(ii),(iii),(v), imposes the COF and RGC properties on closed subgroups before denoting them by $\mathrm{BGT}$. These are hypotheses on the selected subgroups, not assertions about every element of the ambient group.
notes: Constant example and precise distinction between Galois image, conditioned subgroup, and ambient GT.

statement: There are canonical Kummer identifications \[ I_v=\operatorname{Hom}((\Gamma\otimes\mathbb Q)/\Gamma,\mu_\infty) =\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma,T). \] The topology is the inverse-limit topology of finite Kummer quotients. Furthermore \[ 1\longrightarrow I_v\longrightarrow D_v\longrightarrow G_{\kappa(v)}\longrightarrow1 \] splits, noncanonically. Conjugation on inertia is the cyclotomic action. If $r_\ell=\dim_{\mathbb F_\ell}\Gamma/\ell\Gamma$, then \[ I_v\simeq\prod_\ell\mathbb Z_\ell(1)^{r_\ell},\qquad r_\ell\leq\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\Gamma\otimes\mathbb Q) \leq\operatorname{trdeg}_K L-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(v). \] For $\gamma\in\Gamma$, evaluation $\chi\mapsto\chi(\gamma)$ is identically zero exactly when $\gamma\in\Gamma_{\rm div}$. In particular $I_v=1$ exactly when $\Gamma$ is divisible. These statements re-prove FLAGGED\_149 D4 in the characteristic-zero setting at issue here.
notes: Arbitrary-rank tame inertia and divisible-value criterion; D4 re-proved.

statement: Suppose $I_v\ne1$. Let $w=v/\Delta$ be the coarsening defined by the largest divisible convex subgroup of $\Gamma$. Then \[ I_w=I_v,\qquad N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_w. \] Writing $P_{L/K}=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline L/L\overline K)$ gives \[ N_{P_{L/K}}(I_v)=D_w\cap P_{L/K},\qquad 1\to I_v\to D_w\cap P_{L/K}\to G_{\kappa(w)\overline K}\to1. \] Moreover $D_w=D_v$ exactly when the residual valuation $v/w$ on $\kappa(w)$ is henselian. In particular $N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_v$ for every rank-one valuation with nontrivial inertia. If $I_v=1$, its normalizer is all of $G_L$.
notes: D5 re-proved with largest divisible convex coarsening; D6 omissions corrected.

statement: FLAGGED\_149 D3 is valid: $K(x,y)$ has valuations with residue $K$ and value group $\mathbb Q$, or $\mathbb Z[1/2]$, centred at $(0,2)$ on $(\mathbb P^1)^2$. Consequently the centre converse for arbitrary valuations is false on $(\mathbb P^1-\{0,1,\infty\})^2$. More strongly, on $U=(\mathbb P^1-\{0,1,\infty\})^3$ there is a rank-one valuation of $K(U)$ with $I_v\simeq T\ne1$, whose image in $\pi_1(U)$ is trivial, but which has no centre on $U$. For this example $\Delta=0$; the inertia-preserving coarsening of Claim~B.98 does not repair the centre criterion.
notes: D3 Hahn valuations re-proved; new nonzero inertia invisible on a product with rank-one group Q alpha + Z.

statement: Let $X/K$ be smooth proper and $D=X\setminus U$ a simple normal crossings divisor. At a geometric centre $\bar x$ of $v$, write $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ for the branch parameters and $\gamma_i=v(z_i)$. The local geometric group is $T^r$ and the inertia homomorphism is \[ \rho_v:\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma,T)\longrightarrow T^r, \qquad\chi\longmapsto(\chi(\gamma_1),\ldots,\chi(\gamma_r)). \] Its dual is \[ \psi_v:(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)^r\longrightarrow (\Gamma\otimes\mathbb Q)/\Gamma, \qquad(q_i)\longmapsto\sum q_i\gamma_i\bmod\Gamma. \] Its image is the annihilator of $\ker\psi_v$. It is open exactly when that kernel is finite, and surjective exactly when that kernel vanishes. Openness requires rational independence of the $\gamma_i$; under independence its exact criterion is \[ [\Gamma\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}(\gamma_i): \textstyle\sum_i\mathbb Z\gamma_i]<\infty. \] Surjectivity means this index is one. This re-proves FLAGGED\_149 E3, including valuations of every rank.
notes: E3 re-proved; exact local dual image and finite-kernel openness criterion.

statement: Even for a product of two hyperbolic curves, a smooth proper simple normal crossings compactification can have a noninjective boundary homomorphism $T^r\to\pi_1(U)$. For $U=(\mathbb P^1-\{0,1,\infty\})^2$, blow up $(0,2)$ in $(\mathbb P^1)^2$. At the intersection of the exceptional divisor and the strict transform of $x=0$, the homomorphism is \[ T^2\longrightarrow T\hookrightarrow\pi_1(U),\qquad (a,b)\longmapsto a+b. \] Its kernel is the antidiagonal. This counterexample concerns good smooth SNC compactifications; it does not assert that the blow-up is a compactification adapted as a smooth relative curve at every level of the original tower.
notes: Explicit blow-up map T squared to T is sum; local-injectivity lead refuted. Finite matrix certificate supplements proof.

statement: Let $U=U_d\to\cdots\to U_0=\operatorname{Spec}K$ be a tower of smooth geometrically connected curves, each with a smooth proper relative compactification and finite \emph{\'etale} relative boundary. Suppose no factor has type $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$. If $\Gamma_{v,\rm div}=0$, then \[ I_v\longrightarrow\pi_1(U)\text{ is trivial} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v\text{ has a centre on }U. \] This holds in every dimension and for every ordered rank. In particular it proves the DVR assertion of FLAGGED\_149 D7 and extends it to all finitely generated value groups and to groups such as $\mathbb Z[1/2]$. The forward implication is false without the value-group restriction, even when $I_v\ne1$, by Claim~B.99. The reverse implication needs no type or value-group restriction.
notes: D7 re-proved; all allowed factor types; Gamma_div=0 sufficient in every rank. Arbitrary valuations compared through noetherian strict local rings, not unsupported nonnoetherian specialization.

statement: Let $U=\prod_{j=1}^d C_j$ be a product of smooth geometrically connected curves in characteristic zero, with proper smooth completions. Let $x$ be the centre of $v$ on their product, and for each coordinate that is a missing point choose its local parameter $z_j$ and write $\gamma_j=v(z_j)>0$. Then \[ I_v\to\pi_1(U)\text{ is trivial} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \gamma_j\in\Gamma_{\rm div}\quad(j\in B_{\ne\mathbb A^1}). \] Here $B_{\ne\mathbb A^1}$ is the set of boundary coordinates whose curve factor is not geometrically isomorphic to $\mathbb A^1$. Proper factors contribute no condition; affine-line factors contribute no condition. In particular projective-line and elliptic proper factors, and punctured-line factors of type $(0,2)$, are all included.
notes: Exact product criterion with all factor types; no cancellation between independent factors.

statement: For $\mathbb A^1$ a DVR at infinity has no centre and trivial geometric inertia image. The type $(0,0)$ can also cause failure in a nontrivial tower: the $\mathbb G_m$-bundle \[ U=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)^\times\longrightarrow\mathbb P^1 \] is an elementary tower of types $(0,0),(0,2)$, and its geometric fundamental group is trivial. A divisorial valuation along the zero section of $\mathcal O(-1)$ has nonzero inertia and no centre on $U$, yet has trivial global image.
notes: O(-1) minus zero section is A squared minus zero; P1 factor kills subsequent Gm meridian.

statement: Keep the SNC compactification and centre of Claim~B.100. Let $P_x$ be its punctured strictly local neighbourhood over $\overline K$, with group $T^r$. Define a subgroup $\mathcal R_x\subset(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)^r$ as follows. For every connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover $W\to U_{\overline K}$ admitting a pointed lift $P_x\to W$, for every $n>0$, and every class $\alpha\in H^1(W,\mu_n)$, include its restriction to $P_x$. The latter is the residue vector $(a_1/n,\ldots,a_r/n)$ in the indicated group. Then \[ I_v\to\pi_1(U)\text{ is trivial} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sum_i a_i\gamma_i\in n\Gamma \quad\text{for every such finite-cover residue vector}. \] This is valid for every smooth $U$, every elementary tower and every factor type, and every valuation. It uses cyclic cohomology on finite covers, rather than an unspecified kernel of $T^r\to\pi_1(U)$.

statement: For every finite extension $E/K$: \begin{enumerate} \item $\ker\kappa_E=\mu_\infty$. \item If $b\in E^\times$, $\alpha\in\mathbb Q_p$, and $\kappa_E(b)=\alpha\kappa_E(p)$, then $\alpha\in\mathbb Q$. \item For every finite extension $E'/E$, complex conjugation in the chosen complex embedding does not centralize $G_{E'}$. \end{enumerate} These assertions re-prove the inputs A1-B.57--B.58 used below; they are not deductions from a reconstruction theorem.
notes: Old B57 p>=5 and B58 re-proved; all finite extensions; odd-prime nilpotent residual infinite by direct Kummer norm proof; no centralizing complex conjugation.

statement: Let $E/K$ be finite. A class $\xi\in H^1(C,\mathbb Z_p(1))$ on a smooth curve over $E$ whose evaluation at every point over every finite extension is an actual Kummer value has rational geometric boundary residues. More generally, let $V\subset\mathbb A^n_E$ be the complement of a hypersurface, and let $\eta\in H^1(V,\mathbb Z_p(1))$ have that same actual-value property. After a finite extension splitting the irreducible geometric boundary hypersurfaces, with equations $h_1,\ldots,h_s$, there are $q_j\in\mathbb Q\cap\mathbb Z_p$ and an arithmetic class $\beta$ such that \[ \eta=\beta+\sum_jq_j\kappa(h_j) \quad\hbox{in }H^1(V,\mathbb Q_p(1)). \tag{B.NORM.2} \] If $b(t)$ is any actual value of $\eta$ at $t\in V(\overline{\mathbb Q})$, then in the fixed complex embedding \[ |b(t)|^2=C\prod_j|h_j(t)|^{2q_j},\qquad C>0,\quad C\in\overline{\mathbb Q}. \tag{B.NORM.3} \] The constant is independent of $t$; a finite extension of point definition does not change it.
notes: Old B60 re-proved; curve norm residue formula, rational residues, principal affine-space open has Picard zero, uniform positive algebraic norm constants.

statement: Let $X/E$ be smooth geometrically connected affine of dimension $n\geq1$, and let $\phi:X_{\rm et}\to\mathbb A^1_{E,\rm et}$ be a pinned geometric morphism over $E_{\rm et}$. Write $f:X(\overline{\mathbb Q})\to\overline{\mathbb Q}$ for its actual point map. Suppose it is nonconstant. For any finite generically \emph{\'etale} morphism $g:X\to\mathbb A^n_E$ of degree $d$, the polynomials \[ P_t(Z)=\prod_{x\in g^{-1}(t)}(Z-f(x)) \tag{B.NORM.4} \] on its geometric \emph{\'etale} fibres agree, on a nonempty Zariski open set of algebraic $t$, with a monic polynomial $P_g\in\overline{\mathbb Q}(t_1,\ldots,t_n)[Z]$ of degree $d$. No continuity or analyticity of $f$ is assumed.
notes: Finite-grid interpolation reconstructs coefficients without assuming point-map continuity; complexified differential identities and global continuation separate root types; arithmetic equivariance excludes anti factors.

statement: Over a number field, a nontrivial closed pro-$\ell$ subgroup of $F$ is contained in cusp inertia if and only if it is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z_\ell$ and is essentially cyclotomically normalized. Here the latter condition means that some subgroup of its arithmetic normalizer has open image in $G_k$ and acts by $\chi_\ell\circ p$. This is the opened published theorem of Nakamura as stated by Stix. In Stix's 2012 version the relevant references are Definition~26, Definition~29, Theorem~30 and Corollaries~31--32. In the supplied 2008 source, version~3.05, the corresponding numbered statements are Lemma~19, Theorem~20 and Corollaries~21--22; the definitions are unnumbered prose. The count 22--25 in the prompt is not the count produced by this source's shared theorem counter. Every original maximal pro-$\ell$ quotient, and every quotient of it, kills $R$. Moreover every cusp inertia group has trivial intersection with $R$.
