statement: Let $1\ne A\leq F$ be procyclic and let $N\leq E$ normalize $A$, with $p(N)=G_L$. For every $\ell$ with $A_\ell\ne1$ write $\theta_\ell:N\to\mathbb Z_\ell^\times$ for its conjugation character. After replacing $N$ by $AN$, put $D=N\cap F$ and $d_\ell=\ell-1$ for odd $\ell$, $d_2=1$. There is a character \[ \lambda_\ell:G_L\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_\ell^\times, \qquad \lambda_\ell\circ p=\theta_\ell^{d_\ell}. \] There are a finite extension $L_1/L$ and a finite \'etale cover $Y\to U_{L_1}$ in whose geometric homology the image of $A_\ell$ is a nonzero line, with character $\psi$, such that $\lambda_\ell|_{G_{L_1}}=\psi^{d_\ell}$. If $A$ is noncuspidal, this line maps injectively to $V_\ell\operatorname{Jac}(\overline Y)$; in particular $\psi$ has Frobenius weight one and Hodge--Tate weights in $\{0,1\}$, with cyclotomic Hodge--Tate weight one.
notes: Actual arithmetic image retained; enlarge N to AN; Sylow argument descends theta^(l-1); characteristic finite quotient detects a subgroup of R on a curve cover. Noncuspidal alternative has proper Jacobian weight one.

statement: In Claim~B.112 let $M/\mathbb Q$ be a finite Galois extension containing $L$, and let $\mathcal P_M$ be the rational primes unramified in $M$ whose Frobenius conjugacy class is that of a complex conjugation in $\operatorname{Gal}(M/\mathbb Q)$. Either $A$ is contained in a unique cusp inertia group or \[ A_\ell=1\qquad(\ell\in\mathcal P_M). \] Thus cofinite prime support forces cuspidality. If $L$ is totally real, every such $A$ is cuspidal, without a support condition.
notes: LM4 B29 re-proved, including finite-extension Hodge--Tate descent, unit lattice, complex-conjugation Frobenius primes, and totally real normalizer field.

statement: If $A$ in Claim~B.112 is noncuspidal, its actual normalizer field $L$ contains a CM subfield. For each supported $\ell$ and each finite Galois $M/\mathbb Q$ containing $L$, some CM subfield of $M$ embeds in $\mathbb Q_\ell$. In particular, if the normalizer image is the full $G_{\mathbb Q(i)}$, its support consists only of primes split in $\mathbb Q(i)$. For an arbitrary open image $G_L\subset G_{\mathbb Q(i)}$ one must use $L$ in this statement. The character argument alone does not exclude primes inert in $\mathbb Q(i)$. For example $L=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt{-2})$ admits a $\mathbb Q_3$-valued geometric character of Frobenius weight one although $3$ is inert in $\mathbb Q(i)$.
notes: LM6 A53 field-theoretic CM obstruction re-proved; normalizer field L cannot be replaced by Q(i). Explicit CM elliptic curve over Q(sqrt(-2)) has Q3 lines over Q(i,sqrt(-2)), though 3 is inert in Q(i). Only the proposed character inference is refuted; no normalizer subgroup constructed.

statement: Let $U=E_0\setminus\{O\}$ for $E_0:y^2=x^3-x$ over $\mathbb Q(i)$, and let $1\ne C\leq R$ be procyclic with open arithmetic normalizer image. Every weight-one detector of $C$ on a finite cover lies in the Prym kernel of its compactified Jacobian map to $E_0$, and such a detector has compactification genus at least two.

statement: The CM curve $E_0/\mathbb Q(i)$ has the based real descent \[ E':y^2=x^3+4x,\qquad b=(0,0),\qquad (x,y)\longmapsto(u^2x,u^3y),\quad u=(1+i)/2. \] For $U'=E'\setminus\{O\}$ and its rational-point action, complex conjugation $c\in G_{\mathbb Q}$ satisfies \[ F\rtimes\langle c\rangle \simeq\widehat{\mathbb Z}\amalg C_2, \qquad C_F(c)=1. \] The isomorphism over $\mathbb Q(i)$ transports this additional involution to the geometric group in N2. It lies outside $G_{\mathbb Q(i)}$ and is not a real place of that field.

statement: For the based real descent in Claim~B.116, every nontrivial Sylow subgroup of $R$ is a free pro-prime group of rank at least two. There is no nontrivial closed abelian subgroup of $R$ stable under this full $G_{\mathbb Q}$ action, and no nontrivial closed pro-odd subgroup stable under that action. Consequently \[ Z(R)=1,\qquad O_{2'}(R)=1, \] and a nontrivial $R$ has a nonabelian $2$-Sylow subgroup. These conclusions do not assert that every subgroup with an open normalizer image in $G_{\mathbb Q(i)}$ is stable under this full action.

statement: Let $E/B_p$ be finite, $X/E$ smooth geometrically integral affine, and $\phi:X_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathbb A^1_{E,\mathrm{et}}$ a pinned relative morphism with nonconstant actual point map $f$. Fix a finite generically \'etale Noether projection $g:X\to\mathbb A^n_E$ of degree $d$. For $X=\mathbb A^n$ and the identity projection this says $f(t)\in F_pD(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, with one $D$ independent of $t$.

statement: Let $U_d\to\cdots\to U_0=\operatorname{Spec}K$ be an elementary tower in the preceding sense, where $K$ has characteristic zero and every fibre is geometrically connected. Choose a complex realization of a field of definition for the tower and put $G_i=\pi_1^{\rm top}(U_i(\mathbb C))$. For every stage there is an exact sequence of discrete groups \[ 1\longrightarrow N_i\longrightarrow G_i \longrightarrow G_{i-1}\longrightarrow1. \tag{N3.L1} \] The group $N_i$ is a finitely generated free group or a closed orientable surface group when the fibre is hyperbolic. For fibre type $(0,2)$ or $(1,0)$ it is respectively a quotient of $\mathbb Z$ or $\mathbb Z^2$ by the image of the topological transgression; for types $(0,0)$ and $(0,1)$ it is trivial. In particular the abelian quotients here may have torsion. Every $G_i$ and each of its finite-index subgroups is residually finite and good for cohomology with finite modules. Completion of (N3.L1) is exact, including injectivity at its left end. Moreover, for every finitely generated abelian subgroup $A\subset G_i$, the homomorphism \[ \widehat A\longrightarrow\widehat G_i \tag{N3.L2} \] is injective. Thus the profinite topology induced on $A$ is its full profinite topology.

statement: Let $U/K$ be any elementary tower of B.124, put $L=K(U)$, and let $v$ be any valuation of $L$ trivial on $K$, with value group $\Gamma$. Choose a smooth proper compactification $\overline U$ with simple normal crossings boundary. At the centre of a prolongation of $v$, label the boundary branches $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, and put $\gamma_i=v(z_i)>0$. If the centre is in $U$, take $r=0$. Choose corresponding positive complex meridians $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ after spreading out the labelled local pair. They commute in the discrete group $G=\pi_1^{\rm top}(U(\mathbb C))$. Define its integral relation lattice \[ \Lambda_x=\left\{(a_i)\in\mathbb Z^r: m_1^{a_1}\cdots m_r^{a_r}=1\text{ in }G\right\}. \tag{N3.L3} \] This lattice has a finite basis. Choose a unimodular integer matrix $S$ giving Smith coordinates \[ S\Lambda_x=d_1\mathbb Z e_1\oplus\cdots\oplus d_s\mathbb Z e_s,\qquad d_j>0, \] and set $\eta_j=\sum_i S_{ji}\gamma_i$. Then, in the entire arithmetic group defining $U$, \[ I_v\longrightarrow E_U^{\overline L}\text{ is trivial} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \eta_j\in d_j\Gamma,&1\le j\le s,\\ \eta_j\in\Gamma_{\rm div},&s<j\le r . \end{cases} \tag{N3.L4} \] Here $\Gamma_{\rm div}=\bigcap_{n\ge1}n\Gamma$. The test holds in every dimension, for every value group and rank, and for all elementary factor types. The finite relation lattice is obtained recursively from the discrete extension data (N3.L1): first compute relations after projection to $G_{i-1}$, then compute the relations of their lifts in $N_i$. These last calculations are integer relations in a cyclic group or Smith calculations in a finitely generated abelian group. The transgression subgroup is included in the latter's presentation. The local boundary homomorphism $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)^r\to\pi_1(U_{\overline K})$ is injective exactly when $\Lambda_x=0$. Thus neither the factor types alone nor the mere existence of a smooth normal crossings compactification implies local injectivity.

statement: Let $C/L$ be as above, $q=\#L$, $P\in C(L)$, and let $a:J_C(L)\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a nontrivial finite abelian quotient of order prime to $p$. For a nontrivial character $\psi:A\to\overline{\mathbf Q}^{\times}$ define \[ c_d(\psi)=\sum_{E\in\operatorname{Div}^{+}_d(C)(L)} \psi\bigl(a([E-dP])\bigr), \qquad \kappa=[K_C-(2g-2)P]. \] Here an effective divisor is a Galois-invariant effective geometric divisor; it need not be a sum of rational points. The corresponding $P$-split Lang cover has twisted polynomial \[ L_P(\psi,T)=\sum_{d=0}^{2g-2}c_d(\psi)T^d, \qquad c_{2g-2}(\psi)=q^{g-1}\psi(a(\kappa)). \] For $g-1\le d\le2g-2$ one has \[ c_d(\psi)=q^{d+1-g}\psi(a(\kappa)) c_{2g-2-d}(\psi^{-1}). \tag{A.4} \] In particular, modulo any prime above $p$, \[ L_P(\psi,1)\equiv \sum_{d=0}^{g-1}c_d(\psi). \tag{A.5} \] For genus two this is exactly $L_P(\psi,1)\equiv1+\sum_{R\in C(L)}\psi(a([R-P]))$.

statement: With $A$ as in A.7 put \[ \Theta_{C,P,A}=\sum_{d=0}^{g-1} \sum_{E\in\operatorname{Div}^{+}_d(C)(L)}[a([E-dP])] \quad\hbox{in }\mathbf F_p[A]. \] The full $A$-cover satisfies criterion (R) if and only if \[ \bar\psi(\Theta_{C,P,A})\ne0 \quad\text{for every nontrivial } \bar\psi:A\to\overline{\mathbf F}_p^{\times}. \tag{A.6} \] One can equivalently sum through $2g-2$ in the definition of $\Theta$. For $A=\mathbf Z/\ell$, with $\ell$ an odd prime different from $p$, \[ \frac{h_L(D)}{h_L(C)} =\prod_{i=1}^{\ell-1}L_P(\psi^i,1) =N_{\mathbf Q(\zeta_\ell)/\mathbf Q}L_P(\psi,1). \] If $p$ generates $(\mathbf Z/\ell)^\times$, failure of (R) is equivalent to all the coefficients of $\Theta$ in $\mathbf F_p[\mathbf Z/\ell]$ being equal.

statement: For the same fixed character $\psi$ and rational base points $P,P_0$, \[ L_{P_0}(\psi,T) =L_P\bigl(\psi,\psi(a([P-P_0]))T\bigr). \tag{A.7} \] The associated covers differ by the constant torsor with arithmetic Frobenius value $a([P-P_0])$ (up to reversing all Frobenius conventions consistently). statement: For any genus $g\ge2$, any finite quotient $A$ of $J_C(L)$, and $N=\#C(L)$, let $N_b$ count the Abel-image points in the $A$-cosets. statement: The genus-two expression $1+\sum_{R\in C(L)}\psi([R-P])$ does not test relative $p$-divisibility in genus three, even for a prime cyclic cover with $p$ a primitive root. An explicit example is \[ C/\mathbf F_2:\quad y^2+y=x^7+x^3,\qquad P=\infty. \] There is a surjection $\chi:J_C(\mathbf F_2)\to\mathbf Z/3$ whose point-coset counts are $(3,1,1)$ and whose twisted polynomial is \[ L_P(\chi,T)=1+2T+3T^2+4T^3+4T^4. \] Its relative class number is $196$, while the point-only expression reduces to $1$ modulo $2$. This is a counterexample to exporting that numerical test; it is not a collision or a counterexample to A1.

statement: Let $C/L$ be smooth proper of genus $g\ge2$ and not geometrically a separable double cover of a genus-one curve. Let $D\to C$ be a connected \'etale cyclic cover of odd degree $n>1$ prime to $p$, with constant group $\langle\sigma\rangle$ and $P'\in D(L)$ over $P\in C(L)$. Define the homomorphism over $L$ \[ A=\prod_{\ell\mid n}(1-\sigma^{n/\ell}):J_D\to J_D, \qquad P_n=\operatorname{im}(A), \] where the product is over distinct prime factors. If $p\nmid\#P_n(L)$, then $P$ has no collision. Equivalently, a collision forces $p\mid\#P_n(L)$ on every such cover. This proves L4 with all field and nontriviality hypotheses explicit.

Every connected geometric cyclic \'etale cover of either prime degree has ordinary Prym. The same statements hold for the coefficientwise-square conjugate curve.

statement: For $C_0$ in A.18, its conjugate, and every original point $P\in C_0(\mathbf F_4)$, no cyclic $P$-split cover of degree three or five satisfies (R) over any finite extension of $\mathbf F_4$. Thus whenever a degree-seven witness is exhibited for such a point, seven is its least possible odd prime, with the quantifier over all finite extensions included.
notes: Working identifier AC.16. Proved Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $D\to C$ be the constant abelian $A$-cover of A.7 over $L=\mathbf F_q$. Let $E\subset\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ be a finite field containing $L$ and all $|A|$th roots of unity, and let $\bar\psi:A\to E^\times$ be nontrivial. Deck transformations act on cohomology by pullback. Define \[ V_{\bar\psi}= \left(H^1(D,\mathcal O_D)\otimes_L E\right)_{\bar\psi}, \qquad \Phi=(f\mapsto f^q)^*\otimes_L 1_E. \] Here $(f\mapsto f^q)^*$ means the map on coherent cohomology induced by the $q$th-power map of the structure sheaf over $L$; it is $L$-linear. Thus $\Phi$ is its \emph{$E$-linear} extension, not the absolute $q$-semilinear map on coefficients in $E$. It preserves $V_{\bar\psi}$, which has dimension $g-1$. With the local Artin convention of A.7 and reduction $\psi\mapsto\bar\psi$, \[ \overline{L_P(\psi,T)} =\det_E(1-T\Phi\mid V_{\bar\psi}). \tag{A.14} \] The inverse-character convention replaces $\bar\psi$ on both sides. In particular this gives the cohomological form of L2 in every genus, and in genus two \[ \Phi\bigm|V_{\bar\psi} =-\sum_{R\in C(L)}\bar\psi\bigl(a([R-P])\bigr). \]
notes: Working identifier AC.17. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: A.7; Deligne SGA4.5 Theorem2.2(b); Katz XXII Proposition2.2.5. External citations: AC_Deligne1977, AC_Katz1973

statement: Let $L$ be finite of characteristic $p$, let $C/L$ have genus at least two, and let $P\in C(L)$. Suppose $\pi:D\to C$ is a finite \'etale cover, geometrically connected and geometrically Galois, of nontrivial odd degree prime to $p$. Assume only that a point $P'\in D(L)$ above $P$ is specified; the geometric deck group need not be constant over $L$. If $p\nmid h_L(D)/h_L(C)$, then $P$ has no collision. This condition genuinely enlarges the constant-deck criterion over a fixed field. The reduction to a prime cyclic quotient in A.6 is not asserted for this enlargement: a prime cyclic quotient of the geometric group need not be stable under arithmetic Frobenius.
notes: Working identifier AC.18. Proved; broader pointed criterion Explicit owner proof inputs: A.4; A.5.

statement: Use $\mathbf F_4=\{0,1,\alpha,\alpha+1\}$ with $\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0$, and let $C_0$ be the curve of A.18. Its hyperelliptic quadratic twist \[ C_0^{\mathrm t}:\quad v^2+v=z+\frac{(\alpha+1)(z+1)}{z^2+z+\alpha}+\alpha \] has $\#J_{C_0^{\mathrm t}}(\mathbf F_4)=8$. At its point $P=\infty$ there is a pointed geometrically cyclic degree-seven \'etale cover over $\mathbf F_4$ with nonconstant deck group and relative class number $8051=97\cdot83$, hence odd. No nontrivial constant odd-order $P$-split Galois cover over $\mathbf F_4$ satisfies the hypotheses of L1, irrespective of its relative class number. This last assertion concerns the fixed field; it makes no exclusion over its extensions.
notes: Working identifier AC.19. Proved; explicit nonconstant-deck witness Explicit owner proof inputs: A.21; nonconstant_deck_twist.py.

statement:
Let $D	o C$ be a cover satisfying the broadened hypotheses of A.21 over a finite field $L$, and suppose $p
mid h_L(D)/h_L(C)$. There is an intermediate pointed geometrically Galois cover $E	o C$ over the same $L$, with geometric deck group \[ V\simeq(\mathbf Z/\ell)^r, \qquad \ell	ext{ odd},\quad \ell
e p, \quad 1\le r\le2g, \] such that arithmetic Frobenius acts irreducibly on $V$ and $p
mid h_L(E)/h_L(C)$. Let $m$ be the order of this action, so $m\mid\ell^r-1$. Write $L_m/L$ for the degree-$m$ extension. Then the deck group becomes constant over $L_m$ and \[  rac{h_{L_m}(E)}{h_{L_m}(C)} =\left( rac{h_L(E)}{h_L(C)}ight)^m. 	ag{A.15} \] Consequently there is a constant cyclic degree-$\ell$ pointed witness for L1 over $L_m$. For a fixed pair $(C/k,P)$, existence of a witness after some finite extension is therefore equivalent for the broadened criterion A.21 and for the original constant-deck criterion A3. Nonconstant deck groups can lower the field of a witness, as in A.22, but do not enlarge the class of pairs reached when all finite extensions are allowed.
notes: Working identifier AC.20. Proved; simple Frobenius quotient and exact descent power Explicit owner proof inputs: A.6; A.21; finite-field Frobenius determinant.

statement: For the genus-two curve \[ C/\mathbf F_4:\quad y^2+y=x^5+x \] and its hyperelliptic quadratic twist, the least odd prime degree of a constant pointed L1 witness at $P=\infty$, with all finite extensions allowed, is five. A witness is defined over $L=\mathbf F_{256}$. For the specified witness its four nontrivial twisted polynomials are all \[ L_P(\chi^i,T)=1-32T+256T^2=(1-16T)^2, \qquad 1\le i\le4, \] and its relative class number is $225^4=2\,562\,890\,625=3^8 5^8$, which is odd. The covering curve is the smooth Fermat quintic.
notes: Working identifier AC.21. Proved; exact least-prime-five witness Explicit owner proof inputs: A.7; A.25; supersingular_least5.py.

statement: Let $C/k$ be any genus-two curve over a finite field of characteristic two, let $P\in C(k)$, and put \[ \kappa_P=[K_C-2P]\in J_C(k). \] Let $\Theta$ be the geometric theta divisor of the line of locally exact differentials. A constant cyclic degree-three $P$-split cover satisfying L1 exists over some finite extension of $k$ if and only if at least one of the following holds: \begin{enumerate} \item $\Theta$ contains a nonzero point of order three; \item $\kappa_P\notin3J_C(k)$. \end{enumerate} In the second case a witness already exists over $k$. If neither holds, no extension can produce a cubic witness. More precisely, for an individual cubic cover over $L\supseteq k$ with character $\chi:J_C(L)\twoheadrightarrow\mathbf Z/3$, criterion L1 holds exactly when its geometric new two-rank is zero or $\chi(\kappa_P)\ne0$.
notes: Working identifier AC.22. Proved; exact all-extension cubic criterion Explicit owner proof inputs: A.7; A.8; A.20; checked R5.

statement: Let $C/k$ have genus two in any positive characteristic $p$, and let $P\in C(k)$. Suppose $\ell\ne p$ is an odd prime with $-1\in\langle p\rangle\subset(\mathbf Z/\ell)^\times$. If $\kappa_P=[K_C-2P]\notin\ell J_C(k)$, there is a degree-$\ell$ constant $P$-split L1 witness over $k$ itself.
notes: Working identifier AC.23. Proved; canonical-class sufficient condition Explicit owner proof inputs: A.7; A.8.

statement: Let $L$ be a finite field of characteristic two. Suppose $C/L$ has genus at least two and a separable degree-two morphism $f:C\to E$ to an elliptic curve. Let $P\in C(L)$ be a ramification point, and use $f(P)$ as the origin of $E$. Let $\varphi:E'\to E$ be an \'etale isogeny of odd degree $n>1$ over $L$, with no assumption that its kernel is constant, and let \[ D=C\times_E E'. \] Then $D\to C$ is a connected \'etale pointed geometrically Galois cover with odd geometric deck group, but \[ 2\mid h_L(D)/h_L(C). \] Consequently a prime cyclic character factoring through this elliptic quotient cannot be an L1 witness. The assertion persists over every finite extension. Neither L1 nor its nonconstant-deck enlargement A.21 can use this elliptic-isogeny pullback.
notes: Working identifier AC.24. Proved; ramified elliptic-factor obstruction Explicit owner proof inputs: A.5; explicit ramification divisor argument.

statement: Let $c\in\mathbf F_4\setminus\mathbf F_2$ and \[ C_c/\mathbf F_4:\quad y^2+y=x+\frac{c}{x^2+x}, \qquad P=\infty. \] There is no pointed geometrically Galois cover of nontrivial odd degree over $\mathbf F_4$ satisfying the relative-class-number criterion, even if its geometric deck group is nonconstant or nonabelian. Thus the variant of A3 requiring the original field while allowing nonconstant odd deck groups is false. This does not refute A3, which allows finite extensions.
notes: Working identifier AC.25. Proved; a fixed-field obstruction to the enlarged criterion Explicit owner proof inputs: A.23; A.27; coprime elliptic Frobenius factors.

statement: For the pointed curves $(C_c,P)$ of A.28: \begin{enumerate} \item No cubic or quintic constant L1 witness exists over any finite extension of $\mathbf F_4$. \item No nontrivial constant odd-group L1 witness exists over $\mathbf F_{4^m}$ for any $1\le m\le15$. \item At $m=16$, the only possible prime of a prime cyclic witness is $113$. The positive certificate at this degree is supplied in A.31. \end{enumerate} These conclusions about constant covers also hold at every rational hyperelliptic ramification point of $C_c$.
notes: Working identifier AC.26. Proved; stronger all-extension small-prime and field obstructions Explicit owner proof inputs: A.25; A.27; explicit theta equations and Frobenius periods.

statement: Let $k=\mathbf F_q$, $q=2^d$, and let \[ C/k:\quad Y^2+h(x)Y=f(x),\qquad \deg h\le2, \quad f\text{ monic of degree }5 \] be smooth of genus two, based at its unique point $P=\infty$. Let $n>1$ be odd and let $a\in J_C(\overline k)$ have exact order $n$ and satisfy $\sigma_q(a)=[q]a$, where $\sigma_q$ is arithmetic Frobenius. Choose a finite extension $E/k$ containing $a$ and $\mu_n$. For $0<i<n$, write the unique reduced Mumford representative of $ia$ as $(u_i,v_i)$, with $u_i$ monic of degree $r_i\in\{1,2\}$, so that $ia=[D_i-r_iP]$. For $j=2i\bmod n$, compute $c_i$ as follows. If $r_i=1$, put $c_i=h_1$, the coefficient of $x$ in $h$. If $r_i=2$ and $\gcd(u_i,h)$ has degree one, put $c_i=h_2$. Otherwise $r_i=2$ and $\gcd(u_i,h)=1$; let $v$ be the Cantor doubling interpolation of degree at most three, with $u_i^2\mid v^2+hv+f$ and $v\equiv v_i\bmod u_i$. If the reduced double has degree one, put $c_i=1$. If it has degree two, let $v_3$ be the cubic coefficient of $v$ and $b_j$ the coefficient of $x$ in $u_j$, and put $c_i=v_3b_j$. No other case occurs for a nonzero point of odd order. Define \[ A_i=\prod_{s=0}^{d-1}c_{2^s i}^{\,2^{d-1-s}}\in E. \tag{A.17} \] There is a unique constant cyclic $P$-split degree-$n$ cover over $k$ with geometric character subgroup generated by $a$. Its linear coherent $q$-Frobenius scalar on the summand for $ia$ is $\sigma_q^{-1}(A_i)$. Consequently its relative class number is odd if and only if \[ A_i\ne1\qquad(0<i<n). \tag{A.18} \] For the primitive factor alone use only $\gcd(i,n)=1$. These formulas refer to the pointing at infinity; another base point requires the twist of A.9.
notes: Working identifier AC.27. Proved; exact Cartier--Mumford rational test Explicit owner proof inputs: A.20; Serre duality; explicit Cartier calculation.

statement: For the pointed split curves $(C_c,\infty)$ of A.28, the least odd prime of a constant pointed L1 witness over all finite extensions is eleven. A degree-eleven witness is defined over $\mathbf F_{4^{60}}$, and sixty is the least extension degree for that prime. The least extension degree permitting any constant odd-group witness is sixteen, where a degree-$113$ witness exists. For the following eight $\mathbf F_4$ models, write $c\in\{\alpha,\alpha^2\}$ and $\delta\in\{0,\alpha\}$: \[ y^2+y=x+\frac{c}{x^2+x}+\delta,\qquad y^2+y=x+\frac{c}{x^2+x+\alpha}+\delta. \] Each original rational point has an eleven witness over $\mathbf F_{4^{60}}$ and a $113$ witness over $\mathbf F_{4^{16}}$. Whenever the cubic test A.25 fails, eleven is the least odd prime. In particular this holds for every rational point of the split models and for infinity on each quadratic-pole model.
notes: Working identifier AC.28. Proved; mixed witnesses and exact prime/field minima Explicit owner proof inputs: A.27; A.29; A.30; A.32; A.33.

statement: Let $B/k$ be an abelian variety over a finite field of characteristic $p$, and let $k'/k$ have degree $p^r$. Then \[ B(k)[p]=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B(k')[p]=0. \] In particular a relative-class-number $p$-unit for a fixed finite separable cover is preserved by every constant extension of $p$-power degree. If two pointed curves become isomorphic over a $p$-power extension, their existence of prime-degree witnesses over arbitrary extensions, and the set of primes furnishing such witnesses, agree.
notes: Working identifier AC.29. Proved; safe extensions of characteristic-power degree Explicit owner proof inputs: Finite-dimensional identity F^(p^r)-1=(F-1)^(p^r).

statement: For $(C_c,\infty)$ of A.28, no constant pointed degree-seven L1 witness exists over any finite extension of $\mathbf F_4$. The same holds for its coefficient conjugate and every pointed form isomorphic to it at infinity over a power-of-two extension.
notes: Working identifier AC.30. Proved; global seventh-prime exclusion for the bielliptic classes Explicit owner proof inputs: Theta difference bound; F^112=2 on J[7]; semilinear norm; A.32.

statement: Let \[ C/\mathbf F_{16}:\quad y^2+y=x^5,\qquad P=\infty. \] Arithmetic Frobenius on \(J_C\) is the scalar \([-4]\). Nevertheless there is a constant \(P\)-split cyclic cover of degree thirteen over \(\mathbf F_{4096}\), its first possible constant-deck field, whose new factor is ordinary of two-rank twelve and has odd relative class number. More precisely its twisted polynomials are \[ L_P(\chi^i,T) =1+\frac{139-13\left(\frac{i}{13}\right)\sqrt{13}}2\,T +4096T^2,\qquad 1\le i\le12, \] after choosing the sign of \(\sqrt{13}\) consistently with the quadratic Gauss sum. Consequently \[ \frac{P_D(T)}{P_C(T)} =\bigl(1+139T+12473T^2+569344T^3+16777216T^4\bigr)^6 \] and \[ \frac{h_{\mathbf F_{4096}}(D)}{h_{\mathbf F_{4096}}(C)} =17359173^6. \] Thus scalar Jacobian Frobenius, even at a rational hyperelliptic ramification point, does not reduce the rational criterion to vanishing of the geometric new \(p\)-rank.
notes: Working identifier AC.31. Proved counterexample to a scalar-Frobenius reduction Explicit owner proof inputs: A.7; A.30; Tate1966 Theorem2(d); independent explicit Kummer point counts. External citations: AC_Tate1966

statement: Let \(C/k\) have genus two, with \(k\) a finite field of characteristic \(p\), and let \(P\in C(k)\). Let \(\ell\ne p\) be an odd prime such that \(p\) is a primitive root modulo \(\ell\). Set \[ V=J_C(k)/\ell J_C(k),\qquad H=\ell J_C(k),\qquad N=\#C(k), \] and assume \(V\ne0\). If either \[ |V|>N\qquad\hbox{or}\qquad N\equiv-1\bmod p, \] and \[ (p-1)(N-1)>2(|H|-1), \tag{A.19} \] then some surjection \(J_C(k)\to\mathbf Z/\ell\) gives a \(P\)-split L1 witness over \(k\). One may replace (A.19) by the sharper occupancy-dependent condition \[ N_0(N_0-1)+(p-1)(N-N_0)>2(|H|-1),\qquad N_0=\#\{R\in C(k):[R-P]\in H\}. \] The subgroup \(H\) is the image of multiplication by \(\ell\), not the much larger kernel of one chosen cyclic character. No universal assertion about the existence of such a prime and field is implicit in this conditional criterion.
notes: Working identifier AC.32. Proved; a simultaneous genus-two counting criterion Explicit owner proof inputs: A.7; A.8; genus-two difference bound; finite Fourier inversion.

statement: Let \(C/k\) have genus two in characteristic two, with \(P\in C(k)\), and let \(\ell\ge5\) be an odd prime. Write \(F\) for arithmetic Frobenius on \(J_C[\ell](\overline k)\). Suppose that, for some \(d>0\), \[ F^d=sI,\qquad s\in\mathbf F_\ell^\times \text{ of order }\ell-1, \] and that every nonzero quotient functional has exact Frobenius period \(d(\ell-1)\). Then no \(P\)-split constant cyclic cover of degree \(\ell\) satisfies the rational criterion over any finite extension of \(k\). No assumption that two be primitive modulo \(\ell\) is needed. In particular this conclusion holds if the characteristic polynomial of \(F\) is irreducible over \(\mathbf F_\ell\) and \(q=\#k\) generates \(\mathbf F_\ell^\times\).
notes: Working identifier AC.33. Proved; a Frobenius obstruction with a split coefficient algebra Explicit owner proof inputs: Genus-two difference bound; rank-one module overF2[X]/Phi_ell; norm to invariant algebraF2.

statement: Let \(E/L\) be an ordinary elliptic curve in characteristic two, and let \(f:E\to\mathbf P^1\) be a separable degree-three map whose ramification consists of three distinct simple wild points \(R_1,R_2,R_3\). No difference \(R_i-R_j\), \(i\ne j\), is the nonzero geometric two-torsion class. It is nevertheless possible for all three differences to be two-primary. An explicit example over \(\mathbf F_4\), with \(\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0\) and \(\beta=\alpha^2\), is \[ E:\ y^2+xy=x^3+1,\qquad f=(y+\alpha)/x. \] The ramification points are \[ T=(0,1),\quad R=(\beta,0),\quad R'=(\beta,\beta), \] and the pair-difference orders are \(8,8,4\). The unramified residual points in their degree-three fibres are \[ S_\infty=\infty,\qquad S_\beta=(1,1),\qquad S_\alpha=(1,0), \] whose pair-difference orders are \(4,4,2\). The quadratic resolvent is the genus-two curve \[ C:\quad y^2+y=z+\frac{\beta}{z^2+z}+\alpha. \] Its constant pointed cubic cover has \(L(\chi,T)=1+3T+4T^2\) for both nontrivial characters and relative class number \(64\). For a pointed dihedral cubic cover \(D\to C\), twisting by the reflection fixing the chosen lift leaves its elliptic quotient unchanged. Thus this twist cannot reduce the two-primary order of the elliptic group in the proposed argument. These statements exhibit a limitation of that route, not a collision on \(C\).
notes: Working identifier AC.34. Proved; limitation of a trigonal branch-point argument Explicit owner proof inputs: Explicit differential; elliptic addition; quadratic cubic resolvent; A.7.

statement: Let \(C/\mathbf F_q\) be a genus-two curve in characteristic two, with a rational base point and the corresponding point-rigidified Poincare family of degree-zero line bundles, defined over the base field. Suppose arithmetic Frobenius on \(J_C\) is the scalar \([s]\), where \(s^2=q\). On a nonempty rational open of \(J_C\), choose a rational basis \(e_a\) of its one-dimensional nontrivial character cohomology, and write the \(q\)-power coefficient as \[ F_{\rm abs}^{\log_2q}e_a =A(a)e_{[q]a}. \] For the models of A.30, \(A\) is given explicitly by its finite Cartier--Mumford product. On the open \(U\) where this basis and \(A\) are invertible, \[ \mathcal Y:\quad z^{q-1}=A \] is a finite etale \(\mu_{q-1}\)-torsor. Its isomorphism class is independent of the basis on common domains of definition. If \(a\in U(\mathbf F_{q^m})\), the linear coherent return scalar for the pointed character defined by \(a\) is \[ \lambda(a)= N_{\mathbf F_{q^m}/\mathbf F_q} A(a). \] This is exactly the arithmetic Frobenius value of \(\mathcal Y\) at \(a\), with degree \(m\). If \(a\) has odd prime order \(\ell\) and every nonzero multiple of \(a\) lies in \(U\), its pointed cyclic cover over \(\mathbf F_{q^m}\) satisfies (R) exactly when all these Frobenius values differ from one. The torsor furnished by \(C:y^2+y=x^5\) over \(\mathbf F_{16}\) is geometrically nontrivial. This construction supplies a finite etale object detecting the single-character return condition, but does not prove that its nontrivial Frobenius locus contains a whole nonzero prime cyclic subgroup.
notes: Working identifier AC.35. Proved partial reformulation; a finite etale torsor in the scalar case Explicit owner proof inputs: A.20; A.30; scalar Frobenius identity; exact norm calculation.

statement: Let \(L=\mathbf F_{4096}\), let \(D/L\) be the Fermat curve \[ X^{39}+Y^{39}+Z^{39}=0, \] and choose a primitive thirteenth root \(\zeta\in L\). The automorphisms \[ \sigma(X:Y:Z)=(\zeta X:\zeta^3Y:\zeta^9Z), \qquad \tau(X:Y:Z)=(Y:Z:X) \] generate a constant group \(G\simeq C_{13}\rtimes C_3\) acting freely on \(D\). For \(C=D/G\), one has \[ g(D)=703,\qquad g(C)=19. \] For every odd positive integer \(m\), \[ \begin{aligned} J_D(\mathbf F_{4096^m})[2^\infty] &\simeq(\mathbf Z/2)^{24},\\ J_C(\mathbf F_{4096^m})[2^\infty] &\simeq(\mathbf Z/2)^4. \end{aligned} \] Thus this cover has relative class-number valuation \[ v_2\!\left(\frac{h(D)}{h(C)}\right)=20 \] over every such odd extension: it fails (R). Nevertheless every \(P\in C(\mathbf F_{4096^m})\), with \(m\) odd, has a rational lift to this same cover after an additional extension of degree in \(\{1,3,13\}\), and the bounded-exponent nonabelian criterion applies there, since \(39>(2-1)^2\). For an even extension degree \(m\), the exact exponent of \(J_D(\mathbf F_{4096^m})[2^\infty]\) is \(2^{v_2(m)+2}\). In particular it is eight for \(m=2\); the numerical inequality for this order-39 cover then fails. The example distinguishes two sufficient tests on a specified cover; it does not assert that \(C\) has no other (R) witness.
notes: Working identifier AC.36. Proved: an exact nonabelian bounded-exponent example Explicit owner proof inputs: Katz1981 Cor2.4 p181; elementary Frobenius scalar argument; A.53. External citations: AC_Katz1981

statement: On the Fermat curve \(D/\mathbf F_{4096}\) of A.39, choose a primitive thirty-ninth root \(\xi\) and put \[ s(X:Y:Z)=(X:\xi Y:\xi^{17}Z), \qquad \tau(X:Y:Z)=(Y:Z:X). \] The constant nonabelian group \[ G'=\langle s,\tau\rangle \simeq C_{39}\rtimes_{16}C_3 \] has order \(117\) and acts freely. Its quotient \(C_7=D/G'\) has genus seven and zeta numerator \[ P_{C_7}(T)=(1-64T)^2(1+64T)^4 (1-115T+4096T^2)^4. \] Thus \(J_{C_7}(\mathbf F_{4096})[2^\infty] \simeq(\mathbf Z/2)^4\), and \(D/C_7\) again has relative class-number valuation twenty. The bounded-exponent criterion for this cover applies after splitting the pointed fibre over every extension of \(\mathbf F_{4096}\) of odd or twice-odd degree: the relevant exponents are respectively two and eight, and \(117>(8-1)^2\). There is also a more direct (R) witness for this particular quotient. The subgroup \(\langle s^3,\tau\rangle\) is normal of index three and is the order-39 group of A.39, after choosing its generator of order thirteen. Writing \(C_{19}=D/\langle s^3,\tau\rangle\), the cover \(C_{19}\to C_7\) is etale cyclic of degree three, with relative zeta numerator and relative class number \[ (1+64T)^{24},\qquad 65^{24}. \] Its new two-rank is zero, so (R) persists over every extension, and every prescribed base point becomes split after an additional extension of degree at most three. Accordingly, the smaller genus of this quotient does not enlarge the set of curves reached by (R).
notes: Working identifier AC.37. Proved: a free order-117 group and its precise limitation Explicit owner proof inputs: A.39; explicit free group action; Jacobi character invariants.

statement: Let \(C/k\) be a genus-two curve in characteristic two, let \(P\in C(k)\), and suppose Jacobian Frobenius is the scalar \([s]\), where \(s=\varepsilon2^r\), \(\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}\), and \(\#k=s^2\). Let \(\ell\) be an odd prime and put \[ f=\operatorname{ord}_\ell(2),\qquad m=\operatorname{ord}_\ell(s),\qquad d=\frac{f}{\gcd(f,m)}. \] Every geometric cyclic degree-\(\ell\) cover has a \(P\)-pointed descent to \(k\), possibly with nonconstant deck group, and its first constant-deck field has degree \(m\). Suppose \[ d=1, \quad\text{equivalently}\quad \langle2\rangle\subseteq\langle s\rangle \text{ in }\mathbf F_\ell^\times. \] Then all its geometric new two-torsion points are rational over that first constant-deck field. In particular this cover satisfies (R) over a field with constant deck group if and only if its geometric new two-rank is zero. This equivalence holds individually for every cyclic cover, and persists over all further constant fields. No assumption that two is primitive modulo \(\ell\) is required. The condition has the following explicit forms: \[ \begin{array}{c|c} s&\text{condition for }d=1\\ \hline +2^r&\gcd(r,f)=1\\ -2^r,\ f\text{ even}&\gcd(r+f/2,f)=1\\ -2^r,\ f\text{ odd}&\gcd(r,f)=1. \end{array} \] When \(d>1\), the same argument yields a norm in \(\mathbf F_{2^d}^\times\), which need not be one. It therefore gives no converse obstruction in that case.
notes: Working identifier AC.38. Proved: when scalar Frobenius forces the arithmetic test to be geometric Explicit owner proof inputs: A.20 stable cohomology comparison; semilinear norm; fixed-ring calculation.

statement: Let \(G\) be a finite solvable group of order prime to \(p\), and let \(V\) be a finite \(p\)-primary abelian group with a \(G\)-action. For a subgroup \(H\), write \[ e_H=\frac1{|H|}\sum_{h\in H}h \quad\text{on }V. \] The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item For every pair of normal subgroups \(H<K\) of \(G\), one has \(V^H\supsetneq V^K\). \item There is \(v\in V\) such that \(\operatorname{Stab}_G(e_Hv)=H\) for every normal subgroup \(H\) of \(G\). \end{enumerate} In particular, let \(D/k\to C/k\) be a constant solvable prime-to-\(p\) Galois etale cover, with a rational chosen point over \(P\), and put \(V=J_D(k)[p^\infty]\). All relative class-number tests for \[ D/H\longrightarrow D/K, \qquad H<K\text{ normal in }G, \] fail if and only if there is a rational \(p\)-primary class on \(D\) whose norms have free deck orbits on every normal quotient of this particular cover. This is a finite-level statement about classes, with no assertion that they are differences of points.
notes: Working identifier AC.39. Proved: exact finite-level meaning of hereditary relative tests Explicit owner proof inputs: Induction on solvable groups; finite etale character factors; normalized averaging; norm/pullback.

statement: Let \(G\) be a finite solvable group of order prime to \(p\), let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional \(\mathbf F_p\)-vector space with a \(G\)-action, and let \(F\in\operatorname{GL}(V)\) and \(\phi\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)\) satisfy \[ F(gv)=\phi(g)F(v). \] Assume that for every positive integer \(r\) and every \(\phi^r\)-stable pair of subgroups \(A\triangleleft B\) with \(B\triangleleft G\) and \(B/A\) cyclic of prime order, one has \[ (V^A)^{F^r}\supsetneq(V^B)^{F^r}. \tag{A.43.1} \] Then there is \(v\in V^F\) such that \[ \operatorname{Stab}_G(e_Hv)=H \quad\text{for every normal }H\triangleleft G. \tag{A.43.2} \] The subgroups \(H\) in this conclusion need not be \(\phi\)-stable. For a pointed geometrically Galois odd prime-to-\(p\) etale cover \(D/k\to C/k\), take \(V=J_D[p](\overline k)\), with its actual arithmetic Frobenius. Failure of every relative cyclic-prime class-number test over intermediate pointed bases which are geometrically normal over \(C\), and over every finite constant extension, implies (A.43.1). Consequently it supplies the class in (A.43.2). The rational class need not be a point difference.
notes: Working identifier AC.40. Proved: semilinear simultaneous regularity from all relative tests Explicit owner proof inputs: A.42 induction; maximal irreducible-kernel isolation; exact Frobenius orbit comparison; A.23 constantization.

statement: Let $C/k$ be a genus-two curve over a finite field of characteristic two, and let $P\in C(k)$ be a Weierstrass point. Fix a nontrivial geometric connected cyclic etale cover of odd degree $n$, with a chosen point above $P$. Let $k_d/k$ be the first constant extension over which its geometric isomorphism class is stable, and use its unique pointed descent to $k_d$. Suppose Frobenius on its geometric cyclic deck group is multiplication by $a\in(\mathbf Z/n)^\times$, of order $m$. Put \[ U=(\mathbf Z/n)^\times,\qquad T=\langle2\rangle\subset U,\qquad H=\langle a,-1\rangle\subset U. \] If $T\subset H$, every geometric two-torsion point of the primitive factor is rational over the first constant-deck field $k_{dm}$. Consequently, for this pointed cover, the primitive class number is odd over some constant-deck field if and only if its geometric primitive two-rank is zero. When $n=\ell$ is prime, this is the whole relative criterion \textup{(R)}. More generally, the possible primitive Frobenius multipliers over $k_{dm}$ belong to the units of a direct factor of \[ \left(\mathbf F_{2^{\delta}}\right)^c, \qquad \delta=\frac{|T|}{|T\cap H|},\qquad c=\frac{|U|}{|TH|}. \tag{A.44.1} \] Thus the preceding sufficient condition is exactly $\delta=1$ for this fixed-ring argument. In particular, suppose the Jacobian Frobenius of $C/k$ is the scalar $[\varepsilon2^r]$, with $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ and $\#k=2^{2r}$. For an odd prime $\ell$, put $f=\operatorname{ord}_\ell(2)$. The sufficient condition becomes, independently of the sign $\varepsilon$, \[ \begin{cases} \gcd(r,f)=1,&f\text{ odd},\\ \gcd(r,f/2)=1,&f\text{ even}. \end{cases} \tag{A.44.2} \] This sharpens A.41, and also applies to nonscalar Jacobian Frobenius whenever the displayed deck-group condition holds over the first field of definition of the chosen cyclic cover.
notes: Working identifier AC.41. Proved; an all-extension obstruction using the pointed involution Explicit owner proof inputs: A.41; pointed hyperelliptic lift; finite etale fixed-ring calculation.

statement: Fixed algebraic coefficient functions evaluated at prime-to-$p$ torsion points, even when their Frobenius periods are prime to $p$, do not by themselves give a bounded valuation for the return unit minus one. More precisely, put $p=2$, let $\omega$ be a primitive cube root of unity, and set $K=\mathbf Q_2(\omega)$. For $n\ge1$ choose a primitive $3^n$-th root $\zeta_n$ satisfying \[ m_n=3^{n-1},\qquad \zeta_n^{m_n}=\omega. \] These roots are prime-to-two Teichmuller points. The fourth-power Frobenius orbit of $\zeta_n$ has the odd length $m_n$. For the single fixed degree-one coefficient function $A(X)=1-2X$, its orbit return is \[ U_n=\prod_{j=0}^{m_n-1}A(\zeta_n^{4^j}) =N_{K(\zeta_n)/K}(1-2\zeta_n) =1-2^{m_n}\omega. \tag{A.45.1} \] In particular \[ v_2(A(\zeta_n)-1)=1,\qquad v_2(U_n)=0, \qquad v_2(U_n-1)=m_n=3^{n-1}. \tag{A.45.2} \] For the full square-Frobenius orbit over $\mathbf Q_2$, the analogous return is \[ N_{\mathbf Q_2(\zeta_n)/\mathbf Q_2}(1-2\zeta_n) =\Phi_{3^n}(2)=1+2^{m_n}+2^{2m_n}, \tag{A.45.3} \] again a unit whose difference from one has valuation $m_n$. Consequently the annihilator sizes $2^{v_2(U_n-1)}$ grow faster than $3^{gn}$ for every fixed positive integer $g$. There is an integral semilinear module realizing these annihilator sizes. Let $L_n=K(\zeta_n)$, put $M_n=\mathcal O_{L_n}$, and let $\sigma_n$ be the fourth-power Frobenius of $L_n/K$. Give $M_n$ the operator \[ \mathcal F_n(x)=(1-2\zeta_n)\sigma_n(x). \] It normalizes the odd cyclic deck action $\delta_n(x)=\zeta_nx$ by $\mathcal F_n\delta_n\mathcal F_n^{-1}=\delta_n^4$, and \[ \mathcal F_n^{m_n}=U_n,\qquad M_n/(1-\mathcal F_n)M_n \simeq\mathcal O_K/(2^{m_n}),\qquad \exp\bigl((L_n/M_n)^{\mathcal F_n}\bigr)=2^{m_n}. \tag{A.45.4} \] This is an algebraic Frobenius-cocycle countermodel to a proposed intermediate bound. It is not asserted to arise from the Jacobians in A.107, or from pure cohomology of Weil weight one. It therefore does not refute the conditional geometric route in A.107. Indeed $|U_n|^2=4^{m_n}+2^{m_n}+1>4^{m_n}$ under a complex embedding, so the required weight-one equality already fails.
notes: Working identifier AC.42. Proved obstruction to a finite-type-only return bound Explicit owner proof inputs: Elementary cyclotomic norms; unramified Frobenius; integral Smith normal form.

statement: Let $U/\mathbf F_q$ be smooth and geometrically connected, and let $\mathcal L$ be a rank-one unit-root overconvergent $F$-isocrystal on $U$, with coefficients in a fixed finite extension of $\mathbf Q_p$. Write $b_x$ for its Frobenius eigenvalue at a closed point $x$. For every fixed integer $c\ge0$, the finite valuations \[ \{v_p(b_x-1):x\in|U|,\ v_p(\deg x)\le c,\ b_x\ne1\} \tag{A.46.1} \] are uniformly bounded. This assertion would apply to a character family only after its return eigenvalues had been identified with such an overconvergent object. There is a concrete obstruction to that identification in the scalar example $C_0:y^2+y=x^5$ over $\mathbf F_{16}$. Its ordinary character unit roots at the order-three parameters and the order-thirteen parameter of A.34 cannot be interpolated by one rank-one coefficient object with finite geometric monodromy on a common geometrically connected base over $\mathbf F_{16}$ containing those parameter points with their indicated closed-point degrees two and three. In particular no rank-one unit-root overconvergent $F$-isocrystal can have all those prescribed return eigenvalues. This conclusion concerns the proposed interpolation; it does not assert that an intrinsic arithmetic $F$-isocrystal on the ordinary character locus has been constructed.
notes: Working identifier AC.43. Proved limit of a rank-one overconvergence approach Explicit owner proof inputs: Hartl-Pal2025 Proposition8.6; A.34; theta3 pole-gap argument; exact quartic-field arithmetic; Etesse2010 5.4.3.5--11 for scope. External citations: AC_Etesse2010, AC_HartlPal2025

statement: For any member, with \(t\notin\mathbb F_4\), of the genus-two pencil of Claim~\ref{clm:AGprimitivecounterexample} over \(\mathbb F_{2^{38}}\), a nontrivial odd conductor of a primitive two-rank-zero cyclic cover must belong to \[ \{191,229\}. \tag{A.47.1} \] Consequently the incidence estimate of Claim~A.82 improves to \[ \#\{\text{bad parameters}\} \le133086336+229171540=362257876, \] and at least \[ 274877906944-4-362257876=274515649064 \tag{A.47.2} \] parameters have no nontrivial odd primitive-zero cover. These are counts of parameters, not of isomorphism classes. The assertion retains the degree-one qualification of the A6 counterexample and does not exclude rational class-number witnesses.
notes: Working identifier AC.44. Proved by an exact finite certificate Explicit owner proof inputs: A.80--34; A.85; theta difference intersection; exhaustive packet-union search.

statement: Let $C/k$ be smooth, proper and geometrically connected of genus at least two over a finite field of characteristic $p$, and let $P\in C(k)$. Use the full etale fundamental groups in the first row below, and put \[ \Omega=\pi_1(C_{\bar k},\bar P),\qquad \Delta=\Omega^{(p')},\qquad N=\ker(\Omega\longrightarrow\Delta),\qquad V=N^{\mathrm{ab},p}. \tag{A.48.1} \] Here $N^{\mathrm{ab},p}$ is the maximal abelian pro-$p$ quotient. The actual point section $s_P$ acts on these groups; write $F$ for arithmetic Frobenius and also for its induced automorphism of $V$. For the pointed norm module $M_P$ of A.100 there is a natural exact sequence of compact abelian pro-$p$ groups \[ 0\longrightarrow V\xrightarrow{\ F-1\ }V \xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\ }M_P^F \longrightarrow0. \tag{A.48.2} \] Every $m\in M_P^F$ is the compatible $p$-adic abelianized difference from $s_P$ of a continuous section of the \emph{full} arithmetic etale fundamental group of $C$. That section projects to exactly $s_P$ in the geometrically prime-to-$p$ quotient. If $m\ne0$, A1 implies that this full section is not geometrically conjugate to the section of any point of $C(k)$. Projection is surjective at every $F$-stable pointed level, in particular \[ M_P^F\twoheadrightarrow J_C(k)[p^\infty]. \tag{A.48.8} \] Thus nonzero section-origin classes actually exist whenever $J_C(k)[p^\infty]\ne0$. The statement supplies no element with free deck orbit at every level. In particular it neither proves nor refutes A10(c) or the nontrivial-cover existence assertion A3.
notes: Working identifier AC.45. statement: Let $L$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $C/L$ be smooth, proper and geometrically connected of genus at least two, and let $P\ne Q$ in $C(L)$ have conjugate sections in the geometrically prime-to-$p$ arithmetic fundamental group. Let $\pi:D\to C$ be a connected finite etale cover with prime-to-$p$ geometric Galois closure, let $P'\in D(L)$ lie above $P$, and let $\phi:D\to X_0$ be an $L$-morphism to a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least one. Assume $J_{X_0}(L)[p]=0$. Then a lift $Q'\in D(L)$ supplied by R1 satisfies $\phi(Q')=\phi(P')$. Moreover, \[ [\phi_*\pi^*(Q)-\phi_*\pi^*(P)]=0\quad\hbox{in }J_{X_0}(L). \] If $\pi$ is a torsor under a constant finite group $G$ over $L$, then $P'$ makes the entire $P$-fibre rational, the $Q$-fibre is also rational, and the stronger equality of effective divisors holds: \[ \phi_*\pi^*(Q)=\phi_*\pi^*(P). \] For a general cover the same divisor equality holds if the geometric $p$-rank of $J_{X_0}$ is zero, or if $\deg(\pi)$ is strictly less than the geometric gonality of $X_0$.
notes: Working identifier AG.1. Proved; a precise rational correspondence statement Proof-scope references. External citations: AC_Oort2008

statement: Let $\mathcal N$ be the class of smooth proper curves of genus at least two over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ for which the point-section map is injective over every finite field of definition and every finite extension thereof. It has the following closure properties. If $D\to C$ is a connected finite etale cover with prime-to-$p$ geometric Galois closure and $D\in\mathcal N$, then $C\in\mathcal N$. If $C$ has a family of morphisms to curves in $\mathcal N$ which jointly separates geometric points, then $C\in\mathcal N$. One may also use positive-genus targets with geometric $p$-rank zero.
notes: Working identifier AG.2. Proved; the closure operations in L6 Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $C$ be a smooth proper genus-$g$ curve over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ of characteristic $p>0$, and let $L$ be a line bundle of exact order $n>1$, with $(n,p)=1$. Let $D\to C$ be the associated connected cyclic etale cover. For $i\in\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ put $V_i=H^1(C,L^i)$, with a fixed trivialization of $L^n$. Absolute Frobenius gives $p$-semilinear maps $F_i:V_i\to V_{pi}$. For an orbit $O$ of multiplication by $p$ on $(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^\times$, choose $i\in O$ and let $r_O$ be the eventual rank of the iterates of $F^{|O|}:V_i\to V_i$. Then \[ f_p(P_n(D))=\sum_O |O|r_O. \] In particular the primitive part has $p$-rank zero if and only if every such orbit composite is nilpotent. Here $\dim_\Omega V_i=g-1$ for every nontrivial $i$.
notes: Working identifier AG.3. Proved; the exact Frobenius-orbit formula Proof-scope references.

statement: The implication from a nonordinary character-cohomology block to absence of surviving $p$-primary vectors is false. The failure persists for a nonabelian group and a vector with free deck orbit in the abstract module.

statement: Let $\Omega$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p$, and let $\pi:D\to C$ be a connected finite etale Galois cover of smooth proper curves, with $g(C)\ge2$ and group $G$ of order $m$ prime to $p$. Let \[ a=\sum_{g\in G}a_g g\in\mathbf Z[G]\setminus\{0\}, \qquad d=\sum_g|a_g|. \] Assume $(d,m)=1$ and $m>(d-1)^2$. If $G$ is nonabelian, then for any points $P',Q'\in D(\Omega)$ lying above distinct points of $C$ one has \[ a[Q'-P']\ne0\quad\hbox{in }J_D(\Omega). \]
notes: Working identifier AG.5. Proved; a small integral group-ring obstruction Proof-scope references. External citations: AG_Poonen2007

statement: In A.53 suppose all cover data are defined over a finite field $L$, $G$ is constant over $L$, and $P'\in D(L)$ lies above $P\in C(L)$. Put $B_a=\operatorname{im}(a:J_D\to J_D)$, an abelian subvariety over $L$. If $B_a(L)[p]=0$, then $P$ collides with no other point of $C(L)$. The same conclusion holds over all finite fields of definition if $f_p(B_a)=0$ geometrically. Thus an odd nonabelian group can use, for example, $a=(1-\delta)(1-\epsilon)$ whenever the four support elements are distinct and $m>9$.
notes: Working identifier AG.6. Proved; rational and geometric nonabelian criteria Proof-scope references.

Their root-space representations do not give instances of the prime-to-$p$ etale criteria above.

statement: Let $p=2$ or $3$, and let $n>1$ be odd and prime to $p$, with $(p-1)(n-1)\ge4$. Suppose that \[ (p-1)n\mid p^r+1 \] for some positive integer $r$. The smooth proper curve \[ C_{p,n}:y^p-y=x^n \] has a connected cyclic etale cover of degree $n$ whose entire Jacobian, and therefore its primitive conductor-$n$ factor, has $p$-rank zero. For $p=2$ the cover is the Fermat curve $u^n+z^n=1$; for $p=3$ it is the smooth model of $u^n=z^{2n}-1$. In both cases the map is \[ x=uz,\qquad y=z^n. \] Thus these are actual cases of A6 in both small characteristics, without a separability or Galois-closure qualification left over.
notes: Working identifier AG.10. Proved; explicit cyclic zero-rank families in characteristics two and three Proof-scope references. External citations: AG_Crew1984

statement: In characteristic two, let \[ C:y^2+y=x^7,\qquad D:u^7+z^7=1,\qquad (x,y)=(uz,z^7). \] Then $D\to C$ is connected cyclic etale of degree seven, $g(C)=3$, $g(D)=15$, and $f_2(C)=0$, $f_2(D)=6$. Each nontrivial deck-character space has coherent dimension two and stable Frobenius dimension one. In particular both primitive doubling-orbit composites are noninvertible, but neither is nilpotent. The primitive factor has dimension twelve and two-rank six.

statement: In characteristic two, the cyclic etale degree-$35$ cover \[ u^{35}+z^{35}=1\ \longrightarrow\ C:y^2+y=x^{35},\qquad (x,y)=(uz,z^{35}), \] has $g(C)=17$, $g(D)=561$ and $f_2(D)=6$, while its primitive conductor-$35$ factor has dimension $384$ and two-rank zero.

statement: Let $E/L$ be an elliptic curve over a finite field of characteristic two. Then $E(L)[2]=0$ if and only if $E$ is supersingular. Thus an ordinary elliptic target does not weaken the geometric zero-rank requirement in L5 when $p=2$. In characteristic three, if $E$ is ordinary and $E(L)[3]=0$, this vanishing persists over every odd-degree extension of $L$ and fails over every even-degree extension.
notes: Working identifier AG.13. Proved; the elliptic rational lever in characteristics two and three Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $C/\overline{\mathbf F}_2$ be a hyperelliptic curve of genus $g\ge3$. There is a connected cyclic etale cover $D\to C$ of degree three and a smooth proper curve $B$ of genus $g-1$ with two morphisms $D\to B$ which jointly separate geometric points. Consequently, if every genus-$(g-1)$ curve has no collision over its finite fields of definition, then $C$ has no collision. In particular universal A1 in genus two and characteristic two would imply A1 for every hyperelliptic genus-three curve in that characteristic.
notes: Working identifier AG.14. Proved; a genus-lowering closure step in characteristic two Proof-scope references.

statement: Over $\overline{\mathbf F}_2$ let \[ C_a:y^2+y=x^5+a x^3. \] Every genus-two curve of two-rank zero is geometrically isomorphic to some $C_a$. Its Raynaud theta divisor, based at its point $\infty$, is $\Theta_a=\{[R-\infty]:R\in C_a\}$. It has no nonzero point of order three. It has a point of exact order five if and only if $a=0$, and a point of exact order seven if and only if $a^5=1$. Consequently: \begin{enumerate} \item for $a=0$ a degree-five cyclic etale cover has zero primitive two-rank; \item for $a^5=1$ a degree-seven cyclic etale cover has zero primitive two-rank, while every degree-three or degree-five cyclic cover is new-ordinary; \item if $a\ne0$ and $a^5\ne1$, every geometric cyclic cover of degree three, five or seven is new-ordinary. \end{enumerate} These are geometric assertions. The last assertion alone does not exclude rational L1 witnesses of those degrees over a particular field.
notes: Working identifier AG.15. Proved; exact small-prime theta tests in a supersingular genus-two family Proof-scope references.

statement: For $C_a$ in A.63, the Raynaud theta divisor contains a point of exact order eleven if and only if \[ a^{35}+a^{10}+1=0. \] At each such parameter there is a connected cyclic etale degree-eleven cover with zero full new two-rank. At every other parameter all degree-eleven cyclic covers are new-ordinary.
notes: Working identifier AG.16. Proved; the degree-eleven theta locus in the same family Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $\Omega$ be algebraically closed of odd characteristic, and let $D\to C$ be a connected etale Galois cover of smooth proper curves with $g(C)\ge2$ and geometric group $G$ of order $m$ prime to the characteristic. Suppose $m\nmid4$. For points $P',Q'\in D(\Omega)$ in distinct fibres, the class $[Q'-P']$ has trivial stabilizer in $G$. In particular this holds for every nonabelian $G$, including groups of even order. Consequently, over a finite field of odd characteristic, the full relative class-number criterion L1 holds for a pointed geometrically Galois etale cover with such a group. The deck group need not be constant: the geometric average is the rational pullback--norm projector. This supplies an even-group version of the nonabelian criterion, without asserting that its existence reaches a pair outside A3.
notes: Working identifier AG.17. Proved; even deck groups in odd characteristic Proof-scope references.

statement: For the characteristic-two family $C_a$ in A.63, the Raynaud theta divisor contains a point of exact order nine if and only if $a^5=1$. At each such parameter the associated connected cyclic etale degree-nine cover has genus ten and two-rank two. Its primitive conductor-nine factor has dimension six and two-rank zero, whereas its degree-three intermediate cover is new-ordinary. Thus primitive-only vanishing can occur with genus-two base, not just in the genus-seventeen example A.60.
notes: Working identifier AG.18. Proved; primitive-only vanishing already in genus two Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $D\to C$ be a connected etale geometrically Galois cover of smooth proper curves over a finite field $L$ of characteristic $p$, with $g(C)\ge2$, nontrivial geometric group $G$ of order prime to $p$, and a rational point $P'$ above $P\in C(L)$. If \[ p\nmid h_L(D)/h_L(C), \] then $P$ collides with no other point of $C(L)$. There is no odd-order restriction and no constant-deck restriction. For $|G|>2$ the proof is elementary once the rational projector is established. The degree-two case uses the verified odd-characteristic hyperelliptic case of R4.
notes: Working identifier AG.19. Proved; the full-relative criterion for every deck order Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $C$ be an ordinary smooth proper curve of genus at least two over $\overline{\mathbf F}_2$, with a separable degree-two map $C\to E$ to an ordinary elliptic curve. For every connected odd-degree etale isogeny $E'\to E$, the pullback $D=C\times_E E'$ is ordinary. In particular no such $D$ admits a nonconstant morphism to a positive-genus curve of two-rank zero, or a nonzero homomorphism from its Jacobian onto an abelian variety of two-rank zero. This applies to both elliptic quotients of the ordinary genus-two curves in A.28. Thus those isogeny-pullback families supply neither the rational new-part vanishing of A.27 nor the geometric zero-rank targets in L5. It is a restriction on these specified families, not on all odd-degree covers of $C$.
notes: Working identifier AG.20. Proved; an ordinary elliptic-pullback barrier in characteristic two Proof-scope references. External citations: AG_Crew1984

statement: For the characteristic-two family $C_a$ of A.63, put $U=a^5$. Its Raynaud theta divisor contains a point of exact order thirteen if and only if \[ (U+1)(U^3+U+1)(U^4+U+1)(U^6+U^5+1)=0. \tag{A.69.1} \] Each such parameter admits a connected cyclic etale degree-thirteen cover with zero full new two-rank. At every other parameter all degree-thirteen covers are new-ordinary. In particular every degree-thirteen cover of $C_0:y^2+y=x^5$ has ordinary new part.
notes: Working identifier AG.21. Proved; the complete degree-thirteen theta locus Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $C_0/\mathbf F_{16}$ be $y^2+y=x^5$, with $P=\infty$. The Frobenius of $J_{C_0}$ is the scalar $[-4]$. Over $L=\mathbf F_{4096}$ there exists a constant cyclic degree-thirteen $P$-split cover whose relative class number is odd, although its entire new factor is ordinary of dimension twelve. Moreover $L$ is the first extension of $\mathbf F_{16}$ over which any constant cyclic degree-thirteen cover can occur. Thus the distinction already occurs at the minimal constant-deck field under scalar base Frobenius.

statement: Let $C/\mathbf F_q$ be a smooth plane quartic, let $P\in C(\mathbf F_q)$, and let $K$ be its canonical divisor class, represented by a line section. From the closed points of degrees one, two and three, their local expansions, and linear algebra over $\mathbf F_q$, one can compute the entire group $J_C(\mathbf F_q)$ and every pointed cyclic prime-order character. The algorithm below gives the exact twisted $L$-polynomial for every such character; it does not replace the Jacobian group law by the numerical zeta polynomial.
notes: Working identifier AG.23. Proved; a finite divisor algorithm for pointed plane quartics Proof-scope references.

statement: There are exactly $3001$ isomorphism classes of pointed smooth plane quartics $(C,P)$ over $\mathbf F_3$. For every one of them the program \path{code/plane_quartic_F3.cpp} computes all constant odd-prime cyclic pointed tests over $\mathbf F_3$. It retains the exact $L$-polynomials for all $2692$ tested quotients, including failures. There is a successful base-field witness for $2368$ pointed classes. For $637$ classes a degree-five witness succeeds; five is therefore their least admissible odd prime over all finite extensions. For the other $2364$ classes this calculation does not determine the all-extension minimum. The $633$ classes without a base-field witness are not asserted to lack witnesses after extension. Likewise, the smallest successful prime in the base-field table is not called the all-extension minimum when it exceeds five. The $\mathbf F_5$ quartic calculation is given in A.73--A.74, with the same distinction between base-field and all-extension minima.
notes: Working identifier AG.24. Proved by exact computation; every pointed plane quartic over $\mathbf F_3$ Proof-scope references. Internal premises independently audited; forward consequences are excluded.

statement: Every pointed smooth plane quartic over $\mathbf F_5$ has a normalized representative of precisely one of the following three types. Write $u,v$ for the coefficients of $X^4,X^3Y$, respectively, and retain the notation of A.72 for the other coefficients: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{Contact}&\text{Fixed coefficients} &\text{Free}&\text{Weight}\\ \hline 2&a=1,\ b=c=d=0&8&2\\ 3&a=0,\ d=1,\ b=c=e=0&7&3\\ 4&a=d=0,\ u=1,\ b=c=v=0&6&4. \end{array} \] In a row of weight $w$, two normalized forms are pointed isomorphic exactly when related by $(X,Y,Z)\mapsto(AX,A^wY,Z)$ with $A\in\mathbf F_5^\times$, followed by division by $A^w$. Thus $5^8+5^7+5^6=484375$ forms, each under a group of order four, give an exhaustive census. The exact geometric smoothness test of A.72 gives $94283$ smooth pointed isomorphism classes, corresponding to $187512000$ of the original $5^{12}$ normalized coefficient forms.

statement: For all $94283$ pointed smooth plane-quartic isomorphism classes over $\mathbf F_5$, the program \path{code/plane_quartic_F5.cpp} computes every constant odd-prime cyclic pointed test over the base field. There are $134422$ such quotient tests, and their exact cyclotomic $L$-polynomials are retained, including failures. A successful base-field witness exists for $89906$ classes; $4377$ classes have no such base-field witness. For $39917$ classes a degree-three witness succeeds. Consequently three is their least admissible odd prime over all finite extensions. The all-extension least prime for each of the other $54366$ classes remains undetermined by this calculation, even when its base-field table has a larger successful prime.
notes: Working identifier AG.26. Proved by exact computation; every pointed plane quartic over $\mathbf F_5$ Proof-scope references. Internal premises independently audited; forward consequences are excluded.

statement: Let $C/\overline{\mathbf F}_2$ have genus two and let $n>1$ be odd. Put \[ U_n=\langle2,-1\rangle\subset(\mathbf Z/n)^\times, \qquad r_n=\frac{2\varphi(n)}{|U_n|}. \] If a connected cyclic etale degree-$n$ cover of $C$ has primitive conductor-$n$ factor of two-rank zero, then \[ r_n(r_n-1)\le2(n-1). \tag{A.75.1} \] If $C$ is nonordinary, the stronger necessary condition is \[ r_n(r_n+1)\le2(n-1). \tag{A.75.2} \] Consequently degree $127$ and degree $257$ cannot have primitive new two-rank zero for any genus-two base in characteristic two. More generally, no degree $n=2^d-1$ with $d\ge48$ can have this property. These restrictions concern geometric two-rank, and assert no corresponding exclusion of the rational class-number criterion. They also do not exclude the possibility that every curve admits some other degree as in A6.
notes: Working identifier AG.27. Proved; universal degree obstructions for geometric primitive vanishing Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $L=\mathbf F_q$ have characteristic $p$, let $C/L$ be smooth proper and geometrically connected with $g(C)\ge2$, and let $P\in C(L)$. Let $\pi:D\to C$ be a connected finite etale Galois cover with constant group of order $m$ prime to $p$, and choose $P'\in D(L)$ over $P$. Write $p^e$ for the exponent of $J_D(L)[p^\infty]$, with $p^e=1$ when this group is zero. If \[ (q-1)p^e<2(m-1), \tag{A.76.1} \] then $P$ collides with no other point of $C(L)$. The group need not be nonabelian, and its order need not be odd. More precisely, any collision forces \[ \operatorname{ord}[Q'-P']\ge\frac{2(m-1)}{q-1} \] for the rational lifts given by the collision. Consequently, a tower of constant pointed prime-to-$p$ Galois covers over one fixed $L$, of degrees $m_i\to\infty$ and rational $p$-primary exponents $b_i=o(m_i)$, would exclude every collision with $P$. Existence of such a tower for every pointed curve is not established here.
notes: Working identifier AG.28. Proved; a linear rational-exponent criterion at a fixed field Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $D\to C$ be a constant pointed cyclic etale cover of prime degree $\ell\ne p$ over $L=\mathbf F_q$, with $g(C)\ge2$. Put \[ h=\#J_C(L),\quad h_{\rm rel}=\#J_D(L)/h, \quad f=\operatorname{ord}_\ell(p),\quad v=v_p(h_{\rm rel}). \] Choose a faithful character $\chi$ and write $a=L_P(\chi,1)\in\mathbf Z[\zeta_\ell]$ as a polynomial in $\zeta_\ell$. Let $b$ be the degree of its gcd with $\Phi_\ell$ modulo $p$. Define \[ t=\begin{cases} 0,&v=0,\\ 1+(v-b)/f,&v>0. \end{cases} \qquad B=p^{\max\{v_p(h),t\}}. \tag{A.77.1} \] Then $t$ is a nonnegative integer and \[ \exp J_D(L)[p^\infty]\mid B. \] Consequently $(q-1)B<2(\ell-1)$ is a sufficient no-collision criterion at $P$ by A.76. The weaker bound with $t=v/f$ is valid as well. Applying this bound to the complete, already certified quartic polynomials and integer norms of A.72 and A.74 gives the following exact base-field conclusions: \[ \begin{array}{c|r|r|r|r} q&\text{Pointed classes}&\text{L1 successes} &\text{Additional successes}&\text{Total certified}\\ \hline 3&3001&2368&33&2401\\ 5&94283&89906&123&90029. \end{array} \] Every additional class has failed every base-field constant odd-prime L1 test, yet has a successful exponent certificate. There are $52$ individual covers over $\mathbf F_3$ and $272$ over $\mathbf F_5$ which fail L1 and satisfy this exponent criterion. This is a strict enlargement of the verified sufficient tests over the fixed base field. It makes no assertion that those pointed curves lack an L1 witness after extension.
notes: Working identifier AG.29. Proved; cyclotomic exponent bounds and further quartic certificates Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $\Omega$ be algebraically closed, let $D/\Omega$ be a smooth proper curve of genus at least two, let $A$ be an abelian surface, and let $u:A\to A'$ be an isogeny with a nonzero point in its geometric kernel. For every morphism $\phi:D\to A$, the composite $u\phi$ fails to be injective on geometric points. In particular, if $A=E_1\times E_2$ is a product of ordinary elliptic curves in characteristic two, then no joint map \[ D\longrightarrow E_1\times E_2 \xrightarrow{[2^{e_1}]\times[2^{e_2}]} E_1\times E_2, \qquad e_1,e_2\ge1, \] is geometrically point-separating. Thus replacing each of two ordinary elliptic targets by multiplication by its rational two-primary exponent cannot supply a geometrically point-separating family for L6. This does not exclude separation on rational points over a specified finite field: the geometric intersection points in the proof may only appear after extension, when the rational exponents themselves can increase.
notes: Working identifier AG.30. Proved; the geometric limitation of two ordinary elliptic targets Proof-scope references.

statement: There is a finite odd solvable group $G$, a finite $\mathbf F_2[G]$-module $V$, and an automorphism $F$ of $V$ semilinear for an automorphism of $G$, such that \[ (V^H)^F\supsetneq(V^K)^F \quad\text{for every proper inclusion }H<K \text{ of normal subgroups of }G, \] but no $F$-fixed vector has trivial $G$-stabilizer. Thus the constant-deck simultaneous-vector assertion cannot be extended to nonconstant Frobenius using only these normal-chain tests, even if they are imposed over every finite constant-field extension. This is an abstract module counterexample, without a claim that the module is realized by a curve or its Jacobian.
notes: Working identifier AG.31. Proved; a limit of normal-chain tests with nonconstant deck Frobenius Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $C/\mathbf F_{2^{2r}}$ be a genus-two curve with two-rank zero, with rational Weierstrass point $P$, and suppose Jacobian Frobenius is $[\varepsilon2^r]$, where $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$. If a nontrivial connected cyclic \'etale cover of odd degree $n$ has primitive part of two-rank zero, put \[ f=\operatorname{ord}_n(2),\qquad d=\gcd(f,r),\qquad M=\frac{\varphi(n)}d. \] Then \[ M(M+1)\le 2(n-1),\qquad n<10r^3. \tag{A.80.1} \] Consequently the geometric primitive-cover question for this fixed scalar-Frobenius curve has only finitely many possible conductors, with the displayed explicit bound.
notes: Working identifier AG.32. Proved; an effective conductor bound in the scalar supersingular case Proof-scope references.

statement: There are supersingular genus-two curves over $\mathbf F_{2^{128}}$ for which every nontrivial connected cyclic \'etale cover of odd degree has primitive part of positive two-rank. Thus the version of the existence statement A6 requiring degree $n>1$ is false, already for genus two in characteristic two. A completely specified family containing these examples is \[ C_t:\qquad y^2+y= \left(\frac{u^2+t^2u+t}{t^3+1}\right)^3, \qquad t\in\mathbf F_{2^{128}}\setminus\mathbf F_4, \tag{A.81.1} \] where $C_t$ means the smooth proper model. The proof gives an explicit finite incidence set of excluded parameters and a positive exact lower bound for its complement. The program certifies this nonemptiness and the displayed algebraic identities; it does not claim to have enumerated one particular parameter in the complement. All these curves themselves satisfy A1: their Jacobians have geometric two-rank zero. The refutation concerns existence of nontrivial primitive-zero covers, and gives no counterexample to A1 or to the arithmetic criterion A3. The prompt does not explicitly require $n>1$. With its convention $P_1=J_C$, the identity cover is a witness for every curve constructed here. Therefore these examples do not refute the literal degree-one-permitted version of A6; that version remains open for curves of positive $p$-rank.
notes: Working identifier AG.33. Refuted: universal nontrivial primitive-cover existence Proof-scope references. External citations: AG_MoretBailly1979

statement: Consider the fixed smooth elliptic family over the multiplicative group \[ \mathcal E\longrightarrow\mathbf G_{m,\mathbf F_4}, \qquad E_a:\ y^2+xy=x^3+a. \tag{A.83.1} \] For every positive odd integer $m$, there is a closed parameter $a$ of exact degree $m$ over $\mathbf F_4$ such that \[ \#E_a(\mathbf F_{4^m})=4^m, \qquad E_a(\mathbf F_{4^m})\simeq\mathbf Z/2^{2m}\mathbf Z. \tag{A.83.2} \] If $\beta_a\in\mathbf Z_2^\times$ is its unit-root Frobenius eigenvalue, then \[ \beta_a^2-\beta_a+4^m=0, \qquad v_2(\beta_a-1)=2m. \tag{A.83.3} \] The parameter is a point of odd order in $\mathbf G_m(\overline{\mathbf F}_2)$, and its Teichmuller lift is prime-to-two torsion. Thus a single fixed geometric family, ordinary fibers, integral cohomology of Weil weight one, and prime-to-two Frobenius periods do not give a uniform bound for the return unit minus one, even at prime-to-two torsion parameters. The assertion does not put these parameters in the powers of one fixed odd prime, and does not identify this family with the Abel tower of A.107. Those restrictions remain essential unresolved inputs to that route.
notes: Working identifier AG.35. Proved: geometric origin alone does not bound unit-root returns Proof-scope references. External citations: AG_AuerTop2002, AG_Waterhouse1969

statement: For each \(n\geq1\), choose a primitive \(3^n\)-th root \(a_n\in\overline{\mathbb F}_2\), and put \[ d_n=2\cdot3^{n-1},\qquad k_n=\mathbb F_{2^{d_n}},\qquad E_n:\ y^2+xy=x^3+a_n. \tag{A.84.1} \] Let \(\beta_n\in\mathbb Z_2^\times\) be the unit root of \(X^2-t_nX+2^{d_n}\), where \(t_n\) is the Frobenius trace of \(E_n/k_n\). Then \[ \lim_{n\to\infty}v_2(\beta_n-1)=+\infty, \qquad \exp E_n(k_n)[2^\infty]=2^{v_2(\beta_n-1)}. \tag{A.84.2} \] Every \(E_n\) is a fibre of the single smooth ordinary elliptic family \(y^2+xy=x^3+a\) over \(\mathbb G_{m,\mathbb F_2}\). The parameter \(a_n\) has exact degree \(3^{n-1}\) over \(\mathbb F_4\), an odd degree, and has exact multiplicative order \(3^n\). Thus a fixed geometric family, weight-one Weil purity, integrality, ordinariness, a fixed prime-power torsion sequence, and bounded \(2\)-part of the parameter degrees do not imply a uniform bound for the return valuations. The conclusion asserts divergence, without a quantitative comparison between \(2^{v_2(\beta_n-1)}\) and a prescribed power of \(3^n\). It neither identifies this family with the relative factors of an Abel tower nor disproves the weaker polynomial growth bound required by that route.
notes: Working identifier AG.36. Proved Proof-scope references. External citations: AG_KostersWan2016, AG_Sekiguchi2001

statement: For every member \(C_t\) of the explicit family in Claim~A.81 over \(\mathbb F_{2^{38}}\), any nontrivial odd conductor of a primitive two-rank-zero cyclic cover belongs to \[ \{191,229,457,1257\}. \tag{A.85.1} \] More precisely, its theta curve has no point of exact order \(361,419,571,573,647,687,955,1083\), or \(1371\). This assertion is a necessary-condition reduction; it does not select an individual parameter from the nonempty complement in Claim~A.82.

statement: Let \[ \begin{split} M(Z)&=Z^{38}+Z^{14}+Z^{10}+Z^9+Z^8+Z^5+Z^2+Z+1,\\ k&=\mathbb F_2[Z]/(M(Z)),\qquad t=Z\bmod M(Z), \qquad d=t^3+1. \end{split} \tag{A.86.1} \] The polynomial \(M\) is irreducible. Let \(C/k\) be the smooth projective model of the affine equation \[ y^2+y=\left(\frac{u^2+t^2u+t}{d}\right)^3, \tag{A.86.2} \] and let \(P\) be its unique point at infinity. This is a supersingular genus-two curve, with \(P\in C(k)\). For every connected cyclic etale cover \(D\to C_{\bar k}\) of odd degree \(n>1\), and every generator \(\sigma\) of its deck group, the abelian subvariety \[ P_n(D)=\operatorname{im}\left( \prod_{\ell\mid n}(1-\sigma^{n/\ell}):J_D\longrightarrow J_D \right) \] has positive two-rank. Thus the nontrivial-cover version of A6 is false for this completely specified curve, independently of the counting existence argument. The degree-one qualification is essential: \(J_C\) has two-rank zero, so the identity cover satisfies the literal variant that permits \(n=1\). The example also satisfies A1 and is not a collision or a counterexample to A1.
notes: Working identifier AG.38. Refuted, with an explicit finite counterexample: nontrivial primitive-cover existence Proof-scope references.

statement: Let \(C\) be a smooth proper connected complex curve of genus \(g\geq2\), let \(P\in C\), and put \[ U=\{(x,z)\in C\times C:x\ne z\},\qquad F=C-\{P\}. \] Use the second projection \(U\to C\) to identify \(F\) with a fiber. For every prime \(p\), write \(\Gamma^{(p')}\) for the inverse limit of the finite quotients of a group \(\Gamma\) whose orders are prime to \(p\). Then \[ \pi_1(F)^{(p')}\longrightarrow \pi_1(U)^{(p')} \tag{A.87.1} \] is not injective. The same assertion holds for the geometric prime-to-\(p\) etale fundamental groups of every smooth proper curve of genus at least two in characteristic \(p\). In particular it holds for the smooth projective model of \[ C_0/\mathbb F_2:\quad y^2+y=x^5, \qquad P=\infty. \tag{A.87.2} \] This refutes the full prime-to-\(p\) configuration exactness condition proposed as a sufficient route in \cite[Remark 3.13]{AR_ST2009}. It does not supply two coincident point sections and does not refute A1. The proof specifies a finite curve and finite branched-cover construction; it does not enumerate a particular nonidentity profinite kernel element or an individual finite monodromy matrix witnessing the failure.
notes: Working identifier AG.39. Proved: the full prime-to-\(p\) configuration fiber does not inject Proof-scope references.
