statement: Let \(k\) be a finite field of characteristic \(p\), let \(C/k\) be smooth, proper and geometrically connected of genus at least two, and let \(P,Q\in C(k)\). Write \(\Pi_C\) for the arithmetic fundamental group with maximal geometrically prime-to-\(p\) quotient. Fix a prime \(r\ne p\). Let \(G_P\) and \(G_Q\) be the maximal cuspidally pro-\(r\) quotients of the corresponding arithmetic prime-to-\(p\) groups of \(C-P\) and \(C-Q\), relative to their maps to \(\Pi_C\). Suppose there is a continuous isomorphism \[ \beta:G_P\xrightarrow{\sim}G_Q \] over \(\operatorname{id}_{\Pi_C}\) which carries the cuspidal decomposition group at \(P\) to a conjugate of the cuspidal decomposition group at \(Q\). Then \(P=Q\). The isomorphism is in particular over the identity of \(G_k\), so it preserves arithmetic Frobenius.
notes: Working identifier AG.40. Proved: a conditional cuspidal separation criterion Proof-scope references. Internal premises independently audited; forward consequences are excluded. External citations: AR_SGA1, AR_ST2009

statement: Let \(p\) and \(r\) be distinct primes. Let \(C\) be a smooth proper connected complex curve of genus at least two, let \(x\in C\), and set \[ U=(C\times C)-\Delta_C,\qquad V=C-\{x\},\qquad \Delta=\pi_1(C)^{(p')},\quad F=\pi_1(V)^{(p')},\quad E=\pi_1(U)^{(p')}. \tag{A.89.1} \] The fiber embedding uses the second projection \(U\to C\). Define \[ \begin{aligned} K_F&=\ker(F\to\Delta), &K_E&=\ker(E\to\Delta\times\Delta),\\ F_{\mathrm{c}r}&=F/\ker(K_F\to K_F^{(r)}), &E_{\mathrm{c}r}&=E/\ker(K_E\to K_E^{(r)}). \end{aligned} \tag{A.89.2} \] Then the fiber map induces an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow F_{\mathrm{c}r} \longrightarrow E_{\mathrm{c}r} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}\Delta\longrightarrow1. \tag{A.89.3} \] The same statement holds for geometric etale prime-to-\(p\) groups over every algebraically closed field of characteristic \(p\), with the corresponding characteristic relative quotients. More precisely, every finite quotient of \(F_{\mathrm{c}r}\) is dominated, on the fiber, by a finite quotient of \(E_{\mathrm{c}r}\). The finite quotient of the total group can be chosen to have a normal \(r\)-subgroup whose quotient is a finite prime-to-\(p\) quotient of \(\Delta\times\Delta\).
notes: Working identifier AG.41. Proved: fixed-prime cuspidal configuration exactness Proof-scope references. Internal premises independently audited; forward consequences are excluded. External citations: AR_SGA1, FF_KochloukovaZalesskii2011

statement: There is a diagonal boundary decomposition subgroup \(\mathcal D\subset\mathcal E_{\mathrm{c}r}\) with an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_r(1)\longrightarrow\mathcal D \longrightarrow\Pi_C\longrightarrow1, \tag{A.90.1} \] whose map to the proper product is the diagonal map on the last term. For every rational point \(P\), choose compatible geometric paths through this boundary and put \(D_P=s_P(G_k)\subset\Pi_C\) and \(\mathcal E_P=\mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(D_P)\). The fixed-\(r\) configuration theorem identifies \(\mathcal E_P\) with the arithmetic cuspidally pro-\(r\) group of \(C-P\), and under this identification its puncture decomposition group is \[ \mathcal D\cap\mathcal E_P. \tag{A.90.2} \] If two rational points \(P,Q\) have geometrically conjugate proper sections in \(\Pi_C\), there is an isomorphism between the actual cuspidally pro-\(r\) groups of \(C-P\) and \(C-Q\), over the identity of \(\Pi_C\), which carries the first puncture decomposition group to a conjugate of the second. Consequently \(P=Q\): rational point sections of the full proper geometrically prime-to-\(p\) fundamental group are injective up to geometric conjugacy.
notes: Working identifier AG.42. Proved: diagonal boundary and cuspidal transport Proof-scope references. Internal premises independently audited; forward consequences are excluded. External citations: AR_SGA1

statement: For $q=4,8,16$, the supplied programs enumerate every $\mathbf F_q$-isomorphism class of smooth proper genus-two curves, every rational point of each, and every prime-order constant-deck pointed cyclic cover over $L=\mathbf F_q$, up to automorphism of its cyclic deck group. The exact twisted $L$-polynomial and its relative class number modulo two are recorded for every test. The totals are \[ \begin{array}{c|r|r|r|r} q&\text{curve classes}&\text{pointed pairs}&\text{tests}& \text{pairs with a base-field witness}\\\hline 4&146&730&968&613\\ 8&1094&9846&14854&8978\\ 16&8470&143990&263765&138769 \end{array} \] These are all tests over the displayed base field. For pairs without a proved least-prime result, the output makes no assertion of a least prime over arbitrary extensions. This is the ``list of all tests tried'' alternative in A4 for these three genus-two censuses.

statement: Let $\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0$, and let $C_{203}/\mathbf F_4$ have equation \[ Y^2+(z^2+z+\alpha)Y =(z^2+z+\alpha)(z^3+z^2+z+\alpha^2). \] Let $C_{302}$ be its coefficientwise square. In the complete pointed censuses, the numbers are \[ \begin{array}{c|r|r|r} q&\text{original pairs}&\text{least prime is }3& \text{no cubic witness over any extension}\\\hline 4&730&264&466\\ 8&9846&3240&6606\\ 16&143990&40284&103706. \end{array} \] For $q=4$, explicit characters and full twisted polynomials are retained for all $264$ positive pairs, over $\mathbf F_4$, $\mathbf F_{16}$ or $\mathbf F_{256}$. The complete consolidated table is \path{code/A4_quartic_witnesses.csv}. statement: Let $C/k$ be proper hyperbolic over a finite field, and put $\Sigma=\{\ell:\ell\ne p\}$. On the universal geometrically pro-$\Sigma$ covering, let $\widetilde E_C$ consist of points whose decomposition subgroup is commensurate with that of another point; let $E_C$ be its image in the set of closed points of $C$. The following are the statements supplied by the two papers. \begin{enumerate} \item In \cite[Definition~1.5, Lemma~1.7, Proposition~1.8(iii)--(vii), Definition~1.10 and Corollary~1.11]{AR_ST2009}, the commensurability map is injective above a fixed geometric point, is injective above a rational point, has finite fibres, and has finite exceptional image $E_C$ when $\Sigma$ is cofinite. Decomposition subgroups of closed points are recovered injectively outside $E_C$. \item For a $\Sigma$-covering $f:C'\to C$, \cite[Proposition~2.11]{AR_ST2017} proves $E_{C'}=f^{-1}(E_C)$ if $f$ is \'etale. If $f$ is tame Galois, it proves $E_{C'}\subset f^{-1}(E_C)\cup R_f$, where $R_f$ is the non-\'etale locus. \item With $J_C$-largeness as defined in that paper, \cite[Proposition~2.12]{AR_ST2017} places the exceptional points over a proper subfield $F\subset\bar k$, finite of degree at most two over $F_0=\bar k^{\ker\rho_{J_C,\Sigma'}}$. The degree is at most one when $C$ is nonhyperelliptic. Proposition~2.13 gives a prime $\ell$ and finiteness of the exceptional points rational over each finite extension of the unique $\mathbf Z_\ell$-extension of $k$; the precise hypothesis is almost $\Sigma$-separatedness, with the stated $J_C$-large refinements on the choice of $\ell$. \end{enumerate} These results do not assert $E_C=\varnothing$.
notes: Working identifier AR.8. Known, checked; the exact Sa\"idi--Tamagawa statement Proof-scope references. External citations: AR_ST2009, AR_ST2017

statement: For a fixed proper hyperbolic $C/k$, absence of collisions after \emph{every} finite constant extension is equivalent to $E_C$ being empty. Universal A1 is therefore equivalent to emptiness of all these exceptional sets. Absence of collisions only among $C(k)$ is the weaker assertion that no two distinct rational-point decomposition sections become geometrically conjugate at that field. By A.3 all these exceptional sets are empty for $\Sigma=\{\ell:\ell\ne p\}$. This last conclusion is a consequence of the proof in the present return, not an assertion attributed to either of the cited papers.
notes: Working identifier AR.9. Proved; A1 in the exceptional-set language Proof-scope references.

statement: Let $F,K$ be fields finitely generated over $\mathbf F_p$. Let $E_F^{(p')}$ and $E_K^{(p')}$ denote their absolute Galois groupoids with the kernel over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ replaced by its maximal prime-to-$p$ quotient, retaining the maps to $BG_{\mathbf F_p}$. If two $\mathbf F_p$-embeddings $u,v:F\hookrightarrow K$ induce isomorphic morphisms of these groupoids \emph{over} $BG_{\mathbf F_p}$, including the specified relative commutation isomorphisms, then $u=v$. Thus the margin in cote~149, scan~36, concerning Th\'eor\`eme~2 (scan~22), has a correct proof using the genus-zero target $\mathbf G_m$ and its products. This assertion does not settle A1 for proper curves.

statement: Fix $C/k$ and $P\in C(k)$. Over $\bar k$, take all finite connected Galois prime-to-$p$ covers $D_N\to C_{\bar k}$ indexed by open normal subgroups $N\triangleleft\Pi_C$, with compatible lifts $P_N$. There is a well-defined module \[ M_P=\varprojlim_N J_{D_N}(\bar k)[p^\infty] \quad\text{under norm}, \qquad \mathbf Z_p[[\Pi_C]]\times M_P\longrightarrow M_P. \] Arithmetic Frobenius acts semilinearly: if $\alpha$ is its action on $\Pi_C$, then $F(am)=\alpha(a)F(m)$. It need not commute with the deck action. The module itself need not be a torsion group of bounded exponent, although each coordinate is $p$-primary torsion. If $P,Q,R$ have equal point-section classes, their compatible lifted differences satisfy $T_{PR}=T_{PQ}+T_{QR}$ in this same based module. The formula is canonical after choosing the compatible based tower; independently based towers require their path identification first.

statement: A collision of $P\ne Q$ gives a nonzero $F$-fixed vector $T_{PQ}\in M_P$ whose coordinate at every level is a nonzero point difference. Every odd-order geometric deck group acts freely on that coordinate. In characteristic two this covers every level. In odd characteristic the same conclusion for all prime-to-$p$ levels follows using the independently established hyperelliptic case of R4. The converse from an arbitrary free-orbit vector in $M_P$ is not proved: the coordinate must come from actual points, compatibly.

statement: Let $D\to C_{k_m}$ be a geometrically Galois prime-to-$p$ cover with a chosen rational lift of $P$. The projection of $M_P^F$ to its Jacobian is contained in $J_D(k_m)[p^\infty]$. Every homomorphism $h:J_D\to B$ defined over $k_m$ with $B(k_m)[p]=0$ kills that projection. If $D$ is a nontrivial odd-degree L1 witness, its deck group fixes the projection of every element of $M_P^F$. Consequently $M_P^F$ has no element with free deck orbit at \emph{every} level whenever there is an L1 witness for $(C,P)$ over any finite extension. In particular this nonexistence assertion holds for every original $\mathbf F_4$-rational point on every genus-two curve over $\mathbf F_4$, by A.91--A.93. The first requested classes $203$ and $302$ already follow from the degree-seven witnesses of A.92 and A.20.

statement: Let $L$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $C/L$ be smooth, proper and geometrically connected with $g(C)\ge2$, and let $P\in C(L)$. Let $\pi:D\to C$ be a connected finite etale Galois cover with constant nonabelian group $G$ of order $m$ prime to $p$, and choose $P'\in D(L)$ above $P$. The group \[ H=J_D(L)[p^\infty] \] is a finite $\mathbf Z[G]$-module, with the action induced by the $L$-automorphisms of $D$. Suppose a nonzero element $a=\sum_g a_g g\in\mathbf Z[G]$ annihilates $H$, and put $d=\sum_g|a_g|$. If \[ (d,m)=1,\qquad m>(d-1)^2, \] then $P$ collides with no other point of $C(L)$ in the full geometrically prime-to-$p$ arithmetic fundamental group. In particular, if $p^e$ is the exponent of $H$, with $p^e=1$ when $H=0$, it suffices that \[ m>(p^e-1)^2. \tag{A.104.1} \] For characteristic two, a constant pointed nonabelian cover of degree $21$ meets this condition whenever its rational two-primary Jacobian group has exponent at most four.

statement: Let $C/k$ be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite field of characteristic two, and let $P\in C(k)$. Use the full geometrically prime-to-two group and the pointed norm module $M_P$ of A.100. Consider the following three conditions. \begin{enumerate} \item There are a finite extension $L/k$ and compatible pointed finite etale covers $Z\to Y\to C_L$ such that both $Z$ and $Y$ are geometrically Galois of odd degree over $C$, the relative cover $Z\to Y$ is nontrivial and Galois, and $2\nmid h_L(Z)/h_L(Y)$. \item The module $M_P^F$ has no nonzero element whose projection has a free geometric deck orbit at every normal level. \item There are a finite extension $L/k$, a pointed geometrically Galois odd-degree cover $Y\to C_L$, and a pointed cyclic cover $Z\to Y$ of odd prime degree with constant deck group over $L$, such that $Z\to C_L$ has geometric Galois closure of odd degree and $2\nmid h_L(Z)/h_L(Y)$. \end{enumerate} Then condition~1 implies condition~2, and condition~2 implies condition~3. The source $Z$ in condition~3 is not asserted to be normal over $C$. More precisely, if condition~3 fails, then $M_P^F$ contains a nonzero element killed by two with free deck orbit at every normal level. Such an element is not asserted to arise from points of $C$ or of its covers. This is a statement about the entire inverse limit, not just finitely many quotients.

statement: In A.53, its conclusion holds whenever the prime-to-$p$ group $G$ cannot be generated by two elements as an abelian group. More explicitly, it holds if $G$ is nonabelian, or if $G$ is abelian and some Sylow subgroup needs at least three generators. Under the same group hypothesis, the rational annihilator criterion A.104 holds with no change in its field, pointing, or numerical conditions. For a scalar annihilator $p^e\cdot1$, it is enough that the cover is geometrically Galois, with all other data and the chosen lift defined over $L$; rational deck transformations are unnecessary.

statement: Let $C/k$ be smooth, proper and geometrically connected, where $k=\mathbf F_q$ has characteristic $p$, let $g(C)=g\ge2$, and let $P\in C(k)$. Fix an odd prime $\ell\ne p$. Write $J=J_C$ and let $j_P:C\to J$ be the Abel morphism $x\mapsto[x-P]$. For $n\ge1$ form the fibre product over $k$ \[ D_n=C\mathbin{\times}_{J,[\ell^n]}J, \qquad \pi_n:D_n\longrightarrow C. \tag{A.107.1} \] This is a geometrically connected finite etale cover of degree $\ell^{2gn}$, pointed by $(P,0)$. Let $m_n$ be the order of arithmetic Frobenius on $J[\ell^n]$, put $L_n=\mathbf F_{q^{m_n}}$, and let $E_n$ be the exponent of the finite group $J_{D_n}(k)[p^\infty]$, with exponent one for the zero group. If for one $n$ \[ E_n-1<\ell^{gn}, \tag{A.107.2} \] then $P$ collides with no other point of $C(k)$ in the full geometrically prime-to-$p$ arithmetic group. In particular an estimate $E_n=o(\ell^{gn})$ would suffice for this $(C,P,\ell)$. There is an integer $t\ge1$ such that \[ m_n=m_1\ell^{\max(0,n-t)}\quad(n\ge1). \tag{A.107.3} \] Consequently the exponents of $J(L_n)[p^\infty]$ are uniformly bounded. This last bound concerns the base Jacobian only; no bound for the relative parts of $J_{D_n}$, and hence no universal instance of (A.107.2), is asserted here. If $E_n^{\rm const}$ is the exponent over the constant-deck field $L_n$, then $E_n\mid E_n^{\rm const}$, so the analogous bound over $L_n$ would also suffice, but that field enlargement is unnecessary for the scalar criterion.

statement: Let \(k\) have characteristic zero and let \(X/k\) be a finite-type scheme. The isomorphism classes of relative geometric morphisms \(BG_k\to X_{\mathrm{et}}\) are the disjoint union, over the points \(x\in X\), of the continuous sections of \[ G_{k(x)}\longrightarrow G_k, \] modulo conjugation by its kernel, with compatible separable closures understood. A point for which the displayed map is not surjective contributes no section. The closed-point summands are exactly \(X(k)\). In particular, for an integral curve the other summand is the set of birational sections at its generic point. Consequently, for every characteristic-zero field the assertion in cote~149, scan~52, read with \emph{all} relative topos morphisms, is false, even with universal homeomorphisms inverted.

statement: Let \(k/\mathbb Q\) be finitely generated and \(K/k\) a regular one-variable function field. Under conjecture~a) in cote~149, scans~126--127, each section \(G_k\to G_K\) factors through a decomposition group \(D_v\) of a nontrivial valuation trivial on \(k\), with residue field finite over \(k\). For an actual section over \(G_k\), that residue field is \(k\) itself. Its centre lies on the smooth proper model of \(K/k\), and need not lie on a specified open curve with that function field.

statement: Let \(K_0\) be a number field and \(X/K_0\) a smooth proper geometrically connected curve, with \(K=K_0(X)\). Every continuous outer automorphism of \(G_K\) over \(G_{K_0}\), modulo inner conjugation by the geometric kernel, is induced by a unique \(K_0\)-automorphism of \(X\). Preservation of the closed-point inertia and decomposition groups is a consequence, and need not be assumed. In particular the experiment in cote~149, scan~52, has a positive answer for the genus at least two curves asked about.

statement: There is an explicit henselian field \(K/\mathbb Q\) of transcendence degree two, residue characteristic zero and transcendence defect one which fails reconstruction. Namely, in \(\overline{\mathbb Q}((t))\) put \[ u=\sum_{n\geq1}t^{n!},\qquad K=\overline{\mathbb Q}(t,u)^h \] for the induced \(t\)-adic valuation and its henselization inside that complete field. Then \[ \kappa(K)=\overline{\mathbb Q},\qquad v(K^\times)=\mathbb Z,\qquad G_K\simeq\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \tag{F.17.1} \] The transcendence degree two is the smallest possible finite transcendence degree for a nontrivial residue-characteristic-zero valuation with positive transcendence defect.

statement: The following sufficient direction of candidate F3(a) remains unproved and unrefuted in this work: \[ \bigl[C_{\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k)}(G_E)=1 \text{ for every finite }E/k\bigr] \quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal R(k). \tag{F.18.1} \] Nor have we decided every finite-transcendence-degree henselian field with residue characteristic zero and transcendence defect. In particular our arguments do not decide \[ K_* = \mathbb Q\bigl(t,\sum_{n\geq1}t^{n!}\bigr)^h \subset\mathbb Q((t)), \tag{F.18.2} \] with its induced valuation. This is a specified unresolved test, not a claim that it is the least field under inclusion or that its centralizers satisfy (F.18.1). The general mixed-residue-characteristic case is also not classified. A previously unresolved degree-zero test was \[ K_p=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb Z_{(p)}^{sh}), \tag{F.18.3} \] with a chosen strict henselization inside \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\). Its reconstruction is now proved in Claim~\ref{clm:FFstrictreconstruct}, and Claim~\ref{clm:FFdiscretealgebraic} treats every algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\) admitting a mixed-characteristic discrete valuation. These conclusions do not classify arbitrary nondiscrete valuations or all finite-transcendence-degree mixed-characteristic henselian fields. Claims~\ref{clm:FFtamereconstruct}--\ref{clm:FFpadicsubfields} further settle bounded wild ramification. The next specified degree-zero test \(U_5=T_5(\mu_{5^\infty})\) from Claim~\ref{clm:FFcyclotomictest} is also settled positively by Claim~\ref{clm:FFcyclotomicreconstruct}, despite the detector failure in Claim~\ref{clm:FFcyclotomicdetector}. Claims~\ref{clm:FFmaxabelianreconstruct} and \ref{clm:FFnilpotentreconstruct} further settle the maximal abelian and each fixed bounded-nilpotency extension. A remaining specified degree-zero test is the maximal metabelian field \(B_2\) of Claim~\ref{clm:FFmetabeliantest}, which has the centralizer condition over every finite extension. Its reconstruction is not decided. Claims~\ref{clm:FFmetabelianaffine}--\ref{clm:FFhighergenusnorm} subsequently determine affine automorphism point functions, all abelian generic actions on rational and elliptic Galois slices and on the specified genus-two slice, and the portion of the etale site generated by genus-zero covers. This includes all abelian covers of arbitrary genus, all Galois genus-one covers, and all degree-three genus-one covers. Arbitrary covers and noninvertible pinned maps remain unresolved.

statement: The following are sufficient conditions for \(\mathcal R(k_0)\), always in characteristic zero. \begin{enumerate} \item There is a finitely generated \(D/\mathbb Q\) with \(D\subset k_0\), \(k_0/D\) algebraic, and proper normal closure \(N\ne\bar D\) inside \(\bar D\). \item For some finitely generated \(D/\mathbb Q\), the field \(k_0\) is a subfield of a finitely generated extension of \(D^{\mathcal C}\). Here \(\mathcal C\) is a proper isomorphism-invariant class of finite groups, containing all cyclic groups and closed under subgroups, quotients and extensions; \(D^{\mathcal C}\) is the maximal Galois pro-\(\mathcal C\) extension. Equivalently, for some finitely generated \(D_0\subset k_0\), the extension \(k_0/D_0\) is algebraic and its normal-closure group is virtually pro-\(\mathcal C\). This includes AP-F.37 and AP-F.43 by taking \(\mathcal C\) to be the solvable groups, and AP-F.44 in general. \item The field \(k_0\) has positive transcendence degree over \(\mathbb Q\) and is a subfield of a finitely generated extension of \(K_0^{\mathcal C}\), where \(K_0/\overline{\mathbb Q}\) is finitely generated of positive transcendence degree. Equivalently, it is algebraic over some finitely generated \(D_0/\mathbb Q\) of positive transcendence degree whose normal closure \(N/D_0\) has \[ \operatorname{Gal} (N\overline{\mathbb Q}/D_0\overline{\mathbb Q}) \quad\hbox{virtually pro-}\mathcal C. \] This is AP-F.46. In particular every positive-transcendence subfield of a finitely generated extension of \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\) reconstructs, as in AP-F.45. \item In the setting of AP-F.49, let \(D/\mathbb Q\) be finitely generated of positive transcendence degree, and let \(k/D\) be algebraic Galois with \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\subset k\). If \(k\) is Hilbertian, every finitely generated \(L/k\) reconstructs. If instead \(\operatorname{Gal}(k/D\overline{\mathbb Q})\) is small, then also every positive-transcendence subfield \(k_0\subset L\) reconstructs. Small means finitely many open subgroups of each prescribed finite index. \end{enumerate} In (2) and (3), taking the union over \(\mathcal C\) is equivalent to requiring that an open subgroup of the respective normal-closure group have no finite quotient containing some fixed \(A_m\), \(m\ge5\), as a subquotient. These are sufficient classes and equivalences between their descriptions, not a necessary classification of all reconstruction fields. In particular (1) does not assert that arbitrary subfields of a reconstruction field reconstruct.
notes: Working identifier FF.21. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.9; F.10; F.11; Hilbertianity; Stacks 9.26.11. External citations: FF_BarySoroker2008, FF_BarySorokerParan2013, FF_Serre2007, FF_StacksFields

statement: The negative statements AP-F.39--F.42 and AP-F.47--F.48 have the following precise content. \begin{enumerate} \item Every characteristic-zero field with finite absolute Galois group fails \(\mathcal R\); in particular all algebraically closed and real closed fields fail. \item Let \(F\) have characteristic zero and equip \(F(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\), \(r\ge1\), with a monomial valuation whose positive parameter values are rationally independent. Its henselization \(H\), and every algebraic extension of \(H\), fails \(\mathcal R\). This includes every finite-transcendence-degree field over \(\mathbb Q\) with a nontrivial henselian valuation of residue characteristic zero satisfying the Abhyankar equality. \item For any characteristic-zero \(F\), put \[ P(F)=\bigcup_{n\ge1}F((t^{1/n})),\qquad A(F)=\{a\in P(F):a\text{ is algebraic over }F(t)\}, \] with compatible roots throughout. The fields \(F((t))\), \(P(F)\), \(A(F)\), and all their algebraic extensions fail \(\mathcal R\). There are topological isomorphisms \[ (G_{P(F)},\chi_{P(F)})\simeq(G_F,\chi_F),\qquad (G_{A(F)},\chi_{A(F)})\simeq(G_F,\chi_F), \] with the full cyclotomic characters, and \(\lvert A(F)\rvert=\max(\lvert F\rvert,\aleph_0)\). \end{enumerate} The explicit obstruction in (2) and (3) is the lift of \(t_1\mapsto t_1+t_1^2\), respectively \(t\mapsto t+t^2\), centralizing the full absolute Galois group. It gives an actual pinned relative automorphism of the full \(\mathbb G_m\) topos. These ghosts also violate the genus-zero Isom condition in candidate F3(b), already on the four-punctured lines with parameters \(t\) and \(t+t^2\); and they cannot satisfy coherent scalar descent in candidate F3(c). Thus all three candidates correctly exclude these particular ghosts, although candidate (b) is false by its opposite-direction failure in Claim~\ref{clm:F.7}.
notes: Working identifier FF.22. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.6; F.11; ADH 3.3.22; van den Dries--Ribenboim p.314. External citations: FF_ADH2017, FF_vanDenDriesRibenboim1984

statement: Fix a prime \(p\) and a prolongation of its valuation to \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\), and let \(K_p=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb Z_{(p)}^{sh})\) as in (F.18.3). It is countable, algebraic over \(\mathbb Q\), henselian discretely valued, with value group \(\mathbb Z\) and residue field \(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\). It satisfies candidate F3(a)'s centralizer condition over every finite extension and candidate F3(b)'s Isom condition for all hyperbolic curves over every finite extension. For every number field \(D\subset K_p\), its normal closure over \(D\) is \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\). It is not sub-\(q\)-adic for any prime \(q\), and is not a finite extension of a proper normal algebraic extension of a number field. Consequently it lies in none of the sufficient field classes stated in Claims~\ref{clm:F.4}, \ref{clm:FFnormal}, \ref{clm:FFfunction}, and \ref{clm:FFclasses}. Its centralizer condition excludes all the negative ghost classes in Claim~\ref{clm:FFghosts}. Thus it is a specified field on neither earlier list with the smallest possible cardinality and transcendence degree in characteristic zero. We claim no least field under inclusion. Claim~\ref{clm:FFstrictreconstruct} subsequently proves its reconstruction by a different argument.

statement: Fix a prime \(p\), and let \(K_p\) be the field of Claim~\ref{clm:FFstricttest}. \begin{enumerate} \item For every finite extension \(L/K_p\), \[ \bigcap_{n\geq1}(L^\times)^{p^n}=\mu_{p'}\subset K_p^\times, \tag{F.24.1} \] where \(\mu_{p'}\) denotes all roots of unity of order prime to \(p\). \item There is a connected nontrivial finite \'etale Galois cover of an elliptic curve over \(K_p\) whose pullback at every closed point is completely split. Thus the finite-quotient detection statement used in Claim~\ref{clm:FFcore} is false over \(K_p\). \item If \(X/K_p\) is of finite type and a pinned topos morphism \(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}\to \mathbb G_{m,K_p,\mathrm{\acute et}}\) has constant underlying closed-point function with value \(c\in\mathbb G_m(K_p)\), it factors through the closed subtopos \(c_{\mathrm{\acute et}}\). For an integral finite-type curve \(X\), every nonconstant underlying continuous point function has finite fibres over closed target points. \item Every field embedding \(K_p\hookrightarrow K_p\) is an automorphism. \end{enumerate} Consequently neither the invisible prime-to-\(p\) quotients in (2), a residue-tube point function, nor a proper self-embedding supplies a reconstruction counterexample.
notes: Working identifier FF.24. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.23; Hensel lemma; properness.

statement: Let \(K/K_p\) be finite, let \(A/K\) be a semiabelian variety, and put \(V_pA=T_pA\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p\). Every nonzero continuous \(G_K\)-equivariant linear map \[ \lambda:V_pA\longrightarrow\mathbb Q_p(1) \] is detected by a point: for some finite \(L/K\) and \(a\in A(L)\), \[ \lambda_*\kappa_A(a)\ne0 \quad\hbox{in }H^1(G_L,\mathbb Q_p(1)). \tag{F.25.1} \] If \(j:X\to A\) is a morphism based at \(x_0\in X(K)\), with \(j(x_0)=0\), from a geometrically integral finite-type \(K\)-scheme and \(j(X_{\bar K})\) generates \(A_{\bar K}\), the detecting points may be chosen in \(j(X(L))\). Finitely many such points, over one finite extension, jointly detect every member of \(\operatorname{Hom}_{G_K}(V_pA,\mathbb Q_p(1))\).
notes: Working identifier FF.25. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.24; SGA7 IX 3.6/5.6; Tate1967 Theorem4. External citations: FF_SGA7I1972, FF_Tate1967

statement: For every prime \(p\) and every finite extension \(K/\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb Z_{(p)}^{sh})\), the field \(K\) satisfies \(\mathcal R(K)\). Consequently every subfield of such a \(K\) reconstructs.

statement: Let \(F/\mathbb Q\) be algebraic. If \(F\) admits a nontrivial discrete valuation of residue characteristic \(p>0\), then \(\mathcal R(F)\) holds. More precisely, for any prolongation to \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\), the compositum \(FK_p\) is finite over the strict henselization field \(K_p\) attached to that prolongation. Thus the fields in this statement are exactly the subfields of finite extensions of some \(K_p\).
notes: Working identifier FF.27. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.25; F.26; F.11. External citations: FF_ADH2017, FF_StacksHensel

statement: Fix the prolongation of the \(p\)-adic valuation used to define \(K_p\), and set \[ T_p=K_p\bigl(p^{1/m}:(m,p)=1\bigr) \subset\overline{\mathbb Q}, \tag{F.28.1} \] with compatible roots. Every finite extension \(K/T_p\), and every subfield of such a \(K\), satisfies \(\mathcal R\). In particular the positive conclusion includes a henselian field with nondiscrete value group \(\mathbb Z_{(p)}\).
notes: Working identifier FF.28. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.24--26; F.11; Stacks 09EV/0EXW. External citations: FF_StacksRamification

statement: Let \(F/\mathbb Q\) be algebraic, and choose a \(p\)-adic place, normalized by \(v(p)=1\). Suppose that for some integer \(a\geq0\), \[ v(F^\times)\subset p^{-a}\mathbb Z_{(p)}. \tag{F.29.1} \] Then \(FT_p/T_p\) is finite, and \(\mathcal R(F)\) holds. Equivalently this condition says that the \(p\)-parts of the ramification indices of all finite number subfields, at the chosen place, are bounded. These fields are exactly the subfields of finite extensions of \(T_p\).
notes: Working identifier FF.29. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.28; F.11.

statement: Let \(F\subset\overline{\mathbb Q}_p\) be a field of finite transcendence degree over \(\mathbb Q\). Suppose that, for the induced valuation normalized by \(v(p)=1\), \[ v(F^\times)\subset p^{-a}\mathbb Z_{(p)} \quad\text{for some }a\geq0. \tag{F.30.1} \] Then \(\mathcal R(F)\) holds. In particular this applies when the induced valuation on \(F\) is discrete. No henselianity assumption is required.

statement: For every prime \(p\), put \[ U_p=T_p(\mu_{p^\infty}) \subset\overline{\mathbb Q}. \tag{F.31.1} \] This countable, transcendence-degree-zero field has henselian value group \(\mathbb Q\), residue field \(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\), and contains every root of unity. For every finite extension \(E/U_p\), \[ C_{\operatorname{Aut}(\overline{\mathbb Q})} (G_E)=1. \tag{F.31.2} \] It lies on none of the sufficient field lists preceding this claim, including the bounded-wild class, and none of the negative centralizer-ghost lists. Thus \(U_5\) was a specified next test with the smallest possible cardinality and transcendence degree in characteristic zero; no inclusion-minimality is claimed. Claim~\ref{clm:FFcyclotomicreconstruct} subsequently proves reconstruction for every finite extension of \(U_p\).
notes: Working identifier FF.31. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.6; F.23; F.28; Iwasawa1955 Theorem2(ii); Kochloukova--Zalesskii2011 Theorem5.1 CaseI. External citations: FF_Iwasawa1955, FF_KochloukovaZalesskii2011

statement: The functional-detection assertion of Claim~\ref{clm:FFpdetector} fails over the explicit field \(U_5\). More precisely there is an elliptic curve \(A/U_5\) and a nonzero \(G_{U_5}\)-equivariant functional \[ V_5A\longrightarrow\mathbb Q_5(1) \] whose push-forward of every point Kummer class, over every finite extension of \(U_5\), is zero. This is not a counterexample to \(\mathcal R(U_5)\).
notes: Working identifier FF.32. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.31; F.24; explicit CM endomorphism.

statement: Let \(K/U_p\) be finite. Then the integral and rational \(p\)-Kummer kernels of \(K^\times\) are both \(\mu_\infty\). If \(M/\mathbb Q_p\) is finite and \(H=\ker(\chi_p|_{P_M})\), restriction \[ H^1(G_M,\mathbb Q_p(1))\longrightarrow H^1(H,\mathbb Q_p(1)) \tag{F.33.1} \] is injective. The same is true with inertia \(I_M\) in place of \(G_M\).
notes: Working identifier FF.33. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.24; F.31.

statement: Let \(A\) be a semiabelian variety over a finite extension \(M/\mathbb Q_p\), put \(H=\ker(\chi_p|_{P_M})\), and set \[ S=\operatorname{Hom}_H(V_pA,\mathbb Q_p(1)). \tag{F.34.1} \] After a finite extension of the finite local model, the inertia action on this space has a canonical decomposition \[ S=S_0\oplus S_1,\qquad I_M|_{S_0}=1,\quad I_M|_{S_1}=\chi_p. \tag{F.34.2} \] Both summands are stable under the full local Galois group; its unramified action on either summand need not be trivial. For an algebraic model over a finite extension \(K/U_p\), the summand \(S_1\) vanishes on the rational Kummer classes of all points over all finite extensions of \(K\). The summand \(S_0\) is jointly detected by finitely many such point evaluations. If \(j:X\to A\) is pointed and its geometric image generates \(A\), those evaluations may all be taken at points \(j(x)\).
notes: Working identifier FF.34. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: Beilinson3.4/3.6; Fontaine2.7/4.2; Ohkubo3.1; Tate4; F.25; F.33. External citations: FF_Beilinson2012, FF_Fontaine2004, FF_Ohkubo2014, FF_Tate1967

statement: For every prime \(p\), every finite extension of \[ U_p=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb Z_{(p)}^{sh}) \bigl(p^{1/m}:(m,p)=1,\ \mu_{p^\infty}\bigr) \tag{F.35.1} \] satisfies \'etale reconstruction. Every subfield of such an extension also satisfies \'etale reconstruction. In particular, the failure of the functional detector in Claim~\ref{clm:FFcyclotomicdetector} does not prevent reconstruction of \(U_5\).
notes: Working identifier FF.35. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.26; F.33; F.34; CHW4.18(5). External citations: FF_CHW2024, FF_CharlesPoonen2016

statement: Let \(M/\mathbb Q_p\) be finite, and let \(S\) be a Hodge--Tate representation of \(G_M\) whose inertia image is abelian. The inertia representation on \(S\) is semisimple. In particular there is a canonical decomposition \[ S=S^{I_M}\oplus \sum_{g\in I_M}(g-1)S. \tag{F.36.1} \] Its projection onto the first summand commutes with \(G_M\). For every inertia-stable subspace \(N\), that projection sends \(N\) to \(N\cap S^{I_M}\), and taking inertia invariants is exact on \(0\to N\to S\to S/N\to0\). All assertions hold after any finite extension of \(M\).
notes: Working identifier FF.36. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: Fontaine2.7; Ohkubo3.1. External citations: FF_Fontaine2004, FF_Ohkubo2014

statement: Let \(K_p=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb Z_{(p)}^{sh})\) with the chosen embedding in \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\), and let \(K_p^{\rm ab}\) be its maximal abelian extension in that algebraic closure. Every finite extension of \(K_p^{\rm ab}\), and every subfield of such an extension, satisfies \'etale reconstruction. The extension \(K_p^{\rm ab}/U_p\) is infinite, so this is a proper enlargement of Claim~\ref{clm:FFcyclotomicreconstruct} at the level of the specified henselian fields.
notes: Working identifier FF.37. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.25; F.35; F.36; Iwasawa1955. External citations: FF_CHW2024

statement: The following two assertions hold. \begin{enumerate} \item Let \(\Gamma\) be a profinite group nilpotent of some fixed finite class, and let \(\chi:\Gamma\to\mathbb Q_p^\times\) be a nontrivial continuous character. Then \[ H^1(\Gamma,\mathbb Q_p(\chi))=0. \tag{F.38.1} \] \item Let \(S\) be a Hodge--Tate representation of the Galois group of a finite extension \(M/\mathbb Q_p\). If its inertia Lie algebra is nilpotent, that Lie algebra is abelian. After a finite extension of \(M\), the inertia representation is semisimple and has the canonical invariant projection of Claim~\ref{clm:FFabelianHT}. \end{enumerate}
notes: Working identifier FF.38. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: Ohkubo3.1; Fontaine2.7; F.36. External citations: FF_Fontaine2004, FF_Ohkubo2014

statement: Let \(I=G_{K_p}=I_{\mathbb Q_p}\), and define its closed lower central series by \(\gamma_1(I)=I\) and \(\gamma_{r+1}(I)=\overline{[I,\gamma_r(I)]}\). For each integer \(c\ge1\), put \[ K_{p,c}= \overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,\gamma_{c+1}(I)}. \tag{F.39.1} \] Every finite extension of \(K_{p,c}\), and every subfield of such an extension, satisfies \'etale reconstruction. Here \(K_{p,1}=K_p^{\rm ab}\), and every extension \(K_{p,c+1}/K_{p,c}\) is infinite. The nilpotency class \(c\) is fixed and finite in the assertion; no conclusion about the union of these fields or a general solvable closure is included.
notes: Working identifier FF.39. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.25; F.35; F.37; F.38; Iwasawa1955. External citations: FF_CHW2024

statement: Let \(I=G_{K_p}\), let \(I'=\overline{[I,I]}\), let \(I''=\overline{[I',I']}\), and put \[ B_p=\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\,I''}. \tag{F.40.1} \] This maximal metabelian extension of \(K_p\) is a proper countable algebraic subfield of \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\), with henselian value group \(\mathbb Q\), residue field \(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\), and \(\mu_\infty\subset B_p\). For every finite extension \(E/B_p\), \[ C_{\operatorname{Aut}(\overline{\mathbb Q})}(G_E)=1. \tag{F.40.2} \] It belongs to none of the sufficient field families established in this section through Claim~\ref{clm:FFnilpotentreconstruct}, including the subfields of finite extensions of a fixed bounded-nilpotency stage at any prime, and to none of the negative centralizer-ghost families. Moreover, \[ K_p^{{\rm ab},\times}\subset \bigcap_{n\ge1}(B_p^\times)^{p^n}. \tag{F.40.3} \] Thus the exact \(\mu_\infty\) Kummer-kernel input used in Claims~\ref{clm:FFcyclotomicreconstruct}-- \ref{clm:FFnilpotentreconstruct} fails here. No reconstruction failure is asserted.
notes: Working identifier FF.40. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.23; F.31; F.39; Iwasawa1955.

statement: The invariant-lift step of Claim~\ref{clm:FFmaxabelianreconstruct} fails for an actual elliptic curve over the metabelian field \(B_p\), even after every finite change of local arithmetic model. More precisely, put \(H=I''=G_{B_p}\), and take \[ A:\quad y^2+xy=x^3-p. \tag{F.41.1} \] There is a finite local field \(M_0/\mathbb Q_p\) of degree at most two, whose chosen global quadratic model lies in \(K_p^{\rm ab}\), such that the following holds. The space \[ S=\operatorname{Hom}_{H} (V_pA,\mathbb Q_p(1)) \tag{F.41.2} \] is two-dimensional. Let \(N\) be the subspace of functionals whose pushforward of the point Kummer class is zero for every \(a\in A(E)\) and every finite extension \(E/B_p\). Then for every finite extension \(M/M_0\), \[ N\simeq\mathbb Q_p(1),\qquad S/N\simeq\mathbb Q_p,\qquad S^{I_M}=0,\qquad (S/N)^{I_M}=S/N\ne0. \tag{F.41.3} \] The first two isomorphisms describe the actual local Galois representations. Consequently the visible invariant class has no inertia-invariant lift. This is a counterexample to a proposed replacement lemma, not a counterexample to \(\mathcal R(B_p)\).
notes: Working identifier FF.41. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.40; Tate1995 Theorem1 and finite-order section. External citations: FF_Tate1995

statement: Put \(F_p=K_p^{\rm ab}\), and define \[ W_p=\{a\in B_p^\times: a^m\in F_p^\times \text{ for some integer }m\ge1\}. \tag{F.42.1} \] For every finite extension \(E/B_p\), let \(\kappa_E\) denote the rational \(p\)-primary Kummer map. Then \[ \ker\bigl(\kappa_E:E^\times \longrightarrow H^1(G_E,\mathbb Q_p(1))\bigr) =\bigcap_{n\ge1}(E^\times)^{p^n}=W_p. \tag{F.42.2} \] In particular no new element in a finite extension enlarges this kernel. The subgroup recovers its abelian constant field by the equation \[ W_p\cap(1-W_p)=F_p\setminus\{0,1\}. \tag{F.42.3} \] There are two precise value-detection consequences. \begin{enumerate} \item If \(a,b\in E\setminus\{0,1\}\) have the same pair \((\kappa_E(a),\kappa_E(1-a))\), then \(a=b\) or both \(a,b\in B_p\). Thus the pair is injective outside \(B_p\), with no collision between such a value and a value in \(B_p\). \item If \(a,b\in E\) satisfy \[ \kappa_E(a-c)=\kappa_E(b-c) \quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb Q \text{ with }a,b\ne c, \tag{F.42.4} \] then \(a=b\) or both \(a,b\in F_p\). Conversely any two values in \(F_p\) satisfy (F.42.4). Thus all rational target translates detect every value outside \(F_p\) exactly. \end{enumerate}
notes: Working identifier FF.42. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.33; F.40; standard local Kummer theory.

statement: Let \(E/B_p\) be finite and let \(a,b\in E\). There is a proper finite extension \(L/E\) and \(\beta\in L\setminus E\) such that equality of the two pairs \[ \begin{split} &\bigl(\kappa_L(a-\beta), \kappa_L(1-a+\beta)\bigr),\\ &\bigl(\kappa_L(b-\beta), \kappa_L(1-b+\beta)\bigr) \end{split} \tag{F.43.1} \] implies \(a=b\). In fact every proper finite extension and every \(\beta\in L\setminus E\) work. Consequently the following criterion detects the actual point function of a pinned map. Let \(X/B_p\) be of finite type and let \(f,g:X_{\acute et}\to\mathbb A^1_{B_p,\acute et}\) be pinned morphisms over \(BG_{B_p}\). For every finite \(L/B_p\) and \(\beta\in L\), set \[ Y_\beta=\mathbb A^1_L\setminus\{\beta,\beta+1\}, \qquad U_\beta=f_L^{-1}(Y_\beta)\cap g_L^{-1}(Y_\beta) \subset X_L. \tag{F.43.2} \] Suppose the pullbacks by \(f_L\) and \(g_L\) of the two Kummer classes of \(T-\beta\) and \(\beta+1-T\) agree after restriction to \(U_\beta\). Then the two actual geometric point functions are equal, including their values in \(K_p^{\rm ab}\). This is a uniqueness criterion for point functions; it neither constructs the comparison morphism nor asserts that equality of point functions alone identifies arbitrary topos maps.
notes: Working identifier FF.43. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.40; F.42; CHW3.6. External citations: FF_CHW2024

statement: Let \(E/B_p\) be finite. Every pinned automorphism of \(\mathbb A^1_{E,\acute et}\) over \(BG_E\), with its relative structural isomorphism retained, has actual geometric point function \[ x\longmapsto ux+v \qquad (u\in E^\times,\ v\in E). \tag{F.44.1} \] The two coefficients are unique. This is an existence theorem for the actual point function in the automorphism case. It does not assert that the entire topos automorphism equals the one induced by (F.44.1), and does not classify arbitrary pinned morphisms.
notes: Working identifier FF.44. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.40; F.42; CHW3.6. External citations: FF_CHW2024

statement: Let \(k\) be a characteristic-zero field, let \(X/k\) be a smooth geometrically integral curve, and put \(F=k(X)\). A pinned automorphism \(\varphi:X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}\to X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}\) over \(BG_k\) induces a generic outer automorphism \[ \alpha_\varphi\in \operatorname{Aut}_{G_k}(G_F)/ \operatorname{Inn}(G_{\bar k(X)}). \tag{F.45.1} \] If its actual function on \(X(\bar k)\) is the identity and (F.45.1) is trivial, then \(\varphi\) is isomorphic to the identity over \(BG_k\). Consequently, for every finite \(E/B_p\), the remaining pointwise kernel in Claim~\ref{clm:FFmetabelianaffine} injects into the relative birational outer automorphism group of \(G_{E(T)}\). Its image preserves the geometric conjugacy class of every finite-point inertia subgroup, and its induced map on the corresponding residue Galois group is the identity. In particular, an inner generic action cannot hide a nontrivial automorphism of the full etale topos.
notes: Working identifier FF.45. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.23; CHW3.6/A.8/A.9/A.11; Koenigsmann4.1/4.3/4.5. External citations: FF_CHW2024, FF_HoshiMochizukiTsujimura2025, FF_Tsujimura2026

statement: Let \(k\) be a characteristic-zero field and \(X/k\) a smooth geometrically integral curve with function field \(F\). The following data determine an automorphism of \(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}\) over \(BG_k\): a continuous automorphism \(\alpha\) of \(G_F\) over \(G_k\), and a \(G_k\)-equivariant bijection \(\theta:X(\bar k)\to X(\bar k)\), such that \(\alpha\) sends the geometric conjugacy class of \(I_x\) to that of \(I_{\theta(x)}\) for every \(x\in X(\bar k)\). The resulting actual point function is \(\theta\), and the resulting generic action is \(\alpha\), with the usual geometric inner ambiguity. Now let \(E/B_p\) be finite, and let \(\varphi\) be a pointwise-trivial pinned automorphism of \(\mathbb A^1_{E,\mathrm{\acute et}}\) over \(BG_E\). For every finite extension \(L/E\) and every positive integer \(m\), its generic action fixes \[ H^1(G_{L(T)},\mu_m) \] pointwise. Equivalently, it acts trivially on the maximal abelian profinite quotient of \(G_{L(T)}\), after every finite constant base change. All geometric inertia exponents are one, at every prime. Neither assertion identifies the remaining nonabelian generic action with an inner automorphism.
notes: Working identifier FF.46. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.44; F.45; Koenigsmann4.1/4.3/4.5; CHW3.6/A.11. External citations: FF_CHW2024

statement: Let \(E/B_p\) be finite and let \(\varphi\) be a pointwise-trivial pinned automorphism of \(\mathbb A^1_{E,\mathrm{\acute et}}\) over \(BG_E\). Its inverse-image functor is naturally isomorphic to the identity on the full subcategory of quasicompact separated etale objects whose smooth projective geometric components have genus zero. The same assertion holds after every finite constant extension. This constraint is strictly stronger than peripheral and abelianization control for an abstract free profinite four-puncture group. Specifically, the word automorphism \[ x\longmapsto(xy)x(xy)^{-1},\qquad y\longmapsto(xy)y(xy)^{-1},\qquad z\longmapsto z \tag{F.47.1} \] of the free \emph{profinite} group on \(x,y,z\) moves a degree-three genus-zero cover, despite fixing every peripheral conjugacy class and abelianization. Hence it cannot be the geometric action of such a \(\varphi\) on a four-punctured open. This is a statement about the full profinite word automorphism (F.47.1); it is not an assertion about every full automorphism whose pro-\(p\) image equals the corresponding pro-\(p\) word automorphism.
notes: Working identifier FF.47. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.44; F.45; F.46; Koenigsmann4.3/4.5; SGA1 XIII2.12. External citations: FF_SGA1

statement: Let \(E/B_p\) be finite, and let \(\varphi\) be a pinned automorphism of \((\mathbb A^1_E)_{\acute et}\) over \(BG_E\) whose actual geometric point function is the identity. The natural scheme realizations of Claim~\ref{clm:FFgenuszerokernel} extend to the following objects, after every finite extension of constants: finite fibre products of the genus-zero objects, their open subobjects, and finite etale quotients by finite groups. In particular they extend to every subcover of the Galois closure of a connected finite etale genus-zero cover of an open of \(\mathbb A^1\). They consequently extend to every etale restriction of a finite abelian cover of \(\mathbb P^1_E\), of arbitrary genus, and to every finite Galois cover \[ \pi:C\longrightarrow\mathbb P^1_E \quad\hbox{with }g(C)=1. \tag{F.48.1} \] Here ``extend'' means that the induced slice point function is realized by a unique scheme isomorphism \(\varphi^*V\to V\) over the chosen base open, and these isomorphisms are natural in every morphism between the stated objects. The statement includes a quadratic cover with four geometric branch points. It also includes every degree-three cover with genus-one source, without a Galois assumption. Here \(C\) is smooth and geometrically integral. Thus, after identifying the inverse image of any connected cyclic torsor of the stated kind with the original one, its possible fibrewise deck rotation is a single global deck transformation. Point-dependent rotations on cyclic covers of arbitrary genus are excluded. No generation or cofinality claim for all positive-genus covers is asserted.
notes: Working identifier FF.48. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.47; elementary Kummer theory and elliptic isogenies; SGA1 XII5.1 and XIII4.6(a); complete582-tuple certificate. External citations: FF_Guralnick2003, FF_RecillasRodriguez2003, FF_SGA1

statement: Let \(E/B_p\) be finite, let \(\varphi\) be a pinned relative automorphism of \((\mathbb A^1_E)_{\acute et}\) with identity actual geometric point function, and let \[ \pi:C\longrightarrow\mathbb P^1_E \tag{F.49.1} \] be a finite Galois cover with smooth geometrically integral genus-one source. On a branch-complement open, use the unique actual scheme realization of Claim~\ref{clm:FFlatteskernel} to regard its generic slice action as an outer automorphism of \(G_{E(C)}\). For every finite constant extension \(L/E\), every \(m\ge1\), and every \(f\in L(C)^\times\), this outer action satisfies \[ \varphi_C^*\kappa_m(f)=\kappa_m(f). \tag{F.49.2} \] Equivalently it is the identity on the full abelian profinite quotient of \(G_{L(C)}\), after every such constant extension. This includes arbitrary translated rational functions on the elliptic slice. Thus every cyclic generic cover of this slice is preserved as a covering object. Neither its actual point-function realization nor identity on the entire elliptic slice topos is asserted by this claim.
notes: Working identifier FF.49. Proved Explicit owner proof inputs: F.46; F.47; F.48; SGA1 XII5.1; elliptic divisor group law and Kummer norm identity. External citations: FF_SGA1

statement: Retain the pointwise pinned automorphism hypotheses of Claims~\ref{clm:FFellipticshear} and the preceding genus-zero and Lattes results, over a finite extension \(E/B_p\). Let \(C\) be the smooth projective curve \[ C:\quad y^2=(u^2-1)(u^2-2)(u^2-3),\qquad T=u^2. \tag{F.50.1} \] This is a genus-two Galois cover of \(\mathbb P^1_T\) with group \(V_4\). Its transported actual point function, including every completed point, is realized by a unique scheme isomorphism over \(\mathbb P^1_T\). Using that isomorphism to identify its generic action, the automorphism fixes \[ H^1(G_{L(C)},\mu_m) \tag{F.50.2} \] for every finite extension \(L/E\) and every positive integer \(m\). More generally, the same Kummer conclusion holds for a realized smooth proper slice \(C\) whenever it has coherently realized connected finite etale covers \(D_s\to C\), with completed-point compatibility, whose pushforward images in integral geometric first homology are contained in \(\ell^sH_1(C,\mathbb Z_\ell)\), for arbitrarily large \(s\) and each prime \(\ell\).
notes: Working identifier FF.50. Proved: Kummer rigidity for an explicit genus-two slice Explicit owner proof inputs: F.46; F.48; F.49 completed-point comparison; Riemann–Roch dimension proof; integral Poincare duality; degree-two Jacobian norm identities.

statement: The historical and adopted localizer axioms are different formulations. The literal Loc~(1) of XVI ms.~1 consists of isomorphisms, two-out-of-three, and the condition that $gf,fg\in W$ imply $f,g\in W$. Grothendieck calls the first two conditions \emph{saturation faible}, and all three \emph{saturation mod\'er\'ee}. Retract closure is added in Loc~(1 bis); strong saturation is Loc~(1 ter). The literal Loc~(3), XVI ms.~2, is absolute Theorem~A. Relative Theorem~A is Loc~(3 bis), ms.~3. In this paper, a fundamental localizer means the modern relative package specified in the conventions: weak saturation, the terminal-object axiom, and the assertion that a functor $u:A\to B$ over $C$ lies in $W$ whenever $u/c:A/c\to B/c$ lies in $W$ for every $c\in C$. Consequently no argument using relative Theorem~A is an argument from the literal absolute Loc~(3) alone.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.1, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Literal absolute Loc (3) is not the adopted relative axiom.

statement: Intrinsic fibrations and their unconditional closure properties. Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks and let $W$ be invariant under isomorphism of arrows. For $S\in\mathcal M$, let $W_S$ be the inverse image of $W$ under the source functor $\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M$. Define \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*: \mathcal M/B\to\mathcal M/E\text{ sends }W_B\text{ into }W_E\}. \] Thus every test is an arrow $v:T'\to T$ over $B$, with arbitrary structure map $T\to B$, and the tested arrow is $E\times_B T'\to E\times_B T$. This class contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary pullback. These assertions require no two-out-of-three axiom. If $W$ is closed under retracts, then so is $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.2, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: No two-out-of-three needed for composition and base-change closure; retract premise explicit.

statement: The coarse, universal, and local relative classes. Suppose $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal L$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition and pullback. For an arrow $u:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal M/S$, put \[ u\in W_S^{\mathcal L}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(X\times_S T\longrightarrow Y\times_S T\bigr)\in W \quad\hbox{for every }(T\to S)\in\mathcal L. \] Let $W_S^u$ be the same class with all $T\to S$ allowed. Then \[ W_S^u\subseteq W_S^{\mathcal L}\subseteq W_S. \] All three classes contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Their retract closure follows if $W$ has it. These are precisely the relative classes in XII ms.~210 and 220. They must not be confused with the class of universal $W$-equivalences in $\mathcal M$, where the base is the codomain of the arrow being tested.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.3, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Full faithfulness on coefficients need not satisfy two-out-of-three.

statement: What raw reindexing and postcomposition actually preserve. Under the hypotheses of A.3, a map $f:S'\to S$ in $\mathcal L$ induces \[ f^*:(\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L}). \] For every $f:S'\to S$, without assuming $f\in\mathcal L$, postcomposition induces \[ f_\#:(\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L}). \] If $f^*$ also preserves the displayed classes, the ordinary adjunction $f_\#\dashv f^*$ descends to their localizations. For arbitrary $f$, this calculation alone constructs the descended postcomposition functor; it does not construct its right adjoint.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.4, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Raw pullback is proved homotopical only for the stated class; postcomposition works for every map.

statement: The universal saturation of the local test class. Under A.3, define $\widehat{\mathcal L}$ by the following condition on $f:S'\to S$: for every $T\to S$, pullback along $f_T:T\times_S S'\to T$ sends $W_T^{\mathcal L}$ into $W_{T\times_S S'}^{\mathcal L}$. Then $\widehat{\mathcal L}$ contains $\mathcal L$, contains isomorphisms, and is closed under composition and pullback. Moreover \[ W_S^{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=W_S^{\mathcal L} \quad\hbox{for every }S,\qquad \widehat{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=\widehat{\mathcal L}. \] It is the largest composition- and pullback-closed class containing isomorphisms that defines this same family of fine relative classes. This is the corrected, second definition at XII ms.~222; the first definition on that page omits the universal quantifier over $T\to S$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.5, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: The preliminary base-change universal quantifier is indispensable.

statement: The corrected transporter Galois connection. Let $W$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition in a category $\mathcal M$ with pullbacks. Let $A\subseteq W$ contain isomorphisms and be composition-closed, and let $L$ contain isomorphisms and be pullback-closed. Define \[ \begin{split} T_W(A)&=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*\text{ sends every arrow of }A \text{ in }\mathcal M/B\text{ into }W\},\\ K_W(L)&=\{u:X\to Y\in W\mid p^*u\in W \text{ for every }(p:Y'\to Y)\in L\}. \end{split} \] Then $T_W(A)$ contains isomorphisms and is pullback-closed, $K_W(L)$ contains isomorphisms and is composition-closed, and \[ A\subseteq K_W(L)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad L\subseteq T_W(A). \] Both operations reverse inclusions; their composites are extensive, monotone, and idempotent. The closed pairs are exchanged by inverse order-reversing bijections. Their extreme pairs are \[ (W^u,\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M),\qquad (W,\operatorname{Fib}_W), \] where $W^u$ means universal equivalences with respect to the codomain of each arrow.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.6, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Right-hand domain requires pullback closure, not composition closure.

statement: The exact composition criterion, II Proposition 6.1. For a closed pair $A=K_W(L)$, $L=T_W(A)$ of A.6, the following conditions are equivalent: $L$ is composition-closed; pullback along every member of $L$ preserves $A$; and $L=\operatorname{Stab}(A)$, where $\operatorname{Stab}(A)=T_A(A)$. Every stabilizer is composition- and pullback-closed. In particular, a transporter into the larger class $W$ is not generally a stabilizer.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.7, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Correct composition criterion for a closed transporter pair.

statement: Transporters need not compose under the hypotheses of II section 6. The claim in the first version of II~(6.2)--(6.5) that $T_W(A)$ automatically belongs to a right-hand domain requiring composition closure is false. A counterexample is the chain category $0<1<2<3$, with $W$ consisting of the identities and $0\to2,0\to3$, and $A$ consisting of the identities and $0\to3$. Here \[ T_W(A)=\operatorname{Mor}([3])\setminus\{1\to3\},\qquad K_WT_W(A)=A. \] Consequently $1\to2$ and $2\to3$ lie in the transporter while their composite does not.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.8, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: W is composition-closed but not two-out-of-three, exactly as permitted in II section 6.

statement: The meaning of smooth and proper in the manuscript. For a fundamental localizer on $\mathrm{Cat}$, let $\operatorname{As}_W$ consist of $u:A\to B$ for which $A/b\to e$ lies in $W$ for every $b$, and let $\operatorname{Coas}_W$ consist of $u$ for which $b\backslash A\to e$ lies in $W$ for every $b$. The definitions used at II ms.~66 and explicitly reaffirmed at ms.~89 are \[ \operatorname{Liss}_W=\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{As}_W), \qquad \operatorname{Prop}_W=\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{Coas}_W). \] The two mixed transporters contain both the corresponding stabilizer and $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. Neither is the definition of smoothness or properness. The proposed inclusion $\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W$ at XII ms.~225--226 is explicitly qualified by ``peut-\^etre'' and is an extra proposed axiom, not a consequence asserted to have been proved there.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.9, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Smooth/proper are asphericity stabilizers, not the mixed transporters into W.

statement: The three fibre axioms, with their quantifiers. For every $S\in\mathcal M$ let $\mathcal F_S$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal M/S$ on the intrinsic fibrations. The three assertions at XII ms.~215--218 are \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{(a)}&\quad J_S:\mathcal F_S[(W_S^u)^{-1}] \longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}]\text{ is an equivalence};\\ \mathrm{(b)}&\quad W_S^u=W_S\text{ on }\mathcal F_S;\\ \mathrm{(c)}&\quad\mathcal F_S[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow \mathcal H[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}] \text{ are equivalences} \end{aligned} \] for every full $\mathcal F_S\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal M/S$. Axiom (a) implies equality of the strong saturations of $W_S^u$ and $W_S$ on $\mathcal F_S$. It does not by that argument imply equality of the original classes. Axioms (b) and (c) imply (a).
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.10, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Axiom a gives equality of strong saturations; b is equality of the original restricted classes.

statement: Enough intrinsic fibrations implies the exact fibrewise invariance. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has pullbacks, $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three, and every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. Then axiom (b) of A.10 holds, and \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W\cap W=W^u. \] No terminal object, accessibility, functorial factorization, or strong saturation is required for these conclusions.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.11, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: No chosen functorial factorization or terminal object needed.

statement: A functorial replacement proves every intermediate-subcategory comparison. Let $\mathcal A$ be a category with a class $W$ containing isomorphisms and satisfying two-out-of-three, let $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal A$ be full, and suppose there is $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal F$ with a natural transformation $\eta:1_{\mathcal A}\to iR$ whose components are in $W$. For every full $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal A$, both inclusions induce equivalences \[ \mathcal F[W^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal H[W^{-1}] \longrightarrow\mathcal A[W^{-1}]. \] In particular, such slice replacements into $\operatorname{Fib}_W S$, together with enough intrinsic fibrations, verify XII (a), (b), and (c).
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.12, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Sufficient extra replacement hypothesis, not proof from a and b alone.

statement: The implication asked in audit row XIIc B062. The axioms (a) and (b) of A.10, even imposed at every base, do not imply (c). There is a counterexample with six objects, all finite limits and colimits, and strongly saturated $W$. It also refutes the analogous assertion for enhanced localizations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.13, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Six-object finite lattice refutes a+b implies c at every-base scope; W strongly saturated; enhanced version also fails.

statement: The two fine axiom systems in XII ms.225--227. Suppose classes $L,P\subseteq\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M$ contain isomorphisms and are closed under composition and pullback. Define $W_S^g=W_S^L$ and $W_S^d=W_S^P$. The clause called (a) on ms.~226, asserting preservation of $W^g$ by $L$-base change and of $W^d$ by $P$-base change, follows formally from the closure hypotheses. The clause called (b) on that page is the additional pair of assertions \[ \begin{aligned} (L/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^d)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^d\text{ on }L/S,\\ (P/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^g)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^g\text{ on }P/S. \end{aligned} \] Here $L/S$ and $P/S$ denote full subcategories on the corresponding structural maps. Under these additional equivalences, each fine theory is a contravariant pseudofunctor on all of $\mathcal M$. This conclusion does not require $L\cap P\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.14, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: The c of ms.227 is an adjunction axiom, different from c of ms.218.

statement: The four fibration classes and Loc (7), with reference localizer. For a fundamental localizer $W$, the four classes in XVI section~4 are distinct definitions. Besides intrinsic $\operatorname{Fib}_W$, one has Grothendieck fibrations; $\operatorname{Fib}^{\mathrm{weak}}_W$, tested by all arrows $T'\to T$ over the base with $T'$ and $T$ contractible in the category-homotopy sense; and $\operatorname{Parf}_W=\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W$. Here category-homotopy contractibility means that the identity functor is connected to a constant functor by a finite zigzag of natural transformations. It implies weak contractibility of the nerve, but replacing the test family by all weakly contractible nerves is a separate assertion, not the literal definition. Let $\mathcal G_W$ denote Grothendieck fibrations all of whose transport functors lie in $W$. For any arrow class $\mathcal F$, define \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm A(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W,\\ \mathrm B(\mathcal F)&:\quad W_S\cap\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal F/S) \subseteq W_S^u\quad\hbox{for every }S,\\ \mathrm C(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\cap W\subseteq W^u. \end{aligned} \] Loc~(7a), (7b), and (7c) are respectively $\mathrm A(\mathcal G_W)$, $\mathrm B(\mathcal G_W)$, and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G_W)$. For a reference localizer $V\subseteq W$, the conditions $\mathrm A_V,\mathrm B_V,\mathrm C_V$ replace $\mathcal G_W$ by $\mathcal G_V$. The condition $\mathrm D_V$ is $\mathrm A(\operatorname{Parf}_V)$, or its equivalent B and C forms once the hypotheses of A.17 are verified. Loc~(7F) is the factorization condition of A.11, not the inclusion of any one of these reference classes in $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.15, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Four fibration notions and eight reference/factorization variants kept separate.

statement: The implications A to B to C and replacement transfer. Let $W$ and $\mathcal M$ satisfy A.11's initial assumptions. If every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. If identities lie in $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. Suppose that each $p:X\to S$ in $\mathcal F$ admits a comparison $j_p:X\to R_p$ over $S$ in $W_S^u$, with $R_p\to S$ in $\mathcal G$. Then $\mathrm A(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. If for every map $h:X\to Y$ over $S$ between $\mathcal F$-objects the chosen comparisons extend to a commutative square $R(h)j_X=j_Yh$, then also $\mathrm B(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. Functorial replacements suffice; the proof only needs these individual commuting squares.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.16, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Replacement transfer in B needs commuting squares; functoriality suffices.

statement: The full Brown implication with all its premises. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has a terminal object and pullbacks, and $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal F$ contain isomorphisms and all terminal maps, be closed under composition and pullback, and admit a factorization of every arrow as a $W$-map followed by an $\mathcal F$-map. Then \[ \mathrm A(\mathcal F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathrm B(\mathcal F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathrm C(\mathcal F). \] This is the precise abstract assertion of XVI Lemma~4.4.3. The terminal-map premise is part of the statement, not a consequence of an arbitrary intrinsic-fibration factorization.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.17, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Complete relative mapping-path proof, with all terminal-map premises.

statement: The weak constant-coefficient notion does not compose. The universal weak rational cohomological fibrations of I ms.~117--118 need not be closed under composition. The failure occurs for finite categories. Consequently that notion cannot be silently substituted for the intrinsic class in A.2 or for the class in Loc~(7F).
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.18, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Finite covering/opfibration counterexample independently reconstructed.

statement: The local-coefficient repair has an asymmetric conclusion. Let $\mathbb D$ be a derivator in presheaf variance. Suppose that for $p:E\to B$, after every strict base change, the right direct image of every constant coefficient is locally constant and its value at each base object is canonically the right Kan extension from the strict fibre. If $v:T'\to T$ over $B$ is fully faithful on locally constant $\mathbb D$-coefficients, then the pullback $w:E\times_BT'\to E\times_BT$ is a constant-coefficient $\mathbb D$-equivalence. This argument does not assert full faithfulness or an equivalence on all locally constant coefficients upstairs. If the same direct-image and base-change hypothesis is required for every locally constant coefficient on every base-changed total category, then the resulting cohomological-fibration class is closed under composition and pullback. The corresponding statements for left Kan extensions and homology follow by duality.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.19, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Weak constant-coefficient conclusion distinguished from all local systems.

statement: Properness does not imply local constancy of fibres. The inclusion $j:\{1\}\to[1]$ is proper in Grothendieck's presheaf convention, but its comma transition over $0\to1$ is $\varnothing\to e$. Thus the assertion about proper maps at I ms.~102, companion row Ib-C003, is false already for spaces and set coefficients.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.20, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
his_places: I ms.102; Ib-C003; GALOIS D.9; STRATA D.5
notes: Proper cosieve has comma transition empty to point.

statement: Finite products and the one-fibrant-leg pullback comparison. Assume the hypotheses of A.11 and slice replacement equivalences as in A.12. In the localized fibrant slice over $S$, the product of $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ is represented by $X\times_S Y\to S$. Arbitrary derived reindexing preserves these finite products. Moreover, if $X\to S$ is intrinsic and $Y\to\overline Y\to S$ is a replacement with $Y\to\overline Y\in W$ and $\overline Y\to S$ intrinsic, then $X\times_S Y\to X\times_S\overline Y$ lies in $W$. Thus a strict pullback with one intrinsic leg computes the same relative homotopy object as replacing the other leg first. These are the formal assertions at XII ms.~241--248.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.21, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Finite product universal property proved by localizing the product/diagonal adjunction.

statement: The intrinsic factorization content of the weak Quillen axioms. The conditions M2, M$'$, and M$''$ of XIII ms.~8 imply both intrinsic factorizations: every arrow factors as an intrinsic cofibration followed by a $W$-map, and as a $W$-map followed by an intrinsic fibration. They consequently imply the universal-equivalence equalities of XIII Corollary~1, ms.~10, and the fibrewise assertion of XIII Proposition~4, ms.~10--11. They do not identify the designated classes $TC,TF$ with $C\cap W,F\cap W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.22, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Historical exactness W=TF composed TC is distinguished from one-sided equality.

statement: The variance assertions of XIII section 4 are lifting adjunctions. Let $\mathcal M(I)=\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal M)$, suppose the ordinary Kan extensions used below exist, and let the two closed lifting pairs be $(C(I),TF(I))$ and $(TC(I),F(I))$, with $C(I),TC(I)$ defined objectwise. For $u:I'\to I$ one has \[ u^*C(I)\subseteq C(I'),\quad u^*TC(I)\subseteq TC(I'), \quad u_*F(I')\subseteq F(I),\quad u_*TF(I')\subseteq TF(I), \] and \[ \begin{split} u^*F(I)\subseteq F(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!TC(I')\subseteq TC(I),\\ u^*TF(I)\subseteq TF(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!C(I')\subseteq C(I). \end{split} \] If every component of $i\backslash I'$ has an initial object and the relevant coproducts exist, then all four containments in the last two equivalences hold. In particular injective fibrant diagrams are objectwise fibrant. For a walking-arrow diagram $X_0\leftarrow X_1$, injective fibrancy is equivalent to $X_0$ fibrant and $X_1\to X_0\in F$; this also implies that $X_1$ is fibrant.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.23, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Presheaf variance fixes comma orientation and walking-arrow fibrancy.

statement: Ordinary Kan extensions do not automatically descend. For $(\mathrm{Cat},W_\infty)$, ordinary limits of finite diagrams need not preserve objectwise weak equivalences. Thus an ordinary $u_*$ in XIII ms.~45--50 cannot be identified with a derived $u_*$ without a derivability or fibrancy argument.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.24, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Ordinary limit of an objectwise weak equivalence may fail to be weak.

statement: The noetherian sober Alexandrov qualification adds no infinite posets. If a poset with its Alexandrov topology is noetherian and sober, the poset is finite. Hence the apparently more general admissibility qualification in XIII ms.~60--61, requiring the Alexandrov space of $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ to be noetherian and sober, introduces no genuinely infinite poset beyond the finite case.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.25, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
depends_on: Alexandrov closed sets; infinite Ramsey theorem
notes: Noetherian and sober Alexandrov posets are finite; companion observation independently verified.

statement: The intrinsic finite floor does not provide all small Kan extensions. Finite limits, finite colimits, two-out-of-three, and both intrinsic factorization axioms do not imply existence of all small homotopy Kan extensions. A counterexample is the category of finite sets with isomorphisms as $W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.26, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
depends_on: finite-set product and coproduct universal properties
notes: Finite intrinsic floor does not imply infinite Kan extensions.

statement: Closedness upgrades historical exactness to both trivial-class equalities. Let $(C,TC,F,TF)$ satisfy the weak Quillen axioms of XIII ms.~27--28, including two-out-of-three for $W$, the two factorizations, and $TC\subseteq C\cap W$, $TF\subseteq F\cap W$. If both lifting pairs are closed and $W=TF\circ TC$, then \[ TC=C\cap W,\qquad TF=F\cap W. \] Moreover $W$ is retract-closed. With the finite limits and colimits of M0 these data are a closed model structure in the original finite-limit convention. The two intrinsic containments M$''$ make this structure proper. Thus a \emph{closed exact} structure, as required by the uniform hypothesis at XIII ms.~57, is stronger than the unqualified exact structure distinguished in A.22.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.27, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Closedness plus exactness DOES imply both trivial-class equalities; the added premise is essential.

statement: The uniform theorem of XIII and the exact admissibility hypothesis. Assume exactly the uniform-left hypothesis of XIII ms.~57: for every $I$ in the specified diagram domain, the objectwise classes $C(I),TC(I)$ and their right orthogonals $TF(I),F(I)$ form a closed exact weak Quillen structure for the objectwise class $W(I)$. Let $u:I'\to I$ be a functor in the domain for which the ordinary presheaf right Kan extension $u_*$ exists. Then $u_*$ preserves weak equivalences between fibrant diagrams. It consequently induces a right adjoint \[ u^*: \mathcal M(I)[W(I)^{-1}] \rightleftarrows\ \mathcal M(I')[W(I')^{-1}]:\mathbf R u_*. \] If the comma categories $I'/i$ and their inclusions into $I'$ belong to the diagram domain, the canonical pointwise formula is \[ i^*\mathbf R u_*X\ \cong\ \mathbf R\!\lim_{(I'/i)^{\mathrm{op}}}X|_{I'/i}. \] In particular every functor between finite posets is admissible under the source's hypotheses. No restriction to finite posets is necessary for admissibility once the relevant ordinary Kan extension and uniform diagram structures exist. In the historical numbering, this proves the right-hand Der~4 and Der~5 assertions of XIII ms.~61; these numbers do not mean modern Der~4 and strongness Der~5.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.28, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
depends_on: A.17,A.23,A.25,A.27; Quillen 1967 I.1 Theorem 1 and I.4 Theorem 3
notes: All u with existing ordinary Kan extension are admissible under the actual uniform closed exact premise.

statement: The polarity calculation in II section 5 requires closure after a join. For any relation $R\subseteq P\times Q$, the maps $A\mapsto A^\perp=\{q\mid pRq\text{ for all }p\in A\}$ and its transpose define an antitone Galois connection on the power sets. Double orthogonality is an extensive idempotent closure; closed subsets are closed under arbitrary intersections, and their join is the closure of their union. If $P,Q$ are complete posets and the principal-polar condition (D$_0$) of II ms.~69 holds, write $c$ for the induced closure on $P$. For a subset $A\subseteq P$, its polar closure is the principal lower set \[ A^{\perp\perp}=\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee A\right) =\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee_{a\in A}c(a)\right). \] The final closure cannot be omitted from II formula~(5.20), ms.~76. One must also distinguish the element $c(\bigvee A)$ of $P$ from its principal lower set, a subset of $P$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.29, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: The final closure on the supremum and the distinction element/principal lower set are required.

statement: Arbitrary unions do not preserve composition closure. The class of arrow classes containing identities and closed under both pullback and composition is not closed under arbitrary unions, contrary to the preliminary lattice description in II ms.~65--67. Intersections have that property; a join requires taking the closure of the union under the specified operations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.30, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: A union of composition-closed pullback-closed classes need not compose.

statement: The bi-site remark fixes a question rather than a general theorem. At VI ms.~81--84 the data $(\mathcal M,W)$ specify the coarse slice localization, but the proposed fine classes require additional test data. The two comma tests in $\mathrm{Cat}$ have opposite variances: $X/s$ varies covariantly with $s$, and $s\backslash X$ contravariantly. In XII ms.~222 the class labelled $W^g$ uses the former tests and its universal preservation class is the smooth class discussed in Part B; XII ms.~224's $W^d$ uses the latter. The letters on an earlier page are not a substitute for this variance check. The remark that weak globular infinity-groupoids might have no useful localization theory is a suggestion at VI ms.~83--84. It is not a nonexistence theorem about fine relative theories. The attached 2026 claims about higher categories and globular groupoids remain ``claimed (OpenAI, 2026, unrefereed)'' here \citep{OpenAI2026Thomason,OpenAI2026Groupoids}; no conclusion of Part A depends on either.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.31, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Higher-category 2026 claims not used as proof inputs.
