statement: Unipotent detection and the original-section coinvariant splitting Let $g\geq3$, retain $G=\Gamma_{g,0}$, $B=\operatorname{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$, $I$, $P=\widehat I$, $K=\ker(P\to\widehat G)$ and the actual maps $\Phi:K\twoheadrightarrow\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $j:\widehat{\mathbb Z}\to K$ of D.53. Put $L=\ker\Phi$. For a prime $\ell$, let $\mathcal T_\ell$ be the unipotent completion of $I$ over $\mathbb Q_\ell$, and let $\mathcal G_\ell$ be the completion of $G$ relative to its symplectic representation. Write $\mathcal U_\ell$ for the prounipotent radical of $\mathcal G_\ell$. Rational points of these proalgebraic groups have the inverse-limit topology from their finite-dimensional algebraic quotients. There are actual continuous maps, extending the indicated discrete completion maps, \[ \begin{split} P&\longrightarrow I^{(\ell)} \xrightarrow{\ \psi_\ell\ }\mathcal T_\ell(\mathbb Q_\ell),\\ \widehat G&\longrightarrow\mathcal G_\ell(\mathbb Q_\ell). \end{split} \tag{D.250} \] Their composites to $\mathcal G_\ell(\mathbb Q_\ell)$ agree along $P\to\widehat G$. The actual algebraic map $\mathcal T_\ell\to\mathcal U_\ell$ has central kernel $Z_\ell\cong\mathbb G_a$, and $\psi_\ell(K)\subset Z_\ell(\mathbb Q_\ell)$. Here and below $\psi_\ell$ also denotes its composite with $P$. The Heisenberg morphism constructed in D.59 induces an algebraic isomorphism $\alpha_\ell:Z_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb G_a$ for which \[ \begin{split} \alpha_\ell\psi_\ell(k)&=-2a\Phi_\ell(k),\qquad a=\varepsilon(8g+4),\\ \psi_\ell(K)&=\alpha_\ell^{-1}(-2a\mathbb Z_\ell),\qquad \ker(\psi_\ell|_K)=\ker\Phi_\ell. \end{split} \tag{D.251} \] The integer $a$, the character $\Phi$ and its section are exactly those of D.53 and D.59. Consequently \[ \ker\!\left(K\longrightarrow \prod_\ell\mathcal T_\ell(\mathbb Q_\ell)\right)=L, \qquad \operatorname{im}\!\left(K\longrightarrow \prod_\ell\mathcal T_\ell(\mathbb Q_\ell)\right) \cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \tag{D.252} \] The isomorphism in (D.252) is induced by the original $\Phi$ and the displayed $\alpha_\ell$, and is an isomorphism of compact topological groups. In D.59's quotient $Q_\ell$, the kernel of the actual map to $\mathcal T_\ell(\mathbb Q_\ell)$ is precisely $\ker\overline\Phi_\ell$. Use additive notation on the central abelian group $K$. For a profinite abelian $\widehat B$-module $X$, let $X_{\widehat B}$ mean its quotient by the closed subgroup generated by $bx-x$. The original section supplies the following actual isomorphism: \[ \begin{split} K_{\widehat B}&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } L_{\widehat B}\times\widehat{\mathbb Z},\\ [k]&\longmapsto \bigl([k-j(\Phi(k))],\Phi(k)\bigr),\qquad ([l],t)\longmapsto[l+j(t)]. \end{split} \tag{D.253} \] In particular, for a finite abelian group $A$ with trivial action, or for $A=\mathbb Z_\ell$, restriction to $L$ and to $j$ gives \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(K,A)^{\widehat B} &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(\widehat{\mathbb Z},A) \oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(L,A)^{\widehat B},\\ f&\longmapsto(f\circ j,f|_L). \end{split} \tag{D.254} \] Its inverse sends $(h,\chi)$ to $h\circ\Phi+\chi\circ\pi_L$, where $\pi_L(k)=k-j(\Phi(k))$. Thus extension by this original $\pi_L$ makes every invariant character of $L$ invariant on $K$. No equivariance of $j$ on $K$ is required. Here are the remaining cohomology maps with their exact scope. Write $W_A=\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(L,A)^{\widehat B}$ and $\operatorname{ext}_j(\chi)=\chi\pi_L$. For finite constant $A$, there is a natural injection \[ \frac{\mathcal E_B^2(A)^{\widehat B}} {\theta_A\bigl(\Phi^*\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts} (\widehat{\mathbb Z},A) \oplus\operatorname{ext}_j W_A\bigr)} \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\mathcal E_G^2(A). \tag{D.255} \] Its image is exactly the inflation of the invariant arithmetic classes. The entire degree-two group still has D.54's exact sequence \[ \begin{split} 0&\longrightarrow \mathcal E_B^2(A)/\theta_A\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(K,A) \longrightarrow\mathcal E_G^2(A)\longrightarrow P_A \longrightarrow0,\\ P_A&=\ker\!\left[d_3: \ker\bigl(d_2:T_A^{0,2}\to T_A^{2,1}\bigr) \longrightarrow\mathcal E_B^3(A)\right]. \end{split} \tag{D.256} \] The transition maps, inflation, restriction, $d_2$ and $d_3$ are the actual maps specified in (D.179)--(D.189). The residual module $L_{\widehat B}$ and the fibre term $P_A$ are left explicit. For comparison with D.57, set $W_\ell=\operatorname{ext}_j\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts} (L,\mathbb Z_\ell)^{\widehat B}$ and retain $M_\ell,N_\ell,v_\ell$. There are exact intersection identities and an actual quotient map \[ \begin{gathered} \theta_\ell\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts} (K,\mathbb Z_\ell)^{\widehat B} =\mathbb Z_\ell v_\ell\oplus\theta_\ell W_\ell,\\ N_\ell\cap\theta_\ell\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts} (K,\mathbb Z_\ell) =\mathbb Z_\ell v_\ell \oplus(N_\ell\cap\theta_\ell W_\ell),\\ N_\ell/\mathbb Z_\ell v_\ell \longrightarrow M_\ell/\theta_\ell\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts} (K,\mathbb Z_\ell). \end{gathered} \tag{D.257} \] The kernel of the last map is the injective image of $N_\ell\cap\theta_\ell W_\ell$ under the displayed quotient of $N_\ell$. It is a closed submodule of $N_\ell/\mathbb Z_\ell v_\ell\cong\mathbb Z_\ell$. This intersection is not evaluated. statement: The exact arithmetic edge of the Torelli crossed extension Let $g\geq3$, retain $G,B,I,P=\widehat I,K$ and $\Phi$, and put $E=\widehat G$, $C=\overline I\subset E$ and $Q=\widehat B$. The actual sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow P \xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }E\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow1 \tag{D.280} \] is a continuous crossed extension, with the $E$-action on $P$ constructed in D.55. Choose normalized continuous set sections $\sigma:Q\to E$ and $\tau:C\to P$, and put \[ \begin{split} f(x,y)&=\tau\bigl(\sigma(x)\sigma(y)\sigma(xy)^{-1}\bigr),\\ \kappa(x,y,z)&= (\sigma(x)\cdot f(y,z))f(x,yz)f(xy,z)^{-1}f(x,y)^{-1}. \end{split} \tag{D.281} \] This is a normalized continuous $K$-valued three-cocycle, with its actual $Q$-action. For a finite constant abelian coefficient group $A$ and a $Q$-invariant continuous character $\chi:K\to A$, its pushout class \[ \mathfrak k_A(\chi)=[\chi\kappa] \in H^3_{\rm cts}(Q;A) \tag{D.282} \] is independent of those sections. With D.55's bar sign and D.56's arithmetic edge, the exact comparison is \[ d_3^{\rm ar}\bigl(\theta_A(\chi)\bigr) =\mathfrak k_A(\chi). \tag{D.283} \] All coefficient and restriction maps in this formula are the actual maps already used in D.54--D.57. Write \[ Z_A=\ker\bigl[H^3_{\rm cts}(Q;A)\longrightarrow H^3(B;A)\bigr]. \tag{D.284} \] There is a natural isomorphism, followed by an injection, \[ \frac{\mathcal E_B^2(A)^Q} {\theta_A\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(K,A)^Q} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \frac{Z_A}{\mathfrak k_A\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(K,A)^Q} \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\mathcal E_G^2(A). \tag{D.285} \] The first map is induced by $d_3^{\rm ar}$; the second is its inverse followed by D.60's inflation injection. Its image is exactly the inflation of the invariant arithmetic classes. In particular D.60's residual $L$-characters enter by the explicit map $\chi\mapsto\mathfrak k_A(\operatorname{ext}_j\chi)$. Their image and the fibre permanent-cycle group $P_A$ of (D.256) remain unevaluated. The coefficient inverse limits give the corresponding map $\mathfrak k_\ell$ for invariant continuous $K\to\mathbb Z_\ell$ characters. At these integral coefficients one has \[ H^2_{\rm cts}(Q;\mathbb Z_\ell)=0. \tag{D.286} \] Let $E_{\mathbb R}$ be the real-cover extension of $B$ with the original generator of D.52. Its quotient by $2\mathbb Z$ has an actual completed extension \[ 1\longrightarrow C_2\longrightarrow \widehat{E_{\mathbb R}/2\mathbb Z} \longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow1, \qquad \mu\in H^2_{\rm cts}(Q;C_2). \tag{D.287} \] For the original character $\Phi$, the exact values are \[ \begin{split} \mathfrak k_\ell(\Phi_\ell)&=0\qquad(\ell\ne2),\\ \mathfrak k_2(\Phi_2)&=\operatorname{Bock}(\mu)\ne0, \qquad 2\operatorname{Bock}(\mu)=0. \end{split} \tag{D.288} \] The Bockstein is that of $0\to\mathbb Z_2\xrightarrow{2}\mathbb Z_2\to C_2\to0$. Thus the second class has order exactly two. This evaluates only the specified-character pushout of (D.280); it does not evaluate the other classes in (D.285) or the fibre term in (D.256).

statement: The compact invariant lattice and the exact integral crossed kernel Let $g\geq3$, $B=\operatorname{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$, $Q=\widehat B$, and retain $M_\ell,N_\ell,v_\ell$ from D.57 and the actual $K,L,\Phi,j$ from D.53--D.60. statement: The exact completed-bar quotient and its local source Retain $G,B,E,Q,K,L,\Phi,j$ from D.64 and fix a prime $\ell$. statement: The tame relative quotient and the remaining third differential Retain $g\geq3$, $G=\Gamma_{g,0}$, $I$, $E=\widehat G$, $C=\overline I\subset E$, and the actual arithmetic quotient $Q=\widehat B=\prod_pQ_p$, where $Q_p=\operatorname{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb Z_p)$. statement: A primitive Heisenberg pullback with the original central character \emph{Part D(c): an evaluated quotient of the actual genus-three central Torelli extension.} Fix genus three and an odd prime $\ell$. Define \[ \begin{gathered} H_\lambda=V\times\mathbb Z_\ell,\qquad \omega(v,w)=\tfrac12\lambda(v\wedge w),\\ (v,s)(w,t)=(v+w,s+t+\omega(v,w)),\\ f_\lambda(p)=(v(p),b(p)) \quad\text{if }\eta(p)=(v(p),z(p)),\quad b(p)=\lambda(z(p)). \end{gathered} \tag{D.862} \] Let $a:D\to V$ be the original abelian quotient. statement: The integral central-lattice coinvariants and their seven-primary obstruction \emph{Part D(c): exact coinvariant and pushout maps for D.79's original central image, and a specified finite quotient.} Use the original genus-three Johnson lattice $T=\Lambda^3H/(H\wedge\omega_H)$, put $W_{\mathbb Z}=\Lambda^2T$, and retain D.59's determinant polarization $q$ and D.79's inverse bivector $\Omega=\Omega_q$. Use D.79's original central parameter \[ i:\mathbb Z_\ell\longrightarrow W, \qquad i(t)=ut,\qquad u=-\varepsilon\Omega. \tag{D.912} \] For a finite constant $\ell$-primary abelian group $A$, or for $A=\mathbb Z_\ell$ with its compact topology, restriction along this exact injection is the map \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(W,A)^E\cong A \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(\mathbb Z_\ell u,A)\cong A,\\ a\longmapsto-7\varepsilon a. \end{gathered} \tag{D.913} \] The identifications are composition with $q$ and evaluation at $u$, respectively. For $n\in\mathbb Z_\ell$ form the actual module pushout \[ \begin{gathered} M_n=(\mathbb Z_\ell\oplus W)\big/ \{(-nt,ut):t\in\mathbb Z_\ell\},\\ 0\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_\ell \xrightarrow{\ a\mapsto[(a,0)]\ }M_n \xrightarrow{\ [(a,w)]\mapsto[w]\ }Z \longrightarrow0. \end{gathered} \tag{D.914} \] The first coordinate has trivial $E$ action. statement: Exact coinvariants and a seven-primary equivariant splitting obstruction \emph{Part D(c): evaluated finite invariant character spaces, their original quotient maps, and a specified refinement.} Fix genus three and an odd prime $\ell$. Suppose $2r\geq t$ and use D.80's original function $b_P:P\to\mathbb Z_\ell$ with $b_P|_{K_{\rm rel}}=\Phi_\ell$. For the contragredient action define \[ \gamma_e(\pi(p))=f_0(e^{-1}\cdot p)-f_0(p), \qquad p\in\mathcal P_r,\ e\in E. \tag{D.1456} \] This is a continuous one-cocycle with values in $Z_r=\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(U_r,A_t)$, and its class has the exact order \[ \operatorname{ord}[\gamma] =\ell^{\,\min(t,e_{r,t}+v_\ell(7))} \quad\hbox{in }H^1_{\rm cts}(E,Z_r). \tag{D.1457} \] In particular, at $\ell=7$ and $r\geq t$, this order is seven. statement: The actual torsion-character part and torsion-free quotient of the cokernel \emph{Part D(c): the coefficient kernels and the character part of the original cokernel are evaluated through their original compact quotients.} Retain genus three, an odd prime $\ell$, and all original maps of D.101--D.103. statement: The strict completion and its finite representations For every stable $(g,n)$, set \[ \widehat C_{g,n}=\varprojlim_R C_{g,n}/R, \] where $R$ ranges over finite-index congruences on all Hom-sets, with the object set fixed. statement: Cote 143 uses geometric base change, and individual faithfulness \label{sec:E-manuscript} In cote 143, scans 29--33, the group denoted $\widehat\Gamma_{g,n}=\pi_1(\overline M_{g,n})$ is the geometric fundamental group of the \emph{open} moduli stack: the bar in this passage denotes base change to $\overline{\mathbb Q}$. For $(0,3)$ it is the trivial homomorphism to $1$. With the usual pure mapping class groups in the unstable cases, it is trivial for $(0,0),(0,1),(0,2)$ and faithful for $(1,0)$. More precisely \[ \widehat\pi_{0,3}\xrightarrow{\sim} \widehat P\Gamma_{0,4},\qquad \widehat P\Gamma_{0,3}=1. \tag{E.31} \] Thus the tripod automorphism assertion and the four-point modular-group assertion are related by this specified isomorphism; they are not two assertions about the trivial three-point modular group.

statement: The discrete diagonal model loses a completed stabilizer Let $\Gamma$ be a stable mapping class group with a nonempty boundary stratum, let $X$ be its Bers bordification, and put $G=\check\Gamma$. Let $N\triangleleft_oG$ range over open normal subgroups and set $\Gamma_N=\Gamma\cap N$. There is a natural map of sets \[ \Phi:(X\times G)/\Gamma\longrightarrow \varprojlim_N X/\Gamma_N, \qquad \Phi_N([x,g])=[\gamma_N^{-1}x], \quad \gamma_N\equiv g\pmod N. \tag{E.248} \] The action in the source is the diagonal left action. This map is not injective. In particular, the natural isomorphism with this diagonal quotient asserted in the proof of Boggi's Theorem~6.3, PDF p.~29, \cite{ET_Boggi2014} is false as a statement about these underlying sets. For a fixed boundary point $p\in X$, write $S=\operatorname{Stab}_\Gamma(p)$. The exact replacement on its orbit is \[ \Gamma\backslash((\Gamma p)\times G) \cong G/S \longrightarrow G/\overline S \xrightarrow{\sim} \varprojlim_N\Gamma_N\backslash\Gamma/S. \tag{E.249} \] Here the middle map is the actual quotient map and $\overline S$ is closure in $G$. Formula (E.249) is a statement about the fixed orbit and its finite-level completion. No global corrected Bers model is asserted.

statement: The support of a twist commuting with a full pants multitwist Let $S=S_{g,n}$ be stable with $d=3g-3+n>0$, and put $G=\check\Gamma_{g,[n]}$; the same statements hold in its pure subgroup. Choose positive integers $m_\gamma$, for $\gamma\in P$, and $\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}$, and set \[ D_P=\prod_{\gamma\in P}t_\gamma^{\lambda m_\gamma},\qquad \mathcal T_{\rm op}(S)= \{t_\beta^h:\ \beta\in\check C(S)^0, \ h\widehat{\mathbb Z}\text{ is open in } \widehat{\mathbb Z}\}. \tag{E.290} \] Here the power condition means exactly $h=a u$ with $a\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $u\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}$. The complete centralizer, including its finite graph action, is \[ C_G(D_P)= \{g\in\operatorname{Stab}_G(P): m_{g\gamma}=m_\gamma\text{ for every }\gamma\in P\}. \tag{E.292} \] If $P$ is discrete, this is the closure of the discrete centralizer of $\prod_{\gamma\in P}t_\gamma^{m_\gamma}$. statement: The retained manuscript structure and the completed comparisons Cote 143, scans 29--31, defines a modular topos over $\Q$ and then asks for the automorphisms of its geometric base change. E.T8--E.T10 reconstruct the full unringed topos in every stable modular dimension at least three, including the exact semilinear algebraic comparison. E.T13 additionally computes the big etale modular topos with its projection to the big etale base retained, by reconstructing the actual algebraic moduli stack. statement: Full completion at residue characteristics two and three For $p=2$ and $p=3$, put $U_p=\mathbf P^1_{\overline{\F}_p}-\{0,1,\infty\}$. statement: The exact cohomological dimensions and the real exception — Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated of transcendence degree $n$, let $k$ be the algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$ in $K$, and put $P=G_{K\overline k}$ and $E=G_K$. With continuous cohomology of discrete torsion modules, \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell P=n\quad\hbox{for every prime }\ell, \qquad \operatorname{cd}P=n, \] \[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell E=n+2\quad(\ell\ne2),\qquad \operatorname{cd}_2E= \begin{cases}n+2&K\text{ not formally real},\\ \infty&K\text{ formally real}. \end{cases} \] In every case $\operatorname{vcd}_2E=\operatorname{cd}_2G_{K(i)}=n+2$. Thus the equalities proposed in F1 hold, with precisely this exception at two (149, section 1, manuscript p.~6, scan 13). For a general function field, the relevant condition is an ordering of $K$ itself, not just a real embedding of its constant number field.

statement: Finite-order elements and complex conjugation — For a field $F$ of characteristic zero, every nonidentity element of finite order in $G_F=\operatorname{Gal}(F^{\rm sep}/F)$ has order two. Its centralizer is the subgroup of order two that it generates. In $G_{\mathbb Q}$ all such elements are conjugate to the complex conjugation determined by $\overline{\mathbb Q}\subset\mathbb C$. Every open subgroup of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ has trivial centralizer in $G_{\mathbb Q}$. This answers F2 (149, section 1, manuscript p.~6, scan 14).

statement: Open subgroups, torsion, and centers of profinite surface groups — Let $P$ be the full profinite completion of either a free group of finite rank $r\geq2$, or the fundamental group of a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq2$. Every open subgroup has trivial centralizer in $P$, and $P$ has no nonidentity element of finite order. An open subgroup of index $d$ is the full profinite completion of a free group of rank $1+d(r-1)$, respectively a surface group of genus $1+d(g-1)$. The free rank-one exception is $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, whose center and the centralizers of all its open subgroups equal the whole group. These statements answer F3 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~7 and 13, scans 15 and 28).

statement: Corollaries 1(b), 2(c)--(d), and 3 with all comparison maps — A hyperbolic polycurve means a finite tower of smooth pairs whose geometric curve fibres have $2g-2+r>0$, including proper fibres. statement: The Hartogs extension of a rational section — \textup{[F11; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 32, 34--35, 41; scans 65, 70--72, 83.]} Let $S$ be a smooth integral scheme of finite type over a field of characteristic zero. Let $U\to S$ be a smooth pair of constant type different from $(0,0)$ and $(0,1)$. For a closed subset $Z\subset S$ of codimension at least two, restriction is a bijection \[ \operatorname{Sect}_S(U)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Sect}_{S\setminus Z}(U\times_S(S\setminus Z)). \] The same assertion holds for a finite tower of such relative curves.

statement: The trait criterion, including the two nonhyperbolic types — \textup{[F12; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 36--38; scans 74--78.]} Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $K$ its fraction field, and let $U=\bar U\setminus D$ be a smooth pair over $R$ of type other than $(0,0),(0,1)$. Let $f_K\in U(K)$. In characteristic zero for the residue field use all geometric covers; in residue characteristic $p>0$ use the geometrically pro-prime-to-$p$ fundamental groups. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $f_K$ extends to an $R$-section of $U$; \item the continuous lift $G_K\to E_U^{(p')}$ induced by $f_K$ factors through $\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}R)$; \item this lift is trivial on an inertia group at the closed point. \end{enumerate} Here ``factors'' means that the induced map on the quotient is a section of $E_U^{(p')}\to\pi_1(R)$. For nonhenselian $R$, inertia is taken in a chosen decomposition group, and its closed normal closure is the kernel of $G_K\to\pi_1(R)$. The statement extends to a tower of smooth pairs whose curve factors have these types.
notes: Retains the full arithmetic quotient. Geometric pro-prime-to-p quotient only in mixed/residue characteristic p. Includes (0,2),(1,0), with A1 pole counterexample.

statement: The nonabelian intersection formula and the five conditions — \textup{[F12; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 37--39 and 44; scans 75--79, 90.]} Let $R$ be henselian and use the notation of C2. Suppose that the proper extension of $f_K$ meets a rational cusp $q$ in the closed fibre. If $z$ is a local equation of $q$ and $t$ a uniformizer of $R$, write \[ f_K^*z=t^\mu u,\qquad u\in R^*,\qquad \mu>0. \] With positive Kummer inertia defined by $\tau\mapsto\tau(z^{1/n})/z^{1/n}$, the induced continuous homomorphism on inertia is, up to the geometric conjugation arising from the chosen path, \[ I_K\longrightarrow I_K/P_K=T_{p'} \xrightarrow{[\mu]}T_{p'}\xrightarrow{\kappa_q}\Pi^{(p')}. \tag{C.1} \] For $p=0$, $P_K=1$. The formula holds with one cusp. With at least two cusps it induces on the toric part of homology \[ T_\ell\longrightarrow T_\ell^{D(\bar k)}/T_\ell, \qquad a\longmapsto\mu a e_q \pmod{T_\ell\cdot(1,\ldots,1)}. \tag{C.2} \] In equicharacteristic zero, the five conditions a)--e) of scan 90 are equivalent for the lift $\lambda:G_K\to E_U$: injectivity of $\lambda$; the positive-multiplicity formula (C.1); nontrivial inertia; failure of descent to $\pi_1(R)$; and failure of $f_K$ to extend into $U$. In that case its image has index $\mu$ in the cusp normalizer. For $p>0$, replace the domain in the injectivity assertion by $G_K/P_K$, and replace the index by $\mu_{p'}=\prod_{\ell\ne p}\ell^{v_\ell(\mu)}$.
notes: Nonabelian Kummer formula includes one cusp; scan90 full injectivity requires residue characteristic zero, otherwise quotient wild inertia; index is prime-to-p part of mu.

statement: The exact sequence and the centre-free extension — \textup{[F13; \S3, manuscript p.\ 39; scan 79; also scans 64, 73.]} Let $S$ be a connected normal scheme of finite type over a field of characteristic zero, and let $U\to S$ be a hyperbolic smooth pair. Then \[ 1\longrightarrow\Pi\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow1 \tag{C.3} \] is exact. Its formation commutes with the base changes to a normal connected scheme used in this part, with the chosen geometric fibre identified by a path. If $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Out}(\Pi)$ is its continuous outer action, the continuous map \[ E\longrightarrow E_\rho=\{(a,g)\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Pi)\times G: [a]=\rho(g)\},\qquad e\longmapsto(\operatorname{conj}_e,\bar e) \tag{C.4} \] is an isomorphism. For a tower with factors also of types $(0,2)$ or $(1,0)$, exactness holds over an \'etale $K(\pi,1)$ base, and at each stage over a trait as in C2. It is false for arbitrary bases without the hyperbolic or $\pi_2$ hypothesis.
notes: Centre-free fibre removes the pi2 obstruction. Gm and elliptic factors require K(pi,1) base or trait. O(-1)^times over P1 refutes unrestricted exactness.

statement: Unramified rational geometric sections extend — \textup{[F11; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 32, 34--36, 41--42; scans 65, 70--74, 83--84.]} Let $S$ be smooth integral of finite type over a characteristic-zero field, with function field $K$, and let $U/S$ be a tower as in C1 for which the exact geometric sequences of C4 hold. A rational section $f_K$ extends to $S$ if and only if its induced lift \[ \lambda_f:G_K\longrightarrow\pi_1(U) \] kills $\ker(G_K\to\pi_1(S))$. Equivalently, it kills every divisorial inertia subgroup of $G_K$ whose centre has codimension one in $S$.
notes: All maps and hypotheses are stated in the TeX result and proof.

statement: The normalizer extension and its sign — \textup{[F14; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 39--41; scans 79--82.]} Assume the hyperbolic case of C4 and let $q:S\to D$ be a boundary section. Put $M=I_q/I_q^2$ and $N=M^\vee=q^*\mathcal O_{\bar U}(q)$. For a chosen peripheral subgroup $L_q=\kappa_q(T)\subset\Pi$, the normalizer $N_E(L_q)$ fits in an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow T\longrightarrow N_E(L_q) \longrightarrow G\longrightarrow1. \tag{C.5} \] With the positive Kummer inertia convention of C3 its extension class is $c_1(N)$, and hence is $-c_1(M)$. More precisely, its image in $H^2(G,\mu_n)$ corresponds under the comparison map to the Kummer class of $N$ in $H^2(S,\mu_n)$; when $S$ is an \'etale $K(\pi,1)$ this comparison is an isomorphism. For type $(0,2)$ the same conclusion holds whenever the exact sequence of C4 holds (in particular over the arithmetic $K(\pi,1)$ bases of C7): here $L_q=\Pi=T$, its arithmetic normalizer is all of $E$, and the two distinguished boundary sections identify $U$ with the punctured normal line $N^\times$. Type $(1,0)$ has no cusp, so no normalizer extension of this kind is asserted there.
notes: Positive Kummer inertia gives +c1(normal), -c1(conormal). The requested moving-q example has colliding boundary and trivial normal line, so cannot distinguish sign.

statement: The arithmetic splitting and completed-unit criteria — \textup{[F14--F15; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 40--42; scans 81--82, 85.]} Let $S$ be smooth connected of finite type over a field finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, and suppose that $S$ is an \'etale $K(\pi,1)$. Then $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ is finitely generated, the integral continuous comparison in degree two is an isomorphism \[ H^2(G,T)\simeq H^2(S,T), \] and Kummer theory gives \[ H^1(G,T)\simeq H^1(S,T) \simeq\widehat{\mathcal O(S)^*} :=\varprojlim_n\mathcal O(S)^*/\mathcal O(S)^{*n}. \tag{C.6} \] For the boundary section of C6, (C.5) splits if and only if $M$, equivalently $N$, is a trivial line bundle. A global basis of $M$ is sufficient over any characteristic-zero base for which (C.5) exists. Here a ``uniformizer along $q$'' means a basis of $I_q/I_q^2$; the statement does not require a global equation of $q$ on an entire neighborhood of its image.
notes: Pic finite generation has arithmetic finite-type normal hypotheses. Continuous H2 comparison includes the derived-limit check. Surjective normalizer map need not split.

statement: The geometric torsor inside the completed torsor — \textup{[F15; \S3, manuscript p.\ 42; scan 85.]} Under the arithmetic hypotheses of C7, $\mathcal O(S)^*$ contains no nonidentity element divisible by every positive integer in that group. The completion map in (C.6) is injective. When $N$ is trivial, the set of its nowhere-zero sections is a torsor under $\mathcal O(S)^*$. Its tangential splittings inject into the set of $T$-conjugacy classes of splittings of (C.5), a torsor under $H^1(G,T)$. Under these actions the map of torsors is induced by the injective Kummer map \[ \mathcal O(S)^*\hookrightarrow\widehat{\mathcal O(S)^*}. \] For bases of the conormal line, rather than normal vectors, multiplying the basis by $a$ changes this Kummer class by $-\kappa(a)$.
notes: Ordinary units, without a circumflex, act on actual frames. Full splitting classes form completed-unit torsor.

statement: Divisorial failure of extension and tangential specialization — \textup{[F16; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 46--47; scans 93--95.]} Let $S$ be smooth integral in characteristic zero and let $f_K$ be a rational section of a smooth pair as in C1. Let $S'$ be its maximal open domain as a section of $U$. Every irreducible component of $S\setminus S'$ has codimension one. At the generic point of such a component $D_\alpha$, the proper extension meets a unique cusp, and \[ \mu_\alpha=\operatorname{ord}_{D_\alpha}(f_K^*z)>0 \] is its intersection multiplicity, independent of a unit multiple of the local cusp equation $z$. The sum $\sum_\alpha\mu_\alpha D_\alpha$ is an effective Cartier divisor because $S$ is regular. On an open subset $W$ of the regular locus of $D_\alpha$ where the compactified section and the cusp are defined, and where a uniformizer $t$ of $D_\alpha$ has been fixed, write $z\circ f=t^{\mu_\alpha}u$ with $u$ regular and invertible along $W$. The resulting conormal isomorphism is \[ f_W^*(I_q/I_q^2)\xrightarrow{\sim} (I_{D_\alpha}/I_{D_\alpha}^2)^{\otimes\mu_\alpha}, \qquad z\longmapsto u\,t^{\mu_\alpha}. \tag{C.7} \] It produces tangential specialization of the geometric section at every point of $W$, compatible with specialization inside $W$. Changing $t$ to $at$ replaces the leading coefficient by $a^{-\mu_\alpha}u$, and changes the associated Kummer class by $-\mu_\alpha\kappa(a)$ in the scalar-coordinate convention.
notes: All maps and hypotheses are stated in the TeX result and proof.

statement: The model-independent quotient (F18) — Let $X$ and $Y$ be proper, regular, integral finite-type $K$-schemes with function field $L$. Their finite \emph{\'etale} extensions of $L$ form the same full subcategory of finite separable $L$-algebras. Consequently their quotients $G_L\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1(X)$ and $G_L\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1(Y)$ have the same kernel, with the generic geometric point fixed. The assertion also holds in positive characteristic whenever these proper regular models exist. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~57, scans 115--116, ``ne d\'epend pas du mod\`ele $X$ choisi''.
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~57, scans 115--116, ``ne d\'epend pas du mod\`ele $X$ choisi''.

statement: Riemann--Zariski points and the noetherian correction (F21) — The inverse limit of all proper integral $K$-models of $L$, with its colimit local rings, has points exactly the valuation rings $V$ of $L$ containing $K$. This identification uses no resolution of singularities. Its noetherian local rings are exactly $L$ and the discrete valuation rings of $L/K$. A discrete valuation ring need not be divisorial: there exists one for $\mathbb Q(x,y)/\mathbb Q$ with residue field $\mathbb Q$ and hence manuscript codimension two. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~60--61, scans 121--123.

Explicit valuations with divisible value groups — For $K$ of characteristic zero and $L=K(x,y)$, the following valuations trivial on $K$ exist: \[ (\Gamma_v,\kappa(v))=(\mathbb Q,K),\qquad (\Gamma_v,\kappa(v))=(\mathbb Z[1/2],K). \] They have centers on the boundary of $(\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$, and their centers can lie on only one boundary component. This construction will supply the corrections to F19, F20, F22 and F25. \par\emph{Passages:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~59--65, scans 119--131.

Inertia, its ranks, and a splitting (F22) — For every valuation $v$ of $L/K$ there are a continuous exact sequence and a canonical pairing \[ 1\longrightarrow I_v\longrightarrow D_v\longrightarrow G_{\kappa(v)}\longrightarrow1, \qquad I_v\simeq\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q/\Gamma_v,\mu_\infty\bigr) \simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma_v,T). \] The sequence has a continuous splitting, with no canonical choice. The conjugation action on inertia is the cyclotomic action on the values in $T$. More precisely, \[ I_v\simeq\prod_{\ell}\mathbb Z_\ell(1)^{r_\ell},\qquad r_\ell=\dim_{\mathbb F_\ell}(\Gamma_v/\ell\Gamma_v) \le\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q) \le\operatorname{trdeg}_K L-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(v). \] The product decomposition is noncanonical. Neither the manuscript codimension nor, in general, the rational rank determines the inertia group. In particular $\Gamma_v=\mathbb Q$ gives $I_v=1$, and $\Gamma_v=\mathbb Z[1/2]$ gives $I_v=\prod_{\ell\ne2}\mathbb Z_\ell(1)$. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~61, scan 124, ``des $T_\infty^\alpha$ essentiellement'' and ``scinder''.
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~61, scan 124, ``des $T_\infty^\alpha$ essentiellement'' and ``scinder''.
notes: Correct primewise ranks are dim_F_l Gamma/lGamma; rational rank alone is insufficient.

statement: The exact inertia normalizer for arbitrary valuations (F19) — Let $I_v\ne1$. Let $\Delta_v$ be the largest divisible convex subgroup of the ordered group $\Gamma_v$, and let $w$ be the coarsening with value group $\Gamma_v/\Delta_v$, with its prolongation induced by $\overline v$. Then \[ I_w=I_v,\qquad N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_w, \qquad N_{P_{L/K}}(I_v)=D_w\cap P_{L/K}. \] There is an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow I_v\longrightarrow N_{P_{L/K}}(I_v) \longrightarrow G_{\kappa(w)\overline K}\longrightarrow1. \] Here $\kappa(w)\overline K$ is the compositum inside the residue algebraic closure induced by $\overline v$. Consequently geometric self-normalization holds precisely when that compositum is separably closed. The arithmetic identity $N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_v$ holds precisely when the induced residual valuation $v/w$ is henselian on $\kappa(w)$. It holds in particular for every rank-one valuation with nontrivial inertia, including every DVR. For $I_v=1$ the inertia normalizer is all of $G_L$. \par\emph{Passages:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~59 and 63, scans 119--120 and 127.
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~59 and 63, scans 119--120 and 127.
notes: Actual subgroup equality with compatible prolongations; removes largest divisible convex subgroup.

statement: Both unqualified self-normalization assertions (F19) — The geometric assertion $N_{P_{L/K}}(I_v)=I_v$ is false for the $x$-adic valuation of $L=\mathbb Q(x,y)$ over $K=\mathbb Q$. The arithmetic assertion $N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_v$ is false for general valuations with $I_v\ne1$, already for $L=\mathbb Q(x,y,z)$. D5 is the exact replacement. \par\emph{Passages:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~59 and 63, scans 119--120 and 127.
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~59 and 63, scans 119--120 and 127.

statement: Detecting a center: the DVR assertion and its arbitrary-valuation extension (F20) — For a DVR $V$ of $L/K$ and an elementary tower $U/K$ of smooth curves with good relative compactifications and no fiber of type $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$, the homomorphism $I_v\to\pi_1(U)$ is trivial precisely when $V$ has a center on $U$. For an arbitrary valuation, having a center still implies that this homomorphism is trivial, but its converse is false even for $U=(\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$. Outside the indicated curve-type hypothesis the converse fails already for $\mathbb A^1$ and a DVR. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~59, scan 120, ``A t-on une r\'eciproque?''.
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~59, scan 120, ``A t-on une r\'eciproque?''.

statement: Restriction of valuation rings and of local Galois groups (F23) — Let $K\subset L_1\subset L$ and $V_1=V\cap L_1$. Then $V_1$ is a valuation ring with fraction field $L_1$, and reduction embeds $\kappa(V_1)$ into $\kappa(V)$. With compatible algebraic closures and prolongations, restriction gives continuous homomorphisms \[ D_V\longrightarrow D_{V_1},\qquad I_V\longrightarrow I_{V_1}. \] Their existence does not assert that either homomorphism is injective or surjective. If $L_1/K$ has transcendence degree one and $\kappa(V)$ is algebraic over $K$, $V_1$ is the DVR of a closed point on the proper smooth curve with function field $L_1$. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~62, scans 125--126.

The written function-field formula at scan 127 (F24) — Assume here that $K$ is finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$. The two assertions (32)--(33) with subscript $L$ have the same truth value, but their common assertion of triviality is false. For $L=\mathbb Q(t)$, the $t$-adic place, and a decomposition section $s:G_{\mathbb Q}\to D_v\subset G_L$, both fixed groups are $I_v=T\ne1$. Under the quotient to $\pi_1(U)$ for $U=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{1,2,\infty\}$, this section becomes the point section at $0$ and both fixed groups become trivial. For point sections of elementary anabelian $U$ the corresponding $U$-formulas hold. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~63, scans 127--128, (32)--(33).

Normalizers of decomposition groups (completion of F19) — Put $H=L_v^h$. If $\kappa(v)$ is not separably closed, then \[ N_{G_L}(D_v)=D_v. \] If $\kappa(v)$ is separably closed, then $D_v=I_v$; its normalizer is $D_w$ as in D5 when $I_v\ne1$, and is $G_L$ when $I_v=1$. In all cases $N_{P_{L/K}}(D_v)=N_{G_L}(D_v)\cap P_{L/K}$. For the geometric decomposition subgroup $D_v^{\mathrm{geom}}=D_v\cap P_{L/K}$, the same alternatives hold with $G_L,L,\kappa(v)$ replaced by $P_{L/K},L\overline K,\kappa(v)\overline K$: it is self-normalizing when this last residue field is not separably closed; otherwise it equals $I_v$ and D5 gives its normalizer. \par\emph{Passages:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~59 and 63, scans 119--120 and 127.
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~59 and 63, scans 119--120 and 127.
notes: Includes normalizer in arithmetic group and geometric decomposition subgroup normalizer.

statement: The local group and the two local injectivity assertions (F25, 1$^\circ$) — For the strict henselization $R=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ there is a parameter-labelled isomorphism \[ \pi_1\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}R[1/(z_1\cdots z_r)]\bigr)=T^r. \] Its $i$th factor is the meridian of $D_i$, characterized by its action on compatible roots of $z_i$. For an ordinary point $x$, the henselian local group fits into \[ 1\longrightarrow T^r\longrightarrow \pi_1\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cap U\bigr) \longrightarrow G_{\kappa(x)}\longrightarrow1. \] When $\kappa(x)/K$ is finite, injectivity of the entire local homomorphism into $\pi_1(U)$ is equivalent to injectivity of its restriction to $T^r$. This equivalence does not hold for general nonclosed points. If $U$ is a hyperbolic elementary polycurve, each individual branch meridian $T\to\pi_1(U)$ is injective, so the geometric local homomorphism is injective whenever $r=1$. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~64--65, scans 130--131, the two versions of 1$^\circ$.

notes: The whole-local-group equivalence needs finite residue over K; nonclosed-point counterexample supplied.

statement: The blow-up map, and the product compactification (F25, 1$^\circ$) — For $U=(\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$, blow up $(0,2)$ in $(\mathbb P^1)^2$. At the intersection of the exceptional divisor with the strict transform of $x=0$, the local homomorphism is \[ T^2\longrightarrow T\hookrightarrow\pi_1(U),\qquad (a,b)\longmapsto a+b. \] Its kernel is $\{(a,-a):a\in T\}$. Thus 1$^\circ$ is false even for an elementary hyperbolic surface. On the original product compactification of any two smooth hyperbolic curves, every geometric local meridian homomorphism is injective. That product compactification is terminal among smooth proper compactifications of the same $U$ with simple normal crossings boundary: every such compactification has a unique morphism to it inducing the identity on $U$. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~64--65, scans 130--131, the blow-up margin and ``Minimalit\'e''.
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~64--65, scans 130--131, the blow-up margin and ``Minimalit\'e''.
notes: Terminality is among smooth proper SNC compactifications of a product of two hyperbolic curves.

statement: The image of an arbitrary valuation at a crossing (F25, 2$^\circ$) — Let a valuation $v$ have center $x$ on $X$, let the branches through $x$ have parameters $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, and put $\gamma_i=v(z_i)$. The homomorphism from valuation inertia to the local geometric group is \[ \rho_v:\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma_v,T)\longrightarrow T^r, \qquad \chi\longmapsto(\chi(\gamma_1),\ldots,\chi(\gamma_r)). \] It is dual to the homomorphism of discrete torsion groups \[ \psi_v:\mathbb Q^r/\mathbb Z^r\longrightarrow (\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q)/\Gamma_v, \qquad (q_i)\longmapsto\sum_iq_i\gamma_i\pmod{\Gamma_v}. \] Consequently $\operatorname{im}\rho_v$ is open exactly when $\ker\psi_v$ is finite, and it is all of $T^r$ exactly when $\ker\psi_v=0$. More explicitly, openness requires rational independence of the $\gamma_i$. Under that independence, with $\Lambda=\sum_i\mathbb Z\gamma_i$, \[ \ker\psi_v=(\Gamma_v\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{\gamma_i\})/\Lambda. \] Thus openness is exactly finite saturation index, and surjectivity is exactly equality of this saturation with $\Lambda$. Equality of rational rank and number of branches alone is insufficient. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~64--65, scans 130--131, 2$^\circ$ and the monomial example (36).
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~64--65, scans 130--131, 2$^\circ$ and the monomial example (36).
notes: Exact dual saturation criterion; includes divisible groups and nondivisorial DVRs.

statement: The precise criterion for the stratum extension (F26) — Work first over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For a nonempty connected open stratum \[ S=D_J^\circ=\Bigl(\bigcap_{j\in J}D_j\Bigr)\setminus\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\notin J}D_i\Bigr), \qquad L_j=N_{D_j/X}|_S, \] let $P=\prod_{j\in J,S}L_j^\times$ be the product of the punctured normal line bundles. Its fundamental groups have the exact homotopy sequence \[ \pi_2^{\mathrm{et}}(S)\xrightarrow{\partial}T^J \longrightarrow\pi_1(P)\longrightarrow\pi_1(S)\longrightarrow1. \] The same sequence computes the punctured tubular neighborhood of this stratum. With positive fiber meridians and the clutching convention specified below, \[ \partial(a)=\bigl(\langle c_1(L_j),a\rangle\bigr)_{j\in J}. \] In particular (37) is left exact precisely when these Chern evaluations vanish. An equivalent criterion, involving only finite covers and line bundles, is: for every positive integer $n$ there is a connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover $S'\to S$ such that every $L_j|_{S'}$ is an $n$th tensor power in $\operatorname{Pic}(S')$. Vanishing of $\pi_2^{\mathrm{et}}(S)$ suffices, but is not necessary. Over a nonclosed field the same assertion descends with the cyclotomic action and the permutation of geometric branch labels. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~66--67, scans 133--135, (37) and its qualification.
depends_on: E1; Borne-Emsalem-Stix Proposition8 proof, Proposition16 proof
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~66--67, scans 133--135, (37) and its qualification.
notes: Finite-cover/nth-root criterion avoids assuming profinite completion preserves arbitrary exact sequences.

statement: Nonzero Chern boundary for an elementary hyperbolic variety (F26) — The homomorphism $\pi_2(D_J^\circ)\to T^J$ need not vanish for an elementary anabelian $U$, even when $U$ is a product of three copies of the thrice-punctured line. Thus the proposed extension (37) is not left exact for every simple normal crossings compactification of an elementary variety. \par\emph{Passage:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~67, scan 135, ``On va donc admettre que (37) d\'efinit bien une structure d'extension''.
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript p.~67, scan 135, ``On va donc admettre que (37) d\'efinit bien une structure d'extension''.

statement: Algebraic residues need not be finite; the arithmetic openness criterion — A valuation of a finitely generated extension $L/K$ can have residue field algebraic and infinite over $K$, even when it is a DVR. For a valuation with algebraic residue field centered at $x$ on $X$, the entire homomorphism $D_v\to\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}^h\cap U)$ has open image precisely when both $[\kappa(v):\kappa(x)]$ and $|\ker\psi_v|$ of E3 are finite. Its image is the entire local group precisely when $\kappa(v)=\kappa(x)$ and $\ker\psi_v=0$. Thus the inserted ``fini'' on scans 124 and 130 is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of algebraicity. \par\emph{Passages:} cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~61 and 64--65, scans 124 and 130--131.
his_places: cote 149, \S4, manuscript pp.~61 and 64--65, scans 124 and 130--131.

statement: The starred arithmetic centralizer assertion — Fix $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ and write $G_{\mathbf Q}$ for its full profinite Galois group. For every open subgroup $\Gamma'\subset G_{\mathbf Q}$, let $\Gamma'^{\circ}$ be the kernel of its cyclotomic character. Then \[ C_{G_{\mathbf Q}}(\Gamma'^{\circ})=1. \] \passage{Cote 149, \S2, manuscript p.~22, scan 45, starred ``\`a v\'erifier !''.}
notes: The attached return is cited under explicit prompt authorization; its unramified-prime supplement is retained.

statement: The local extension and the normalizer correction — Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\mathbf Q$, let $U=X\setminus D$ be a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve, and let $c\in D(K)$. Choose a geometric base point and a lift of $c$ to the normalized universal covering. Its inertia $I_c$ and decomposition group $D_c$ satisfy \[ D_c=N_{E_U}(I_c),\qquad 1\longrightarrow I_c=\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1) \longrightarrow D_c\longrightarrow G_K\longrightarrow1, \qquad C_{E_U}(I_c)=D_c\cap p^{-1}(\ker\chi_K). \] A local parameter supplies a splitting. The $I_c$-conjugacy classes of splittings form a torsor under $H^1(K,\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1))=\varprojlim_n K^*/K^{*n}$. \passage{Cote 149, \S3, manuscript p.~26 and continuation, scans 53--54, formulas (2)--(3).}
notes: Exact centralizer formula retained; a uniformizer supplies the splitting.

statement: Embedded, disjoint cusp packets, including type $(0,3)$ — Under the hypotheses of F10a the map from local splitting classes to $\pi_1(U_{\overline K})$-conjugacy classes of sections of $E_U\to G_K$ is injective. Its image is disjoint from the classes of points of $U(K)$ and from every other rational cusp packet. These assertions hold after each finite extension of $K$. \passage{Cote 149, \S3, manuscript pp.~26--27, scans 54--55, Proposition and its margin.}
notes: All hyperbolic types including (0,3).

statement: The first assertion of scan 54 in type $(0,2)$ — For $U=\mathbf G_{m,K}$ each of the two rational cusp packets equals the entire set of section classes, and in particular contains every point section. The first assertion of scan 54 is therefore false in this type. For every affine characteristic-zero type with nontrivial geometric fundamental group, the disjointness conclusion holds exactly in the hyperbolic cases covered by F10b. \passage{Cote 149, \S3, continuation of manuscript p.~26, scan 54.}
notes: Type (0,2) is an explicit failure of disjointness of point and cusp packets.

statement: The 1-faithfulness assertion over the stated base — \textup{[F9; \S2, manuscript p.\ 25; scan 52.]} For a locally noetherian scheme $S$, a reduced $S$-scheme $X$ locally of finite presentation, and an $S$-scheme $Y$ locally of finite presentation, the map \[ \operatorname{Hom}_S(X,Y)\longrightarrow \pi_0\operatorname{Hom}_{S_{\mathrm{et}}}(X_{\mathrm{et}},Y_{\mathrm{et}}) \tag{F.1} \] is injective. Thus the manuscript's 1-faithfulness statement does not need its tentative characteristic-zero restriction.
notes: Relative 2-isomorphism must have the identity base component. Carlson–Stix Lemma5.4 needs reduced source, not reduced fibres.

statement: The precise full-faithfulness theorems — \textup{[F9; \S2, manuscript pp.\ 25--26; scans 51--52.]} Let $\mathrm{UH}$ denote the universal homeomorphisms. The functor \[ (\operatorname{Sch}^{\mathrm{ft}}_k)[\mathrm{UH}^{-1}] \longrightarrow \operatorname{RTop}^{\mathrm{pin}}_{k_{\mathrm{et}}}, \qquad X\longmapsto X_{\mathrm{et}}, \tag{F.2} \] is fully faithful for every infinite field $k$ finitely generated over its prime field, and for every sub-$p$-adic field $k$ (a subfield of a finitely generated extension of some $\mathbb Q_p$). The first assertion is Carlson--Haine--Wolf, Theorem 0.1; the second is Carlson--Stix, Theorem A (=Theorem 4.1). In characteristic zero, the localization is represented by seminormalization; in positive characteristic it is represented by perfection. There is also the following relative assertion. Let $S$ be noetherian, Nagata, geometrically unibranch, and suppose each generic residue field of $S$ is sub-$p$-adic. Restrict to finite-type $S$-schemes each of whose irreducible components is universally open over $S$. After inverting $\mathrm{UH}$, the topos functor into chivalrous geometric morphisms over $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ is fully faithful. This is Carlson--Stix, Theorem D (=Theorem 6.12 and Proposition 6.11).
notes: Pinned maps over fields; chivalrous maps for the stated relative theorem. Arbitrary topos maps are not covered.

statement: Fullness into all topoi, and fullness over an algebraically closed field — \textup{[F9; \S2, manuscript p.\ 25; scan 52.]} Without a restriction on geometric morphisms, the proposed fullness fails already over $\mathbb Q$. With pinned morphisms retained, it fails over $\mathbb C$, even for smooth proper genus-one curves and even after universal homeomorphisms are inverted.
notes: All maps and hypotheses are stated in the TeX result and proof.

statement: A finite-field obstruction to pinned fullness — \textup{[F9 and the characteristic question in its margin; \S2, manuscript p.\ 25; scan 52.]} Pinned fullness after universal-homeomorphism localization fails for $\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb F_3}$ over $\mathbb F_3$. Thus the positive transcendence-degree hypothesis in the positive-characteristic case of F9.2 has an actual obstruction.
notes: Finite-field counterexample checks every possible natural 2-isomorphism, not just the canonical Frobenius one.

statement: The proposed function-field automorphism test — \textup{[F9; \S2, manuscript p.\ 25; scan 52.]} Let $k$ be a number field, $C/k$ a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of any genus, $L=k(C)$, and $\Delta=\ker(G_L\to G_k)$. Then \[ \operatorname{Aut}_k(C)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Isom}_{G_k}(G_L,G_L)/\operatorname{Inn}(\Delta) \tag{F.3} \] is bijective, with the usual contravariance on function fields. In particular the additional requirement that the automorphism preserve all loop subgroups is unnecessary for this conclusion; the automorphism obtained from (F.3) preserves them by functoriality of valuations.
notes: All maps and hypotheses are stated in the TeX result and proof.

statement: The nonabelian criterion and the valid forward implications — \textup{[F17; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 49--51; scans 100--103.]} Let $R$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$ and residue characteristic $p\geq0$. Let $U=\bar U\setminus D$ be a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve over $K$, with $\bar U$ smooth proper and $D$ reduced and geometrically \'etale. Good reduction means a smooth proper model of $\bar U$ over $R$ on which the boundary extends to a finite \'etale divisor. Good reduction is equivalent to trivial inertia in $\operatorname{Out}(\Pi^{(p')})$; it is also equivalent to trivial inertia in $\operatorname{Out}(\Pi^{(\ell)})$ for one, equivalently every, prime $\ell\ne p$. For $p=0$ the pro-prime-to-$p$ group is the full geometric group, so this proves exactly a)$\Leftrightarrow$b). Good reduction implies c) and d) with prime-to-$p$ coefficients, through the characteristic quotient maps $\Pi^{(p')}\to\Pi^{(p'),\mathrm{ab}}\to H_1(U_{\bar K},\mathbb Z_\ell)$. When the residue field is finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, a) and b) imply e) for every splitting of the residue exact sequence: the resulting outer action is that of the actual smooth special fibre.
notes: All maps and hypotheses are stated in the TeX result and proof.

statement: A compact-type genus-two counterexample, including class two — \textup{[F17; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 49--51; scans 100, 102--103.]} Over $R=\mathbb Q[[t]]$, the smooth projective completion of \[ C_t:\quad y^2=(x^3-t^6)(x^3-1) \tag{F.4} \] has genus two, bad reduction, and trivial inertia on all of its abelianizations. Its inertia action is even trivial on every class-two nilpotent geometric quotient. Its full outer inertia action is nontrivial. Thus c)$\Rightarrow$a) and d)$\Rightarrow$a) are false for proper curves.
notes: Explicit genus2 compact-type model, separating twist trivial on class2 but nontrivial on full group.

statement: Colliding cusps detected by class-two monodromy — \textup{[F17; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 50--51; scans 102--103.]} Let \[ U_t=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q((t))}\setminus\{0,t,1,\infty\}. \tag{F.5} \] It has bad marked reduction and trivial inertia on $\Pi^{\mathrm{ab}}=\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)^3$, while inertia acts nontrivially in the outer automorphism group of its class-two pro-$\ell$ quotient for every prime $\ell$.
notes: Four colliding marked points; abelian inertia trivial, outer class2 twist nontrivial for every prime.

statement: Homological unramifiedness need not give a geometric residue action — \textup{[F17; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 50--51; scans 101--103, condition e).]} For the curve (F.5), choose the coefficient splitting $G_{\mathbb Q}\to G_{\mathbb Q((t))}$ which fixes compatible roots of $t$. The resulting outer action on $\widehat F_3$ is not realized by a smooth hyperbolic curve over any finite extension of $\mathbb Q$. Thus neither c) nor d) implies e), even allowing the finite extension in e).
notes: Five cyclotomically normalized loops, but any curve with geometric group free rank3 has at most4 cusps. Checked by second agent against Nakamura2.1.1.

statement: A geometric residue action can coexist with bad reduction — \textup{[F17 and an additional flagged step; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 50--51; scans 101, 103.]} Over $K=\mathbb Q((t))$ let \[ E_t:y^2=x^3-t^2x,\qquad U_t=E_t\setminus\{O\}. \tag{F.8} \] It has bad reduction. For every continuous splitting $s:G_{\mathbb Q}\to G_K$, however, its restricted outer action is realized by a once-punctured elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ itself. Thus e)$\Rightarrow$a) is false even with ``every splitting'', and bad reduction alone does not force the proposed residue action to be nongeometric.
notes: Ramified quadratic twist; every residue splitting yields an actual quadratic twist over Q. Refutes e⇒a even with every-splitting quantifier.

statement: Stable bad reduction obstructs every geometric residue action — \textup{[F17; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 49--51; scans 100--103; supplied R4 and H2.]} Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$ finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$. Let $U/K$ be a hyperbolic curve whose smooth proper compactification and reduced boundary have a stable marked model $(\mathcal C,\mathcal D)$ over $R$. Put $\Pi=\pi_1(U_{\bar K})$, with its full profinite topology. For a continuous section $s:G_k\to G_K$ of the residue map, let \[ E_s=\pi_1(U)\mathbin{\times}_{G_K,s}G_k. \] Every geometric node of $\mathcal C_k$ gives an injected subgroup $I_e\simeq\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)$ of $\Pi$, well defined up to $\Pi$-conjugacy. In $E_s$ it is essentially cyclotomically normalized: after a finite extension of $k$ fixing that node and its two branches, a closed subgroup of its normalizer maps onto the residue Galois group and acts on $I_e$ by the cyclotomic character. This holds for every $s$. Distinct geometric nodes and cusps give distinct conjugacy classes of maximal procyclic subgroups. If $\mathcal C_k$ has a node, the extension $E_s$ is not isomorphic, over $G_k$, to the arithmetic fundamental-group extension of any smooth hyperbolic curve over $k$, and it does not become so after any finite extension of $k$. If $r>0$ is the number of geometric cusps, the number of conjugacy classes of essentially cyclotomically normalized maximal procyclic subgroups of $\Pi$ equals $r$ exactly when this stable marked model is smooth. In the singular case it is at least $r+n$, where $n>0$ is the number of geometric nodes.
depends_on: F17.2; CF_Hoshi2009; CF_HoshiMochizukiNodes; CF_Illusie2002; CF_MochizukiComb2007; PriorCyclotomic
notes: Full logarithmic comparison proved over a henselian DVR with residue field finitely generated over Q. Every stable node is injected and essentially cyclotomically normalized after fixing node and branches. Proper and affine stable-bad residue actions are nongeometric after every finite residue extension; graph quotient and tree cusp-rank arguments include the one-cusp case.

statement: Condition e detects potential good reduction — \textup{[F17; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 50--51; scans 101--103; the correction proposed in the reader's notes.]} Let $R,K,k,U$ have the hypotheses of F17.6 except that a stable model over $R$ is not assumed. Fix any continuous residue splitting $s:G_k\to G_K$. The following three assertions are equivalent: $U$ has good marked reduction after a finite extension of $K$; the outer action obtained through $s$ is realized by a smooth hyperbolic curve over $k$; that action is realized after restriction to $G_{k'}$ for some finite extension $k'/k$. Consequently ``some splitting'' and ``every splitting'' give the same condition e), and allowing a finite residue extension does not enlarge it in these hypotheses.
notes: For every chosen residue splitting, e is equivalent to potential good marked reduction. The potentially-good special fibre descends to k itself via the actual finite Galois action extended to the stable model and explicit projective descent. The full action comparison uses Q=Gal(K1/K)×_{Gal(k1/k)}G_k and q∘s(g)=(alpha(g),g), retaining the infinite arithmetic action. Finite-residue-extension and no

statement: Individual node invariance needs the finite-extension qualification — \textup{[F17; \S3, manuscript pp.\ 50--51; scans 101--103; the literal individual-node assertion in supplied H2(b).]} The full residue Galois group can permute the node groups. The strongest uniform conclusion used in F17.6 is invariance under an open subgroup fixing the node and its branches, with cyclotomic action there.
notes: Literal invariance under all of G_k is false: the two nodes of y2=(x2+1)^2(x2-2)+t over Q[[t]] are exchanged. Their groups are distinct by commensurable terminality. Discriminant and node jets checked exactly.

statement: Local form and invariant complex structure — A nonidentity orientation-preserving finite-order homeomorphism of a connected surface has isolated fixed points, each with fixed-point index $+1$. A cyclic finite group acting by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms on a surface of finite type preserves a complex structure of a smooth algebraic curve of that type. \passage{Cote 142, opening, continuation of manuscript p.~1 (scan 6), and p.~3 (scan 7). The reading order is 4, 6, 5, 7.}
notes: Orientation-preserving hypothesis is exact; reflection supplies the other case.

statement: Periodic homological rigidity, with the level-two exception — For a hyperbolic surface $S$, a finite-order homeomorphism acting trivially on $H_1(S,\mathbf Z)$ is the identity. The same conclusion follows from trivial action on $H_1(S,\mathbf Z/n)$ for any $n\geq3$. In particular, a periodic homeomorphism isotopic to the identity is the identity. The assertion with $n=2$ is false: $z\mapsto-z$ on $(\mathbf R^2/\mathbf Z^2)\setminus\{0\}$ is a counterexample of type $(1,1)$. \passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript p.~2, scan 5; continuation p.~3, scan 7.}
notes: Integral and mod-n n≥3 rigidity; explicit n=2 failure.

statement: The complete-curve translation assertion used in scan 7 — For a complex hyperbolic curve $Y$ in its generalized Jacobian torsor, an equality $Y+u=Y$ implies $u=0$. The assertion involving a nonempty open subset $W\subset Y$ and only $W+u\subset Y$ requires the correction given in Part~B; that assertion fails for type $(1,1)$. \passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript p.~3, scan 7; cote 149, \S1, manuscript p.~18, scan 37.}
notes: Full stability Y+u=Y; does not assert the false open-subset lemma.

statement: Components, stabilizers, and the finiteness of covering orbits — Let $X,Y$ be connected hyperbolic finite-type surfaces. In the space of orientation-preserving finite covering maps $X\to Y$, each connected component is homeomorphic to $A_0(X)$ and is contractible. Its isotopy class has stabilizer, under precomposition by $M(X)$, exactly the finite deck group of that covering, embedded by its mapping classes. There are finitely many $M(X)$-orbits of isotopy classes. As the target $Y$ varies, a finite subgroup of $M(X)$ occurs as such a stabilizer exactly when it has a free realization on $X$ by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms. \passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript pp.~1--3, scans 3,4,6--8.}
notes: Compact-open connected components identified with identity homeomorphism group, including openness proof.

statement: The finite-subgroup margin of scan 8 — The assertion that every finite subgroup of $M(X)$ occurs as a deck stabilizer for the fixed source $X$ is false. A hyperelliptic involution on a closed genus-two surface gives a subgroup of order two which cannot occur. \passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript p.~3, scan 8, first NB.}
notes: Free realization is the exact criterion; genus-two involution refutes all-finite-subgroups margin.

statement: Hausdorff profinite envelope under the finite-index condition — For every small $C_0$ satisfying the preceding finite-index condition there is a category $\widehat C_0$ with the same objects and \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{\widehat C_0}(X,Y)= \coprod_{uA_X\in\operatorname{Hom}_{C_0}(X,Y)/A_X} \overline{S_u}\backslash\widehat A_X. \tag{G.1} \] Its Hom spaces are locally compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected; composition is continuous and associative, and extends composition in $C_0$. Each double orbit also equals the quotient of $\widehat A_X\times\widehat A_Y$ by the closure of $G_u$, with the opposite-action convention dictated by $bu=ua$. The functor $C_0\to\widehat C_0$ has dense image in each Hom space. It is conservative, and \[ \operatorname{Isom}_{\widehat C_0}(X,Y)= \operatorname{Isom}_{C_0}(X,Y) \mathop{\times}^{A_X}\widehat A_X, \qquad \operatorname{Aut}_{\widehat C_0}(X)=\widehat A_X. \tag{G.2} \] The displayed contracted product for isomorphisms is a torsor product, so no closure correction is needed there. Among Hausdorff topological categories with continuous composition and profinite automorphism groups, every functor from $C_0$ extends uniquely to a continuous functor from this envelope whenever the target Hom topology induces its stated profinite automorphism-group topology. This characterizes the envelope up to a unique isomorphism fixing $C_0$. \passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript pp.~4--6, scans 9--12 and 14; formulas (12)--(17), NB of scan 11, and conservativity NB of scan 14.}
notes: General separated profinite envelope, actions, continuous associative composition and conservativity proved.

statement: Two missing qualifications in the general categorical formulas — The set-theoretic contracted products in scan 12 need not be Hausdorff under the finite-index condition alone. Also the abstract completion $\widehat G_u$ need not embed in the product of the completed endpoint automorphism groups. The corrected subgroup in G6 is $\overline G_u$. \passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript pp.~5--6, scans 12 and 14, (17) and the final NB.}
notes: Two explicit categories prove both corrections.

statement: The surface category and the marked-factorization assertion — The isotopy category of orientation-preserving finite covers of connected hyperbolic surfaces satisfies the condition of G6. Its finite deck groups embed in the profinite completions of the source mapping-class groups. For this category, $\widehat G_u\to\widehat M(X)\times\widehat M(Y)$ is injective and its image is the arrow stabilizer. Every completed arrow has a factorization $u\widehat f_0$, where $u$ is an original finite cover and $\widehat f_0$ a completed isomorphism; the resulting \emph{marked factorization} is determined up to a unique original isomorphism over the target. \passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript pp.~5--6, scans 11 and 14.}
depends_on: G2; G4; G6; G_Paris Theorem1.4; G_FarbMargalit Theorem8.8
notes: Finite deck group is closed and separated; full residual finiteness is proved.

statement: Injectivity alone does not give the general uniqueness claim — For an arbitrary category satisfying the finite-index condition, the injectivity of every $S_u\to\widehat A_X$ does not by itself imply the marked-factorization uniqueness asserted in scan 14. Closedness of its image is also needed. Finite stabilizers, as in G8, have this property. \passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript p.~6, scan 14.}
notes: Dense stabilizer Z in hatZ gives failure of the stated general hypothesis.

statement: The category with already profinite automorphism groups — Let $C$ be a small category with profinite automorphism groups $A_X$. For every arrow $u:X\to Y$, suppose that $G_u=\{(a,b):bu=ua\}$ is closed in $A_X\times A_Y$ and its image $H_u$ in $A_Y$ has finite index. Give each double orbit its compact quotient topology, and give each Hom set the disjoint union topology. Composition is continuous. The image $H_u$ is closed and open, and the right $A_X$-orbits are open in each double orbit. \passage{Cote 142, manuscript pp.~4--5, scans 10--11, especially (14)--(16).}
notes: Actual composition in an already profinite-automorphism category is continuous under the stated conditions.

statement: The doubtful homology qualification in scan 5 — For orientation-preserving periodic homeomorphisms of a hyperbolic finite-type surface, trivial action on ordinary $H_1$ or on Borel--Moore $H_1$ with integral coefficients implies the identity. The same is true with coefficients $\mathbf Z/n$, $n\geq3$. Without the orientation-preserving hypothesis, still for periodic homeomorphisms, the Borel--Moore version is false, whereas the ordinary version remains G2. Replacing either by the homology of the compactification alone is also false. \passage{Cote 142, manuscript p.~2, scan 5: the doubtful word following $H_1$, transcribed as ``propre''.}
notes: Explicit intersection pairing and two counterexamples test the alternatives without settling paleography.

statement: An affine hyperbolic polycurve need not immerse in a semiabelian variety — The semiabelian-immersion assertion on scan 26, repeated parenthetically on scan 32, is false for the class of successive elementary hyperbolic fibrations used in Corollary 1(b). There is a smooth affine hyperbolic polycurve of dimension two every morphism from which to a semiabelian variety contracts its curve fibres; this occurs even when both levels have genus zero. This gives sweep rows ZAB1 and ZAB6 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~12, 15 and 17, scans 26, 32 and 36), including the parenthetical claim that genus-zero fibres supply a global torus immersion. B5 proves the stated corollaries without this assertion.
depends_on: Milne AV I.3.2 and I.1.5; explicit diagonal finite quotients; unit divisors; AB_checks.py
notes: Sweep ZAB1 and ZAB6. Gives examples with both levels genus2 and with both levels genus0. Every map to any semiabelian target contracts the fibre.

statement: The field-map image, conservativity, and the limit groupoid — For a finitely generated field extension $L/F$, restriction $G_L\to G_F$ has open image $G_{F_s}$, where $F_s$ is the relative separable algebraic closure of $F$ in $L$. The map is injective exactly when $L/F$ is algebraic, and is an isomorphism exactly when $L/F$ is finite purely inseparable. Thus the field functor of scans 5--6 is conservative in characteristic zero, and becomes conservative after inverting finite purely inseparable extensions in positive characteristic. For an arbitrary field $F=\varinjlim F_i$, where $F_i$ runs through its finitely generated prime-field subfields, the compatible absolute groups satisfy $G_F\simeq\varprojlim G_{F_i}$; the analogous statements hold for the profinite groupoids and their finite-cover topoi. Keeping the whole pro-system retains the faithfulness of B10, whereas taking only its limit does not. This closes sweep row ZAB2 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~2--3, scans 5--8).
depends_on: Finite separable algebra descent; divisorial Kummer extension; pro-category Hom formula; B10
notes: Sweep ZAB2. All restriction and limit maps are typed. The marked pro-system is distinguished by a precise comparison from its inverse-limit groupoid.

statement: Cofinal Artin models and the dimension of their groups — In characteristic zero every smooth integral variety has a dense open which is a tower of affine smooth hyperbolic curves with smooth proper compactifications and finite \'etale boundary. Thus such opens are cofinal among models of a finitely generated field, and their full geometric groups are successive extensions of nonabelian free profinite groups. A tower of length $n$ has $\ell$-cohomological dimension exactly $n$ for every prime. This closes the additional assertions on scans 10--13, sweep row ZAB3 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~4--6).
depends_on: Projection to a transcendence basis; spreading smooth curves and boundary; C4; A3; Serre finite-index theorem; Hochschild–Serre and Shapiro
notes: Sweep ZAB3. Cofinal smooth affine hyperbolic Artin towers and exact cd_l of their geometric groups, including the lower bound.

statement: Reconstruction of a centerless extension and uniqueness of lifted maps — For a profinite extension $1\to P\to E\to\Gamma\to1$ with $Z(P)=1$, the outer action determines the extension, with its identified kernel and quotient, by \[ E\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \operatorname{Aut}(P)\times_{\operatorname{Out}(P)}\Gamma, \qquad e\longmapsto(\operatorname{int}(e)|_P,\bar e). \] Use the compact-open topology on continuous automorphisms and the quotient topology on outer automorphisms; the displayed pullback is profinite because it is isomorphic to $E$. If two extension maps over $\Gamma$ restrict to the same map $P\to P'$, and its image has trivial centralizer in $P'$, the extension maps are equal. Conversely a continuous homomorphism $\varphi:P\to P'$ whose class modulo target inner automorphisms commutes with the two outer $\Gamma$-actions, and whose image has trivial centralizer in $P'$, extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism $E\to E'$ over $\Gamma$. These are the formal claims of scans 16--20 and 29, sweep row ZAB4 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~7--9, 14). They do not require $\operatorname{Aut}(P)$ itself to be profinite for an arbitrary infinitely generated $P$.
depends_on: Compact-open topology; centerless pullback reconstruction; direct conjugation computation
notes: Sweep ZAB4. Gives the actual extension isomorphism and uniqueness of lifted homomorphisms. Does not call Aut(P) profinite for arbitrary infinite-rank P.

statement: The semiabelian Albanese homology claim for arbitrary reduced sources — For a general reduced connected finite-type scheme, a universal semiabelian recipient of pointed morphisms need not have the same $\ell$-adic $H_1$. Thus the assertion numbered 3 on scan 25 does not justify Corollary 1(a) in all of its stated source generality. B3 supplies a proof in that generality. This is sweep row ZAB5 (149, section 1, manuscript p.~12, scan 25).
depends_on: Explicit nodal normalization; complex finite-cover comparison; cyclic chain covers; AB_checks.py
notes: Sweep ZAB5. The pointed semiabelian recipient is zero for the nodal rational cubic, whereas H1 is Z_l. B3 avoids the failed comparison.

statement: The toric-kernel disjointness assertion on scan 38 — Let $Y=C\setminus D$ be a smooth hyperbolic curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $J_D\to J_C$ be its compact-Jacobian quotient. For $g(C)\geq1$, every nonzero $u\in\ker(J_D\to J_C)$ satisfies $(\alpha(Y)+u)\cap\alpha(Y)=\varnothing$. This assertion is false for genus zero. There, for any nonidentity translation, the intersection has at most one geometric point, and its existence is determined by the equations below. This corrects the bracketed claim and the margin ``$g\geq2$?'' on scan 38, sweep row ZAB8 (149, section 1, manuscript p.~18).
depends_on: Explicit generalized Abel coordinates; degree-one function criterion; AB_checks.py
notes: Sweep ZAB8. Positive-genus disjointness proved for nonzero toric-kernel translations; genus-zero intersections classified exactly.

statement: The open birational Hom statement, and the withdrawn unrestricted version — \textup{[\S2, manuscript pp.\ 20--22; scans 41--46.]} Let $k$ be a number field, and let $L,M$ be finitely generated regular extensions of $k$. With compatible separable closures, restriction gives a bijection \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-fields}}(M,L) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}^{\mathrm{open}}_{G_k}(G_L,G_M) /\operatorname{Inn}(G_{M\bar k}). \tag{ZCF.1} \] All homomorphisms on the right are continuous. Thus a) and b) of scan 44 are equivalent after the common constant field has been fixed and the geometric kernels are the kernels for that same field. No supplementary compatibility with a filtration by models is required for this open-Hom statement. The version with arbitrary homomorphisms in scans 41--42 is false, as the manuscript itself observes in scan 43.
notes: All maps and hypotheses are stated in the TeX result and proof.

statement: Recovering an extension map from an equivariant geometric map — \textup{[\S2, manuscript p.\ 21; scans 43--44.]} Let $1\to P_i\to E_i\to G\to1$ be profinite extensions and let $\phi:P_1\to P_2$ be continuous. Suppose its conjugacy class is $G$-equivariant and $C_{P_2}(\phi(P_1))=1$. Then $\phi$ extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism $F:E_1\to E_2$ over $G$. Here equivariance means that, for every $e_1\in E_1$ and any $e_2\in E_2$ with the same image in $G$, the maps $\phi\circ\operatorname{int}(e_1)$ and $\operatorname{int}(e_2)\circ\phi$ differ by an inner automorphism from $P_2$. The stronger hypothesis involving every open subgroup in scan 43 implies the centralizer hypothesis just stated.
notes: All maps and hypotheses are stated in the TeX result and proof.

statement: Geometric homology alone does not determine a morphism — \textup{[\S2, manuscript p.\ 23; scan 47.]} Two morphisms into an elementary hyperbolic variety can induce the same map on every geometric $H_1(-,\mathbb Z_\ell)$ and different arithmetic fundamental-group homomorphisms. Consequently the unqualified sentence in scan 47 is false, for either direction of the doubtful source/target notation.
notes: All maps and hypotheses are stated in the TeX result and proof.

statement: An explicit nondominant map inducing an isomorphism of full fundamental groups — \textup{[\S2, manuscript pp.\ 24--25; scans 49--50.]} Let $C/\mathbb Q$ be the smooth projective completion of $y^2=x^5-x$, and let $Y=C^3$. On $(\mathbb P^1)^3$ take the trihomogeneous polynomial whose affine expression is \[ F=1+7x_1+3x_2+2x_3+13x_1x_2+11x_1x_3 +5x_2x_3+19x_1x_2x_3. \] Let $H\subset Y$ be its inverse-image zero divisor under the product of the three hyperelliptic maps. Then $H$ is a smooth geometrically connected surface and the closed immersion $H\hookrightarrow Y$ induces an isomorphism $\pi_1(H)\simeq\pi_1(Y)$ over $G_{\mathbb Q}$. It is not dominant. Thus the open-Hom assertion of scan 50 is false for the stated higher-dimensional elementary targets, already for constant inverse systems.
notes: Fully specified trilinear surface inside (y2=x5-x)^3. Eight Groebner ideals, eighteen slice determinants,216 branch triples checked exactly.

statement: The centralizer precisions and the necessary half of the fundamental conjecture — \textup{[\S2--3, manuscript pp.\ 23--31; scans 48--49, 53--63.]} For a hyperbolic curve $U/k$, with $k$ finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, and a continuous section $s:G_k\to E_U$, put $G_k^\circ=\ker\chi$. The checked attached return A6--A7 and AE1 \cite{PriorCyclotomic} gives \[ C_\Pi(s(G_k^\circ))= \begin{cases}I_c,&s\text{ is cuspidal at its unique lifted cusp }c,\\ 1,&s\text{ is noncuspidal.}\end{cases} \tag{ZCF.2} \] For every open $\Omega\subset G_k^\circ$ the same formula holds with $\Omega$ in place of $G_k^\circ$. In particular genuine finite point sections have zero cyclotomic centralizer. The same zero centralizer conclusion holds for point sections of hyperbolic polycurves. It proves a)$\Rightarrow$b) in scan 48 for actual morphisms into these varieties.
depends_on: A4; A6; A7; C4; F10a; F8a; CF_Stix2008; PriorCyclotomic
uses: FLAGGED_149:A4, FLAGGED_149:A6, FLAGGED_149:A7, FLAGGED_149:C4, FLAGGED_149:F10a, FLAGGED_149:F8a
notes: All maps and hypotheses are stated in the TeX result and proof.

statement: The existence assertions retained after the centralizer computation — \textup{[\S2--3, manuscript pp.\ 22--34 and 51; scans 45, 48--49, 51, 56--57, 59--63, 66--69, 104.]} The following exact assertions are not proved or refuted here. They are recorded separately from the proved uniqueness and centralizer assertions. \begin{enumerate} \item For $U=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, every continuous section $s:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\pi_1(U)$ with $C_\Pi(s(G_{\mathbb Q}^\circ))=1$ is the section of a rational point. This is the smallest retained instance of the sufficiency in scan 48 and of Conjecture A in scan 56. \item Every continuous section $G_{\mathbb Q}\to G_{\mathbb Q(t)}$ has image in the decomposition group of a rational place. By the checked return B7, this is exactly the assertion that its geometric cyclotomic centralizer is nonzero. This is the smallest retained birational instance of scan 45. \item Every section of a hyperbolic curve admits a compatible lift through the maps $\pi_1(U\setminus D)\to\pi_1(U)$ as the finite closed subsets $D$ grow, sufficient to obtain a birational section. The precise lifting problem is about continuous sections and their geometric-conjugacy classes, not just individual lifts of elements of $G_k$. \item The assertion of Conjecture B' of scan 63 for arbitrary abstract semilinear $G_{\mathbb Q}$-actions on the universal pro-cover of $\mathbb P^1_{\overline{\mathbb Q}} \setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$: every such action has a unique $G_{\mathbb Q}^\circ$-fixed compatible geometric point in its completed pro-cover. statement: The proposed extension to cyclotomic ground fields — \textup{[\S3, manuscript pp.\ 30--31; scans 62--63.]} Let $F=\mathbb Q(\mu_\infty)$. The smooth projective normalization $C/F$ of $z^6+2y^3+4=0$ has genus four, no $F$-rational point, and a continuous section of $\pi_1(C)\twoheadrightarrow G_F$. statement: The commensurability assertion for universal algebraic pro-covers — \textup{[\S3, manuscript p.\ 30; scan 62.]} For smooth connected curves $U,V$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, their universal connected finite-\'etale pro-covers are isomorphic as schemes over that field exactly when some connected finite \'etale cover of $U$ is isomorphic to a connected finite \'etale cover of $V$. No compatibility of an initial isomorphism with either deck group is assumed.

statement: A basis of the more special elementary neighborhoods — \textup{[\S3, manuscript pp.\ 33--34; scans 68--69.]} Let $X$ be smooth over a characteristic-zero field $k$. Every point has a fundamental system of Zariski-open neighborhoods which are towers of hyperbolic curve fibrations, each curve fibration being a finite \'etale cover of a relative punctured projective line with finite \'etale boundary of degree at least three. The bottom field may be a finite extension of $k$, accounting for geometric connected components. This proves the geometric neighborhood assertion of scan 68 in its characteristic-zero context; it does not construct the additional sections needed in scan 67.
