notes: Finite support of either coordinate or their ratio already gives the rational-point reconstruction.

statement: Infinite ramification at every coefficient prime. \label{prop:ghost-infinite-ramification} For an ordinary pair with infinite support, its abelian \(\ell\)-primary Kummer component ramifies at infinitely many rational primes, for every \(\ell\). Its abelian component at no \(\ell\) is the component of a rational point or a cuspidal section. For every finite set of rational primes \(S\), the vectors \((v_q(A),v_q(B))\), \(q\notin S\), span \(\mathbb Q_\ell^2\) for every \(\ell\). In particular the abelian geometric inertia images outside any finite set containing \(\ell\) generate an open submodule of \(\mathbb Z_\ell(1)^2\).
notes: An infinite-support ordinary pair has unbounded ramification support at every coefficient prime.

statement: Compact higher-weight cocycles. \label{lem:ghost-higher-z1} For every \(r\geq2\), the module \(Z^1_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,\mathbb Z_\ell(r))\) is a finite free \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-module, and its module topology is its compact-open topology. Every such cocycle factors through \(G_{\mathbb Q,\{\ell,\infty\}}\).
depends_on: Tame inertia weights; finite ramification outside ell; finite-coefficient global cohomology
notes: Applies to weights at least two; the abelian coordinate is fixed separately.

statement: The integral Hall coordinate model. \label{lem:ghost-hall-model} For fixed \(r\), ordered basic commutators of weights at most \(r\) identify \(N_{r,\ell}\), as a topological space, with \(\mathbb Z_\ell^{h_r}\). Multiplication, inversion, and taking \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-powers have coordinates given by rational polynomials. Their denominators have a fixed bound depending on \(r\). The quotient to \(N_{r-1,\ell}\) deletes the weight-\(r\) coordinates, and setting those coordinates equal to zero gives a continuous section of this quotient as a map of spaces. The coordinate functions of \(g(u)\), for the actual action of \(G\), are rational polynomials in the coordinates of \(u\), with coefficients that are continuous functions of \(g\). They too have bounded denominators at each fixed \(r\).
depends_on: Integral Hall collection and actual free nilpotent pro-ell quotients
notes: All coefficient primes, including two and three, are retained.

statement: Finite polynomial families of integral primitives. \label{lem:ghost-primitive-family} Let \(T\) be a finite free \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-module with a continuous \(G\)-action. Fix continuous rational two-cochains \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\in C^2(G,T\otimes\mathbb Q_\ell)\). Then \[ R=\left\{u\in\mathbb Z_\ell^m: \sum_i u_i c_i\in\delta C^1(G,T)\right\} \] is a closed finite free submodule of \(\mathbb Z_\ell^m\). There is a continuous \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-linear map \(h:R\to C^1(G,T)\) satisfying \(\delta h(u)=\sum_i u_i c_i\). Each coordinate of \(h\), relative to finitely many fixed continuous cochains, is the restriction to \(R\) of a \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-linear form on \(\mathbb Q_\ell^m\).
depends_on: C.1.3; noetherian closed submodules; finite polynomial family
notes: The finite polynomial parameters and actual integral cochains are retained.

statement: Compactness for a fixed abelian cocycle. \label{prop:ghost-compact-fibres} Every \(\mathscr S_{r,\ell}(a)\) is compact Hausdorff. More precisely, it is the continuous image of a closed subset \(X_r\subseteq\mathbb Z_\ell^{d_r}\), and its Hall coordinate functions are rational polynomials in these parameters, with continuous cochain coefficients.
notes: This compactness concerns one specified pair, with the exact forgetful maps.

statement: Exact compatibility equivalence for one fixed pair. \label{thm:ghost-fixed-pair-compatible} For any fixed power-completed Kummer pair \((A,B)\), the following two statements are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item For every integer \(r\geq1\), there exists a continuous section of \(E/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi\to G_{\mathbb Q}\) whose abelian Kummer class is \((A,B)\). \item There exists a continuous section of \(E/\bigcap_r\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi\to G_{\mathbb Q}\) whose abelian Kummer class is \((A,B)\). \end{enumerate} The corresponding equivalence also holds with the requirement that all restrictions be geometrically conjugate to one fixed family of local point sections, or of local cuspidal sections, at every level.
depends_on: C.1.6; compact inverse-limit finite intersection argument
notes: Nonempty lifts at every integral nilpotent class yield one compatible pronilpotent section for that same pair.

statement: The weight-twelve, coefficient-691 kernel. \label{prop:ghost-h2-691} Put \(\ell=691\), \(T=\mathbb Z_{691}(12)\), and \(S=\{691,\infty\}\). Inflation is injective and its image has the following properties: \[ H^2_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathbb Q,S},T) \simeq\mathbb Z/691\mathbb Z \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow H^2_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathbb Q},T). \] Every class in this image restricts to zero in \(H^2_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathbb Q_v},T)\) for every place \(v\). Its image in \(H^2(G_{\mathbb Q},T/691^nT)\) is zero for every \(n\geq1\).
depends_on: Integral Milnor sequence; Poitou–Tate duality; K22(Z) at 691; local duality
notes: A Z/691 class is nonzero globally, locally zero everywhere, and zero in every finite coefficient reduction.

statement: An actual continuous extension with every finite reduction split. \label{cor:ghost-integral-extension} There is an exact sequence of profinite groups \[ 1\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_{691}(12) \longrightarrow\mathcal E\longrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q} \longrightarrow1 \] with no continuous group-theoretic section, such that its restriction to every \(G_{\mathbb Q_v}\) has a continuous section and \(\mathcal E/691^nT\to G_{\mathbb Q}\) has a continuous section for every \(n\geq1\).
notes: The displayed profinite extension is genuine; no unsupported identification with a curve-fundamental-group quotient is made.

statement: The exact derived-limit kernel and a regular-prime example. \label{prop:ghost-uncountable-kernel} For every odd prime \(\ell\) and every \(r\geq2\), the kernel of the actual integral localization map is exactly \[ \ker\!\left(H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_\ell(r)) \longrightarrow\prod_v H^2_{\rm cts} (G_{\mathbb Q_v},\mathbb Z_\ell(r))\right) \simeq\varprojlim_n^{\,1}H^1 (G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z/\ell^n(r)). \] At \(\ell=3,r=2\), this kernel contains a subgroup isomorphic to \[ \frac{\prod_{j\geq1}\mathbb Z_3} {c_0(\mathbb Z_3)},\qquad c_0(\mathbb Z_3)= \{(z_j):z_j\longrightarrow0\text{ in }\mathbb Z_3\}. \] In particular it is uncountable. The unramified integral group \(H^2(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},\mathbb Z_3(2))\) is nevertheless zero.
depends_on: Milnor exact sequence; finite-coefficient local-global injectivity; explicit residue tower
notes: At ell=3 and weight two it contains an uncountable product/c0 quotient.

statement: The ordinary continuous cup vanishes. \label{prop:ghost-ordinary-cup} Every ordinary completed pair \((A,B)\in\mathcal G_{\rm ord}\) satisfies \[ A\cup B=0\quad\hbox{in}\quad H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\widehat{\mathbb Z}(2)). \] This proves the continuous cup assertion used in SECTIONS A.27 without assuming its omitted strict localization comparison.

notes: Includes ell=2 and the real place, with a compatible integral primitive.

statement: Every ordinary pair has an actual global class-two lift. \label{cor:ghost-class2-lift} Put \(U=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\), base it at the tangent vector \(\overrightarrow{01}\), and write \(\Pi=\pi_1(U_{\overline{\mathbb Q}},\overrightarrow{01})\). Every ordinary completed pair is the abelianization of a continuous section of \[ \pi_1(U,\overrightarrow{01})/\Gamma_3\Pi \longrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q}. \] Consequently no ordinary pair is excluded by unrestricted global lifting at nilpotency class one or two.
depends_on: C.1.11; explicit integral class-two section coordinates
notes: Local matching is a separate restriction of the actual section space; the C.2.2 obstruction applies there.

statement: Integral localization with the coefficient maps retained. \label{thm:ghost-strict-localization} For every prime \(\ell\) and every integer \(r\ge2\), put \(T=\mathbb Z_\ell(r)\), \(S=\{\ell,\infty\}\), and \[ R_\ell=\{(z_q)_{q\ne\ell}\in\prod_{q\ne\ell}\mathbb Z_\ell: z_q\longrightarrow0\},\qquad (d_rz)_q=(q^{r-1}-1)z_q. \] Fix compatible Tate coordinates at the finite residue fields. There is a natural, in those coordinates, exact sequence of abelian groups \[ 0\longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q,S},T) \xrightarrow{\rm inf}H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},T) \xrightarrow{\Psi_{\ell,r}}R_\ell/d_rR_\ell \longrightarrow0. \] The quotient uses the actual image \(d_rR_\ell\). In particular this proves the exactness assertion used in SECTIONS A.65.8. For \(r=3\), inflation has zero source, so \(\Psi_{\ell,3}\) is an isomorphism for every \(\ell\), as asserted abstractly in SECTIONS A.46.2.
depends_on: Coefficient-compatible supports triangle; derived inverse limit; real-place H3 comparison; K4(Z)=0
notes: The image dR is literal, not its closure; in weight three the global obstruction is exactly the stated c0/dc0 quotient.

statement:
The cochain representative of strict tame localization. \label{prop:ghost-tame-cochain} Use the morphism \(\Psi_{\ell,r}\) of Theorem~ef{thm:ghost-strict-localization}. The section \(s\) lifts to the full integral class-three quotient exactly when, for every \(\ell\), both coordinatewise quotients \[ \left( rac{Z_{D,q}}{q^2-1}ight)_{q

statement: Rational Magnus conjugacy detects pro-\(\ell\) conjugacy. \label{lem:ghost-magnus-conjugacy} Let \(F^{(\ell)}=\langle x,y\rangle^{(\ell)}\) be the free pro-\(\ell\) group, embedded by the Magnus map \(x\mapsto1+X\), \(y\mapsto1+Y\) in \(1+(X,Y)\mathbb Z_\ell\langle\!\langle X,Y\rangle\!\rangle\). The conjugacy relation induced on this group by the full unit group of \(\mathbb Q_\ell\langle\!\langle X,Y\rangle\!\rangle\) is exactly its own pro-\(\ell\) conjugacy relation.
depends_on: Integral cyclic-word sums; finite ell-group augmentation ideals; compact conjugator fibres
notes: The rational formal conjugator is never evaluated in an integral finite group algebra.

statement: Continuous first cohomology in weight two. \label{prop:ghost-h1-weight2} There are isomorphisms \[ H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_\ell(2)) \simeq \begin{cases} \mathbb Z/8,&\ell=2,\\ \mathbb Z/3,&\ell=3,\\ 0,&\ell\ge5, \end{cases} \qquad H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\widehat{\mathbb Z}(2)) \simeq\mathbb Z/24. \] The latter group is generated by the integral continuous cocycle \(\eta(g)=(\chi(g)^2-1)/24\).

statement: Exactly twenty-four class-two section classes. \label{cor:ghost-class2-fibre24} For every ordinary completed pair \((A,B)\), the fibre of geometric-conjugacy classes of continuous sections of the actual class-two arithmetic quotient above \((A,B)\) is a simply transitive \(\mathbb Z/24\)-set. For the geometrically pro-\(\ell\) quotient, the corresponding fibre has eight elements at two, three at three, and one at every \(\ell\ge5\). More explicitly, choose literal abelian cocycles \(a,b\) and one lift with central coordinate \(h\). Representatives for all twenty-four classes are \[ y^{b(g)}x^{a(g)}C^{h(g)+k\eta(g)}s_0(g), \qquad k\in\mathbb Z/24. \]
depends_on: C.1.12; C.1.18; vanishing of global weight-one invariants
notes: Every ordinary pair has precisely 24 pronilpotent class-two section classes; pro-ell fibre is singleton for ell>=5.

statement: The exact coefficient-five class-two prefix. \label{lem:ghost-prefix-five} Choose a first pair \(q_0,r_0\) by the original A.44 rules, and put \[ a_1=3q_0^{24},\qquad b_1=-2r_0^{24},\qquad n_j=(j+4)!. \tag{45} \] Choose the old local roots \((\xi_p,\eta_p)\) in its stage \(j=1\), so that \(a_1\xi_p^{120}+b_1\eta_p^{120}=1\). Let \(P,R\) be positive rational integers that are units at \(q_0,r_0\), with \[ P\equiv\xi_p\pmod p,\qquad R\equiv\eta_p\pmod p \quad(p=q_0,r_0). \tag{46} \] There is a class-two homomorphism \[ \rho_*:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow H_5\rtimes\mathbb F_5^\times \tag{47} \] with abelian Kummer pair \((a_1,b_1)\), uniquely determined up to central geometric conjugacy by the two inertia prescriptions in the proof. It is unramified outside \(2,3,5,q_0,r_0\). Its image is the full group of order five hundred, and its fixed field \(L_*\) has maximal abelian subfield \(\mathbb Q(\mu_5)\). For every original A.44 continuation with the chosen stage-one local roots and with \[ q_j\equiv r_j\equiv1\pmod{q_0r_0} \quad(j\ge2), \tag{48} \] the coefficient-five reduction of every integral class-two section, after aligning its abelian cocycles, is centrally conjugate to \(\rho_*\). In particular this field is fixed before the choice of \(q_1\) and \(r_1\).
depends_on: C.1.11; C.1.15; C.1.18; original A.44 local invariant; exact integral primitive comparison; coefficient-five restricted-ramification cohomology
notes: Rational placeholders fix the integral local primitives modulo5 at q0,r0. Every continuation with the displayed principal-unit tails has the same actual H5 semidirect C4 quotient of order500, up to central conjugacy. Its maximal abelian subfield is Q(mu5).

statement: A finite prefix determines every fixed class-two coefficient quotient. \label{lem:ghost-finite-prefix-determines} Fix \(\ell\ge5\) prime and \(N\ge1\). Let \(J_N\) be the least index with \(v_\ell((J_N+4)!)\ge N\). In an original A.44 prefix containing all indices \(i<J_N\), put \[ \begin{split} S_{\ell,N}&=\bigl(\{2,3\}\cup \{q_i,r_i:i<J_N\}\bigr)\setminus\{\ell\},\\ D&=N+\max_{p\in S_{\ell,N}}v_\ell(p-1). \end{split} \tag{76} \] Extend this prefix through an index \(L-1\), with \(L\ge J_N\) and \(v_\ell((L+4)!)\ge D\). Every integral class-two section of every ordinary original-A.44 continuation of that finite prefix has the same coefficient-\(\ell^N\) class-two reduction up to geometric conjugacy. After their abelian cocycles are aligned by the explicit representatives in the proof, the conjugacy is central.
depends_on: C.1.15; C.1.18; original factorial exponents; literal integral Kummer sums; exact tame relations and division by p−1 before reduction
notes: For ell>=5 and exponentN, an explicit finite prefix using D=N+max v_ell(p−1) fixes the coefficient-ell^N class-two section class of every continuation. Its proof compares actual continuous cocycles and their local integral primitives, then kills the unramified central difference by the checked weight-two cohomology.

statement: Level-dependent survival and the first exclusions. \label{task:ghost-c2} The literal quantifiers of SECTIONS A.65 and A.72 allow the pair and section to depend on the selected depth or quotient. Their statements do not assert one fixed pair at every level. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-fixed-depth-survival} now certifies the full A.65 fixed-depth assertion. Its missing A.66 arithmetic input is reconstructed in Lemma~\ref{lem:ghost-variable-exponent-image} and Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-general-exponent-arithmetic}, with the exact local shell images and every radical/CRT intersection checked. The certification uses the proved strict localization morphism, a uniform finite unramified annihilator including coefficient two, and an actual Bockstein correction retaining the stated finite Magnus congruence. Thus for every fixed integral class there is one ordinary infinite-support pair surviving that class. The stronger assertion that no one pair survives every integral nilpotency class remains unresolved, exactly as specified under C.1. The displayed A.65 outputs converge to the rational pair \((3,-2)\), by Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-a65-limit}. A common-cofinal family of A.72 sections retaining the point-three component at every finite quotient likewise has abelian class exactly \((3,-2)\), since the quotients include every abelian exponent. Neither calculation excludes other choices of deeper sections. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-factorial-selmer32} supplies a fully specified residue-prescribed variant of A.44 whose first failure of local matching is exactly class two, detected by the indicated geometric group of order \(32\). The proof does not claim failure of unrestricted global lifting. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-1129-unramified} proves that the prime \(1129\) contributes no local third obstruction for any global class-two lift of this witness, and gives a full local pro-\(\ell\) lift there for every \(\ell\ne1129\). The class-three residue criterion retains the support primes and their convergence condition as the unresolved global calculation for this particular pair. No smallest excluding level has been established for every output of the canonical least-choice A.44 recursion. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-first-integral-class3} supplies a different completely specified variant, with exponents \(5(j+4)!\) and a first-prime Frobenius condition in the point-three Heisenberg field. Its first unrestricted integral failure is exactly class three: every integral class-two lift has a nonzero coefficient-prime-five local third obstruction at that first support prime. The reduction of each such obstruction modulo twenty-five is nonzero. The theorem keeps the integral domain of these reductions; arbitrary finite coefficient class-two sections can have additional ramified classes, which this calculation does not classify. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-original-first-integral-class3} strengthens this construction to a choice of primes allowed by the original A.44 recursion, with exponents \((j+4)!\). Its obstruction occurs at coefficient prime three, modulo nine, and the first-prime rule is an explicit cubic-radical Frobenius test. The question for every allowed A.44 choice, including an independently prescribed least-choice output, remains unresolved. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-passing-first-class3} settles the unrestricted third obstruction for a selected family inside the compact-passing domain of Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-passing}. It keeps all original factorial exponents, freezes the old integral primitive values using Lemma~\ref{lem:ghost-prefix-five}, and imposes a compatible nonzero central Heisenberg Frobenius at the second positive support prime \(q_1\). All twenty-four integral class-two lifts fail there at coefficient five, already modulo twenty-five. Every compact elliptic test and the full affine abelian cover quotient still have the stated surviving classes. The unrestricted calculation for all the other compact-passing outputs is not settled. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-dense-class3} nevertheless places such an exclusion after every finite legal original prefix, and Corollary~\ref{cor:ghost-open-dense-class3} strengthens this to a finite extension whose every legal continuation is excluded. This is an open dense statement in the exact original-prefix topology, with the factorial exponents unchanged. It does not decide the remaining closed domain. SECTIONS A.137 and A.139 impose the specified local matching conditions and obtain finite Brauer reciprocity exclusions; their omitted A.134 arithmetic construction prevents a full independent certification from this attachment alone. They refer to the same harmonic pair: A.137 names a detector of class seventeen, and A.139 one of class eight. The latter's actual group \((\mathbb Z/2)^8\rtimes\mathbb Z/16\), its order \(4096\), and exact class eight have been independently verified by the nine Schreier generators and the powers of the eight-cycle's augmentation operator. Detector class alone does not establish the smallest failing class. A.207 and A.209 assert a global class-four lift and failure of local matching at class two; forgetting the local conjugacy conditions is the exact map relating those assertions. The order-32 local-matching obstruction has been independently proved here. A.196 is over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt[3]3)\), and its local class modulo ninth powers realizes no ordinary point or cusp, by Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-a196-scope}. Its finite supported obstruction and its claimed continuous absolute obstruction must retain their respective source Galois groups. The independent weight-twelve example of Corollary~\ref{cor:ghost-integral-extension} proves that absolute finite coefficient splitting can indeed coexist with continuous nonsplitting over \(\mathbb Q\), without asserting that this example arises from a unit-equation pair.
notes: The fixed-level witnesses vary with the level; absence of every all-depth ghost has not been proved.

statement: The displayed fixed-depth outputs tend to the rational pair. \label{prop:ghost-a65-limit} The abelian pairs prescribed by the displayed congruence formulas in SECTIONS A.65 converge to \((3,-2)\) in the power-completion topology as the depth tends to infinity.

statement: First class-three failure inside the compact-passing original family. \label{thm:ghost-passing-first-class3} There is a recursively specified original A.44 output \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{(j+4)!},\qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}r_j^{(j+4)!} \tag{55} \] for which every \(q_j\) has three a noncube and every \(r_j\) has two a noncube. It therefore passes every compact elliptic support-order test (16) and admits the full profinite affine-cover abelian section of Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-all-passing-genjac}, with proper class zero. Nevertheless its first empty unrestricted integral nilpotent section fibre is class three. All twenty-four integral class-two section classes have a nonzero local third obstruction at \(q_1\), at coefficient prime five, already nonzero after reduction modulo twenty-five.

statement: Dense class-three failure with the original factorial exponents. \label{thm:ghost-dense-class3} For every \(k\ge0\), the actual prefix maps satisfy \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{pr}_k(\mathscr F_3) &=\operatorname{pr}_k(\mathscr A),\\ \operatorname{pr}_k(\mathscr F_3\cap\mathscr A_c) &=\operatorname{pr}_k(\mathscr A_c). \end{split} \tag{64} \] Thus class-three-excluded outputs are dense among all original A.44 outputs, and among the outputs passing the compact tests. In the latter domain, every constructed pair has a full profinite section of the affine-cover abelian quotient with proper class zero, while its metabelian cover section fibre is empty. More precisely, after any specified finite prefix the construction chooses a coefficient prime \(\ell\ge5\) and a later support prime \(q_{\ell-4}\) at which every integral class-two section has nonzero third obstruction, already detected modulo \(\ell^2\). All exponents remain the original \((j+4)!\).

Choose a new coefficient prime ell, retain original factorial exponents, freeze every old integral local primitive, and impose a nonzero central Frobenius at q_(ell-4). The exact residue is nonzero modulo ell squared. All constructed compact-passing pairs have abelian cover sections and no metabelian cover lifts. Densi

statement: Open dense failure and finite prefixes forcing exclusion. \label{cor:ghost-open-dense-class3} Let \(\mathscr U_3\subset\mathscr A\) consist of the original A.44 outputs having a nonzero local third-obstruction class at some coefficient prime \(\ell\ge5\), detected at some finite coefficient exponent. Then \(\mathscr U_3\) is open and dense in \(\mathscr A\), and \(\mathscr U_3\cap\mathscr A_c\) is open and dense in \(\mathscr A_c\). Every member has first unrestricted integral failure at class three. In particular, every finite legal prefix has a finite extension whose every ordinary legal continuation is excluded at class three. In the compact-passing domain such forcing prefixes can be chosen within that domain, retaining the affine abelian cover section and excluding its metabelian lifts.
depends_on: C.1.21; C.2.8; C.1.19; exact Hall reduction through class three for ell>=5; C.3.10; C.3.11
notes: Every finite legal prefix has a finite extension forcing class-three exclusion for every ordinary continuation. The proof retains geometric conjugacy invariance of the finite obstruction through the actual central extension. The residual set is closed with empty interior; its emptiness and all higher lifting conditions remain unresolved.

statement: The exact coefficient-prime image. \label{lem:ghost-variable-exponent-image} Let \(d\ge2\), let \(24\mid C\), and let \(n=h!\), where \(h\ge2d^2\) and every prime divisor of \(C\) is at most \(h\). Put \[ E(Z)=Cn\prod_{r=2}^d(Z^r-1),\qquad D=Cd!n^d. \] For a prime \(p\mid n\), write \[ v=v_p(n),\quad e=v_p(d),\quad a_p=\begin{cases}1,&p\ne2,\\2,&p=2,\end{cases} \qquad W_p=v_p(C)+(d+1)v+v_p(d!)+a_p+e. \] The continuous map \[ F_p(z)=\exp\bigl(E(z)\log z\bigr) \] is a bijection from \(1+p^v+p^{v+a_p}\mathbb Z_p\) onto \[ F_p(1+p^v)\bigl(1+p^{W_p}\mathbb Z_p\bigr). \tag{VX.1} \] Every point of this domain satisfies \[ v_p(z-1)=v,\qquad v_p(E(z))=v_p(D), \qquad W_p\le2v_p(D). \tag{VX.2} \] The map preserves congruences modulo \(p^L\) between points of the domain. For positive integers in the domain it is the ordinary power \(z^{E(z)}\).
depends_on: Exact restricted power series; coefficient valuations; contraction on each p-adic shell; integral exponential and logarithm
notes: For the literal exponent C n product_(r=2)^d(z^r−1), an explicitly specified input shell maps bijectively to the stated full multiplicative coset. Exact exponent valuations and congruence preservation are proved, including the dyadic shell. Finite certificates check32 exact local permutations and2867 valuations; the proof treats every allowed parameter.

statement: Reconstruction of SECTIONS A.66. \label{thm:ghost-general-exponent-arithmetic} Fix \(d\ge2\), a positive integer \(C\) divisible by \(24\), and an integer \(J\ge2d^2\) at least every prime divisor of \(C\). Put \[ n_j=(j+J)!,\qquad D_j=Cd!n_j^d,\qquad E_j(Q)=Cn_j\prod_{r=2}^d(Q^r-1). \tag{VX.6} \] There are three sequences of distinct primes \(q_j,r_j,s_j>3\), disjoint from one another, for which \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}\frac{q_j^{E_j(q_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}}, \qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}\frac{r_j^{E_j(r_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}} \tag{VX.7} \] are an ordinary completed unit-equation pair. Their valuations at two and three are respectively \((0,1)\), \((1,0)\), and their other nonzero valuation pairs are exactly \[ \begin{array}{c|c} q_j&(E_j(q_j),0)\\ r_j&(0,E_j(r_j))\\ s_j&(-E_j(s_j),-E_j(s_j)). \end{array} \tag{VX.8} \] Both coordinates have infinite support. In the global power completion, \(A/3\) and \(B/(-2)\) are \(C\)-th powers. The construction is a recursion by finite CRT conditions and specified Chebotarev classes; all its simultaneous field conditions are compatible.

notes: The three disjoint prime sequences have the literal stated tame-denominator exponents and satisfy all ordinary local conditions. Every fresh-prime gcd equals the previous factorial, all simultaneous CRT/radical classes are compatible, and the pair is a prescribed C-th power perturbation of point3 with infinite support. The arithmetic certificate checks705 finite-field image cases; no enormous comp

statement: SECTIONS A.65, with its arithmetic and localization inputs proved. \label{thm:ghost-fixed-depth-survival} For every integer \(R\ge1\) and positive integer \(N\), there is an ordinary infinite-support completed pair \((A,B)\) and a continuous section \[ s:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow E_R=\pi_1(U,\overrightarrow{01})/\Gamma_{R+1}\Pi \] whose abelianization is \((A,B)\). Here all lower central subgroups are closed. The section agrees with the rational-point section of three in the actual finite arithmetic quotient defined by truncating the integral Magnus expansion at degree \(R\) and reducing its coefficients modulo \(N\), as specified in the proof. Its abelian pair is neither a rational point image nor a cuspidal image. The pair and the section in this statement are allowed to depend on \(R,N\).

statement: A weighted augmentation bound in the five-coordinate group. \label{lem:ghost-weighted-augmentation} Let \(p\ge5\) be a prime, let \(a\ge1\), and put \(M=p^a\). statement: A uniform rigid target. \label{task:ghost-c3} Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-target} identifies an actual degree-\(27\) finite cover excluding the family of Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-original-first-integral-class3}: it is the elliptic curve \(y^2=x^3+9\) with twenty-seven geometric punctures, with its explicit cover map through \(y^2=x^3-243\) and \(3u^3-2v^3=1\). All three mod-three central classes are accounted for: two already fail the third obstruction at two, and every surviving full section must factor through the single pointed cover. At the constructed first support prime its ordinary point has no rational lift to that cover. This proves the full pro-three section exclusion using the actual cover map. The compactification kills boundary inertia that maps nontrivially to \(U\); the proof therefore retains the open curve and does not claim exclusion from its compact elliptic quotient alone. Propositions~\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-selmer}--\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-support-test} compute the exact three-isogeny Selmer groups and the absolute continuous cohomology \(H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},T_3E')=\mathbb Z_3\kappa(6,15) \oplus(\mathbb Z/3)\kappa(0,3)\). The exact translated isogeny identity then forces, for every original A.44 output admitting a full pro-three section, that \((-2,1)\) have prime-to-three order at every positive support prime \(q_j\), and that \((3,-6)\) have prime-to-three order at every negative support prime \(r_j\). Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-passing} constructs an original A.44 family satisfying every one of these finite elliptic tests. The remaining case for this compact elliptic calculation is therefore explicitly nonempty; existence or exclusion of a full section for it remains unresolved. Lemma~\ref{lem:ghost-elliptic-two-fibre} proves that the compact comparison at two adds no restriction on the two global coefficients. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-genjac-image} identifies the full affine-cover geometric abelianization with the Tate module of the generalized Jacobian, retains its exact map to the two original Kummer coordinates, and computes its image by the norms from the three boundary algebras. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-boundary-hasse-norm} proves that these are degree-nine fields with normal-closure group \(H_3\rtimes C_2\), and that their norm-one tori satisfy both the Hasse norm principle and weak approximation. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-original-genjac-survival} then constructs an original, unscaled A.44 output with an actual full profinite section of \(\pi_1(U)/\overline{[K,K]}\), where \(K=\pi_1(Y_{\overline{\mathbb Q}})\), factoring through the generalized-Jacobian quotient of \(Y\). Its proper class is zero. The remaining cover-lifting kernel is the explicitly retained \(\overline{[K,K]}\). Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-all-passing-genjac} strengthens this survival statement to every original A.44 output satisfying the compact support-order tests: the boundary norms are surjective over \(\mathbb Q_3\), so the extra congruence used in the first construction is unnecessary. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-passing-first-class3} and Corollary~\ref{cor:ghost-metabelian-cover-exclusion} then exclude a selected subfamily by the actual metabelian quotient of \(Y\). Its abelian cover section fibre is nonempty, but every member has empty lift fibre through \(\pi_1(Y)/\overline{[[K,K],[K,K]]}\). The exact map to the downstairs class-three quotient comes from \(\overline{[[K,K],[K,K]]}\subset\Gamma_4\Pi\). Thus the retained commutator problem is genuinely nonempty and can obstruct, while a universal exclusion or full lift for all the remaining compact-passing outputs is still unresolved. The order-32 quotient above excludes the residue-prescribed family. The complete attached A.72 argument has been checked: for every one fixed finite geometric quotient \(Q\), it constructs an ordinary infinite-support pair with a locally matching section in \[ E/(N\cap[\Pi,\Pi]) =E_Q\mathbin{\times}_{E_{Q^{\rm ab}}}E_{\rm ab}, \qquad N=\ker(\Pi\to Q), \] whose \(Q\)-component is the section of three. The equality is induced by the diagonal quotient map; its kernel is the displayed intersection, and compatibility over \(Q^{\rm ab}\) allows any pair of lifts to be adjusted by the two kernels. Therefore no single finite geometric quotient uniformly excludes all these A.72 ordinary ghosts. A finite collection of quotient tests has the same limitation, by taking its common finite quotient. A geometrically connected finite \emph{etale} cover \(Y\to U\) of degree \(d\) gives an open subgroup of the full fundamental group. Its geometric subgroup has index \(d\) in the free profinite group of rank two and therefore has rank \(d+1\), by the Schreier generators and relations, so is infinite. A.72 constructs matching sections of the specified finite-quotient fibre product; it does not construct a section of \(\pi_1(Y)\) or solve every quotient test of that infinite group. No proof has been obtained of a uniform exclusion through a full finite-cover fundamental group, a configuration-space target, or a modular target, and no proof has been obtained that every target of those specified types fails. This is the precise remaining target problem.

statement: The pointed Heisenberg cover as an open elliptic curve. \label{prop:ghost-elliptic-target} Let \(Y\to U\) be the degree-\(27\) finite etale cover defined by the class-two exponent-three geometric quotient \(H_3\) and the point-three section: its arithmetic fundamental group is the inverse image of that section in the arithmetic \(H_3\)-quotient. Its smooth compactification, pointed by the sheet above three, is \[ E':\ y^2=x^3+9. \] The open curve \(Y\) is the complement of the twenty-seven geometric points above \(0,1,\infty\). The map to \(U\) is the restriction of the explicit composite \[ E'\xrightarrow{\ \phi\ } E \xrightarrow{\ \iota^{-1}\ } C \xrightarrow{\ t=3u^3\ }\mathbb P^1, \quad E:y^2=x^3-243,\quad C:3u^3-2v^3=1, \tag{8} \] where \[ \phi(x,y)=\left(\frac{x^3+36}{x^2}, \frac{y(x^3-72)}{x^3}\right) \] and, for \(d=3u(u-1)-2v(v-1)\), \[ \iota(u,v)= \left(\frac{18(uv-1)}d, -\frac{27[3u(u+1)+2v(v+1)]}d\right). \tag{9} \] For every pair constructed in Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-original-first-integral-class3}, its ordinary local point at \(q_0\) has no rational lift to \(Y\). There is no continuous section of the geometrically pro-three arithmetic fundamental group of \(Y\) whose pushforward to \(U\) has that abelian pair.

statement: Descent and the two proofs of R3 — The specified comparison in both supplied proofs of R3 is valid. The first proof also applies to any $\U$-small colimit of representables. In the second proof, filteredness is used precisely to preserve the injections induced by an acyclic map.

All invariant small colimits of representables — The $\Winfty$-invariant presheaves on $\Cathot_\U$ that are $\U$-small colimits of representables are exactly the presheaves \[ X\longmapsto\colim_{i\in I}\pi_0\Fun(\Pi_1X,G_i), \] where $I$ is any $\U$-small category and $G:I\to\Ho(\Grpd_\U)$ is a diagram. For an invariant presentation $H=\colim_i h_{K_i}$ the canonical comparison \[ \colim_i h_{K_i}\longrightarrow\colim_i h_{\Pi_1K_i} \tag{B.2.1} \] is an isomorphism of presheaves, for the original index $I$.

Truncation localizers — For every integer $n\geq1$, the $\W_n$-invariant $\U$-small ind-objects are exactly the ind-groupoids. The $\W_0$-invariant ones are exactly the ind-objects of discrete sets. Their canonical representatives are respectively $(\Pi_1K_i)_i$ and $(\pi_0K_i)_i$. For representable presheaves the corresponding classes consist of objects isomorphic in $\Cathot$ to groupoids and to discrete categories.

Integral homology and homologically local groups — Let $\mathcal G_{\mathbb Z}$ be the full subcategory of groupoids whose isotropy groups are local for the homomorphisms inducing an isomorphism on $H_1(-;\mathbb Z)$ and a surjection on $H_2(-;\mathbb Z)$. The $\W_{\mathbb Z}$-invariant $\U$-small ind-objects of $\Cathot$ are exactly the ind-objects of $\mathcal G_{\mathbb Z}$. Their canonical presentation is $(E_{\mathbb Z}\Pi_1K_i)_i$, where $E_{\mathbb Z}$ is groupwise integral homological localization. The invariant representables are exactly the categories isomorphic in $\Cathot$ to objects of $\mathcal G_{\mathbb Z}$.

The enlarged-universe classification — Restriction along $q:\Cathot_\U\to\Hot_\U$ gives an equivalence from $\Ind_\V(\Hot_\U)$ onto the full subcategory of $\Winfty$-invariant objects in $\Ind_\V(\Cathot_\U)$. In particular every $\U$-small homotopy type has a $\V$-small filtered ind-presentation on $\Cathot_\U$.

An exact algebraic classification for every larger localizer — Let $\W\supseteq\Winfty$ be any fundamental localizer in $\Cat_\U$. Let $\mathcal G=\Ho(\Grpd_\U)$ and let $S_{\W}$ be the class of arrows $\Pi_1u$ for $u\in\W$. Form the ordinary localization $q_{\W}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal D_{\W}=\mathcal G[S_{\W}^{-1}]$ in $\V$. Under the fully faithful embedding of ind-groupoids as presheaves, the exact class of invariant small ind-objects is \[ \Ind_\U(\mathcal G)\ \cap\ q_{\W}^*\operatorname{PSh}(\mathcal D_{\W}). \tag{B.6.1} \] Here the intersection is an intersection of essential images inside presheaves on $\mathcal G$. Its membership is given by the explicit extension and equality tests below. For representables, it consists of groupoids $G$ satisfying the displayed algebraic bijection (B.6.2). These descriptions require no accessibility or reflectivity assumption on $\W$.

The sharp cardinal threshold for bounded tests — Let $\mu,\kappa\in\U$ be infinite cardinals, and let $K:I\to\Cathot_\U$ have $\U$-small filtered index and $|\Mor K_i|\leq\mu$ for every $i$. Among such presentations, invariance on all categories with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows forces the canonical global ind-groupoid isomorphism for every $K$ exactly in the range \[ \mu^+<\kappa. \tag{B.7.1} \] Outside this range, every small homotopy type occurs on those tests using stages with at most $\mu$ arrows. In particular $K(C_2,2)$ gives a presentation that is invariant on the prescribed tests and has no global ind-groupoid isomorphism.

All bounded invariant restrictions — Fix an infinite $\kappa\in\U$, and let $\mathcal C_{<\kappa}$ be a skeleton of categories with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows, with transformation-homotopy morphisms. Its localization is denoted $\mathcal D_{<\kappa}$. The restrictions of small ind-objects that are invariant on these tests are exactly the presheaves on $\mathcal D_{<\kappa}$ whose pullbacks $F$ satisfy the following finite conditions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $F(\varnothing)$ is a singleton and $F(A\amalg B)\to F(A)\times F(B)$ is bijective; \item for every pair $u,v:A\rightrightarrows B$, with $C$ the specified Grothendieck homotopy coequalizer of B.5 and $w:B\to C$, the function \[ F(C)\longrightarrow\Eq\bigl(F(B)\rightrightarrows F(A)\bigr) \] is surjective. \end{enumerate} Every such restriction has a presentation by stages with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows. For $\kappa>\aleph_0$, these classes are equivalently $\Ind_\U(\Hot_{<\kappa})$, where a type belongs to $\Hot_{<\kappa}$ when it has a simplicial model of size less than $\kappa$. For $\kappa=\aleph_0$, the two displayed finite conditions give the classification directly on the localization of finite categories.
Every small filtered diagram with a uniform finite bound m on stage arrows is isomorphic in Ind(Cat_hot) to a constant category with at most m arrows.

A finite relative example with a nontrivial mapping-space fundamental group — For any small groupoid $G$, form $M$ by adjoining objects $a,b$, with no arrows between them, no arrows from $G$ to them, and one arrow from each of $a,b$ to every object of $G$. statement: The proposed classification by two-types and two-groupoids — The strict $2$-groupoid $\mathbf B^2C_2$ with one object, one $1$-arrow, and $2$-automorphism group $C_2$ is not local in either transformation convention. For $X=\mathbf BC_2$, the canonical comparison has a singleton domain and a two-element codomain: \[ \Hom_{\mathcal H_2}(\mathbf BC_2,\mathbf B^2C_2) \longrightarrow [BC_2,K(C_2,2)]. \tag{E.1.1} \] Consequently the statement that all strict $2$-groupoids are local is false.

The groupoid reflection in every strict dimension — For $1\leq n\leq\infty$, let $\Pi X$ be the groupoid with generators the $1$-cells of $X$, relations for their strict compositions, and the relation $f=g$ for every $2$-cell $f\Rightarrow g$. The strict functor $\eta_X:X\to\Pi X$ induces the fundamental groupoid of $B_nX$. It gives a reflection \[ \Pi:\mathcal H_n\rightleftarrows\Ho(\Grpd):j. \] For each groupoid $G$, its canonical comparison is bijective: \[ \Hom_{\mathcal H_n}(X,G)\cong[B_nX,BG]. \tag{E.2.1} \]
The quotient localizes to ordinary homotopy types — The functor $\mathcal H_n\to\Hot_\U$ induced by $B_n$ is localization at Street-nerve weak equivalences, for every $1\leq n\leq\infty$.

Descent of transformations along the R2 quotients — Let $C$ be a strict $n$-category with at most $\mu$ cells in all dimensions, where $\mu$ is infinite. Let $p:G\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma$ be a group quotient such that every homomorphism from $G$ to a group of cardinality at most $\mu$ kills $\ker p$. Restriction along $\mathbf Bp$ is an isomorphism on the categories of strict functors and normal lax transformations from $\mathbf B\Gamma$ and $\mathbf BG$ to $C$. It induces a bijection on transformation-homotopy classes, including the pseudo convention.

Invariant small ind-objects in every strict dimension — For $1\leq n\leq\infty$, the Street-nerve invariant $\U$-small ind-objects of $\mathcal H_n$ are exactly the ind-objects of ordinary groupoids. For an invariant diagram $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ the canonical morphism \[ (K_i)_{i\in I}\longrightarrow(\Pi K_i)_{i\in I} \] is an isomorphism in $\Ind_\U(\mathcal H_n)$. The same assertion about canonical presheaves holds for arbitrary $\U$-small colimits of representables.

Representable homotopy types and local objects — For each $1\leq n\leq\infty$, a small space $Y$ has $X\mapsto[B_nX,Y]$ representable on $\mathcal H_n$ precisely when $Y$ is a $1$-type. The local objects are exactly those isomorphic in $\mathcal H_n$ to ordinary groupoids, equivalently those whose canonical map $K\to\Pi K$ is an isomorphism there. These conclusions apply to both requested transformation conventions in dimension two.

u)$ consists of a group $\pi$, a finite index set $I$ of cardinality $
u$, a free rank-one integral orientation module $T$, and exterior homomorphisms $\kappa_i:T	o\pi$. Here an exterior homomorphism is a conjugacy class, under conjugation in the target, of actual homomorphisms. After choosing a generator of $T$, representatives $c_i=\kappa_i(1)$, an ordering of $I$, and the handle generators, these data admit the presentation \[ \pi_{g,
u}=\left\langle a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_g,b_g,c_1,\ldots,c_

When $I$ is empty one additionally identifies $T$ with the dual of $H^2(\pi;\Z)$, or its continuous profinite counterpart. This is the covariant orientation convention of scan 116. More precisely, an earlier cohomological marking $\kappa:H^2(\pi;\Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{\mathrm{coh}}$ on scan 91 gives, by dualization, $\kappa^\vee:T_{\mathrm{coh}}^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}H_2(\pi;\Z)$; the covariant module used here is $T=T_{\mathrm{coh}}^\vee$. For an isomorphism of groups with loops the data are an isomorphism $f:\pi	o\pi_1$, a bijection $s:I	o I_1$, and an isomorphism $t:T	o T_1$ such that $f\kappa_i$ is conjugate to $\kappa_{s(i)}t$ for every $i$, with the corresponding dual-cohomology compatibility when $I$ is empty. An exterior group with loops regards two such $f$ as equivalent when they differ by target inner conjugation, with the same $s,t$. Thus its isomorphism sets are explicitly the quotient of the preceding isomorphism sets by $\Inn(\pi_1)$. In all nontrivial admitted types $L_i=\kappa_i(T)$ recovers its source by A.2; the one-puncture sphere requires the original source map. For $

The same list holds for their profinite completions. The peripheral maps from the source orientation group $\Z$ to $\pi$ are injective except at $(0,1)$, among the types admitted in scans 91--92. statement: Discrete peripheral rigidity in every hyperbolic type — For $2g+\nu>2$, the group $\pi=\pi_{g,\nu}$ has trivial centre and $C_\pi(H)=1$ for every finite-index subgroup $H$. For every peripheral subgroup and every integer $n\ge1$, \[ N_\pi(L_i)=C_\pi(L_i)=C_\pi(L_i^n)=L_i. \] Distinct peripheral indices give distinct, noncommensurable conjugacy classes.

statement: Exact exceptional-case table — The discrete and profinite exceptional groups have the following properties; in the profinite column replace $\Z$ by $\widehat\Z$. \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} (g,\nu)&\pi& Z(\pi)&C_\pi(H)\ (H\text{ finite index/open})&\text{peripherals}\\\hline (0,0)&1&1&1&\text{none}\\ (0,1)&1&1&1&L_1=1\\ (0,2)&\Z&\Z&\Z&L_1=L_2=\pi\\ (1,0)&\Z^2&\Z^2&\Z^2&\text{none} \end{array} \] Consequently the peripheral normalizer and power-centralizer equalities hold in the plane and annulus, while distinctness of the two peripheral classes fails on the annulus. The nonzero vector $1$ on the annulus and $(1,0)$ on the torus witness failure of both centre and finite-index-centralizer assertions. The plane's failure is the noninjective source map, not a nontrivial centre. For the standard base-element formula of scan 501, the annulus satisfies the equality since its basis element generates its whole group. On the torus $C(\langle(1,0)\rangle^n)=\Z^2$ for every $n\ge1$, and $(0,1)$ witnesses its failure to equal $\langle(1,0)\rangle$. The same vector works after completion. The sphere and plane have no nontrivial base elements to test.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.4; computation locations are specified in that proof.
notes: A.b; A.c. The four abelian types are fully tabulated. Explicit centre/open-centralizer witnesses on annulus and torus, coinciding annulus peripherals, and torus base-element counterexample.

statement: Peripheral decomposition groups and transporters — Let $1\to\pi\to E\xrightarrow{p}\Gamma\to1$ arise from an action on a hyperbolic marked surface. Choose one peripheral subgroup $L_s$ and the corresponding peripheral lift group $E_s\subset E$; thus $E_s\cap\pi=L_s$ and $p(E_s)=\Gamma_s$, the stabilizer of that puncture. Define \[ \operatorname{Trans}_E(L_s^d,L_s) =\{e\in E:eL_s^de^{-1}\subseteq L_s\}\qquad(d\ge1). \] Then $N_E(L_s)=\operatorname{Trans}_E(L_s^d,L_s)=E_s$. The same assertions hold for the corresponding profinite extension and closed peripheral groups. On the annulus these assertions fail for $z\mapsto1/z$: with $E=\Z\rtimes C_2$ and the involution acting by inversion, $E_s=\Z$ but $N_E(L_s)=E$ and every transporter is $E$. More generally for every annulus action both normalizer and transporter equal $E$, while $E_s$ is the inverse image of the end stabilizer. Thus their equality with $E_s$ holds exactly when the action fixes both ends. On the one-puncture sphere the peripheral mixed group maps onto $E=\Gamma$ with kernel $\Z$; using its image, both equalities hold, whereas identifying that mixed group itself with a subgroup is invalid. The closed sphere and torus have no peripheral statement.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.5; computation locations are specified in that proof.
notes: A.b; A.c. All geometric hyperbolic actions; all annulus actions have N=Trans=E, with equality to the peripheral lift exactly when both ends are fixed. Plane peripheral mixed map is not injective. Profinite transporter proved using compact recurrence, not an overstatement of edge uniqueness.

statement: Centre-free extension reconstruction and its abelian correction — For a centre-free discrete group $\pi$ and a homomorphism $\rho:\Gamma\to\Out(\pi)$, the extension inducing $\rho$ is, up to a unique isomorphism inducing the identity on its prescribed kernel and quotient, \[ E_\rho=\{(a,\gamma)\in\Aut(\pi)\times\Gamma:[a]=\rho(\gamma)\}. \] The same formula holds for a topologically finitely generated centre-free profinite $\pi$ and continuous $\rho$, with the profinite topology. For $A=\Z$ or $\Z^2$ and a prescribed action $\rho:\Gamma\to\Aut(A)$, extension classes with their kernel and quotient identified are instead classified by $H^2(\Gamma;A_\rho)$. Their automorphisms inducing the identity on both ends form $Z^1(\Gamma;A_\rho)$. For finite $\Gamma$ this statement holds with $A=\widehat\Z$ or $\widehat\Z^2$ and continuous cochains. Thus both the annulus and the torus require the abelian correction.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.6; computation locations are specified in that proof.
notes: A.b; A.c. Pullback extension and unique identified-end isomorphism proved. Annulus and torus corrections are H2 extension classes with Z1 automorphism groups; explicit split/nonsplit C2 extensions supplied.

statement: The full profinite rigidity statements, with reductions — For the full profinite completion $\Pi=\widehat\pi_{g,\nu}$ of a hyperbolic type, $\Pi$ is torsion-free, $C_\Pi(H)=1$ for every open subgroup $H$, and \[ N_\Pi(\widehat L_i)=C_\Pi(\widehat L_i^n)=\widehat L_i \quad(n\in\Z_{>0}). \] Distinct peripheral classes are noncommensurable. The same conclusions hold for the pro-$p$ completions, for every prime $p$, including $2$ and $3$. The four exceptional types have exactly the completed table of A.4, and A.5 supplies the extension and transporter assertions.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.7; computation locations are specified in that proof.

statement: Lemme 5 from open-subgroup centralizers alone — Let $P$ be a discrete or profinite group for which the centralizer of every finite-index, respectively open, subgroup is trivial. Let $H\subset P$ be such a subgroup and let $u\in\Aut(P)$ preserve $H$. An automorphism restricting to the identity on $H$ is the identity on $P$. An automorphism whose restriction equals $\operatorname{conj}_h$ for some $h\in H$ equals $\operatorname{conj}_h$ on $P$.

Faithfulness of $\Gamma\to\Out(\pi_1(U_{\overline k}))$ implies faithfulness of $\Gamma\to\Out(\pi_1(V_{\overline k}))$.

The discrete filling isomorphism and all compatibility maps — Let $U=X\setminus S$ be hyperbolic, choose $b\in U$, and put $U'=U\setminus\{b\}$, $\pi'=\pi_1(U')$, and $\pi=\pi'/\langle\!\langle L_bangle\!angle$. Choose the peripheral representative $L_b\subset\pi'$. The normalization of representatives defines an isomorphism of discrete groups \[ d_b:\Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi';b)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Aut_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi). \] On both sides old punctures may be permuted and orientation may be reversed. It identifies the pure orientation-preserving subgroups, whose common index is $2
u!$, where $
u=|S|$. It commutes with forgetting the distinguished puncture, with the maps to $\Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi)$, with orientation characters, with the permutation maps to $\mathfrak S_

statement: Filling into the two abelian targets — Exactly one of the drilled and filled groups is abelian in the two cases $(0,3)\to(0,2)$ and $(1,1)\to(1,0)$. In the first, the homomorphism on automorphisms of the underlying groups with peripheral subgroup classes is \[ C_2\times C_2=\Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(F_2;[\langle xy\rangle]) \longrightarrow\Aut(\Z)=C_2, \] with kernel of order two. Its nontrivial element has representative $x\mapsto y^{-1}$, $y\mapsto x^{-1}$. Its restriction to the positive-orientation subgroup is an isomorphism. Retaining the two indexed peripheral source maps and their orientation line on the annulus enlarges the target automorphism group to $C_2\times C_2$ and restores the full isomorphism. In the second case the filling map is the isomorphism $\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z)\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z)$, with positive subgroup $\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z)$.

statement: Primitive loops in finite-step solvable quotients — Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty set of primes, $F$ a free pro-$\Sigma$ group of finite rank at least two, and $F^{[j]}$ its closed derived series. Put $F_m=F/F^{[m]}$, $m\ge2$. For any element $x$ of a free basis and any positive integer $n$, \[ C_{F_m}(x^n)=N_{F_m}(\overline{\langle x\rangle}) =\overline{\langle x\rangle}\simeq\Z_\Sigma, \qquad \Z_\Sigma=\prod_{p\in\Sigma}\Z_p. \] Every open subgroup of $F_m$ has trivial centralizer. For $\nu\ge2$, all peripheral loops of the pro-$\Sigma$ group of type $(g,\nu)$ satisfy these formulas in every $F_m$. Their indexed conjugacy classes are pairwise distinct in all hyperbolic types.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.14; computation locations are specified in that proof.
notes: A.c. Primitive peripheral powers, normalizers, open centralizers and distinctness for nu>=2 at every depthm>=2.

statement: The compact intersection calculation used in descent — Let $(H_\alpha)$ be a decreasing directed family of closed subgroups of a profinite group $P$, and put $K=\bigcap_\alpha H_\alpha$. Then \[ K^{[j]}=\bigcap_\alpha H_\alpha^{[j]}\quad(j\ge0). \] For a closed subgroup $L\subset P$ and decreasing closed normal subgroups $N_\alpha$ of $P$, one also has $\bigcap_\alpha LN_\alpha=L(\bigcap_\alpha N_\alpha)$.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.15; computation locations are specified in that proof.

notes: A.c. Closed derived subgroups commute with decreasing directed intersections; closed products with a fixed closed subgroup also commute with such intersections. Finite quotient and nested compact fibre proofs included.

statement: The one-puncture solvable threshold, with a finite certificate — Let $F$ be the pro-$\Sigma$ completion of $\pi_{g,1}$, $g\ge1$, let $c=\prod_{j=1}^g[a_j,b_j]$ (the inverse peripheral generator), and write $c$ for its image in $F_m=F/F^{[m]}$. For every positive integer $n$, \[ \begin{array}{ll} m=2:& C_{F_2}(c^n)=N_{F_2}(\overline{\langle c\rangle})=F_2',\\[2pt] m\ge3:&C_{F_m}(c^n)=N_{F_m}(\overline{\langle c\rangle}) =\overline{\langle c\rangle}. \end{array} \] In the first line the inclusion $\overline{\langle c\rangle}\subset F_2'$ is strict. Thus peripheral rigidity fails at the smallest solvable depth $m=2$ and is restored at every $m\ge3$, for the full profinite and every pro-$p$ version.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.16; computation locations are specified in that proof.
notes: A.c. One-puncture threshold proved: m=2 gives F2-prime strictly larger than peripheral; m>=3 gives exact procyclic centralizer and normalizer. UT4 finite certificates run at p=2,3,5.

statement: Centre and torsion in all finite-step surface quotients — Let $P$ be the full profinite or pro-$\Sigma$ completion of a hyperbolic surface group, open or closed, and let $P_m=P/P^{[m]}$. For every $m\ge2$, $P_m$ is torsion-free and centre-free. This verifies the form of \cite[Theorem 2.9 and Corollary 2.10]{A_Yamaguchi2026} needed here by the following argument from finite covers and transfer.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.17; computation locations are specified in that proof.
his_places: Strengthened PartA(c); Yamaguchi2026 Theorem2.9 and Corollary2.10
notes: A.c. Independent proof of torsion and centre claims in every requested finite-step geometric surface quotient, checking closed-subgroup abelianization, finite deck homology action and transfer.

statement:
The remaining affine solvable rigidity list and a closed bound — For all hyperbolic types with $
u>0$, and all $m\ge2$, the maximal $m$-step-solvable full profinite or pro-$\Sigma$ quotient has trivial centre and trivial centralizers of open subgroups, and is torsion-free. Peripheral conjugacy classes remain distinct. For $
u\ge2$ all peripheral normalizer and integer-power-centralizer equalities hold at every $m\ge2$; for $
u=1$ their exact values are those of A.16. In an extension obtained by quotienting a geometric action extension by the $m$th closed derived subgroup of its kernel, the equality $N_E(L_s)=E_s$ holds in the former cases and at $m\ge3$ in the latter. At $
u=1,m=2$ its correct value is $N_E(L_s)=F_2'E_s$, with the intersection $F_2'\cap E_s=L_s$. In all these cases every transporter $\operatorname{Trans}_E(L_s^d,L_s)$, $d\ge1$, equals the same displayed normalizer. Since the kernels are centre-free by A.17, the extension reconstruction of A.6 also applies to all these solvable quotients. Standard free-basis generators satisfy the power-centralizer formula at every $m\ge2$ by A.14. For a closed hyperbolic group $P$ and an open subgroup $H\subset P_m$, the proven universal bound is \[ C_{P_m}(H)\subseteq P_m^{[m-1]}. \]
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.18; computation locations are specified in that proof.
notes: A.c. Full affine solvable list, extension normalizers and one-sided transporters. Closed containment is subsequently strengthened to zero by A.19.

statement: Closed finite-step power centralizers and slimness — Let $P$ be the pro-$\Sigma$ completion of a closed oriented surface group of genus $g\ge2$, let $m\ge2$, and put $P_m=P/P^{[m]}$. Let $x$ be represented by a nonseparating simple closed curve, in particular by any standard handle generator. Then for every positive integer $n$, \[ C_{P_m}(x^n)=N_{P_m}(\overline{\langle x^n\rangle}) =\overline{\langle x\rangle}\simeq\Z_\Sigma. \] Consequently $C_{P_m}(H)=1$ for every open subgroup $H$. This includes the full profinite and every pro-$p$ quotient, without a restriction at $p=2$ or $3$.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.19; computation locations are specified in that proof.

statement: The typed completion comparison for filling — For the two hyperbolic groups in A.12, put $\Pi'=\widehat{\pi'}$ and $\Pi=\widehat\pi$. There is a commutative diagram of profinite groups \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \widehat{\Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi';b)} &\xrightarrow{\ \widehat{d_b}\ }& \widehat{\Aut_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi)}\\ \big\downarrow c_{\mathrm{out}}&&\big\downarrow c_{\mathrm{aut}}\\ \Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(\Pi';b) &\xrightarrow{\ d_b^{\mathrm{cont}}\ }& \Aut_{\mathrm{lac}}(\Pi). \end{array} \] The upper horizontal map is an isomorphism. The lower horizontal map is the normalized filling homomorphism on all continuous loop automorphisms. The vertical maps are induced by extending discrete automorphisms to group completions. The same construction with pro-$p$ completions of the surface groups still has the full profinite completions of the discrete automorphism groups in its upper row. These assertions specify the precise consequence of the discrete filling theorem; no isomorphism assertion for the lower horizontal or vertical arrows is used.
where_proved: Paper, Part A, statement A.20; computation locations are specified in that proof.
notes: A.d; typed completion comparison. Completed discrete filling isomorphism compared by a commutative square with full continuous automorphism filling. No identification of its vertical images with all continuous automorphisms is asserted or needed. Explicit odd-p involution obstruction to replacing the upper completions by pro-p completions.

statement: Finite plane actions and simultaneous local models — Every faithful action of a finite group $H$ on $\R^2$ by homeomorphisms is conjugate to an orthogonal action. When $H^+\ne1$, $H^+$ is cyclic, $H$ is cyclic or dihedral, and $(\R^2)^H$ is a single point. A nontrivial orientation-reversing involution has a fixed line. Every stabilizer in a finite action on a surface with universal cover $\R^2$ has an invariant disc on which the whole stabilizer acts by an orthogonal action. These conclusions supply the two local assertions used in \S15, folios 70--74, scans 141--149, and \S33, scan 440.
where_proved: Paper, Part B, statement B.1; computation locations are specified in that proof.

statement: The omitted orientation hypothesis in scans 146--147 — The displayed lemma on scan 147, taken without its preceding orientation hypothesis, is false. Its correct form is: an orientation-preserving finite-order homeomorphism $u$ of $\C$ commuting with $T(z)=z+1$ and satisfying $u(0)=0$ is the identity. The quotient $\C/\Z$ provides a complete proof along the route proposed in the manuscript.
where_proved: Paper, Part B, statement B.2; computation locations are specified in that proof.

statement: Sections and isolated fixed points — Let $\widetilde U\cong\R^2$. A faithful finite action on $U$ with $G^+\ne1$ has a bijection \[ U^G\longrightarrow \operatorname{Sec}(E\to G)/\pi. \] For every section subgroup $K$, $C_\pi(K)=1$. Existence of a section forces $G$ to be cyclic or dihedral. More generally, every nontrivial finite subgroup of $E$ whose orientation-preserving part is nontrivial is contained in exactly one maximal finite subgroup of $E$. For an orientation-preserving action the map from points with nontrivial stabilizer to maximal partial-section classes is a $G$-equivariant bijection. These are the theorem and corollary of \S15, folios 73--75, scans 148--151, with their stated orientation hypotheses.
where_proved: Paper, Part B, statement B.3; computation locations are specified in that proof.

statement: Reflection sections, ovals, and punctured ovals — Let $\sigma$ be an orientation-reversing involution of $U$ with $\widetilde U\cong\R^2$, and let $E\to C_2$ be its lift extension. There is a bijection \[ \pi_0(U^\sigma)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sec}(E\to C_2)/\pi. \] For the section $s$ associated with a component $Z$, inclusion induces an isomorphism $\pi_1(Z)\cong C_\pi(s)$. Thus the centralizer is $1$ for a line and $\Z$ for an oval. This includes punctures fixed or permuted by $\sigma$ and proves \S33, folios 222--225, scans 440--445, in the required noncompact cases.
where_proved: Paper, Part B, statement B.4; computation locations are specified in that proof.

statement: Recovering the incidence and cyclic order of real punctures — For a hyperbolic $U=X\setminus S$ with anti-involution $\sigma$, its discrete extension together with its indexed peripheral subgroups determines the following finite graph. Its vertices are the section classes of B.4, its edges are the real punctures, and each edge is attached to its two adjacent real half-branches. Every punctured oval gives one cycle, allowing a loop or two parallel edges. The graph recovers which punctures lie on each oval and their cyclic order up to reversal. Unpunctured ovals are the vertices with infinite cyclic centralizer. The claim uses the extension and peripheral incidence maps; a naked set of section classes alone has no such incidence information.
where_proved: Paper, Part B, statement B.5; computation locations are specified in that proof.

statement: The fundamental loop lemma of \S18 — Let $\pi=\pi_1(U)$ be hyperbolic and discrete, with its indexed peripheral structure and orientation module. A finite-order orientation-preserving automorphism of $\pi$ fixing a peripheral index and normalizing its subgroup $L_i$ is the identity. Consequently the peripheral extension attached to a nontrivial finite-order positive outer automorphism fixing $i$ cannot split. This proves the lemma and corollary of scans 193--194 without adding realizability to the hypotheses.

statement: The unrestricted fixed-subgroup question, with its replacement — The assertion $\pi^G=1$ for every finite $G\le\Aut_{\rm lac}(\pi)$ is false. For a hyperbolic discrete $\pi$, a nontrivial finite genuine loop action has fixed subgroup $1$ when its positive part is nontrivial. Its remaining possibility is a reflection action of $C_2$; its fixed subgroup is $1$ or $\Z$, as in B.4. For any finite-type faithful geometric action there are finitely many classes of full and partial sections. This answers questions (c) and (e), scans 197--198.

statement: Unique maximal sections fail for reflections, already in type $(0,3)$ — The orientation-free extension of question (d), scan 198, and of the expectation on scan 155 is false. Put \[ E=\langle s_0,s_1,s_2\mid s_j^2=1, (s_0s_1)^2=1, (s_1s_2)^3=1\rangle. \] There is a geometric extension $1\to\pi_{0,3}\to E\to S_3\times C_2\to1$. The reflection subgroup $\langle s_1\rangle$ is contained in two distinct maximal finite subgroups $\langle s_0,s_1\rangle\cong C_2^2$ and $\langle s_1,s_2\rangle\cong S_3$, which are not $\pi_{0,3}$-conjugate. The valid uniqueness statement is B.3, requiring a nontrivial positive part.

statement: The valid normalizer assertion — For a hyperbolic discrete group with loops, a nontrivial finite subgroup $K\le\Aut^+_{\rm lac}(\pi)$ is cyclic and \[ N_{\Aut^+_{\rm lac}(\pi)}(K)=C_{\Aut^+_{\rm lac}(\pi)}(K). \] An orientation-reversing element of its full normalizer acts on $K$ by inversion. Every finite positive overgroup of $K$ is cyclic. These are the valid assertions within the passage labelled ``Ultra fort!'' on scans 198--199.

statement: An intrinsic discrete formula for the multiplier — For a geometric finite extension of a hyperbolic discrete surface group, $E$ with its peripheral structure and orientation module $T$ determines $\mu_E$ on all torsion elements. On $E^+$ it is the rotation number of its canonical oriented boundary action. More explicitly, let $\widetilde{\operatorname{Homeo}}^+(S^1)\to\operatorname{Homeo}^+(S^1)$ be the central extension by the positively oriented deck translation $z$. For $u\in E^+$ of order $n$ and any lift $\widetilde u$, write $\widetilde u^{,n}=z^k$. Then \[ \mu_E(u)=\frac{k}{n}\pmod{\Z}\quad\hbox{in }T\otimes\Q/\Z. \] For a nonidentity orientation-reversing torsion element we put $\mu_E(u)$ equal to the unique nonzero element of order two. With this convention the formula is natural under isomorphisms preserving the loops and transporting $T$, satisfies $\mu(u^m)=m\mu(u)$, and has the same order as $u$. This answers the discrete intrinsicity question of \S15, folios 77--79, scans 155--160.

statement: Finite annulus and torus actions, and their multipliers — Every finite topological action on the torus is topologically conjugate to an affine action on $V/\Lambda$, where $\Lambda\cong\Z^2$ and $V=\Lambda\otimes\R$. For a fixed finite operator group $G$ such an action is specified by a homomorphism $A:G\to GL(\Lambda)$ and a cocycle $b\in Z^1(G,V/\Lambda)$, subject to faithfulness of $g\mapsto(x\mapsto A_gx+b_g)$. Translation conjugacy corresponds exactly to a coboundary, and \[ H^1(G,V/\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(G,\Lambda) \] is the connecting homomorphism. Linear changes of the lattice give the further conjugacies. Every finite annulus action has a simultaneous normal form \[ (x,t)\longmapsto(\epsilon_g x+a_g,\eta_g t), \qquad x\in\R/\Z,\quad t\in\R,\quad \epsilon_g,\eta_g\in\{1,-1\}. \] These descriptions determine the multiplier of every finite-order element in the respective lift extensions.

statement: The ``only counterexample'' of scan 179 — The assertion that a faithful homotopically trivial finite annulus action failing to be a translation action must be the single anti-involution $z\mapsto1/\overline z$ is false. For the two non-simply-connected abelian types, the exact replacement is: homotopically trivial torus actions are translation actions; homotopically trivial annulus actions are the finite subgroups of $SO(2)\times C_2$ in the normal form of B.14. Those contained in $SO(2)$ are translations, while those with nontrivial second projection include two different types of anti-involution and groups of arbitrarily large order.

statement: Complete topological classification of anti-involutions — Conjugacy classes of anti-involutions of a closed oriented genus-$g$ surface are classified by the orientability of the quotient and its number $b$ of boundary components. The possibilities are \[ \begin{array}{ll} \text{nonorientable quotient:}&0\le b\le g,\quad h=g+1-b\ge1\text{ crosscaps};\\ \text{orientable quotient:}&b\ge1,\quad g=2h+b-1,\quad h\ge0. \end{array} \] There are $(g+1)+\lfloor(g+2)/2\rfloor=\lfloor(3g+4)/2\rfloor$ classes. For $\nu$ unlabelled invariant punctures the additional data are an integer $r\ge0$ and an unordered list $(q_1,\ldots,q_b)$ of nonnegative integers with $2r+\sum q_i=\nu$: $r$ is the number of interior punctures of the quotient, and $q_i$ counts punctures on its $i$th boundary circle.

statement: The two centralizer corollaries in both quotient families — Let $g\ge2$, and let an anti-involution of $X_g$ have $b>0$ ovals, with outer class $\sigma$. There are exactly $b$ classes of order-two genuine loop automorphisms lifting $\sigma$, under conjugacy by $\pi_g$. For each lift $u$, $\pi_g^u\cong\Z$. The positive centralizer of $\sigma$ acts transitively on those $b$ classes. More precisely, writing $A=\Aut_{\rm lac}(\pi_g)$ and $O=\Out_{\rm lac}(\pi_g)$, there is an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow\pi_g^u\longrightarrow C_{A^+}(u) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Stab}_{C_{O^+}(\sigma)}([u])\longrightarrow1, \] and the last group has index $b$ in $C_{O^+}(\sigma)$. The corresponding full centralizer image also has index $b$. This proves Corollaries 1 and 2, folios 225--226, scans 445--448, for both orientable and nonorientable quotients.

statement: The tube twists, their maximality property, and their normalizer — For $g\ge2$, the elements $\rho_j$ of \S33, scans 453--470, are full Dehn twists about a cut system $c_1,\ldots,c_g$: disjoint nonseparating curves with connected complement. They generate $H\cong\Z^g$. This is not a maximal free abelian subgroup of $\mathcal T_g$: it is contained in a multitwist subgroup of rank $3g-3$. It has the precise maximality property of being a full multitwist group of largest rank whose supporting multicurve has connected complement. Furthermore \[ N_{\mathcal T_g}(H)=\operatorname{Stab}_{\mathcal T_g}(\{c_1,\ldots,c_g\}), \qquad N_{\mathcal T_g}(H)/C_{\mathcal T_g}(H)\cong S_g\times C_2. \] The action on $H$ permutes its basis and multiplies every basis vector by the same orientation sign. Cutting and capping gives an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow N_{\mathcal T_g}(H) \longrightarrow\mathcal T^{\rm pairs}_{0,2g}\longrightarrow1, \] where the last extended sphere mapping class group preserves the partition of its $2g$ punctures into the $g$ unordered gluing pairs.

statement: Presentation (52) and its exact correction — For $g\ge2$, presentation (52) on scan 469 does not present the stated $\Z^g$-by-finite group. Put $r=\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_1$ and $\rho_j=r^j\tau'\tau r^{-j}$, $0\le j<g$. The printed presentation gives \[ F_g\rtimes\bigl(D_{4g}\times\langle\tau\rangle\bigr), \] where $D_{4g}=\langle r,\varepsilon_1\mid r^{2g}=\varepsilon_1^2=1, \varepsilon_1r\varepsilon_1=r^{-1}\rangle$ permutes the free generators through its action on $\Z/g$, and $\tau$ inverts each free generator. Adding the relations $[\rho_i,\rho_j]=1$ for $i<j$ gives exactly $\Z^g\rtimes(D_{4g}\times C_2)$ with the manuscript's specified action.

statement: The one-holed-torus subgroups and the proved part of the analogy — For $g\ge2$, choose a one-holed torus $W_j$ containing $c_j$ and a transverse curve $d_j$ with $i(c_j,d_j)=1$. Its group fixing its boundary pointwise embeds by extension by the identity into $\mathcal T_g^+$. It is \[ B_3=\langle A_j,B_j\mid A_jB_jA_j=B_jA_jB_j\rangle, \] and capping the boundary gives \[ 1\longrightarrow\langle T_{\partial W_j}\rangle\cong\Z \longrightarrow B_3\longrightarrow SL_2(\Z)\longrightarrow1, \qquad (A_jB_j)^6=T_{\partial W_j}^{\pm1}. \] This extension has no section. For disjoint chosen $W_j$, their supported subgroups commute and, together with $H$, preserve their boundary multicurve; they do not generate $\mathcal T_g^+$. On explicit generators the tube subgroup and these two twists act by \[ \begin{array}{lll} \rho_j:&a_j\mapsto a_j,&b_j\mapsto b_ja_j,\\ B_j:&a_j\mapsto a_jb_j^{-1},&b_j\mapsto b_j, \end{array} \] fixing the other handle generators of $\pi_g=\langle a_j,b_j\mid\prod_j[a_j,b_j]=1\rangle$.

statement: Explicit outer words for the antipodally paired tube model — For $g\ge2$, put $n=2g$ and label the equatorial holes by $j\in\Z/n$, with $j$ glued by a tube to $j+g$. The following presentation and substitutions compute the entire exterior action requested on scan 467: \[ \pi_g=\left\langle x_0,\ldots,x_{g-1},p_0,\ldots,p_{g-1} \ \middle|\ R=1\right\rangle, \qquad R=x_0\cdots x_{g-1} \prod_{j=0}^{g-1}(p_j^{-1}x_j^{-1}p_j). \] Extend the notation, with all subscripts read modulo $n$, by \[ \begin{gathered} x_{j+g}=p_j^{-1}x_j^{-1}p_j,\qquad p_{j+g}=p_j^{-1},\\ u_j=(x_0\cdots x_j)^{-1},\quad u_{n-1}=1,\qquad q_j=u_j^{-1}p_j u_{j+g-1}. \end{gathered} \] Let $r=\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_1$ and $s=\varepsilon_1$ as in B.20. Representatives of their outer automorphisms, and of $\tau$ and $\rho_k$, are specified on the $2g$ displayed generators by \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} &x_j&p_j\\ \hline r&x_{j+1}&p_{j+1}\\ s&u_{-j}^{-1}x_{-j}u_{-j}&q_{-j}\\ \tau&u_{j+g-1}^{-1}x_{j+g}^{-1}u_{j+g-1}&q_j^{-1}\\ \rho_k&x_j&x_j^{\delta_{jk}}p_j. \end{array} \] The map to $\operatorname{Out}(\pi_g)$ defined by these substitutions is the geometric action of $\Z^g\rtimes(D_{4g}\times C_2)$ of B.20. The finite factor acts by \[ r\rho_jr^{-1}=\rho_{j+1},\qquad s\rho_js^{-1}=\rho_{-j},\qquad \tau\rho_j\tau^{-1}=\rho_j^{-1}, \] with indices in these three formulas taken modulo $g$.

statement: Relations for arbitrary strips and a uniform obstruction to generation — Choose for each $c_j$ one simple transversal $d_j$, using a strip in the complement of the other tubes, so that $i(c_i,d_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Let $W_j$ be a regular neighbourhood of $c_j\cup d_j$, a one-holed torus, and put $A_j=T_{c_j}=\rho_j$, $B_j=T_{d_j}$. Its supported subgroup is the central extension $\langle A_j,B_j\rangle\cong B_3$ of B.21, with quotient $SL_2(\Z)$. The exact pairwise relations are \[ [A_i,A_j]=1,\quad [A_i,B_j]=1\ (i\ne j),\qquad A_jB_jA_j=B_jA_jB_j. \] For distinct $i,j$, the two supported subgroups commute precisely when $i(d_i,d_j)=0$. For intersection one, $B_i,B_j$ obey the braid relation and do not commute; for intersection at least two they freely generate a free group of rank two. For every such choice of one strip per tube and every $g\ge2$, these $g$ supported subgroups, together with $H$, generate a proper subgroup of $\mathcal T_g^+$.

statement: The invariant braid group and nonabelian cohomology — Let a finite group act faithfully and orientation preservingly on a hyperbolic $U$, and let $R=U^!$ be its finite set of points with nontrivial stabilizer. Put $V=U\setminus R$, $B=\{f\in A^0:f|_R=\id\}$, and $B^0=\operatorname{Homeo}(V)^0$. With the action by conjugation, we have \[ (B/B^0)^\Gamma=1,\qquad H^1(\Gamma,B^0)=1, \qquad (A^0)^\Gamma=B^\Gamma\cong \operatorname{Homeo}(V/\Gamma)^0. \] Here the quotient group identifies canonically with $\pi_1(\operatorname{Conf}_R(U),R)$ by evaluation, and its invariant subgroup is the $H^0$ asked for on scan 285.

statement: The oriented drilling equivalence and the bijection — Fix a finite group $\Gamma$ and faithful orientation-preserving outer actions on discrete hyperbolic groups with loops. Let $\Phi(\pi,\Gamma)$ be the set of $\pi$-conjugacy classes of nontrivial maximal finite subgroups of the canonical extension. Filling a specified $\Gamma$-stable set $J$ of punctures with nontrivial stabilizers induces an equivalence between the category of such drilled actions and the category of filled actions with a specified subset $J\subset\Phi(\pi,\Gamma)$. In particular \[ \Phi(\pi',\Gamma)\amalg J\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Phi(\pi,\Gamma) \] is a canonical $\Gamma$-equivariant bijection. Drilling all of $\Phi$ produces a torsion-free extension, uniquely up to the unique exterior isomorphism over the specified filled object.

statement: Torsion-free finite extensions with peripheral data — Let $\pi$ be a discrete hyperbolic surface group, possibly punctured, and let $1\to\pi\to E\to\Gamma\to1$ be a torsion-free extension by a finite group whose outer action preserves the loop structure. Then $E$ is the fundamental group of a finite-type surface, possibly nonorientable. Its peripheral subgroups are the centralizers in $E$ of the peripheral subgroups of $\pi$. With their conjugacy classes it is a surface group with loops in this extended sense. The associated compact surface and boundary groups form a Poincar\'e duality pair of dimension two with its orientation local system.

statement: Zero-level fidelity for a faithful infinite cyclic sphere action — Let $\Gamma=\Z$ act faithfully on $S^2$ by an irrational axis rotation, $u(1)(\theta,t)=(\theta+2\pi\alpha,t)$ with $\alpha\in\R\setminus\Q$ and the usual collapse of the latitude circles at $t=\pm1$. The induced transporter map has \[ \pi_1(M,1)=\Z\longrightarrow\pi_1(N,1)=\Z/2, \qquad n\longmapsto n\bmod2. \] Its kernel is $2\Z$, so level $0$ fails for this faithful action of an infinite group. This is the exact fundamental-groupoid comparison; C.24 separately retains the higher homotopy of $A$ when computing the untruncated homotopy-fixed space. The hyperbolic zero-level question recorded in C.12 has its stated, stronger surface hypothesis.

statement: Transitive centralizers on a closed hyperbolic surface — Let $X$ be a closed connected orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and give $A=\operatorname{Homeo}(X)$ the compact-open topology. For every subgroup $L\leq A$ acting transitively on $X$, the centralizer $C_A(L)$ is finite. Consequently, for an arbitrary strict action $u:\Gamma\to A$ and a based loop $f_t$ in $C_{A^0}(u(\Gamma))$, the loop is equivariantly null-homotopic whenever the subgroup generated by its values acts transitively on $X$. There also exists a closed torsion-free Polish subgroup $G\leq\operatorname{Homeo}(D^2,\partial D^2)$ with $\pi_1G=\Z$; extension by the identity embeds it closedly in every hyperbolic $A^0$, where its displayed generator becomes null-homotopic. This last subgroup is not asserted to be a centralizer.

statement: Orbit types of a loop-generated plane group — Let $t\mapsto f_t$ be a compact-open continuous based loop in $\operatorname{Homeo}^+(\R^2)$, with $f_0=f_1=\id$, and put \[ L=\{f_t:0\leq t\leq1\},\qquad P=L\cup L^{-1}, \qquad G=\langle P\rangle. \] Every $G$-orbit is one of the following: an open subset of the plane; a point; a Jordan curve; or the image of a continuous injective map $\eta:\R\to\R^2$ that restricts to a homeomorphism on every compact interval. In the last case its intrinsic arc order identifies it with the line, but no global homeomorphism from $\R$ to the orbit with its subspace topology is asserted. The loop restricts continuously in the compact-open topology to the intrinsically ordered line. Every homeomorphism commuting with $G$ carries these orbit types to the same types and induces a homeomorphism between the corresponding intrinsic lines, allowing reversal of their orders.

statement: Circle centralizers and the winding of a plane loop — For every subgroup $H\leq\operatorname{Homeo}(S^1)$, put $C=C_{\operatorname{Homeo}^+(S^1)}(H)$, with the compact-open topology. Its image lies in $\Z^H$, with $H$ acting on $\Z$ by its orientation character. A based loop of winding zero has an explicit contraction in $C$ that is natural under all homeomorphisms between circles. In particular, a based null-homotopic loop in $\operatorname{Homeo}^+(\R^2)$ preserving a Jordan curve restricts to a winding-zero loop on that curve. Its restriction therefore has this natural contraction against every commuting circle homeomorphism.
