statement: Properness of a transitive-action centralizer — Let $V$ be a connected second-countable surface without boundary, and let $K$ be a closed subgroup of $\operatorname{Homeo}(V)$ acting transitively on $V$, with the compact-open topology. Put $N=C_{\operatorname{Homeo}(V)}(K)$. Then $N$ is locally compact, its action on $V$ is free and proper, and for every $x\in V$ evaluation is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset \[ N\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{ev}_x\ } N_K(K_x)/K_x\ \subseteq\ K/K_x\cong V. \tag{C.30.1} \] Under the normalizer-quotient group structure, this is an anti-isomorphism of topological groups. For an open orbit $O$ of the loop-generated group in C.28, the image in $\operatorname{Homeo}(O)$ of its operator stabilizer lies in such an $N$; the closure of that image acts freely and properly on $O$.

statement: Track control and continuity at the fixed stratum — Let $f_t$ be a based null-homotopic loop in $\operatorname{Homeo}^+(\R^2)$, let $G$ be its generated group as in C.28, and let $Y$ be the union of the nonopen $G$-orbits. This is a closed subset of the plane. Define $Q_{s,t}$ on $Y$ by C.27 on each intrinsic line orbit, by the descended formula of C.29 on each circle orbit, and by the identity on point orbits. Then every $Q_{s,t}$ is a bijection of $Y$ preserving each orbit, and \[ Q_{s,t}^{-1}=Q_{s,t}[f^{-1}],\qquad Q_{s,t}(x)\in\{f_u(x):0\leq u\leq1\},\qquad Q_{s,t}^{-1}(x)\in\{f_u^{-1}(x):0\leq u\leq1\}. \tag{C.31.1} \] Here $Q[f^{-1}]$ means the same construction applied to the based inverse loop $u\mapsto f_u^{-1}$, which generates the same group. Both evaluation maps $(s,t,x)\mapsto Q_{s,t}^{\pm1}(x)$ are continuous at every point of $[0,1]^2\times Z$, where $Z=\{x:f_u(x)=x\text{ for all }u\}$ is the point-orbit stratum. statement: A closed genus-two counterexample to full profinite recognition — The assertion that every torsion-free finite extension of a full profinite closed hyperbolic surface group is a completed surface group is false. There is an exact extension \[ 1\longrightarrow H=\widehat\pi_1(\Sigma_2) \longrightarrow E\longrightarrow C_2\longrightarrow1 \tag{D.30.1} \] with $E$ torsion-free and with a faithful outer action, such that \[ H^2(E;\mathbb F_3)=\mathbb F_3,\qquad H^2(E;\mathbb F_5)=0. \tag{D.30.2} \] No profinite completion of a discrete surface group has these two cohomology groups. The exact maximal pro-$p$ quotients are \[ E^{(2)}\cong\widehat{\pi_1(N_3)}^{(2)},\qquad E^{(3)}\cong\mathbb Z_3^2,\qquad E^{(p)}\cong\widehat F_2^{(p)}\quad(p\ne2,3), \tag{D.30.3} \] where $N_3$ is the closed nonorientable surface of genus three. Thus the counterexample also gives the precise maps through which its separate pro-$p$ surface presentations arise. Its outer involution is conjugate to no element of the extended geometric completion. Its fixed discretization and prediscretization sets are both empty.

statement: One exact conjugator equation and its finite obstructions — Let $P$ be the full pure three-cusp group of D.32, let $F=\widehat F(x,y)$, and put $\delta(x)=x^{-1}$, $\delta(y)=y^{-1}$. The fibers of the assignment are exactly $(\mu,h,u)\mapsto(\mu,h,u(xy)^a)$ for $a\in\widehat\Z$. It therefore induces a homeomorphism from the corresponding quotient of $\mathcal S_\alpha$ to (D.35c). For $\alpha\in GT_0$, the inclusion $GT_0\hookrightarrow P$ gives the equality of actual conjugator sets \[ \operatorname{Conj}_{GT_0}(\delta,\alpha) =\operatorname{Conj}_{P}(\delta,\alpha). \tag{D.35d} \] The defining Harbater--Schneps relations for the conjugating pair follow from the proof below; they are not discarded. statement: Full generation and exact negative conjugator equations — Put $F=\widehat F(x,y)$ and $c=[x,y]$. Every closed subgroup $J\leq F$ satisfying $c\in\overline{[J,J]}$ is $F$ itself. Consequently every continuous endomorphism of $F$ carrying $c$ to a conjugate of $c^\mu$, with $\mu\in\widehat\Z^\times$, is an automorphism. Let $b$ be any negative full once-punctured-torus outer involution, with the specified extension \[ E=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle,\quad v^2=1,\quad vcv^{-1}=c^{-1}. \] Let $A_2$ be its action on $H_1(F,\Z_2)$. Set $v_i=c^iv$ and $\alpha_i=\operatorname{Inn}(v_i)|_F$, for $i=0,1$. On a separate free profinite group $F_0=\widehat F(X,Y)$, with $c_0=[X,Y]$, use the two standard actual negative involutions \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} &X&Y\\ \hline \beta_0&YXY^{-1}&Y^{-1}\\ \beta_1&Y&X . \end{array} \tag{D.61a} \] For $j=0,1$, let $\mathcal T_j(b)$ be the space of peripheral outer isomorphisms $[\phi]:F_0\to F$ conjugating $[\beta_j]$ to $b$. The peripheral requirement is $\phi(c_0)\sim_F c^\mu$ for a full unit $\mu$. Identifying $F_0$ with $F$ by $X\mapsto x$, $Y\mapsto y$ identifies this with the usual outer conjugator space. For $A_2\bmod2=I$, define \[ \begin{split} \mathcal S_{0,i}=\{(\mu,h,w):\ &\mu\in\widehat\Z^\times,\ h\in F,\quad w^2=1,\ w\in E\setminus F,\\ &w\text{ belongs to the other full section class},\\ &[h,w]=1,\quad [h,v_i]=c^\mu\}. \end{split} \tag{D.61b} \] Here \emph{other} means the class distinct from the common cusp-reflection class of D.58. There is a continuous bijection, with continuous inverse, \[ \mathcal S_{0,0}\sqcup\mathcal S_{0,1} \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathcal T_0(b),\qquad (\mu,h,w)\longmapsto [\,X\mapsto h,\ Y\mapsto v_iw\,]. \tag{D.61c} \] For $A_2\bmod2\ne I$, define \[ \mathcal S_{1,i} =\{(\mu,f)\in\widehat\Z^\times\times F: [f,\alpha_i(f)]=c^\mu\}. \tag{D.61d} \] The corresponding continuous bijection is \[ \mathcal S_{1,0}\sqcup\mathcal S_{1,1} \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathcal T_1(b),\qquad (\mu,f)\longmapsto [\,X\mapsto f,\ Y\mapsto\alpha_i(f)\,]. \tag{D.61e} \] Equivalently, writing $z=fv_i$, the last equation is \[ z\in E\setminus F,\qquad [z^2,v_i]=c^\mu. \tag{D.61f} \] The two basis images are then $zv_i,v_iz$. statement: Primitive homology centralizers and the exact cusp-transporter root test — Let $F=\widehat F(x,y)$ and let $g\in F$ have primitive abelianization: there is a continuous homomorphism $\rho:F\to\widehat\Z$ with $\rho(g)=1$. Now use the exact negative torus extension of D.58--D.61: \[ \begin{gathered} E=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle,\qquad v^2=1,\qquad \alpha=\operatorname{Inn}(v)|_F,\qquad c=[x,y],\qquad \alpha(c)=c^{-1},\\ C=C_F(v),\qquad gvg^{-1}=cv. \end{gathered} \tag{D.62b} \] D.59 supplies the required primitive abelianization of this $g$ and the exact inclusion $C\subseteq\overline{F'}$. For every $g'\in gC$, the following two conditions are equivalent: \[ \begin{split} &\alpha(g')\text{ is conjugate to }g'\text{ in }F;\\ &C_E(g')\text{ contains an element outside }F. \end{split} \tag{D.62c} \] Their consequences and converse maps are exact: \begin{enumerate} \item In the two-section-class case of D.58, they are equivalent to the existence of an involution $w\in E\setminus F$ centralizing $g'$. The specified continuous finite wreath maps consequently have the same full images on $K^+$ and $D^+$, for every coefficient prime. The full source-membership equation remains unresolved. Let $\rho=r_*:\widehat L_0\longrightarrow\widehat L_2$. The induced involution and its fixed subgroup are \[ R_*(u,v)=(\rho^{-1}(v),\rho(u)),\qquad (\widehat L_0\times\widehat L_2)^{R_*} =\{(u,\rho(u)):u\in\widehat L_0\}. \tag{F.15.3} \] The actual fixed-configuration map \[ i:M\setminus\{a_+,a_-\}\longrightarrow X,\qquad z\longmapsto(z,r(z)) \tag{F.15.4} \] induces a full profinite embedding, and \[ \begin{split} C_{\widehat J}(\mathsf r) &=\widehat i_*\, \widehat{\pi_1(M\setminus\{a_+,a_-\},x_0)} \ \cong\widehat F_7,\\ p\bigl(C_{\widehat J}(\mathsf r)\bigr) &=(\widehat L_0\times\widehat L_2)^{R_*},\\ C_B(\mathsf r) &\cong\ker\bigl( \widehat{\pi_1(M\setminus\{a_+,a_-\},x_0)} \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{fill}_{a_+,a_-}\ } \widehat{\pi_1(M,x_0)}\bigr). \end{split} \tag{F.15.5} \] In particular the last kernel is the closed normal subgroup generated by the two based branch meridians in this specified $\widehat F_7$. More precisely, there is a homeomorphism of compact spaces \[ \begin{split} C_B(\mathsf r)\backslash B &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } Z^1(R_*,B):=\{\delta\in B:\delta R_*(\delta)=1\},\\ C_B(\mathsf r)b&\longmapsto b^{-1}R_*(b). \end{split} \tag{F.15.6} \] Consequently the quotient map $\pi:P_8\to P_8/B$ gives the exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow C_B(\mathsf r) \longrightarrow C_{P_8}(\mathsf r) \xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }(P_8/B)^{R_*} \longrightarrow1 . \tag{F.15.7} \] For the exact equalizer $\mathcal E_7$ of F.14, set \[ \mathcal B_u=\{b\in B:b^{-1}R_*(b)=d(u)\}. \tag{F.15.8} \] This is a nonempty left $C_B(\mathsf r)$-coset for every $u\in\mathcal E_7$. The centralizing representatives of its actual $B$-coset are exactly \[ \bigl(\widehat\phi(u)B\bigr)\cap C_{P_8}(\mathsf r) =\widehat\phi(u)b^{-1}C_B(\mathsf r) \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_u). \tag{F.15.9} \] The source embedding has trivial intersection with $B$. It follows that the intersection of (F.15.9) with $\widehat\phi(\widehat{\pi_1(Y)})$ is either empty or the singleton $\{\widehat\phi(u)\}$, and is the latter exactly for $u\in\mathcal E$. These formulas determine the correction and its ambiguity; triviality of the full residual group $\mathcal E$ is still unresolved.

statement: The exact trace obstruction and all affine marginal images with scalar field of order nine — Retain the actual inclusions $\mathcal K_\pm\leq R_\pm\leq V_\pm$ of F.19--F.25. Fix either sign, and temporarily write these groups as $K\leq R\leq V$. A proper affine marginal image $\rho(K)\subsetneq\rho(R)$, for a continuous $\rho:V\to\operatorname{Aff}_1(k)$ over a finite field, has an actual continuous affine image of the following form: \[ \begin{gathered} \rho':V\longrightarrow k_0\rtimes D,\qquad \rho'(V)=k_0\rtimes D,\qquad \rho'(R)=k_0\rtimes C,\\ \rho'(K)\ \leq\ \ker\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/k_1}:k_0\to k_1\bigr) \rtimes C,\\ C=\chi(R)=\chi(K)\ne\{1\},\qquad D=\chi(V),\qquad k_1=\mathbb F_p(C)\subsetneq k_0=\mathbb F_p(D). \end{gathered} \tag{F.26.1} \] Here $\chi$ is the original scalar character, retained by the explicit conjugation and coefficient map constructed below. In particular the last group in (F.26.1) is a proper subgroup of the displayed $R$ image. For any finite-field data $k_0,\chi,C,k_1$ as in (F.26.1), including the equality case $k_1=k_0$, put $q_1=|k_1|$ and $m=[k_0:k_1]$. The exact coefficient map is \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr T_\chi: Z^1_{\rm cont}(V,k_{0,\chi})&\longrightarrow Z^1_{\rm cont}(K,k_{1,\chi|K}),\\ d&\longmapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/k_1}(d|K). \end{aligned} \tag{F.26.2} \] Its known kernel subspace is \[ \mathscr P_\chi= \{\,g\mapsto(\chi(g)-1)b: b\in k_0,\ \operatorname{Tr}(b)=0\,\}. \tag{F.26.3} \] Every element of $\ker\mathscr T_\chi\setminus\mathscr P_\chi$ gives a proper actual affine marginal image, and every proper affine marginal image gives such an element for the data in (F.26.1). Thus $\ker\mathscr T_\chi=\mathscr P_\chi$ for all the stated data is an exact remaining criterion for the full scalar affine image equality. The proof gives an explicit coefficient isomorphism identifying this criterion with the summed restrictions for the distinct characters $\chi^{q_1^j}$, $0\leq j<m$. Its rank target is $6m+1$ on $7m$ columns; no general attainment of that rank is asserted here. For the scalar field of order nine that rank is attained. More precisely, for every finite field $k$ and every continuous $\rho:V_\pm\to\operatorname{Aff}_1(k)$ whose scalar values generate a subfield of order nine, \[ \rho(\mathcal K_\pm)=\rho(R_\pm). \tag{F.26.4} \] Consequently this equality holds for every continuous map $V_\pm\to\operatorname{Aff}_1(\mathbb F_9)$, including maps whose scalar field is $\mathbb F_3$. The finite calculation proving the additional field case exhausts exactly $7\,560$ character tuples and retains the literal F.23 source automorphisms.

statement: Torsion in an acting group and its action on torsion are different assertions Lochak and Schneps (1997, Proposition 4(i)) prove \(C_F(c)=1\); Proposition 4(ii) proves that \(c\) is self-centralizing in \(\widehat{GT}\). Schneps (1997, \S1.4(4)) and Lochak and Schneps (2006, Question 1.4) ask whether all nonidentity torsion in \(\widehat{GT}\) consists of conjugates of \(c\). Harbater and Schneps (2000, Main Theorem(a), proved by Propositions 3--4 and Theorem 2) identify \(\widehat{GT}_0\) with the centralizer in \(\mathcal P\) of the geometric \(S_3\). Collas's genus-zero Theorems 3.3 and 3.10 identify prime-order torsion in \(\widehat\Gamma_{0,[n]}\) with discrete torsion and prove the \(\lambda\)-conjugacy action of \(\widehat{GT}\). His genus-one Theorems 6.3 and 6.5 give the corresponding statements with acting group \(\widehat{GR}\), isomorphic to the subgroup denoted \(I\Gamma\) in that article; replacing it there by all of \(\widehat{GT}\) is not justified by those theorems.\cite{A_LS1997,A_Schneps1997,A_LS2006,A_HS2000,A_Collas2012a,A_Collas2012b}

statement: Relative pronilpotent levels recover the full peripheral group For an open characteristic subgroup \(U\) of \(F\), put \[ R_U=R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U),\quad F_U=F/R_U,\quad P_U=\operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(F_U). \] For \(V\subset U\), the quotient \(F_V\to F_U\) induces a continuous epimorphism \(P_V\to P_U\). There is an isomorphism of profinite groups \[ \mathcal P \xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_U P_U. \] Two elements of \(\mathcal P\) are conjugate in \(\mathcal P\) if and only if their images are conjugate in every \(P_U\). This proves Lead 1.
notes: All transition maps typed; conjugacy detection uses compact transporter sets.

statement: A central quotient is the exact obstruction to a peripheral lift Let \(N\) be a closed characteristic subgroup of \(F\), and let \([N,F]\) denote the closed subgroup generated by commutators between \(N\) and \(F\). An automorphism \(a\) of \(F/N\), with specified conjugators \(b_i\) satisfying \[ a(\bar x_i)=b_i\bar x_i b_i^{-1},\qquad (x_1,x_2,x_3)=(x,y,z), \] lifts to a peripheral automorphism of \(F\) with these conjugators if and only if it lifts to a peripheral \emph{automorphism} of \(F/[N,F]\) with conjugators above the \(b_i\). This proves Lead 2.
notes: Central quotient lift must itself be an automorphism; no equivariant lift inferred.

statement: Full conjugacy is an additional quotient of nonabelian cohomology With the notation of A.7, the full \(G\)-conjugacy classes of nonidentity involutions are \[ \widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}\backslash H^1(C_2,H_G). \] The action of \(\mu\), using any lift \(\theta_\mu\), is \[ [a]\longmapsto[\,\theta_\mu a\,c(\theta_\mu^{-1})\,]. \] For \(\mathcal N=\ker(\mathcal P\to P_F)\), the \(\mathcal N\)-conjugacy classes of involutions with image exactly \(c_F\) are \(H^1(C_2,\mathcal N)\). notes: Some local multiplier-one conjugator exists, not necessarily the specified h.

statement: A peripheral reflection triangle is equivalent to full conjugacy For a nontrivial involution \(\alpha\in\mathcal P\) let \(E=F\rtimes_\alpha C_2\). Then \(\alpha\) is conjugate to \(c\) in \(\mathcal P\) exactly when there are involutions \(t_0,t_1,t_2\) representing its three section classes such that \[ a=t_1t_0,\qquad b=t_0t_2,\qquad d=t_2t_1 \] generate conjugates of the respective inertia groups of \(x,y,z\), and the \(t_i\) generate \(E\) topologically. The last condition is equivalent to generation in every \(E/R_U\).
notes: Cote145 scan23 product-order convention made explicit.

statement: Dyadic and mixed-prime involution obstructions A.9 does not determine all two-primary classes or all gluing classes over \(U=F'F^3\) and \(U_{12}\). A.25 below constructs an actual involution with parity one in the image of \(\widehat{GT}_0\) at \(U_{12}\), and A.24 proves that this parity descends to that outer image. Thus the existence assertion at this specified relative level is proved. Lead 3 still needs a compatible order-two full lift. Neither R2 nor A.3 supplies that further equivariance. For a surjection \(G\to Q\) with kernel \(L\), a chosen lift \(t\) of an involution can be corrected to an involution \(ut\), \(u\in L\), exactly when \[ u(tut^{-1})=t^{-2}. \] Surjectivity asserts the existence of \(t\), not solvability of this nonabelian norm equation. The map \(C_4\to C_2\) disproves that implication in general, but is not a counterexample in the peripheral groups. The residual task is to solve the norm equations compatibly in the actual relative-level kernels with the specified frames and \(\Delta=1\), or to prove they are insoluble.
notes: A.25 gives an actual parity-one involution at U12; A.31 continues it compatibly through all relative principal-congruence levels. Complete dyadic/mixed-prime classification and arbitrary smaller characteristic levels remain open.

statement: Parity on arbitrary involutions For an involution \(\tau=(-1,f)\) in \(\widehat{GT}_0\), R3 gives \(\Delta(\tau)=\delta((1,f))\). It is zero for A.7's continuum family and for every \(\widehat{GT}_0\)-conjugate of \(c\). The cocycle relation alone gives only \(2\Delta(a)=0\) in \(\mathbb F_2\). A.25 gives such an involution in an actual relative outer image of \(\widehat{GT}_0\), but no full involution of parity one or universal full vanishing proof is obtained, in \(\widehat{GT}_0\) or \(\widehat{GT}\).
notes: A.25 and A.31 give Delta-one involutions in actual relative outer images and their congruence-tower inverse limit. No full Delta-one involution or universal full vanishing proof.

statement: The three full conjugacy assertions We have not decided whether every involution of \(\mathcal P,\widehat{GT}_0,\widehat{GT}\) is conjugate to \(c\) in its respective group. A.2 detects conjugacy of a fixed pair on all relative levels; A.11 identifies the equivalent peripheral generation condition. Neither supplies the compatible local conjugators or reflection triangles whose existence is required. For \S31, folios 198--199 verso, scans 391--394, the full finite-subgroup conclusion proved by R1 is that the only abstract possibilities in \(\mathcal P\) are \(1,C_2\), and \(C_2=\langle c\rangle\) occurs. Exhaustion of its embedding conjugacy classes is exactly the remaining assertion.
notes: All three full conjugacy assertions unresolved; no claim of complete resolution.

statement: The pronilpotent lifting kernel also has continuum many cohomology classes Put \(Q=\mathcal P_F\), \(\mathcal N=\ker(\mathcal P\to Q)\), and write \(c_Q\) for the image of \(c\). There is a canonical closed injection \[ C_Q(c_Q)/\langle c_Q\rangle \longrightarrow H^1(C_2,\mathcal N),\qquad \bar\beta\longmapsto[\beta c\beta^{-1}c]. \] Its image is exactly the \(\mathcal N\)-conjugacy classes in the fibre over \(c_Q\) which are conjugate to \(c\) in \(\mathcal P\). Both its domain and \(H^1(C_2,\mathcal N)\) have cardinality \(2^{\aleph_0}\). Thus the large cohomology set does not itself provide an additional full involution-conjugacy class.
notes: The large H1 is not evidence of an exotic full conjugacy class. All displayed classes are full P-conjugates of c.

statement: A prescribed reflection splits every pro-two extension of the symmetric group Let \(1\to K\to E\xrightarrow{q}S_3\to1\) be an extension of profinite groups with \(K\) pro-two. If a transposition \(t\in S_3\) has an involution lift \(\widetilde t\in E\), then there is a continuous section \(j:S_3\to E\) satisfying \(j(t)=\widetilde t\).
depends_on: Restriction/corestriction double-coset identities; finite extension cocycles; compactness
notes: The proof uses the special Sylow-2 double-coset structure of S3, not a general order-preserving lifting assertion.

statement: The parity-one relative frame can be chosen anti-invariant under conjugation In the notation of R2, put \(H_0=F'F^3\), \(\Gamma_2=\widehat B/O^2(H_0)\), and let \(d=\operatorname{Inn}(s)\circ c\), so that \(d(s)=s\), \(d(r)=r^{-1}\), \(d(x)=y^{-1}\), and \(d(y)=x^{-1}\). There is an actual element \[ b\in C_{H_0^{(2)}}(r),\qquad q(b)=[5I],\qquad d(b)=b^{-1}. \] Consequently the identity automorphism of \(\widehat B/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(H_0)\), with \(s\)- and \(\tau\)-frames one and \(r\)-frame equal to \(b\) at two and one at all other primes, is a framed cocycle for conjugation by \(c\). Its modulo-twelve frame parity is one. This establishes local equivariance of these data; it does not assert an equivariant full lift.
depends_on: R2/E58 joint quotient; A.16; coprime complement conjugacy
notes: Only local framed equivariance is proved. An R2 lift sigma has Delta=1 and (sigma c)^2 in the specified frame kernel L; the full norm equation in L remains open.

statement: R2 does not admit an unrestricted order-preserving refinement There is an actual involution of \(\operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(F/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(F))\) which lifts to a full peripheral automorphism by R2 but has no involution lift in \(\mathcal P\).
depends_on: R1; R2; A.2; product decomposition in A.15
notes: Refutes an unrestricted order-preserving strengthening of R2. The multiplier is mixed-sign; the globally negative fibre of A.17 remains open.

statement: The square obstruction at an abelian refinement and the character-lifting test Suppose \(a\) is a lift of a quotient involution, \(a^2\in L\), and \(L_0\triangleleft\langle L,a\rangle\) is contained in \(L\), with \(M=L/L_0\) finite abelian. Conjugation by \(a\) makes \(M\) a \(C_2\)-module. An involution exists above that quotient element in \(\langle L,a\rangle/L_0\) exactly when \[ [a^2]=0\quad\hbox{in}\quad H^2(C_2,M)=M^{a}/(1+a)M. \] This obstruction vanishes when \(M\) has odd order. For elementary abelian two-primary \(M\), its target is \(\ker(a+1)/\operatorname{im}(a+1)\). If \(\Delta\) has a continuous lift to a character \(\widehat{GT}_0\to\mathbb Z/4\), then it vanishes on every involution. The same conclusion follows from a continuous lift of \(\delta\) on \(\mathcal H\) which is invariant under conjugation by \(c\). Existence of either lift is not established here.
notes: Odd-primary abelian obstructions vanish; dyadic ones may survive. No global norm solution or Z/4 lift of Delta is proved.

statement: The locally glued symmetric subgroup does not lift in the standard extension Let \(H_0\), \(d\), and \(b\) be as in A.17. In the standard relative extension \[ \bigl(\widehat B/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(H_0)\bigr) \rtimes\langle d\rangle \] there is a subgroup \(S_{\mathrm{loc}}\simeq S_3\), generated by the named \(r\) and a transposition with component \(bd\) at two and \(d\) at every odd prime. No finite subgroup of the standard full extension \(\widehat B\rtimes\langle d\rangle\) maps onto \(S_{\mathrm{loc}}\). The obstruction is visible already in \(Q\rtimes\langle d\rangle\), with \(|Q|=576\).
depends_on: A.17; Herfort-Ribes1985 Theorems A-prime/B-prime/1; exact modulo12 sign calculation
notes: Blocks a lift inside the standard extension only. It is not an obstruction inside an unknown twisted extension associated with an exotic involution.

statement: Real projectivity and a rank-two open free subgroup do not imply finite graph recognition There exists a finitely generated real-projective profinite group \(E_*\) with an open normal subgroup isomorphic to \(\widehat F_2\), quotient \(C_2\), and self-centralizing involutions, which is not the profinite fundamental group of a finite graph of finite groups. It has one conjugacy class of involutions, so it does not satisfy R1's three-section conclusion.
depends_on: Herfort-Ribes1985 Theorems A-prime/B-prime/1 and open Kurosh; Pal-Quick2025 Theorem2.1
notes: Explicit E*=C2 coproduct ((product odd Zp) semidirect Z2). It has one section class, so is not a counterexample to the three-section pants case.

statement: The three distinguished reflections normally generate, and a proper generated subgroup has infinite index Let \(\alpha\) and \(h\) be as in R1, and put \(E=F\rtimes_\alpha\langle t\rangle\), \(b=hyh^{-1}\). The three involutions \[ t_0=t,\qquad t_1=xt,\qquad t_2=b^{-1}t \] represent the three section classes and normally generate \(E\). If their closed generated subgroup \(J\) is proper, then \([E:J]\) is infinite. Normal generation alone does not supply the full generation required in A.11.
notes: Normal generation is strictly separated from the generation required by A.11; this does not prove existence of a generating reflection triangle.

statement: Torsion and cusp centralizers in the relative primary modular groups Let \(q:\widehat B=C_2\amalg C_3\to D\) be a finite quotient injective on the two factors, with torsion-free kernel \(U\), and write \[ \Gamma_p=\widehat B/O^p(U),\qquad V_p=U^{(p)}. \] For \(a=s\) or \(r\), of prime order \(\ell\), the following statements hold: \[ \begin{array}{ll} p\ne\ell:&C_{\Gamma_p}(a)\longrightarrow C_D(q(a)) \text{ is onto},\\[2pt] p=\ell:&C_{\Gamma_p}(a)=\langle a\rangle. \end{array} \] For \(U=U_{12}=\ker q_{12}\) in the projective modular quotient, put \(\Gamma=\widehat B/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U)\). Then \[ C_{\Gamma_p}(\tau)=\overline{\langle\tau\rangle}, \qquad C_\Gamma(\tau)=\overline{\langle\tau\rangle} \simeq\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \] In the second formula the closure is taken in \(\Gamma\); in the first it is taken in \(\Gamma_p\).
depends_on: Open Kurosh; Herfort-Ribes1985 Theorem B-prime; Schur-Zassenhaus; boundary homology
notes: The coprime and equal-prime cases permit precise gluing of the literal r and s frames; the cusp statement includes x and y through sixth powers.

statement: The parity character descends to the actual outer image at level twelve Let \[ F_{12}=F/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U_{12}),\qquad G_{12}=\operatorname{im}\!\left( \widehat{GT}_0\longrightarrow \operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(F_{12})\right). \] The map is well-defined by the finite covariance in refereed LM7\_PUSH E.65, which preserves \(U_{12}\). There is a unique continuous character \(\Delta_{12}:G_{12}\to\mathbb F_2\) such that \(\Delta=\Delta_{12}\circ\pi_{12}\).
notes: The proof identifies outer-trivial normalized multiplier-one actions with identity actions, so no accessory framed target is substituted for the required outer image.

statement: An actual parity-one involution exists at the relative level twelve The group \(G_{12}\) of A.24 contains an involution \(a_{12}\) with \[ \lambda(a_{12})=-1, \qquad\Delta_{12}(a_{12})=1. \] It is not conjugate to the image of \(c\) in \(G_{12}\). Thus the first, specified-relative-level assertion of Lead~3 holds at \(U_{12}\). The existence of an involution lifting it in the full group is not asserted.
depends_on: R2; R3 CM comparison; A.23; A.24
notes: Constructed by a cubed Galois c-cocycle at p=2 and identity at all other primes, with literal frames glued over Q12. A full lift remains a nonabelian norm equation in ker(GT0 to G12).

statement: Finite frame visibility prevents arithmetic-only continuation Put \[ U=U_{12},\qquad V=\overline{U'U^6},\qquad D_6=\widehat B/V. \] This is a finite quotient of order \(576\cdot6^{97}\), and \(V\) is characteristic in \(U\), normal in \(\widehat B\), and preserved by \(\widehat{GT}_0\). The two normalized CM bits of an element of \(\mathcal H\) are determined by its actual action on \(D_6\). In particular both bits are zero for an element acting identically on \(D_6\). Let \(H_6\) be the actual image of \(\mathcal H\) in \(\operatorname{Aut}(D_6)\), and \(J_6=\langle H_6,c_6\rangle\). There is a character \(\Delta_6:J_6\to\mathbb F_2\) induced by \(\Delta\) on \(\mathcal H\rtimes\langle c\rangle\). The involution of A.25 induces an actual involution \(a_6\in J_6\) with \(\Delta_6(a_6)=1\). No Galois element of multiplier \(-1\) has the same actual action on \(D_6\).
notes: D6 has order 576*6^97. This excludes arithmetic-only componentwise continuation below its kernel; it does not exclude nongalois lifts or solve the full norm equation.

statement: The exact finite real-reflection count and its properness condition Let \(\pi:E\twoheadrightarrow D\) be an epimorphism of finite groups. Fix involutions \(d_0,d_1,d_2\in D\) which generate \(D\), and subsets \(T_{ij}\subseteq\pi^{-1}(d_id_j)\), for \((i,j)=(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)\). For every subgroup \(J\leq E\), put \[ I_i(J)=\{u\in J:\pi(u)=d_i,\ u^2=1\}, \qquad M_{ij}(J)_{u,v}=\mathbf1_{T_{ij}}(uv). \] Thus \(M_{ij}(J)\) is a rectangular matrix with rows indexed by \(I_i(J)\) and columns indexed by \(I_j(J)\). The number of triples of involutions in \(E\) with the specified images and pair products, and which generate \(E\), is \[ \sum_{J\leq E}\mu(J,E) \operatorname{tr}\bigl(M_{01}(J)M_{12}(J)M_{20}(J)\bigr), \tag{A.27.1} \] where \(\mu\) is the ordinary subgroup-lattice M\"obius function. Empty index sets contribute zero. This count concerns actual homomorphisms from \(C_2*C_2*C_2\), with actual quotient data.
depends_on: Elementary matrix expansion and subgroup-lattice inversion
notes: A perfect-kernel S5/A5 control has 1000 weak reflection triples and no proper one. This general control is excluded by the actual pants conditions, as separately checked.

statement: A negative finite peripheral action is stopped by a central spin obstruction There is an epimorphism \(q:F\twoheadrightarrow A_6\) and an involutory automorphism \(\vartheta\) of \(A_6\) which sends each of the three labelled cusp images to an \(A_6\)-conjugate of its inverse, but no multiplier-minus-one peripheral automorphism of \(F\) satisfies \[ q\Phi=\vartheta q. \] In particular no full negative peripheral involution induces this finite action. The obstruction is already visible in a central double cover; it is not a counterexample to R2 or A.3.
depends_on: R1 for the separate section-incidence explanation; exact ATLAS-generator double-cover enumeration for the stronger central obstruction
notes: The x,y,z passport is (4,4,4). All three cusp lifts require the nontrivial central character value, contradicting xyz=1. No R2 lift or characteristic-level automorphism is assumed.

statement: The new relative involution has exactly three section classes For the involution \(a_{12}\) constructed in A.25, choose its actual representative \(\phi c\) on \(F_{12}=F/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U_{12})\). Then \[ \bigl|H^1(C_2,F_{12})\bigr|=3, \] where the action is this specified representative. Its relative dyadic component likewise has exactly three section classes and has trivial fixed subgroup in its orientation kernel. These are section classes of the group extension, not conjugacy classes of peripheral automorphisms.
depends_on: A.25; open Kurosh; Herfort-Ribes1985; odd-primary Schur-Zassenhaus
notes: This computes H1(C2,F12) for the specified action, not H1(C2,H) or conjugacy of peripheral automorphisms. The new relative example already passes the three-section test.

statement: The level-twelve frames can also satisfy the involution relations The construction in A.25 can be made with its literal relative frames \(A,\beta\in\Gamma\) so that the associated r-normalizer and s-normalizer in \(\Gamma\rtimes\langle\phi c\rangle\) are actual subgroups \(S_3\) and \(C_2\times C_2\), with the finite frame values still \[ q(A)=1,\qquad q(\beta)=b. \] Consequently an R2 lift \(a=\widetilde\sigma c\) can be chosen with \[ a^2\in L_{12}^{\mathrm{fr}},\qquad L_{12}^{\mathrm{fr}} =\{k\in\mathcal H:\Phi_k|_\Gamma=1, \ A_k|_\Gamma=\beta_k|_\Gamma=1\}. \tag{A.30.1} \] This is a smaller kernel than the unframed \(L_{12}\). It does not assert a lift at a smaller characteristic level or solve the remaining norm equation.
notes: No smaller characteristic-level lift is claimed. The exact norm equation in the framed kernel is sufficient for the full lift; failure there alone would not exclude all unframed lifts.

statement: Parity-one involutions are compatible through the entire relative principal-congruence tower For every positive integer \(N\) divisible by twelve, put \[ \begin{gathered} Q_N=\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z/N)/\{\pm I\},\qquad U_N=\ker(\widehat B\longrightarrow Q_N),\\ \Gamma_N=\widehat B/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U_N),\qquad F_N=F/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U_N). \end{gathered} \] These kernels are preserved by the actual normalized \(\widehat{GT}_0\)-action. Let \(G_N\) be its actual outer image on \(F_N\). There is a single full element \(a\in\widehat{GT}_0\) such that \[ \lambda(a)=-1,\qquad \Delta(a)=1,\qquad a_N^2=1\quad\hbox{for every }12\mid N, \qquad a_N=\pi_N(a)\in G_N. \tag{A.31.1} \] The \(a_N\) are compatible and each has order exactly two. The character \(\Delta\) descends to every \(G_N\), and \(\Delta_N(a_N)=1\). In particular their inverse limit is an involution of parity one in the image of the full group on this entire tower. The assertion is restricted to this tower. The full element \(a\) is not proved to have order two, and the relative principal-congruence tower is not cofinal in the tower in A.2.
depends_on: A.23-A.25; R2; R3 global covariance and CM comparison; Marin2008 Section4 p776; inertia at three; compactness
notes: The full a is not proved an involution. This relative tower is not cofinal: its common kernel maps onto A7. No claim about faithfulness of the GT0 action follows from that group-kernel fact.

statement: Congruence CM refinements cannot supply the invariant fourth-root character obstruction Let \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{cong}}\) be the image of \(\mathcal H\) on the family of actual groups \(\Gamma_N\), for \(12\mid N\). The character \(\delta=\Delta|_{\mathcal H}\) descends to this image. There is no continuous homomorphism \[ \eta:\mathcal H_{\mathrm{cong}}\longrightarrow \mathbb Z/4 \] whose reduction modulo two is \(\delta\) and which is invariant under conjugation by \(c\). The same exclusion applies to a proposed character on \(\mathcal H\) depending only on its congruence CM-frame data, including any refinement at moduli 24 or 48, or continuously on their entire tower.
notes: Covers CM refinements modulo 24 and 48 and the entire congruence frame tower. A global character using additional noncongruence data remains open.

statement: The compatible congruence family also has equivariant literal frames The full element \(a=hc\) in A.31 can be chosen so that its square belongs to \[ L_{\mathrm{cong}}^{\mathrm{fr}}= \bigcap_{12\mid N}\{k\in\mathcal H: \Phi_k|_{\Gamma_N}=1,\quad A_k|_{\Gamma_N}=\beta_k|_{\Gamma_N}=1\}. \tag{A.33.1} \] At every level, the literal r- and s-frames can therefore be retained with the actual finite normalizers \(S_3\) and \(C_2^2\) from A.30. This strengthens the compatible actual-action assertion without asserting a full order-two lift.
depends_on: A.16; A.23; A.30; A.31; elementary integral matrix conjugacy; R2; compactness
notes: The remaining norm equation is in L_cong-fr. No full order-two lift or arbitrary characteristic refinement is proved.

statement: The full peripheral lifting theorem holds over any closed normal relative kernel Let \(\Pi\) be either the full free three-cusp group \(F\), or the full modular group \(\widehat B\), with the respective three peripheral elements \((x,y,z)\) or \((s,r,\tau^{-1})\). Let \(V\triangleleft\Pi\) be any closed normal subgroup, without an openness or characteristicity assumption, and put \(R=R_{\mathrm{nil}}(V)\). Every continuous automorphism of \(\Pi/R\) preserving the three positive peripheral conjugacy classes, with specified literal conjugators there, lifts to a full peripheral automorphism of \(\Pi\) with those conjugators. The lift stabilizes \(R\). If a specified peripheral conjugator is one, that peripheral can be fixed literally. For a descending directed family of closed subgroups \((V_i)\) of any profinite group, one also has \[ R_{\mathrm{nil}}\Bigl(\bigcap_i V_i\Bigr) =\bigcap_i R_{\mathrm{nil}}(V_i). \tag{A.34.1} \] In particular, if \(K_{\mathrm{cong}}=\bigcap_NU_N\), the group kernel \(T\) in A.31 is exactly \(R_{\mathrm{nil}}(K_{\mathrm{cong}})\).
depends_on: R2 finite central-refinement count; A.3; compact finite-image stabilization
notes: No openness or characteristicity is required. R=[R,V]=[R,Pi]. The lift stabilizes R because it induces the specified quotient automorphism. It does not impose square one or create missing quotient data.

statement: The full framed congruence correction kernel contains a closed dyadic procyclic subgroup Let \(L_{\mathrm{cong}}^{\mathrm{fr}}\leq\mathcal H\) be the kernel in A.33, retaining the actual action and both literal full relative frames at every principal congruence level. Then \[ \mathbb Z_2\ \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow L_{\mathrm{cong}}^{\mathrm{fr}} \tag{A.35.1} \] is a continuous closed embedding. The image may also be required to lie in all three corrected resolvent kernels of B.53. In particular the remaining norm kernel of A.33 is not pro-odd. This statement alone neither obstructs nor solves its twisted norm equation.
notes: The perfect-socle construction is repeated retaining the entire relative congruence quotient. This excludes a pro-odd kernel argument but gives neither the action of the negative lift on Z2 nor a nonzero norm obstruction.

statement: A peripheral conjugator to a Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller involution satisfies the pentagon Let \(\alpha\in\widehat{GT}\) be an involution and let \(g\in\mathcal P\) satisfy \(\alpha=g c g^{-1}\). Then \(g\in\widehat{GT}\). Consequently \[ \widehat{GT}\cap\{g c g^{-1}:g\in\mathcal P\} =\{g c g^{-1}:g\in\widehat{GT}\}. \tag{A.36.1} \] For an involution already in \(\widehat{GT}\), conjugacy to \(c\) in any of \(\mathcal P,\widehat{GT}_0, \widehat{GT}\) is therefore equivalent. This statement does not assert that every involution is so conjugate.
notes: Exact ambient conjugacy descent for involutions already in GT; no existence assertion and no presumed GT0 action in arity four.

statement: Every full Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller involution gives a unique pentagon solution Let \(\alpha=(-1,f)\in\widehat{GT}\) be an involution. Let \(k\in F'\) be the unique solution supplied by R1 of \(f=k^{-1}\alpha(k)\), and put \(u=k^{-1}\). Then \(u\) satisfies the full profinite pentagon. Moreover \(\alpha\) is conjugate to \(c\) in \(\widehat{GT}\) if and only if there exists \(\mu\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}\) such that \[ x^\mu u^{-1}y^\mu u\sim_F(xy)^\mu. \tag{A.37.1} \]
depends_on: R1; A.36 fixed-arrow proof; C.28; C.29
notes: Unique R1 coboundary satisfies pentagon; full conjugacy is equivalent to one unit third-cusp equation. Automatic generation is an independently audited LM4 D.35 assertion.

statement: The prescribed coboundary gives peripheral conjugators at two and three Let \(\alpha\in\widehat{GT}\) be an involution, and let \(u\in F'\) be its canonical parameter from A.37. Use the lower central series \(\gamma_2(F)=[F,F]\), \(\gamma_3(F)=[\gamma_2(F),F]\) and define \(t\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}\) by \[ u\equiv[x,y]^t\pmod{\gamma_3(F)}, \qquad D=1+24t. \tag{A.38.1} \] The commutator convention is the one whose logarithm has leading term \([X,Y]\), as in A.4. For a prime \(p\), there exists a peripheral conjugator from \(c_p\) to \(\alpha_p\) of the specific normalized form \[ g_p(x)=x^{\mu_p},\qquad g_p(y)=u_p^{-1}y^{\mu_p}u_p, \qquad \mu_p\in\mathbb Z_p^{\times}, \tag{A.38.2} \] if and only if \(D_p\) is a square unit in \(\mathbb Z_p\). This condition always holds at \(p=2\) and \(p=3\). For \(p\geq5\), it is equivalent to \(D_p\bmod p\) being a nonzero quadratic residue. In particular every involution already in full \(\widehat{GT}\) is peripherally conjugate to the standard involution on its maximal pro-\(2\) quotient.
depends_on: A.37; A.4; Furusho2010 Corollary12; pro-p Frattini criterion
notes: Actual maximal pro-2 and pro-3 statements. No arbitrary relative-level conclusion or corresponding claim for all P/GT0 involutions.

statement: The audited full conjugacy question is one unit third-cusp equation Let \(\alpha=(-1,f)\in\mathcal P\) be a nonidentity involution. Let \(u\in F'\) be the unique solution of \(u=f\alpha(u)\), supplied by R1 after inverting its coboundary parameter. Define \[ \mathcal M_\alpha= \{\mu\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}: x^\mu u^{-1}y^\mu u\sim_F(xy)^\mu\}. \tag{A.39.1} \] Then \(\alpha\) is conjugate to \(c\) in \(\mathcal P\) if and only if \(\mathcal M_\alpha\ne\varnothing\). This set is either empty or exactly \(\{\mu,-\mu\}\) for one unit \(\mu\). If \(\alpha\) belongs to \(\widehat{GT}_0\), respectively \(\widehat{GT}\), both resulting conjugators belong to that same group. The existence of a unit satisfying (A.39.1) is detected by all characteristic finite quotients of \(F\). For a specified unit \(\mu\), the validity of (A.39.1) is not detected by the maximal pro-\(p\) quotients alone, even with \(u=1\). The basic one-equation criterion and automatic generation were asserted in the supplied LM4 D.35; D.49 asserted the two-element conjugator fibres. This statement audits those conclusions using C.29's independent covering proof, R1's now-unique parameter, and A.6. A.36 supplies the additional descent to full \(\widehat{GT}\).
depends_on: R1; A.6; A.36; C.29; supplied LM4 D.35 and D.49 audited
notes: General criterion and generation already in LM4 D.35; full GT descent is additional. Exact S4 witness shows all maximal pro-p tests can miss the full third cusp for a mixed-sign multiplier.

statement: A parity-one involution survives an actual noncongruence perfect-socle refinement Put \[ \Pi=\widehat B,\qquad R=R_{\mathrm{nil}}(K_{\mathrm{cong}}),\qquad C=\Pi/R, \qquad \widehat K=\ker(\Pi\longrightarrow A_5). \] There is a finite quotient \[ q:\Pi\twoheadrightarrow Q=M\rtimes A_5, \qquad M=A_9^t\quad(t\geq60), \tag{A.40.1} \] whose kernel is invariant under the full \(\widehat{GT}_0\)-action, and for which the \(A_5\)-action on the simple factors is a union of regular orbits. Let \[ W=R\cap\ker q, \qquad D=\Pi/W, \qquad F_D=F/W. \] There is a full \(a\in\widehat{GT}_0\) with \(\lambda(a)=-1\) and \(\Delta(a)=1\) whose actual induced automorphism on \(D\) has order two. Its outer image on \(F_D\) has order two and projects to the entire compatible family of A.31. The literal \(C\)-frames from A.33 may also be retained. This quotient genuinely extends the relative principal-congruence tower: \(D\) maps onto \(C\) and has an \(A_9\) composition factor, which no finite quotient of \(C\) has. The statement does not assert \(a^2=1\) in the full group, nor that \(W\) is characteristic under all automorphisms of the underlying free group.

notes: Full GT0-invariant family of A9 tripod kernels; actual central refinement splits over retained congruence quotient; quotient image order two, not a full involution.

statement: The parity-one involution is compatible through a whole semisimple tripod tower Keep \(R,C,\widehat K\) from A.40. Let \(\mathscr S\) range over finite nonabelian simple groups not isomorphic to \(\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb F_p)\) for any prime \(p\). For each such group take all kernels of epimorphisms from the antipodal-pair tripod fillings of \(\widehat K\) onto that group. For every finite collection of targets let \(q_J:\Pi\twoheadrightarrow Q_J\) be the joint induced quotient over \(A_5\), and put \[ W_J=R\cap\ker q_J, \qquad W_* =\bigcap_J W_J, \qquad D_* =\Pi/W_*. \tag{A.41.1} \] There is one full \(a\in\widehat{GT}_0\) with \(\lambda(a)=-1\) and \(\Delta(a)=1\) whose actual action on \(D_*\) has order two. It retains A.33's literal \(C\)-frames and induces standard conjugation on every \(Q_J\). This is an assertion about the specified joint tower; no cofinality or full order-two lift is asserted.
notes: One full negative element acts involutively on the joint relative-congruence and all specified noncongruence-simple-tripod tower; no cofinality or arbitrary nonsimple chief-layer lifting claim.

statement: Every full Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller involution has its prescribed conjugator at every prime Let \(\alpha=(-1,f)\in\widehat{GT}\) be a nonidentity involution, and let \(u\in F'\) be the unique full solution of \(u=f\alpha(u)\) from A.37. Then \[ D=1+24c_2(u)\in (\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times})^2. \tag{A.42.1} \] In particular there is a full unit \(\mu\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}\) with \(\mu^2=D\). For every prime \(p\), and either local root \(\mu_p\), the prescribed pair \((\mu_p,u_p)\) belongs to the pro-\(p\) Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group and its normalized peripheral automorphism conjugates \(c_p\) to \(\alpha_p\). Any choice of a full square root in (A.42.1) therefore gives a compatible conjugator on the maximal pronilpotent quotient \(\prod_p F_2^{(p)}\). No corresponding full profinite conjugator or arbitrary relative-level conjugator is asserted. In particular the statement does not settle the dyadic case for an arbitrary \(\mathcal P\)- or \(\widehat{GT}_0\)-involution.
notes: The remaining full condition is the existential third-cusp/hexagon equation; no arbitrary relative-level or arbitrary P/GT0 dyadic claim.

statement: The actual first scalar central refinement also carries the compatible parity-one involution For any finite family in A.40 or A.41, put \[ W_1=[W,\Pi],\qquad W_2=[W_1,\Pi]. \] Then \[ W_2=W_1. \tag{A.43.1} \] There is a full negative element of parity one whose actual action on \(\Pi/W_1\) has order two and retains the prescribed \(C\)-frames. These refined involutions may be chosen as the images of one full element for all finite families simultaneously. Thus A.41 extends to the actual quotient \[ \Pi\Big/\bigcap_J[W_J,\Pi]. \tag{A.43.2} \] The square is still not shown to vanish in the full group.

statement: The canonical substitution passes all dihedral tests and the parity-relative pro-prime generation test Let \(\alpha=(-1,f)\in\mathcal P\) be a nonidentity involution and let \(u\in F'\) be its canonical parameter, \(u=f\alpha(u)\). Put \[ y'=u^{-1}yu,\qquad \psi(x)=x,\quad\psi(y)=y', \qquad V=\ker\bigl(F\to C_2,\ x,y\mapsto-1\bigr). \] The substitution \(\psi\) is onto every finite dihedral quotient in which \(x,y\) are generating reflections. For every prime \(p\), it induces an automorphism of \[ G_p=F/O^p(V), \tag{A.44.1} \] and that automorphism conjugates the induced standard action to the induced \(\alpha\)-action. This is a generation and unmarked automorphism statement. It does not assert preservation of the third cusp by \(\psi\).
notes: Applies to every full P involution. Degree-p sphere-cover incidence excludes collapse; the conclusion is generation and unmarked relative conjugacy, not third-cusp preservation.

statement: The canonical word determines the only possible full multiplier For \(\alpha,u\) as in A.44, use the universal full dihedral quotient \[ q:F\twoheadrightarrow D_\infty^{\wedge} =\widehat{\mathbb Z}\rtimes C_2,\qquad q(x)=a,\quad q(y)=at,\quad ata=t^{-1}. \] Write \(q(u)=t^k\) and define \[ d_\alpha=2k+1. \tag{A.45.1} \] Then \(k\in2\widehat{\mathbb Z}\), \(d_\alpha\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}\), and \((d_\alpha)_2\equiv1\pmod4\). The involution acts identically on \(D_\infty^{\wedge}\). Its full conjugacy criterion is the single equation \[ x^{d_\alpha}u^{-1}y^{d_\alpha}u \sim_F(xy)^{d_\alpha}. \tag{A.45.2} \] If a full peripheral conjugator exists, its multiplier is exactly \(d_\alpha\) or \(-d_\alpha\). The same equivalence holds in \(\widehat{GT}_0\) or \(\widehat{GT}\) when \(\alpha\) belongs to the respective group. For \(\alpha\in\widehat{GT}\), full conjugacy would in particular imply \[ d_\alpha^2=1+24c_2(u). \tag{A.45.3} \] Its dyadic component already holds by A.42. The other components of (A.45.3), and the full equation (A.45.2), are not proved here.
notes: d=2k+1 is a full unit; full conjugacy iff its single third-cusp equation holds. The dyadic square coefficient matches; the other components and full equation remain open.

statement: Generation over the full elementary abelian two quotient Let \(\alpha,u,\psi\) be as in A.44, and put \[ V_4=\ker\bigl(F\longrightarrow C_2^2\bigr) =\overline{F'F^2}. \] For every prime \(p\), the canonical substitution \(\psi(x)=x\), \(\psi(y)=u^{-1}yu\) induces a continuous automorphism of \[ F/O^p(V_4). \tag{A.46.1} \] It intertwines the induced involution with the standard negative involution. This asserts generation and unmarked relative conjugacy; it does not assert that this automorphism preserves the third cusp.

statement: A genuine noncentral two layer in the compatible parity-one tower Let \(V\) be the augmentation submodule of the natural permutation module \(\mathbb F_2^9\) for \(A_9\), and put \(S=V\rtimes A_9\). Enlarge the tower of A.41 by all tripod quotients of \(\widehat K\) onto \(S\) whose three retained cusps form an antipodal pair and one other vertex and have images of order seven. This family is nonempty. Its actual joint quotient with \(C=\Pi/R\), and its actual scalar central refinement, carry compatible negative involutory images with \(\Delta=1\). One full negative element realizes these images simultaneously with the whole tower of A.41. The same assertion holds for all such regular-head tripod families with targets \(W\rtimes T\), where \(T\) is a finite nonabelian simple group excluded from A.31's congruence composition factors and \(W\) is a nontrivial finite irreducible \(T\)-module. No nonemptiness assertion is made for every possible module. The explicit group \(2^8\rtimes A_9\) proves that the enlarged tower contains a noncentral chief layer of characteristic two. No full involution or cofinality assertion follows.

statement: Nonregular orbit-one simple quotients also admit compatible images The parity-one tower of A.47 can be enlarged by all finite invariant families of simple quotients of \(\Pi=C_2\amalg C_3\) excluded from the congruence composition factors of A.31, together with their actual scalar central refinements. These quotients have \(A_5\)-orbit length one on their simple \(\widehat K\)-head kernels; regular permutation of head factors is not required for this assertion. One explicit nonempty family consists of all epimorphism kernels \(\Pi\to A_9\) for which \(\tau\) has order fifteen. One full negative element still realizes the compatible involutory images with \(\Delta=1\). This statement does not provide a full involution or control a nonperfect noncentral kernel over a mixed solvable head.

statement: A nonperfect mixed-head layer has an exact Clifford refinement Let \(H=\operatorname{AGL}_1(\mathbb F_7)\), let \(V\subset\mathbb F_2^7\) be its augmentation module, and put \(G=V\rtimes H\). The complete family of \(\Pi\to G\) epimorphism kernels consists of two kernels, exchanged by \(c\). Write their joint quotient as \[ \overline G=\overline V\rtimes\overline H, \qquad \overline V=V_+\oplus V_-, \qquad \overline H=C_7^2\rtimes C_6. \] For \(R,C\) as in A.31--A.34 and \(W=R\cap\ker(\Pi\to\overline G)\), one has \[ q(R)=\overline V, \qquad \Pi/[W,\Pi] \simeq\bigl((P_+\times P_-)\rtimes\overline H\bigr) \times_{\overline H}C, \tag{A.49.1} \] where \(P_\pm\simeq2_+^{1+6}\) are the specified Clifford central covers of \(V_\pm\). Moreover \[ [[W,\Pi],\Pi]=[W,\Pi]. \tag{A.49.2} \] A full negative element with \(\Delta=1\) realizes an involutory image on this actual refinement, compatibly with the entire earlier tower of A.48. The residual image \(\overline V\) is noncentral and nonperfect. This is a particular mixed solvable-head calculation, not a general norm vanishing or a full order-two construction.

statement: A nonzero torsion-frame class has an explicit correction and norm cancellation The tower of A.49 admits a further compatible parity-one involutory image on an actual central refinement whose residual module has nonzero \(H^1(C_2,-)\). Its retained odd head is \(H=\operatorname{Heis}_7\rtimes C_6\), and its residual module is the pair of 21-dimensional \(\mathbb F_2\)-Schr\"odinger modules with opposite central characters. The actual central kernel is the additive group \(\mathbb F_8\). A compensating \(C_{12}\)-extension of the head is essential for the order-two torsion lift. The scalar central refinement stabilizes, so the specified involution is the image of a full negative element with \(\Delta=1\), compatibly with all preceding towers. The retained s-frame determines a nontrivial possible linear correction. It is explicitly conjugation by an odd central-head lift, and its norm under \(c\) is one. No general norm vanishing, cofinality, or full involution is asserted.

statement: An actual nonzero second scalar layer over a filiform odd head Let \(R\), \(C=\Pi/R\) be the initial congruence pronilpotent base of A.31--A.34. There is a finite quotient \(G\) of \(\Pi\), with a nonperfect elementary-abelian residual image, such that, on putting \[ W=R\cap\ker(\Pi\to G),\qquad W_{i+1}=\overline{[W_i,\Pi]},\qquad W_0=W, \] one has \[ W_2\subsetneq W_1,\qquad W_1/W_2\simeq C_2, \qquad W_3=W_2. \tag{A.51.1} \] Both scalar refinements are identified by explicit finite central covers. Thus immediate scalar stabilization is not a general consequence of \(R=\overline{[R,\Pi]}\), or of the odd sensitivity of the new irreducible chief modules. This assertion does not supply a negative norm obstruction. The single chosen head is not assumed to be \(c\)-stable.

The first-to-second scalar kernel is \(C_2^2\), and the third scalar step stabilizes. The full element is not proved to be an involution, and the family is not proved cofinal.

statement: Every finite abelian residual layer has bounded actual scalar depth Let \(K_0\) be any closed normal subgroup of \(\Pi=C_2\amalg C_3\), and put \[ R=R_{\rm nil}(K_0),\qquad C=\Pi/R. \] Let \(W\) be closed normal in \(\Pi\), contained in \(R\), with \(V=R/W\) finite abelian. Define \[ W_0=W,\qquad W_{i+1}=\overline{[W_i,\Pi]}. \] Write \(\exp(V_2)=2^{e_2}\) and \(\exp(V_3)=3^{e_3}\), with exponent index zero when that primary summand is absent, and set \[ m=\max\{1,e_2+1,2e_3+1\}. \tag{A.53.1} \] Then the actual scalar refinements stabilize: \[ W_{m+1}=W_m. \tag{A.53.2} \] In particular, for an elementary-abelian \(\ell\)-group \(V\), the respective bounds are \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} \ell&2&3&\ell\geq5\\ \hline \text{stabilization}&W_3=W_2&W_4=W_3&W_2=W_1. \end{array} \tag{A.53.3} \] More generally, the same conclusions hold for any closed normal \(R\) satisfying \(R=\overline{[R,\Pi]}\), provided \[ H^1_{\rm cont}(C,V^\vee)=0, \qquad V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}(V,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z). \tag{A.53.4} \] For every \(i\geq1\), the R-preimage \(M_i=R/W_i\) has abelianization \(V\), has nilpotency class at most two, and has finite derived subgroup \[ Z_i=M_i'=W/W_i, \qquad Z_i\text{ a quotient of } \textstyle\bigwedge^2_{\mathbb Z}V. \tag{A.53.5} \] Its p-primary action factors through the maximal pro-p quotient of \(\Pi\): \(C_2\), \(C_3\), or the trivial group. These are assertions about the actual relative central refinements. They do not supply the peripheral automorphism or solve its negative norm equation.

statement: The exact new-base cohomology can obstruct a successive reuse of A.53 Use the initial relative-pronilpotent base and a stabilized layer from A.53, and put \[ P=R/W_m,\qquad C'=\Pi/W_m, \qquad P^{\rm ab}=V. \] Let \(T\) be a finite C-module such that, for each prime \(p\), its p-primary part has zero invariants under the actual normal subgroup \(N_{p'}\) of \(N=K_0/R\). Inflate \(T\) to \(C'\). Then restriction gives \[ H^j(C,T)=0\quad(j\geq0),\qquad H^1(C',T)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_C(V,T). \tag{A.54.1} \] In particular \[ H^1(C',V)\simeq\operatorname{End}_C(V), \tag{A.54.2} \] which is nonzero for \(V\ne0\). The failure of automatic vanishing can occur for an actual next residual layer. In the single-head construction of A.51, let \(U\) be its 42-dimensional simple module and let \(R'=W_2\). There exists a closed normal \(W'\subset R'\) with \[ R'/W'\simeq U^\vee, \qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_2}H^1(C',U)=1. \tag{A.54.3} \] Thus the cohomology hypothesis for the next application of A.53 is genuinely nonzero, although \(R'=\overline{[R',\Pi]}\). This is not a negative norm obstruction.

notes: The new s=0,r=zeta²e1 class is independent of the retained r=e1 class. This is an actual next residual layer with nonzero dual-coefficient H1. Simultaneous enlargement over the original base remains available; no norm obstruction.

statement: The actual second scalar center of an elementary two-layer is an explicit exterior-square coinvariant module Let \(K_0\) be closed normal in \(\Pi=C_2\amalg C_3\), put \(R=R_{\rm nil}(K_0)\), \(C=\Pi/R\), and let \(W\subset R\) be closed normal in \(\Pi\) with \(A=R/W\) finite elementary abelian of characteristic two. Let \(H\) be the finite image of C on A, and put \[ K=O^2(H),\qquad M=(\mathop{\bigwedge}\nolimits^2_{\mathbb F_2}A)_K, \qquad W_{i+1}=\overline{[W_i,\Pi]},\quad W_0=W. \tag{A.55.1} \] The natural commutator maps give \[ W/W_2\simeq M,\qquad W/W_1\simeq M_H. \tag{A.55.2} \] Thus an extension of C by an explicit finite class-two group attains the actual second scalar center. If H acts trivially on M, then \(W_1=W_2\). The same conclusion holds for general \(R=\overline{[R,\Pi]}\) if the actual quotient \(\Pi/W\) is identified with \(A\rtimes C\), if \(H^1(C,A^\vee)=0\), and if H has a normal odd subgroup J with \(A_J=0\). No peripheral automorphism or equivariant frame is asserted.

statement: The forced CM frame extends through an actual self-dual central layer with both involutory normalizers Retain the actual base C, positive action \(h_C\), negative involution \(b_C=h_Cc_C\), and literal equivariant frames of A.33. There is an actual further quotient over C whose finite residual group P is class two and satisfies \[ \begin{gathered} P^{\rm ab}=V^8,\qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_2}V=108, \qquad\operatorname{End}_C(V)=\mathbb F_8,\\ P'=\operatorname{Sym}^2_{\mathbb F_8}(\mathbb F_8^8), \qquad\dim_{\mathbb F_2}P'=108. \end{gathered}\tag{A.56.1} \] The module V is simple and self-dual. This quotient has a positive peripheral automorphism over \(h_C\), fixing the actual cusp and retaining the original literal C-frames, whose negative companion and prescribed s- and r-normalizers are involutory. Its scalar refinement is already stabilized. The complete action and frames are realized by a full positive lift, simultaneously retaining every previous finite family in A.47--A.52 and hence their tower. The full negative companion has parity one and order-two images in these quotients. For the original stored finite action and s-frame, A.76 proves that its full square is nontrivial. Later reselected action/frame tuples and the cofinality question remain unresolved. The retained r-frame is specifically the one constructed in A.33: its positive odd relative components are one, and its negative normalizer there is \(sc\). No assertion about an unrestricted different odd r-frame is made.

statement: An actual four-dimensional family of nonsplit next layers is detected by an integral Bockstein Let \(C_{\rm new}\) be the actual quotient of A.56, with finite residual group P over C, and let V be its simple module over \(k=\mathbb F_8\). There is a four-dimensional k-subspace of \[ \ker\!\left(H^2(C_{\rm new},V)\longrightarrow H^2(\Pi,V)\right) \tag{A.57.1} \] whose nonzero elements define nonsplit extensions attained by actual quotients of \(\Pi\). Moreover, a k-basis of this subspace is attained simultaneously by an actual quotient with kernel \(V^4\) over \(C_{\rm new}\). This is a family of actual next chief-module directions; it is not asserted to exhaust the next extensions, to be scalar-stable, or to admit a negative involution.

statement: The complete finite abelian residual layer has an exact exterior-square scalar center Let \(K_0\) be closed normal in \(\Pi=C_2\amalg C_3\), set \(R=R_{\rm nil}(K_0)\), \(C=\Pi/R\), and suppose \(A=R/W\) is finite abelian for a closed normal subgroup \(W\subset R\) of \(\Pi\). Let H be the finite C-action image on A. For each prime p put \[ K_p=O^p(H),\qquad M_p=\left(\mathop{\bigwedge}\nolimits^2_{\mathbb Z} A_p\right)_{K_p}, \qquad M=\prod_p M_p. \tag{A.58.1} \] Write \(W_0=W\), \(W_{i+1}=\overline{[W_i,\Pi]}\), let \(p^{e_p}\) be the exponent of \(A_p\), taking \(e_p=0\) if \(A_p=0\), and put \[ m=\max\{1,e_2+1,2e_3+1\}. \tag{A.58.2} \] The natural commutator map is an isomorphism \[ W/W_m\simeq M, \qquad (W_j/W_m)_p=I_p^jM_p\quad(0\leq j\leq m), \qquad W_{m+1}=W_m. \tag{A.58.3} \] Here \(I_p\) is the augmentation ideal of the cyclic action \(H/K_p\), which is a quotient of \(C_2\) for p two, of \(C_3\) for p three, and is trivial otherwise. In particular, if H acts trivially on M, already \(W_1=W_2\) and \(W/W_1=M\). The same conclusion holds for a general \(R=\overline{[R,\Pi]}\) under the following actual hypotheses: \(\Pi/W=A\rtimes C\), \(H^1(C,A^\vee)=0\), and, for each p, H has a normal subgroup \(J_p\) of order prime to p with \((A_p)_{J_p}=0\). The theorem identifies an actual quotient; it does not provide a peripheral automorphism or a negative norm solution on that quotient.

statement: The Bockstein quotient has an exact eighteen-dimensional first scalar refinement For the simultaneous actual quotient \(C_{\rm Bock}\) of A.57, let \(W_{\rm Bock}=\ker(\Pi\to C_{\rm Bock})\). Its first scalar refinement has kernel \(k^6\), where \(k=\mathbb F_8\), and the following refinement is stable: \[ W_{\rm Bock}/\overline{[W_{\rm Bock},\Pi]}\simeq k^6, \qquad \overline{[[W_{\rm Bock},\Pi],\Pi]} =\overline{[W_{\rm Bock},\Pi]}. \tag{A.59.1} \] This identifies an actual additional central kernel of dimension eighteen over \(\mathbb F_2\). No lifted negative norm or literal normalizer assertion is included.

statement: The actual Bockstein quotient retains an involutory negative action Let h be a full positive peripheral lift realizing the A.56 quotient action and fixing \(\tau=sr\) literally. Put \(b=hc\). Then the actual simultaneous Bockstein quotient \(C_{\rm Bock}\) of A.57 is stable under h and c, and the induced b-action on it has square one. Its action also has square one on the actual scalar-stable quotient of A.59. This assertion concerns the actual quotient kernel of A.57, independently of the chosen integral cocycle representatives. It does not assert the literal normalizer frames on that additional center or a full involution.

statement: The Bockstein scalar refinement admits simultaneous involutory frames after refining the new central frame choices The parity-one quotient action of A.56 extends to the actual scalar-stable quotient above \(C_{\rm Bock}\) in A.59, with simultaneously involutory s- and r-normalizers. It retains the literal C-frames of A.33 and the earlier A.47--A.52 finite families. A full positive peripheral lift realizes this quotient action and these frames. Its full negative square is not asserted. The new central frame choices introduced in A.56 may change. In particular this assertion does not preserve the particular stored \path{Q6_actual_central_solution.json} frame tuple, nor a separately fixed newer cross-section transporter. The quotient action itself is retained.

statement: A compatible unbounded integral cusp tower admits parity-one involutory images and simultaneous frames The construction of A.61 extends to every \(\mathcal O_n=\operatorname{GR}(2^n,3)\), simultaneously. There are actual nested scalar-stable kernels \(U_{n+1}\subset U_n\) in \(\Pi\), with quotient \(D_n=\Pi/U_n\) over C, whose residual abelianization and center have types \[ A_n=L_n^4\oplus V^4,\qquad L_n=\mathcal O_n^{36}, \qquad M_n\simeq C_{2^n}^{18}\oplus C_2^{90}. \tag{A.62.1} \] A full positive lift has parity-one negative image of order two on every \(D_n\), with compatible involutory s/r-normalizers, while retaining all the earlier C and A.47--A.52 data. The newer A.56 central frames may vary; surjectivity onto arbitrary earlier choices is not asserted. The kernel \(U_\infty=\bigcap_nU_n\) is itself relatively perfect. Thus the compatible data also form an actual closed-normal quotient to which A.3 applies. The tower is not claimed cofinal, and no full order-two element follows.

statement: Six independent cross-cup directions give an actual nonsplit next quotient beyond the integral tower Let \(D_\infty\) be the actual quotient of A.62, and let \(V^{(2)}\) denote the monomial H-module obtained from V by squaring every scalar and retaining each permutation. There is an actual source quotient \[ 1\longrightarrow T\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow D_\infty \longrightarrow1,\qquad T=(V^{(2)})^6, \tag{A.63.1} \] with six k-linearly independent nonsplit coordinate extension classes. They are the cross cup products of the four cusp classes. The joint source kernel is preserved by the full positive lift h supplied at the end of A.62 and by c. The same extension already descends from the A.56 quotient \(D_1\) over the initial profinite C. These quotients need not be finite; their explicit finite group models pull back over C. statement: An odd relation-module lift and a finite negative action with no full involutory realization, without prescribing a cusp normalization Let \(\Pi=C_2\amalg C_3=\langle s,r\rangle\), \(\tau=sr\), and let \(q:\Pi\twoheadrightarrow Q\) be a finite quotient injecting the two factors. statement: The actual reflection augmentation module is projective at every prime and free at the dyadic prime Let \(E=F\rtimes C_2\), where \(F=\widehat F_2\), be one of the actual pants extensions already considered: the pure negative extension of C.28, or the regular extension of C.43. Here \(n=3\) in the first case and \(n=1\) in the second. For every prime p put \[ \Lambda_G=\mathbb Z_p[[G]],\qquad P_p=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathbb Z_p[[E/C_i]],\qquad R_p=\ker(P_p\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_p), \tag{A.82.1} \] where the last map sums the augmentations. These are actual compact modules over the full group E. For every finite discrete E-module A, the restriction maps satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} H^1(E,A)&\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{i=1}^n H^1(C_i,A) &&\text{is onto},\\ H^2(E,A)&\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{i=1}^n H^2(C_i,A) &&\text{is injective}. \end{aligned} \tag{A.82.2} \] Consequently \(R_p\) is finitely generated projective for every p, and \[ R_p\oplus(R_p\otimes\varepsilon)\simeq\Lambda_E^{\,n+1}, \qquad R_2\simeq\mathbb Z_2[[E]]^{(n+1)/2}. \tag{A.82.3} \] In particular the two dyadic ranks are two and one, respectively. This does not produce a finite graph of groups or a generating marked reflection system.

statement: Actual odd finite-head twisted duality fixes all self-dual multiplicities Let E be the pure negative pants extension in A.82, and let K be an open normal subgroup of E contained in F. Under this same prime-to-order hypothesis, A.82 and the isomorphism force every self-dual simple S to occur in \(\overline R\) with multiplicity \[ 2\dim_{\operatorname{End}_Q(S)}S. \tag{A.83.3} \] In particular, if every simple \(k[Q]\)-module is self-dual and \(p\nmid|Q|\), then \(\overline R\simeq k[Q]^2\). statement: The actual compact augmentation module has orientation-twisted projective duality Let E be the pure negative pants extension of A.82. For every prime p put \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z_p[[E]]\) and let \(\iota:\Lambda\longrightarrow\Lambda\) be the continuous anti-involution induced by \(g\mapsto g^{-1}\). For a finitely generated projective compact left \(\Lambda\)-module P define its projective dual by \[ P^\#=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda,\mathrm{cont}}(P,\Lambda), \qquad (a\cdot f)(v)=f(v)\iota(a). \tag{A.84.1} \] This is a compact left module; it is not the linear or Pontryagin dual of the underlying infinite compact abelian group. The actual module of A.82 satisfies \[ R_p^\#\simeq R_p\otimes\varepsilon. \tag{A.84.2} \] For every odd p and every finite head \(Q=E/K\), where \(K\trianglelefteq_o E\) and \(K\subseteq F\), the finite module \(\overline R=\mathbb F_p\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}(R_p)_K\) therefore satisfies the actual isomorphism \[ \overline R^*\simeq \overline R\otimes\varepsilon, \tag{A.84.3} \] including when \(p\mid |Q|\). More precisely, let S be a simple \(\mathbb F_p[Q]\)-module and \(P(S)\) its projective cover. If \(S\simeq S^*\), its projective cover occurs as a direct summand of \(\overline R\) exactly \[ 2\dim_{\operatorname{End}_Q(S)}S \tag{A.84.4} \] times. When every simple is self-dual, this gives \(\overline R\simeq\mathbb F_p[Q]^2\), without the prime-to-order restriction. In the modular case (A.84.4) concerns projective-cover summands, not composition-factor multiplicities. Neither (A.84.2) nor (A.84.4) removes the nonselfdual multiplicity ambiguity or proves the required incidence map surjective.

statement: The actual canonical Fox defect is induced under the joint Klein-four action Let \(\alpha=(-1,f)\in\widehat{GT}_0\) be a nonidentity involution, and let \(u\in F'\) be its unique canonical parameter, where \(F=\widehat F(x,y)\). Thus \[ \alpha(x)=x^{-1},\quad \alpha(y)=f^{-1}y^{-1}f, \qquad u=f\alpha(u),\qquad \iota(u)=u^{-1}, \tag{A.85.1} \] and \(\iota\) interchanges x and y. Put \[ \begin{gathered} w=u^{-1}yu,\qquad \psi(x)=x,\quad\psi(y)=w, \qquad H=\overline{\langle x,w\rangle},\\ v=\operatorname{Inn}(u^{-1})\iota,\qquad \tau=\alpha v,\qquad V=\langle\alpha,v\rangle. \end{gathered} \tag{A.85.2} \] Then V is the actual Klein-four group acting on F and H. For every prime p use the full coefficient ring \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z_p[[F]]\), and define \[ \begin{gathered} B=1+(y-1)u_y,\qquad L_H=\Lambda(x-1)+\Lambda(w-1),\\ C_p=I_F/L_H \simeq\ker\bigl(\mathbb Z_p[[F/H]]\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_p\bigr). \end{gathered} \tag{A.85.3} \] The derivatives are the continuous left Fox derivatives specified below. The actual coset space \(X=F/H\) satisfies \[ X^\alpha=X^v=X^\tau=\{H\}. \tag{A.85.4} \] There is a closed pointed transversal \((Y,H)\) for its nontrivial V-orbits, and a compact \(\mathbb Z_p\)-module \(D_p=\ker(\mathbb Z_p[[Y]]\to\mathbb Z_p)\), such that \[ C_p\simeq\mathbb Z_p[V]\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}D_p \quad\hbox{as compact \(\mathbb Z_p[V]\)-modules}. \tag{A.85.5} \] In particular its Tate cohomology vanishes for V and every subgroup of V. The complete coupled full-ring Fox identities are (A.85.8)--(A.85.11) below. For any one p, \[ B\in\Lambda^\times \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C_p=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H=F. \tag{A.85.6} \] Neither (A.85.5) nor the coupled identities prove these equivalent conditions. The induced description is over the constant finite-group ring; no \(\Lambda\)-linear splitting or induced description is asserted.

statement: A canonical full cusp word compares the dihedral and relative Alexander units Retain the actual negative-\(\widehat{GT}_0\) data of A.85, and put \(z=(xy)^{-1}\), \(G_v=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle\). Let \(d=d_\alpha\) be the actual full unit from A.45: in the universal dihedral quotient \[ \pi(x)=a,\qquad\pi(y)=aT,\qquad\pi(u)=T^k, \qquad d=2k+1,\qquad k\in2\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \tag{A.86.1} \] In particular \(d_2\equiv1\pmod4\). There is a unique \(h_0\in F'\) satisfying \[ \tau(z)=h_0^{-1}z^{-1}h_0, \] and a unique \(q\in F\) such that \[ h_0\tau=q\tau q^{-1},\qquad q_{\mathrm{ab}}=(t,-t) \quad\text{for some }t\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \tag{A.86.2} \] Define actual full-group elements \[ \begin{gathered} e=(xu)v,\qquad b=q^{-1}eq,\qquad \Omega_\alpha=(x^dv)b^{-d}\in F,\\ \sigma=\operatorname{Inn}(h_0)\tau,\qquad g=e(qvq^{-1})=xu\,v(q)q^{-1}\in F. \end{gathered} \tag{A.86.3} \] Then \[ \begin{gathered} e^2=xy,\qquad\tau(b)=b^{-1},\qquad \sigma(g)g^{-1}=z,\\ a_{\mathrm{reg}}:=1-4t\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times},\qquad (\Omega_\alpha)_{\mathrm{ab}} =\left(\frac{d-a_{\mathrm{reg}}}{2}, -\frac{d-a_{\mathrm{reg}}}{2}\right). \end{gathered} \tag{A.86.4} \] The element g is exactly C.44's unique solution for the normalized regular involution \(\sigma\); \(a_{\mathrm{reg}}\) is its image in \(F/\langle\!\langle z\rangle\!\rangle\), with generator the image of x. The full criterion is \[ \begin{aligned} \Omega_\alpha=1 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x^du^{-1}y^du\sim_F(xy)^d\\ &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \alpha\text{ is conjugate to }c\text{ in }\widehat{GT}_0. \end{aligned} \tag{A.86.5} \] If \(\alpha\in\widehat{GT}\), the last condition is also equivalent to conjugacy in \(\widehat{GT}\). These last group membership assertions use exactly A.39, with A.6 and A.36 for the respective descents, and A.45 for the fixed multiplier d. When (A.86.5) holds, the original cusp equation has the specified conjugator \[ x^du^{-1}y^du=q^{-1}(xy)^dq. \tag{A.86.6} \] It follows that the canonical Fox element of A.85 is a unit at every coefficient prime. No converse from that Fox-unit condition alone is asserted here. Neither \(a_{\mathrm{reg}}=d\) nor \(\Omega_\alpha=1\) is proved by this statement.

statement: The actual marked three-cycle and the explicit canonical cusp frame Retain the actual negative involution \(\alpha=(-1,f)\in\widehat{GT}_0\), its canonical \(u\in F'\), and the notation of A.85--A.86. Use the actual modular marking \[ \begin{gathered} B=C_2(s)\amalg C_3(r),\qquad \delta=sr,\qquad x=\delta^{-2},\quad y=sxs,\quad z=(xy)^{-1},\\ \rho=\operatorname{Ad}(r)|_F,\qquad \iota=\operatorname{Ad}(s)|_F,\qquad v=u^{-1}s,\qquad \tau=v\alpha. \end{gathered} \tag{A.87.1} \] Here \(\rho\) sends x,y,z cyclically to y,z,x. Automorphisms and their involutory symbols in the indicated actual semidirect products are distinguished by context. Let \(d=d_\alpha\) be A.45's full unit, put \(m=(d-1)/2\), and set \[ T_d=v\delta^d,\qquad \Xi_d=T_d^3. \tag{A.87.2} \] Then the full marked cusp obstruction of A.86 has the exact equivalent form \[ \Xi_d=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Omega_\alpha=1. \tag{A.87.3} \] Unconditionally \(\Xi_d\in F'\), \(\tau(\Xi_d)=\Xi_d^{-1}\), and there is a unique \(a_d\in F\) with \[ \Xi_d=a_d\tau(a_d)^{-1},\qquad (a_d)_{\rm ab}=(\ell_d,-\ell_d). \tag{A.87.4} \] No vanishing of \(\Xi_d\) or \(a_d\) is asserted. Let A be the unique pure r-frame of the \emph{actual} positive element \(\Sigma=\alpha c=(1,f)\): \[ \Phi_\Sigma(r)=ArA^{-1}=f^{-1}r,\qquad A\in F. \tag{A.87.5} \] Then \(A\in F'\), and the unique normalized cusp frame of A.86 is \[ \begin{gathered} f=\rho(A)A^{-1},\qquad \alpha(A)=\iota(A^{-1})f,\qquad \tau(A)=u^{-1}\rho(A)^{-1}u,\\ h_0=\rho^2(A)\rho(A)^{-1}u,\qquad h_0\tau=r^{-1}(\delta^{-1}\alpha)r. \end{gathered} \tag{A.87.6} \] Writing \(h_0=q\tau(q)^{-1}\) with A.86's unique q, and \(q_{\rm ab}=(t,-t)\), its unique Alexander solution can be transported to the original first-cusp marking. There is a unique \(G\in F\) with \[ \Phi_\alpha(G)=\delta^{-1}G\delta^{-1},\qquad G_{\rm ab}=(-2t,a_{\rm reg}),\qquad a_{\rm reg}=1-4t. \tag{A.87.7} \] Its image in \(F/\langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle\), with generator y, is \(y^{a_{\rm reg}}\). If \(k\) is the actual A.45 dihedral exponent, the remaining coefficient comparison is precisely \[ a_{\rm reg}=d_\alpha \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G_{{\rm ab},x}=k. \tag{A.87.8} \] Neither this equality nor the nonlinear equation (A.87.3) is proved here.

statement: A full-head Alexander coefficient test and the canonical congruence modulo eight Retain the actual negative-GT0 data and the two full units \(a=a_{\rm reg}\), \(d=d_\alpha=2k+1\) of A.86--A.87. For \(b\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}\), let \(D_b\in\Lambda\) be the unique continuous geometric sum defined by \[ (T-1)D_b=T^b-1. \tag{A.88.2} \] Then the actual full-head identity is \[ \Theta_uD_{a_{\rm reg}}=1. \tag{A.88.3} \] In particular the remaining full coefficient equality has the exact test using the canonical u alone: \[ a_{\rm reg}=d_\alpha \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Theta_uD_{d_\alpha}=1 \quad\hbox{in }\mathbb F_2[[\widehat{\mathbb Z}]]. \tag{A.88.4} \] The head in this ring is the full procyclic group, so (A.88.4) is not only a dyadic comparison. Consequently \[ (\Omega_\alpha)_{\rm ab} \in4\widehat{\mathbb Z}\,(1,-1). \tag{A.88.6} \] No higher congruence, full equality of the two units, full Fox-unit claim, or nonlinear vanishing of \(\Omega_\alpha\) is inferred.

statement: The actual hexagon defect and the full-GT dyadic coefficient comparison Let \(\alpha=(-1,f)\in\widehat{GT}_0\) be the actual negative involution, with canonical \(u\in F'\), and retain the full marked data of A.87--A.88. Put \[ \begin{gathered} z=(xy)^{-1},\qquad d=d_\alpha,\qquad m=(d-1)/2\in2\widehat{\mathbb Z},\\ u_0=u(x,y),\quad u_1=u(y,z),\quad u_2=u(z,x),\\ \mathcal H_d=u_0x^m u_2z^m u_1y^m . \end{gathered} \tag{A.89.1} \] This is the entire actual hexagon word, whether or not it is trivial. Let \(K=\overline{\langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle}\), \(\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[[\widehat{\mathbb Z}]]\), and identify \(K/\overline{K^2[K,K]}=\Lambda[x]\), with retained head \(T=y\) and \([x]=1\), as in A.88. For the involution on coefficients write \(\overline{P}(T)=P(T^{-1})\), and set \[ U=[u_0],\qquad W=[u_1],\qquad R_d=[\mathcal H_d],\qquad \Theta_u=1+(T-1)(U+\overline U). \tag{A.89.2} \] Use A.88's full continuous geometric sums \((T-1)D_b=T^b-1\). statement: The exact remaining odd-head coefficient criterion Assume the actual negative involution belongs to full \(\widehat{GT}\), and retain A.89's notation \(a=a_{\rm reg}\), \(d=d_\alpha\), \(\Theta_u\) and \(R_d\). statement: The exact abelian scope of the marked cube reversal Retain the actual \(\widehat{GT}_0\) data of A.87 and put \[ T_d=v\delta^d,\qquad \Xi_d=T_d^3,\qquad \sigma_d=\operatorname{Ad}(\delta^{-d})\Phi_\alpha|_F. \tag{A.91.1} \] For \(i=x,y,z\), let \[ K_i=\overline{\langle\!\langle i\rangle\!\rangle}_F,\qquad M_i=K_i/\overline{[K_i,K_i]},\qquad M=M_x\oplus M_y\oplus M_z. \tag{A.91.2} \] Then \(\sigma_d(\Xi_d)=\Xi_d^{-1}\), but the induced action of \(\sigma_d\) on the entire \(M_x\) is \(-\mathrm{id}\). Thus this reversal equality is tautological on every invariant abelian coefficient quotient of \(M_x\). More precisely, let \(\mathsf t\) be conjugation by \(T_d\) on the three-cover sum M. The actual \(\mathsf t,\tau\) actions satisfy \[ \mathsf t^3=1,\qquad \tau^2=1,\qquad \tau\mathsf t\tau=\mathsf t^{-1}. \tag{A.91.3} \] If \(\jmath_x:M_x\to M\) is the summand inclusion, the map \[ a\longmapsto \jmath_x(a)+\mathsf t\jmath_x(a)+\mathsf t^2\jmath_x(a) \tag{A.91.4} \] is a continuous isomorphism onto \[ \{w\in M:\mathsf t(w)=w,\ \tau(w)=-w\}. \tag{A.91.5} \] In particular these actual dihedral covariance identities impose no further restriction on a single cover coordinate. No assertion is made that every such vector comes from one common full word or a canonical hexagon defect.

statement: Exact common-word and swap-duality images at every odd Alexander head Let \(F=\widehat F(x,y)\), let \(z=(xy)^{-1}\), and let \(\iota\) interchange x and y. For an odd positive integer n put \(A_n=\mathbb F_2[C_n]\), with specified generator T, and let \(I_n\) be its augmentation ideal. The three actual cyclic-cover maps, written with their additive module coordinate before their head, are \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} &x&y\\ \hline \kappa_x&(1,1)&(0,T)\\ \kappa_y&(0,T)&(1,1)\\ \kappa_z&(0,T)&(T^{-1},T^{-1}). \end{array} \tag{A.92.1} \] Their targets are \(A_n\rtimes C_n\), with \((P,T^a)(Q,T^b)=(P+T^aQ,T^{a+b})\). In the third map z goes to \((1,1)\); the retained generators are respectively y, x, and x. Restricting to the closed commutator subgroup gives a continuous homomorphism \[ \pi_n:F'\longrightarrow I_n^3. \] It is surjective. Moreover, for every \(U,W\in I_n\) satisfying \(\overline W=TW\), there is one actual \(u\in F'\) such that \[ \iota(u)=u^{-1},\qquad \pi_n(u)=(U,U,W),\qquad [u(x,y)]_x=U,\quad [u(y,z)]_x=W. \tag{A.92.2} \] Here the bar sends T to \(T^{-1}\). Both conclusions hold simultaneously for all odd n: a compatible triple, or a compatible pair in (A.92.2), is realized by a single full profinite source word. These are source-word realization statements. They do not assert that the constructed word is canonical for an involution, satisfies the pentagon, or has a specified Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller multiplier.
