statement: The actual canonical and negative-hexagon equations in the three modules Let \(\alpha=(-1,f)\) be an actual nonidentity negative \(\widehat{GT}_0\)-involution, with the canonical \(u\in F'\) of A.85--A.89. Retain the original markings \[ \begin{gathered} \alpha(x)=x^{-1},\quad \alpha(y)=f^{-1}y^{-1}f, \quad u=f\alpha(u),\quad z=(xy)^{-1},\\ \iota(x)=y,\quad\iota(y)=x,\quad \iota(u)=u^{-1},\quad\iota(f)=f^{-1},\\ v=\operatorname{Inn}(u^{-1})\iota,\qquad \tau=\alpha v. \end{gathered} \tag{A.93.1} \] Use the full characteristic-two procyclic coefficient ring \(\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[[\widehat{\mathbb Z}]]\) in the three cyclic-cover coordinates of A.92. Define \[ \begin{gathered} U=[u]_x=[u]_y,\qquad W=[u]_z=[u(y,z)]_x,\\ F_f=[f]_x=[f]_y,\qquad G_f=[f]_z=[f(y,z)]_x, \qquad j(P)=T^{-1}\overline P. \end{gathered} \tag{A.93.2} \] Then the actual canonical equation and the actual negative hexagon imply \[ F_f=U+\overline U,\qquad G_f=0, \qquad j(W)=W. \tag{A.93.3} \] The complete joint action on the direct sum of these three kernel modules is \[ \begin{aligned} \alpha(P_x,P_y,P_z)&=(\overline{P_x},\overline{P_y},j(P_z)),\\ v(P_x,P_y,P_z)&=(P_y,P_x,j(P_z)),\\ \tau(P_x,P_y,P_z)&=(\overline{P_y},\overline{P_x},P_z). \end{aligned} \tag{A.93.4} \] In these modules, the canonical equation is precisely \[ (U,U,W)=(F_f,F_f,0)+(\overline U,\overline U,j(W)). \tag{A.93.5} \] Thus it supplies no additional relation between U and W at this level once the displayed negative-hexagon consequences are retained. This is not a redundancy claim for the full nonlinear canonical equation. There is also an independent exact source-word assertion. For every odd n the joint map consisting of A.92's three coordinates and the marked odd dihedral quotient \[ D_{2n}=\langle a,R\mid a^2=R^n=1,\ aRa=R^{-1}\rangle, \qquad x\mapsto a,\quad y\mapsto aR \tag{A.93.6} \] has image \(I_n^3\times C_n\) on \(F'\). Every permitted U,W and every rotation exponent k modulo n can be simultaneously realized by one actual full-source duality word u. The same holds at all odd heads simultaneously for compatible data. Those realizing words are not asserted to be canonical \(\widehat{GT}_0\) or \(\widehat{GT}\) parameters.

statement: The full affine-character boundary of the marked pentagon Use the standard pure generators \[ (a,b,c,d,e,f)=(A_{12},A_{13},A_{23},A_{14},A_{24},A_{34}). \tag{A.94.1} \] For every field k, every homomorphism \(P_4\to\operatorname{Aff}_1(k)=k\rtimes k^\times\) with nonabelian image factors through one of the following five marked free-two quotients, expressed by the images of the original generators: \[ \begin{array}{c|l} \mathrm{(i)}&a=b=d=1,\quad cef=1,\\ \mathrm{(ii)}&a=c=e=1,\quad bdf=1,\\ \mathrm{(iii)}&b=c=f=1,\quad ade=1,\\ \mathrm{(iv)}&d=e=f=1,\quad abc=1,\\ \mathrm{(v)}&a=f,\quad c=d,\quad b=(df)^{-1},\quad e=(fd)^{-1}. \end{array} \tag{A.94.2} \] Consequently, if \(u\in\widehat F(X,Y)'\) satisfies the exact swap duality \(u(Y,X)=u(X,Y)^{-1}\), its marked pentagon \[ u(a,ce)u(bc,f)=u(c,f)u(ab,ef)u(a,c) \tag{A.94.3} \] holds after every homomorphism from \(\widehat P_4\) to a finite affine group over a field. More generally it holds after every homomorphism to any finite group with an elementary abelian two-kernel and odd abelian quotient. Thus the entire first elementary-two layer over every odd abelian head adds no pentagon condition beyond exact swap duality. This is a theorem about these actual quotient maps, not about the pentagon in \(\widehat P_4\), the realization of canonical parameters, or the vanishing of the full cusp word.

Its full completion is \(\widehat N\rtimes\widehat B\). For every finite quotient Q of B, writing \(H=\ker(B\to Q)\), the actual relative quotient \[ \widehat G/O^2(\widehat N\rtimes\widehat H) \tag{A.96.3} \] retains an embedded free pro-two group \(N^{(2)}\) of rank three, with P primitive and nontrivial. Here \(O^2\) denotes the kernel of the maximal pro-two quotient.

Then \(\alpha\) preserves \(\widehat N\), induces a negative peripheral involution \(\alpha_0\) on \(\widehat B\), and acts as minus identity on \((\widehat N)_{\rm ab}\). There is a unique full transporter \(h_0\in\widehat N\) with zero L-coordinate in the basis \((L,A,C)\) and \[ \alpha(L)=h_0^{-1}L^{-1}h_0. \tag{A.97.1} \] It satisfies \[ \begin{gathered} h_0\alpha(h_0)=1,\qquad \beta=\operatorname{Inn}(h_0)\alpha, \qquad \beta^2=1,\\ \beta|_{\widehat B}=\alpha_0,\qquad \alpha(b)=h_0^{-1}\alpha_0(b)h_0\quad(b\in\widehat B). \end{gathered} \tag{A.97.2} \] Both involutions act on every actual relative pro-two quotient over the specified odd-dihedral base head, with this same correction.

statement: The original cabling arrows determine the full correction Let \(\alpha=(-1,\varphi)\in\widehat{GT}\) be the actual involution, with canonical \(u\in\widehat F'\) satisfying \(u=\varphi\alpha(u)\). statement: The original regular cusp frame in the same sphere kernel In the literal rank-two copy of A.98, write \(\alpha_* =\gamma|_{\widehat F(A,S)}\), \(\varphi=\varphi_\alpha(A,S)\), \(u=u_\alpha(A,S)\). The unique zero-abelianization regular transporter of A.86 is exactly \[ h_{\rm reg}=S^{-1}tA\varphi^{-1}Su, \qquad \tau_*(z_*)=h_{\rm reg}^{-1}z_*^{-1}h_{\rm reg}. \tag{A.99.2} \] If \(h_{\rm reg}=q_*\tau_*(q_*)^{-1}\) is the actual A.86 norm frame, with \((q_*)_{\rm ab}=(\xi,-\xi)\) in the (A,S)-basis, then \[ \begin{gathered} h_0=S q_*\tau_*(q_*)^{-1}u^{-1}S^{-1} \varphi A^{-1}p,\\ (q_*)_{\rm ab}=(-\xi,2\xi,0) \quad\hbox{in the basis }(L,A,C). \end{gathered} \tag{A.99.3} \] These are full-word identities retaining the same h0 and both based cabling factors; they do not by themselves determine xi.

statement: The full-GT pentagon forces the full coefficient equality For an actual negative involution \(\alpha\in\widehat{GT}\), the actual regular-frame unit and canonical dihedral exponent satisfy \[ a_{\rm reg}=d_\alpha=2k_\alpha+1 \quad\hbox{in }\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \tag{A.100.1} \] Equivalently the actual regular scalar is \(\xi=-(d_\alpha-1)/4\); the full abelianization of \(\Omega_\alpha\) is zero. statement: Full-ring Alexander vanishing of the actual hexagon Let alpha be an actual negative full-GT involution, u its canonical word, \(k=(d_\alpha-1)/2\in2\widehat{\mathbb Z}\), and \[ \mathcal H_d=u(x,y)x^k u(z,x)z^k u(y,z)y^k, \qquad z=(xy)^{-1}. \tag{A.101.1} \] For \(K_x=\overline{\langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle}\), put \(D_x=\overline{K_x^2[K_x,K_x]}\), and define \(D_y,D_z\) by the same actual cyclic marking. Then \[ \mathcal H_d\in D_x\cap D_y\cap D_z. \tag{A.101.2} \] In particular the first-cover Alexander coordinate is zero in \(\mathbb F_2[[\widehat{\mathbb Z}]]\), including every finite head \(N=2^r n\), n odd. This is not a full-word vanishing claim.

statement: Every marked odd boundary cover retains its full free pro-two Schreier kernel and the original canonical involution \label{stmt:A102} Use the actual sphere quotient and original full-GT involution of A.96--A.98: \[ G=N\rtimes B,\qquad N=F(P,A,C),\quad B=F(d,f),\qquad P=def,\quad A=af^{-1},\quad C=cd^{-1}. \] For an odd integer $n>1$ let \[ N_n=\ker\bigl(N\to C_n,\ P\mapsto1,\ A,C\mapsto0\bigr), \quad p=P^n,\quad A_i=P^iAP^{-i},\quad C_i=P^iCP^{-i}. \] Then $N_n$ has the literal free basis \[ p,\ A_0,\ldots,A_{n-1},\ C_0,\ldots,C_{n-1}. \] The four signed base actions are the full indexed formulas below, with their nonperiodic $p$ wraps retained. There is an actual finite head $G\to C_n\times D_{2n}$ with kernel $K_n=N_n\rtimes B_n$ for which \[ K_n^{(2)}=N_n^{(2)}\rtimes B_n^{(2)}. \] Consequently the actual relative quotient \[ G_{(n,\mathrm{rel})} =\widehat G/O^2(\widehat K_n) \] contains the embedded free pro-two group $N_n^{(2)}$ on the displayed basis. Both the original involution $\alpha$ and its precisely specified normalized reflection act on this quotient, with the full correction $h_0$ retained inside that kernel. No pair-twist square or class-two relation is imposed in this proposition.

statement: The uniform affine pentagon and the full signed congruence hexagon Let \(F=\widehat F(x,y)\), and let \(u\in F'\) satisfy duality \(u(y,x)=u(x,y)^{-1}\) and the original marked sphere pentagon \[ u(a_0,c_0e_0)u(b_0c_0,f_0) =u(c_0,f_0)u(a_0b_0,e_0f_0)u(a_0,c_0). \tag{A.103.1} \] Here the six letters are the original \((A_{12},A_{13},A_{23},A_{14},A_{24},A_{34})\) in the completion of \(G=P_4/\langle\Delta_4^2\rangle\). In the universal dihedral group \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}_{T}\rtimes\langle s\rangle\), use \(x\mapsto s,\ y\mapsto sT\), and define \(k\) by \(u(s,sT)=T^k\). Put \[ d=1+2k,\qquad z=(xy)^{-1},\qquad H_d=u(x,y)x^k u(z,x)z^k u(y,z)y^k. \tag{A.103.2} \] Then \(k\in2\widehat{\mathbb Z}\), and \(d\) is a unit. For the original signed representation \[ \begin{gathered} q:F\longrightarrow\operatorname{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb Z}), \qquad X=q(x)=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad Y=q(y)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-2&1\end{pmatrix},\\ U=q(u),\qquad b=U_{12}, \end{gathered} \tag{A.103.3} \] one has the exact identities \[ dU_{11}=1,\qquad U=\begin{pmatrix}d^{-1}&b\\b&d(1+b^2)\end{pmatrix}, \qquad q(H_d)=I. \tag{A.103.4} \] Every assertion holds in every signed congruence quotient, including even and mixed moduli. For an actual canonical word of a negative full-GT involution, A.37 supplies exactly (A.103.1). The theorem itself requires no norm equation.

statement: The actual congruence automorphism and the exact kernel-surjectivity gate Retain the actual \(u,k,d,q,U,b\) of A.103 and put \[ \begin{gathered} \psi_d:F\longrightarrow F,\qquad \psi_d(x)=x^d,\quad \psi_d(y)=u^{-1}y^du,\\ C=q(F),\qquad N=\ker q,\qquad H=\begin{pmatrix}1&-b\\0&d^{-1}\end{pmatrix}. \end{gathered} \tag{A.104.1} \] Then \(H\) normalizes the actual closed congruence image \(C\), and \[ q\psi_d=\operatorname{Ad}(H)q,\qquad \psi_d^{-1}(N)=N. \tag{A.104.2} \] Writing \(L=\psi_d(F)\), one has the exact equalities \[ \begin{gathered} L=\overline{\langle x,u^{-1}yu\rangle},\qquad F=NL,\qquad L\cap N=\psi_d(N),\\ L=F\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \psi_d(N)=N. \end{gathered} \tag{A.104.3} \] Thus the remaining full-surjectivity question is exactly surjectivity of the actual restriction \(\psi_d:N\to N\). No surjectivity on that infinite kernel is asserted. For actual normalized full-GT data \[ \alpha(x)=x^{-1},\quad \alpha(y)=\varphi^{-1}y^{-1}\varphi,\quad u=\varphi\alpha(u), \tag{A.104.4} \] let \(c_0\) denote the automorphism inverting both \(x,y\), and put \(J_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\). The original involution preserves \(N\), and its actual action on \(C\) is \[ \begin{gathered} q\alpha=\operatorname{Ad}(K)q,\qquad K=HJ_0H^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&2bd\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\\ q(\varphi)=Y^{-bd}X^{bd} =\begin{pmatrix}1&2bd\\2bd&1+4b^2d^2\end{pmatrix}. \end{gathered} \tag{A.104.5} \] In particular the quotient involutions are conjugate by \(\operatorname{Ad}(H)\). This conclusion is proved directly from the original peripheral action and norm, without cancelling an unproved automorphism \(\psi_d\).

statement: The central modular quotient creates incompatible pure frame choices and a nontrivial cyclic lifting obstruction Retain the actual signed congruence map and first relative-central quotient of A.106--A.107: \[ \begin{gathered} q:F\longrightarrow C\leq\mathrm{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbf Z}), \qquad N=\ker q,\quad N_1=\overline{[N,F]},\\ B_1=B/N_1,\qquad E_1=F/N_1,\qquad \rho=\operatorname{Ad}(r). \end{gathered} \] The original \(B=C_2(s)\amalg C_3(r)\), signed matrices and based free generators are those of A.105 and A.109. There exists an element \[ h\in(E_1')^\rho,\qquad q_4(h)=I,\qquad q_3(h)=-I. \tag{A.110.1} \] Thus the identity automorphism of \(B_1\) has the two equally pure quotient \(r\)-frames \(1,h\), with the same \(s\)-frame \(1\). They have identical abelian normalization. Applying the literal original LM7\_PUSH~E.65.2--4 recipe to these two choices gives respectively zero and one. Consequently that recipe does not descend to an unframed quotient automorphism when arbitrary pure quotient frames are allowed. This does not disprove an extension with additional coherent frame data, or decide whether the actual GT character factors through a suitably specified action image. The element \(h\) has no \(\rho\)-fixed lift to \(F'\). For any lift \(w\in F'\), the cocycle \[ w^{-1}\rho(w)\in Z^1(C_3,N_1) \tag{A.110.2} \] represents a nonbase cohomology class. In particular \[ H^1(C_3,N_1)\ne\{*\},\qquad N_1 \text{ is not a pro-two group}. \tag{A.110.3} \] The actual full-GT CM parity remains open.

statement: A coherent factor-frame obstruction whose signed image is the original CM character Retain the actual full-GT negative involution \(\alpha=(-1,\phi)\), the canonical norm word \(u\), the even dihedral exponent \(k\), and \(d=1+2k\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{\times}\) of A.103--A.108. Let \(N_1=\overline{[\ker q,F]}\), \(E_1=F/N_1\), and \(B_1=B/N_1\). All actions below are genuine continuous actions on these actual profinite quotients. Put \[ e=d\bmod3\in\{1,-1\},\qquad \varepsilon=(1-e)/2,\qquad R_e=y^{\varepsilon}r,\qquad v=u^{-1}s=su. \tag{A.111.1} \] Here the two values of \(e\) are ordinary integer representatives. Thus \(R_1=r\) and \(R_{-1}=sr^{-1}s\). The automorphism \(\Psi_1\) of A.107 has \(\Psi_1(s)=v\) and, by A.108, admits a pure frame \[ \Psi_1(r)=hR_eh^{-1},\qquad h\in E_1. \tag{A.111.2} \] Use the ORIGINAL unique full-group frame \(A_r\) of A.105, and use the following full-group words, then their images in \(B_1\): \[ J_e^{\alpha}= \begin{cases}s\phi A_r,&\varepsilon=0,\\ A_rs,&\varepsilon=1. \end{cases} \tag{A.111.3} \] Define the closed profinite group and its involution \[ T_e=C_{E_1}(R_e),\qquad \kappa_e(t)=(J_e^{\alpha})^{-1}\alpha(t)J_e^{\alpha}. \tag{A.111.4} \] Then \[ w_h=(J_e^{\alpha})^{-1}\alpha(h)^{-1}vh \in Z^1(C_2,T_e),\qquad \omega_{\alpha}=[w_h]\in H^1(C_2,T_e) \tag{A.111.5} \] is independent of the choice of the pure quotient frame \(h\). We use continuous nonabelian cohomology, with cocycles \(w\kappa_e(w)=1\) and equivalence \(w\sim a^{-1}w\kappa_e(a)\), \(a\in T_e\). The class \(\omega_{\alpha}\) is the distinguished point if and only if a frame in (A.111.2) can be chosen to satisfy \[ \alpha(h)J_e^{\alpha}=vh. \tag{A.111.6} \] Furthermore the actual signed reduction restricts to a continuous \(C_2\)-equivariant homomorphism \[ \chi_e=q_3|_{T_e}:T_e\longrightarrow\{I,-I\}, \tag{A.111.7} \] where the target has trivial action. Its induced map on pointed cohomology sets satisfies \[ \boxed{\quad \chi_{e,*}(\omega_{\alpha}) =\epsilon_A eI=(-1)^{\Delta(\alpha)}I. \quad} \tag{A.111.8} \] The sign \(\epsilon_A\) and the character \(\Delta\) are exactly those of A.105 and original LM7\_PUSH~E.65. Thus a nonzero original CM character obstructs (A.111.6). This theorem neither decides that character nor asserts that its vanishing suffices to make \(\omega_{\alpha}\) the distinguished point.

statement: The actual first congruence-central quotient is a specified product, and its odd coherent obstruction coordinates are binary Retain the original signed congruence map \(q:F\to\mathcal C\), put \[ \begin{gathered} N=\ker q,\quad N_1=\overline{[N,F]},\quad P=F^{(2)},\\ M_2=\ker(P\to\mathcal C_{(2)}),\quad M_{21}=\overline{[M_2,P]},\quad P_*=P/M_{21}. \end{gathered} \] and write \(G_p=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z_p)\). Let \(\chi:G_3\to C_3\) be its actual abelianization character, normalized by \(\chi(q_3(x))=\chi(q_3(y))=1\). There is an isomorphism of actual compact groups \[ E_1=F/N_1\ \cong\ P_*\times\bigl(G_3\times_{C_3}\mathbb Z_3^2\bigr) \times\prod_{p\geq5}\bigl(G_p\times\mathbb Z_p^2\bigr). \tag{A.112.1} \] The fiber product uses \(\chi\) and \((a,b)\mapsto a+b\bmod3\). All maps in this identification are the original coordinate maps, and \[ E_1'=P_*'\times G_3'\times\prod_{p\geq5}G_p. \tag{A.112.2} \] Put \(J=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). For \(e\in\{1,-1\}\), set \(\varepsilon=(1-e)/2\), \[ R_e=y^\varepsilon r,\qquad \rho_e=\operatorname{Ad}(R_e),\qquad J_e=\operatorname{diag}(1,e)J\operatorname{diag}(1,e)^{-1}. \] Then \[ \begin{split} T_e=C_{E_1}(R_e) &=(P_*')^{\rho_e}\times T_{3,e}\times\prod_{p\geq5}T_{p,e},\\ T_{3,e}&=C_{G_3'}(J_e),\qquad T_{p,e}=C_{G_p}(J_e)\quad(p\geq5). \end{split} \tag{A.112.3} \] For the actual full-GT negative involution and the ORIGINAL negative frame \(J_e^\alpha\) of A.111, let \(\kappa_e(t)=(J_e^\alpha)^{-1}\alpha(t)J_e^\alpha\). This action is inversion on every odd factor in (A.112.3), and \[ H^1(C_2,T_e;\kappa_e)\ \cong\ H^1(C_2,(P_*')^{\rho_e};\kappa_e)\times \prod_{p\ {\rm odd}}C_2 \tag{A.112.4} \] as pointed compact spaces. Its three-adic coordinate is the actual scalar reduction \(q_3\). For the specified coherent class of A.111, that coordinate is \(\epsilon_A(d\bmod3)I=(-1)^{\Delta(\alpha)}I\). No value of this coordinate, of the other odd coordinates, or of the dyadic class is asserted.

statement: The entire first-kernel cyclic cohomology is its pure fixed group, and a central sign twist preserves the quotient negative-frame equations Retain \(N_1\), \(E_1=F/N_1\), and \(\rho=\operatorname{Ad}(r)\) in their actual original markings. There is a canonical pointed homeomorphism \[ \partial:T=C_{E_1}(r)=(E_1')^\rho \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ H^1(C_3,N_1),\qquad \partial(h)=[w^{-1}\rho(w)],\quad w\in F',\ wN_1=h. \tag{A.113.1} \] There is an exact central extension of compact groups \[ 1\longrightarrow K^\rho\longrightarrow T \longrightarrow C_{\mathcal C'}(J)\longrightarrow1,\qquad K=(N\cap F')/N_1\ \text{pro-two}. \tag{A.113.2} \] The natural map \(H^1(C_3,N_1)\to H^1(C_3,K_3')\) is, under A.109 and (A.113.1), exactly \(q_3:T\to\{I,-I\}\). Here \(K_3'=\ker(q_3|_{F'})\). For the ORIGINAL LM7\_PUSH~E.61/E.65 pure \(r\)-frame \(A_r\), all pure quotient frames of the same action are \(\overline A_rT\). The class of the exact transporter defect of a lift of \(\overline A_rh\) is \(\partial(h)\). Only \(h=1\) admits the original full transporter. There is moreover an actual central involution \[ c_*\in Z(B/N_1)\cap E_1',\qquad \alpha(c_*)=c_*,\quad q_4(c_*)=I,\quad q_3(c_*)=-I. \tag{A.113.3} \] For the specified negative frame \(J_e^\alpha\) in A.111, both \(J_e^\alpha\) and \(J_e^\alpha c_*\) obey the same two quotient negative-frame equations and induce the same \(\kappa_e\) on \(T_e\). Their coherent classes differ by multiplication by \(c_*\); this is a fixed-point-free involution of the compact cohomology space, toggling its three-adic coordinate. It does not change the original full-group frame, and does not decide the actual CM value.

statement: The next modular central refinement and a full peripheral lift Assume the original negative involution belongs to full \(\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}\), and retain its canonical \(u\), actual \(d=1+2k\), and ordered \(H_d\). statement: The entire residual cyclic cohomology and coherent comparison preserve the original odd coordinates Use the exact residual of A.116, \[ R=N_1\cap O=N\cap F'\cap O,\qquad E_R=F/R=P\times D_o,\qquad P=F^{(2)}. \] All kernels are the actual closed kernels. Put \(\rho=\operatorname{Ad}(r)\) and retain the integral matrix \(J=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). Then \[ \begin{gathered} T_R=C_{E_R}(r)=(E_R')^\rho,\\ T_R\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ H^1(C_3,R),\qquad h\longmapsto[w^{-1}\rho(w)],\quad w\in F',\ wR=h,\\ T_R=(P')^\rho\times C_{\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z_3)'}(J) \times\prod_{p\geq5}C_{\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z_p)}(J). \end{gathered} \tag{A.117.1} \] The middle identification is a pointed homeomorphism. Writing \(T_1=C_{E_1}(r)\), the natural comparison is the exact sequence of compact groups \[ 1\longrightarrow M_{21}^\rho\longrightarrow T_R \longrightarrow T_1\longrightarrow1. \tag{A.117.2} \] Under A.113 and (A.117.1) it is exactly the natural map of the two cohomology spaces; its basepoint fiber corresponds to \(M_{21}^\rho\). Its further map to A.109's two-point space is the SAME original \(q_3\) coordinate. For \(e=d\bmod3\), put \(R_e=y^{(1-e)/2}r\) and \(\rho_e=\operatorname{Ad}(R_e)\). Retain the ORIGINAL full negative frame \(J_e^\alpha\), its images in both quotients, and \(\kappa_e(t)=(J_e^\alpha)^{-1}\alpha(t)J_e^\alpha\). Then \[ \begin{split} T_{R,e}=C_{E_R}(R_e) &=(P')^{\rho_e}\times T_{3,e}\times\prod_{p\geq5}T_{p,e},\\ H^1(C_2,T_{R,e};\kappa_e) &\cong H^1(C_2,(P')^{\rho_e};\kappa_e) \times\prod_{p\ {\rm odd}}C_2. \end{split} \tag{A.117.3} \] The comparison to A.112 is the identity on every odd coordinate. For an actual lift \(h_R\) of a positive factor frame, its coherent defect is \[ w_{h_R}=(J_e^\alpha)^{-1}\alpha(h_R)^{-1}vh_R. \tag{A.117.4} \] It projects to the same defect in \(B/N_1\), and \[ q_3(w_{h_R})=\epsilon_A(d\bmod3)I=(-1)^{\Delta(\alpha)}I. \tag{A.117.5} \] Existence of a coherent frame is exactly the full norm condition \[ w_{h_R}=\kappa_e(t)t^{-1}\quad\text{for some }t\in T_{R,e}. \tag{A.117.6} \] Thus passage through the pro-two kernel preserves, but does not determine, the original odd obstruction coordinates. There is a separate, exact ORIGINAL cubic gate. Set \(\eta=v\delta^d\) in the full group \(B\). For any full pure lift \(h\in F\) of a factor frame in \(E_R\), put \(a_h=h^{-1}\eta hR_e^{-1}\in R\). Then \[ a_h\rho_e(a_h)\rho_e^2(a_h) =h^{-1}u^{-1}H_d^{-1}uh. \tag{A.117.10} \] In particular this SPECIFIED element is a \(C_3\)-cocycle if and only if the original full word \(H_d\) is one. The cohomology classification cannot be applied to it before that condition holds.

statement: A normalized GT-zero residual involution and its transported pentagon Let \(\alpha\) be the original negative involution of full \(\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}\), with canonical \(u\), parameter \(\phi\), actual even \(k\), and \(d=1+2k\). statement: The entire residual involution cohomology is the compact product of the odd unit groups Let \(R\), \(E_R=F/R=P\times D_o\), and the original negative full-GT \(\alpha\) be as in A.116. Let \(\Gamma\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0\) be the actual normalized full lift in A.118, put \(\beta=\Gamma^{-1}\alpha\Gamma\), and write \(c(x)=x^{-1}\), \(c(y)=y^{-1}\). All three actions preserve \(R\). The actions of \(c\) and \(\beta\) on \(E_R\) coincide, whereas the actual \(\Psi_R\) conjugates \(c\) to \(\alpha\) there. For each \(a\in\{c,\alpha,\beta\}\) there is a canonical pointed homeomorphism \[ \partial_a:E_R^a\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ H^1(C_2,R;a), \qquad h\longmapsto[w^{-1}a(w)],\quad w\in F',\ wR=h. \tag{A.119.1} \] In particular \[ \begin{gathered} E_R^c=E_R^\beta =\prod_{p\ {\rm odd}} \{\operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1}):t\in\mathbb Z_p^\times\},\\ E_R^\alpha=\Psi_R(E_R^c),\\ H^1(C_2,R;a)\ \cong\ \prod_{p\ {\rm odd}}\mathbb Z_p^\times \qquad(a=c,\alpha,\beta) \end{gathered} \tag{A.119.2} \] as pointed compact spaces, with the identity-unit tuple as basepoint. statement: Every odd coherent class becomes trivial after the positive-factor centralizer constraint is forgotten Retain the actual full-GT negative involution \(\alpha\), its original parameter \(\phi\), canonical word \(u\), and unit \(d\) of A.104--A.118. Let \(R=N_1\cap O\) be the actual residual of A.116, and put \[ E_R=F/R,\qquad P=F^{(2)},\qquad G_p=\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z_p). \] Thus A.112 and A.116 give the actual compact derived group \[ E_R'=P'\times G_{\rm odd}',\qquad G_{\rm odd}'=G_3'\times\prod_{p\geq5}G_p. \tag{A.120.1} \] For \(e=d\bmod3\in\{1,-1\}\), put \(\epsilon=(1-e)/2\) and \(R_e=y^\epsilon r\). Use the ORIGINAL LM7\_PUSH~E.61/E.65 pure frame \(A_r\) and the specified negative frame from A.111: \[ J_e^\alpha= \begin{cases} s\phi A_r,&e=1,\\ A_rs,&e=-1, \end{cases} \qquad \kappa_e=\operatorname{Ad}\bigl((J_e^\alpha)^{-1}\bigr)\alpha . \tag{A.120.2} \] This is an involution on \(E_R'\). Its restriction preserves the actual positive-factor centralizer \[ \begin{gathered} T_{R,e}=C_{E_R}(R_e)=T_{2,e}\times T_{{\rm odd},e},\\ T_{2,e}=(P')^{\rho_e},\qquad T_{{\rm odd},e}=C_{G_3'}(J_e)\times \prod_{p\geq5}C_{G_p}(J_e),\\ J_e=\operatorname{diag}(1,e)J\operatorname{diag}(1,e)^{-1}, \qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}. \end{gathered} \tag{A.120.3} \] All products and actions are the actual ones proved in A.112 and A.117. Then \[ H^1(C_2,G_{\rm odd}';\kappa_e)=\{*\}, \qquad H^1(C_2,T_{{\rm odd},e};\kappa_e) \simeq\prod_{p\ {\rm odd}}C_2 . \tag{A.120.4} \] The map induced by the actual inclusion of coefficient groups \[ H^1(C_2,T_{R,e};\kappa_e) \longrightarrow H^1(C_2,E_R';\kappa_e) \] is, under the natural product homeomorphisms, exactly \[ \begin{gathered} H^1(C_2,T_{2,e};\kappa_e)\times \prod_{p\ {\rm odd}}C_2 \longrightarrow H^1(C_2,P';\kappa_e),\\ ([z_2],\varepsilon_{\rm odd})\longmapsto \operatorname{incl}_*([z_2]). \end{gathered} \tag{A.120.5} \] These are continuous maps of pointed compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular every class with basepoint dyadic coordinate becomes trivial after this inclusion, regardless of all its odd coordinates. No coordinate of the specified original coherent class is evaluated.

statement: The exact elliptic boundary and original third-cusp bridge Let \(\alpha\) be the original negative involution of full \(\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}\), with original parameter \(\phi\), canonical commutator word \(u\), and actual \(d=1+2k\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}\) with the same even \(k\) as above. In \(E=\widehat F(X,Y)\), put \[ p=[Y,X],\qquad q=X,\qquad z=(pq)^{-1}=YX^{-1}Y^{-1},\qquad H=\overline{\langle p,q\rangle}. \tag{A.122.1} \] The pair \((p,q)\) is a free profinite basis of the actual embedded subgroup \(H\), with its full profinite topology. Write \[ \begin{gathered} u_0=u(p,q),\quad u_2=u(z,p),\quad U=u(q,p)=u_0^{-1},\quad V=u_2,\\ \Phi=\phi(q,p),\qquad Q=\phi(z,p),\\ \xi=U X^dU^{-1},\qquad \omega=p^kVYU^{-1},\qquad \eta(X)=\xi,\quad\eta(Y)=\omega . \end{gathered} \tag{A.122.2} \] Let \(\Theta\) be the actual elliptic involution supplied by A.121 and the full profinite section, and let \(c_{\mathrm{ell}}(X)=X^{-1},\ c_{\mathrm{ell}}(Y)=p^{-1}Y\). Then \[ \Theta(\xi)=\xi^{-1},\qquad \Theta(\omega)=p^{-d}\omega, \tag{A.122.3} \] and the following three conditions are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} \Theta\eta=\eta c_{\mathrm{ell}},\qquad [\omega,\xi]=p^d,\\ \psi_d(z)=\operatorname{Ad}\bigl(p^ku(z,p)\bigr)(z^d), \quad \psi_d(p)=p^d,\quad\psi_d(q)=u_0^{-1}q^du_0 . \end{gathered} \tag{A.122.4} \] The third condition is a specified conjugacy at the original third cusp of \(H\). statement: A boundary-power automorphy criterion and the original free-factor restriction Let \(E=\widehat F(X,Y)\), \(K=[Y,X]\), and let \(\eta\) be a continuous endomorphism. statement: The actual elliptic cubic has a unique continuous pure transporter and an exact involution obstruction Let \(\mathcal G=B_{1,3}\) be the discrete reduced elliptic braid group in A.121, and put \(\mathcal P=P_{1,3}=\ker(\mathcal G\to S_3)\). All completions in this statement are full profinite completions. Use the actual marked generators \(\sigma,\tau,X,Y\), and put \[ L=\tau^{-1}\sigma^{-1},\qquad \Pi_0=LY, \qquad \bar r=\pi(\Pi_0)\in S_3. \tag{A.124.1} \] There are exactly four conjugacy classes of nontrivial finite subgroups of \(\widehat{\mathcal G}\), all cyclic of order three, and eight conjugacy classes of nonidentity torsion elements. The latter are distinguished exactly by their eight nonzero images in the indicated odd factor of \[ \mathcal G^{\rm ab} =C_2\langle\sigma\rangle\times C_3\langle X\rangle\times C_3\langle Y\rangle. \tag{A.124.2} \] The centralizer and normalizer of every nontrivial finite subgroup of \(\widehat{\mathcal G}\) equal that subgroup itself. For every profinite commutator word \(w\) satisfying A.121's original pentagon, let \(\Pi_w\) be its specified elliptic cubic. There is a unique \(p_w\in\widehat{\mathcal P}\) such that \[ \Pi_w=p_w\Pi_0p_w^{-1}. \tag{A.124.3} \] The map \(w\mapsto p_w\) is continuous on the closed space of these words, and \(p_1=1\). There is a unique \(h_u\in\widehat{\mathcal P}\) with \[ \Theta(\Pi_u)=h_u\Pi_uh_u^{-1},\qquad \Theta(h_u)h_u=1. \tag{A.124.4} \] Write \(z_u=h_u^{-1}\) and let \(\vartheta\) denote the order-two generator in \(\widehat{\mathcal G}\rtimes_\Theta\langle\vartheta\rangle\). Then \(z_u\vartheta\) is an involution commuting with \(\Pi_u\), and \[ \langle\Pi_u,z_u\vartheta\rangle\cong C_6. \tag{A.124.5} \] Its section class \([z_u]\in H^1(C_2,\widehat{\mathcal P};\Theta)\) is trivial exactly when a pure conjugate of \(\Pi_u\) is fixed by \(\Theta\). This class is the same for every \(\Pi_w\) above, with \(\Theta\) held fixed. Neither its triviality nor the original third-cusp equation or CM parity is asserted.

statement: The elliptic transporter lies in the pure derived subgroup Retain the actual groups \(\mathcal G,\mathcal P\), element \(\Pi_0\), and unique pure transporters \(p_w,h_w\) of A.124. statement: The actual elliptic Brunnian kernel is a closed commutator Retain the actual pure completed elliptic group \(P\), its closed derived subgroup \(P'\), and the based deletion maps of A.126. statement: The actual GT0 two-strand reflection and its noncusp fixed group Let \(\alpha=(-1,\phi)\) be the original normalized negative involution in \(\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0\), and let \[ E=\widehat F(X,Y),\quad K=[Y,X],\quad z=(KX)^{-1}=YX^{-1}Y^{-1},\quad \Phi=\phi(X,K),\quad Q=\phi(z,K). \] The generator assignments \[ T(X)=\Phi X^{-1}\Phi^{-1},\qquad T(Y)=K^{-1}QY\Phi^{-1} \tag{A.130.1} \] define an actual involutory automorphism of \(E\), with \[ T(K)=K^{-1},\qquad T(\Phi)=\Phi^{-1},\qquad Tj=j^{-1}T, \tag{A.130.2} \] where \(j\) is the original two-strand action of A.126. Z_u=u(t_2,\tau^2),\qquad r_S=U_SZ_u. \end{gathered} \tag{A.135.3} \] The actual source involution \(\theta_T\) satisfies the literal source identities \[ \begin{gathered} \theta_T(t_2)=t_2^{-1},\qquad statement: The closure-intersection step is an unproved implication The proofs of Proposition 2.4 of \citet{Boggi2026} and Theorem 5.1(iii) of \citet{BoggiZalesskii2025} contain the same unproved passage. After the per-element comparisons, the equality that remains to be established is \[ \bigcap_{x\in S}\overline{C_G(x)} =\overline{\bigcap_{x\in S}C_G(x)} =\overline{C_G(H)},\qquad H=\langle S\rangle . \] Here \(S\) is a finite generating set of the finite subgroup \(H\leq G\), and all closures are in the specified profinite completion of \(G\). The cited per-element comparisons alone give only the inclusion from right to left. This observation does not refute either theorem. The exact published scopes must be retained. In Proposition 2.4, $G$ is assumed residually finite, good, and of finite virtual cohomological type; the assertion is quantified over every finite $H\leq G$. Its central conclusion is $Z_{\widehat G}(\iota(H))=\overline{\iota(Z_G(H))}$. In Theorem 5.1, a class $\mathscr C$ of finite groups is fixed. The group is residually $\mathscr C$, $\mathscr C$-good, and of finite virtual $p$-cohomological type at the relevant primes. Every finite solvable $\mathscr C$-subgroup has a normalizer with those same properties and with its full pro-$\mathscr C$ topology induced from $G$. Part (iii) asserts $C_{G_{\widehat{\mathscr C}}}(H)=\overline{C_G(H)}$ for every finite $\mathscr C$-subgroup $H$, while its normalizer assertion is restricted to solvable $H$. We audit these statements with their hypotheses, not a version in which goodness alone is substituted for all of them.

statement: The normalizer comparison repairs the solvable centralizer case Let \(G\) be residually finite and \(H\leq G\) finite. statement: The exact coset obstruction Let \(U\trianglelefteq G\) have finite index and \(U\cap H=1\). Write \(\widehat U=\overline U\leq\widehat G\). For \(\bar g\in C_{G/U}(\bar H)\), choose \(g\in G\) mapping to \(\bar g\) and put \[ a_g(h)=ghg^{-1}h^{-1}\in U\qquad(h\in H). \] With \(H\) acting on \(U\) by conjugation, this is a nonabelian one-cocycle. The class \([a_g]\in H^1(H,U)\) is independent of the choice of \(g\) in the left coset \(Ug\). Then \[ \begin{split} \bar g\in\im\bigl(C_G(H)\to G/U\bigr) &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ [a_g]=1\text{ in }H^1(H,U),\\ \bar g\in\im\bigl(C_{\widehat G}(H)\to G/U\bigr) &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ [a_g]=1\text{ in }H^1(H,\widehat U). \end{split} \] Hence centralizer equality is equivalent to triviality of the completion kernel on these \emph{coset obstruction classes}, at every \(U\).

Then restriction induces a canonical isomorphism \[ \ker\bigl(\Out(E)\longrightarrow\Out(H)\bigr) \ \simeq\ C_{\Out(L)}(H). \] The groups carry their profinite automorphism topologies when they are topologically finitely generated.

statement: Explicit periodic braids over the icosahedral action Put \(Z=\Delta_{12}^{2}\), where \(\Delta_{12}=(\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{11})(\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{10}) \cdots(\sigma_1\sigma_2)\sigma_1\) is the Garside half twist in the discrete Artin braid group \(B_{12}\). There are explicit braids \(\beta_2=\Delta_{12}\) and \(\beta_3\) satisfying \[ \beta_2^2=\beta_3^3=Z. \] We specify \(\beta_3\) by listing the indices of its positive letters, in multiplication order: \[ \begin{gathered} 1,11,5,7,10,2,9,3,8,4,2;\\ 7,3,6,2,5,4,3,2,7,10,6;\\ 1,7,9,10,8,5,9,7,2,6,10;\\ 5,4,7,3,5,8,4,2,5,7,6. \end{gathered} \] With \(a=\beta_2\beta_3^{-1}\) and \[ R_{12}=\sigma_{11}\sigma_{10}\cdots\sigma_2\sigma_1^2 \sigma_2\cdots\sigma_{10}\sigma_{11}, \] the stronger Artin-group identity is \[ a^5=Z R_{12}^{-1}. \] Consequently the images in \(B_{12}(S^2)\), where \(R_{12}=1\), satisfy \(a^5=\beta_3^3=(a\beta_3)^2=Z\) and generate the binary icosahedral group of order \(120\). Their mapping-class image is the icosahedral \(A_5\).

statement: The normalizer formulation and its three-coset test Let \(E=\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12],1}\), with the usual completed Birman homomorphism \(p:E\to\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12]}\), and identify \(\widehat B=p^{-1}(A_5)\). statement: The properly typed tripod tests For \(\Phi\in\mathcal H\) and a fixed three-subset \(t\) of the twelve labelled cusps, let \(N_t\trianglelefteq\widehat K\) be the closed normal subgroup generated by all other cusp subgroups. Then restriction and quotient define a continuous homomorphism \[ \mathfrak T_t:\mathcal H\longrightarrow \Out_{\partial}(\widehat K/N_t)\cong\mathcal P. \] The last identification requires an ordered identification of the three surviving cusps with \(0,1,\infty\). We have \(\mathfrak T_t(\mathcal K)=1\) and \(\mathcal K\cap G_{\mathbb Q}=1\), for the specified faithful Galois embedding. statement: The topological quintic resolvent and its distinct quotient types The preimage \(\Gamma_T\leq B\) of an \(A_4\leq A_5\) has signature \((0;2,3,3;\infty)\) and presentation \(C_2*C_3*C_3\). Its degree-five modular map has the model \[ j=t^3(t^2+5t+40),\qquad j-1728=(t-3)(t^2+4t+24)^2. \] The two unramified points above \(j=0\), hence the two order-three orbifold points, are conjugate over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-15})\). Filling either order-three point gives \(C_2*C_3\); filling the order-two point gives \(C_3*C_3\), not \(C_2*C_3\).

statement: The proposed identities on the full Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group B.53 below proves P4's exact quadratic-character domain, both quintic homomorphisms, their arithmetic identity, and the kernel inclusion for $\mathcal K$. Its third map has the corrected weighted-orbifold target $\operatorname{Out}_{\partial}(C_3\amalg C_3)$. B.55 constructs a nonempty set of full R2 lifts $\Phi\in\mathcal H$ for which $\mathfrak T_\pm(\Phi)\ne\Phi$, proving the first assertion of P5. B.57 refutes P7's full common-kernel equality by a separate full central-extension construction. What remains undecided here is the assertion that $\mathfrak T_\pm$ fixes every element of $\widehat{GT}\cap D$. That assertion does not follow from the arithmetic restriction or from a linearized calculation. The exact source distinction is decisive: Nakamura--Schneps, Theorem 1.1 and Definition 1.1, prove their additional relations on the Galois image and use them to define the subgroup \(I\Gamma\); Theorem 1.2 proves that it is a subgroup containing that image \citep{NakamuraSchneps2000}. These statements do not assert that all of \(\GT\) satisfies the new relations. Hoshi--Mochizuki--Tsujimura, Definition 3.3, retain the additional COF and RGC conditions in their BGT framework \citep{HoshiMochizukiTsujimura2025}. Replacing those groups by \(\GT\) would remove a hypothesis. The unresolved requirement is a proof of that replacement, or a concrete element violating the claimed identity, together with its typed restriction maps.

statement: The graded assertion of P7 fails in weight four Over \(\mathbb Q\), the common kernel of the four forgetting maps from outer special derivations of the four-punctured sphere to outer special derivations of three-punctured spheres is strictly larger than the pure braid Lie algebra. In weight four its dimension is six, whereas the braid subspace has dimension three. An explicit element of the difference is given below.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The full group-theoretic equality in P7 is false The common kernel of the three corrected resolvent maps strictly contains \(\mathcal K\). The full counterexample is the nonempty lift set of B.57, whose members induce the identity on all three full filled targets but have a nontrivial tripod action detected by the outer transposition of \(A_9\).
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: An exact list of the 495 cross-ratio pairs Let \(T\leq\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb Q(i))\) be generated by \[ u\longmapsto-u,\qquad u\longmapsto1/u,\qquad u\longmapsto\frac{u+i}{u-i}. \] It is tetrahedral of order twelve. Label its twelve elements in the order of the breadth-first construction in \texttt{code/crossratio\_495.py}, and write \(g_j(u)=(a_ju+b_j)/(c_ju+d_j)\). The ordered tetrahedral parameter curve is \[ S_T=\mathbb P^1\setminus E,\qquad E=\{\infty\}\cup V\bigl(u(u^4-1)(u^8+14u^4+1)\bigr); \] it has fourteen punctures and fundamental group \(F_{13}\). There is an explicit labelling of \[ S_5=\mathbb P^1\setminus\bigl(\{0,\infty\}\cup\mu_5\bigr), \qquad (0,\infty,1,\omega,\ldots,\omega^4, t,t\omega,\ldots,t\omega^4) \] which agrees at an icosahedral basepoint with the tetrahedral labelling. For each increasing four-subset \(q=(i,j,k,l)\), the attached \texttt{data/crossratio\_495.csv} gives the rational functions \(\psi_q:S_T\to M_{0,4}\) and \(\phi_q:S_5\to M_{0,4}\), with that common basepoint. We use the ordered covers: on the unlabelled quotient tripods a fixed four-subset need not be invariant under the label monodromy.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The paired four-point equations have nontrivial discrete solutions There is an explicit nonidentity word \(w\in\pi_1(S_T,u_0)\) such that \[ \psi_{q*}(w)=1=\phi_{q*}(1) \qquad\text{for all }q\in\binom{\{1,\ldots,12\}}4. \] The same equalities hold after full profinite completion. Thus these equations alone do not characterize the icosahedral centralizer: they already admit noncentralizing discrete tetrahedral braids.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The degree-one coprime fixed group and the direction of its lifting Let \(P=\Gamma_{0,12}\) be the pure discrete group, and let \(P^{(\ell)}\) be its pro-\(\ell\) completion. Conjugation by the specified geometric \(A_5\) defines a genuine action on it. For \(\ell\nmid60\), \[ C_{P^{(\ell)}}(A_5)\longrightarrow (P^{(\ell),\mathrm{ab}})^{A_5}\cong\mathbb Z_\ell^2 \] is onto. Thus the fixed group is infinite. Under the continuous geometric outer action on \(\widehat K^{(\ell)}\), every such fixed element has the same relative pro-\(\ell\) outer action as some element of \(\mathcal H\), obtained by R2 for \(U=K\). This asserts lifting to \(\mathcal H\), not lifting to \(C_{\widehat\Gamma}(A_5)=\mathcal K\).
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The sixfold cyclic cover and its multiplicity-free representation Let \(X\) be the smooth compactification of the cyclic cover of the twelve-punctured icosahedral sphere which sends every positive cusp meridian to \(1\in C_6\). Its genus is \(25\). With \(E=\mathbb Q(\zeta_6)=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})\), its primitive-character cohomology has dimension ten over \(E\). The \(A_5\)-representation on it is \[ V=V_1\oplus V_4\oplus V_5, \qquad\dim_E V_i=i, \] where all three constituents are absolutely irreducible and occur once. Its polarization has signature \((1,9)\), with the one-dimensional constituent of one sign and the other two of the opposite sign. The unramified cover is the fibre product defined by \(K\cap B'\leq B\). This is a congruence subgroup of exact level thirty, and \(B/(K\cap B')\cong A_5\times C_6\).
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: Three ordinary linear characters do not exist on the stated full domain Lead 7's construction does not give three ordinary unit-valued characters on every element of \(\{\Phi\in\GTzero:\lambda\equiv\pm1\pmod5\}\). Complex conjugation, which belongs to that domain, exchanges the two primitive sixth-root eigenspaces. On a single \(E\)-module its action is semilinear. The valid scalar constructions must first restrict to \(\lambda\equiv1\pmod6\), or have a semilinear target and a crossed multiplication law.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The real compact torus and its congruence centralizer Write \(\mathcal O_E=\mathbb Z[\zeta_6]\) and let \(\Lambda\) be the rank-ten Eisenstein lattice of the twelve-equal-weight Deligne--Mostow representation. Its projective arithmetic group is the projectivization of \(\Aut(\Lambda)\), with Hermitian signature \((1,9)\). The algebraic centralizer of the icosahedral image in the projective unitary group is the \(\mathbb Q\)-torus \[ T=\bigl(\operatorname{Res}^{,1}_{E/\mathbb Q}\mathbb G_m\bigr)^3 /\operatorname{Res}^{,1}_{E/\mathbb Q}\mathbb G_m, \] the denominator embedded diagonally. It has dimension two and is compact over \(\mathbb R\). For \(\ell\nmid30\), put \(U_\ell^1=\{u\in(\mathcal O_E\otimes\mathbb Z_\ell)^\times: u\bar u=1\}\). The centralizer in the local congruence closure is the projective image of \[ \left\{(u_1,u_4,u_5)\in(U_\ell^1)^3: u_1u_4^4u_5^5\in\mu_3\right\}. \tag{B.23.1} \] In particular it is infinite. This is a computation in the congruence quotient of the lattice, not in \(\widehat\Gamma\).
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The exact lifting obstruction and the four-point control Let \(\rho:\widehat\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow L\) be any specified compact quotient, put \(N=\ker\rho\), and suppose \(A_5\) embeds in \(L\). For \(t\in C_L(A_5)\), choose \(g\in\widehat\Gamma\) lifting it and define \[ a_t(h)=ghg^{-1}h^{-1}\in N\qquad(h\in A_5). \] Then \([a_t]\in H^1(A_5,N)\) is independent of the chosen lift, and \(t\) lifts to \(\mathcal K\) if and only if \([a_t]=1\). This applies to every element of (B.23.1). At four points the analogous discrepancy can be computed fully: in the modular quotient \(\widehat{C_2*C_3}\), the centralizer of the geometric \(C_3\) is just \(C_3\), whereas its congruence centralizer contains a one-dimensional norm-one torus. Precisely the three elements of \(C_3\) have trivial lifting obstruction in that quotient.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: Solvable triangular controls and levels three and four For a finite solvable geometric group \(G\leq\Gamma_{0,[n]}\), the independently proved normalizer comparison, together with B.2, gives the centralizer comparison. If its punctured quotient is a triangle orbifold, the discrete normalizer modulo deck transformations is finite. The pure part of its completed centralizer is therefore trivial. In particular the tetrahedral and octahedral groups give \(\mathcal K_3=\mathcal K_4=1\). At six equal-weight points the octahedral representation has a two-summand scalar commutant and an infinite compact local torus, although only the identity can lift from that torus to the full geometric centralizer.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The arithmetic local calculation does not decide the global centralizer For twelve points we have not determined which elements of (B.23.1) have trivial class in \(H^1(A_5,\ker(\widehat\Gamma\to L_\ell))\). Neither compactness at the real place nor strong approximation computes this nonabelian cohomology set. Thus Lead 6's infinite congruence centralizer is verified, but it proves neither \(\mathcal K=1\) nor its negation. The formulas at \(\ell\mid30\) need integral representations with their nonsplit isotypic lattices; the good-prime decomposition has not been extended to those primes in this return.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The remaining arithmetic-character calculations The normalized Jacobi-sum values on \(G_{\mathbb Q(\zeta_{15})}\), the values for the R2 lifts at \(U=K\) and level thirty, and vanishing on \(\mathcal K\) remain undecided. B.21 supplies the cover and the precise rational representation; B.22 corrects the domains, the deck ambiguity, and the integral projector issue before any such calculation is meaningful. Since no vanishing has been proved, the proposed implication to the two Fibonacci representations has not been used.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The pure tetrahedral and cyclic intersection Put $P=P\Gamma_{0,12}$, choose the named $T=A_4$ and $D=C_5$ inside the geometric $A_5$, and put \[ H_T=C_P(T),\qquad H_5=C_P(D). \] In the full profinite completion of the pure mapping class group, \[ \mathcal K=C_{\widehat P}(A_5) =\widehat{H_T}\cap\widehat{H_5},\qquad H_T\simeq F_{13},\quad H_5\simeq F_6, \qquad H_T\cap H_5=1. \] Both displayed completions are their actual embedded closures in $\widehat P$. The ordered parameter curves and their basepoint choices are those of B.18. In particular the equality is an intersection in one specified ambient group, not an abstract intersection of two unrelated free profinite groups.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The precise arithmetic normalizer restriction Let $X/k$ be a smooth affine hyperbolic curve over a number field, with geometric fundamental group $F=\pi_1(X_{\overline k})$ and arithmetic fundamental group $E=\pi_1(X)$. Let $1\ne A\leq F$ be closed and procyclic, and suppose that a closed subgroup $N\leq E$ normalizes $A$ and has image $G_L\leq G_k$, with $L/k$ finite. For a finite Galois extension $M/\mathbb Q$ containing $L$, let $\mathcal P_M$ be the rational primes unramified in $M$ whose Frobenius class is the class of a complex conjugation in $\operatorname{Gal}(M/\mathbb Q)$. Then either $A$ is contained in a unique cusp inertia group, or \[ A_\ell=1\quad(\ell\in\mathcal P_M). \tag{B.29.1} \] Consequently cofinite prime support implies cuspidality. If $L$ is totally real, every such $A$ is cuspidal, without a prime-support condition. These are cuspidality conclusions, not nonexistence conclusions in an arbitrary curve group.
depends_on: Stix Theorem20 and Proposition11/Corollaries12–13; Serre local algebraicity; explicit descent
notes: Repairs missing N←AN step; corrects LM6A14 citation; cuspidality rather than nonexistence; all primes if normalizer field totally real.

statement: The tetrahedral centralizer has its full profinite topology Let $T=A_4$ act on the twelve vertices and put $F_T=C_{\Gamma_{0,[12]}}(T)$. The natural map \[ \widehat{F_T}\longrightarrow\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12]} \tag{B.30.1} \] is injective, and its image is exactly $C_{\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12]}}(T)$. In particular $F_T\simeq F_2$ gives $\overline{F_T}\simeq\widehat F_2$, and the pure subgroup $F_T\cap\Gamma_{0,12}\simeq F_{13}$ also has its full profinite topology induced from the ambient mapping class group.
depends_on: Boggi2026 §§3.1–3.2 restricted to p-groups; BZ2025TheoremA; V4/C3 induction; finite-extension topology
notes: Reaudits LM4F7.4–6; separate completion embedding and centralizer density; no nonsolvable intersection equality.

statement: A totally real arithmetic model at the icosahedral point For the tetrahedral action generated by \[ u\longmapsto-u,\qquad u\longmapsto1/u, \qquad u\longmapsto\frac{u+i}{u-i}, \] the curve of unlabelled free orbits is the $\mathbb Q$-curve \[ C_T=\mathbb P^1_v\setminus\{\infty,6\sqrt{-3},-6\sqrt{-3}\}, \qquad v=\frac{u^{12}-33u^8-33u^4+1}{u^2(u^4-1)^2}. \tag{B.31.1} \] In the embedding used for the cross-ratio computation, the icosahedral point is $v_0=-22\sqrt5/5\in C_T(\mathbb Q(\sqrt5))$. The injection \[ \pi_1(C_{T,\overline{\mathbb Q}},\overline v_0) \simeq\widehat F_2\longrightarrow\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12]} \tag{B.31.2} \] has image $\overline{F_T}$. For the actual Galois action defined by the rational point $v_0$ and its image family, $\mathcal K\leq\overline{F_T}$ is stable under the full group $G_{\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)}$.
notes: Unlabelled curve overQ, v0=−22√5/5; actual full G_Q√5 normalization via rational-point section and family, not unspecified open subgroup.

statement: No tetrahedral cusp inertia meets the icosahedral kernel For every cusp inertia group $I$ of $\pi_1(C_{T,\overline{\mathbb Q}},\overline v_0)$, including every conjugate inertia group, \[ I\cap\mathcal K=1. \tag{B.32.1} \] The statement concerns the whole $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ inertia, including subgroups supported at one prime.
depends_on: B.30–31; BZ2025TheoremA atC5; rigid7-subset forgetting; local ramification
notes: Every conjugate inertia and arbitrary prime-supported exponent excluded. Five-point/H1 tests alone miss antipodal-pair partition.

statement: The abelian case of Lead 8 and the cofinite-support exclusion For the actual subgroup $\mathcal K$ of the question, \[ \mathcal K\text{ abelian} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal K=1. \tag{B.33.1} \] Moreover $\mathcal K$ has no nontrivial closed procyclic subgroup with open arithmetic normalizer on $C_T$ and nonzero pro-$p$ component at all but finitely many rational primes. The same exclusion holds with arbitrary prime support if the normalizer projects onto the Galois group of a totally real number field.
depends_on: B.29–B.32; abelian subgroups of free profinite groups
notes: Actual K abelian⇒K=1. Cofinite-support procyclic subgroup with open arithmetic normalizer cannot lie inK. Does not prove K abelian.

statement: The missing commutativity assertion in Lead 8 It remains undecided here whether $\mathcal K$ is abelian. No two noncommuting elements of $\mathcal K$ have been constructed either. B.33 proves that this is equivalent, for this particular group, to the unresolved assertion $\mathcal K=1$. The arithmetic restriction supplies no way to extract from an arbitrary nonabelian $G_{\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)}$-stable closed subgroup of $\widehat F_2$ a nontrivial procyclic subgroup with open arithmetic normalizer. A chosen element's procyclic closure need not have an open stabilizer. Similarly, projecting $\mathcal K$ to a pro-$p$ or metabelian quotient does not establish commutativity in the full group. These are the exact remaining steps in the two arithmetic approaches attempted here. The finite cross-ratio and rigid-subconfiguration tests in the other subsections impose necessary constraints but do not repair this inference.
depends_on: B.33; necessary finite and rigid-subconfiguration tests
notes: Neither commutativity nor two noncommuting full elements established; arithmetic stability does not give open normalizer of a chosen cyclic closure.

statement: A sufficient product-separability condition with its quantifiers Let $G$ be residually finite and $H,J\leq G$. Suppose that for every finite-index normal subgroup $U\trianglelefteq G$ the product $(H\cap U)(J\cap U)$ is closed in the profinite topology of $G$. Then \[ \overline H\cap\overline J=\overline{H\cap J} \quad\hbox{inside }\widehat G. \] Applied to $H_T,H_5$ in B.28, this condition would prove $\mathcal K=1$. B.52 proves the unrefined product $H_TH_5$ is closed. The refined condition above remains unresolved; B.46--B.49 and B.52 explain exactly why the unrefined result does not yet establish it.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

The torsion-centralizer comparisons in LM7\_PUSH E.64 are cyclic-factor comparisons; its sewing comparison uses the specified twist stabilizer and genus-two congruence identification. ANABELIAN\_149\_PUSH A.29l uses the separate orbifold theorem of Boggi--Zalesskii (2019), Lemma 3.1. None of these passages uses the unproved nonsolvable closure-intersection equality in B.1.

statement: The level-six control also has trivial residual kernel For $N=2,3,4,6$, the group $\mathcal K_N$ of task B.5 is trivial. For $N=6$ this uses the full profinite mapping class group of the genus-one curve $Y(6)$ with its twelve cusps; it is not a prime-by-prime linear computation.

statement: The remaining congruence levels No determination of $\mathcal K_N$ for all $N$ is obtained here. In particular $\mathcal K_5=1$ is the main unresolved assertion, and the corresponding level-seven and level-eleven kernels remain undecided. Their quotient compactifications have genera three and twenty-six, respectively. An index-seven or index-eleven resolvent alone supplies neither an injective comparison back to the original group nor a simultaneous lifting theorem inside the profinite mapping class group. For levels with higher genus one must additionally distinguish the image in the loop-outer group from the abstract full mapping class completion and its congruence kernel. Even when $N\mid M$, this paper does not assert $\mathcal K_M\subseteq\mathcal K_N$ without proving the required equivariant profinite covering-descent comparison.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The nonsolvable direction and the published assertions For a finite solvable subgroup of a genus-zero mapping class group, the centralizer is the closure of the discrete centralizer, by the prime-power normalizer induction in B.30 and the open-kernel argument B.2. This proves the solvable direction of the refined triangle-orbifold statement in task B.6. For $A_5$ on twelve vertices the reverse direction would assert $\mathcal K\ne1$, which remains undecided. Accordingly Conjecture $2^-$ is not proved or refuted here. Neither Boggi's Proposition 2.4 and Theorem C(iii), nor Boggi--Zalesskii's Theorem 5.1(iii), is refuted by this audit. Their nonsolvable centralizer conclusions remain unsupported by the displayed proofs at the step B.1 isolates. Boggi's Theorem A in its general ramified nonsolvable case also retains the missing input in Lemma 3.2, where the configuration-group centralizer is identified using Proposition 2.4. The free-action proof in Section 3.1 and the prime-power repairs above do not use that missing step. For a particular action whose discrete centralizer is already trivial, its own congruence property is tautological; that observation does not prove the general ramified theorem or the ambient profinite centralizer comparison.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The complete relative images and the bad-prime refinements remain undetermined B.20 proves the stated coprime pro-$\ell$ invariant construction and a lift to the full peripheral group. It does not determine the full relative images requested at $U=K$ or at $U=K'K^p$ for $p=2,3,5$. Membership in the actual profinite mapping class image is equivalently the normalizer or three-coset equation in B.9. B.54 now constructs relative data at $U=K$, at the good prime seven, for which every full peripheral R2 lift has a nontrivial tripod action. None is a braid lift. Thus the universal assertion that R2 can always be carried out inside that braid image is false. This obstruction does not classify the two complete relative images or their intersection, nor their compatibility over finer characteristic levels. No computation in this paper suppresses the primes $2,3,5$ or upgrades coprime invariant lifting to those primes.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: Parity and further-orbit lifting in the hypothetical nontrivial kernel If $\mathcal K\ne1$, neither the restriction of $\Delta$ to all its elements nor its extension along every required icosahedral marked-orbit locus has been determined. The latter extension would have to be constructed with compatible based maps and then checked against the pentagon; it does not follow from centralization of $A_5$ at one level. B.10 does prove that a nonidentity element of $\mathcal K$ which also satisfied the pentagon would lie outside the Galois image. No such element or complete lifting chain is constructed here. This conditional implication is retained without using it as evidence that either hypothesis holds.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: A nontrivial arithmetic ambiguity in every E.58 lift Put $H_0=F'F^3\trianglelefteq\widehat B$ and \[ R_{\rm sol}=\bigcap_{G_{\mathbb Q}\twoheadrightarrow D, \ D\ \mathrm{finite\ solvable}}\ker(G_{\mathbb Q}\to D). \] This is a nontrivial closed subgroup of $G_{\mathbb Q}$. For every $\sigma\in R_{\rm sol}$, the normalized modular automorphism induced by $\sigma$ has multiplier one and is the identity on $\widehat B/R_{\rm nil}(H_0)$. Its two canonical pure accessory frames have image one in this same relative quotient. Consequently right multiplication by any such $\sigma$ preserves every prescribed relative automorphism and relative frame coordinate in the construction of LM7\_PUSH E.58, including its finite modulo-twelve frame classes.

notes: Prosolvable Galois residual kills exact relative automorphism and frame data; includes signed modulo12 frames through2-relative quotient. No CM assertion for X12.

statement: A finite simple group excluded uniformly from these relative levels Let $S=A_{10000}$. No subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_d(\mathbb F_p)$, for $d\leq97$ and any prime $p$, has $S$ as a quotient of a subgroup. Consequently every finite section of a closed subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(\widehat F_d^{(p)})$ also avoids $S$.

statement: A simultaneous nontrivial arithmetic kernel for both lifting data Let $N_{12}=\ker(\widehat B\to \operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z/12)/\{\pm I\})$. There is a nontrivial closed subgroup $Z\leq G_{\mathbb Q}$ with multiplier one whose normalized automorphisms and both canonical accessory frames are the identity at every relative pro-$p$ level over $H_0$ and over $N_{12}$, simultaneously. Thus it kills the whole relative pronilpotent source and the specified relative frame coordinates in both LM7\_PUSH E.58 and LM7 D.46.

statement: The relative prescriptions leave all tripod and corrected resolvent values undetermined Fix any actual full lift $\Phi$ allowed by LM7\_PUSH E.58, or by R2 applied to the specified relative action and frames of LM7 D.46. For the subgroup $Z$ of B.44, every $\Phi\sigma$, $\sigma\in Z$, is another allowed lift with the same relative data. For every three-subset $t$ of the icosahedral cusps, the map \[ Z\longrightarrow\mathcal P, \qquad \sigma\longmapsto \mathfrak T_t(\Phi\sigma) \tag{B.45.1} \] is injective. The same is true of $\sigma\mapsto\mathfrak R(\Phi\sigma)$ for each of the three typed resolvent homomorphisms $\mathfrak R$ constructed in B.53: the first two have target $\widehat{GT}_0$, and the third has the peripheral outer automorphism group of $C_3\amalg C_3$ as its target. Thus neither existential construction specifies a single value of any tripod test or of any of these corrected resolvent maps. At most one element of the coset $\Phi Z$ can belong to $\mathcal K$.
depends_on: B.10; B.44; B.53; exact frame composition law; degree-three root-stack cover
notes: Every specified lift has an admissible arithmetic coset with injectively varying values of every tripod test and all three typed resolvents. At most one member inK. No existence inK or identification of the common kernel is asserted.

statement: The exact refined-product criterion For subgroups $H,J$ of a residually finite group $G$, the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $HJ$ is closed in the profinite topology of $G$, and $\overline H\cap\overline J=\overline{H\cap J}$ in $\widehat G$; \item for every finite-index subgroup $L\leq G$ containing $H\cap J$, the subset $(H\cap L)J$ is closed in that topology. \end{enumerate} This is \citet[Theorem 1.1]{DE_Minasyan2023}; its proof is Proposition 2.4 together with Proposition 3.1. For the actual $P,H_T,H_5$ of B.28, it gives the equivalence \[ \left\{\begin{array}{c} H_TH_5\text{ is closed in }P,\\ \mathcal K=1 \end{array}\right. \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (H_T\cap L)H_5\text{ is closed in }P \quad\text{for every }L\leq_f P. \] Equivalently, every product $H_0J_0$ is closed for finite-index $H_0\leq H_T$ and $J_0\leq H_5$. The quantifier over refinements cannot in general be omitted.
notes: Includes independent proof for trivial discrete intersection; one unrefined product is not enough.

statement: A closed product with a nontrivial profinite intersection Let $V=M_2(\mathbb Z)$ additively, let $S=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ act on $V$ by left multiplication, and put \[ G=V\rtimes S, \qquad H=\{(0,B):B\in S\}, \qquad J=(I,1)H(I,1)^{-1}. \] Then $G$ is residually finite, $H\cap J=1$, and $HJ$ is closed in the full profinite topology of $G$. Both factors have the full induced profinite topology; every finite-index subgroup of either factor is separable in $G$. Nevertheless \[ \overline H\cap\overline J \cong\ker\bigl(\widehat{\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)} \longrightarrow\mathrm{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb Z})\bigr) \ne1. \] In fact this intersection has a quotient isomorphic to $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb F_8)$. This is the example of \citet[Example 4.1]{DE_Minasyan2023}, with the failure witnessed here by an explicit finite quotient. It is a counterexample to the general implication from one closed product to equality of intersections. It is not a counterexample to the icosahedral assertion.
notes: Full semidirect-product topology proved; all finite-index factor subgroups individually separable; not a counterexample for the actual icosahedral centralizer. The failure also persists in the torsion-free ambient subgroup M2(Z) semidirect Gamma(3), with both factors free of rank three.

statement: The hypotheses of the recent separability criteria Put $\Pi=\pi_1(S^2\setminus V_{12})\cong F_{11}$ and use the faithful Dehn--Nielsen map $P\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}(\Pi)$. For $H\leq P$, write \[ \widetilde H=\{\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Pi): [\alpha]\in H\}. \] If $\widetilde H$ is conjugacy separable, then $H$ is separable in $\operatorname{Out}(\Pi)$, and therefore in $P$. This is the exact specialization of \cite[Corollary D]{DE_FournierFacio2025}. For $H=H_T,H_5$ the preimages are, after choosing lifts of free bases, $F_{11}\rtimes F_{13}$ and $F_{11}\rtimes F_6$. The cited criterion concerns individual subgroups and does not assert closure of their products.
notes: Multitwists rule out convex cocompactness; no suitable relative-hyperbolic or central-extension ambient comparison proved for products.

statement: A finite-action reformulation of every refined product Retain the fixed embedding $\iota:A_5\hookrightarrow \Gamma=\Gamma_{0,[12]}$, with the generating subgroups $T=A_4$ and $D=C_5$, and identify them with their images. Let $L\leq_f P$ and $g\in P$. Then $g$ belongs to the closure of $(H_T\cap L)H_5$ in $\widehat P$ if and only if there are a monomorphism $\iota_g:A_5\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ and $u\in\overline L\leq\widehat P$ satisfying \[ \iota_g(t)=t\quad(t\in T),\qquad \iota_g(d)=g d g^{-1}\quad(d\in D),\qquad \iota_g(a)=u a u^{-1}\quad(a\in A_5). \] The monomorphism, when it exists, is unique from its first two prescriptions. For such a monomorphism, \[ g\in(H_T\cap L)H_5 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \iota_g=h\iota h^{-1}\text{ for some }h\in L. \] Consequently the refined closure condition in B.46 is exactly the following assertion, for all $L$ and $g$: every displayed homomorphism conjugacy realized in $\overline L$ is realized in $L$. This is simultaneous conjugacy of homomorphisms, with the restrictions on $T$ and $D$ retained.

statement: The actual regional boundary subgroup is a fully embedded profinite free product, with an exact discrete and completed neck intersection \label{stmt:B118} Use the actual annular regional marking of B.112--B.114, before the two additional cross relations. Write \[ B=CbC,\qquad z=Ch,\qquad f=hk^{-1}=Czk^{-1}, \qquad K=F(a,B,d,e,f)\leq R. \] Let $c=aCa^{-1}$ be the selected upper-gap cone, and put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B118-marked-boundary} P=P_5=O_1O_2O_3O_4O_5=aBfde,\qquad T=cP=abzde k^{-1},\qquad H=\langle c,k,T\rangle\leq R. \end{equation} Then the indicated generators give an isomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B118-H} H\cong C_2(c)*\mathbb Z^2(k,T), \end{equation} and $H$ has its full induced profinite topology in $R$. The actual neck intersection is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B118-intersections} K\cap H=\langle P\rangle,\qquad \widehat K\cap\widehat H =\overline{\langle P\rangle}\quad\text{inside }\widehat R. \end{equation} Here the hats are full profinite completions embedded by the proved induced-topology comparisons. This is a comparison with the isolated corner: no embedding after the remaining regional or mirror relations, and no properness assertion for an additional profinite amalgam, is included in the theorem.

statement: The actual one-neck ordinary group has a complete thirteen-generator presentation, and its eight-family filling has exactly the actual free-two fixed source in both full categories \label{stmt:B119} Let $\mathcal G=G_{\rm ann}$ be the actual orbifold group of B.114, over the two complete annuli joined through the first regular neck. Use its actual common disk marking $K=F(a,B,d,e,f)$, actual selected gap cones $c=c_-$ and $\tau=c_+$, and actual far-section loops $m=k_-$, $p=k_+$. Let $\mathcal G^0$ be the ordinary index-two subgroup: $c,\tau$ are odd and $K,m,p$ are even. Put \[ \widetilde u=cuc\quad(u=a,B,d,e,f),\qquad g=\widetilde f,\qquad x=\tau c. \] Then $\mathcal G^0$ has the following complete marked presentation: thirteen generators \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-thirteen} a,B,d,e,f,\ \widetilde a,\widetilde B,\widetilde d, \widetilde e,g,\ m,p,x, \end{equation} and the sixty-four regional relators specified by the explicit two-sheet rewriting scheme in the proof. The two cross commutators are eliminated by exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-cross-elimination} cmc=x^{-1}mx,\qquad cpc=p. \end{equation} No regional relator or signed base-loop consequence is discarded. Let $\mathcal N$ be the ordinary normal closure of the eight actual deleted-family meridians \[ a,B,d,e,\widetilde a,\widetilde B,\widetilde d,\widetilde e, \] and let $Q^0=\mathcal G^0/\mathcal N$ be the actual filling of both families. Then there is an exact marked isomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-filled-semidirect} Q^0=F(f,g,x)\rtimes F(m,p), \end{equation} where conjugation by $m,p$ acts on the free fiber by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-base-actions} \begin{array}{c|ccc} &f&g&x\\ \hline \alpha_m&f^{-1}gf&f&xg^{-1}f\\ \alpha_p&fxgx^{-1}f^{-1}&gx^{-1}fxg^{-1}&fxg^{-1}. \end{array} \end{equation} The six actual positive source generators from B.114 map, in their actual order, to \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-source-images} 1,\ 1,\ 1,\ 1,\ v=f^{-1}p,\ m. \end{equation} Write $S=\langle m,v\rangle\leq Q^0$. Then $S\cong F_2$ is an actual source splitting of the geometric base projection, and conjugation $\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)$ satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-fixed-equalities} (Q^0)^\delta=S, \qquad (\widehat{Q^0})^\delta=\widehat S. \end{equation} All completions are full profinite completions, and $S$ has its full induced topology. Equivalently, for the filled orbifold group $Q=Q^0\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle$, \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-orbifold-centralizers} C_Q(\tau)=S\times\langle\tau\rangle, \qquad C_{\widehat Q}(\tau)=\widehat S\times\langle\tau\rangle. \end{equation} These are assertions about the actual eight-family filling. They do not give a splitting back into $\mathcal G^0$, a fixed-element lift through $\mathcal N$, or a centralizer formula for the family-unfilled one-neck group.

statement: The actual boundary amalgam has a proper full completion, an exact discrete free-six cone centralizer, and a fully embedded carrier for the four remaining prefix relations \label{stmt:B120} Use the actual regional marking of B.112, B.114 and B.118. To distinguish the adapted cone from the selected upper-gap cone, write \[ \bar x=CxC,\quad B=CbC,\quad z=Ch,\quad f=hk^{-1},\quad K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\quad c=aCa^{-1}. \] The actual physical neck basis and its prefixes are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-prefixes} \begin{gathered} (O_1,O_2,O_3,O_4,O_5) =(aBa^{-1},a,fde d^{-1}f^{-1},d,d^{-1}fd),\\ P_i=O_1\cdots O_i,\qquad P=P_5=aBfde,\qquad T=cP. \end{gathered} \end{equation} In particular $P_1,\ldots,P_5$ are a free basis of the actual $K$. Let $R$ be the whole regional group, including every annular node relation and the retained zero-loop action. By B.118 its actual boundary subgroup is \[ H=\langle c,k,T\rangle=C_2(c)*\mathbb Z^2(k,T),\qquad K\cap H=\langle P\rangle, \] and $H$ and $K$ have their full induced topology in $R$, with $\widehat K\cap\widehat H=\overline{\langle P\rangle}$ there. Put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-corner-amalgam} \begin{split} W_{\partial}&=\langle D,u,k,j\mid D^2=j^2=1, \ [k,D]=[k,u]=1,\ juj=u^{-1}\rangle,\\ M&=R*_{H}W_{\partial}, \end{split} \end{equation} where the corner edge map is $c\mapsto jDj$, $T\mapsto uD$, and $k\mapsto k$. Both are the actual embedded edge maps of B.118. Then the full completion is a proper profinite amalgam: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-full-completion} \widehat M\cong \widehat R\amalg_{\widehat H}\widehat{W_{\partial}}. \end{equation} Here both vertex completions, and hence the indicated edge completion, inject. Let $L\cong F_5$ be the actual selected regional source in $R$, so that $C_R(c)=L\times\langle c\rangle$ by B.112 after the specified conjugation by $a$. With $k'=jkj$ one has the exact \emph{discrete} formulas \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-discrete-centralizers} \begin{aligned} C_M(c)&=(L*\langle k'\rangle)\times\langle c\rangle \cong F_6\times C_2,\\ C_M(D)&=(jLj*\langle k\rangle)\times\langle D\rangle. \end{aligned} \end{equation} The full actual mirror extension $X$ of the annular one-neck group is precisely \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-final-quotient} X=M/\langle\!\langle(jP_i)^2:\ 1\leq i\leq4\rangle\!\rangle. \end{equation} The four relations lie in the genuinely embedded subgroup \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-carrier} J_0=\langle K,j\rangle =F(w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4)*C_2(j)*C_2(jP_5),\qquad w_i=jP_i. \end{equation} This carrier has its full induced topology in $M$, so its full completion also embeds in $\widehat M$. The six words identified below are actual source prelifts in the free factor of $C_M(D)$; their images under \eqref{eq:B120-final-quotient} are the six original based source words. Neither a centralizer formula in $\widehat M$ nor survival of these source generators after the four relations is asserted.

statement: The actual six-cone mirror neck is a retract of an original-parity index-two subgroup after all four final relations; its free-five neck is a retract in the ordinary annular group \label{stmt:B121} Keep the whole actual marking and intermediate group $M$ of B.120. In particular $C$ is the adapted regional cone, $c=aCa^{-1}$ is the selected gap cone, $K=F(a,B,d,e,f)$ with $B=CbC$, and $P_i=O_1\cdots O_i$ are the actual five prefixes. Let \begin{equation}\label{eq:B121-actual-quotient} X=M/\langle\!\langle(jP_i)^2:\ 1\leq i\leq4\rangle\!\rangle, \qquad Q=K\rtimes_\eta C_2(j) =\mathop{*}_{i=0}^{5}C_2(r_i), \quad r_0=j,\ r_i=jP_i. \end{equation} The canonical homomorphism $\iota:Q\to X$ comes from the actual neck and mirror, with every remaining relation imposed. Let $\varepsilon:X\to C_2$ be the original ordinary-cover character, extended by $\varepsilon(j)=0$, so $\varepsilon(C)=1$ and it vanishes on the ordinary regional generators. Let $\mu:X\to C_2$ be mirror parity, zero on $R$ and one on $j$. Write \[ X^0=\ker\varepsilon,\qquad \Gamma=\ker\mu,\qquad \Gamma^0=\ker\mu\cap\ker\varepsilon. \] Thus $\Gamma$ is the actual annular one-neck orbifold group and $\Gamma^0$ is its actual ordinary double cover. The two characters are distinct. There is a literal retraction \begin{equation}\label{eq:B121-retractions} \mathcal R:X^0\longrightarrow Q, \qquad \mathcal R\iota=1_Q, \qquad \mu|_Q\circ\mathcal R=\mu|_{X^0}. \end{equation} In particular $\iota$ is injective. Restricting this retraction along mirror parity gives a retraction \begin{equation}\label{eq:B121-ordinary-neck-retract} \mathcal R|_{\Gamma^0}:\Gamma^0\longrightarrow K, \qquad \mathcal R|_K=1_K. \end{equation} Consequently $Q$ has its full induced profinite topology in $X$ and $K$ has its full induced profinite topology in $\Gamma^0$ and $\Gamma$. The natural full completions therefore embed: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B121-completed-embeddings} \widehat Q\hookrightarrow\widehat X, \qquad \widehat K\hookrightarrow\widehat{\Gamma^0} \hookrightarrow\widehat\Gamma. \end{equation} This is a statement about the actual final quotient. It does not assert that either regional vertex embeds after the final relations, or that the source image is free, or that a selected-cone centralizer is exhausted by the source.

statement: The selected-cone centralizer in the full completion of the intermediate boundary amalgam is exactly the closure of its actual discrete source centralizer \label{stmt:B122} Use the complete marked intermediate group of B.120, \[ M=R*_{H}W_{\partial},\qquad H=C_2(c)*\mathbb Z^2(k,T),\qquad c=aCa^{-1}, \] with the actual selected regional source $L\cong F_5$ and \[ \begin{gathered} W_{\partial}=\langle D,u,k,j\mid D^2=j^2=1, [k,D]=[k,u]=1,\ juj=u^{-1}\rangle,\\ c=jDj,\qquad T=uD,\qquad k'=jkj. \end{gathered} \] All completions below are full profinite completions embedded by the proved induced-topology comparisons. Closures are taken in $\widehat M$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B122-closure-centralizers} \begin{aligned} C_{\widehat M}(c) &=\overline{C_M(c)} =\overline{\langle L,k',c\rangle},\\ C_{\widehat M}(D) &=\overline{C_M(D)} =\overline{\langle jLj,k,D\rangle}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Thus the completed centralizer contains no elements beyond the closure of the actual discrete centralizer from B.120. This is a closure equality. It does not assert that the full completion of $F_6\times C_2$ embeds under its discrete centralizer map, or that the completed centralizer is a free profinite amalgam. The four remaining prefix relations defining the actual final group are not imposed in this statement.

statement: The whole ordinary one-neck group has an exact free-eleven, two-source-operator presentation, and its fixed-source question reduces to the actual family kernel in both categories \label{stmt:B123} Use the actual common marking of B.114 and B.119: \[ K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\qquad c=c_-,\qquad \tau=c_+,\qquad m=k_-,\quad p=k_+. \] The two cones are odd and the other generators are ordinary. Let \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-generic-fiber} E_0=K*C_2(c)*C_2(\tau),\qquad F=\ker(E_0\longrightarrow C_2). \end{equation} Then $F$ is the actual free group of rank eleven, with marked basis \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-free-eleven} a,B,d,e,f,\ cac,cBc,cdc,cec,g=cfc,\ x=\tau c. \end{equation} There are two explicitly specified automorphisms $\alpha_m,\alpha_v$ of $F$, defined below by the complete regional markings and partial inner automorphisms. There is a finite list $\mathcal A$ of \emph{forty} marked words, namely both ordinary sheets of all twenty regional node words. Put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-whole-closure} \begin{gathered} S=F(m,v),\qquad N=\left\langle\!\left\langle \alpha_s(r):r\in\mathcal A,\ s\in S \right\rangle\!\right\rangle_F,\qquad W=F/N. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Here $s$ ranges over \emph{every signed word} in $m,v$, with $\alpha_s(w)=sws^{-1}$; no bound on its length is imposed. There is an exact marked isomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-actual-splitting} \mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}=W\rtimes S. \end{equation} The actual fifth source word is $v$, and its sixth source word is $m$. The four contact source words give explicit elements $s_1,\ldots,s_4\in W$. Their full image is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-source-orbit} H=I\rtimes S,\qquad I=\left\langle\alpha_s(s_i):s\in S,\ 1\leq i\leq4\right\rangle \leq W. \end{equation} The brackets defining $I$ denote a subgroup, not an ambient normal closure. Conjugation $\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)$ preserves $W$ and fixes $S$ pointwise. Let $J=\ker(W\to F(f,g,x))$ be the actual eight-family filling kernel. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-discrete-gate} (\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann})^\delta=W^\delta\rtimes S, \qquad W^\delta=J^\delta,\qquad (\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann})^\delta=H \ \Longleftrightarrow\ J^\delta=I. \end{equation} There are also exact full-completion comparisons \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-compact-gate} \begin{gathered} \widehat{\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}}=\widehat W\rtimes\widehat S, \qquad \widehat W=\widehat F/\overline N,\qquad \overline H=\overline I\rtimes\widehat S,\\ \bigl(\widehat{\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}}\bigr)^\delta =\widehat W^{\,\delta}\rtimes\widehat S, \qquad \widehat W^{\,\delta}=\overline J^{\,\delta},\\ \bigl(\widehat{\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}}\bigr)^\delta=\overline H \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \overline J^{\,\delta}=\overline I, \qquad \overline J=\ker\bigl(\widehat W\to\widehat{F(f,g,x)}\bigr). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Here $\overline N$ is the closure of $N$ in $\widehat F$; $\overline I$ is the closure of the discrete actual source-orbit subgroup in $\widehat W$; and $\overline H$ is the image of the completed actual source. The notation $\overline J$ means the displayed actual closed kernel. No identification of it with $\widehat J$, or of $\overline N$ with $\widehat N$, is asserted. The equalities $J^\delta=I$ and $\overline J^{\,\delta}=\overline I$ remain open.
