statement: The actual outer five-source factor is a retract after all final relations, and the complete actual source has free abelianization of rank six \label{stmt:B124} Let $\Gamma^0$ be the actual ordinary annular one-neck group of B.119--B.123, after all regional node, cross and prefix relations. Use its six based positive source loops \[ (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4,v,m) \] from B.123, with $s_i$ the four contact loops, $v$ the outer annular source loop and $m$ the inner source loop. Let \[ L_+=\langle s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4,v\rangle,\qquad H_{\mathrm{src}}=\langle L_+,m\rangle\leq\Gamma^0. \] Then the displayed five generators freely generate $L_+\cong F_5$, and there is an actual retraction \begin{equation}\label{eq:B124-source-retract} \rho_+:\Gamma^0\longrightarrow L_+, \qquad \rho_+(s_i)=s_i, \quad\rho_+(v)=v,\quad\rho_+(m)=1. \end{equation} In particular $L_+$ has its full induced profinite topology in $\Gamma^0$ and in the actual orbifold group $\Gamma$ containing $\Gamma^0$ with index two. Let $\iota:F_6\to\Gamma^0$ be the actual source map and let $p_{\mathrm{out}}:F_6\to F_5$ kill $m$, while $p_{\mathrm{base}}:F_6\to F(v,m)$ kills the four contacts. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B124-kernel-bounds} \ker\iota\subseteq\ker p_{\mathrm{out}}\cap\ker p_{\mathrm{base}}, \qquad \ker\widehat\iota\subseteq \ker\widehat p_{\mathrm{out}}\cap\ker\widehat p_{\mathrm{base}}. \end{equation} The second statement uses the actual map into $\widehat{\Gamma^0}$ and the full completions of the source free factors. If $\overline H_{\mathrm{src}}$ denotes the actual compact source image in $\widehat{\Gamma^0}$, then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B124-source-abelianization} H_{\mathrm{src}}^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong\mathbb Z^6, \qquad (\overline H_{\mathrm{src}})^{\mathrm{ab}}_{\mathrm{cont}} \cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,6}, \end{equation} with the indicated six source generators as basis. The continuous abelianization means quotient by the closed commutator subgroup. These statements do not assert injection of the entire $F_6$ or identify the actual compact source image with its abstract completion.

statement: The pre-cross ordinary cover is a proper full profinite star amalgam, and the actual cross filling is one specified commutator quotient \label{stmt:B125} Use the actual B.112--B.114 regional marking \[ R,\quad R^0=\ker\varepsilon_R,\quad K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\quad B=CbC,\quad h=fk,\quad c=aCa^{-1}. \] Here $\varepsilon_R(C)=1$, every generator of $K$ and $k$ has ordinary parity zero, and $\eta$ is the actual based neck reflection. Put $Q=K\rtimes_\eta\langle j\rangle$, with $j^2=1$, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-pre-cross} A=R*_{K}Q,\qquad X=A/\langle\!\langle[jcj,k]\rangle\!\rangle. \end{equation} Thus $X$ is the actual final mirror extension of B.114 and B.121; all regional relations and all five neck-prefix inversions are already present in $A$. Extend $\varepsilon_R$ to $\varepsilon:A\to C_2$ by killing $Q$, and write $A^0=\ker\varepsilon$. Let $j_0=j$, $j_1=CjC$, and $K_1=CKC$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-star} A^0=Q_0*_{K}R^0*_{K_1}Q_1, \qquad Q_0=Q,\quad Q_1=CQC. \end{equation} The two edge embeddings and all three vertex embeddings induce their full profinite topologies, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-completed-star} \widehat{A^0} =\widehat Q_0\amalg_{\widehat K}\widehat{R^0} \amalg_{\widehat K_1}\widehat Q_1 \end{equation} is a proper full profinite star amalgam. Define the actual words \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-single-words} \begin{gathered} a_1=CaC,\quad k_1=CkC,\quad t_0=j_0a a_1^{-1}j_1,\\ j'_0=a^{-1}j_0a,\quad j'_1=a_1^{-1}j_1a_1,\quad g=j'_0j'_1,\quad z_*=gh. \end{gathered} \end{equation} The original-parity character descends to $X$, and its kernel has the exact presentation \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-final-single} X^0=A^0/\langle\!\langle[z_*,k]\rangle\!\rangle_{A^0}. \end{equation} Here $z_*$ is the entire existing word in \eqref{eq:B125-single-words}, not a new free stable letter. The selected opposite cone is $\tau=jcj=t_0C$. The five exact selected regional source words $s_1,\ldots,s_5$ of B.120 give the actual six source prelifts \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-source-prelifts} j_0s_1j_0,\ldots,j_0s_5j_0,k. \end{equation} Their images are the actual source words after the cross filling. The mirror character $\mu$ takes $j_0,j_1$ to $1$ and kills $R^0$; it is distinct from $\varepsilon$. The actual ordinary one-neck group is $X^0\cap\ker\mu$, and all words in \eqref{eq:B125-source-prelifts} lie in it. No vertex survival or selected-centralizer equality after \eqref{eq:B125-final-single} is asserted.

statement: The intermediate corner has the exact completed face, while the four final roots form a discrete malnormal cyclic family with sharp two-edge axis overlaps \label{stmt:B126} Use the actual intermediate amalgam of B.120: \[ M=R*_{H}W_\partial, \qquad H=\langle c,k,T\rangle=C_2(c)*\mathbb Z^2(k,T), \qquad P=P_5=cT. \] The corner satisfies $j^2=1$, $jPj=P^{-1}$ and $[jcj,k]=1$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B126-corner-face} H\cap jHj=\langle P\rangle, \qquad \widehat H\cap j\widehat H j =\overline{\langle P\rangle} \quad\hbox{inside }\widehat W_\partial. \end{equation} The completed subgroups here are the actual full embedded completions from B.118--B.120. Let $\mathcal T_M$ be the ordinary Bass--Serre tree, let $e=H$ be its base edge, and for $1\leq i\leq4$ put \[ w_i=jP_i,\qquad \mathcal A_i=\operatorname{Axis}_{\mathcal T_M}(w_i). \] Each $w_i$ has translation length $2$. Distinct translates of these four axes intersect in at most two edges, and that bound is attained. Moreover \begin{equation}\label{eq:B126-axis-stabilizers} \operatorname{Stab}_M(\mathcal A_i) =C_M(w_i)=N_M(\langle w_i\rangle)=\langle w_i\rangle. \end{equation} The four cyclic groups form a malnormal family: if \[ \langle w_i\rangle\cap g\langle w_l\rangle g^{-1}\ne1, \] then $i=l$ and $g\in\langle w_i\rangle$. These axis statements concern the ordinary tree and discrete $M$. They are not asserted for the full completed action or after the four actual relations $w_i^2=1$ are imposed.

statement: The actual family kernel has an exact all-orbit Schreier presentation, a literal retained section, and a paired discrete abelianization \label{stmt:B127} Use the actual free-eleven presentation of B.123. Write \[ \mathcal U=(a,B,d,e,\bar a,\bar B,\bar d,\bar e) =(a,B,d,e,cac,cBc,cdc,cec),\qquad T=F(f,g,x), \] where \(g=cfc\), \(x=\tau c\), and bars exchange the two four-label halves. Thus \(F=F(\mathcal U)*T\). Let \(\pi:F\to T\) kill the eight family letters, let \(L=\ker\pi\), and let \(N\) be the entire defining normal subgroup of B.123, including every signed source translate of all forty marked ordinary node words. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B127-section} N\subseteq[L,L],\qquad J=L/N,\qquad W=F/N=J\rtimes T. \end{equation} The section of \(T\) is the literal subgroup on \(f,g,x\). It is a retained-fiber section, not a section of the whole coarse one-neck group into the unfilled group. The exact Schreier free basis of \(L\) is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B127-basis} X_{t,i}=tU_i t^{-1},\qquad t\in T,\quad U_i\in\mathcal U. \end{equation} The selected involution \(\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)\) acts on this entire basis by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B127-pairing} \delta(X_{t,i})=X_{\delta_T(t)x,\bar i},\qquad \delta_T(f)=xgx^{-1},\quad \delta_T(g)=xfx^{-1},\quad \delta_T(x)=x^{-1}. \end{equation} It is a fixed-point-free permutation of the basis. There is an exact discrete module identification \begin{equation}\label{eq:B127-ab} J_{\rm ab} =\bigoplus_{\substack{t\in T\\i\in\mathcal U}}\mathbb Z e_{t,i}, \qquad \delta(e_{t,i})=e_{\delta_T(t)x,\bar i}. \end{equation} In particular its Tate cohomology for this \(C_2\)-action vanishes in every degree. All nonlinear source corrections admit the uniform formula \eqref{eq:B127-nonlinear} below, and the exact relation subgroup is \eqref{eq:B127-L-closure}, with no cutoff on either source or retained-deck words. On actual full completions the retained section gives \[ \widehat W=\overline J\rtimes\widehat T,\qquad \overline J=\ker(\widehat W\to\widehat T). \] No equality \(\widehat J=\overline J\), no completed version of \eqref{eq:B127-ab}, and no lifting of invariant abelian classes to fixed group elements is asserted here.

statement: The continuous abelianization of the actual closed family kernel is a free completed group-ring module with paired involution, while the closed source has a proper image in its invariants \label{stmt:B128} Use the actual free presentation and full signed source orbit of B.123: \[ F=F(U_1,\ldots,U_8)*T,\qquad T=F(f,g,x),\qquad W=F/N, \] where the ordered family generators are \[ (U_1,\ldots,U_8)=(a,B,d,e,\bar a,\bar B,\bar d,\bar e), \qquad \bar U=cUc. \] Let $L=\ker(F\to T)$, $J=L/N$, and let $I\leq J$ be the actual source-family image generated by all signed source translates of the four contact words. statement: A residue-three free-fiber quotient gives an actual equivariant free-two retract and proves nonlinear nonlifting in both categories \label{stmt:B129} Use \(F,L,N,W,J,T\) and \(\delta\) from B.123 and B.127. statement: The actual six-generator one-neck source map is noninjective in both categories, and its image contains an explicitly retracted copy of $\mathbb Z^2$ \label{stmt:B130} Let $\mathcal G=\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}$ be the actual ordinary one-neck group of B.114, B.119 and B.123. statement: The corrected d-contact does not commute with the inner source loop, discretely or in the actual full completion \label{stmt:B131} Use the complete actual presentation of B.123 and the actual kernels of B.127--B.128: \[ \begin{gathered} F=F(U_1,\ldots,U_8)*T,\quad T=F(f,g,x),\quad L=\ker(F\to T),\\ W=F/N,\quad J=L/N,\quad \Gamma_0=W\rtimes S,\quad S=F(m,v). \end{gathered} \] The ordered family labels are $(a,B,d,e,\bar a,\bar B,\bar d,\bar e)$, where $\bar U=cUc$. statement: The actual pre-cross six-source subgroup has its full profinite topology, and the final source kernels are specified ambient normal-closure intersections \label{stmt:B133} Use the actual B.112--B.125 marking \[ K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\qquad c=aCa^{-1},\qquad Q=K\rtimes_\eta\langle j\rangle,\qquad j^2=1, \] and the proper pre-cross amalgam and its actual cross quotient \begin{equation}\label{eq:B133-pre-cross} A=R*_{K}Q,\qquad r_\times=[jcj,k],\qquad X=A/\langle\!\langle r_\times\rangle\!\rangle_A. \end{equation} Here $R$ is the entire regional orbifold group, $R^0$ is its original ordinary subgroup, $\eta$ is the actual based neck reflection, and $k$ is the actual regional base loop. Let $S=\langle s_1,\ldots,s_5\rangle\leq R^0$ be the actual regional source group of B.112, with its entire selected-gap conjugations. Let $\Gamma_0$ be the actual ordinary one-neck subgroup of $X$, the joint kernel of the original and mirror characters. All six words in \eqref{eq:B133-source} map into $\Gamma_0$. Define \[ N_\times=\langle\!\langle r_\times\rangle\!\rangle_A, \qquad \mathcal N_\times= \overline{\langle\!\langle r_\times\rangle\!\rangle}^{\,\widehat A}. \] With the embedding in \eqref{eq:B133-free-completion}, the exact discrete and compact source kernels are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B133-kernel-intersections} \begin{aligned} \ker(\mathscr F\longrightarrow\Gamma_0) &=\mathscr F\cap N_\times,\\ \ker(\widehat{\mathscr F}\longrightarrow\widehat\Gamma_0) &=\widehat{\mathscr F}\cap\mathcal N_\times. \end{aligned} \end{equation} These are intersections with the actual ambient normal closures. No equality between the closure of the first kernel and the second kernel is asserted. The theorem does not assert injectivity of the final six-source map, whose nonzero kernel was exhibited in B.130, or identify its full internal normal-generating family.

statement: Both mirror sheets give an exact edge pushout, an ordinary kernel-matching closure, and an independent finite matching-normal criterion \label{stmt:B134} Use the actual ordinary pre-cross star of B.125, with $j_0=j$, $j_1=CjC$, $K_1=CKC$ and $p=\operatorname{Ad}(j_0)$. The kernel of mirror parity in that star has the proper presentation \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-pre-HNN} \begin{gathered} V=R^0*_{K}p(R^0),\qquad p(u)=\eta(u)\quad(u\in K),\qquad t=j_0j_1,\\ \langle V,t\mid tut^{-1}=\sigma(u)\ (u\in K_1)\rangle, \qquad \sigma(CuC)=p(C\eta(u)C)\quad(u\in K). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Let $\theta=\operatorname{Ad}(j_0)$ on $V$; it interchanges the two vertex groups, and on the pre-cross HNN group sends $t$ to $t^{-1}$. Let $E_1=C\langle K,k\rangle C$ be the actual B.117 subgroup, and set \[ (u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4) =\bigl(CaC,CdC,CeC,C(f^{-1}Bf)C\bigr). \] Its exact presentation is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-E1} E_1=\langle f_1,k_1,u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4\mid [(f_1k_1)^2,k_1],\ [k_1,u_i]\ (1\leq i\leq4)\rangle. \end{equation} Define the five target words in $V$ by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-rhos} \rho_0=[(\sigma(f_1)s)^2,s],\qquad \rho_i=[s,\sigma(u_i)]\quad(1\leq i\leq4). \end{equation} Put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-initial-quotient} \begin{gathered} N_* =\langle\!\langle\rho_i,\theta(\rho_i) \ (0\leq i\leq4)\rangle\!\rangle_V, \qquad V_*=V/N_*,\\ E=E_1*\langle y\rangle. \end{gathered} \end{equation} There are genuine homomorphisms $i,j:E\to V_*$ defined on $E_1$ by its actual inclusion and by $(K_1,k_1)\mapsto (\sigma(K_1),s)$, respectively, and on the extra generator by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-extra-edge} i(y)=s',\qquad j(y)=p(k_1). \end{equation} Neither map is presumed injective. With these maps, \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-pushout} \Gamma_0=\langle V_*,t\mid ti(e)t^{-1}=j(e)\ (e\in E)\rangle. \end{equation} Define normal subgroups of $V_*$ by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-saturation} \begin{split} M_0&=1,\\ M_{n+1}&=\langle\!\langle M_n,\ i(j^{-1}(M_n)),\ j(i^{-1}(M_n))\rangle\!\rangle_{V_*},\\ M_\infty&=\bigcup_{n\geq0}M_n. \end{split} \end{equation} Then $V_*/M_\infty$ embeds in \eqref{eq:B134-pushout} as the base of a proper ordinary HNN extension. In particular \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-discrete-base-kernel} \ker(V_*\longrightarrow\Gamma_0)=M_\infty. \end{equation} No finite stabilization is asserted. Independently, let $\mathcal B$ consist of the finite-index normal subgroups $N\triangleleft V_*$ satisfying $i^{-1}(N)=j^{-1}(N)$. statement: The actual whole group has a marked inner-star relative presentation whose base map is noninjective in both categories; on an explicit retract block its kernel and the new source fixed subgroup are exact \label{stmt:B135} Use the actual one-neck marking and source operators of B.123. All tuples, node words and operators used below are specified by finite word formulas in the proof. Let $R_-$ be the actual minus annular vertex, including its ten node relations and their full $m$-orbit. Before the remaining plus filling, the actual marked presentation is the proper amalgam \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-inner-star} G_{\rm in}=R_-*_{\langle m\rangle} (\langle m\rangle\times C_2(\tau)). \end{equation} Its selected-cone centralizers, discretely and after full completion, are \[ C_{G_{\rm in}}(\tau)=\langle m\rangle\times\langle\tau\rangle, \qquad C_{\widehat G_{\rm in}}(\tau) =\overline{\langle m\rangle}\times\langle\tau\rangle. \] Thus the entire original ordinary inner subgroup has fixed subgroup $\langle m\rangle$, and its actual full completion has fixed subgroup $\overline{\langle m\rangle}\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}$. If $\beta$ is the actual $v$-operator and $\mathcal R_+$ the ten actual plus orbifold node words, the \emph{whole} actual group is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-whole-relative} E_{\rm act}= \left\langle G_{\rm in},v\ \middle|\ v yv^{-1}=\beta(y)\ (y=a,b,d,e,f,C,\tau),\quad \mathcal R_+\right\rangle . \end{equation} In particular this presentation retains all signed source translates of both node families, as well as every fiber conjugate. It does not assert that $\beta$ descends to an automorphism of $G_{\rm in}$. The element \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-killed-word} w=[a,a^*]=a\tau a\tau a^{-1}\tau a^{-1}\tau \end{equation} is nontrivial in $G_{\rm in}$ and in its full completion, but maps to one in $E_{\rm act}$ and its full completion. These noninjectivity assertions also hold on the original ordinary index-two subgroup and its full completion. The following sharper comparison concerns actual subgroup blocks. There are retractions onto \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-blocks} \begin{gathered} B=\langle a,\tau,m\rangle\leq G_{\rm in},\qquad B\cong(\mathbb Z(a)*C_2(\tau))\times\mathbb Z(m),\\ Q=\langle a,\tau,m\rangle\leq E_{\rm act},\qquad Q\cong(\mathbb Z^2(a,a^*)\rtimes_{\rm swap}C_2(\tau)) \times\mathbb Z(m). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Writing $B_0=B\cap G_{\rm in}^0$ and $Q_0=Q\cap\Gamma_0$, \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-block-kernels} \begin{gathered} B_0=F(a,a^*)\times\mathbb Z(m),\qquad Q_0=\mathbb Z^3(a,a^*,m),\\ \ker(B\to E_{\rm act})=\langle\!\langle w\rangle\!\rangle_B, \qquad \ker(B_0\to\Gamma_0)=\langle\!\langle w\rangle\!\rangle_{B_0}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Each displayed subgroup has its full induced profinite topology in the indicated ambient group. The corresponding kernels on their actual completed closures are precisely the closed normal closures of $w$. The retraction $\Gamma_0\to Q_0$ is $\delta$-equivariant. For the corrected actual contact $A_s=s_1s_4^{-1}s_1^{-1}$ of B.130, the fixed subgroups on this block are exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-fixed-creation} \begin{gathered} B_0^\delta=\langle m\rangle,\qquad (\widehat B_0)^\delta=\overline{\langle m\rangle},\\ Q_0^\delta=\langle aa^*,m\rangle =\langle A_s,m\rangle\cong\mathbb Z^2,\qquad (\widehat Q_0)^\delta =\overline{\langle A_s,m\rangle}\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,2}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Thus the filling creates this known source fixed norm. These statements do not determine the whole kernel of $G_{\rm in}\to E_{\rm act}$ or the full fixed subgroup of $\Gamma_0$ or $\widehat\Gamma_0$.

statement: The unfilled inclusion edge embeds, its target contains a full free-six subgroup, and the proper local filling has an explicit fixed-point-free involution \label{stmt:B136} Use the actual B.134 marking \[ V=R^0*_{K}p(R^0),\quad K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\quad K_1=CKC, \quad L=\langle K,k\rangle,\quad E_1=CLC, \] where $p|_K=\eta$ and $\theta$ interchanges the two vertices. statement: The two actual unfilled edge groups have trivial ordinary intersection, by exact vertex and incident-direction comparisons \label{stmt:B137} Use the actual unfilled B.134/B.136 amalgam $V=R^0*_{K}p(R^0)$, with $p|_K=\eta$ and its vertex-exchanging involution $\theta$. Put $E_1=C\langle K,k\rangle C$ and \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-edge-groups} \begin{gathered} H_i=\langle E_1,s'\rangle =\langle E_1,a^{-1}p(k)a\rangle,\\ H_j=\theta(H_i)=\langle p(E_1),s\rangle =\langle p(E_1),\eta(a)^{-1}k\eta(a)\rangle,\\ B_i=\langle f,a^{-1}p(k)a\rangle\leq p(R^0),\qquad B_j=\langle\eta(f),\eta(a)^{-1}k\eta(a)\rangle\leq R^0. \end{gathered} \end{equation} The two displayed equalities retain the actual B.134 words $w_0=aa_1^{-1}$, $v_0=p(w_0)$, $s'=w_0^{-1}p(k)w_0$, $s=v_0^{-1}kv_0$, and $a_1=CaC$. There are embedded ordinary subamalgams \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-subamalgams} H_i=E_1*_{\langle f\rangle}B_i,\qquad H_j=B_j*_{\langle\eta(f)\rangle}p(E_1). \end{equation} Their standard vertex and edge intersections are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-standard-intersections} \begin{gathered} H_i\cap R^0=E_1,\quad H_i\cap p(R^0)=B_i,\quad H_i\cap K=\langle f\rangle,\\ H_j\cap R^0=B_j,\quad H_j\cap p(R^0)=p(E_1),\quad H_j\cap K=\langle\eta(f)\rangle. \end{gathered} \end{equation} The actual vertex overlaps are trivial: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-overlaps} E_1\cap B_j=1,\qquad p(E_1)\cap B_i=1. \end{equation} In fact their whole ordinary intersection is trivial: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-whole-intersection} H_i\cap H_j=1. \end{equation} This conclusion uses the additional incident-direction comparison proved below, not just the two standard vertex stabilizers. No completed intersection, free-product assertion for the generated overgroup, or survival after the two local fillings is inferred.

statement: The actual unfilled cyclic-edge subgroups have full induced topology, trivial whole completed intersection, and one exact ordinary translated overlap \label{stmt:B138} Retain every marking of B.134--B.137. Put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B138-data} \begin{gathered} V=R_L*_{K}R_R,\quad R_L=R^0,\quad R_R=p(R^0),\quad p|_K=\eta,\\ E_1=C\langle K,k\rangle C,\qquad \zeta=\eta(a),\\ B_i=\langle f,a^{-1}p(k)a\rangle,\qquad B_j=\langle\eta(f),\zeta^{-1}k\zeta\rangle,\\ H_i=E_1*_{\langle f\rangle}B_i,\qquad H_j=B_j*_{\langle\eta(f)\rangle}p(E_1). \end{gathered} \end{equation} These are the actual embedded ordinary subamalgams. Both $H_i,H_j$ have their full induced profinite topology in $V$. Bars below mean actual closures in the indicated full completions. In particular \begin{equation}\label{eq:B138-whole-compact} \overline{H_i}\cap\overline{H_j}=1 \qquad\text{inside }\widehat V. \end{equation} Their completed vertex and edge intersections are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B138-compact-vertices} \overline{H_i}\cap\widehat R_L=\widehat E_1,\quad \overline{H_i}\cap\widehat R_R=\widehat B_i,\quad \overline{H_i}\cap\widehat K=\overline{\langle f\rangle}, \end{equation} with the corresponding actual $\theta$-images for $H_j$. In the ordinary group there is also the specified whole translated intersection \begin{equation}\label{eq:B138-shifted} H_i\cap\zeta H_j\zeta^{-1}=\langle k\rangle. \end{equation} The full two-family initial normal subgroup $N_*$ of B.134 meets $\langle k\rangle$ trivially; its closed normal closure meets the actual $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(k)$ trivially as well. All these assertions precede the initial fillings. They do not assert that $D_{\rm loc}$ survives in $V_*$, that its actual kernel is $\kappa$-invariant, or that all translated intersections are controlled. No completed analogue of \eqref{eq:B138-shifted} is used or asserted.

statement: The actual one-family quotient has a complete graph presentation and exact discrete and completed fixed-source image; the original comparison reduces to its actual remaining kernel \label{stmt:B139} Use the complete marked group $\Gamma_0$, source operators and selected involution $\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)$ of B.123 and B.135. In the minus local tuple \[ E_0=F(a,b,d,e,f)*C_2(C)*C_2(\tau) \] fill $b,d,e$ and their selected mates by their full normal closure in the actual ordinary group. Denote the resulting actual quotient by $\pi:\Gamma_0\to\Gamma_a$, put $K_{\rm rem}=\ker\pi$, and let $H_{\rm src}$ be the actual six-source image in $\Gamma_0$. Every signed source translate and both ordinary node sheets remain part of the quotient presentation. Write $J_a=\pi(H_{\rm src})$ and $a^*=\tau a\tau$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B139-main} \Gamma_a^\delta=J_a=\langle aa^*,m,v\rangle,\qquad (\widehat{\Gamma_a})^\delta=\overline{J_a}. \end{equation} The second closure is the actual closure in the full completion, not a presumed abstract completion of $J_a$. The quotient has an exact graph presentation as follows. Put \[ Q_f=C_2(C)*\mathbb Z(f)*C_2(\tau),\qquad S=F(m,v),\qquad Q=Q_f\rtimes S. \] The action and its marked conjugator cocycle are specified in the proof. The stabilizer $H=\langle m,fv\rangle\leq Q$ maps isomorphically onto $S$. Define a graph $\mathcal G$ with vertices $Q/H$ and edges \begin{equation}\label{eq:B139-graph} \{qH,qCH\},\quad \{qH,q\tau H\}\qquad(q\in Q). \end{equation} Repeated edges are identified. If $A(\mathcal G)$ is its graph group, then the actual orbifold quotient and its ordinary subgroup are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B139-split} E_a=\Gamma_a\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle =A(\mathcal G)\rtimes Q,\qquad \Gamma_a=A(\mathcal G)\rtimes Q^0 . \end{equation} Here the original orientation is odd on both cones and even on $f,S$ and all graph generators; $Q^0$ is its kernel. For the original group there are the exact, generally nonsplit, reductions \begin{equation}\label{eq:B139-kernel-reductions} \begin{gathered} 1\longrightarrow K_{\rm rem}^{\delta} \longrightarrow\Gamma_0^\delta \longrightarrow\Gamma_a^\delta\longrightarrow1,\qquad \Gamma_0^\delta=H_{\rm src}K_{\rm rem}^\delta,\\ (\widehat{\Gamma_0})^\delta =\overline{H_{\rm src}}\,(\overline{K_{\rm rem}})^\delta . \end{gathered} \end{equation} Consequently the original discrete and completed fixed-source equalities are respectively equivalent to \begin{equation}\label{eq:B139-remaining-gates} \begin{gathered} K_{\rm rem}^\delta=H_{\rm src}\cap K_{\rm rem},\\ (\overline{K_{\rm rem}})^\delta =\overline{H_{\rm src}}\cap\overline{K_{\rm rem}}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} All bars in the last two displays denote actual closures in $\widehat{\Gamma_0}$. Neither remaining equality is asserted.

statement: The two named retained sections fail to be source-invariant after the whole filling, and no family-kernel adjustment of the outer source repairs either section, discretely or in full completion \label{stmt:B140} Use the actual B.123 groups \[ \begin{gathered} F=F(U_1,\ldots,U_8)*T,\quad T=F(f,g,x),\quad L=\ker(F\to T),\\ W=F/N,\qquad J=\ker(W\to T),\qquad \Gamma_0=W\rtimes S. \end{gathered} \] where $S=F(m,v)$ and $N$ is the entire forty-seed normal closure under all signed source and retained-deck translates. The family labels, in the original $F_{11}$ basis, are \[ (U_1,\ldots,U_8)=(a,B,d,e,\bar a,\bar B,\bar d,\bar e), \qquad \bar u=cuc,\quad g=cfc,\quad x=\tau c. \] By B.127, $N\subseteq[L,L]$ and $J_{\rm ab}=M=\mathbb Z[T]^8$ with its left deck action. Consider the following two actual sections of $W\to T$: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B140-sections} \begin{aligned} \sigma_o(f,g,x)&=(f,g,x),\\ \sigma_\ell(f,g,x) &=(f,a^{-1}\bar a g\bar a^{-1}a,\ x\bar a^{-1}a) =(f,CfC,\tau C),\qquad C=a^{-1}ca . \end{aligned} \end{equation} Both named subgroups, and their conjugates in $\Gamma_0$, have their full induced profinite topology. The old section is not preserved by either signed $m$ or either signed $v$ action. The local section is preserved by both signed $m$ actions but not by either signed $v$ action. All these noninvariance assertions hold after the entire node filling, and after full completion. More strongly, there is no $j\in J$ for which $jv$ normalizes either subgroup in \eqref{eq:B140-sections}. There is likewise no $j\in\overline J$ for which $jv$ normalizes either actual completed subgroup. These exclusions also apply after replacing a named section by any common $J$-conjugate, or completed section by any common $\overline J$-conjugate. In particular a section of the whole coarse quotient cannot restrict to either named retained section or these conjugates. An arbitrary nonconjugate retained section is not excluded. No original fixed-source equality is decided.

statement: The regional neck-retraction kernel has an explicit graph presentation, and the complete initial filling obstructs the specified opposite-kernel retractions \label{stmt:B141} Let $r:R^0\to K=F(a,B,d,e,f)$ be the actual B.114/B.117 neck retraction, with $B=CbC$, $h=fk$ and $k_1=CkC$. Its kernel $N_{\rm reg}$ is the explicit graph group described below. The actual subgroup $E_1=C\langle K,k\rangle C$ meets this kernel in a full coordinate graph subgroup. The entire actual neck action is given by retained translations, the height shift and the ordered section correction in \eqref{eq:B141-cocycle}. For the actual unfilled $V=R_L*_KR_R$ of B.134, its common-retract kernel therefore has a faithful ordinary graph presentation \begin{equation}\label{eq:B141-ambient-kernel} \ker(V\to K)=N_L*N_R=A(\Sigma_L\sqcup\Sigma_R). \end{equation} All ten initial relations have the exact mixed form \eqref{eq:B141-mixed-family} and its actual $\theta$-image. In particular the existing retraction $V\to R_L$, identity on $R_L$ and the common-neck retraction on $R_R$, does not descend through the actual initial quotient $V_*$, either discretely or continuously through its full completion. The mirrored retraction fails in the same way. This is failure of specified retractions; it does not assert that their nontrivial regional images are killed in $V_*$, or that either local quotient fails to embed.

statement: The actual eight-family coarse filling has no section in either category; its one-color first-jet extension class has infinite order and every odd-prime reduction remains nonzero in full completion \label{stmt:B142} Use the actual groups of B.123 and B.127: \[ \begin{gathered} F=F(U_1,\ldots,U_8)*T,\qquad T=F(f,g,x),\qquad L=\ker(F\to T),\\ W=F/N,\qquad J=\ker(W\to T),\qquad S=F(m,v),\qquad \Gamma_0=W\rtimes S. \end{gathered} \] Here $N$ is the entire forty-seed normal closure, with both ordinary node sheets and every signed source and deck translate. The actual eight-family filling is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B142-coarse-map} \pi:\Gamma_0\longrightarrow Q_0=T\rtimes S. \end{equation} Neither $\pi$ nor its map on full profinite completions has a group-homomorphic right inverse, continuous in the latter category. No equivariance, prescribed branch or cone lift, common conjugator, or source normalization is imposed on a proposed section. More precisely, put $M=J_{\mathrm{ab}}=\mathbb Z[T]^8$ and let $I\subset\mathbb Z[T]$ be the augmentation ideal. Keeping only the original $B$ color, whose $F_{11}$ label is $2$, gives the actual $Q_0$-module quotient \[ V=\mathbb Z[T]/I^2\cong\mathbb Z^4. \] The resulting actual abelian extension \begin{equation}\label{eq:B142-integral-extension} 1\longrightarrow V\longrightarrow E_V \longrightarrow Q_0\longrightarrow1 \end{equation} has an infinite-order class in $H^2(Q_0,V)$. For every odd prime $p$, its reduction has kernel $V_p=V/pV$ and middle group $E_p$, with \begin{equation}\label{eq:B142-finite-extensions} \begin{gathered} 1\longrightarrow V_p\longrightarrow E_p \longrightarrow Q_0\longrightarrow1,\\ 1\longrightarrow V_p\longrightarrow\widehat E_p \longrightarrow\widehat Q_0\longrightarrow1. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Both corresponding extension classes are nonzero, in ordinary and continuous cohomology respectively. The second sequence has its \emph{actual embedded finite kernel}; no completion of $J$ or identification of the continuous abelianization of $\overline J$ is assumed. These assertions concern the specified coarse filling and do not decide the remaining fixed-source equality of B.139.

statement: Neither actual filling admits a virtual section, while its first-jet classes restrict to zero on the actual fixed source \label{stmt:B143} Let \(\pi:\Gamma_0\to Q_0=T\rtimes S\) be B.142's actual eight-family coarse filling. For every finite-index subgroup \(H\leq Q_0\), the restriction \(\pi^{-1}(H)\to H\) has no group-homomorphic right inverse. For every open subgroup \(\mathcal H\leq\widehat Q_0\), the restriction of the actual completed map has no continuous group-homomorphic right inverse. The same conclusions hold for B.139's actual one-family filling \(p_a:\Gamma_0\to\Gamma_a\), over every finite-index subgroup of \(\Gamma_a\) and every open subgroup of its full completion. These are statements about whole-group virtual sections. In contrast, write \(J_a=\Gamma_a^\delta\) for the actual one-family fixed-source image, and \(\overline{J_a}\) for its actual closure in \(\widehat\Gamma_a\). B.142's integral first-jet class and every odd-prime class pull back to zero on \(J_a\); every corresponding continuous odd-prime class pulls back to zero on \(\overline{J_a}\). The subgroups \(J_a\) and \(\overline{J_a}\) have infinite index and are not open, respectively. No obstruction to a fixed-source section follows from these particular classes.

statement: The actual one-family fixed source is a coset-permutation free-by-free group and an explicit centralizer extension; its marked fixed section is equivalent to one whole-stabilizer commutation condition \label{stmt:B144} Use B.139's actual groups and graph \[ \begin{gathered} Q_f=C_2(C)*\mathbb Z(f)*C_2(\tau),\qquad S=F(m,v),\qquad Q=Q_f\rtimes S,\\ H=\langle m,fv\rangle=\{h_s^{-1}s:s\in S\},\qquad \mathcal G^{(0)}=Q/H,\\ \mathcal G^{(1)}=\bigl\{\{qH,qCH\},\{qH,q\tau H\}:q\in Q\bigr\}. \end{gathered} \] Projection $H\to S$ is an isomorphism, and \[ E_a=A(\mathcal G)\rtimes Q, \qquad\Gamma_a=A(\mathcal G)\rtimes Q^0 \] are the actual one-family orbifold quotient and its ordinary subgroup. Write $\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)$, $a^*=\tau a\tau$, $A=aa^*$, and define the \emph{entire actual stabilizer} \begin{equation}\label{eq:B144-stabilizer} L=H\cap S=\{s\in S:h_s=1\}. \end{equation} Then the actual discrete fixed-source image has the exact descriptions \begin{equation}\label{eq:B144-source-structure} J_a=\Gamma_a^\delta =F(S/L)\rtimes S \cong S*_{L}\bigl(L\times\mathbb Z(A)\bigr). \end{equation} The free basis indexed by the left cosets $sL$ is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B144-norm-basis} A_{sL}=a_{sH}a_{\tau sH}=sAs^{-1}. \end{equation} In particular the kernel of the free-source map $F(A,m,v)\twoheadrightarrow J_a$ is exactly \[ \langle\!\langle[A,l]:l\in L\rangle\!\rangle. \] In the original $\Gamma_0$, let $A_{\rm src}=s_1s_4^{-1}s_1^{-1}$ be the actual corrected source word of B.130. The marked assignment \begin{equation}\label{eq:B144-marked-section} A\longmapsto A_{\rm src},\qquad m\longmapsto m, \qquad v\longmapsto v \end{equation} extends to a homomorphism $J_a\to\Gamma_0^\delta$ if and only if \begin{equation}\label{eq:B144-whole-gate} [A_{\rm src},l]=1\quad\text{for every }l\in L. \end{equation} If it extends, it is a discrete section of the actual fixed-subgroup surjection. The equality $L=\langle m\rangle$ and condition \eqref{eq:B144-whole-gate} are not asserted. Nor is an abstract completion of \eqref{eq:B144-source-structure}, a compact fixed section, or the original fixed-source equality inferred.

statement: The actual center kernel admits an exact cyclic-preimage retraction and two-generator square normalization, with an explicit ambient discontinuity \label{stmt:B145} Use the actual regional neck retraction $r_{\rm reg}:R^0\to K$ and the two-region group $V=R_L*_KR_R$ of B.141. Its explicit two-sided recursion also eliminates the corresponding center symbols in the complete ordinary presentation, provided every remaining graph edge, every $K$-translate and both mirror families are carried along. statement: The complete cyclic mixed-square and four-leaf filling is a proper internal amalgam, with an explicit all-word ambient restriction kernel \label{stmt:B146} In the actual B.141 unfilled group $V=R_L*_KR_R$, write \[ \begin{gathered} K=F(a,B,d,e,f), \\ (V_1,V_2,V_3,V_4)=(a,d,e,f^{-1}Bf), \\ q=\eta(afa^{-1})^{-1}. \end{gathered} \] Let $\mathfrak d:K\hookrightarrow R_R$ denote the complete marked map of B.141, and put $\gamma=\mathfrak d(f)$, $x_i=\mathfrak d(V_i)$. With $N_R=\ker(r_R:R_R\to K)$, the actual cyclic subgroup and its complete five-relation filling are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B146-carrier} \mathscr D=\langle k\rangle*B_q,\qquad B_q=N_R\rtimes\langle q\rangle, \end{equation} \begin{equation}\label{eq:B146-five} \begin{gathered} R_{\rm cyc}=\langle\!\langle P_0,P_1,P_2,P_3,P_4 \rangle\!\rangle_{\mathscr D},\\ P_0=[(\gamma k)^2,k],\quad P_i=[k,x_i]. \end{gathered} \end{equation} There is an exact proper ordinary amalgam \begin{equation}\label{eq:B146-amalgam} \begin{gathered} \mathscr D/R_{\rm cyc} =B_q*_{F_*}E_{\rm new},\\ F_*=\mathfrak d(K)=F(\gamma,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4), \end{gathered} \end{equation} where $E_{\rm new}$ is specified in the proof. Both vertex groups embed internally. The full initial filling still uses every $K$ translate and the actual $\theta$-family; its restriction on this carrier is exactly \eqref{eq:B146-ambient-kernel}. Neither internal properness nor the cyclic normalization makes that kernel trivial.

statement: The prescribed center basis change has no injective extension to the actual regional kernel, even with arbitrary changes of the family images \label{stmt:B147} Let $N_{\rm reg}=A(\Sigma)$ be B.141's actual ordinary, unfilled regional kernel. Let $\varphi$ be B.145's automorphism of its center free subgroup, sending each pivot $Z_n$ to $u_n=\nu_nZ_n\nu_n^{-1}$ and fixing every complementary center. There are three specified nontrivial actual family generators $\lambda_\alpha,\lambda_\delta,\lambda_\epsilon$ such that every endomorphism $\Phi:N_{\rm reg}\to N_{\rm reg}$ extending $\varphi$ must satisfy \begin{equation}\label{eq:B147-forced-killing} \Phi(\lambda_\alpha)=\Phi(\lambda_\delta) =\Phi(\lambda_\epsilon)=1. \end{equation} Thus no injective endomorphism, and in particular no compatible basis automorphism, extends the prescribed center change. The family images may be changed arbitrarily in this assertion; they are not required to retain their names, conjugacy classes or abelian coordinates. Noninjective extensions do exist. This is an ordinary unfilled obstruction, not a statement about any compact extension, any different center normalization or any ambient filling collapse.

statement: The complete one-family stabilizer is an exact primitive-word return subgroup \label{stmt:B148} All groups in this statement belong to the actual one-neck annular model of B.114 and B.139. Put \[ Q_f=\langle C,\tau,f\mid C^2=\tau^2=1\rangle, \qquad S=F(m,v),\qquad E=Q_f\rtimes S. \] The actual operators and ordered peripheral cocycle are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B148-input} \begin{gathered} \alpha_m(f)=f^{-1}CfCf,\quad \alpha_m(C)=f^{-1}Cf, \quad\alpha_m(\tau)=\tau,\\ \alpha_v(f)=\tau f\tau,\quad \alpha_v(C)=f^{-1}Cf, \quad\alpha_v(\tau)=\tau,\\ h_m=1,\quad h_v=f^{-1},\qquad h_{st}=\alpha_s(h_t)h_s. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Thus the actual graph section is $H=\{h_s^{-1}s:s\in S\}=\langle m,fv\rangle$. Set $u=m^{-1}v$ and \[ r=\tau f^{-1}C,\qquad \bar r=\tau r\tau=f^{-1}C\tau, \qquad w=\tau C. \] Then $T_0=Q_f^0=F(r,\bar r,w)$, $E^0=T_0\rtimes S$, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:B148-actions} \begin{array}{c|ccc} &r&\bar r&w\\\hline m&r&\bar r&rw^{-1}\bar r^{-1}\\ m^{-1}&r&\bar r&\bar r^{-1}w^{-1}r\\ u&w^{-1}rw&w\bar r w^{-1}&w\\ u^{-1}&wrw^{-1}&w^{-1}\bar r w&w \end{array} \end{equation} For every integer $n$, $h_{u^n}=w^{-n}r^n$. The entire discrete centralizers and stabilizer are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B148-centralizers} \begin{gathered} C_{E^0}(r)=\langle r\rangle\times H,\qquad L:=H\cap S=\{s\in S:\alpha_s(r)=r\},\\ C_E(\langle\tau,r\rangle)=L. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Moreover the whole subgroup with the $u$ direction has the two equivalent presentations \begin{equation}\label{eq:B148-vertex} \begin{aligned} T_0\rtimes\langle u\rangle &=\langle u,w,r,\bar r\mid[u,w],[wu,r],[w^{-1}u,\bar r]\rangle\\ &=\langle u,k,h,\bar r\mid[u,k],[h,k],[u^2k^{-1},\bar r]\rangle, \quad k=wu,\ h=r^{-1}k. \end{aligned} \end{equation}

statement: The actual one-family stabilizer is cyclic and its fixed projection has a marked ordinary section \label{stmt:B149} In the exact marking of B.148, \[ H\cap S=\langle m\rangle. \] Consequently the actual one-family fixed group and its marked lift are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B149-section} \begin{gathered} J_a=\Gamma_a^\delta =\langle A,m,v\mid[A,m]=1\rangle \cong(\mathbb Z_A\times\mathbb Z_m)*\mathbb Z_v,\\ \sigma:J_a\longrightarrow\Gamma_0^\delta, \qquad(A,m,v)\longmapsto(A_{\rm src},m,v),\qquad A_{\rm src}=s_1s_4^{-1}s_1^{-1},\\ p_a\sigma=\operatorname{id}_{J_a}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Here $p_a$ is the actual one-family filling in the one-neck annular model; the section is a section of its fixed subgroup restriction. If $K_{\rm rem}=\ker p_a$ and $H_{\rm src}$ is the full six-source image, then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B149-split} \begin{aligned} \Gamma_0^\delta&=K_{\rm rem}^\delta\rtimes\sigma(J_a),\\ H_{\rm src}&=(H_{\rm src}\cap K_{\rm rem})\rtimes\sigma(J_a). \end{aligned} \end{equation}

statement: The source part of the remaining ordinary fixed kernel has an exact three-orbit presentation \label{stmt:B150} Use the actual groups and marked section of B.149. Define the corrected contact words \begin{equation}\label{eq:B150-contact} \begin{aligned} A_s&=s_1s_4^{-1}s_1^{-1},& B_s&=A_s^{-1}s_1^{-1}A_s,\\ D_s&=s_2s_1s_3^{-1}s_1^{-1}s_2^{-1},& E_s&=s_2^{-1}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} For $j\in J_a$, let $B_j,D_j,E_j$ be formal symbols and put $\mathcal F=F(B_j,D_j,E_j:j\in J_a)$. There is an actual subgroup identification \begin{equation}\label{eq:B150-kernel} I_{\rm src}:=H_{\rm src}\cap K_{\rm rem} =\mathcal F/\mathcal R\ \le K_{\rm rem}^{\delta}, \end{equation} where $X_j$ evaluates to $\sigma(j)X_s\sigma(j)^{-1}$ for $X=B,D,E$, and $\mathcal R$ is exactly the full actual relation preimage described below. In particular these three whole $J_a$ orbits generate $I_{\rm src}$ as a subgroup; they are not replaced by an ambient normal closure. The ordinary local fixed-source equality is equivalent to surjectivity of the inclusion in \eqref{eq:B150-kernel}. Moreover \[ \mathcal R\cap F(D_{m^n}:n\in\mathbb Z)=1. \]

statement: The entire first filling has an exact free-coset kernel, while the opposite square remains coupled to the base \label{stmt:B151} Retain the actual ordinary groups and both marked families of B.141. There is a retract \[ \mathcal B=L_L*_KR_R\ \le\ V=R_L*_KR_R,\qquad L=\langle K,k\rangle, \] such that \(V\) is a free-coset extension of \(\mathcal B\). All five first-family relators lie in \(\mathcal B\). If \[ R_i=\langle\!\langle P_0,\ldots,P_4\rangle\!\rangle_{\mathcal B}, \quad M_i=\langle\!\langle P_0,\ldots,P_4\rangle\!\rangle_V, \quad \mathcal B_i=\mathcal B/R_i, \] then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B151-main} \begin{gathered} M_i\cap\mathcal B=R_i,\\ V/M_i=F\left(\coprod_j\mathcal B_i/S_{ji}\right) \rtimes\mathcal B_i. \end{gathered} \end{equation} The four actual subgroups \(S_{ji}\) are specified below as image subgroups, without assuming their presentations survive. The restriction of \(M_i\) to the original free family kernel is exactly the normal closure of the induced coset identifications. statement: The complete mirrored neck is a retract through both initial families, and its ordinary kernel is a full coordinate free factor \label{stmt:B152} In the notation of B.151, put \[ J_*=\theta(\mathfrak d(K))=aCKCa^{-1}. \] Its actual image in \(V_i=V/M_i\), and then in the complete initial quotient \(V_*\), is a free group of rank five with the literal marked basis below. statement: The two actual completed sections intersect in the procyclic closure of the marked inner source \label{stmt:B153} Use B.148's actual coarse group $E^0=T_0\rtimes S$, with $T_0=F(r,\bar r,w)$, $S=F(m,u)$, and graph section $H=\{h_s^{-1}s:s\in S\}$. statement: The actual mixed fixed source has full induced topology and a marked completed section \label{stmt:B154} In the actual one-neck annular model, the subgroup $J_a=\Gamma_a^\delta\cong\mathbb Z^2*\mathbb Z$ of B.149 carries its full induced profinite topology in $\Gamma_a$. statement: The remaining local fixed-kernel question has an exact paired-free presentation with one cone factor \label{stmt:B155} Use the actual pre-node ordinary group and involution of B.123: \[ G_{\mathrm{gen}}=F_{11}\rtimes S,\qquad S=F(m,v),\qquad \Gamma_0=G_{\mathrm{gen}}/N. \] Here $N$ is the normal closure of the entire forty-node scheme, with both regions, both ordinary covering sheets and every signed source translate. Put \[ J_a=\Gamma_a^\delta =\langle A,m,v\mid[A,m]=1\rangle,\qquad U=\ker(J_a\to S),\qquad W_a=\ker(\Gamma_a\to S), \] and define $P=q_a^{-1}(J_a)$ and $Q=P\cap F_{11}$. In this presentation the ordinary remaining fixed-source question is exactly \[ (Q/N)^\delta=H_f, \qquad H_f=I_{\mathrm{src}}\rtimes\sigma(U). \] There is also the actual-closure version \begin{equation}\label{eq:B155-compact-question} (\mathcal Q/\mathcal N)^\delta=\overline{H_f}, \end{equation} with $\mathcal Q,\mathcal N$ defined in the proof. Neither displayed fixed-generation equality is asserted here.

statement: The paired relative fiber has a complete ordinary free-product basis retaining every deleted family core \label{stmt:B156} In B.155 use the actual generic orbifold tuple \[ E=F(a,b,d,e,f)*C_2(C)*C_2(\tau),\qquad x=\tau C,\qquad z^*=\tau z\tau. \] The ordinary fiber has the literal decomposition \begin{equation}\label{eq:B156-factors} F_{11}=R*D,\qquad R=F(x,a,a^*,f,f^*),\quad D=F(b,b^*,d,d^*,e,e^*). \end{equation} Let $N_a=\ker(R\to W_a)$ and $R_U=(R\to W_a)^{-1}(U)$. The displayed six deleted-family cores and all of their coset copies are therefore simultaneous free-basis letters exchanged in pairs. The retained factor $R_U$ also admits a paired free basis. These are ordinary statements; no compact free-product decomposition of this infinite-index subgroup is asserted.

statement: The actual recursive dihedral-cover heads are not cofinal for B.75's source \label{stmt:B157} Let \(G_V=\langle e,a_0,c_1,c_2\mid e^2=1\rangle\) be the actual based source of B.75. The topology generated solely by the permutation heads of all iterates of its degree-five rational cover, including finite products, restrictions, and subquotients of these heads, is strictly weaker than its full profinite topology. In particular it cannot replace the characteristic-neighborhood quantifier in B.75.6. This does not decide the actual completed residual group \(\mathcal K\).

statement: Solvable source heads cannot be cofinal, while a solvable Birman target alone gives no such obstruction \label{stmt:B158} The actual B.75 source has a specified epimorphism to \(A_5\). statement: The marked fixed-source section already exists generically, with one exact crossed defect and a minimal invariant filling \label{stmt:B159} Let $G_{\mathrm{gen}}=F_{11}\rtimes S$, $S=F(m,v)$, and let $q_a:G_{\mathrm{gen}}\to\Gamma_a$ be the composite through the FULL actual nodal quotient. There is a literal section \[ \lambda:J_a\hookrightarrow P,\qquad \lambda(A)=A_0,\quad\lambda(m)=m,\quad\lambda(v)=v, \qquad P=K_a\rtimes\lambda(J_a). \] Its involution defect \begin{equation}\label{eq:B159-crossed} \kappa(j)=\delta(\lambda(j))\lambda(j)^{-1} \end{equation} is an ordered crossed map, with \[ \kappa(A)=c_0=[a^*,a]\ne1,\qquad \kappa(m)=\kappa(v)=1,\qquad \kappa^{-1}(1)=S. \] Let $N_\lambda=\langle\!\langle c_0\rangle\!\rangle_P$. It is the smallest $P$-normal subgroup in $K_a$ for which this section becomes pointwise fixed, is $\delta$-stable, and is contained in the complete actual node kernel $N$. statement: Characteristic finite nilpotent Birman targets cannot satisfy B.75.6 for the specified alternating source quotient \label{stmt:B160} Let \(N=B_4(S_{0,4})\) and \(G_V\) have their exact B.75 markings. Consequently its identity-point stabilizer cannot be contained in B.158's specified \(U_A\). The same holds for finite collections of such targets. statement: The unfilled source double has an exact free coset kernel, and its intersections with both actual defect fillings are determined \label{stmt:B161} Let $G_{\rm gen}=F_{11}\rtimes S$, $S=F(m,v)$, be the actual generic ordinary group of B.123, with $\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)$. Use the \emph{filled} composite of B.139 \[ G_{\rm gen}\longrightarrow\Gamma_0=G_{\rm gen}/N \longrightarrow\Gamma_a, \qquad q_a:G_{\rm gen}\longrightarrow\Gamma_a. \] Put $J=\langle A,m,v\mid[A,m]=1\rangle\cong\mathbb Z^2*\mathbb Z$, $K_a=\ker q_a$, and $P=q_a^{-1}(J)$. The actual generic section $\lambda:J\to P$ of B.159 sends $A$ to $A_0=a\tau a\tau$ and fixes $m,v$. Write \[ D_0=\langle\lambda(J),\delta\lambda(J)\rangle,\qquad D_+=\langle D_0,\tau\rangle. \] Then these are actual embedded groups with presentations \begin{equation}\label{eq:B161-double} D_0=J*_{S}J,\qquad D_+=J*_{S}(S\times C_2(\tau)). \end{equation} The two copies in $D_0$ are interchanged by $\delta$. Its fold kernel $R=\ker(D_0\to J)$ is free on the entire family \begin{equation}\label{eq:B161-basis} X_{jS}=\delta\lambda(j)\lambda(j)^{-1}, \qquad jS\in J/S,\quad jS\ne S. \end{equation} Set $X_S=1$. The complete formulas are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B161-action} \begin{gathered} D_0=R\rtimes\lambda(J),\qquad \lambda(g)X_{hS}\lambda(g)^{-1}=X_{gS}^{-1}X_{ghS},\\ \delta(X_{jS})=X_{jS}^{-1}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} For $c_0=X_{AS}=[a^*,a]$, $a^*=\tau a\tau$, and $N_\lambda=\langle\!\langle c_0\rangle\!\rangle_P$, one has \begin{equation}\label{eq:B161-kernels} \begin{gathered} R=\langle\!\langle c_0\rangle\!\rangle_{D_0} =\langle\!\langle c_0\rangle\!\rangle_{D_+},\qquad N_\lambda=\langle\!\langle R\rangle\!\rangle_{K_a},\\ N_\lambda\cap D_+=N\cap D_+=K_a\cap D_0=R. \end{gathered} \end{equation} These statements retain all source words; they assert no free-product factor position for $R$ in the entire generic group.

statement: The actual unfilled double has full induced topology, while its infinite discrete fold kernel does not; the actual closed kernel has a continuous pointed-coset free model \label{stmt:B162} Use B.161. The groups $D_+$ and $D_0$ have their full induced profinite topologies in their actual generic ambient groups. Write bars for the corresponding actual closures. If \[ X=\widehat J/\widehat S,\qquad *=\widehat S, \] and $U$ is the free profinite group on the \emph{continuous pointed} space $(X,*)$, then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B162-model} \overline{D_0}=\widehat{D_0} =U\rtimes\widehat\lambda(\widehat J),\qquad \overline R=U. \end{equation} The notation means continuous pointed families of elements, not the abstract profinite completion of the discrete group in B.161. statement: The closed fold kernel has pointed-coset first cohomology, which injects into the actual deletion kernel and exactly measures its kernel on the split preimage \label{stmt:B163} Use B.161--B.162 and take every closure inside the full completion of the actual generic group. Put \[ \mathcal K_a=\overline{K_a},\qquad \mathcal P=\overline P=\mathcal K_a\rtimes \widehat\lambda(\widehat J),\qquad \mathcal R=\overline R,\qquad \mathcal N=\overline N. \] For the continuous action of $\Delta=\langle\delta\rangle\cong C_2$, there is a natural pointed homeomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B163-H1} \widehat J/\widehat S\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^1(\Delta,\mathcal R),\qquad j\widehat S\longmapsto[X_{j\widehat S}]. \end{equation} Here $H^1$ is the pointed space of cocycles $z\delta(z)=1$, modulo $z\sim b^{-1}z\delta(b)$; it is not asserted to be a group. The composite to $H^1(\Delta,\mathcal K_a)$ is injective, and its image is exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:B163-image} \ker\bigl[H^1(\Delta,\mathcal K_a) \longrightarrow H^1(\Delta,\mathcal P)\bigr]. \end{equation} Moreover $\mathcal R\le\mathcal N\le\mathcal K_a$. Consequently the map through $H^1(\Delta,\mathcal N)$ is injective as well, and its image meets the kernel of $H^1(\Delta,\mathcal N)\to H^1(\Delta,\mathcal K_a)$ only at the basepoint.

statement: The remaining local fixed-source equality is exactly a contact-image equality in nonabelian cohomology, with a complete ordered continuous source model and an equivalent cofinal finite criterion \label{stmt:B164} Use B.163 and the actual three discarded contacts $\mathscr C=\{B_s,D_s,E_s\}$ of B.150. In $\widehat{\Gamma_0}=\widehat G_{\rm gen}/\mathcal N$ put \[ \mathcal K=\mathcal K_a/\mathcal N=\overline{K_{\rm rem}},\qquad \mathcal I=\overline{I_{\rm src}}. \] The connecting map \begin{equation}\label{eq:B164-connecting} \partial:\mathcal K^\delta\longrightarrow H^1(\Delta,\mathcal N), \qquad t\mathcal N\longmapsto[t^{-1}\delta(t)] \end{equation} is an injective continuous map with closed image \[ \operatorname{im}\partial =\ker[H^1(\Delta,\mathcal N)\to H^1(\Delta,\mathcal K_a)]. \] Consequently the actual local completed equality is equivalent to \begin{equation}\label{eq:B164-gate} \begin{gathered} (\widehat{\Gamma_0})^\delta=\overline{H_{\rm src}}\\ \Longleftrightarrow\quad \ker[H^1(\Delta,\mathcal N)\to H^1(\Delta,\mathcal K_a)] =\partial(\mathcal I). \end{gathered} \end{equation} This kernel is nontrivial: it contains the nonbase class of the actual $D_s$ contact. Thus the right side cannot be replaced by injectivity of the whole cohomology map. Neither equality in \eqref{eq:B164-gate} is concluded by this proposition.

statement: The whole deletion-kernel cohomology is the completed source coset space, and the filling-kernel cohomology maps onto it with a continuous pointed section \label{stmt:B165} Retain the actual generic ordinary group of B.123/B.135 and the \emph{filled} composite of B.139: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B165-filled} G_{\mathrm{gen}}=F_{11}\rtimes S \longrightarrow \Gamma_0=G_{\mathrm{gen}}/N \longrightarrow\Gamma_a,\qquad q_a=\text{the composite}, \quad S=F(m,v). \end{equation} Here \(N\) is the whole actual node normal closure, with all forty ordinary seeds and every signed source translate. The section \(\lambda:J\to G_{\mathrm{gen}}\) sends \(A\) to \(aa^*\), where \(a^*=\tau a\tau\), and fixes \(m,v\); its completed embedding is the actual one of B.159/B.162. Let \(\Delta=\langle\delta\rangle\cong C_2\), with \(\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)\). Moreover \begin{equation}\label{eq:B165-section} H^1(\Delta,\mathcal N)\longrightarrow H^1(\Delta,\mathcal K_a) \end{equation} is surjective and has the continuous pointed section supplied by \(H^1(\Delta,\mathcal R)\). statement: The entire filling-kernel cohomology is a left-coset space of the actual fixed subgroup, with the contact source as its exact closed subspace \label{stmt:B166} Use B.165's actual groups and closures and put \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal K=\mathcal K_a/\mathcal N,\qquad \mathcal G=\mathcal P/\mathcal N =\mathcal K\rtimes\widehat\sigma(\widehat J),\\ \mathcal H=\overline{H_{\mathrm{src}}} =\mathcal I\rtimes\widehat\sigma(\widehat J), \qquad \mathcal I=\overline{I_{\mathrm{src}}} =\mathcal H\cap\mathcal K . \end{gathered} \] Here \(\widehat\sigma\) is the actual filled section of B.154; \(\mathcal H,\mathcal I\) are the closed actual contact groups, not abstract completions of their discrete kernels. Identify \(\widehat S\) with its embedded image in \(\mathcal G\). Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B166-fixed} \widehat{\Gamma_0}^{\,\delta} =\mathcal G^\delta =\mathcal K^\delta\rtimes\widehat\sigma(\widehat J), \end{equation} and there is a natural pointed homeomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B166-homeomorphism} \widehat S\backslash\mathcal G^\delta \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^1(\Delta,\mathcal N), \qquad \widehat S(t\mathcal N)\longmapsto[t^{-1}\delta(t)]. \end{equation} The left-coset convention in \eqref{eq:B166-homeomorphism} is essential. The actual contact-source image in \eqref{eq:B166-homeomorphism} is precisely the closed subspace \begin{equation}\label{eq:B166-source-subspace} \widehat S\backslash\mathcal H \ \subseteq\ \widehat S\backslash\mathcal G^\delta. \end{equation} Consequently the following are equivalent: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B166-equivalences} \begin{gathered} \widehat{\Gamma_0}^{\,\delta}=\mathcal H;\\ H^1(\Delta,\mathcal N) \text{ equals the image of }\widehat S\backslash\mathcal H;\\ \ker\!\left[ H^1(\Delta,\mathcal N)\longrightarrow H^1(\Delta,\mathcal K_a) \right]=\partial(\mathcal I). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Here \(\partial\) is B.164's injective continuous connecting map. These are equivalent formulations of the remaining local contact gate; none is asserted to hold.

statement: The actual \(m\)-orbit of \(D_s\) is a free profinite continuous family, embeds in the whole contact presentation without relations, and has a strictly different topology from its discrete infinite-rank kernel \label{stmt:B167} Retain the actual marked pair \[ H_D=\langle m,D_s\rangle\le\Gamma_0 \] of B.132. It is free of rank two and has its full induced profinite topology in the actual group with the entire node filling. Write \(\mathcal H_D=\overline{H_D}\cong\widehat F(m,D_s)\). Use the filled one-family projection, the actual source section, and the closed groups of B.150, B.154, and B.164: \[ \begin{gathered} \widehat q_a:\widehat{\Gamma_0}\longrightarrow\widehat{\Gamma_a}, \qquad \widehat J=\widehat{\langle A,m,v\mid[A,m]=1\rangle}, \qquad \widehat\sigma:\widehat J\longrightarrow\widehat{\Gamma_0},\\ \mathcal K=\ker\widehat q_a,\qquad \mathcal I=\overline{H_{\mathrm{src}}}\cap\mathcal K,\qquad \mathcal U_D=\mathcal H_D\cap\mathcal K. \end{gathered} \] Then \(\mathcal U_D\) is the free profinite group on the compact generating space \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}\), with the exact continuous marked family \begin{equation}\label{eq:B167-family} d_z=m^zD_sm^{-z}\qquad(z\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}). \end{equation} It is contained in \(\mathcal I\le\mathcal K^\delta\). For the entire continuous contact presentation of B.164, put \[ W=F_{\mathrm{prof}}\bigl(\widehat J\times\{B,D,E\}\bigr), \qquad \operatorname{ev}:W\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal I, \qquad\mathcal R_{\mathrm{src}}=\ker\operatorname{ev}. \] The closed subgroup \(W_D\) generated by \(e_{m^z,D}\) is a retract of \(W\), and evaluation identifies it with \(\mathcal U_D\). In particular \begin{equation}\label{eq:B167-restriction} \mathcal R_{\mathrm{src}}\cap W_D=1. \end{equation} The actual compact family is not the full completion of the discrete kernel \(U_{\mathrm{disc}}=\ker(H_D\to\mathbb Z_m)\): the canonical map \begin{equation}\label{eq:B167-not-completion} \widehat{U_{\mathrm{disc}}}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal U_D \end{equation} is surjective and noninjective.

statement: A specified mixed contact lies outside the entire compact \(m\)-orbit kernel of \(D_s\), with an actual finite ambient separator obtained from one prescribed \(S_4\) fiber map \label{stmt:B168} Use the commutator convention \([x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}\). In the notation of B.164 and B.167, set \[ r=[m,B_sD_sB_s^{-1}]. \] Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B168-strict} r\in\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal U_D,\qquad \mathcal U_D\subsetneq\mathcal I,\qquad \partial(\mathcal U_D)\subsetneq\partial(\mathcal I). \end{equation} The last two cohomological subspaces are compact and closed. This is a strict comparison inside the known contact image, not a counterexample to the remaining equality \(\mathcal I=\mathcal K^\delta\). The separate even-sum free-seven detector of B.132 kills \(r\); it is therefore not faithful on this actual mixed contact subgroup.

statement: The actual one-sided five-generator image has full induced profinite topology, and its whole contact kernel is an exact continuous free family receiving the actual source kernel \label{stmt:B169} Use the entire actual one-sided quotient of B.131.5: \[ \Gamma_0\longrightarrow G=F(a,B,d,E,f,h,y)\rtimes S,\qquad S=F(m,v). \] The four corrected source contacts map to \((a,B,d,E)\). The subgroup \[ H_1=\langle a,d,B,E,m\rangle\le G,\qquad H_1\cong\bigl(F(a,d)\times\mathbb Z_m\bigr)*F(B,E) \] has its full profinite topology induced by \(G\). Consequently its actual closure is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B169-image-completion} \mathcal H_1= \bigl(\widehat F(a,d)\times\widehat{\mathbb Z}_m\bigr) \amalg\widehat F(B,E)\ \le\ \widehat G. \end{equation} Here and below \(\amalg\) is the full profinite coproduct. The kernel of \(\mathcal H_1\to J_0=\widehat{\mathbb Z}_a\times\widehat{\mathbb Z}_m\) is the free profinite group on the continuous compact family \begin{equation}\label{eq:B169-compact-labels} d_i\quad(i\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}),\qquad B_{i,n},E_{i,n}\quad((i,n)\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,2}). \end{equation} Write this kernel as \(\mathcal U_1\). In the actual filled source, put \[ H_5=\langle A_s,B_s,D_s,E_s,m\rangle,\qquad \mathcal H_5=\overline{H_5}\le\widehat{\Gamma_0},\qquad \mathcal I_5=\mathcal H_5\cap\ker\widehat q_a, \] where \(\widehat q_a\) is the \emph{filled} one-family map of B.139 and B.154. The whole one-sided quotient gives \begin{equation}\label{eq:B169-source-triangle} \pi_+:\mathcal H_5\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal H_1,\qquad \pi_+(\mathcal I_5)=\mathcal U_1,\qquad \mathcal I_5\le\mathcal I. \end{equation} The group \(\mathcal I\) is the actual known contact-source kernel of B.164 and B.166. No presentation or embedding of the original \(H_5\) is asserted.

statement: The actual five-generator contact kernel retracts onto its continuous one-sided image, and the whole kernel of that image is the normal closure of the specified noncommuting contact defect \label{stmt:B170} Use the actual groups and maps of B.169, and abbreviate \(A=A_s,B=B_s,D=D_s,E=E_s\) inside the source. statement: A nontrivial pro-odd kernel in a projective group cannot be small Let $B$ be a closed subgroup of a free profinite group. Suppose that \[ 1\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow B \xrightarrow{\chi}\widehat{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow1 \] is exact. For every prime $p$, the group $K^{(p)}$ is either trivial or an infinitely generated free pro-$p$ group. Consequently, if $K$ is pro-odd and nontrivial, it has an infinitely generated free pro-$p$ quotient for some odd prime $p$. In particular such a $K$ is not topologically finitely generated. If $K$ is abelian, then $K=1$, without any pro-odd assumption.

statement: The coarse structural data of LM4 D.78 do not force its kernel to vanish There is a two-generated projective profinite group $B$, embedded as a retract of $\widehat F_2$, with a split epimorphism $\chi:B\to\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ such that \[ B^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z},\qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_2}H^1(B_0,\mathbb F_2)=1 \quad\text{for every open }B_0\leq B, \] but $\ker\chi$ is a nontrivial pro-$3$ group. Thus projectivity, these mod-two ranks, and the split pro-odd-kernel description alone do not imply $\ker\chi=1$. This is not an example of a torus involution or a refutation of the actual question C.1 of the prompt.
