statement: For $g\geq2$, distinct real components of the moduli stack with individually labelled real markings remain distinct in the procongruence extended mapping class group and in its full profinite completion. The analogous injectivity holds for unordered markings, including conjugate pairs of nonreal markings. More precisely, an isomorphism of the real arithmetic fundamental group extensions which preserves the peripheral conjugacy classes recovers the compact type $(g,r,a)$ and the real boundary incidence data of Proposition~\ref{C-boundary-order}. In the dividing case, the recovered cyclic orders on labelled marked ovals are identified only by simultaneous reversal, as in Proposition~\ref{C-marked-count}.

statement: Write \[ 1\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow P^{\pm} \xrightarrow{q} Q^{\pm}\longrightarrow1 \] for the full-completion to procongruence quotient of an extended mapping class group, and let $P$ and $Q$ denote its orientation-preserving subgroups. Fix a discrete real involution $\tau\in P^{\pm}$, put $\bar\tau=q(\tau)$, and let $\alpha=\operatorname{Ad}(\tau)$. The action \[ C_Q(\bar\tau)\times H^1(C_2,K)\longrightarrow H^1(C_2,K), \qquad q(g)\star[k]=[gk\alpha(g)^{-1}] \tag{C.15.1} \] is well defined, where $g\in P$ lifts the indicated centralizer element. The fibre over $[\bar\tau]$ of the map on conjugacy classes of orientation-reversing involutions is exactly \[ C_Q(\bar\tau)\backslash H^1(C_2,K). \tag{C.15.2} \] For every cocycle $k\in K$, the centralizer fits into the exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow K^{k\tau}\longrightarrow C_P(k\tau) \xrightarrow{q} \operatorname{Stab}_{C_Q(\bar\tau)}([k]) \longrightarrow1. \tag{C.15.3} \] In particular the image on centralizers at $\tau$ is the stabilizer of the trivial cohomology class for (C.15.1). For the general extension calculation underlying these formulas, the action does not automatically preserve that distinguished class, as the finite example in the proof verifies.

statement: Fix a hyperelliptic involution $\iota$ of $S_3$, and put $H^{\pm}=C_{\Gamma_3^{\pm}}(\iota)$ and $H=H^{\pm}\cap\Gamma_3$. The map of full profinite completions \[ \widehat{H^{\pm}}\longrightarrow\widehat{\Gamma_3^{\pm}} \tag{C.16.1} \] is injective, with image $\overline{H^{\pm}}$. Every orientation-reversing involution of this closed subgroup is $\overline H$-conjugate to a discrete involution in $H^{\pm}$. For every such discrete involution $\tau$, \[ C_{\widehat{\Gamma_3}}(\tau)\cap\overline H =C_{\overline H}(\tau) =\overline{C_H(\tau)}. \tag{C.16.2} \] Each of the six real genus-three topological types has a representative $\tau$ in this $H^{\pm}$.

statement: Let $\tau\in\Gamma_3^{\pm}$ be a real involution with at least one oval, and put \[ P=\widehat{\Gamma_3},\qquad Q=\check\Gamma_3, \qquad K=\ker(P\xrightarrow{q}Q),\qquad C=C_{\Gamma_3}(\tau). \] For closures in the indicated groups, restriction of $q$ gives an isomorphism \[ \overline C^{\,P}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } C_Q(\bar\tau)=\overline C^{\,Q}. \tag{C.17.1} \] The full profinite centralizer has the topological semidirect product description \[ C_P(\tau)=K^\tau\rtimes\overline C^{\,P}. \tag{C.17.2} \] Thus the centralizer action (C.15.1) fixes the trivial class for each of these five genus-three types. The value of the remaining group $K^\tau$ and the other cohomology orbits is not determined here. The fixed-point-free genus-three type is excluded from this theorem.

statement: Let $\tau$ be a fixed-point-free orientation-reversing involution of $S_3$, let $N_4=S_3/\langle\tau\rangle$, and put \[ E=\widehat{\pi_1(N_4)},\qquad \Delta=\widehat{\pi_1(S_3)},\qquad Q^\pm=\check\Gamma_3^\pm,\qquad Q=\check\Gamma_3. \] The inclusion of the orientation double cover gives the exact sequence $1\to\Delta\to E\to C_2\to1$, whose outer action is $\bar\tau$. Let $\operatorname{Aut}_Q(E;\Delta)$ be the group of automorphisms preserving $\Delta$ whose restriction to $\Delta$ has outer class in $Q^\pm$, and define \[ \mathcal A=\operatorname{Aut}_Q(E;\Delta)/ \operatorname{Inn}(E). \] There is a canonical topological isomorphism \[ \mathcal A \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ C_{Q^\pm}(\bar\tau)/\langle\bar\tau\rangle \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ C_Q(\bar\tau). \tag{C.18.1} \] The first arrow is induced by restriction. The second sends the class of $b$ to $b$ when $b$ preserves orientation and to $b\bar\tau$ otherwise. Under this isomorphism the closure of the ordinary mapping class group of $N_4$ is exactly $\overline{C_{\Gamma_3}(\tau)}^{\,Q}$. Consequently the remaining congruence-centralizer assertion for this type is the explicit density problem \[ \overline{\operatorname{Mod}(N_4)}^{\,\mathcal A} \stackrel{?}{=}\mathcal A. \tag{C.18.2} \] This density, and the corresponding full-completion centralizer, are not established here.

statement: Let $\tau$ be the fixed-point-free orientation-reversing involution of $S_3$, and let \[ j:\operatorname{Mod}(N_4) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}C_{\Gamma_3}(\tau) \] be the unique orientation-preserving lift of the orientation double cover, as in Proposition~\ref{C-free-reflection-comparison}. For every finite-index subgroup $H$ of $\operatorname{Mod}(N_4)$, the centralizer $C_{\Gamma_3}(j(H))$ has no nonidentity element of finite order. In particular no such $j(H)$ is contained in the centralizer of a hyperelliptic involution of $S_3$. The standard hyperelliptic mapping class subgroup of $\operatorname{Mod}(N_4)$ therefore has infinite index.

statement: Grothendieck's assertion on \S8, folio 33, scan 65 is the finiteness of $\operatorname{Sec}(C/K)$. The actual maps relevant to it are \[ C(K)\ \xrightarrow{\ \kappa\ }\ \operatorname{Sec}(C/K) \ \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{loc}\ }\ C(\mathbb A_K)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}cov}} \ \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\ \prod_{v<\infty}C(K_v)\times \prod_{v\mid\mathbb R}\pi_0(C(K_v)). \] Here $\kappa$ is injective, and $\operatorname{loc}$ is bijective. Consequently the following are exact equivalences: \[ \begin{split} \kappa\text{ is bijective} &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ C(\mathbb A_K)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}cov}}=C(K),\\ \#\operatorname{Sec}(C/K)<\infty &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \#C(\mathbb A_K)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}cov}}<\infty. \end{split} \] The first equality and Faltings's theorem give the second finiteness. Finiteness of $\operatorname{Sec}(C/K)$ gives finiteness of $C(K)$ through the displayed injection. For a finite section set, its cardinality equals that of $C(K)$ exactly when $\kappa$ is bijective.

statement: The extension with geometric kernel $\Delta^{\rm ab}=TJ$ is a class in $H^2_{\rm cts}(K,TJ)$. Its section set is empty when that class is nonzero. A choice of one section identifies its section set with $H^1_{\rm cts}(K,TJ)$. In particular, a point of $C(K)$ supplies such a choice. There are exact sequences \[ 0\longrightarrow\widehat{J(K)} \longrightarrow H^1_{\rm cts}(K,TJ) \longrightarrow T H^1(K,J)\longrightarrow0 \] and \[ 0\longrightarrow\widehat{J(K)} \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sel}(TJ) \longrightarrow T\Sha(K,J)\longrightarrow0. \] The Selmer subgroup in the second line is the inverse image of the local Kummer images at every place. Here the hats are inverse limits modulo multiplication by positive integers, and $T$ is the inverse limit of torsion with the corresponding multiplication transition maps.

statement: The abelian section set is infinite in general, even for curves of genus two with a rational base point. One example is the smooth completion of \[ C_+:\quad y^2=x^6-x^2+1. \] Moreover, on the genus-two curve \[ C_0:\quad y^2=x^5-x+1 \] with base point $\infty$, the class \[ \kappa_J\bigl(2[(0,1)-\infty]\bigr) \in H^1(K,TJ),\qquad K=\mathbb Q, \] is a global section of the abelianized extension which is induced by no point of $C_0(K_v)$ at any finite place $v$.

statement: Every section is induced by a unique rational point for every proper hyperbolic curve $C/K$ with a nonconstant map to an abelian variety $A/K$ satisfying \[ \#A(K)<\infty,\qquad \Sha(K,A)_{\rm div}=0 . \] In particular this holds for $X_0(N)$ and $X_1(N)$ over $\mathbb Q$ of genus at least two. The section set is finite in each case. Explicit genus-two examples over $\mathbb Q$ are the completions of \[ y^2=x^6+a,\qquad a\in\{-2,-1,1,2\}. \] Explicit genus-three examples are \[ y^2=x^8+4,\qquad y^2=x^8+64. \]

statement: For $K$ containing no CM subfield, the image $\operatorname{loc}_v\operatorname{Sec}(C/K)$ is finite at every finite place $v$. For arbitrary number fields $K$, the reduction of Selmer sections on a set of strongly positive density determines their classes. Strongly positive density means positive upper density after pullback to the primes of every finite extension of $K$.

statement: Put \[ L=\mathbb Q(\zeta_9,\sqrt[3]{3}),\qquad X_9:\ X^9+Y^9+Z^9=0 . \] The proper curve $X_9/L$ has genus $28$. Its geometrically pro-$3$ arithmetic fundamental group has infinitely many section classes which are induced by no $L_w$-point at a place $w$ above $3$. The same construction gives such sections after passing to each of its geometric pro-$3$ nilpotent or solvable quotients of positive class or derived length. This is an explicit instance of the global phenomenon in Hoshi's 2010 Theorems A and B, whose proof and scope we checked; we make no priority claim~\cite{Hoshi2010}.

statement: For a fixed proper curve $C/\mathbb Q$, order arithmetic quotients by their specified continuous epimorphisms $E_C\twoheadrightarrow Q$ over $G_{\mathbb Q}$: a smaller quotient is obtained by a commuting further epimorphism. Say that $Q$ has property $\mathcal P_C$ when every global section of $Q\to G_{\mathbb Q}$ is, at every place $v$, in the image of the actual map $C(\mathbb Q_v)\to\operatorname{Sect}(Q_v)/\ker(Q_v\to G_v)$. There is no least quotient with $\mathcal P_C$ for the explicit smooth projective genus-five curve \[ C:\quad y^2=-(u^6+1)(u^6+4). \tag{D11.1} \] There are two quotients $Q_1,Q_2$, each with geometric kernel $C_2$, which have no global sections and hence have $\mathcal P_C$. Their only common further quotient over $G_{\mathbb Q}$, with the indicated maps from $E_C$, is $G_{\mathbb Q}$; that quotient fails $\mathcal P_C$. Together with Proposition~\ref{D-literal-minimum}, this decides the least-quotient request in D(c) under the literal stated property. The genus-five example also has $C(\mathbb Q_2)=\varnothing$, so the failure persists when only finite places are required.

statement: Put $B=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, $F=\pi_1(B_{\overline{\mathbb Q}})$, and $N_n=\pi_1(U_{n,\overline{\mathbb Q}})$, with compatible geometric base points for the cover $t=-X^n/Z^n$. Then \[ N_n=\ker\bigl(F\longrightarrow(\mathbb Z/n)^2\bigr), \qquad F'=\overline{[F,F]}\subset N_n. \] The extensions (371), (372), and the top row of (373), in \S51.16, folios 733v--735, scans 172--175, are respectively \begin{align*} 1&\longrightarrow N_n\longrightarrow\pi_1(U_n) \longrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow1,\\ 1&\longrightarrow N_n\longrightarrow\pi_1([U_n/S_3]) \longrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q}\times S_3\longrightarrow1,\\ 1&\longrightarrow N_n/F'\longrightarrow\pi_1([U_n/S_3])/F' \longrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q}\times S_3\longrightarrow1. \end{align*} Here $S_3$ permutes homogeneous coordinates, and the second quotient is the fundamental group of $BS_3\times\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Q$. The geometric kernel in the last row is \[ N_n/F'\simeq n\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)^2. \] The intrinsic geometric abelianization and metabelian quotient are connected to this kernel by the continuous epimorphisms \[ N_n/N_n''\longrightarrow N_n/N_n'\longrightarrow N_n/F'. \] The middle group has rank $n^2+1$ as a $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$-module. Thus the precise quotient in (373) is the rank-two toric quotient. This corrects the identification of that row in Lead 4.

statement: Let $T=\mathbb G_m^3/\mathbb G_m$, with coordinates $u=X/Z$, $v=Y/Z$. The pushout of (371) by $N_n\to N_n/F'$ is isomorphic, as an extension over $G_{\mathbb Q}$, to $\pi_1(T)\to G_{\mathbb Q}$. Its section classes form \[ H^1(\mathbb Q,\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)^2) =(\widehat{\mathbb Q^\times})^2, \] where \[ \widehat{\mathbb Q^\times} =\{\pm1\}\times \left\{(a_p)_p\in\prod_p\widehat{\mathbb Z}: \ \text{for every }m,\ a_p\in m\widehat{\mathbb Z} \text{ for all but finitely many }p\right\}. \] The map to the base tripod's toric quotient sends a class $(a,b)$ to $(-a^n,-b^n)$ in multiplicative Kummer notation. For each $n$ the restriction to actual rational points of $U_n$ is injective. The image contains formal section classes independently of the equation defining $U_n$.

statement: For every positive even $n$, the intrinsic geometrically abelianized extension of $U_n/\mathbb Q$ has no section. The same holds for every quotient mapping onto its geometric pro-$2$ abelianization, including the full metabelian and full profinite extensions. The first intrinsic nilpotent obstruction is at class one. More precisely, for complex conjugation $c$, \[ H_1(U_n(\mathbb C),\mathbb Z_2) \simeq\mathbb Z_2\oplus \mathbb Z_2[C_2]^{\,n^2/2} \quad\text{as a }\mathbb Z_2[C_2]\text{-module}, \] and the real extension represents the nonzero element of $H^2(C_2,H_1)=\mathbb Z/2$.

statement: Let $U/\mathbb Q$ be a hyperbolic curve with smooth compactification $X$, and let $s$ be a Selmer section. Let $Z\subset X$ be a finite reduced subscheme. When all finite localizations of $s$ have underlying points in $Z(\mathbb Q_v)$, the section belongs to a point or cusp above an element of $Z(\mathbb Q)$. In particular, a nonconstant morphism $f:X\to W$ to a proper curve satisfying $W(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})_\bullet^{\mathrm{f-cov}}=W(\mathbb Q)$ makes every Selmer section of $U$ point-induced or cuspidal.

statement: Let $\ell$ be odd, let $N$ be a free pro-$\ell$ group of finite rank with a specified continuous action of a profinite group $G$, and put $A=N^{\mathrm{ab}}$, $B=\bigwedge^2 A$. For the actual quartic decomposition of E.17, $A=W\oplus j(V^3)$ at $\ell=3,5$, where $V=T_\ell E_+$, the mixed component for $a=b+j_{\mathbf r}h$ has at every good prime $p\ne2,\ell$ the following actual local representative. Let $v_p=b(t_p)$ and $u_p=(F_{E,p}-1)^{-1}h(F_p)$, with the choices of E.14. Its unique rational tame correction is \[ c_p=v_p\wedge j_{\mathbf r}u_p . \tag{E15.4} \] Writing $t=\min_i v_\ell(r_i)$ and $\operatorname{ord}(u_p+V)=\ell^{m_p}$, this correction is integral exactly when \[ v_\ell(v_p)+t\ge m_p\qquad(m_p>0). \tag{E15.5} \] After replacing $u_p$ by its fractional representative, the sequence of corrections is restricted exactly when $v_\ell(v_p)+t-m_p\to+\infty$ on the primes with $m_p>0$. These are the polarization and mixed support maps in LM7 E.115 and E.117, with the arithmetic linear term retained. statement: Let $P$ be the geometric pro-three group of $E\setminus\{O\}$, with free generators $x,y$, and let $N=\ker(P\to(\mathbb Z/3)^2)$. statement: Let $\mathcal G=G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}}$, and retain $\mathcal H$, $B_w$, $\mathcal A$, and $A^+$ from E.23--E.25. In the cusp basis of E.18 put \[ b_0=e_{A_0}+e_{B_0},\quad b_1=e_{A_1}+e_{B_1},\quad b_2=e_{A_2}+e_{B_2},\quad b_3=e_{C_1}+e_{C_2}. \] There is an integral decomposition with its indicated bases, \[ V^+= \mathbb Z_3(1)\{b_0,b_1+b_2,b_3\} \ \oplus\ \mathbb Z_3(1)\varepsilon_K\{b_1-b_2\}, \tag{E27.2} \] and \[ H^1(\mathcal G,V^+)=\mathbb Z_3^3\oplus\mathbb Z/3. \tag{E27.3} \] After rationalization the first three coordinates in (E27.1) are therefore uniquely specified scalar multiples of $\kappa_3(3)$ in the three displayed Tate directions, mapped to $A(-1)$ by $v\mapsto[v,w]$. statement: Let $U=E\setminus E[3]$ be the cubic curve with the specified tangential base point at $O$, and retain its rational class-three Malcev group. The origin-fixing geometric group $\mu_6$ has an actual based action on this group, normalized by the arithmetic action: \[ g\beta g^{-1}=\beta^{\chi(g)\bmod6} \qquad(g\in G_{\mathbb Q}), \tag{E.29.1} \] where $\beta$ lifts a generator of $\mu_6$ and has order six. Its cube is the rationalization of the based involution of E.24. Thus the actual class $[\eta]$ lies in the image of \[ H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S_3},A_{\mathbb Q_3}^{\mu_6}(-1)) \longrightarrow H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S_3},A_{\mathbb Q_3}(-1)). \tag{E.29.2} \] Together with E.23, E.27 and E.28, this places the class in the canonical rational direct sum \[ \operatorname{image} H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S_3},B_{\mathbb Q_3}^{\mu_6}(-1)) \ \oplus\ H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S_3},H(1)), \tag{E.29.3} \] of dimensions $2+1=3$. Here $B_{\mathbb Q_3}^{\mu_6}(-1)\simeq\mathbb Q_3(1)^2$. The first two coordinates are multiples of the Kummer class of $3$; the third is the remaining elliptic cohomology coordinate. Their actual values are not determined by this proposition. The denominator six in the based action and averaging is used rationally, so no integral torsion coordinate is discarded.

statement: Let $U=E\setminus E[3]$ be the plus Fermat cubic with origin $O$, over $\mathbb Q$, and choose the rational tangential section $s_O$ used above. In this statement $N_{\mathrm{all}}$ denotes the full geometric profinite group, and \[ M=N_{\mathrm{all}}/N_{\mathrm{all}}'',\qquad A=N_{\mathrm{all}}^{\mathrm{ab}},\qquad D=N_{\mathrm{all}}'/N_{\mathrm{all}}''. \] There is an injective continuous family of arithmetic section classes \[ \mathbb Z_3\longrightarrow \operatorname{Sec}(M\rtimes_{s_O}G_{\mathbb Q})/M, \qquad a\longmapsto[s_a], \tag{E.31.1} \] whose abelianized section is $[s_O]$ for every $a$. The class $[s_0]$ is $[s_O]$. Every $a\ne0$ gives a noncuspidal section of this full profinite metabelian quotient. Its images in every finite quotient, including quotients with several coefficient primes, are the images of this one actual continuous section. The first nonzero family member is detected in the intrinsic class-two three-primary quotient with coefficients modulo $27$. The construction does not give a lift to the full geometric fundamental group. In particular it supplies actual full metabelian classes for task LM7-E.23(iii), while the complete section image and its other fibres remain as stated in E.21.

statement: Let $n=\ell^r$ with $\ell\in\{3,5\}$ and $r\ge1$, and let $N=\pi_1(U_{n,\overline{\mathbb Q}})$ be the full profinite geometric group of the plus Fermat curve. Use the rational unit tangent at $O=[0:-1:1]$ to specify the arithmetic action. Its maximal pronilpotent quotient has the canonical description \[ N^{\mathrm{nil}}=\prod_q N^{(q)}, \qquad N/\gamma_{c+1}N\simeq \prod_q N^{(q)}/\gamma_{c+1}N^{(q)}\quad(c\ge1). \tag{E.32.1} \] Here $q$ ranges over all primes and lower central subgroups are closed. At each quotient, the cuspidal classes in this statement are the images of the actual cusp packets under $D_c\hookrightarrow\pi_1(U_n)\twoheadrightarrow E^{(c)}$. This specifies the packet map even at class one, where the normalizer of a boundary line can contain further sections. The arithmetic extension with geometric kernel $N^{\mathrm{nil}}$ has infinitely many continuous section classes whose image in every displayed positive-class nilpotent quotient is noncuspidal. Consequently no level of this full profinite nilpotent tower selects precisely the cuspidal section classes at these Fermat levels.

statement: Retain the actual rational cubic class $[\eta]$ of E.19, its compact splitting $V_{\mathbb Q_3}=H\oplus W$, and the primitive determinant vector $w=u\wedge v$. Put $x=-X/Z$, $y=-Y/Z$, so that $x^3+y^3=1$, and use the unit tangent for $q=Z/X$ at $O=[1:-1:0]$. The two functions \[ f=1-x,\qquad h=y-1 \tag{E.35.1} \] are units on $U$. Their geometric Kummer maps $\ell_f,\ell_h:V_{\mathbb Q_3}\to\mathbb Q_3(1)$ vanish on $H$. Let \[ b=\ell_f\wedge\ell_h: \bigwedge^2W\longrightarrow\mathbb Q_3(2), \qquad J:H\otimes\bigwedge^2W\longrightarrow\operatorname{Lie}_3(V), \quad J(a\otimes(r\wedge s))=[a,[r,s]]. \tag{E.35.2} \] The map $J$ is injective. The two-dimensional invariant elliptic summand $D_{HW^2}$ of E.28 is contained in its image, and contraction defines an actual $G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant isomorphism \[ \Phi=(1_H\otimes b)J^{-1}: D_{HW^2}\xrightarrow{\sim}H(2). \tag{E.35.3} \] This fixes a normalization of the remaining elliptic coordinate, without choosing a scalar generator of its one-dimensional arithmetic cohomology group. Here is its value as a specified cohomology class. Write $\Gamma=P\rtimes C_2$ for the actual free pro-three arithmetic quotient of E.16, and $\mathcal E=N\rtimes\Gamma$ for the geometrically pro-three extension with its chosen tangent. For the Hochschild--Serre edge map with the convention specified in the proof, put \[ \begin{aligned} \rho&=\kappa(f)\smile\kappa(h) \in H^2_{\rm cts}(\mathcal E,\mathbb Q_3(2)),\\ \operatorname{edge}_H(\rho)&\in H^1_{\rm cts}\bigl(\Gamma, \operatorname{Hom}(H,\mathbb Q_3(2))\bigr),\\ \iota_w(\lambda)&=u\lambda(v)-v\lambda(u). \end{aligned} \tag{E.35.4} \] In the last line the determinant twist gives the equivariant map $\iota_w:\operatorname{Hom}(H,\mathbb Q_3(2))\to H(1)$. In (E.35.5), $\Phi_*$ is induced by the explicitly twisted map $\Phi(-1):D_{HW^2}(-1)\to H(1)$. If $[\eta]_{\rm ell}$ denotes the invariant elliptic component in E.29, then \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi_*[\eta]_{\rm ell} =-\iota_{w*}\operatorname{edge}_H(\rho) \quad}\qquad\text{in }H^1(\Gamma,H(1)). \tag{E.35.5} \] Inflation gives the same equality for the original $G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}}$ action. Since $\kappa_3(-1)=0$, the cup product in (E.35.4) is also $\kappa(1-x)\smile\kappa(1-y)$, the Kummer cup attached to the Ross symbol. Formula (E.35.5) computes an exact comparison class. Its numerical three-adic value, its vanishing or nonvanishing, and the integral torsion coordinates remain unevaluated. Proposition~\ref{E-kummer-values} below evaluates the two Kummer coordinates of E.29.

statement: Retain the cubic lattice $A=\operatorname{Lie}_3(V)$, the genuine normalized cocycle $\eta$ of E.19, and the unit tangent at $O$ used in E.36. There is an explicit surjective integral $G_{\mathbb Q}$-module map \[ \Psi:A(-1)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_3(1) \quad\text{with}\quad \Psi\eta(g)=6\kappa_3(3)(g) \quad(g\in G_{\mathbb Q}). \tag{E.37.1} \] The Kummer cocycle is normalized using the positive real compatible roots of $3$. In particular the class $[\eta]$ is nonzero already after the displayed coefficient pushout and reduction modulo nine. The actual zero-abelian class-two section \[ s_{19}(g)=\kappa_3(19)(g)w\,s_O(g) \quad\text{in }N_2\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q} \tag{E.37.2} \] has no lift to $N_3\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q}$. Consequently no lift to the geometrically pro-three metabelian group, or to the full geometric group, can have (E.37.2) as its class-two image.

statement: Retain the cubic lattice $V$, the cusp order and the matrix $U$ of (E18.8)--(E18.9), and put $K=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3)$. For each nonorigin cusp $d$, let $f_d=L_d/L_O$ be the normalized tangent-line unit of E.36, and let $\ell_d:V\to\mathbb Z_3(1)$ be its geometric Kummer map. statement: Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated and let $U/K$ be a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve. For every continuous section $s:G_K\to E_U$, \[ C_{P_U}(s(H_K))=1 \quad\hbox{or}\quad C_{P_U}(s(H_K))=I_c\simeq T, \] where the second case holds precisely when $s(G_K)$ is contained in the decomposition group of a unique lifted rational cusp $c$. The centralizer of a point section is $1$. Restricting the section to an open subgroup of $H_K$ preserves this centralizer. More generally, for a closed subgroup $B\subset E_U^{\circ}$ whose projection to $H_K$ is open, $C_{P_U}(B)$ is trivial or one entire cusp inertia. Consequently the same proof recognizes every nontrivial procyclic subgroup essentially cyclotomically normalized over an open subgroup of $G_K$; no splitting of that normalizer is required.

statement: Let $L/K$ be finitely generated of characteristic zero, and let $v$ be a valuation of $L$ trivial on $K$. Fix its prolongation to $\overline L$, and write $\Gamma_v=v(L^*)$. statement: Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated, $V/K$ a smooth geometrically connected variety, $U/K$ a hyperbolic curve, and $f:E_V\to E_U$ a continuous $G_K$-homomorphism. Consequently condition (F1)(b) implies that $H$ is open or trivial. In the trivial case the actual factorization is \[ E_V\longrightarrow G_K\xrightarrow{\,s\,}E_U, \] with $s$ a continuous section. This proves the first assertion of F(b)(5) with the local section theorem explicitly supplied as tool (1) in the prompt~\cite{B_OpenAIPadic}. Its October 2026 preprint status and lack of a formal verification are retained as the status of that input; no independent proof of that input is asserted here. Together with Proposition~\ref{F-full-curve-reduction}, this completes the requested curve-target reduction, without asserting the remaining global section-surjectivity statement.

statement: The cited higher-dimensional theorems yield the following precise parts of F(b)(6). For a sub-$p$-adic field $K$, a normal variety $V/K$, a hyperbolic polycurve $U/K$ of dimension $n$, and an open arithmetic homomorphism $f:E_V\to E_U$, Hoshi's Theorem A gives a unique dominant morphism in each of these ranges: \[ \begin{array}{c|l} n&\text{additional hypotheses}\\ \hline 1&\text{none}\\ 2&\ker f\text{ is topologically finitely generated}\\ 3&\ker f\text{ is finite},\quad V\text{ is of LFG type},\quad\dim V\ge3\\ 4&f\text{ is injective},\quad V\text{ is a hyperbolic polycurve}, \quad\dim V\ge4 . \end{array} \] Here LFG means that every nonconstant morphism from a normal geometric variety to $V_{\overline K}$ has infinite geometric fundamental-group image. In dimension three the resulting map is quasi-finite and $\dim V=3$; in dimension four it is finite \'etale and $\dim V=4$. For $K/\mathbb Q$ finitely generated, Schmidt--Stix, Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.6, identify isomorphisms of strongly hyperbolic Artin neighborhoods with outer arithmetic group isomorphisms. The neighborhood hypothesis is a tower of elementary hyperbolic fibrations in which every intermediate variety embeds locally closed into a product of hyperbolic curves. Holzschuh--Schmidt--Stix, in the sharp theorem at the end of their paper, gives dominant relative Hom for $U\to S$ a relative hyperbolic curve, with $S$ normal, connected, excellent and of characteristic zero, and with sub-$p$-adic generic field. The source $V$ is normal and connected, $V\to S$ is flat and of finite type with connected geometric generic fibre, and the smooth locus of $V\to S$ surjects onto $S$. This includes the smooth surjective source in their introductory Theorem A. Its input is a $\pi_1$-open map of profinite \'etale homotopy types over $\mathrm{Et}(S)$, with its commutation homotopy. When $S$ is a hyperbolic polycurve this is exactly the corresponding relative outer-homomorphism datum, through the canonical maps to classifying spaces. Every open arithmetic map between the objects of (F1) satisfies (b). Thus the displayed Hom ranges prove both (a) and (b) for their open maps. The Isom result is the isomorphism range of the same comparison, through the explicit inclusion of isomorphisms among open homomorphisms.

statement: The assertion that an arbitrary open arithmetic map to a hyperbolic polycurve surface must come from a dominant morphism is false already for a smooth proper curve as source. For $C/\mathbb Q$ a smooth proper curve of genus at least two, there is a smooth geometrically connected ample curve $D\subset C\times C$ for which \[ E_D\longrightarrow E_{C\times C} \] is surjective and satisfies (b), although its unique geometric realization is the nondominant inclusion. Its kernel is not topologically finitely generated. For every product $U=U_1\times\cdots\times U_r$ of hyperbolic curves, every open arithmetic map from a normal variety is induced by a unique morphism to $U$, with dominance determined by that morphism's actual image. On arbitrary arithmetic maps, condition (b) is exactly the conjunction of the conditions (b) on all coordinate maps. Consequently universal (F1) for product targets over number fields is equivalent to universal (F2) for curves over number fields, through those coordinate maps.

statement: The comparisons requested in F(a) are given by the following actual forgetful maps, restrictions and identifications. For hyperbolic pairs $(X',S')$, $(X,S)$ over a number field, put $U'=X'\setminus S'$ and $U=X\setminus S$. There is a commutative square \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \operatorname{Hom}^{\rm dom,\partial}(U',U)&\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow& \operatorname{Hom}^{\rm dom}(U',U)\\ \downarrow\scriptstyle\sim&&\downarrow\scriptstyle\sim\\ \operatorname{Hom}^{\rm open}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B_{U'},\mathcal B_U) &\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow& \operatorname{Hom}^{\rm open}_{G_K}(E_{U'},E_U)/P_U . \end{array} \] The boundary superscript means the literal boundary condition $\overline f^{-1}(S)=S'$ of the corrected 1981 category. The bottom arrow forgets the boundary diagram, its local conjugators and its positive integer degrees. Its image is exactly the inverse image, under the right-hand reconstruction, of that boundary condition. Thus the open curve part of (F1) implies the corrected dominant 1981 assertion; the latter recovers the same (F1) assertion on precisely this displayed image. Every dominant geometric map is represented in the boundary category after the explicitly described shrinkings in the proof. No equivalence obtained by silently forgetting that boundary restriction is asserted. On sections of a geometric curve, the corrected admissibility condition of Longue Marche scan 79 is \[ \text{normalizes no cusp inertia} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C_{P_U}(s(H_K))=1. \] Consequently its assertion that all admissible effective lifts are point sections is equivalent to (F2), and also to the point-source case of (F1), with every cusp packet retained on the (F2) side. The letter's conjecture (7), with its packet correction, is the same point-or-cusp assertion. Its cyclotomic postscript is the right-hand zero-centralizer condition in this displayed comparison. The stronger guess of scan 433 holds for point sections and fails for every cusp section: their $H_K$-fixed subgroups are respectively $1$ and $I_c$. For the full Galois group and all open subgroups its fixed subgroup is $1$ in both cases. Thus the comparison from the full action to its restricted $H_K$-action is literally restriction of the same action, and the exact change of fixed subgroup is as stated. Axioms (1)--(6) of scans 412--421, on realized geometric objects with actual interior points, have the meanings and descent maps proved in B.13. On those objects, replacing ``interior point'' by the intrinsic zero-centralizer selection adds exactly the surjectivity assertion in (F2). For arbitrary abstract outer actions, the inclusion of the geometric objects into that larger collection does not prove essential surjectivity or the intrinsic forms of axioms (5)--(6); those are the unresolved tasks identified in Part B. The first enlargement of the explicitly stated source category in these 1983 assertions is the arbitrary regular finite-type source in scan 48. The relation to the 1981 dimension-at-most-one category is its restriction along $(X,S)\mapsto X\setminus S$. A product of two positive-dimensional hyperbolic curves has dimension two and is permitted as a source in (F1), whereas it is not an object of that stated 1981 category. statement: Let $\mathrm{SC}_{\rm nf}$ denote (F2) over all number fields. There is a proved implication from this assertion to (F2) over finitely generated characteristic-zero fields for every hyperbolic curve $U/K$ admitting a geometric finite \'etale cover $Y\to U_{\overline K}$ and a nonconstant map $Y\to A_{\overline K}$, where $A$ is defined over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$. This includes all proper hyperelliptic curves, every hyperbolic type of genus at most two, and every affine curve with such a cover mapping nonconstantly to the tripod. Every curve has a nonempty open subcurve in this last range. This is an implication between the two section assertions, not an assertion that $\mathrm{SC}_{\rm nf}$ has been proved. The general implication asked in F(c), with no cover hypothesis, remains open in this return. The precise next map after spreading already occurs over $K=k(B)$ for a hyperbolic affine curve $B$ over a number field $k$: For a smooth proper hyperbolic family $X\to B$, a generic section gives \[ r:E_B\longrightarrow E_X, \qquad p r=\mathrm{id}, \qquad E_{X_\eta}=E_X\times_{E_B}G_{k(B)}. \] Every such $r$ satisfies (F1)(b) and has non-open image. A geometric reconstruction of this particular $r$ as a map $B\to X$ is exactly a section of the family and supplies the generic rational point. The curve-target dichotomy of Proposition~\ref{F-local-dichotomy} does not provide that higher-dimensional reconstruction.

statement: Fix the rational tangent of parameter $1$ at $0$ on $T=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$. Every parameter $t\in\mathbb Q^*$ has the following exact characterization using a specified four-puncture diagram. Put \[ W_t=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,t,\infty\},\qquad p(z)=z,\quad q(z)=z/t, \qquad p,q:W_t\longrightarrow T. \] Repeated punctures at $t=1$ are simply omitted. There is a unique class in the cusp packet at $0$ of $W_t$ whose image under $q_*$ is the parameter-$1$ class; its image under $p_*$ is the parameter-$t$ class of $T$. In packet coordinates the actual maps are \[ p_*:c\longmapsto c,\qquad q_*:c\longmapsto c-\kappa(t). \] In a normalized tripod presentation $P_T=\langle x,y\rangle^{\wedge}$ with the parameter-$1$ section and \[ \rho_\sigma(x)=x^{\chi(\sigma)},\qquad \rho_\sigma(y)=f_\sigma^{-1}y^{\chi(\sigma)}f_\sigma, \qquad f_\sigma\in[P_T,P_T], \] changing that section by a cusp cocycle $c$ gives exactly \[ f^{\,c}_\sigma=f_\sigma x^{-c(\sigma)},\qquad (f^{\,c}_\sigma)^{\rm ab}=(-c(\sigma),0). \] Thus inserting the already specified Kummer cocycle $\kappa(t)$ into these relations recognizes its parameter class. Neither construction removes its input: the first retains the four-puncture diagram with cross-ratio $t$, and the second retains the Kummer character of $t$ and the chosen origin. They do not yet answer the intrinsic single-tripod GT-recognition question left in Proposition~\ref{F-open-tangents}.

statement: Let $U\to B$ be a hyperbolic curve fibration over a hyperbolic curve over a finitely generated characteristic-zero field $K$. Let $c\in(\overline B\setminus B)(K)$. Suppose that near $c$ the fibration has a smooth proper relative compactification with finite \'etale boundary. Write $Y_c$ for its hyperbolic special fibre with that boundary deleted. There is the following exact extension comparison, after a choice of specialization paths: \[ E_U\mathbin{\times}_{E_B}D_c \simeq E_{Y_c}\mathbin{\times}_{G_K}D_c. \tag{F.42.1} \] Consequently every section of $E_U\to G_K$ whose base projection is in the packet at $c$ corresponds to a pair consisting of that same cusp section and a section of $E_{Y_c}\to G_K$. When the latter is a point or cusp section, the original section has a birational lift to $G_{K(U)}$, constructed by a rank-two valuation and its specified inertia coordinates. In particular the universal curve-lifting assertion (F4)(b) over finitely generated fields implies (F4)(b) for all such surfaces whose fibration has good marked reduction at every rational base cusp after every finite extension. This extends Proposition~\ref{F-proper-polycurve-lifting} to this affine-base range. The remaining affine-base case includes genuinely bad marked reduction at the cusp selected by the projected section.

statement: Let $(X,D)$ be a smooth normal-crossings pair over a characteristic-zero field, $U=X\setminus D$, and $S=D_J^*$ a connected open stratum with its $r$ branches labelled. Write $N_j$ for their normal lines on $S$, $P_S=\prod_{j\in J,S}N_j^\times$, and $\mathcal T_S$ for the punctured henselian normal tube. Paths and geometric points are fixed in every displayed fundamental-group map. \begin{enumerate} \item Normal specialization identifies the finite-covering categories of $\mathcal T_S$ and $P_S$. Its profinite geometric homotopy sequence is \[ \pi_2^{\rm et}(S_{\bar K})\xrightarrow{(c_1(N_j))_j} T^J\longrightarrow\pi_1(\mathcal T_{S,\bar K}) \longrightarrow\pi_1(S_{\bar K})\longrightarrow1. \tag{F.43.1} \] The first map means Chern transgression, evaluated on spherical classes. The composite $\iota:T^J\to P_U$ kills its image. Thus injectivity of the full global inertia implies left exactness in (F.43.1). For a relative cusp of a hyperbolic smooth pair, the tube extension maps isomorphically onto the cusp normalizer extension of Proposition~\ref{F-torsors}, with extension class $c_1(N)$. \item At a geometric boundary point, $\iota:T^J\to P_U$ is injective precisely when every finite covering germ is an open and closed sub-germ of the restriction of a finite global covering. If $R_{\bf n}$ is the finite root stack with orders $n_i$, and $M_{\bf n}$ is the closed normal subgroup of $P_U$ generated by the $n_i$th powers of boundary inertia, then \[ \pi_1(R_{{\bf n},\bar K})=P_U/M_{\bf n},\qquad \ker(T^J\to\pi_1(R_{{\bf n},\bar K})) =\iota^{-1}(M_{\bf n}),\qquad \bigcap_{\bf n}\iota^{-1}(M_{\bf n})=\ker\iota. \tag{F.43.2} \] In particular a finite root stack can enlarge this kernel. \item Horizontal cusp inertia injects in a tower of punctured hyperbolic smooth pairs. In the recursively compatible stable toroidal range of LM5 F.39, the full crossing inertia injects as well. The hypothesis here retains the stable incidence data: the kernel of the local contact matrix is the fibre puncture or the essential vanishing cycle. On split branches the Galois action is cyclotomic; in general it also permutes the factors. A monomial map $z'_j=u_j\prod_i z_i^{m_{ji}}$ induces the matrix $(m_{ji})$ on these inertia groups. \item For $y^2=x^3+t$, the model \[ [\{Y^2=X^3+1\}\times\mathbb A^1_s/\mu_6],\qquad \zeta(X,Y,s)=(\zeta^{-2}X,\zeta^{-3}Y,\zeta s), \tag{F.43.3} \] has open part identified with the original family by $t=s^6$, $x=s^2X$, $y=s^3Y$. Its normal meridian injects; the full corner meridian does too when the infinity section is retained. On the ordinary embedded cusp resolution the two exceptional-tail crossing maps instead have respective kernels $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(-3,1)$ and $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(-2,1)$. These are maps into the same open fundamental group, with the explicit substitutions above and in the proof. \item The maps in (F.43.1), restricted to a relative cusp or a trait meeting that cusp, are exactly the maps in FLAGGED\_149 C3, C4, C6, C8, and C9. C1, C2, and C5 give the corresponding extension tests for an \emph{already given rational geometric section}. Their geometric premise is retained; the tests do not construct a geometric point from an arbitrary section. \end{enumerate} This supplies the added comparison of LM5 F.21--F.23, F.35, F.39 with FLAGGED\_149 C1--C6, C8, C9.

statement: Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated and let $U\to B$ be a hyperbolic curve fibration over a hyperbolic curve. Let $s:G_K\to E_U$ project to a cuspidal section $\tau$ at $c\in(\overline B\setminus B)(K)$. Suppose the fibre over $K((t))$, for a parameter $t$ at $c$, has potentially good marked reduction. Let $Y_\tau/K$ be the smooth residue curve obtained by the descent construction of Proposition~\ref{F-reduction}; it has an identified arithmetic extension \[ E_{Y_\tau}\simeq E_{U_{K((t))}}\mathbin{\times}_{G_{K((t))},\tau}G_K. \tag{F.44.1} \] Every $s$ whose induced section in (F.44.1) is a point or cusp section has a birational lift $G_K\to G_{K(U)}$. The lift can be obtained through the decomposition group of a rank-two valuation of $K((t))(U)$ with residue $K$. Consequently universal curve lifting implies surface lifting for hyperbolic fibrations with potentially good marked reduction at every rational base cusp after finite constant extension. This extends the good-reduction range of Proposition~\ref{F-good-boundary-lifting}; the implication is an implication between the two universal assertions, not an assertion of universal curve lifting.

statement: Let $K$ be a number field, $U=\mathbb P^1_K\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, $E=\pi_1(U)$, and $\Delta=\ker(E\to G_K)$. Fix an actual lifted cusp inertia $I_0\subset\Delta$ above $0$ and a continuous section $s:G_K\to N_E(I_0)$. Its class is induced by a nonzero $K$-rational tangent vector at $0$ precisely when the following entirely group-theoretic relation holds. There exist an open subgroup $H\subset E$ with image $G_K$, a cusp inertia $J$ of $H$, a continuous section $\sigma:G_K\to N_H(J)$ of the arithmetic projection, and two continuous open homomorphisms over $G_K$, \[ p,q:H\longrightarrow E, \] such that \[ \begin{gathered} p|_J:J\xrightarrow{\sim} I_0,\qquad q(j)=p(j)^2\quad(j\in J),\\ [p\circ\sigma]=[q\circ\sigma]=[s] \quad\text{modulo conjugation by }\Delta. \tag{F.45.1} \end{gathered} \] Here a cusp inertia of $H$ is an intersection $H\cap aI_i a^{-1}$ for one of the three ambient peripheral classes and an actual geometric conjugator $a$. The peripheral classes themselves are characterized by the cyclotomic-normalizer criterion. Thus all the quantifiers in (F.45.1) refer to the one ambient arithmetic group, its open subgroups, their continuous homomorphisms, and their sections; the test does not first declare any source section geometric. The same relation after restriction to some finite extension $L/K$ is equivalent to (F.45.1) over $K$. For every specified $t\in K^\times$, one can moreover choose $H,J,p,q$ so that the common-image relation in (F.45.1), with $\sigma$ in that cusp packet, has the unique image $[s_t]$, the tangent with coordinate $t$ in the standard coordinate $z$ at $0$. This supplies a uniform global relation recognizing the geometric splittings in F(g)(5), using two open Hom maps. It does not replace those maps by a word involving only the automorphisms of the tripod or only the two entries of a Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller pair. That more restrictive formula remains the separate question in Proposition~\ref{F-open-tangents}.

statement: In Theorem~\ref{F-two-Hom-tangents} over $K=\mathbb Q$, impose the additional requirement that both $p$ and $q$ be injective. The resulting relation holds exactly for \[ [s_{16}],\quad [s_{-16}]. \tag{F.46.1} \] More generally, over a number field $K$, every tangent parameter selected by this restricted relation belongs to $16\mu(K)$, where $\mu(K)$ is the group of roots of unity in $K$. This conclusion still holds when the local degrees one and two in that relation are replaced by any two unequal positive degrees $d,e$: require that $p$ and $q$ send the selected cusp inertia into $I_0$ with these respective indices, and keep the common-image equation for the section. Every common image is then an ordinary tangent in $16\mu(K)$. In particular, over $\mathbb Q$ even the union of all these unequal-degree finite-\'etale tests selects exactly the two classes in (F.46.1). The condition $d\ne e$ is essential: taking $p=q$ gives an equal-degree relation satisfied by every member of the corresponding packet. The additional requirement is exactly that the two reconstructed morphisms from the common finite cover to the tripod are finite \'etale. In that case $q\circ p^{-1}:p(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}q(H)$ is an actual isomorphism between open arithmetic subgroups. Thus the forgetful map from these finite-cover relations to the open-Hom relations of Theorem~\ref{F-two-Hom-tangents} has a strictly smaller set of common section images: $[s_2]$ is an explicit witness. This refutes replacing the two maps in that criterion by such commensurations while retaining its inertia degrees and equal-image equation. It makes no assertion that every different formula using only GT automorphisms has this same restriction.

statement: Put $K=\mathbb Q(i)$, $\Gamma=G_K$, $\Gamma^\circ=G_{K(\mu_\infty)}$, and $U=\mathbb P^1_K\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$. There is an abstract semilinear $\Gamma$-action on the geometric universal covering $\mathcal U$ of this same tripod for which the following statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item Its restriction to every open subgroup of $\Gamma^\circ$ is not functionwise continuous. Its action on the finite geometric homology quotient $H_1(U_{\overline K},\mathbb F_3)$ is already discontinuous. \item No open subgroup of $\Gamma^\circ$ admits a finite-type quotient $\mathcal U\to W$ which is a connected pro-\'etale covering and on which the induced semilinear action is functionwise continuous. In particular, no open subgroup of $\Gamma$ admits such a quotient. \item The completed universal covering nevertheless has exactly one fixed pro-point under this abstract $\Gamma^\circ$-action, namely the chosen lift of $1/2$. It is also fixed by the whole abstract $\Gamma$-action. \end{enumerate} Thus the inclusion of continuous actions into abstract actions is strict already on the actual cyclotomic-kernel domain occurring in (B$'$). The continuous finite-form descent of Proposition~\ref{F-continuous-action} does not extend to these actions. The universal fixed-point existence assertion for arbitrary abstract actions is neither proved nor refuted by this example.

statement: A positive-density set with the same exact one-prime reduction. statement: Tame abelian inertia in a metabelian section lies on one cusp line. Let $k$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_q$ with $q\ne3$, and let \[ s:G_k\longrightarrow(N/N'')\rtimes G_k \] be a continuous section. statement: Class-two mixed examples have no metabelian or marked-depth lift. Let $I_{\rm mark}$ be the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia at $Q_c$, so that the marked depth quotient in the task is $N/\gamma_3(I_{\rm mark})$. The class-two sections of A.5 and A.6 have no lift to either \[ N/N''\quad\text{or}\quad N/\gamma_3(I_{\rm mark}). \tag{A.18.1} \] This holds for every class-two lift of their specified $N^{\rm cc}$ sections, and continues to hold after every finite number-field extension. statement: The relative arithmetic presentation at every inert prime $q\equiv2,5\pmod9$. Put \[ \Xi=\{q\text{ prime}:q\equiv2\text{ or }5\pmod9\}. \tag{A.25.1} \] This set has natural density $1/3$ and contains $2$. For $q\in\Xi$ let $\mathfrak q=(q)$ be the unique prime of $K_0$ above $q$, and write $P_q=G_{K_0,\{\lambda,\mathfrak q,\infty\}}(3)$. After conjugating the local embedding compatibly with the fixed global complex conjugation, there is an isomorphism \[ P_q\simeq D_{q^2}*_{3}\mathbb Z_3^{\langle z\rangle}, \qquad D_{q^2}=\langle\phi,\tau\mid \phi\tau\phi^{-1}=\tau^{q^2}\rangle_3, \tag{A.25.2} \] and its relative arithmetic quotient is \[ \Gamma_q\simeq (D_{q^2}*_{3}\mathbb Z_3^{\langle z\rangle}) \rtimes\langle c\rangle, \qquad c\phi c^{-1}=\phi,\quad c\tau c^{-1}=\tau^{-1},\quad czc^{-1}=z^{-1}. \tag{A.25.3} \] Here $c^2=1$. Thus $\sigma=zc$ is another involution, with no further relation beyond (A.25.3). The source category in these presentations consists of profinite groups whose kernel over $\langle c\rangle$ is pro-three; the kernel free product is precisely the pro-three free product, as displayed. For an inert prime $q\equiv8\pmod9$, the two unit Frobenius values used in this construction are both zero modulo three. In particular $q=17$ is the smallest prime not covered by $\Sigma\cup\Xi$; (A.25.2) is not asserted there. The union $\Sigma\cup\Xi$ has natural density $5/9$. \par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.16, folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379).}

statement: The normalized integral Frobenius at an inert prime and the explicit Heisenberg test at seventeen. Retain the free pro-three basis $u,v=cuc$ of $P_3$ from A.10, and write $[u,v]=uvu^{-1}v^{-1}$. For an inert rational prime $q\ne3$, conjugate its local order-two complement in $P_3\rtimes\langle c\rangle$ to $\langle c\rangle$. Let $\varphi_q\in P_3$ be the resulting arithmetic Frobenius of the prime of $K_0$ of norm $q^2$. Its image in the integral class-two quotient is exactly \[ \varphi_q\bmod\gamma_3P_3 =u^{a_q}v^{a_q}[u,v]^{-a_q^2/2}, \qquad a_q=\frac{\log(-q)}{\log7}\in\mathbb Z_3. \tag{A.27.1} \] The image in (A.27.1) is independent of the conjugator used to identify the local order-two complement with $\langle c\rangle$. Put $\theta=\zeta_9$, $\beta^3=\lambda$, and \[ u_i=1-\zeta^i\theta\quad(0\le i\le2),\qquad \omega=u_1u_2^2, \qquad L=K_0(\theta,\beta,\omega^{1/3}). \tag{A.27.2} \] Then $L/K_0$ is the full exponent-three class-two quotient of $P_3$: its Galois group has order $27$ and presentation \[ \langle\sigma,\tau,\rho\mid \sigma^3=\tau^3=\rho^3=1,\quad \rho\text{ central},\quad[\sigma,\tau]=\rho\rangle. \tag{A.27.3} \] The field is Galois over $\mathbb Q$, and complex conjugation acts by \[ c\sigma c=\tau\sigma, \qquad c\tau c=\tau^{-1}, \qquad c\rho c=\rho^{-1}. \tag{A.27.4} \] For every prime $q\equiv8\pmod9$, the Frobenius of the prime of $K_0$ above $q$ is trivial in (A.27.3). In particular this holds at $17$, although $v_3(a_{17})=1$ in the integral formula (A.27.1). statement: The exact equivariant one-relator presentation at every inert prime. Let $q\ne3$ be any inert rational prime, and let $P_q=G_{K_0,\{3,q\}}(3)$ and $\Gamma_q=P_q\rtimes\langle c\rangle$. After the local-complement identification used in A.27, choose a tame generator $t$ and an arithmetic Frobenius $\phi$ at the prime over $q$, with \[ c(t)=t^{-1},\qquad c(\phi)=\phi, \qquad \phi t\phi^{-1}=t^{q^2}. \tag{A.28.1} \] Choose a lift $x\in P_q$ of $u\in P_3$ and put $y=cxc$. The lift can and will be chosen with $\kappa_q(x)=0$ modulo three. Let $F=F_3(x,y,t)$ be the free pro-three group with involution $c(x)=y$, $c(y)=x$, $c(t)=t^{-1}$. Its natural equivariant map to $P_q$ is surjective. There is a $c$-fixed pro-three word $W\in F$ mapping to the actual local Frobenius $\phi$, and for every such choice the natural map gives the exact presentations \[ \begin{split} P_q&\simeq F/\overline{\langle\!\langle WtW^{-1}t^{-q^2}\rangle\!\rangle},\\ \Gamma_q&\simeq \bigl(F/\overline{\langle\!\langle WtW^{-1}t^{-q^2}\rangle\!\rangle}\bigr) \rtimes\langle c\rangle. \end{split} \tag{A.28.2} \] These are continuous pro-three presentations, with the indicated finite operator group in the second line. In particular \[ P_q^{\mathrm{ab}}\simeq \mathbb Z_3^2\oplus\mathbb Z_3/(q^2-1), \qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_3}H^2(P_q,\mathbb F_3)=1. \tag{A.28.3} \] At $q=17$, $W$ lies in $\Phi(F)$, and the relator in (A.28.2) lies in the third Zassenhaus subgroup of $F$. Its image on killing $t$ is the actual Frobenius of A.27; in particular its integral class-two image is given by (A.27.1) and (A.27.5). For any of the geometric quotients $B$ under consideration, (A.28.2) gives the following exact section parameterization. Normalize the value at $c$ to one; assign the values $a,c(a),b$ at $x,y,t$. If $\Omega_W(a,b)$ denotes the value at $W$ of this continuous free-group cocycle, the remaining equations are precisely \[ c(b)=b^{-1},\qquad \Omega_W(a,b)F_{q^2}(b)\Omega_W(a,b)^{-1} =b^{q^2}. \tag{A.28.4} \] Classes are the orbits under $B^c$ acting by \[ (a,b)\longmapsto (h^{-1}a\,x(h),\ h^{-1}bh). \tag{A.28.5} \] \par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.16, folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379); Tasks A.6 and B.4 beyond the prime families A.16 and A.25.}

statement: The nonzero cubic Frobenius term at seventeen and its failure to be a cube. Let $L_0=K_0(\alpha)$ with $\alpha^3=3$, and let $H=G_{L_0,\{3\}}(3)\subset P_3$. statement: The exact marked global image and ramified fibers on $\Sigma\cup\Xi$. Put $R=N/\gamma_3(I_{\mathrm{mark}})$, $A=N/\gamma_3N$, and $J_R=\ker(R\to A)$. For every $q\in\Sigma\cup\Xi$, the three global class-two images coincide and are exactly \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(N) \to\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(A)\bigr) &=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(N/N'') \to\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(A)\bigr)\\ &=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(R) \to\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(A)\bigr) =\operatorname{res}_q^{-1}(\mathscr L_q), \end{split} \tag{A.32.1} \] where $S_q=\{3,q,\infty\}$ and $\mathscr L_q$ is the actual local unramified and cusp-packet set of A.24. Fix a ramified class-two target in this image and let $d\in D(\mathbb Q_q)$ be its unique local cusp. Define its local marked lifting-class set by \[ \mathcal L_{q,d}= \begin{cases} \{*\},&d\ne Q_c,\\ \mathcal C_{\mathbb Q_q,Q_c},&d=Q_c, \end{cases} \tag{A.32.2} \] using exactly the reference and quotient of B.12--B.13. Restriction gives a surjection from the global marked fiber onto $\mathcal L_{q,d}$. For each element of this local class set, choose a normalized global marked lift above it. The inverse image of that element is precisely \[ \begin{cases} J_R/J_R^c,&q\in\Sigma,\\ J_R^\Theta\backslash J_R,&q\in\Xi, \end{cases} \tag{A.32.3} \] with right and left cosets, respectively. In the second case $\Theta=\operatorname{Ad}(X_0)\circ\sigma$ is the actual involution specified by the chosen lift in A.26. Thus (A.32.2)--(A.32.3) describe the entire fiber without identifying different local marked classes or asserting a canonical product decomposition. Targets unramified at $q$ have exactly the unramified fiber of A.20 for $R\to A$. The exact image of $\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(N)\to \operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(R)$ consists of the classes unramified at $q$, the unmarked ramified cusp classes, and the marked ramified classes whose local parameter in $\mathcal C_{\mathbb Q_q,Q_c}$ is zero. Its nonempty ramified fibers are given by (A.32.3) with $J_R$ replaced by $\gamma_3(I_{\mathrm{mark}})$ and the corresponding chosen full lift. In particular there are global marked sections supported at $\{3,q\}$ which have no full lift, although their class-two image has a full lift. These examples still have no full lift after any finite number-field extension. \par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.16, folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379); the marked higher image and fibers in Task A.6.}

statement: A class-three lift for every finite-support locally cuspidal class-two section. Let $S'$ be any finite set of rational primes containing three, with the real place included. Put $A=N/\gamma_3N$ and $M_3=\gamma_3N/\gamma_4N$. Every section of $A$ over $G_{\mathbb Q,S'}$ whose restriction at each $q\in S'\setminus\{3\}$ belongs to the actual local image $\mathscr L_q$ of B.8 has a section lift to $N/\gamma_4N$ over the same arithmetic group. Its lifting fiber is a torsor under \[ H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S'},M_3) =H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},M_3) =\mathbb Z_3^{166}\oplus(\mathbb Z/3)^7 \oplus(\mathbb Z/9)^{56} \oplus(\mathbb Z/27)^{25} \oplus(\mathbb Z/81)^3. \tag{A.33.1} \] These assertions concern the actual common class-three quotient of the full and metabelian groups. There is also an exact obstruction to choosing this global lift with prescribed actual cuspidal local class-three restrictions. Let $J\subset S'\setminus\{3\}$ be the primes where the class-two target is ramified. Choose any global class-three lift $s_3$. At each $q\in J$ the unique actual cuspidal class-three lifting class determines a difference $\Delta_q(s_3)\in M_3/(F_q-1)M_3$. The element \[ \left[(\Delta_q(s_3))_{q\in J}\right] \in\operatorname{coker}\left( H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},M_3) \xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}} \bigoplus_{q\in J}M_3/(F_q-1)M_3\right) \tag{A.33.2} \] is independent of $s_3$. It vanishes exactly when a global class-three lift can have all the indicated cuspidal restrictions. Every full or metabelian global lift of the class-two target forces (A.33.2) to vanish.

statement: The restriction map at seventeen and a class-three lift that stops at class four. Use the actual arithmetic generators $m,n,c$ of A.31. On the degree-three lattice $M_3$, the restriction map \[ H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},M_3) \longrightarrow H^1(G_{\mathbb Q_{17}},M_3) =M_3/(F_{17}-1)M_3 \tag{A.34.1} \] has image of dimension $15$ after reduction in the local target modulo three. The target modulo three has dimension $164$, and the cokernel of (A.34.1) modulo three therefore has dimension $149$. Fix free geometric generators $x_0,\ldots,x_9$ whose abelianizations are the integral basis of A.7, with the first eight entries the non-$O$ cusp generators. In $M_3$ put $e=[[x_8,x_0],x_9]$. The exact normalized cocycle \[ \beta(c)=0,\qquad \beta(m)=(1+c)e, \qquad\beta(n)=0 \tag{A.34.2} \] is unramified outside three. Start with the actual full $O$-cuspidal section whose tangent parameter is $17$, project it to $N/\gamma_4N$, and twist by $\beta$. The resulting global section $s_3$ has the same class-two image as that full cuspidal section, but $s_3$ has no lift to $N/\gamma_5N$. In particular it has no full or metabelian lift, and no lift to the marked quotient with marked cusp $Q_c$. Thus a class-two target with a full lift can have a class-three lifting class with a nonzero next obstruction. The theorem does not assert non-lifting of that class-two target: its original full cuspidal lift is specified above.

statement: A fifteen-dimensional toric family with zero first mod-three gluing class. Let $B\in(\bigwedge^2W)^{c=-1}$. This eigensublattice has rank fifteen. The exact prescriptions \[ \gamma_B(c)=0,\qquad \gamma_B(m)=0, \qquad\gamma_B(n)=B \tag{A.35.1} \] define an unramified-outside-three class-two central cocycle. Twist the class-two image of the global $O$-cuspidal section with tangent parameter $17$ by $\gamma_B$. Its restriction at seventeen is the same actual class-two cusp section, including its Frobenius coordinate. This target has a global class-three lift with unchanged local inertia. For the exact gluing class (A.33.2), its image in the cokernel of (A.34.1) modulo three is zero. No assertion of integral vanishing of (A.33.2) is made here.

statement: Miller covers and their two exact norm comparisons at seven. The Fermat curve in the task has the following specified isomorphism with the minimal Weierstrass curve $E_m:y_m^2+y_m=x_m^3-7$: \[ x_m=\frac{-3z}{x+y},\quad y_m=\frac{4x-5y}{x+y},\qquad [x:y:z]=[y_m+5:4-y_m:-3x_m]. \tag{A.36.1} \] It carries $O$ to the Weierstrass origin and carries $P,Q_c$ to $(3,-5),(3,4)$, respectively. All of $E_m[9]$ is defined over the unramified degree-three extension of $\Q_7$. Its reduction over $k=\F_7[\theta]/(\theta^3-2)$ has exactly 81 points. One point above $P$ under multiplication by three is \[ Q=(2+\theta^2,\ 1+\theta+6\theta^2),\qquad \varphi Q-Q=(6,2), \tag{A.36.2} \] where $\varphi$ raises the residue coordinates to their seventh powers. The unique nine-torsion lifts give the corresponding identities over the unramified local extension. For each of the nine points $Q$ above either $d=P$ or $d=Q_c$, let $v_R=x_m-x_m(R)$ and let $\ell_{R,S}$ be the line through $R,S$, tangent at $R$ when $R=S$, normalized to have $y_m$ coefficient one. Then the actual function \[ a_Q=\frac{\ell_{Q,Q}\ell_{2Q,Q}}{v_{2Q}v_d},\qquad \operatorname{div}(a_Q)=3(Q)-(d)-2(O), \tag{A.36.3} \] defines a connected cubic cover $w^3=a_Q$ which is finite \'etale over $U$. Its geometric character is an explicit Kummer class with nonzero cusp valuations at $d,O$. With $\iota(R)=-R$, the following function identities hold: \[ a_Q\,\iota^*a_Q=\frac{(x_m-x_m(Q))^3}{x_m-x_m(d)}, \qquad \prod_{i=0}^2 a_{\varphi^iQ}=g_Q^3. \tag{A.36.4} \] In the second identity, put $Q_i=\varphi^iQ$, $S=Q_0+Q_1$, and \[ g_Q=\frac{\ell_{Q_0,Q_1}\ell_{S,Q_2}}{v_Sv_d}. \tag{A.36.5} \] This function is defined over $\Q_7$, and its reduction is defined over $\F_7$. For the exact Fermat parameter $s=z/x$ and its unit tangent, the regularized constants are \[ (s^2a_Q)(O)=9, \qquad (s^2(x_m-3))(O)=(s^2(x_m-3\zeta^2))(O)=9. \tag{A.36.6} \] In the large model $Y^2=X^3-432$, $X=4x_m$, $Y=8y_m+4$, the corresponding normalized Miller function is $4a_Q$, with regularized constant 36. For the residue embedding $\zeta\mapsto2\in\F_7$, the cubic residue of 9 is $4=\zeta^2$, whereas that of 36 is 1. These are arithmetic cover data; no central Galois action on an intrinsic Heisenberg quotient is inferred from them.

statement: An order-eighty-one arithmetic quotient and a tame-letter Frobenius coefficient at seventeen. Put $K_0=\mathbb Q(\zeta)$, $\zeta^2+\zeta+1=0$, and $L_{17}=K_0(\beta)$ with $\beta^3=17$. Let $\sigma(\beta)=\zeta\beta$ and set \[ \delta=\frac{-7-\zeta-3\beta-\beta^2}{3},\qquad \delta_i=\sigma^i(\delta),\qquad r_i^3=\delta_i\quad(i\in\mathbb Z/3). \tag{A.37.1} \] The extension \[ M_{17}=L_{17}(r_0,r_1,r_2)/K_0 \tag{A.37.2} \] is Galois, unramified outside three and seventeen, with group \[ G=(\mathbb F_3)^3\rtimes\langle s\rangle, \qquad s^3=1, \tag{A.37.3} \] where $s(r_i)=r_{i+1}$ and $s(\beta)=\zeta\beta$. For $a=(a_0,a_1,a_2)$ write $\tau_a(r_i)=\zeta^{a_i}r_i$, $\tau_a(\beta)=\beta$. Then $s\tau_as^{-1}=\tau_{Sa}$, where $(Sa)_i=a_{i-1}$. The group has order $81$, lower-central orders $81,9,3,1$, exponent nine, and trivial fourth three-Zassenhaus subgroup. Use the arithmetic generators $m,n,t$ of A.28 and A.31, with the exact Kummer normalization of A.35. Their modulo-three characters are \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} &m&n&t\\\hline \kappa_\zeta&1&0&0\\ \kappa_{17}&0&0&1 \end{array}. \tag{A.37.4} \] The restriction map to (A.37.2), composed with the actual free pro-three presentation, is a continuous epimorphism \[ F_3(m,n,t)\longrightarrow G_{K_0,\{3,17\}}(3)\longrightarrow G. \tag{A.37.5} \] Let $W\in D_3(F_3(m,n,t))$ be the actual arithmetic Frobenius word of A.30. Under (A.37.5), \[ W\longmapsto\tau_{(2,2,2)},\qquad [t,[t,m]]\longmapsto\tau_{(1,1,1)}. \tag{A.37.6} \] In the restricted degree-three Lie algebra $D_3(F_3)/D_4(F_3)$, this map annihilates the three generator cubes and every ordinary degree-three component except the multidegree $(1,0,2)$ component generated by $[t,[t,m]]$. Consequently the coefficient of this bracket in the full $W$ is exactly $2\in\mathbb F_3$. This records a coefficient involving tame inertia; the map killing $t$ in A.31 does not retain it. \par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.16, folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379); Tasks A.6 and B.4.}

statement: An actual Frobenius basis with completely specified finite class-two action. Let $F_2=\langle x,y\rangle$ be the geometric pro-three group of $\mathbb P^1-\{0,1,\infty\}$, based at the unit tangent at zero, and let \[ N=\ker(F_2\longrightarrow(\mathbb Z/3)^2),\qquad K=N^3\gamma_3N. \tag{A.38.1} \] Here $N^3$ is the closed subgroup generated by cubes. There is an actual Frobenius $u$ at the prime $(7,\zeta-2)$ of $K_0$ such that $u,v=cuc$ are a free basis of $P_3$, their integral action on $V$ is exactly A.7, and their action on $N/K$ is the following fully specified finite action. Complex conjugation is induced by $x\mapsto x^{-1},y\mapsto y^{-1}$. The restriction of Frobenius $u$ to $N/K$ equals the restriction of the following automorphism of $F_2/K$: \[ x\longmapsto x^7,\qquad y\longmapsto f_0^{-1}y^7f_0. \tag{A.38.2} \] In the ordered Schreier basis \[ \begin{split} &(yxy^{-1}x^{-1},\ y^2xy^{-2}x^{-1},\ y^3,\ xyxy^{-1}x^{-2},\ xy^2xy^{-2}x^{-2},\ xy^3x^{-1},\\ &\hspace{25mm}x^3,\ x^2yxy^{-1},\ x^2y^2xy^{-2},\ x^2y^3x^{-2}), \end{split} \tag{A.38.3} \] write $N/K$ as $\mathbb F_3^{10}\oplus\bigwedge^2\mathbb F_3^{10}$ with product $(a,z)(b,w)=(a+b,z+w+\tfrac12a\wedge b)$. The word-class representative $f_0$ defining this finite automorphism has coordinates \[ a_f=(0,0,1,1,2,0,2,0,1,2), \tag{A.38.4} \] and, in lexicographic order $i<j$, the forty-five central coordinates are \[ \begin{split} z_f={}&(2,1,2,1,1,2,0,1,2,\ 1,1,0,0,0,2,2,0,1,\\ &1,1,1,1,1,0,1,1,0,0,1,2,0,0,1,0,1,1,\\ &0,0,1,2,0,2,2,0,0). \end{split} \tag{A.38.5} \] Thus (A.38.2)--(A.38.5) specify every coordinate of the images of the ten geometric generators. They specify a representative for the induced finite action; the actual Ihara word can differ by the kernel of its map to that action. The arithmetic basis is obtained from any initial Frobenius basis by at most four explicitly described conjugations below. The underlying Galois action and tangential origin are retained; all cocycles and all arithmetic Frobenius words are transported by the resulting actual source automorphism.

statement: Global exclusions at seventeen inside the exact local cusp packet. Use the actual arithmetic basis of A.38, with $m,n$ and the normalized local Frobenius $\varphi=\varphi_{17}$ transported as there. Put $M_2=\bigwedge^2V$ and define the integral normalized cochain module and its actual evaluation map by \[ \begin{split} D&=M_2^{c=1}\oplus M_2^{nc=-1},\\ E_\varphi:D&\longrightarrow M_2^{c=1},\quad (a,b)\longmapsto\gamma_{a,b}(\varphi),\\ R&=\ker E_\varphi. \end{split} \tag{A.39.1} \] Here $\gamma_{a,b}$ is the unique continuous cocycle on $P_3\rtimes\langle c\rangle$ with values $(a,b,0)$ at $(m,n,c)$. The lattice $D$ has rank $45$, and $R$ is a saturated lattice of rank $24$. For $r\in R$, twist the class-two image of the global $O$-cuspidal section with tangent parameter $17$ by $\gamma_r$. This defines an injectively parameterized family of global class-two section classes, unramified outside $\{3,17,\infty\}$. Every member has the same exact local $O$-cusp section at seventeen, including its Frobenius coordinate, and every member has a global class-three lift. There is an $\mathbb F_3$-linear obstruction on $R/3R$ of rank at least three which vanishes on every member lifting to any of \[ N,\qquad N/N'',\qquad N/\gamma_3(I_{Q_c}). \tag{A.39.2} \] Consequently, from any integral basis $r_1,\ldots,r_{24}$ of the kernel in (A.39.1), at least three of the resulting twenty-four class-two section classes have none of the lifts in (A.39.2). This is an unconditional finite-family existence certificate. It does not select an unevaluated individual basis vector as a counterexample. No assertion of full local liftability at three is included. An individually specified member of $R$ with nonzero obstruction, including all integral generator coordinates and a nine-term detecting functional, is given in B.20.

statement: The exact completed Fox image and fibers on the cusp family. For the family $R$ in A.39 put \[ Q=N/N'',\qquad M=N'/N'',\qquad \Lambda=\mathbb Z_3[[V]],\qquad \mathfrak a=\ker(\Lambda\to\mathbb Z_3),\qquad J=\mathfrak aM. \tag{A.41.1} \] Give $M$ the arithmetic action twisted by the actual reference $O$ section with tangent parameter $17$. Thus $m,n,c$ have their original actions, and tame inertia acts by conjugation by $c_O$. Define \[ \begin{split} D_M&=M^{c=1}\oplus M^{nc=-1},\qquad D_J=J^{c=1}\oplus J^{nc=-1},\\ E_W:D_M&\longrightarrow M^{c=1},\qquad E_W(a,b)=\beta_{a,b}(W), \end{split} \tag{A.41.2} \] where $\beta_{a,b}$ is the continuous crossed cochain on the free arithmetic source with values $(a,b,0,0)$ at $(m,n,t,c)$. These are continuous linear maps of compact $\mathbb Z_3$-modules. The natural quotient $M\to M_2$ gives $\pi:D_M\twoheadrightarrow D$, with kernel $D_J$, and the complete metabelian image on this family is exactly \[ R_{\rm met}=\pi(\ker E_W)\subset R. \tag{A.41.3} \] Equivalently, it is the kernel of the explicit continuous map \[ \begin{split} \mathfrak o_M:R&\longrightarrow J^{c=1}/E_W(D_J),\\ r&\longmapsto[\,E_W(\widetilde r)\,], \end{split} \tag{A.41.4} \] where $\pi(\widetilde r)=r$. Every nonempty fiber of $\operatorname{Sec}(Q)\to\operatorname{Sec}(N/\gamma_3N)$ over this family is an affine copy of \[ \ker(E_W:D_J\longrightarrow J^{c=1}). \tag{A.41.5} \] There is no remaining conjugacy quotient after the actual local normalization in the proof. Formulas (A.41.2)--(A.41.5) retain the completed arithmetic Fox operator. They do not assign a numerical value to an unevaluated coefficient of $W$ or of its action.

statement: A complete affine Fox criterion for every one-prime inert metabelian target. Let $q\ne3$ be inert in $K_0$, and let $s$ be any class-two section unramified outside $\{3,q,\infty\}$. Use the actual presentation of A.28, written in the free basis $m,n,t$ with $c(m)=m$, $c(n)=n^{-1}$, $c(t)=t^{-1}$, and put $Q_q=q^2$. Retain its actual $c$-fixed Frobenius word $W$. Normalize $s(c)=1$, and choose an equivariant lift $\widetilde s$ of its three generator values to $Q=N/N''$ on this free source. Such a lift always exists before imposing the single relator. Let $\rho_\alpha$ be the action on $J=\gamma_3N/N''$ obtained by conjugation by $\widetilde s$, where $\alpha$ is the prescribed abelian section. Set \[ U=\rho_\alpha(m),\quad B=\rho_\alpha(n),\quad T=\rho_\alpha(t),\quad C=\rho_\alpha(c),\quad \Phi=\rho_\alpha(W). \tag{A.42.1} \] This action depends only on $\alpha$ and descends to the actual arithmetic group. In particular $\Phi T\Phi^{-1}=T^{Q_q}$. Define \[ \begin{split} \mathcal D_\alpha&= J^{C=1}\oplus J^{BC=-1}\oplus J^{TC=-1},\\ \mathcal J_\alpha&=J^{T^{Q_q}C=-1},\\ \mathcal E_W(a,b,d)&= \rho_\alpha\!\left(\frac{\partial W}{\partial m}\right)a+ \rho_\alpha\!\left(\frac{\partial W}{\partial n}\right)b+ \rho_\alpha\!\left(\frac{\partial W}{\partial t}\right)d,\\ \mathcal L_s(a,b,d)&=(1-T^{Q_q})\mathcal E_W(a,b,d) +\left(\Phi-\sum_{i=0}^{Q_q-1}T^i\right)d,\\ e_s&=\widetilde s(WtW^{-1}t^{-Q_q})\in\mathcal J_\alpha. \end{split} \tag{A.42.2} \] The full global metabelian image consists exactly of the targets for which \[ [e_s]=0\quad\text{in}\quad \mathcal J_\alpha/\mathcal L_s(\mathcal D_\alpha). \tag{A.42.3} \] For every target in that image, its fiber is an affine torsor under the explicitly specified compact group \[ \frac{\ker\mathcal L_s} {\{((U-1)h,(B-1)h,(T-1)h):h\in J^{C=1}\}}. \tag{A.42.4} \] All source actions, the affine error, and the finite images of $W$ in these formulas are the actual based ones. The criterion is an exact completed linear system, including its affine origin and every conjugation. Its numerical evaluation for arbitrary input is not asserted.

statement: Finite arithmetic image and fiber tests with arbitrary ramification support. Let $s$ be an exact continuous class-two section, normalized by $s(c)=1$, and let $\alpha$ be its abelian projection. The following construction applies to each of \[ G=N,\qquad G=N/N'',\qquad G=N/\gamma_3(I_{Q_c}). \tag{A.43.1} \] It gives an exact image criterion and every fiber using explicit finite arithmetic fields, finite groups, and finite cocycle sets. The target may have infinite ramification support. Put $H_0=N$, $H_{n+1}=\Phi(H_n)=H_n^3[H_n,H_n]$, with closures understood. The finite tests below are indexed by $n\ge1$; set \[ \begin{split} P_n&=N/H_n,\qquad A_n=N/(H_n\gamma_3N),\\ G_n&=P_n,\quad P_n/P_n'',\quad P_n/\gamma_3(I_n), \end{split} \tag{A.43.2} \] in the three cases, where $I_n$ is the normal closure of the actual image of $c_{Q_c}$ in $P_n$. Write $s_n$ for the exact target cocycle in $A_n$, and let \[ S_n=\{3,\infty\}\cup \{q\ne3:\alpha\bmod3^n\text{ is ramified at }q\}. \tag{A.43.3} \] These are explicitly determined finite increasing sets at each precision. All finite geometric groups and their based arithmetic actions are constructed by the iterated elementary abelian covers in the proof. Let $F_n$ be the finite Galois field splitting the action on $G_n$. Let $K_n$ be its compositum with the finite Galois field cut out by the target homomorphism $g\mapsto(s_n(g),\rho_{A_n}(g))$. If $s_n$ is ramified outside $S_n$, the solution set below is empty immediately. Otherwise put \[ d_n=|G_n|[F_n:\mathbb Q],\qquad B_n=\prod_{p\in S_n\setminus\{\infty\}} p^{d_n(1+\lfloor\log_p d_n\rfloor)}. \tag{A.43.4} \] Set $\Omega_0=\mathbb Q$. Construct $\Omega_n$ as the compositum of $\Omega_{n-1}$ and all Galois extensions $E/\mathbb Q$ containing $K_n$, unramified outside $S_n$, and of degree at most $d_n$. The degree and discriminant bound $B_n$ make this a terminating finite field enumeration. Put $\Delta_n=\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega_n/\mathbb Q)$. Define $X_n(s,G)$ by finite enumeration of all functions $z:\Delta_n\to G_n$ satisfying \[ \begin{split} z(gh)&=z(g)\,g(z(h)),\qquad z(c)=1,\\ \pi_n z&=s_n, \end{split} \tag{A.43.5} \] and the following finite additional conditions: for every $k\le n$, its projection to $G_k$ is trivial on the inertia groups at every prime of $S_n\setminus S_k$. The target and coefficient actions in (A.43.5) are inflated through their specified finite fields. A failed immediate test makes all subsequent solution sets empty. There are explicitly induced transition maps between these finite sets, and \[ [s]\in\operatorname{im} \bigl(\operatorname{Sec}(G)\to\operatorname{Sec}(N/\gamma_3N)\bigr) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X_n(s,G)\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }n. \tag{A.43.6} \] Let $J_n=\ker(G_n\to A_n)$, with its actual $c$-action. The entire fiber over $[s]$ is \[ \varprojlim_n\bigl(X_n(s,G)/J_n^c\bigr), \tag{A.43.7} \] where $h\in J_n^c$ acts by $z(g)\mapsto h^{-1}z(g)g(h)$. Thus the finite quotients in the fiber use the kernels $J_n$, with no replacement by a finite-level centralizer of the target. Each stage is a terminating arithmetic construction from the finite target data at that precision. statement: The three abelian cusp packets, with their framed origins. Put $J=J_{E,D}$ and use the frame coordinates of LM7 (E24.4). Let $z_P$ be the framed line bundle $\mathcal O(P-O)$ with frames $(x/z)^{-1}$ at $P$, $z/x$ at $O$, and the canonical section at the other cusps. Define $z_Q$ in the same way from $Q_c-O$, using $y/z$ at $Q_c$. Put $\alpha_P=\kappa(z_P)$, $\alpha_Q=\kappa(z_Q)$ and $\alpha_O=0$. The three packets in $H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},V)$ are \[ \mathscr P_d^V=\alpha_d+e_d\,\mathcal R_{\mathbb P}(\mathbb Z_3), \qquad d=O,P,Q_c. \tag{B.1} \] Here $e_d\,\mathcal R_{\mathbb P}(\mathbb Z_3)$ denotes the image of the continuous homomorphism on cohomology induced by the $G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant inclusion $\mathbb Z_3(1)\to V$, $1\mapsto e_d$. The torus-point relation specifying the second framed origin is \[ z_P+z_Q= (3^{-1},3^{-1},-\lambda^{-1},-\lambda^{-1},\zeta\lambda^{-2}). \tag{B.2} \] In the presentation (E24.7), eliminate the first $\lambda$-generator and retain $z'$. Write $g_2,g_3$ for the remaining two $\lambda$-generators and $\tau_3$ for $\zeta$ in the third quadratic factor. After pro-$3$ completion the origins have toric coordinates zero, divisible-cohomology coordinate zero, and remaining coordinates \[ \alpha_P=\kappa(z'),\qquad \alpha_Q=\kappa(2z'+g_2+g_3-\tau_3). \tag{B.3} \] The inertia maps in the original frame coordinates are \[ \begin{split} i_O(u)&=(u^{-1},u^{-1},u^{-1},u^{-1},u^{-1}),\\ i_P(u)&=(u,1,1,1,1),\qquad i_Q(u)=(1,u,1,1,1). \end{split} \tag{B.4} \] Their images under the two coordinate-unit characters are respectively $(-\kappa u,-\kappa u)$, $(\kappa u,0)$ and $(0,\kappa u)$. The three sets in (B.1) are pairwise disjoint, and each displayed parameter map is injective.

statement: The inherited class-two image need not be a point or cusp image. The exclusion proposed in Lead 1 is false. There are sections of $N\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q}$ whose image in $\operatorname{Sec}(H)$ has toric coordinates $(\kappa(3),2\kappa(3))$. Every such image lies outside the three rational cusp packets, and $U(\mathbb Q)$ has no point producing it. It therefore supplies the asserted counterexample already with a full geometric pro-$3$ lift.

statement: The cusp packets in the cuspidally central quotient. In $N^{\rm cc}=C\times_TV$, let the generator of the central $\mathbb Z_3(1)$ of $C$ be the elliptic commutator $[a,b]$. Choose the reference $C$-section above the elliptic class zero to be the tangent at $O$; above $\kappa(P-O)$ and $\kappa(Q_c-O)$ choose the images of the respective unit tangents. Use these references for every abelian class in the corresponding three elliptic fibers. With these explicit choices for the torsors denoted by $s(\alpha,a)$, the cusp packets are \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} d&\alpha&a\\ \hline O&e_O\kappa(u)&-\kappa(u)\\ P&\alpha_P+e_P\kappa(u)&0\\ Q_c&\alpha_Q+e_{Q_c}\kappa(u)&0 \end{array} \tag{B.6} \] Here $u$ ranges over the full pro-$3$ completion of $\mathbb Q^\times$. This parametrization is injective on each row, and the rows have disjoint images.

statement: Lead 4 for the full geometric pro-three group. For every continuous section $s:G_{\mathbb Q}\to N\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q}$ put $\Delta=\ker(\chi:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times})$. Then \[ C_N(s(\Delta))= \begin{cases} I_{\widetilde d},&s\text{ is cuspidal at the lifted cusp }\widetilde d,\\ 1,&s\text{ is noncuspidal}. \end{cases} \tag{B.7} \] In the first case the lifted cusp is unique and its image is one of $O,P,Q_c$. Thus both implications in Lead 4 hold for the actual pro-$3$ group, with its genuine section action.

statement: The cuspidal members of the full unramified family. Let $\mathscr F_S$ be the image of $H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},N)$ in $H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},N)$, using the integral tangent at $O$. Its cuspidal subset is the disjoint union of the three packets obtained by twisting the unit tangents at $O,P,Q_c$ by $t\kappa(3)$, $t\in\mathbb Z_3$. Every other full section class in $\mathscr F_S$ has centralizer $1$ over $\Delta$. The centralizer of each cuspidal member is its complete pro-$3$ inertia group.

statement:
The complete global one-prime image and its fibers. Fix a rational prime $q

Choose its exact cocycle representative with $s(c)=1$, and write $\alpha$ for its projection to $V$. Define \[  egin{split} H_0&=N,\qquad H_{n+1}=H_n^3[H_n,H_n],\ P_n&=N/H_n,\qquad A_n=P_n/\gamma_3P_n,\qquad J_n=\gamma_3P_n,\ S_n&=\{3,\infty\}\cup \{q:\alpha|_{I_q} mod3^n
e0\}. \end{split} 	ag{B.6.1} \] All subgroups are closed. The exact finite target $s_n$ is the image of $s$ in $A_n$. Use the explicitly constructed finite based action on $P_n$ and its splitting field $F_n$ from A.43. Let $K_n$ be the compositum of $F_n$ with the field of the target graph $(s_n,ho_{A_n})$. If $s_n$ is ramified outside $S_n$, the test fails. Otherwise form the finite Galois field $\Omega_n$ as the compositum of $\Omega_{n-1}$ and all Galois extensions $E/\mathbb Q$ containing $K_n$, unramified outside $S_n$, of degree at most $|P_n|[F_n:\mathbb Q]$, starting with $\Omega_0=\mathbb Q$. The discriminant and polynomial bounds in (A.43.4)--(A.43.10) give a terminating finite enumeration of these fields. Let $X_n$ be the finite set of functions $z:\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega_n/\mathbb Q)	o P_n$ satisfying the actual cocycle equation, $z(c)=1$, and $z mod J_n=s_n$ literally. For every $k\le n$, require its projection to $P_k$ to be trivial on inertia at the primes of $S_n\setminus S_k$. These conditions give the actual transition maps of A.43. Then \[  egin{split} [s]\in\operatorname{im} igl(\operatorname{Sec}(N) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sec}(A) igr) &\Longleftrightarrow X_n
e\varnothing\quad	ext{for all }n\ &\Longleftrightarrow [s]	ext{ lifts to }N/\gamma_rN \quad	ext{for all }r\ge3. \end{split} 	ag{B.6.2} \] Every such full or nilpotent lift is unramified outside $S$. The complete fiber on section classes is \[ \varprojlim_n X_n/J_n^c, 	ag{B.6.3} \] where $h\in J_n^c$ acts by $z(g)\mapsto h^{-1}z(g)g(h)$. Thus (B.6.2) is an exact sequence of terminating finite arithmetic tests, and (B.6.3) retains all compatible conjugacy data. A bounded stopping rule for every positive instance is not asserted. The necessary local condition is precisely the unramified class or a member of the actual cusp packets (B.8.1). The integral section of B.20, with abelian class $\kappa(17)e_O$ and central generator values $\gamma(m)=0$, $\gamma(n)=b$, has exactly the local $O$-cuspidal class-two restriction. It has a global $N/\gamma_4N$ lift and no $N/\gamma_5N$ lift, hence no full, metabelian, or marked-depth lift.
