statement: Every nontrivial tame inertia in a full section is cuspidal. Let $q\ne3$ be a rational prime, put $k=\mathbb Q_q$, and use the actual pro-three fundamental group $N$ of the marked Fermat cubic with the integral unit tangent at $O$ as origin. For a continuous section $s:G_k\to N\rtimes G_k$, its restriction to inertia is either trivial or has image in one cuspidal inertia subgroup. In the latter case the whole section is contained in that cusp's decomposition group. The cusp is $k$-rational and the lifted cusp is unique. Moreover, a full section is unramified at $q$ exactly when its image in $V$ is unramified there.

statement: The exact local image of ramified full sections in class two. With $k=\mathbb Q_q$, $q\ne3$, let $A=N/\gamma_3N$. For each $d\in D(k)$ choose the coordinate unit tangent used in C.10, its actual section $s_{d,1}$, and a peripheral generator $c_d$ based at $O$. The ramified part of the image of full sections in $\operatorname{Sec}_k(A)$ is precisely the disjoint union \[ \coprod_{d\in D(k)} \left\{ \left[g\longmapsto c_d^{\kappa_q(u)(g)}s_{d,1}(g)\right]: u\in k^{\times\wedge_3},\ v_q(u)\ne0 \right\}. \tag{B.8.1} \] Here the expression is multiplication in the arithmetic group, followed by its actual class-two quotient. Its parameter space is explicitly \[ k^{\times\wedge_3} =\mathbb Z_3\kappa(q)\oplus\mu_{3^{v_3(q-1)}}(k). \tag{B.8.2} \] There are nine packets for $q\equiv1\pmod3$ and three for $q\equiv2\pmod3$. In the central cuspidal lattice $I/[N,I]=\mathbb Z_3(1)[D]$ the tame vector of a packet is $v_q(u)c_d$, with exactly this one cusp coordinate nonzero. In particular the mixed-inertia counterexamples in A.5 and A.6 cannot lift to full $N$.

statement: All inherited class-two cusp origins. Use exactly the diagonal coordinates of LM7 E.29 for $H$, based at the lifted cusp $P$ over $t=0$, and put \[ f(g)=\frac{\chi_3(g)^2-1}{24}\in\mathbb Z_3(2). \tag{B.9.1} \] The three rational cusp packets in $\operatorname{Sec}(H)$ have the following continuous cocycle representatives: \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} &u(g)&v(g)&w(g)\\ \hline P&\kappa(a)(g)&0&0\\ Q_c&0&\kappa(a)(g)&f(g)\\ O&-\kappa(a)(g)&-\kappa(a)(g)&f(g)/2 \end{array} \qquad a\in\mathbb Q^{\times\wedge_3}. \tag{B.9.2} \] Each row is injectively parametrized and the rows are pairwise disjoint. Above inherited abelian class $(0,0)$ the three unit tangents give, respectively, the central labels $0,2,1\in\mathbb Z/3$ relative to $g\mapsto(\chi_3(g)^2-1)/3$. The actual arithmetic map from the intrinsic group based at $O$ to this $H$-extension is \[ (n,g)\longmapsto \bigl(q_O(n)(0,0,f(g)/2),g\bigr), \tag{B.9.3} \] after the geometric path choices in the proof. Thus (B.9.2) retains the change of section origin between the $O$ and $P$ base points.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The full global image at the specified prime seven. Let $A=N/\gamma_3N$, and use the normalized pair coordinates $(a,b)$ and the $A^c$-action of A.15 for sections supported at $\{3,7,\infty\}$. Such a class has a full $N$-lift exactly in the following cases: \[ b=1, \quad\text{or its restriction to }G_{\mathbb Q_7} \text{ belongs to one of the nine ramified packets (B.8.1).} \tag{B.10.1} \] Equivalently these are precisely the classes which lift to every lower-central quotient. A full lift can be chosen unramified outside $\{3,7,\infty\}$. Here is an exact packet parametrization in the pair coordinates. Fix the embedding $\zeta_3\equiv2\pmod7$, a Frobenius $\phi$ fixing compatible roots of $7$, and the actual unit-tangent values $g_d=s_{d,1}(\phi)\in A$. Use the same based inertia element $c_d\in A$ in each case. The ramified part of the global image is \[ \left\{ \bigl[(c_d^{2j}g_d,c_d^v)\cdot h\bigr]: d\in D(\mathbb Q_7),\quad v\in\mathbb Z_3\setminus\{0\},\quad j\in\{0,1,2\}, \quad h\in A/A^c \right\}. \tag{B.10.2} \] Here $(a,b)\cdot h=(h^{-1}aF(h),h^{-1}bh)$, so $A/A^c$ means right cosets, and the displayed parameters are injective after these explicit choices. The symbols $g_d$ retain the actual tangential Frobenius origins; they are not replaced by arbitrary solutions of a graded normalization equation.

statement: No new ramification above class two and compactness for a finite set of primes. Let $S$ be any finite set of rational places containing $3$ and infinity, and let $s_2$ be a class-two section unramified outside $S$. Every lift of $s_2$ to $N/\gamma_rN$, $r\ge3$, is unramified outside the same set $S$. Moreover the following assertions are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} s_2\text{ lifts to }N;\\ s_2\text{ lifts to }N/\gamma_rN\text{ for every }r\ge3. \end{gathered} \tag{B.11.1} \] The separately given nilpotent lifts need not be compatible. The conclusion supplies a compatible continuous full lift, also unramified outside $S$.

statement: The marked local classification when the filled-curve projection is unramified. Let $k/\mathbb Q_q$ be finite, $q\ne3$, with residue cardinality $Q$, and let $d=Q_c$ be the marked cusp. Write \[ \mathscr Q=N/\gamma_3I_{\rm mark},\qquad B=N/I_{\rm mark},\qquad \mathscr I=I_{\rm mark}/\gamma_3I_{\rm mark},\qquad Z=\gamma_2I_{\rm mark}/\gamma_3I_{\rm mark}. \tag{B.12.1} \] All groups carry the actual arithmetic action, and the quotient $B$ is the full geometric pro-three group of the curve obtained by filling $d$. Choose tame three-inertia $\tau$, arithmetic Frobenius $\phi$, the peripheral generator $c$ at $d$, and the unit tangential reference $s_{d,1}$ compatibly. Put $F_0=s_{d,1}(\phi)$. The induced based action $\Phi$ of $F_0$ on $B$ is the action of the point $d$ on the filled curve. There are actual equivariant identifications \[ M:=\mathscr I^{\rm ab} =\mathbb Z_3[[B]](1),\qquad Z=\widehat{\bigwedge}^{\,2}M,\qquad (F_0)_M=Q\Phi,\quad (F_0)_Z=Q^2\widehat{\bigwedge}^{\,2}\Phi. \tag{B.12.2} \] Here the completed modules are inverse limits over finite continuous partitions of the profinite label set $B$; the label $1$ is the chosen lift of the marked cusp. Every local section of $\mathscr Q$ whose projection to $B$ is unramified and whose tame inertia is nontrivial has, up to geometric conjugation, exactly the following form: \[ s(\tau)=c^a,\qquad s(\phi)=c^r\exp(z)F_0, \quad \begin{cases} a\in\mathbb Z_3\setminus\{0\},\\ r\in\mathbb Z_3/(Q-1)\mathbb Z_3,\\ [z]\in\mathcal C_{k,d}:= Z/(Q^2\widehat{\bigwedge}^{\,2}\Phi-1)Z . \end{cases} \tag{B.12.3} \] In particular its $B$-section is the point section at $d$. The quotient in (B.12.3) uses the actual image; that image is closed because $Z$ is compact. Every displayed parameter occurs, and two displayed sections are conjugate exactly when all three parameters agree. Under $\mathscr Q\to N/\gamma_3N$, their image is exactly the ramified local cusp packet at $d$. For each member of that packet the entire local fiber is the group $\mathcal C_{k,d}$, acting simply transitively after the displayed reference is fixed. Finally a local marked section whose abelian tame inertia in $V$ is zero is itself unramified.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The central marked local fiber is a countable product of three-adic integers. The group $\mathcal C_{k,d}$ in (B.12.3) is a nonzero, torsion-free, compact metrizable $\mathbb Z_3$-module. After a choice of divisible basis of its discrete dual, there is a continuous $\mathbb Z_3$-linear isomorphism \[ \mathcal C_{k,d} \simeq\prod_{n\ge1}\mathbb Z_3 . \tag{B.13.1} \] The coordinates in (B.13.1) depend on that stated choice; the quotient and the section action in (B.12.3) are intrinsic to the displayed reference. In particular there are actual local marked sections with the same ramified class-two cusp image which are not cuspidal and have no full-$N$ lift.

statement: The complete local marked image and the unmarked ramified fibers. Retain the local data and actual quotients of B.12. If the projection of a section of $\mathscr Q$ to $B$ is ramified, that section is itself cuspidal at a unique unmarked cusp $d'\in D(k)\setminus\{d\}$. For a fixed ramified $B$-section the lift to $\mathscr Q$, up to geometric conjugation, is unique and is the image of its actual full cusp section. Consequently the complete local image of $\operatorname{Sec}_k(\mathscr Q)$ in $\operatorname{Sec}_k(N/\gamma_3N)$ equals the local full image: all unramified classes and the disjoint ramified cusp packets of B.8. The fiber over a ramified unmarked cusp class is a singleton; the fiber over a ramified marked cusp class is exactly the group $\mathcal C_{k,d}$ of B.12--B.13.

statement: An explicit cleaned Heisenberg detector at seven. Put $k=\mathbb F_7(\theta)$, $\theta^3=2$, and write $[a,b,c]=a+b\theta+c\theta^2$. On $E_k:y^2+y=x^3$, let $\zeta=2$ and \[ \begin{split} P&=(3,2),\qquad P^-=(3,4),\\ Q&=([4,1,1],[2,0,2]),\\ S&=([0,6,5],[1,4,3]),\\ T_1&=([3,3,3],[6,2,2]),\qquad T_2=-T_1 . \end{split} \tag{B.15.1} \] The following functions are explicit: \[ \begin{aligned} a&=\frac{x^2+[1,6,5]x+[0,1,4]+[4,4,4]y}{x-3},& b&=x-3,\\ f_1&=\frac{x^2+[2,3,5]x+[6,4,6]+[6,1,6]y} {x-[3,3,3]},\\ f_2&=\frac{x^2+[2,3,5]x+[0,3,0]+[1,6,1]y} {x-[3,3,3]},\\ m&=\frac{x^2+[2,5,2]x+[6,2,2]+[2,4,5]y} {x-[3,3,3]},& f&=\frac{m}{f_1f_2^2(x-[3,3,3])}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.15.2} \] Define $p(v)=\sum_{i=0}^5p_iv^i$ and $h(v)=\sum_{i=0}^3h_iv^i$ by \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrrrr} i&0&1&2&3&4&5\\ \hline p_i&[3,0,0]&[0,6,6]&[6,1,5]&[4,0,2]&[4,1,2]&[1,5,4]\\ h_i&[6,1,4]&[6,0,1]&[2,0,0]&[1,5,4]&& \end{array} \tag{B.15.3} \] In $k(E)(v)$ with $v^3=b$, put \[ u(v)=\frac{p(v)+y}{v h(v)},\qquad r=f\,u(v)u(\zeta v)^2. \tag{B.15.4} \] Then \[ v^3=b,\qquad w^3=a,\qquad z^3=r \tag{B.15.5} \] defines a connected Galois cover of degree $27$, with Heisenberg group of exponent three. It is finite \'etale over $U_k=E_k\setminus E_k[3]$. The actual deck generators are \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} &v&w&z\\ \hline \sigma&\zeta v&w&u(\zeta^2v)z/w\\ \tau&v&\zeta w&z\\ \rho&v&w&\zeta z , \end{array} \qquad [\sigma,\tau]=\rho. \tag{B.15.6} \] For the Fermat tangent parameter $s$ at $O$, the first two radicals retain the leading coefficient $9$, whose reduction is $2$. The cleaned central radical satisfies $r\sim s^4$. Thus the based Puiseux choices are \[ v\sim\theta s^{-2/3},\qquad w\sim\theta s^{-2/3},\qquad z\sim s^{4/3}. \tag{B.15.7} \] There is also an explicit Frobenius transport on the compositum of the three coefficient-conjugate covers. Let a superscript $[j]$ mean raising every coefficient to $7^j$, with $j$ read modulo three, and use the same choices (B.15.7) for $w_j,z_j$. The arithmetic Frobenius at the framed tangent is \[ \begin{split} \Phi(v)&=\zeta^2v,\qquad \Phi(w_j)=\zeta^2w_{j+1},\\ \Phi(z_j)&= \frac{\zeta w_{j+1}z_{j+1}} {u^{[j+1]}(\zeta v)},\qquad \Phi^3=1 . \end{split} \tag{B.15.15} \]

statement: The integral depth-one map through the cyclic-nine cover. Let $F$ be the free pro-three group on the standard tripod inertia generators $x,y$, with $[x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$. For $f\in F'$ write its metabelian image as $[x,y]^{h(X,Y)}$, where $X=x-1$, $Y=y-1$ act by conjugation. There is an actual continuous metabelian quotient in which \[ \begin{gathered} x\longmapsto(1,0),\qquad y\longmapsto(0,1),\\ (m,a)(n,b)=(m+t^a n,a+b),\\ m,n\in\mathbb Z_3[[t-1]],\qquad a,b\in\mathbb Z_3. \end{gathered} \tag{B.16.1} \] In this quotient the image of $f$ is $(m_f,0)$, with \[ m_f(t)=(1-t)h(0,t-1). \tag{B.16.2} \] Let $H_9=\ker(F\to\mathbb Z/9)$, where $x\mapsto0$, $y\mapsto1$. Its actual cover is \[ z^9=1-t_{\rm base},\qquad Y_9=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,\infty,\mu_9\}. \tag{B.16.3} \] In $H_9^{\rm ab}/3$, write the image of $f$ as $\sum_{j=0}^8c_j\,y^jxy^{-j}$; its $y^9$ coordinate is zero. Then \[ \begin{pmatrix}h_{0,3}\\h_{0,5}\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0&0&0&0&2&1&0&1&2\\ 0&0&0&0&0&0&2&2&2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}c_0\\c_1\\c_2\\c_3\\c_4\\c_5\\c_6\\c_7\\c_8\end{pmatrix} \quad\text{in }\mathbb F_3. \tag{B.16.4} \] For the standard path $\beta$ from $\overrightarrow{01}$ to $\overrightarrow{10}$ and the convention $f_g=\beta(g\beta)^{-1}$, these coordinates are explicit framed Kummer coordinates on (B.16.3). The relevant endpoint-to-start ratios are \[ r_0=9,\qquad r_j=\frac{-\zeta_9^j}{1-\zeta_9^j} \quad(1\leq j\leq8),\qquad \prod_{j=0}^8r_j=1. \tag{B.16.5} \] Choose their compatible roots by continuing the units $z-\zeta_9^j$ along the lifted path from $z=1$ to $z=0$, using the actual start velocity $-1/9$ for $j=0$. If \[ \frac{g(r_{\chi(g)^{-1}j}^{\,1/3^n})} {r_j^{\,1/3^n}} =\zeta_{3^n}^{\,\kappa_j(g)}, \tag{B.16.6} \] where the index is taken modulo nine, then $c_j=-\kappa_j(g)\pmod3$. In particular (B.16.4)--(B.16.6) evaluate the two coefficients by finite cyclic-cover Kummer data for the full cyclotomic action; no restriction to $\ker\chi$ is imposed.

statement: The actual norm-289 depth-one Frobenius coordinates. Let $g_{17}$ be an arithmetic Frobenius of norm $289$ at the prime above seventeen of $K_0=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3)$, viewed through the specified tangential arithmetic action. Use the path and commutator conventions of B.16, and write the metabelian Ihara word as $f_{g_{17}}=[x,y]^{h(X,Y)}$. Then \[ h(0,Y)\equiv-Y^6-Y^7\pmod{(3,Y^8)}, \qquad h_{0,3}=h_{0,5}=0\quad\text{in }\mathbb F_3. \tag{B.17.1} \] An explicit residue-field embedding is \[ \begin{gathered} k=\mathbb F_{17}[\theta]/(\theta^2-3),\\ \overline\zeta_9=7+4\theta,\qquad \overline\zeta_3=\overline\zeta_9^3=8+15\theta. \end{gathered} \tag{B.17.2} \] For the nine framed ratios of B.16 the actual local Kummer coordinates and geometric cusp coordinates are \[ \begin{aligned} (\kappa_j(g_{17}))_{j=0}^8 &=(0,1,2,0,1,2,0,1,2),\\ (c_j)_{j=0}^8&=(0,2,1,0,2,1,0,2,1). \end{aligned} \tag{B.17.3} \] The entries are in $\mathbb F_3$. These values hold for each prime of $\mathbb Q(\zeta_9)$ above seventeen, with its compatible embedding of $\zeta_3=\zeta_9^3$.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The full finite arithmetic image and the exact Frobenius action at seventeen. Use the actual source basis of A.38 and the $c$-adapted basis $m,n$ of A.31. Let \[ \rho:P_3\longrightarrow \operatorname{Aut}\bigl(N/(N^3\gamma_3N)\bigr) \] be the actual arithmetic action. Its image $G$ has order $243$, nilpotency class three, and exponent nine. In the $10+45$ coordinates of A.38, its linear image has order nine, and its identity-linear kernel has dimension three over $\mathbb F_3$. The exact dimensions are \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} &\gamma_2(G)&\gamma_3(G)&\gamma_4(G)\\\hline \dim_{\mathbb F_3}&2&1&0 \end{array} \qquad \begin{array}{c|ccc} &D_2(G)&D_3(G)&D_4(G)\\\hline \dim_{\mathbb F_3}&3&2&0. \end{array} \tag{B.18.1} \] In particular $D_4(P_3)$ acts trivially on this specified geometric quotient. Put $M=\rho(m)$ and $N_*=\rho(n)$. Then the entire actual Frobenius action at seventeen is \[ \rho(\varphi_{17}) =M^6[N_*,[N_*,M]]=M^6\ne1. \tag{B.18.2} \] It has order three. Its Johnson block has rank two and annihilates all nine cusp vectors. The full matrix is retained in \texttt{bc\_ihara\_finite\_image\_certificate.npz}.

statement: A finite precision determining the integral local kernel. Let $M_2=\bigwedge^2V$, and let \[ \mathcal D=M_2^c\oplus \ker(1+\rho(n)c:M_2\longrightarrow M_2) \] be the rank-$45$ lattice of normalized source cocycles used in A.39. Define the actual Frobenius evaluation \[ E_\varphi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M_2^c, \qquad E_\varphi(\gamma)=\gamma(\varphi_{17}), \qquad R=\ker E_\varphi. \] The integral operator $B=(F_\varphi-1)|M_2^c$ has three-adic Smith exponents \[ \underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{6},\quad \underbrace{2,\ldots,2}_{7},\quad \underbrace{3,3}_{2},\quad \underbrace{4,\ldots,4}_{6}. \tag{B.19.1} \] Identify $R/3R$ with its image in $\mathcal D/3\mathcal D$. Then its exact finite-precision description is \[ \frac{R}{3R} =\operatorname{im}\left( \ker\left( \mathcal D/243\mathcal D \xrightarrow{\ E_\varphi\ } M_2^c/243M_2^c\right) \longrightarrow\mathcal D/3\mathcal D\right). \tag{B.19.2} \] More explicitly, for every integral $d\in\mathcal D$ with $E_\varphi(d)\in243M_2^c$, put \[ h=B^{-1}E_\varphi(d)\in3M_2^c, \qquad \gamma=d-\delta h, \qquad (\delta h)(g)=g(h)-h. \tag{B.19.3} \] Then $\gamma\in R$ and $\gamma\equiv d\pmod{3\mathcal D}$. The matrix $B$ and the bound (B.19.1) are computed in the attached certificate. Evaluating the separate arithmetic matrix $E_\varphi\bmod243$ remains the finite calculation needed to list the resulting $24$-dimensional subspace individually.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: An individually specified class-two target with no class-four lift. Use the actual arithmetic basis $m,n,c$ of A.38 and A.31. Write the ten integral A.7 basis vectors as \[ \begin{split} (v_0,\ldots,v_7) &=(e_P,e_{Q_c},e_A,e_{\bar A},e_B,e_{\bar B},e_C,e_{\bar C}),\\ v_8&=(\Psi(1,0)/3,(1,0)),\qquad v_9=(\Psi(0,1)/3,(0,1)) \quad\text{in }L_\Psi\subset W_{\mathbb Q_3}\oplus T_{\mathbb Q_3}. \end{split} \tag{B.20.1} \] Let $C_2$ be the actual action of $c$ on $M_2=\bigwedge^2V$. Define the integral vectors \[ b_0=3v_8\wedge v_9+ \sum_{i=0}^7 \bigl(\Psi_{i,2}v_i\wedge v_8 -\Psi_{i,1}v_i\wedge v_9\bigr), \qquad b=(1-C_2)b_0. \tag{B.20.2} \] Here the columns of $\Psi$ are numbered one and two. In the basis $v_i\wedge v_j$, $i<j$, all nonzero coordinates of $b$ are the following; every other coordinate is zero: \[ \begin{array}{cr|cr|cr} (i,j)&b_{ij}&(i,j)&b_{ij}&(i,j)&b_{ij}\\\hline (0,8)&-2&(1,8)&2&(2,6)&-1\\ (2,7)&1&(2,8)&2&(2,9)&2\\ (3,6)&1&(3,7)&-1&(3,9)&-2\\ (4,6)&1&(4,7)&-1&(4,8)&-2\\ (4,9)&-2&(5,6)&-1&(5,7)&1\\ (5,9)&2&(6,8)&2&(6,9)&-2\\ (7,8)&-2&(7,9)&2&(8,9)&6. \end{array} \tag{B.20.3} \] The prescriptions \[ \gamma(m)=0,\qquad \gamma(n)=b, \qquad \gamma(c)=0 \tag{B.20.4} \] define an actual continuous $M_2$-cocycle unramified outside three. Let $s_{O,17}$ be the actual $O$-cuspidal section with tangent parameter seventeen. In $A=N/\gamma_3N$, put \[ s_b(g)=\gamma(g)s_{O,17}(g). \tag{B.20.5} \] This is an actual class-two section, with abelian class $\kappa_{17}e_O$. Its restriction at seventeen equals the specified local cuspidal section exactly. It has a global lift to $N/\gamma_4N$, but no global lift to $N/\gamma_5N$. Consequently it has no full, metabelian, or marked-depth lift. The projection of (B.20.4) to $\bigwedge^2T$ has the exact generator values $0,6$. If $a=\kappa_3(n)\in\mathbb Z_3^\times$ in this actual source basis, this cocycle is $(6/a)\kappa_3$. Only $a\equiv1\pmod3$ is used; its integral value has not been replaced by one.

statement: No arithmetic centralizer in the class-two geometric group. For every number field $L$ and every continuous section $s:G_L\to A\rtimes G_L$, \[ C_A(s(G_L))=1. \tag{C.1} \] The assertion uses the whole $G_L$, in contrast to the subgroup $\ker\chi$ in B.4; the comparison map between the two assertions is the inclusion of subgroups, which reverses inclusions of their centralizers.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: All restriction maps are injective and finite Galois descent is exact. For number fields $L\subset L'$, restriction is the injective map of pointed sets \[ \operatorname{res}_{L'/L}:\operatorname{Sec}_L \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sec}_{L'}, \qquad [z]\longmapsto[z|_{G_{L'}}]. \tag{C.2} \] For $L'/L$ finite Galois it identifies its source with precisely the $\operatorname{Gal}(L'/L)$-fixed classes in its target. Writing $\rho$ for the based action on $A$, the action by $g\in G_L$ is represented by \[ (g\cdot z)(h)=\rho(g)z(g^{-1}hg),\quad h\in G_{L'}. \tag{C.3} \] Thus the kernel of (C.2), as a pointed-set map, is its base point, and its image in the invariant set is the entire set.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The action and fields of definition of germs. The set \[ \mathscr G=\varinjlim_{L\subset\overline{\mathbb Q}} \operatorname{Sec}_L \tag{C.4} \] has a well-defined $G_{\mathbb Q}$-action obtained by (C.3) together with conjugation of the field of definition. Every transition map is injective. Each germ has an open stabilizer and a finite orbit. For every number field $L$, \[ \operatorname{Sec}_L\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \mathscr G^{G_L}. \tag{C.5} \] In particular the image of $\operatorname{Sec}_{\mathbb Q}$ is exactly the fixed-germ set. The fixed field of the stabilizer of a germ is its smallest field of definition.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The R2 obstruction does not disappear as a germ. Let $c=9\kappa(3)\cup\beta$ be the nonzero R2 class specified by LM7 (E.32f), so that in $H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_3(2))= \mathcal R/d\mathcal R$ it is represented by \[ z_{q_j}=q_j-1\quad(j\ge3),\qquad z_q=0 \text{ at the other primes}. \tag{C.6} \] For every finite number field $L$, $\operatorname{res}_{L/\mathbb Q}(c)\ne0$. In fact these restrictions all have infinite additive order. Consequently $c$ gives a nonzero element of $\varinjlim_L H^2_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathbb Z_3(2))$. The vanishing assertion in the first sentence of Task C.4 is false.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: Restriction is injective on the Tate-twist phantom subgroup. For $\mathbb Z_3(2)$ the kernel of the finite-coefficient comparison map in R2 is torsion-free, and restriction from $\mathbb Q$ to any finite number field is injective on this kernel. This extends C.4 from its particular cup-product witness to every nonzero class in that kernel.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: Complete class-two germ classification. Task C.1 requests the full explicit residue complex, obstruction residues, convergence criterion, and fibers over every number field $L$. C.11 disproves a verbatim pure-residue extension of Part A; C.12 gives the exact replacement, including the finite-$S_L$ arithmetic class and the lift torsor. C.13 evaluates the preceding cuspidally central obstruction by the local quadratic pairings at the places above three, with their global sum relation. C.14 computes the finite-$S_L$ complexes by finite Galois cochain matrices and Artin--Verdier duality, and C.15 evaluates the retained class by explicit compact-support cup traces. Together with the restricted-family condition in C.12, these give the full number-field criterion and fibers requested in Task C.1. For Task C.2, C.1--C.3 give injective restriction, the actual Galois action and exact descent. Formula (C.5) identifies $\operatorname{Sec}_L$ with all $G_L$-fixed germs. For Task C.3, C.8--C.9 prove injectivity of the point map and separation from cusp germs. C.10 gives the nine disjoint cusp parameter spaces with their torsion and Galois action. C.16 evaluates every point's abelian and central coordinates by finite algebraic operations at each precision; C.17 is an explicit nonzero central instance. C.18 gives the exact point-image set, its equivariance and its full central membership criterion. Its coordinate maps retain the E36 origin and the lift-fiber translation. Finally C.4--C.5 and C.7 prove that both specified phantom classes remain nonzero after every finite number-field extension and in the germ colimit, settling Task C.4.

statement: The intrinsic phantom obstruction also survives every finite extension. The nonzero obstruction in $H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathcal K)$ constructed in A.4 remains nonzero over every finite number field and in the filtered colimit over all number fields. More generally, restriction to every finite number field is injective on the phantom subgroup for $\mathcal K$ computed in A.2.

statement: An exact tangent-line separation identity. Let $\ell_d$ be a row vector defining the flex tangent line at $d\in D$. The nine rows can be chosen as \[ (1,\zeta^a,0),\quad(0,1,\zeta^a),\quad(\zeta^a,0,1) \qquad (a=0,1,2). \] Set $P_d=\ell_d^*\ell_d/2$, a rank-one Hermitian projector on $\mathbb C^3$. The real-linear map \[ \operatorname{Herm}_3(\mathbb C)\longrightarrow\mathbb R^9, \qquad H\longmapsto\bigl(\operatorname{tr}(P_d H)\bigr)_d \] is an isomorphism, and \[ \sum_d P_d=3I_3,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(P_dP_e)= \begin{cases}1&d=e,\\1/4&d\ne e.\end{cases} \tag{C.8.1} \] The kernel after deleting coordinate $d$ is the line $\mathbb R(4P_d-I_3)$. A positive semidefinite matrix with the eight undeleted measurements of $vv^*$, where $v\ne0$ and $\ell_d(v)=0$, is exactly $vv^*$.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: Injective point germs and their separation from cusp germs. The canonical map \[ U(\overline{\mathbb Q})\longrightarrow \varinjlim_L\operatorname{Sec}_L(N/\gamma_3N) \] is injective and $G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant. Its image is disjoint from all the cuspidal germs. Both assertions already hold after projecting to the germ colimit of $H^1(G_L,V)$. The smallest field of definition of a point germ is the field of definition of the point.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The nine disjoint cusp germ packets and their Galois action. Define the abelian germ parameter group \[ \mathscr K=\varinjlim_{L\subset\overline{\mathbb Q}} H^1_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathbb Z_3(1)) =\varinjlim_L\varprojlim_n L^\times/L^{\times3^n}. \tag{C.10.1} \] All transition maps are restriction. Choose at each cusp $d\in D(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ the unit tangent for the parameter $x/z$ when $x=0$, $y/z$ when $y=0$, and $z/x$ when $z=0$. These choices are $G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant. The map \[ \coprod_{d\in D(\overline{\mathbb Q})}\mathscr K \longrightarrow\mathscr G, \qquad (d,u)\longmapsto[s_{d,1}\text{ twisted by }u] \tag{C.10.2} \] is injective, and its image is exactly the cuspidal germ set. There are nine packets. The $G_{\mathbb Q}$-action in these coordinates is \[ g(d,u)=(gd,gu), \tag{C.10.3} \] where $gu$ transports a Kummer class over $L$ to its class over $gL$ by the field isomorphism $g:L\to gL$. The parameter group has injective restriction maps, is divisible, and has torsion subgroup canonically $\mu_{3^\infty}$, with its usual Galois action. In particular, distinct torsion parameters and distinct cusp packets do not merge in the germ colimit.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The pure-residue computation over the rationals does not extend verbatim to every number field. Let \[ L=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3,\sqrt{10}),\qquad S_L=\{v:v\mid3\}\cup\{v:v\mid\infty\}. \] For the actual rank-forty-four module $\mathcal K$, \[ H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K)\ne0. \tag{C.11.1} \] Its inflation into $H^2_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathcal K)$ is injective, and every one of its classes has zero residue outside $S_L$. Consequently the pure-residue isomorphism (A.1.3) cannot be transported to this $L$ by replacing the rational primes with its finite primes. The finite-$S_L$ complex is a necessary part of Task C.1.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The exact general number-field criterion with its retained arithmetic term. For any number field $L$, put $S_L=\{v\mid3,\infty\}$, $A_v=\mathcal K(-1)$ and $D_v=F_v-1$ for $v\notin S_L$. Let $\mathcal R_L(A)$ denote the families in these integral lattices tending to zero three-adically. Then there are exact maps \[ \begin{aligned} 0\longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K) &\xrightarrow{\rm inf}H^2_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathcal K)\\ &\xrightarrow{\rm res} \mathcal R_L(A)/D\mathcal R_L(A) \longrightarrow0. \end{aligned} \tag{C.12.1} \] \[ H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K) \xrightarrow{\sim}H^1_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathcal K). \tag{C.12.2} \] The quotient in (C.12.1) uses the actual image of $D$. The first term is the inverse limit of the finite groups $H^2(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K/3^n)$. For a section of $N^{\rm cc}$ over $L$, take its actual local path-origin residues $r_v$ by the formula (A.8.3), with residue size $\#k(v)$ and the restricted $G_L$-action. Its intrinsic obstruction vanishes exactly when both of the following tests hold: \[ y_v=-D_v^{-1}r_v\in A_v\text{ for every }v\notin S_L, \qquad (y_v)_v\in\mathcal R_L(A); \tag{C.12.3} \] \[ \eta(s)=0\quad\text{in }H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K). \tag{C.12.4} \] Here, once (C.12.3) holds, $\eta(s)$ is the unique class whose inflation is the full continuous obstruction of $s$. Every nonempty class-two lift fiber is a torsor under $H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K)$, with no further geometric-stabilizer quotient. This statement retains the finite-$S_L$ test; it does not claim an evaluation of that test for arbitrary $L$.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The initial cuspidally central obstruction over every number field. Let $L\subset\overline\Q$ be a number field and let $\alpha\in H^1(G_L,V)$, with image $\beta\in H^1(G_L,T)$. Orient $\bigwedge^2T\simeq\Z_3(1)$ by the commutator in the once-punctured elliptic curve, and write $\omega$ for this alternating pairing. For each $v\mid3$ define \[ q_v(\beta)=\tfrac12\operatorname{inv}_v \omega_*(\beta_v\smile\beta_v)\in\Z_3. \tag{C.13.1} \] Here $\operatorname{inv}_v:H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L_v},\Z_3(1)) \xrightarrow{\sim}\Z_3$ is the inverse limit of the normalized local Brauer invariant maps. Then \[ \alpha\in\operatorname{im} \bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_L(N^{\rm cc})\to H^1(G_L,V)\bigr) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q_v(\beta)=0\text{ for every }v\mid3. \tag{C.13.2} \] The tuple satisfies $\sum_{v\mid3}q_v(\beta)=0$. Every nonempty fiber is a torsor under $H^1(G_L,\Z_3(1))=\varprojlim_n L^\times/(L^\times)^{3^n}$, with no further stabilizer quotient. In particular, every abelian section lifts to $N^{\rm cc}$ over a number field having exactly one place above three, including $\Q$. This statement makes no assertion that every tuple subject to the displayed sum occurs as a self-pairing. \par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.16, folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379).}
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: An explicit finite Galois construction of the retained arithmetic groups. Fix a number field $L\subset\overline{\mathbb Q}$ and put $S=\{v:v\mid3\}\cup\{v:v\mid\infty\}$. For $n\ge1$ write \[ A_n=\mathcal K/3^n,\qquad A_n^D=\operatorname{Hom}(A_n,\mu_{3^n}),\qquad F_n=L(J_{E,D}[3^n],\mu_{3^n}),\qquad d_n=3^{44n}[F_n:L]. \tag{C.14.1} \] The homomorphisms in the dual have their usual contragredient Galois action. Let $\Omega_n$ be the compositum, inside the fixed algebraic closure, of all finite Galois extensions $E/L$ containing $F_n$, unramified outside $S$, and satisfying $[E:L]\le d_n$. Put $G_n=\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega_n/L)$. At each $v\mid3$ choose a prolongation to $\Omega_n$ and write $D_{n,v}\le G_n$ for its decomposition subgroup. These are finite fields and finite groups, obtained by the bounded enumeration in the proof. For a finite $G_n$-module $A$, use the finite matrices \[ \begin{split} (\delta^0 b)(g)&=g b-b,\\ (\delta^1 z)(g,h)&=g z(h)-z(gh)+z(g). \end{split} \tag{C.14.2} \] Define the following finite abelian groups by kernels and images of these matrices: \[ U_n=\ker\bigl(\delta^1:\operatorname{Map}(G_n,A_n) \to\operatorname{Map}(G_n^2,A_n)\bigr) /\delta^0 A_n, \tag{C.14.3} \] and \[ \begin{split} C_n={}&\{(z,(b_v)_{v\mid3}): \delta^1z=0,\ b_v\in A_n^D,\\ &\hspace{26mm}z(g)=g b_v-b_v \text{ for }g\in D_{n,v}\}\big/ \{(\delta^0 b,(b)_{v\mid3}):b\in A_n^D\}. \end{split} \tag{C.14.4} \] In (C.14.4), $z$ ranges over all functions $G_n\to A_n^D$. There are canonical identifications \[ \begin{split} H^1(G_{L,S},A_n)&\simeq U_n,\qquad H^2(G_{L,S},A_n)\simeq C_n^\vee,\\ H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S},\mathcal K)&\simeq\varprojlim_n U_n,\qquad H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S},\mathcal K) \simeq\varprojlim_n C_n^\vee . \end{split} \tag{C.14.5} \] Here $C_n^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}(C_n,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$; the transition maps are induced by coefficient reduction and its Cartier dual. Thus the arithmetic terms of C.12 are specified by finite arithmetic fields and finite matrices at every precision. The construction applies to every $L$; it does not assume that either displayed inverse limit is zero.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The complete number-field class-two test with its finite arithmetic evaluations. Let $s$ be a continuous section of $N^{\rm cc}$ over $L$. Use the actual obstruction two-cocycle $o$ and its origin-corrected residue family $r=(r_v)_{v\nmid3,\infty}$ from A.8, restricted to $G_L$. Write $D_v=\operatorname{Frob}_v-1$ on $\mathcal K(-1)$. First require \[ y_v=-D_v^{-1}r_v\in\mathcal K(-1),\qquad (y_v)_v\in\mathcal R_L(\mathcal K(-1)). \tag{C.15.1} \] The actual localization homotopy-fibre cycle $(o,y)$ then supplies, at each $n$, a two-cocycle $\xi_n\in Z^2(G_{L,S},A_n)$, by the comparison below. For every class represented by $(z,(b_v))$ in the explicit finite group $C_n$ of C.14, choose a continuous two-cochain $a$ with values in $\mu_{3^n}$ satisfying \[ da=\xi_n\cup z. \tag{C.15.2} \] Such a cochain always exists. Define \[ \ell_n(s)(z,(b_v)) =\sum_{v\mid3}\operatorname{inv}_v \bigl((\operatorname{res}_v\xi_n)\cup b_v -\operatorname{res}_v a\bigr). \tag{C.15.3} \] The expression in each local invariant is a two-cocycle. Formula (C.15.3) is independent of all the auxiliary cochain choices and is an element of $C_n^\vee$. There is an exact criterion \[ s\text{ lifts to }N/\gamma_3N \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \text{(C.15.1) holds and } \ell_n(s)=0\text{ for every }n\ge1. \tag{C.15.4} \] Every nonempty fibre is a torsor under $\varprojlim_n U_n$, with $U_n$ given by the finite matrices (C.14.3), and no further geometric-stabilizer quotient. Together with C.13 for the initial lift, C.14--C.15 give the number-field version requested in Task C.1: both the residue convergence and the arithmetic test are retained.

statement: Finite algebraic formulas for every point's abelian and central coordinates. Put $m=3^n$. Two successive Kummer covers and a quotient of their finite deck group construct a based finite cover $X_n\to U$ with group \[ P_n=N/(N^{3^n}\gamma_3N). \tag{C.16.1} \] Its multiplication, arithmetic action, transition maps, and fibers at algebraic points are computed by finite algebraic operations. The tangential base point is the specified $s=z/x$, tangent one. Choose compatible lifts $y_1,\ldots,y_{10}$ of a $\mathbb Z_3$-basis of $V$. For every $A\in U(L)$ the construction gives compatible finite cocycles \[ c_{A,n}(g)=(v_{A,n}(g),z_{A,n}(g)) \in(V/3^n)\oplus(\bigwedge\nolimits^2V/3^n). \tag{C.16.2} \] They are obtained by evaluating roots of rational functions at $A$ and comparing the resulting fibers with the Puiseux fiber at $O$. Their inverse limit is a continuous cocycle whose class is the class-two point section of $A$. Thus (C.16.2) evaluates all forty-five central coordinates with their tangent origin.

statement: An evaluated nonzero central point coordinate. Let $\alpha^3=2$, $\zeta=\zeta_3$, $\eta=\zeta_9$ with $\eta^3=\zeta$, and $L=\mathbb Q(\zeta,\alpha)$. For $A=[1:-\alpha:1]\in U(L)$ an explicit quotient of $P_1$ of order $27$ has zero abelian point coordinates and central coordinate \[ -\kappa_L(\zeta)\in H^1(G_L,\mathbb F_3) \tag{C.17.1} \] in the prescribed unit-tangent origin at $O$. This class is nonzero.

statement: The point-image set and its exact central membership criterion. The point-image subset of the class-two germ set is \[ \left\{ \left[\left(\varprojlim_n v_{A,n}, \varprojlim_n z_{A,n}\right)\right]: A\in U(\overline{\mathbb Q}) \right\}, \tag{C.18.1} \] where each finite function is algebraically evaluated by (C.16.3)--(C.16.13). This parametrization is injective, disjoint from the nine packets (C.10.2), and equivariant for $A\mapsto gA$. Its stabilizer at $A$ is $G_{\mathbb Q(A)}$. Given a section and an algebraic point $A$, choose a common number field $L$ of definition. Let $d_n$ be the section cocycle in $P_n$ and $c_{A,n}$ the evaluated cocycle above. Their germs agree exactly when every finite set \[ \mathcal T_n=\{h\in P_n: d_n(g)=h^{-1}c_{A,n}(g)\rho_n(g)h \text{ for all }g\in G_L\} \tag{C.18.2} \] is nonempty. Each test is a computation on a finite Galois group. Combined with the injective abelian point map C.9, it gives a complete central membership criterion for (C.18.1).

statement: The weight-five image of the full profinite special group. For every prime $\ell\geq5$, the rational weight-five metabelian leading image of $\operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(\widehat F_2)$ is \[ (X+Y)\langle X^2,XY,Y^2\rangle_{\Q_\ell}[x,y], \qquad\dim_{\Q_\ell}=3. \] All three displayed basis vectors are leading derivation coordinates of actual multiplier-one full profinite special automorphisms.

statement: The extra weight-nine direction for the full profinite gentle group. For every prime $\ell\geq5$, the rational weight-nine metabelian leading image of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0$ has dimension two and is \[ \Q_\ell G_9[x,y]\oplus\Q_\ell p_{\mathrm{extra}}[x,y], \qquad G_n=\frac{(X+Y)^n-X^n-Y^n}{XY},\quad p_{\mathrm{extra}}=X^2Y^2(X+Y)^3. \] There is an actual full multiplier-one gentle pair with first pro-$\ell$ pair coefficient $p_{\mathrm{extra}}[x,y]$ in weight nine. Its normalized derivation coordinate is $-p_{\mathrm{extra}}[x,y]$. This pair fails the full pentagon.

statement: The finite pentagon comparison in the weight-nine stratum. At the compatible quotients $PB_n/(\gamma_{11}PB_n\,PB_n^{101})$, for $n=3,4$, the complete multiplier-one, weight-at-least-nine gentle shadow stratum has $101^{37}$ elements. Exactly $101^2$ of these satisfy the complete pentagon. Their degree-nine leading spaces have dimensions four and one, respectively; their metabelian images have dimensions two and one. The latter image is the line generated by $G_9$. Statements D.7--D.8 give the finite comparison and an exact integer certificate. Its characteristic-zero comparison, together with the actual Galois lower bound in D.20, derives R9 in weight nine. The enumeration is of the entire stratum that can contribute a weight-nine leading term, with its degree-ten corrections; it is not an enumeration of other multipliers or of lower leading weights.

statement: Recomputed targets and the checked pentagon upper bound. The original rational program reproduces R8's four rows in weights $1,\ldots,10$. In weight nine its invariant metabelian image has basis $p_0=p_{\mathrm{extra}}$ and \[ \begin{split} p_1={}&2X^7+8X^6Y+17X^5Y^2+23X^4Y^3\\ &+23X^3Y^4+17X^2Y^5+8XY^6+2Y^7, \end{split} \qquad G_9=\frac{15}{2}p_0+\frac92p_1. \] The leading metabelian image of full $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ is contained in $\Q_\ell G_n$ in positive odd weight $n$, and is zero in positive even weight. In particular $p_{\mathrm{extra}}$ is excluded in weight nine by this implication from the pentagon.

statement: Cyclic-cover compatibility for every full profinite GT element. Let $H_N=\ker(\widehat F\to\Z/N)$, where $x\mapsto1$ and $y\mapsto0$. The continuous homomorphism \[ \delta_N:H_N\longrightarrow\widehat F, \quad x^N\mapsto x,\quad y\mapsto y,\quad x^ayx^{-a}\mapsto1\quad(0<a<N) \] is defined on a profinite free basis. For every $(\lambda,f)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, with the convention $x\mapsto x^\lambda$, $y\mapsto f^{-1}y^\lambda f$, one has \[ \delta_N(f)=y^{c_N(f)}f,\qquad c_{MN}(f)=c_M(f)+c_N(f), \] where $c_N(f)$ is the $y$ coordinate of $\delta_N(f)$ in $\widehat F^{\mathrm{ab}}$. These are Enriquez's Theorem 8.1 and Remark 8.6 \cite{DE_Enriquez2007}.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The exact finite test and its remaining quantifier. For a finite-index normal subgroup $N_0\triangleleft B_3$ contained in $PB_3$, the reduction maps of finite shadow sets satisfy \[ \im\bigl(\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0\to\mathrm{GT}(N_0)\bigr) =\bigcap_{K\subset N_0} R_{K,N_0}\bigl(\mathrm{GT}(K)\bigr), \] where $K$ ranges over all finite-index normal subgroups of $B_3$ contained in $N_0$. This is Dolgushev--Guynee, Theorem 5.2, Corollary 5.4 and Proposition 5.5 \cite{DE_DolgushevGuynee2024}, with the full profinite identification supplied by Harbater--Schneps, Main Theorem (a) \cite{DE_HarbaterSchneps2000}.

statement: Compatible finite three- and four-strand shadows. Write $P_n=PB_n$, $p=101$, and \[ K_n=\gamma_{11}P_n\,P_n^p\triangleleft B_n\qquad(n=2,3,4), \qquad K_F=\gamma_{11}F\,F^p, \] where a power subgroup is generated by all the indicated powers. All these groups are discrete until their finite quotients are taken. We use $F=\langle x=A_{12},y=A_{23}\rangle\le P_3$ and the same braid generators as in D.4. Let $\mathcal G_9$ be the finite gentle shadows at $K_3$ with $m=0\pmod p$ and $f\in\gamma_9(F/K_F)$. Let $\mathcal P_9\subset\mathcal G_9$ be those satisfying the pentagon in $P_4/K_4$. The logarithm bijection makes both sets vector spaces over $\mathbb F_{101}$ and gives the following dimensions: \[ \begin{array}{c|rr} &\mathcal G_9&\mathcal P_9\\\hline \log f\text{ in degrees }9,10&37&2\\ \text{degree-nine projection}&4&1\\ \text{degree-nine metabelian projection}&2&1. \end{array} \tag{D.7.1} \] The last right-hand space is exactly $\mathbb F_{101}G_9[x,y]$. The induced three-strand kernel associated to $K_4$ in the finite parenthesized-braid definition is exactly $K_3$, so $\mathcal P_9$ consists of actual finite pentagon shadows in that definition, not merely solutions in an unrelated Lie target.

statement: An integer pentagon certificate and the weight-nine comparison. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero or characteristic at least five. In the free Lie algebra $L_k(X,Y)$ put \[ V_9=\{h\in L_k(X,Y)_9: h(X,Y)+h(Y,X)=0,\quad [X,h(X,Y)]=[X+Y,h(-X-Y,Y)]\}. \] Then $\dim V_9=4$, its metabelian image has dimension two, and the infinitesimal pentagon map $P:V_9\to(\mathfrak t_4)_9$ has rank three. Its one-dimensional kernel has metabelian image $k\,G_9(X,Y)[X,Y]$. The complete finite projection in D.7 is this kernel when $k=\mathbb F_{101}$. For every $\ell\ge5$, applying the corresponding rational leading-term map to the full profinite pentagon equation and using D.20 gives precisely $\mathbb Q_\ell G_9(X,Y)[X,Y]$ as the weight-nine metabelian image of $\widehat{\rm GT}$ and of the Galois image.

statement: The checked Galois and full GT gamma line in every odd weight. For every prime $\ell\ge5$ and every odd integer $m\ge3$, the rational leading metabelian image of $G_\Q$, and therefore of $\widehat{\rm GT}$, is exactly \[ \Q_\ell G_m[x,y],\qquad G_m=\frac{(X+Y)^m-X^m-Y^m}{XY}. \tag{D.20.1} \] The leading image is zero in weight one and every positive even weight. In particular R9 has dimensions $0,0,1,0,1,0,1,0,1,0$ in weights one through ten, with the specified coordinate $p(X,Y)[x,y]$. This verifies the lower bound used in Tasks D.1--D.3; the full gentle and special image questions in D.1--D.2 remain separate questions about the displayed inclusion maps. \par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.15, manuscript pages 725--733 in the supplied transcription, scans 156--170. The transcription does not establish the recto/verso labels for this range.}

statement: The weight-five full special image has dimension one or three. Let $\ell\ge5$, and let $\mathscr I_{5,\ell}$ be the rational weight-five metabelian leading image of the full profinite group $\operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(\widehat F_2)$, with the source filtration and leading map specified at the beginning of Part D. Then \[ \dim_{\Q_\ell}\mathscr I_{5,\ell}\in\{1,3\}. \tag{D.21.1} \] In particular the intermediate value two offered in Task D.1 is excluded. The symmetry comparison gives the displayed two possible dimensions; the full-source construction in D.50--D.51 proves that the actual value is three. More precisely, the polynomial coordinate map \[ (X+Y)q(X,Y)[x,y]\longmapsto q(X,Y) \quad:\quad (X+Y)\Q_\ell[X,Y]_2[x,y]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \Q_\ell[X,Y]_2 \tag{D.21.2} \] identifies the target with the direct sum of the gamma line $\Q_\ell(X^2+XY+Y^2)$ and an absolutely irreducible two-dimensional $\mathfrak S_3$-module. The image in (D.21.1) contains that line and is stable under this actual geometric symmetry action. \par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.15, manuscript pages 725--733 in the supplied transcription, scans 156--170; the full special-image question of LM7 D.13.}

statement: Exact integral rank recovery and a finite-congruence limitation. Let $M$ be a finite free $\Z_\ell$-module and let $L\subset M$ be the image of a continuous homomorphism from a compact group to the additive group of $M$. Write $L_n$ for its image under the specified reduction $M\twoheadrightarrow M/\ell^nM$. There are integers $e_1,\ldots,e_r\geq0$ such that \[ \log_\ell|L_n|=\sum_{i=1}^r\max(n-e_i,0),\qquad \dim_{\Q_\ell}(L\otimes\Q_\ell) =\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_\ell|L_n|}{n}=r. \tag{D.22.1} \] The successive difference of the displayed logarithms equals $r$ for every $n>\max_i e_i$. For each $a\geq1$ and each $\ell\geq5$, the actual $\mathfrak S_3$-module $M=\Z_\ell[X,Y]_2$ of D.21 contains two $\mathfrak S_3$-stable closed submodules with the same image in $M/\ell^aM$, both containing $\Z_\ell q_0$, and with rational dimensions one and three, respectively. The corresponding two-dimensional target of D.2 contains submodules with the same finite reduction and rational dimensions one and two. These are explicit submodules; we assert no realization of them as images of the profinite sources in D.1 or D.2. They refute the inference of a rational upper bound from one vanishing extra congruence without further control of the integral image.

statement: The complete abelian peripheral obstruction and chief-step count. Let \[ 1\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow E\xrightarrow{\pi}G \longrightarrow1 \tag{D.23.2} \] be an extension of finite groups with $A$ elementary abelian of characteristic $p$. Choose generators $X_1,X_2$ of $E$, put $X_3=(X_1X_2)^{-1}$ and $g_i=\pi(X_i)$, and denote the resulting epimorphisms by $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ and $q_G=\pi q_E$. Let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ and $\lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times$ satisfy $\alpha(g_i)\sim_G g_i^\lambda$ for all three indices. Write $A_G=A/[E,A]$, use additive notation in $A$, and set $C_i=C_G(g_i)$. There are well-defined homomorphisms \[ \kappa_i:C_i\longrightarrow A_G, \qquad c\longmapsto[\widetilde c,X_i]\bmod[E,A], \qquad H=\sum_{i=1}^3\operatorname{im}\kappa_i. \tag{D.23.3} \] Choose $h_i\in G$ with $\alpha(g_i)=h_i g_i^\lambda h_i^{-1}$, choose lifts $H_i\in E$, and put \[ U_i=H_iX_i^\lambda H_i^{-1},\qquad r=U_1U_2U_3\in A. \tag{D.23.4} \] The class $o(\alpha,\lambda)=[r]\in A_G/H$ is independent of these choices. It vanishes exactly when there is a continuous homomorphism $f:\widehat F\to E$ such that \[ \pi f=\alpha q_G, \qquad f(x_i)\sim_E X_i^\lambda\quad(1\leq i\leq3). \tag{D.23.5} \] The number of these literal homomorphisms is zero for nonzero $o(\alpha,\lambda)$; for zero obstruction it is \[ C(E,G;X_1,X_2)= \frac{|A|^2|A_G|\prod_{i=1}^3|C_G(g_i)|} {|H|\prod_{i=1}^3|C_E(X_i)|}. \tag{D.23.6} \] When $A$ is an irreducible $\mathbf F_p[G]$-module, every nonempty set in \textup{(D.23.5)} contains an epimorphism. More precisely, let $b(E,G;X_1,X_2)$ be the number of complements $C$ to $A$ in $E$ whose unique section $s_C:G\to C$ satisfies $s_C(g_i)\sim_E X_i$ for every $i$. For zero obstruction the number of epimorphisms in \textup{(D.23.5)} is exactly $C-b>0$. Thus every noncentral elementary-abelian chief step admits a generating peripheral lift. The possible abelian chief obstruction is confined to a central kernel of order $p$. The fixed-$h_i$ obstruction $[r]\in A_G$ is the relative extension class under the explicit identification \[ H^2(\widehat F,\{S_1,S_2,S_3\};A_{\alpha q_G}) \simeq A_G. \tag{D.23.7} \] Moreover $[r]$ comes from $H_2(G,\mathbf F_p)$ by the universal central $p$-cover comparison in \textup{(D.23.12)} below. In particular $p\nmid|G|$ forces the obstruction to vanish.

statement: A peripheral-preserving finite automorphism with no peripheral lift. Let $S=\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_{11})$ and \[ E=\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf F_{11})\times S, \qquad G=S\times S, \qquad\pi=(\text{central quotient},1). \tag{D.24.1} \] There is an explicit epimorphism $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ for which the factor-swap automorphism $\alpha:G\to G$, $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a)$, preserves each of the three labelled peripheral conjugacy classes with multiplier one, but no homomorphism \textup{(D.23.5)} exists. Its obstruction is the nonidentity element of $\ker\pi=\{(I,1),(-I,1)\}$. The maximal pro-$\ell$ quotients of both $E$ and $G$ are trivial for every prime $\ell$. More precisely, for any two-generated finite $\ell$-group $L$ with a specified generating triple $l_1l_2l_3=1$ and any multiplier-one peripheral automorphism $\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(L)$, the corresponding product quotient has maximal pro-$\ell$ quotient exactly $L$. The automorphism $\alpha\times\beta$ of $G\times L$ has no peripheral lift to $E\times L$, whereas $1_G\times\beta$ has an explicit generating peripheral lift. Thus the same prescribed finite pro-$\ell$ component has both an obstructed and an admitted choice of perfect component in this example.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: An order-five peripheral cycle obstructed by a central kernel of order two. There are finite groups \[ E\xrightarrow{\pi}G=A_8^5,\qquad |\ker\pi|=2, \tag{D.25.1} \] an epimorphism $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$, and a multiplier-one, labelled peripheral automorphism $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ of order five, such that none of $\alpha,\alpha^2,\alpha^3,\alpha^4$ has a weak peripheral lift through $\pi$. The kernel is central and its obstruction group in D.23 is exactly $\mathbf F_2$. Consequently taking a $5$-adic unit power cannot remove this obstruction. In particular the order of the obstruction group does not, by itself, bound the exponent of a power that removes a pointed peripheral lifting obstruction. Both groups in \textup{(D.25.1)} are perfect, and their maximal pro-five quotients are trivial. Thus this counterexample corrects a proposed lifting argument; it imposes no restriction on a nonzero pro-five leading coordinate in D.1.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: The exact covering restriction of the central peripheral obstruction. Keep the finite groups, epimorphism $q_G:\widehat F\to G$, factor-swap automorphism $\alpha$, and central extension $\pi:E\to G$ of D.24. Put $\theta=\alpha q_G$ and $S_i=\overline{\langle x_i\rangle}$, with $x_3=(x_1x_2)^{-1}$. For any open subgroup $H\leq\widehat F$ of index $d$, take representatives $t\in F=\langle x_1,x_2\rangle$ of $H\backslash\widehat F/S_i$ and set \[ e_{i,t}=[S_i:S_i\cap t^{-1}Ht],\qquad h_{i,t}=t x_i^{e_{i,t}}t^{-1},\qquad S_{i,t}=\overline{\langle h_{i,t}\rangle}\leq H. \tag{D.26.1} \] Let $b_H$ be the number of these induced peripheral subgroups. The number of continuous homomorphisms $v:H\to E$ satisfying \[ \pi v=\theta|_H,\qquad v(h_{i,t})\sim_E X_i^{e_{i,t}} \quad\text{for every }(i,t) \tag{D.26.2} \] is exactly \[ \begin{cases} 0,&d\text{ odd},\\ 2^{\,d+2-b_H},&d\text{ even}. \end{cases} \tag{D.26.3} \] These are literal weak lifts with the fixed base map; no surjectivity or quotient by conjugation is imposed on the count. In particular every cover of odd index retains the nonzero peripheral obstruction of D.24. For every odd prime $\ell$, this includes every open subgroup obtained as the inverse image of a subgroup of a finite $\ell$-group quotient of $\widehat F$. The exact map controlling this assertion is restriction \[ \begin{split} H^2_{\cts}(\widehat F,\{S_i\};\F_2)&\longrightarrow H^2_{\cts}(H,\{S_{i,t}\};\F_2),\\ \F_2\ni a&\longmapsto d a\in\F_2, \end{split} \tag{D.26.4} \] where both identifications use the sum of the oriented boundary coordinates. Thus passage to deeper covers of odd index cannot solve this specified finite peripheral problem.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: Exact coupled fibres over normalized finite pro-five shadows. There are explicit two-generated finite groups \[ E_0\xrightarrow{\pi_0}G_0\xrightarrow{\rho}C_5, \qquad |\ker\pi_0|=2, \tag{D.27.1} \] whose respective kernels over $C_5$ are perfect, and in which $C_5$ acts nontrivially on those kernels by permutation of five simple factors in each of five rows. The groups have an order-five, multiplier-one peripheral automorphism $R\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_0)$ inducing the identity on $C_5$. Each of $R,R^2,R^3,R^4$ is obstructed at the central kernel in \textup{(D.27.1)}. Here is their exact comparison with a prescribed pro-five component. Let $L=\langle l_1,l_2\rangle$ be a finite $5$-group with an epimorphism $\eta:L\to C_5=\langle t\rangle$ satisfying $\eta(l_1)=t$, $\eta(l_2)=1$, and put $l_3=(l_1l_2)^{-1}$. Let $\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(L)$ be specified by the peripheral equalities \[ \beta(l_1)=l_1,\qquad \beta(l_2)=f^{-1}l_2f,\quad \eta(f)=1, \qquad\beta(l_3)=h l_3h^{-1}. \tag{D.27.2} \] The condition on $f$ holds in particular for the usual normalized multiplier-one form with $f\in L'$. Define the actual fibre products \[ E_L=E_0\times_{C_5}L, \qquad G_L=G_0\times_{C_5}L. \tag{D.27.3} \] The paired source generators give epimorphisms $\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E_L\twoheadrightarrow G_L$, and the coordinate maps $E_L\to L$ and $G_L\to L$ are their maximal pro-five quotient maps. The automorphism \[ \alpha_-=(R,\beta)\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_L) \tag{D.27.4} \] has the prescribed three peripheral conjugacy classes and has no weak peripheral lift to $E_L$. On the same quotient and over the same $\beta$, the automorphism $\alpha_+=(1,\beta)$ has the explicit generating peripheral lift $(1,\beta)\in\operatorname{Aut}(E_L)$. The construction includes an explicit nonidentity $\beta$ of order five on a finite two-generated $5$-group, given in \textup{(D.27.15)--(D.27.18)} below. Thus the perfect kernel, its action by the quotient, and the prescribed pro-five automorphism can all be nontrivial. The admitted branch is proved for every datum \textup{(D.27.2)}; these coupled quotients therefore do not exclude such a prescribed pro-five shadow.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: Generating relative lifts for transitive $A_5$ wreath kernels. Let $D\leq\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a transitive finite $5$-group, let $n=|\Omega|\geq25$, and let $q:\widehat F=\langle x_1,x_2\rangle\twoheadrightarrow D$ be an epimorphism. Put $x_3=(x_1x_2)^{-1}$ and $d_i=q(x_i)$. Assume that each of the three permutations $d_i$ has no fixed point on $\Omega$. Give $\Omega$ its right $D$-action, and write \[ M=A_5^{\Omega},\qquad (d\cdot a)(\omega)=a(\omega d),\qquad W=M\rtimes D. \tag{D.28.1} \] For every three elements $U_i\in W$ above $d_i$ there exist $a_i\in M$ such that \[ V_i=a_iU_ia_i^{-1},\qquad V_1V_2V_3=1,\qquad\langle V_1,V_2\rangle=W. \tag{D.28.2} \] Equivalently, every such finite relative lifting problem has a generating solution, with the three base conjugators fixed. The kernel $M$ is a nonabelian chief factor: it is a product of nonabelian simple groups, and $D$ permutes its factors transitively. In particular this applies to the regular action of every noncyclic two-generated finite $5$-group $D$. It also has the following exact coupled consequence. Let $L$ be a finite $5$-group with epimorphism $\eta:L\to D$, and suppose specified epimorphisms from $\widehat F$ to $W$ and $L$ have the same projection to $D$. Let $\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(L)$ induce an automorphism $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)$, and suppose its three source peripheral images satisfy \[ \beta(l_i)=h_i l_i^\lambda h_i^{-1} \quad(1\leq i\leq3),\qquad \lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times. \tag{D.28.3} \] Then $\beta$ has a generating peripheral lift from $\widehat F$ to the actual fibre product $W\times_D L$, over the map $\beta q_L$, with the same multiplier $\lambda$ and with the given $h_i$ retained in the $L$-coordinates of its conjugators.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement: Exact peripheral count invariance for every $A_5$ chief step over an odd-order group. Let \[ 1\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow E\xrightarrow{\pi}D \longrightarrow1, \qquad A\simeq A_5^{\Omega}, \tag{D.29.1} \] be a finite extension, with $D$ of odd order and $A$ a nonabelian chief factor of $E$. Let $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ be an epimorphism, $X_i=q_E(x_i)$, $q=\pi q_E$, and $d_i=q(x_i)$. Let $q_1:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D$ be any epimorphism, let $\lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times$, and let $h_i\in D$ be specified elements such that \[ q_1(x_i)=h_i d_i^\lambda h_i^{-1}. \tag{D.29.2} \] choose any lifts $H_i\in E$ of $h_i$. There is an epimorphism $f:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ such that \[ \pi f=q_1, \qquad f(x_i)=a_iH_iX_i^\lambda H_i^{-1}a_i^{-1} \quad\text{for some }a_i\in A. \tag{D.29.3} \] The number of these literal epimorphisms is exactly the number for $(q_1,\lambda,h_1,h_2,h_3)=(q,1,1,1,1)$. In particular it is positive. There is no degree or fixed-point restriction on the transitive factor action on $\Omega$. The same assertion holds in every actual fibre product $E\times_D L$, for a finite odd-order group $L$ and a prescribed peripheral epimorphism $q_{L,1}:\widehat F\to L$ over $q_1$, relative to the original source epimorphism $q_L:\widehat F\to L$: there is a generating lift over $q_{L,1}$, with its specified peripheral conjugators retained in the $L$-coordinate. Here both maps to $L$ compose to the indicated maps to $D$, and the new peripheral values are the specified conjugates of the $\lambda$th powers of the original ones. Thus every $A_5$ chief extension over a finite odd-order group, including its coupled pullbacks, admits all the peripheral shadows described in \textup{(D.29.2)--(D.29.3)}. In particular this applies over every finite $\ell$-group for every odd prime $\ell$.

statement: Exact peripheral count invariance for every finite $A_5$ chief extension. Let \[ 1\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow E\xrightarrow{\pi}D \longrightarrow1,\qquad A\simeq A_5^{\Omega}, \tag{D.30.1} \] be a finite extension in which $A$ is a nonabelian chief factor. Let $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ be an epimorphism, put $X_i=q_E(x_i)$, $q_0=\pi q_E$, and $d_i=q_0(x_i)$. Let $q_1:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D$ be any epimorphism, and suppose its three specified peripheral values are \[ q_1(x_i)=h_i d_i^\lambda h_i^{-1},\qquad h_i\in D,\quad \lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times. \tag{D.30.2} \] For arbitrary chosen lifts $H_i\in E$ of $h_i$, there is an epimorphism $f:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ with \[ \pi f=q_1,\qquad f(x_i)=a_iH_iX_i^\lambda H_i^{-1}a_i^{-1} \quad(a_i\in A). \tag{D.30.3} \] The number of these literal epimorphisms equals the number for $(q_1,\lambda,h_1,h_2,h_3)=(q_0,1,1,1,1)$. In particular it is positive. There is no restriction on the order of $D$, the degree of its factor action, its fixed peripheral points, or its outer action on $A$. The result applies at every successive $A_5$ chief step of a finite tower with its given original source epimorphism and its prescribed new peripheral base epimorphism.

statement: A proper-lift obstruction and its complete forgetful fibre. There is an actual chief extension \[ 1\longrightarrow\operatorname{Inn}(A_6) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(A_6) \xrightarrow{\pi}\mathbf F_2^2\longrightarrow1 \tag{D.31.1} \] and a generating peripheral triple $(X,Y,Z)$ of orders $(2,8,8)$ such that the following holds. Put $d_1=\pi(X)$, $d_2=\pi(Y)$, and $d_3=d_1+d_2$. With the same base epimorphism $q_1=q_0$, multiplier $\lambda=1$, and prescribed base conjugators \[ (h_1,h_2,h_3)=(0,0,d_1), \tag{D.31.2} \] there are exactly ninety weak lifts and no epimorphic lift. Every weak lift has image isomorphic to \[ C_8\rtimes_5 C_2 =\langle r,s:r^8=s^2=1,\ srs^{-1}=r^5\rangle. \tag{D.31.3} \] The original choice $(h_1,h_2,h_3)=(0,0,0)$ has exactly 360 lifts, all epimorphic. More precisely, write $h_i=p_i d_1+q_i d_2$, with $p_i,q_i\in\mathbf F_2$. The complete prescribed-conjugator count is \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} q_1+p_2+p_3+q_3&\text{weak lifts}&\text{epimorphic lifts}\\\hline 0&360&360\\ 1&90&0. \end{array} \tag{D.31.4} \] Thus each row occurs for 32 of the 64 possible base-centralizer triples. Forgetting the prescribed base conjugators gives a union of 1800 weak lifts and 1440 epimorphic lifts. These form exactly two simultaneous $\operatorname{Aut}(A_6)$-conjugacy orbits, of sizes 1440 and 360, respectively. The first is the orbit of the original generating triple. In particular the ordinary peripheral lift fibre is nonempty. Both groups in \textup{(D.31.1)} have trivial maximal pro-five quotient. For every finite five-group $L$ and every specified multiplier-one peripheral automorphism $\beta$ of its given two-generated source quotient, the actual products of \textup{(D.31.1)} with $L$ have maximal pro-five quotient $L$. Over the same base shadow $1_{\mathbf F_2^2}\times\beta$ they have both the obstructed prescribed-conjugator branch above and an explicit admitted branch.

statement: An exhausted Nielsen family obstructs the ordinary generating lift. There is a split finite chief extension \[ 1\longrightarrow A_6\longrightarrow\mathcal E \xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal D\longrightarrow1, \qquad |\mathcal D|=4\cdot360^{12},\quad |\mathcal E|=4\cdot360^{13}, \tag{D.32.1} \] an actual source epimorphism $q_{\mathcal E}:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E$, and an order-two automorphism $\alpha$ of $\mathcal D$ preserving all three labelled peripheral conjugacy classes, such that no epimorphism $f:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E$ satisfies \[ \pi f=\alpha\pi q_{\mathcal E},\qquad f(x_i)\in q_{\mathcal E}(x_i)^{\mathcal E}. \tag{D.32.2} \] All base conjugators are allowed in \textup{(D.32.2)}. There are exactly 2160 weak lifts; each is the graph of an explicit coordinate projection of $\mathcal D$, conjugated in the added $A_6$ factor, and has image a complement to that factor. For the original base map, the corresponding ordinary peripheral fibre has 3240 weak lifts, of which 1080 are epimorphic and 2160 have complementary image. The maximal pro-five quotients of $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal D$ are trivial. For every prescribed finite-five-group multiplier-one peripheral automorphism $\beta$, taking the actual products with its source quotient gives both an ordinary obstructed base shadow $\alpha\times\beta$ and an explicitly admitted base shadow $1\times\beta$, with the same induced pro-five shadow $\beta$.

statement: Every odd-order multiplier-one ordinary shadow lifts across a single $A_6$ kernel. Let \[ 1\longrightarrow S\longrightarrow E \xrightarrow{\pi}D\longrightarrow1, \qquad S\simeq A_6, \tag{D.33.1} \] be a finite extension, with a given epimorphism $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ and peripheral values $X_i$, whose images in $D$ are $d_i$. Let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)$ have odd order $m$ and satisfy $\alpha(d_i)\in d_i^D$ for the three labelled peripherals. There is an actual automorphism $\widetilde\alpha$ of $E$, of order $m$, covering $\alpha$, fixing $S$ pointwise, and satisfying \[ \widetilde\alpha(X_i)\in X_i^E. \tag{D.33.2} \] Consequently $\widetilde\alpha q_E$ is an ordinary peripheral epimorphic lift of $\alpha\pi q_E$. In particular a multiplier-one ordinary obstruction of order five cannot occur at a single $A_6$ kernel.

statement: Cyclic outer image admits every multiplier-one peripheral base automorphism. Let \[ 1\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow E \xrightarrow{\pi}D\longrightarrow1 \tag{D.34.1} \] be a finite extension with $Z(A)=1$ and a given source epimorphism $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$. Let $X_i=q_E(x_i)$ and $d_i=\pi(X_i)$. Write $\epsilon:D\to\operatorname{Out}(A)$ for its actual outer action, and suppose its image is cyclic. Every $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)$ with $\alpha(d_i)\in d_i^D$ has an actual automorphism lift $\widetilde\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(E)$ satisfying $\widetilde\alpha(X_i)\in X_i^E$. The full group $\operatorname{Out}(A)$ need not be abelian.

statement: A two-group outer image admits every order-five multiplier-one peripheral shadow. In \textup{(D.34.1)}, retain $Z(A)=1$ and the given two-generated source. Every order-five automorphism $\alpha$ of $D$ preserving the three labelled peripheral conjugacy classes has an ordinary peripheral automorphism lift of order five to $E$, fixing $A$ pointwise. In particular an order-five ordinary obstruction with kernel $A_6^\Omega$ requires its transitive factor-permutation image to have non-two-power order. It cannot occur with two simple factors or with any purely two-group factor-permutation action.

statement: Every nonidentity power of an ordinary peripheral order-five shadow is obstructed. Put \[ \begin{split} m&=61478762617650840213814367698461663428608,\\ h&=61478762617650840528585632300833961934848. \end{split} \tag{D.36.1} \] There are explicitly specified finite groups, a split chief extension, and an actual source epimorphism \[ 1\longrightarrow A_6^{20}\longrightarrow\mathcal E \xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal B\longrightarrow1, \qquad q_{\mathcal E}:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E, \tag{D.36.2} \] with \[ |\mathcal B|=5662310400\cdot360^{100m}, \qquad |\mathcal E|=5662310400\cdot360^{100m+20}. \tag{D.36.3} \] An actual automorphism \(\gamma\) of \(\mathcal B\) has order five and preserves the three labelled peripheral conjugacy classes of \(q_{\mathcal B}=\pi q_{\mathcal E}\), with multiplier one. For every \(k=1,2,3,4\), the ordinary fibre \[ \left\{f:\widehat F\longrightarrow\mathcal E: \pi f=\gamma^kq_{\mathcal B},\ f(x_i)\in q_{\mathcal E}(x_i)^{\mathcal E} \ (i=1,2,3)\right\} \tag{D.36.4} \] has weak solutions and has no epimorphic solution. All base conjugators, including their full centralizer ambiguity, are allowed in this assertion. The maximal pro-five quotients of \(\mathcal B\) and \(\mathcal E\) are trivial. Taking their actual products with a prescribed finite five-group source \(L\) retains an obstructed branch \(\gamma^k\times\beta^k\), for each \(k=1,2,3,4\), and an admitted branch \(1\times\beta^k\), over the same multiplier-one pro-five shadow \(\beta^k\). In particular, every \(5\)-adic unit power of the specified order-five finite component remains obstructed. These maps concern a specified finite component; the simultaneous admitted branch is part of the asserted comparison with D.1.

statement: An exact characteristic Magnus target and all three ordinary outer parameters. For every \(n\geq1\) there is an explicitly specified characteristic finite quotient \[ \rho_n:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow P_n,\qquad |P_n|=5^{17n+2}, \tag{D.37.1} \] which is metabelian of nilpotency class six. It has \(P_n^{\rm ab}\simeq(\mathbf Z/5^{n+1})^2\), derived subgroup \((\mathbf Z/5^n)^{15}\), and centre \(\gamma_6P_n\simeq(\mathbf Z/5^n)^5\). Its kernel is fully invariant, by an explicit Fox substitution map. Coefficient reduction gives onto maps \(P_{n+1}\to P_n\). There is a specified injective homomorphism \[ (\mathbf Z/5^n)^3\longrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(P_n), \qquad (A,B,C)\longmapsto[\beta_{A,B,C}], \tag{D.37.2} \] whose representatives fix \(x_1\) and have actual multiplier-one conjugators at \(x_2\) and \(x_3\). The parameters have exactly the requested leading coordinate \[ (X+Y)(AX^2+BXY+CY^2)[x,y]. \tag{D.37.3} \] The homomorphism is injective in the ordinary outer group, including all inner automorphisms of the finite quotient. At \(n=1\), every nonzero parameter gives an actual automorphism of order five of the characteristic group of order \(5^{19}\). The parameter maps and their geometric \(\mathfrak S_3\) action are compatible with coefficient reduction. These are fixed finite source targets for the full profinite lifting question. No assertion that a non-gamma parameter in \textup{(D.37.2)} has a full profinite peripheral lift is included.

statement: Exact constraints on the first mixed tests above the characteristic five-group. Every automorphism \(\beta_Q\) of \(P_1\) constructed in D.37 is class-preserving. There is an explicit conjugator for every element, given in \textup{(D.38.3)} below. The nonzero parameters nevertheless retain their nonzero ordinary outer classes by the exact centralizer calculation of D.37. In addition, let \[ 1\longrightarrow A_6^\Omega\longrightarrow E \xrightarrow{\pi}D\longrightarrow1 \tag{D.38.1} \] be a finite chief extension with \(D\) of odd order. Fix an epimorphism \(q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E\), write \(X_i=q_E(x_i)\), \(q=\pi q_E\), \(d_i=q(x_i)\), and let \(q_1:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D\) be any epimorphism with \(q_1(x_i)=h_i d_i^\lambda h_i^{-1}\), for specified \(h_i\in D\) and \(\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{\times}\). For any lifts \(H_i\) of \(h_i\), there is an epimorphism \(f:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E\) satisfying \[ \pi f=q_1,\qquad f(x_i)=a_iH_iX_i^\lambda H_i^{-1}a_i^{-1} \quad(a_i\in A_6^\Omega). \tag{D.38.2} \] The number of these literal epimorphisms is the same as in the original case \((q_1,\lambda,h_i)=(q,1,1)\). The comparison also holds in the actual coupled pullback with any finite odd-order group over \(D\), retaining its prescribed peripheral epimorphism and conjugators. In particular every \(\beta_Q\) passes every such chief step over its fixed characteristic target \(P_1\).

statement: Actual automorphisms and every generating lift at the first coprime characteristic cover. Let \(q:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D\) be an epimorphism to a finite group, let \(K=\ker q\), and let \(p\nmid |D|\). Put \[ \Phi_p(K)=\overline{K^p[K,K]},\qquad E=\widehat F/\Phi_p(K),\qquad M=K/\Phi_p(K),\qquad n=|D|. \tag{D.39.1} \] Then \(E\) is finite of order \(n p^{n+1}\), and \(M\) is the actual \(D\)-module of first homology of the regular pants cover. If \(K\) is characteristic in \(\widehat F\), so is \(\Phi_p(K)\). Write \(X_i\) for the images of the three peripheral generators in \(E\), \(d_i=q(x_i)\), and \(e_i=\operatorname{ord}(d_i)\). For every \(\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)\), \(\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{\times}\), and specified \(h_i\in D\) with \[ \alpha(d_i)=h_i d_i^\lambda h_i^{-1}, \tag{D.39.2} \] there is an actual automorphism \(\widetilde\alpha\) of \(E\) covering \(\alpha\) such that, for any chosen lifts \(H_i\) of \(h_i\), \[ \widetilde\alpha(X_i) =a_iH_iX_i^\lambda H_i^{-1}a_i^{-1} \quad\text{with }a_i\in M. \tag{D.39.3} \] Every generating source lift above \(\alpha q\) factors through an automorphism of this same \(E\). Let \(B\subset M\) be the boundary submodule and \(C=M/B\). The complete fibre with the base conjugators \(h_i\) fixed has, after stated linear choices, the parameter set \[ (M/M^D)\ \times\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf F_p[D]}(C,B)\ \times\ \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf F_p[D]}(C). \tag{D.39.4} \] Its literal cardinality is \[ p^{n-1} \bigl|\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf F_p[D]}(C,B)\bigr| \bigl|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf F_p[D]}(C)\bigr|. \tag{D.39.5} \] Allowing every ordinary base conjugator multiplies this cardinality by \[ \prod_{i=1}^3 \frac{|C_D(d_i)|}{e_i}. \tag{D.39.6} \] These formulas count literal generating source maps, or equivalently actual automorphisms of \(E\), before taking any outer quotient. In particular all D.37 parameters have the explicitly described nonempty full fibre at each first universal elementary-\(p\) cover with \(p\ne5\).

statement: Pairing-compatible lifts through the universal abelian coprime covers. Retain the actual source \(q:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D\), its kernel \(K\), and the specified data \((\alpha,\lambda,h_i)\) of D.39, and assume that \(D\) has odd order and \(p\nmid |D|\). For every \(a\geq1\) put \[ E_{p,a}= \widehat F/\overline{[K,K]K^{p^a}},\qquad E_{p,\mathrm{ab}}=\varprojlim_a E_{p,a}. \tag{D.40.1} \] There is a continuous peripheral automorphism of \(E_{p,\mathrm{ab}}\) above \(\alpha\), with the prescribed multiplier and base conjugators, whose compatible automorphisms of all \(E_{p,a}\) induce \(\lambda_p\)-similitudes of the compact cover intersection form over \(\mathbf Z_p\). The same maps preserve the full \(D\)-equivariant group-ring-valued intersection form through the coefficient automorphism induced by \(\alpha\). They are compatible with restriction and transfer on all intermediate covers of this regular cover. In particular every one of the D.37 weight-five parameters passes the equivariant intersection-form test at \(p=2\) and \(p=3\), at every prime-adic precision. At \(p=2\) the induced map also preserves the unique \(D\)-invariant quadratic refinement on compact homology modulo two.

statement: The exact pairing-compatible abelian image and all relative pro-$p$ peripheral lifts. Let \(q:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D\) have finite odd-order image, let \(K=\ker q\), and let \(p\nmid |D|\). Write \(R=K^{(p)}\) for the maximal pro-\(p\) quotient of the actual open subgroup \(K\), and put \[ E_p=\widehat F/\ker(K\to R),\qquad E_{p,\mathrm{ab}}=E_p/\overline{[R,R]}. \tag{D.41.1} \] Then \(R\) is free pro-\(p\) of rank \(|D|+1\), and \(1\to R\to E_p\to D\to1\) is the actual source extension. Fix \(\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)\) and specified \(h_i\in D\) with \(\alpha(d_i)=h_i d_i h_i^{-1}\), and use multiplier one. Every pairing-compatible automorphism of \(E_{p,\mathrm{ab}}\) above \(\alpha\), with these specified peripheral conjugators, lifts to a peripheral automorphism of \(E_p\) above the same \(\alpha\) and with the same conjugator projections. Here pairing-compatible means that its induced map on the compact homology \(C_p\) of D.40 preserves the actual integral intersection form. Conversely every such automorphism of \(E_p\) has this property. This gives the exact image of the full relative pro-\(p\) peripheral fibre in its abelian fibre. The fibre is nonempty for every specified \((\alpha,h_1,h_2,h_3)\). Every generating source map \(\widehat F\to E_p\) above \(\alpha q\) factors through an automorphism of this same \(E_p\). Its full literal peripheral fibre has the exact normalizer parameterization in \textup{(D.41.22)--(D.41.24)} below. In particular all D.37 weight-five shadows admit compatible generating lifts to the full relative pro-\(p\) cover for every \(p\ne5\), with their specified characteristic five-group quotient retained.

statement: Compatible relative lifts over an actual pro-prime-to-$p$ quotient. Let \(q:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D\) be an actual profinite quotient, let \(K=\ker q\), and suppose that every finite quotient of \(D\) has order prime to \(p\). Fix \(\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)\) and actual elements \(h_i\in D\) such that \[ \alpha(d_i)=h_i d_i h_i^{-1}. \tag{D.43.1} \] For a profinite group \(H\), write \[ O^p(H)= \bigcap_{\substack{N\triangleleft_{\mathrm{open}}H\\ H/N\ {\rm a\ finite}\ p{\rm\text{-}group}}}N. \tag{D.43.2} \] Then the actual source extension \[ E_p(D)=\widehat F/O^p(K),\qquad 1\longrightarrow K^{(p)} \longrightarrow E_p(D)\longrightarrow D\longrightarrow1 \tag{D.43.3} \] has a multiplier-one peripheral automorphism above \(\alpha\), with peripheral conjugator projections exactly \(h_i\). Choose any cofinal decreasing sequence of characteristic open normal subgroups \(W_j\) of \(D\), put \(D_j=D/W_j\), \(K_j=q^{-1}(W_j)\), and \(E_{j,p}=\widehat F/O^p(K_j)\). The full literal fibre in \textup{(D.43.3)} is canonically the inverse limit of the complete finite-base fibres of D.42: \[ \begin{split} E_p(D)&\ \simeq\ \varprojlim_j E_{j,p},\\ \mathscr X(D,\alpha,h)&\ \simeq\ \varprojlim_j\mathscr X(D_j,\alpha_j,h_j). \end{split} \tag{D.43.4} \] Both comparisons retain the original map from \(\widehat F\). The fibres are compact and the inverse limit is nonempty. Every generating source map \(\widehat F\to E_p(D)\) above \(\alpha q\) factors through an automorphism of this same \(E_p(D)\); its three peripheral conditions are exactly those in the displayed fibre. In particular let \(K_n=\ker(\widehat F\to P_n)\) for the D.37 quotient. For every odd prime \(p\ne5\), every D.37 parameter has a multiplier-one peripheral realization on the single actual quotient \[ \widehat F/ O^p\bigl(O^2(K_n)\bigr). \tag{D.43.5} \] It induces a chosen full relative pro-two lift from D.41, and hence induces the given \(\beta_Q\) on \(P_n\). Its maximal pro-five quotient is exactly \(P_n\). The resulting automorphisms are compatible through all the finite two-primary stages and their relative \(p\)-central stages.

statement: Exact modular descent and gentle normalization over a coprime base. Let \(\widehat B=C_2\amalg C_3=\langle s,r\mid s^2=r^3=1\rangle\), let \(F=\ker(\widehat B\to\mathfrak S_3)\), and use \[ \tau=sr,\qquad x=\tau^{-2},\qquad y=sxs,\qquad z=(xy)^{-1}. \tag{D.44.1} \] Let \(q:\widehat B\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma\) be an actual pro-prime-to-\(p\) quotient retaining the displayed \(\mathfrak S_3\) quotient, and put \(K=\ker q\). Thus \(p\geq5\). Suppose that an old automorphism \(\alpha_0\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)\) satisfies the following exact multiplier-one conditions: it fixes \(\tau\), sends \(s,r\) to conjugates of the same positive generators, and \[ f_0=s\alpha_0(s) \ \in\ \operatorname{im}(F'\to\Gamma). \tag{D.44.2} \] Then on the actual relative cover \[ G=\widehat B/O^p(K) \tag{D.44.3} \] there is an automorphism \(\sigma\) inducing exactly \(\alpha_0\), fixing \(\tau\), and having \[ \begin{aligned} f=s\sigma(s)&\in\operatorname{im}(F'\to G),& q(f)&=f_0,\\ \sigma(x)&=x,& \sigma(y)&=f^{-1}yf. \end{aligned} \tag{D.44.4} \] It satisfies the exact gentle equations \[ f(y,x)f(x,y)=1,\qquad f(z,x)f(y,z)f(x,y)=1 \tag{D.44.5} \] in the actual pure quotient \(H=\operatorname{im}(F\to G)\). Here evaluations use any one preimage of \(f\) in \(F'\); their values are independent of that choice at the displayed arguments. Its pure outer automorphism centralizes the actual \(\mathfrak S_3\)-outer action, by the explicit comparison below. The finite \(\sigma\)-stable quotient maps from this one \(G\) give a compatible family of generating gentle shadows retaining the literal old \(f_0\), and hence its old outer coordinates. statement: The complete Ferrari-homology pentagon test and its affine fibres. Put $H_3=\F_3^2\rtimes\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_3)$, with the standard left action on column vectors.
