notes: All eight categories reconstructed; 48 scalar entries agree. Universal intrinsic entries proved separately from finite checks.

statement: The requested fibration-axiom table. Let $\mathcal F_W$ denote Grothendieck fibrations with $W$-equivalent transport functors. We use the printed meanings: (7a) is $\mathcal F_W\subseteq\Fib_W$; (7b) says a $W$-map between two members of $\mathcal F_W$ over a common base is universally in $W$; (7c) says $\mathcal F_W\cap W$ is universally in $W$; and (7F) is existence of $W$-then-$\Fib_W$ factorizations. Then \begin{center}\begin{tabular}{lccccc} \toprule $W$ & (7a)&(7b)&(7c)&(7F)&$\Liss_W\cap\Prop_W\subseteq\Fib_W$\\\midrule $W_0$ & no&no&no&yes&no\\ $W_1$ & no&no&no&yes&no\\ $W_n$, $n\geq2$ & no&no&no&yes&no\\ $W_{\mathbb Q}$ & no&no&no&no&no\\ $W_{D(\mathbb Q)}^{\mathrm{lc}}$ & no&no&no&no&no\\ $W_\infty$ & yes&yes&yes&yes&yes\\\bottomrule \end{tabular}\end{center}
notes: All six localizer rows settled, including negative factorization entries for the two rational localizers.

statement: Trivial monodromy is necessary and sufficient for integral and rational homology. Let $p:E\to B$ be a categorical covering, that is, a discrete fibration and discrete opfibration. For either $k=\mathbb Z$ or $k=\mathbb Q$, it belongs to $\Fib_{W_{Hk}}$ if and only if its monodromy on every fibre set is trivial. Equivalently, over each connected component $B_0$ it is isomorphic to a product $B_0\times S_0\to B_0$, where $S_0$ may be empty or infinite. In particular a nonempty connected covering of a connected base is intrinsic for either of these two homology localizers exactly when it is isomorphic over the base to its identity covering. This assertion is specific to these coefficients; D.8 gives the contrary mod-$p$ behavior.
notes: Exact covering classification for HZ and HQ; arbitrary empty or infinite fibres allowed. Matrix checks only support the universal proof.

statement: All alternating fixed-shape path spaces for the marked chain. Let $P=[2]$ and let $W$ consist of its identities and $0\to2$. For $n\geq2$, let $F_n(a,b)$ be the full poset of paths of type $(-,+)^n$ from $a$ to $b$, with backward arrows in $W$ and arbitrary endpoint-fixed vertical arrows. Every $F_n(a,b)$ is contractible, except $F_n(1,1)$, which is the disjoint union of an isolated point and a contractible nonempty poset. These two components are preserved by identity padding. The corresponding assertions hold integrally in every homological degree and for all homotopy groups, not only through a finite range.
depends_on: Explicit closure operator; code/AE/path_chain.py and chain_closure_check.py
notes: Uniform all-n>=2 proof for full fixed alternating-shape categories, all endpoints, all homotopy groups. Computational lengths 2,4,6,8,10,12 support but do not replace the proof.

statement: The comparison $J$ is an equivalence for the marked chain. For $([2],\{\mathrm{id},0\to2\})$, the specified comparison from weak-vertical paths to full paths is a weak equivalence for every pair of endpoints. Its infinity-localization is equivalent to the ordinary walking-retraction category, with objects $A,B$, arrows $i:A\to B$, $r:B\to A$, and $ri=1_A$. Its mapping spaces are discrete; $\operatorname{End}(B)=\{1_B,ir\}$, and every other hom-set is a singleton. The objects $0,2$ map to $A$ and $1$ maps to $B$.
depends_on: E.1; directly checked enriched type contractions; Grothendieck homotopy-colimit/cofinality; Dwyer–Kan 1980; Arakawa–Cnossen supplied source
his_places: VII ms.65–67 for the marked three-object chain; PATHS B.6/B.8/C.P2–C.P3; prompt E(1)
notes: Proves the specified J and the walking-retraction infinity-localization. The all-word length<=6 truncation itself was not computed or proved equivalent to the limit; the proof uses the cofinal sequence of alternating shapes.

statement: Complete relative-poset catalogue through four objects. There are respectively $1,3,14,102$ isomorphism classes of pairs $(P,W)$ on $1,2,3,4$ objects, where $P$ is a poset and $W$ contains identities and satisfies two-out-of-three. The attached catalogue lists every pair and also the unique empty relative poset, for $121$ types in all. The program computes all endpoint full-path posets of types $(-,+)^n$, $n=1,2,3$, giving $5313$ rows. In $5307$ rows all connected components are certified contractible by beat-point removal. Exactly six rows have a non-discrete remaining core, all for $P=[3]$ and $W=\{\mathrm{id},0\to2,1\to3\}$. These are bounded calculations, not a proof of the all-type comparison for all $120$ pairs.
notes: Complete catalogue of 121 relative posets including empty. All 5313 endpoint rows for alternating lengths 2,4,6 have integral homology and pi1 certificates. Four rows have S1 type; all others are homotopy discrete. The unbounded J assertion for every pair is not proved.

statement: Transient higher homotopy in a four-object calculation. For $P=[3]$ marked only at identities, $0\to2$, and $1\to3$, the full fixed-shape path poset $F_2(1,2)$ of type $(-,+)^2$ has classifying space $S^1$, whereas the infinity-localization of $(P,W)$ is the terminal infinity-category. Thus a fixed finite path shape need not already give the localization mapping space, even in this small example.
depends_on: E.3; localization universal property; explicit four-point nerve
his_places: Prompt E(2), limitation of fixed-shape stabilization
notes: Checked transient S1 at length 4 for [3] with 02 and 13 marked, although the infinity-localization is terminal. This is not a counterexample to the unbounded map J.

statement: No universal finite length bound for all four-object cases. The full path category for every relative poset on at most four objects is not computed by a finite all-word length cutoff, even at the level of components.
depends_on: Four-point circle poset; ordinary groupoid completion; E.3 catalogue
his_places: Prompt E(1)–E(2), requested universal finite-cutoff premise
notes: Refutes any finite all-word cutoff computing every four-object case: loop components are Z but each finite cutoff has finitely many objects.

statement: The general comparison and the additive and pointed refinements. The specified map $J$ for arbitrary two-out-of-three relative categories, its all-endpoint assertion for the remaining four-object relative-poset cases, and the literal all-vertical and ind-stage transfers in PATHS C.9--C.10 remain unresolved here. E.7--E.8 below give the additive and pointed refinements of the corrected localized hom-spaces. E.2 settles the particular three-object example that PATHS B.8 singled out. E.3 does not settle the unbounded four-object assertion. The standard weak-vertical definition computes the localization and has strict concatenation, but a general additive or smash-product refinement requires additional coherent structure; none is deduced solely from the computations above.
his_places: VII ms.65–67 in general; PATHS B.8/C.9–C.10; prompt E(2)–E(4)
notes: General J and the unbounded <=4-object catalogue remain open. Corrected additive/pointed localized mapping-space refinements are proved below; literal all-vertical and ind-stage transfers remain open.

statement: The corrected additive refinement under direct-sum stability. Let $k$ be a commutative ring in the fixed universe, let $C$ be a small additive $k$-linear category, and let $W$ be a wide subcategory closed under finite direct sums of arrows. The infinity-localization $\mathcal L=C[W^{-1}]$ has a coherent enrichment in the connective derived infinity-category of $k$-modules, written $D^{\leq0}(k)$ in cohomological grading. Its underlying mapping spaces are the localization mapping spaces, and its composition is $k$-bilinear. Consequently the corrected weak-vertical path categories admit composition-compatible $D^{\leq0}(k)$-refinements whose underlying spaces are their nerves. No model-category or suspension--loop hypothesis is required for this assertion about the corrected model.
depends_on: Localization universal property; Badzioch 2002 Theorems1.3/6.4; Dold–Kan; reflected Day convolution
his_places: PATHS C.9 for corrected weak-vertical localized hom-spaces; prompt E(4)
notes: Requires commutative k, small additive k-linear C, and W closed under finite direct sums. Explicit finite-free-module action and monoidal reflection provide coherent composition, not merely objectwise rigidification. No claim for unproved full-path J.

statement: The corrected pointed refinement after localization. Let $C$ be a small category with a zero object $0$, and let $W$ be any wide subcategory. Its infinity-localization is pointed. Its localization mapping spaces, and therefore the corrected weak-vertical path spaces with the zero-arrow basepoints, admit associative unital composition through the smash product, coherently in all variables. This assertion concerns the localized hom-spaces; it does not assert a strictly absorbing operation on every prescribed finite path stage.
depends_on: E.7 adjunction-descent argument; zero-object factorizations; canonical hammock comparison
his_places: PATHS C.10 at corrected localized mapping-space level; prompt E(4)
notes: Smash composition is coherently associative and unital. Does not prove strict absorption at each finite path stage or a uniform later stage for the literal ind-pointed statement.

statement: The action criterion used in this part. Here total asphericity means the condition of XII ms.~88 tested by all ordinary final images; we do not substitute the different diagonal-asphericity terminology used elsewhere in the literature. For a nonempty connected small category $A$, total $W_\infty$-asphericity is equivalent to every connected component of $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$ being weakly contractible, for every covariant $H:A\to\mathrm{Set}$. It is also equivalent to the same condition with integral acyclicity in place of weak contractibility. Exactness of $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$ implies these conditions.
depends_on: Quillen Theorem A; category-of-elements bar resolution; homological Whitehead
his_places: XII ms.88; TOTASPH D.7; PATHS A.8 (specified special cases)
notes: Totality here means XII ms.88 final-image totality. It is not diagonal asphericity.

statement: What totality forces before the affine gap. A totally $W_\infty$-aspherical category has common successors for every finite family of objects. For every original parallel pair $a,b:p\to q$, there are an object $r$ and $t\in\mathbb Z[A(q,r)]$ of augmentation one such that $ta=tb$.
his_places: XII ms.88; TOTASPH D.7; PATHS A.8 (specified special cases)
notes: Only original parallel arrows are affine-equalized; this does not settle all affine parallel pairs.

statement: The requested injection and free-category examples. Let $A_S$ be the full subcategory of $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ on $[n]$, $n\in S\subseteq\mathbb N$. It is totally $W_\infty$-aspherical exactly when $S$ is a singleton or unbounded. In these cases its integral colimits are exact. The category of finite sets and injections, with or without the empty set, is not totally $W_\infty$-aspherical. The one-object category of injective self-maps of $\mathbb N$ is not totally $W_\infty$-aspherical. For the free category on any small directed graph, total $W_\infty$-asphericity is equivalent to filteredness; local finiteness is unnecessary.
his_places: XII ms.88; TOTASPH D.7; PATHS A.8 (specified special cases)
notes: Complete classifications for full injective-ordinal subcategories and free categories; the FI and Inj(N) candidates are not total.

statement: Weakly terminal objects and the finite-object case. A totally $W_\infty$-aspherical category with a weakly terminal object is filtered. Consequently the universal Cat-colimit property in Part F(3) implies filteredness for every category with a weakly terminal object, and for every nonempty connected category with finitely many objects.
his_places: XII ms.88; TOTASPH D.7; PATHS A.8 (specified special cases)
notes: Weakly terminal case complete; includes finite-object connected categories.

statement: The exact connected converse. For a nonempty connected small category $A$ with no weakly terminal object, we do not settle whether total $W_\infty$-asphericity forces exactness of $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$. The exact gap is whether the hypotheses of F.2 equalize every parallel pair in $\operatorname{Aff}_{\mathbb Z}(A)$, not merely every original parallel pair. F.3 resolves the listed injection and free-category candidates but does not remove this gap for a general countable category. Exact integral colimits remain a proved sufficient condition, and the affine-filtered criterion is the precise algebraic reformulation. The original claims of equality with filteredness are false by the unbounded $A_S$ examples.
notes: The general countable exact-colimit implication is not proved.

statement: Total presheaves and composition of dwyerienne sieves. We do not settle whether every totally $W_{\mathbb Z}$-aspherical presheaf is totally $W_\infty$-aspherical, or equivalently the composition assertion specified in TOTASPH F.27. The proof of F.1 does not transfer: for a presheaf $H$ on $A$, totality tests only those covariant actions on its element category pulled back from $A$, whereas the cyclic-cover argument needs arbitrary actions on that element category. The search over all monoids of order at most six and all presheaves of cardinality at most six was not performed in this return. The smaller monoid catalogue in Part A is not such a search and cannot certify this assertion. No acyclic-group example satisfying the required universal restricted-action test is provided here.
notes: No complete monoid<=6/presheaf<=6 search. Cyclic-cover proof does not apply to the restricted-action presheaf question.

statement: Universal Cat-colimit shapes without a weakly terminal object. For a connected countable category $I$ without a weakly terminal object, and hence also in general, the implication from the universal ordinary-Cat-colimit comparison to filteredness remains unresolved here. F.4 gives a necessary totality condition and the full weakly-terminal case. The unbounded injective-ordinal examples do not refute this implication: the diagram $[n]\mapsto B\mathbb N^{n+1}$ has categorical colimit $B\mathbb N\simeq S^1$, whereas its Grothendieck construction has integral homology $\mathbb Z$ in every degree. On all of $\Delta_{\rm inj}$ its degree-$k$ fibre homology, for $k\geq1$, is the projective representable $\mathbb Z[\Delta_{\rm inj}([k-1],-)]$; the homotopy-colimit spectral sequence collapses. On an arbitrary unbounded full subcategory $A_S$, the restricted diagram need not be representable. Instead its higher derived colimits vanish by exactness in F.3, and its colimit is $\mathbb Z$: any two marked $k$-element ordered subsets admit embeddings into a common larger ordinal identifying their marks, then into an object of $A_S$. The categorical colimit is still $B\mathbb N$, since the same embeddings identify all coordinate generators and introduce precisely their commutative-monoid relation. Thus all these shapes fail the premise. This prevents importing the nonfiltered total example as an answer to the different Cat-colimit question.
notes: General countable Cat-colimit converse remains Open; injective ordinals do not satisfy the premise.

statement: The proposed assignment \[ R(F)=\operatorname*{hocolim}_{I\in\mathcal I(\mathbb R)}F(I)\times I \longrightarrow\mathbb R, \] where $\mathcal I(\mathbb R)$ consists of bounded nonempty open intervals and arrows are inclusions, need not have open-inverse-image homotopy cosheaf $F$. This failure already occurs for a represented cosheaf.
notes: Refutes only the proposed hocolim formula, not the localization equivalence.

statement: The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $|\kappa|-|\sigma|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1.

statement: The preceding proof does not follow from \citet[Proposition A.5.10]{GHIJMann2022} by taking $I$ to be all smooth maps and $P$ to be the isomorphisms. That specialization violates the suitable-decomposition cancellation requirement. Indeed $p:[1]\to*$ and $pg:*\to*$, where $g$ selects $1\in[1]$, are smooth, but $g$ is not smooth: the incoming arrow $0\to1$ has no lift. Thus $p,pg\in I$ does not imply $g\in I$. The span universal property used in I.3 is the needed replacement. Contractible uniqueness of individual adjoints, without this extension statement or an explicit unfurling construction, by itself does not state the necessary coherence theorem. The program \texttt{code/GHIJ/small\_counterexamples.py} enumerates the incoming lifts for $p$, $pg$, and $g$, verifying this finite cancellation counterexample.
notes: The failed Mann specialization does not refute the formalism; newer exact span theorem supplies it.

statement: The second stages for spectra and mod-$p$ coefficients. Fix a Grothendieck universe $\mathcal U$, and use a larger universe for categories of $\mathcal U$-small objects. Let $\mathcal C$ be either $\operatorname{Sp}_{\mathcal U}$ or $D(\mathbb F_p)$, with its indicated presentable infinity-category enhancement. We number the stages by \[ W_{\mathcal C}^{(0)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}}^{\mathrm{lc}}, \qquad \mathcal C_1=\mathcal S_{W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}^{\mathrm{lc}}. \tag{I.9.1} \] Here $\mathcal S_W$ is the accessible reflective localization of spaces at exactly the class $W$, and $\mathbb D_{\mathcal E}(A)=\operatorname{Ho}\operatorname{Fun}(NA^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)$. The localizations in (I.9.1) exist and preserve finite products. Their constant-coefficient classes satisfy $W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}=W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}$. For every map $u:X\to Y$ of small spaces, \[ u\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective and } \Omega_xu\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}. \tag{I.9.2} \] The loop condition is tested at one basepoint in every component of $X$. Consequently \[ W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(1)} =W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(2)}=W_\infty, \tag{I.9.3} \] and \[ u\in W_{D(\mathbb F_p)}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective},\\ \pi_i(u)\text{ is an integral isomorphism for }i=1,2,\\ H_*(u\langle2\rangle;\mathbb F_p)\text{ is an isomorphism}. \end{cases} \tag{I.9.4} \] For a pointed connected component, $X\langle2\rangle$ means the homotopy fibre at its chosen basepoint of $X\to\tau_{\leq2}X$. The map $u\langle2\rangle:X\langle2\rangle\to Y\langle2\rangle$ is induced by $u$ and the basepoints. The last two conditions of (I.9.4) are tested on every corresponding pointed component. There are no nilpotence or finite-type hypotheses. The second class is again accessible and product stable, so $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal S_{W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)}}$ realizes it as an ordinary constant-coefficient class. This construction can be iterated at every finite stage for these two starting coefficients. It is a specified realization by localized spaces; functorial construction on all bare derivators and all exact morphisms remains the separate Open assertion of I.7.

statement: The two principal assertions. The classification of all noncuspidal continuous sections of $E_U\to G_\Q$ by $U(\Q)$, and the lifting of every such section along the continuous surjection $G_{\Q(t)}\to E_U$, remain unresolved in this manuscript.
notes: Both full assertions remain undecided.

statement: Local multiplicative completions. For every finite prime $p$, the canonical homomorphism $\Q_p^\times\to\widehat{\Q_p^\times}$ is injective. The canonical homomorphism $\R^\times\to\widehat{\R^\times}$ has kernel $\R_{>0}$ and identifies its target with $\{\pm1\}$.
notes: Real completion records sign only; finite places retain ordinary elements injectively.

statement: Statement (G) as printed. The assertion (G) of L2 and A12 is false, even with every $u_c$ represented by a nonzero rational number.
notes: Explicit finite-coordinate/real-coordinate counterexample; no countersection asserted.

statement: Every finite puncture test in A12. For each finite $S\subset\Q$, the version of (G) testing only $c\in S$ admits a nondiagonal tuple with $x_p\in U(\Q_p)$ at every finite prime and all $u_c$ rational. Consequently no finite $S\supset\{0,1\}$ has the property requested in A12.
notes: A counterexample for every finite rational puncture set, with every coordinate ordinary.

statement: The exact content of one rational Kummer class. Fix $c\in\Q$, $r\in\Q^\times$, and a tuple $(x_v)\in\prod_v\Pj^1(\Q_v)$. The comparison demanded in (G) for $u_c=r$ holds exactly when $x_p\in\{c,c+r,\infty\}$ at each finite prime $p$, and at the real place either $x_\infty\in\{c,\infty\}$ or $\operatorname{sgn}(x_\infty-c)=\operatorname{sgn}(r)$.
notes: Exact permitted finite values and real sign condition.

statement: The entire rational-class part of (G). For a tuple satisfying (G) with every $u_c$ represented by a nonzero rational number, either all finite coordinates are $\infty$, or there is a unique $r\in\Q$ such that every finite coordinate is in $\{r,\infty\}$. In the second case the real coordinate is also in $\{r,\infty\}$. Conversely every such mixed tuple satisfies (G); when all finite coordinates are $\infty$, any real coordinate is permitted with suitable rational choices of $u_c$.
notes: Classifies the part of literal (G) where all selected classes are rational.

statement: All nonconstant self-morphisms of the tripod. Over a characteristic-zero field, every nonconstant morphism $U\to U$ is one of the six automorphisms permuting $\{0,1,\infty\}$. In particular its degree is one.
notes: All nonconstant Q-morphisms U to U; exact ramification count.

statement: The proposed higher-degree self-cover action. The maps $4t(1-t)$ and $j(t)/1728$ do not define self-morphisms of $U$. Their actual finite \'etale restrictions have degrees two and six and domains \[ V_2=\Pj^1\setminus\{0,1,\tfrac12,\infty\}, \qquad V_6=U\setminus\{-1,\tfrac12,2,\zeta_6,\zeta_6^{-1}\}, \] respectively. Consequently L12(iv) and L13 do not define the asserted semigroup action on $\Sec(U/\Q)$ by these maps.
notes: Explicit source opens and spans for the quadratic and j maps.

statement: L12(i) with every coefficient prime. The ordinary rational point section at $t=5$ gives, at the ramified prime 5, a local geometric pro-5 section outside every cuspidal packet. This already holds in its mod-5 geometric abelianization.
notes: Actual point t=5 refutes all-coefficient cuspidality at its coefficient prime.

statement: Explicit valuation coordinates. There is an isomorphism of topological abelian groups \[ \widehat{\Q^\times}\simeq \{\pm1\}\times \left\{(a_q)_q\in\prod_q\widehat{\Z}: \text{for every }n,\ a_q\in n\widehat{\Z} \text{ for all but finitely many }q\right\}. \] It is induced by the sign and the prime valuations. The group on the right is given the inverse-limit topology: a basic neighbourhood of zero requires every coordinate, simultaneously, to vanish modulo a fixed $n$. This specifies the topology used in the isomorphism. A class is locally represented by an element of $\Q_p^\times$ exactly when its $p$-valuation belongs to $\Z\subset\widehat{\Z}$. It is represented by a rational number exactly when all these valuations are integers and only finitely many are nonzero.
notes: Inverse-limit topology and integer-valuation locus are specified.

statement: Infinite-support ordinary solutions exist. The ordinary local completed unit equation has pairs whose two valuation vectors have infinite support. An explicit recursive construction, with actual nonzero $p$-adic local values at every finite prime and cofinally divisible ordinary integer valuations, is given and proved in A.44. Thus the existence assertion in L9 is true.
notes: Infinite-support ordinary-local ghost existence is proved by the explicit recursion in A.44.

statement: Rational absolute irreducibility. For every noncuspidal Selmer section $s$ of $U/\Q$ and every prime $\ell$, the representation $V_{s,\ell}$ is absolutely irreducible. This assertion does not assume finite ramification.
depends_on: R5 in Selmer range; Hodge–Tate character calculation
notes: Full Selmer sections; rational representations, every coefficient prime.

statement: Residual irreducibility and its exact coefficient range. For a noncuspidal Selmer section, $\bar\rho_{s,\ell}$ is absolutely irreducible for every $\ell\ge5$. At $\ell=3$ this fails for an actual rational point section; at $\ell=2$ the representation is trivial for every section.
depends_on: A.12; R2; Stoll Corollary 8.8; Mazur pp.129–131
notes: Residual absolute irreducibility for ell≥5; explicit failures at 2 and 3.

statement: The repaired bounded-support equivalence. For noncuspidal Selmer sections of $U/\Q$, the following four properties define the same class: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item One finite set contains the prime-to-$\ell$ ramification supports of all $\bar\rho_{s,\ell}$, $\ell\ge5$. \item $V_{s,\ell}$ is finitely ramified for at least one $\ell\ge5$. \item The local sections are points $x_p\in U(\Z_p)$ at all but finitely many primes. \item One finite set contains the prime-to-$\ell$ ramification supports of all $V_{s,\ell}$. \end{enumerate} Every section in this class has a rational Tate-system realization $V_{s,\ell}\simeq V_\ell(E)$ for one elliptic curve $E/\Q$ and every $\ell$. The statement does not assert that all noncuspidal sections belong to the class.
depends_on: A.12; A.13; Pan Theorem 1.0.4; Helm–Voloch Proposition 6
notes: Equivalence only; it supplies no common finite ramification set for arbitrary sections.

statement: Prime residual supports do not detect arbitrary cusp contacts. There is a globally cuspidal section for which every prime residual support, away from its coefficient prime, is contained in $\{2\}$, while every adic Legendre representation is infinitely ramified.
notes: A cuspidal example tests the inference from residual support to full support.

statement: An integral Legendre realization. Every noncuspidal Selmer section in the class of A.14 has $\lambda_0\in\Q\setminus\{0,1\}$ and an isomorphism \[ \prod_\ell L_{s,\ell}\simeq \prod_\ell T_\ell(E_{\lambda_0}) \tag{A.16.1} \] of continuous $\widehat\Z[G_\Q]$-modules respecting the ordered level-two structure. The elliptic curve here is an actual Legendre curve over $\Q$; the quadratic twist is detected and removed below.
depends_on: A.14; isogeny lattices; mod-four Kummer matrix
notes: Integral Tate systems and the actual labeled Legendre model.

statement: The exact geometric-conjugator obstruction. In the standard Legendre basis the closure of geometric monodromy is \[ H=\prod_{\ell\ne2}\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z_\ell)\ \times\ \left\{\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\in \operatorname{SL}_2(\Z_2): b,c\in2\Z_2, \ a,d\equiv1\pmod4\right\}. \tag{A.17.1} \] For a labeled integral conjugator $g$ in A.16, the class of its Weil multiplier \[ [\det g]\in \widehat\Z^\times/(\widehat\Z^\times)^2 \tag{A.17.2} \] is independent of $g$. There is a conjugator in $H$ exactly when this class is trivial. Its triviality for every section in A.14 has not been proved here.
notes: Determinant square class of an intertwiner, with its precise conjugator group.

statement: The local rigidity claim L16. At a good ordinary prime an integral Tate representation, even with its Weil pairing, need not determine the Legendre parameter or its $j$-invariant.
depends_on: explicit 2-isogeny; Tate modules of good ordinary curves
notes: Two specified Q17 curves, different j and symplectically isomorphic integral Tate modules.

statement: The exact modular-unit argument. Put $U'=U\setminus\{-1,\tfrac12,2,t^2-t+1=0\}$. Its unit \[ u(t)=1-1728/j(t)= \frac{(t-2)^2(t+1)^2(2t-1)^2}{4(t^2-t+1)^3} \tag{A.19.1} \] has value one at each old cusp $0,1,\infty$. A noncuspidal Selmer section of $U$ admitting a Selmer lift to $U'$ which is integral on $U'$ at almost every prime and whose local cusp centres all belong to the old boundary is a rational point section. The unrestricted lifting equivalence and the phrase ``whatever the cusp labels'' in L17 have not been proved.
depends_on: R7 in its actual unit range
notes: The five removed points include one quadratic closed point; new cusp labels require control.

statement: The quadratic twist in the Fermat conductor assertion. The raw residual Legendre representation of a Selmer section of the Fermat quintic need not be unramified outside $2\cdot5$. LM6-E.8's assertion after the specified quadratic twist is not refuted.
notes: The raw residual Fermat assertion needs its quadratic twist.

statement: An honest point in an analytic-rank-zero cubic class. The point $t=1/2$ lifts to $(1:1:1)$ on $C_2:X^3+Y^3=2Z^3$. This genus-one curve has Jacobian of Mordell--Weil rank zero and analytic rank zero. Thus honest points need not belong to positive-rank cubic classes.
depends_on: explicit cubic map; 2-descent; positive Mellin integral
notes: An actual rank-zero twist selected by a rational point section.

statement: The rank-zero part of A10. Let $V\to U$ be a geometrically connected finite etale cover whose completion admits a specified nonconstant $\Q$-morphism to an elliptic curve of analytic rank zero. Every Selmer section lifting to $V$ is a point or cuspidal section. This applies to a diagonal cubic when its Jacobian has analytic rank zero, and to the explicit quartic and sextic elliptic quotients below when their analytic rank is zero.
depends_on: R2; Stoll range; modular rank-zero finiteness
notes: Exact cubic, quartic and sextic quotient maps are included.

statement: Primary profinite multiples that do not lift. On $C_9:X^3+Y^3=9Z^3$ put $O=(1:-1:0)$, $P=(1:2:1)$, and $V=C_9\setminus\{XYZ=0\}$. The point $P$ has infinite order. For every prime $\ell\ge5$ and every $0\ne a\in\Z_\ell$, the element $a e_\ell P$ of $\widehat{C_9(\Q)}$, where $e_\ell\in\widehat\Z$ is the $\ell$-primary idempotent, is not the compactified Kummer class of any Selmer section of $V$.
notes: A specified family of profinite multiples is excluded; full positive-rank lift locus remains open.

statement: The remaining Legendre route to A1. This route has not proved cofinite integrality for every noncuspidal section, the vanishing of the multiplier class (A.17.2) for every section in A.14, or recognition of a full section from its image under the Legendre representation. Neither assertion of A1 follows from the results above. The unclassified profinite multiples in A10 and the full nonabelian lifting assertion in A8 also remain unresolved.
notes: The missing finite-ramification and full congruence-kernel steps.

statement: finite-coefficient vanishing for the actual ghost locus. Let $\mathcal G$ be the set of pairs $(A,B)\in \widehat{\Q^\times}^{\,2}$ such that, for each finite prime $p$, there is $x_p\in\Q_p\setminus\{0,1\}$ with $A_p=\kappa(x_p)$ and $B_p=\kappa(1-x_p)$. For every integer $n\geq1$ the image of $A\cup B$ in $H^2(G_\Q,\mu_n^{\otimes2})$ is zero. The continuous class lies in the kernel in the exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\varprojlim_m^{\,1} H^1(G_\Q,\mu_{m!}^{\otimes2}) \longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,\widehat{\Z}(2)) \longrightarrow\varprojlim_m H^2(G_\Q,\mu_{m!}^{\otimes2}) \longrightarrow0. \] Its restrictions to all continuous local cohomology groups, including the real one, are zero. No local section theorem is used.
notes: Finite and local vanishing for the actual ordinary-local locus, including real and 2-primary classes.

statement:
the alternating continuous residue at the coefficient prime three. Write \[ R_3=\{(z_q)_{q
e3}\in\prod_{q
e3}\Z_3: z_q\longrightarrow0	ext{ in the cofinite sense}\}, \qquad d(z)_q=(q-1)z_q. \] For $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$, choose local tame Frobenius lifts at $q
e3$ and integral Kummer cocycles. Let their Frobenius values be $\alpha_q, eta_q\in\Z_3$, and let their inertia values be the ordinary integer valuations $a_q=v_q(x_q)$ and $b_q=v_q(1-x_q)$. Then the vector \[ z_q=\alpha_q b_q- eta_q a_q \] belongs to $dR_3$. In particular its class in $R_3/dR_3$ is zero.
notes: Exact alternating residue divisibility at 3; identified with the cup in A.27.

statement: The full continuous cup vanishes on the ordinary local unit-equation locus. For every $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$, \[ A\cup B=0 \quad\text{in }H^2_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_\Q,\widehat\Z(2)). \tag{A.27.1} \] This includes the $2$-primary component and all first derived inverse-limit components. The assertion imposes no finite-support condition on the valuation vectors. It constructs no infinite-support element of $\mathcal G$ and makes no assertion about the obstruction in weight three.
depends_on: A.25; A.26; strict residue map; Weibel VI.8.2
notes: All coefficient primes and the actual first-derived-limit component are computed.

statement: the exact height data supplied by L8. For $n\ge2$ the root stack $\mathcal X_n=\Pj^1_\Q[\sqrt[n]{0},\sqrt[n]{1},\sqrt[n]{\infty}]$ has orbifold Euler characteristic $-1+3/n\le1/2$. It therefore does not satisfy the Euler-characteristic hypothesis $\chi>1$ of Bhargava--Poonen's Theorem 5. A local tuple, by itself, does not specify the global point and metrized vector bundle appearing in Ellenberg--Satriano--Zureick-Brown's Definition 2.11 of height. In particular the notation $N_n$ in L8 has not been identified there with such a height.
depends_on: root-stack charts; Bhargava–Poonen Theorem 5; ESZB Definition 2.11
notes: Exact Euler-characteristic comparison and missing global height inputs; no height bound claimed.

statement: the exact Kummer twist selected at every exponent. Let $s$ be a full continuous section of $E_U\to G_\Q$, and choose $a,b\in\Q^\times$ representing $A_s,B_s$ modulo $n$. Then $s$ lifts to the finite étale cover \[ V_{a,b,n}:\quad aX^n+bY^n=1,\quad XY\ne0, \qquad t=aX^n. \] Its class as a $\mu_n^2$-twist of the specified Kummer cover depends only on the two classes of $a,b$. The word unique here refers to this torsor-twist class, with its map to $U$, rather than to a unique unmarked isomorphism class of projective curves.
notes: The marked torsor twist is identified, with its finite etale map.

statement: the rational-map action at the birational level. The monoid of nonconstant rational functions $f\in\Q(t)$ acts, by pushforward, on continuous birational section classes of $G_{\Q(t)}\to G_\Q$. The action comes from the field embeddings $\Q(z)\hookrightarrow\Q(t)$, $z\mapsto f(t)$, and induces the correspondences of A.8 on model sections. It induces a morphism $U\to U$ exactly for the six nonconstant maps of A.7.
notes: An actual action on birational section classes and its model comparisons.

statement: the framed fibre over a congruence section. Let $q:E_U\to E_U/K$ be a continuous quotient with closed normal $K\subseteq\Pi$, and let $s_0$ be a fixed continuous section. The set of continuous sections $s$ satisfying $qs=qs_0$, modulo conjugation by $K$, is canonically the pointed nonabelian cohomology set $H^1_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,K)$ for the action $g\cdot k=s_0(g)ks_0(g)^{-1}$. In particular this describes the framed fibre for the kernel of geometric Legendre monodromy.
notes: Exact framed fibre, with the additional centralizer ambiguity after forgetting the frame.

statement: a finite-support ghost is a rational point. On $\mathcal G$, finite prime support of either coordinate forces $(A,B)=(\kappa(r),\kappa(1-r))$ for a unique $r\in\Q\setminus\{0,1\}$. Its ordinary finite local points are all equal to $r$.
notes: Finite support of one coordinate suffices for a genuine ordinary-local pair.

statement: why the finite-unit argument over $\Q$ needs modification over a number field. Let $K=\Q(\sqrt2)$, $\epsilon=1+\sqrt2$, and $e_3\in\widehat{\Z}=\prod_\ell\Z_\ell$ have $3$-component $1$ and all other components $0$. The element $A=\epsilon^{e_3}\in\widehat{K^\times}$ is represented by an ordinary unit of $K_v$ at every finite place $v$, but is not in the image of $K^\times$. All its finite valuations are zero.
notes: A completed unit with honest local units; not asserted to be a ghost pair or section.

statement: A full integral Tate comparison fixes the multiplier. Let $F$ be a finite extension of $\Q_p$, and let $E_1,E_2/F$ have potentially multiplicative reduction. Suppose an isomorphism \[ g:\prod_\ell T_\ell(E_1) \longrightarrow\prod_\ell T_\ell(E_2) \] of continuous $\widehat\Z[G_F]$-modules is given. Its Weil multiplier is a square in $\widehat\Z^\times$. Consequently, for a section in A.14, the multiplier obstruction A.17 vanishes whenever a potentially multiplicative place of its realized Legendre curve is an ordinary point place of the section.
depends_on: A.16; A.17; integral Tate extension comparison
notes: An ordinary potentially multiplicative local restriction fixes the multiplier square class.

statement: The exact remaining local locus. A rational Legendre curve with no potentially multiplicative odd prime has parameter $\lambda\in\{-1,\tfrac12,2\}$ and $j=1728$. For every other realization in A.16, a multiplier class not yet settled by A.34 can occur only when the section is locally cuspidal at every potentially multiplicative prime of the realized curve.
notes: Exact remaining locus, retaining the CM and all-cuspidal bad-place cases.

statement: An invariant line over $\Q(i)$ recognizes a section. Let $s$ be a Selmer section of $U/\Q$. If $\bar\rho_{s,5}|_{G_{\Q(i)}}$ has an invariant line, then $s$ is a rational point or cuspidal section. In particular, every noncuspidal section in A.14 whose realization has $j=1728$ is a rational point section. Thus that case of A.35 is completely recognized.
depends_on: A.13; rank-zero X0(20) over Q(i); R2
notes: Mod-five invariant-line recognition; includes every j=1728 realization.

statement: One cusp label and one bad place are recognized. A noncuspidal Selmer section in A.14 whose locally cuspidal centres have at most one of the three labels is a rational point section. Every locally cuspidal place is a potentially multiplicative place of the realized elliptic curve. In particular, every such section whose realization has at most one potentially multiplicative prime is a rational point section.
notes: Local cusps lie at potentially multiplicative primes; one label gives recognition.

statement: Every ordinary local unit-equation pair lifts to the full profinite class-two quotient. Let $\Pi=\pi_1(U_{\bar\Q})$ and let $\Gamma_3\Pi=\overline{[\Pi,\overline{[\Pi,\Pi]}]}$ be its third closed lower-central subgroup. Put $E_2=E_U/\Gamma_3\Pi$ and $E_{\rm ab}=E_U/\overline{[\Pi,\Pi]}$. For every $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$, the continuous abelian section of $E_{\rm ab}\to G_\Q$ given by its Kummer classes has a continuous lift through \[ E_2\twoheadrightarrow E_{\rm ab}. \tag{A.38.1} \] This is the full profinite class-two quotient, with its actual arithmetic action and all coefficient primes, including two.
depends_on: A.27; Ihara action; free profinite class-two collecting formula
notes: Full profinite class two, including coefficient 2; no full or class-three lift claimed.

statement: The realizations $\lambda_0=6$ and $7$ are recognized. Every noncuspidal Selmer section in A.14 whose labeled integral Legendre realization in A.16 has parameter $\lambda_0=6$ or $7$ is a rational point section. Together with A.36--A.37, this recognizes every such realization with integral parameter $2\leq\lambda_0\leq9$.
depends_on: A.16; A.37; exact cubic quotient of GL2(F3)
notes: Recognizes labeled integral realizations 6 and 7, completing integer parameters 2 through 9.

statement: The twenty-four central twists and the exact local matching map. Use the actual class-two quotient $E_2=H(\widehat\Z)\rtimes G_\Q$ and its coordinates from A.38. There are isomorphisms \[ H^1_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,\Z_\ell(2))\simeq \begin{cases} \Z/8,&\ell=2,\\ \Z/3,&\ell=3,\\ 0,&\ell\ge5, \end{cases} \qquad H^1_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,\widehat\Z(2))\simeq\Z/24. \tag{A.40.1} \] In the chosen Tate coordinates a generator of the last group is the continuous cocycle \[ \eta(g)=\frac{\chi(g)^2-1}{24}. \tag{A.40.2} \] For $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$, the geometric conjugacy classes of sections of $E_2\to G_\Q$ above its fixed abelian section class form a torsor under this group. Thus this fiber contains exactly twenty-four classes. The localization homomorphism on these central twists is \[ \operatorname{loc}:\Z/24\longrightarrow \prod_{q<\infty}H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\Q_q},\widehat\Z(2)), \qquad k\longmapsto(\operatorname{res}_q(k\eta))_q. \tag{A.40.3} \] It is injective. Its composite with the two coordinate projections at $(q,\ell)=(2,3),(3,2)$ is the isomorphism \[ \begin{split} \Z/24&\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \Z_3/3\Z_3\oplus\Z_2/8\Z_2,\\ k&\longmapsto(k/8\bmod3,\ k/3\bmod8). \end{split} \tag{A.40.4} \] For each ordinary local coordinate $x_q$ of $(A,B)$, the actual local point section determines a local comparison class $\delta_q$ relative to any chosen global class-two lift, as constructed in the proof. The subset of global lift classes agreeing with all these local point-section classes is exactly \[ \bigl\{s+k\eta:\ k\in\Z/24, \ (\delta_q)_q=\operatorname{loc}(k)\bigr\}. \tag{A.40.5} \] Consequently this subset has at most one element. For every $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$, there is a unique global class-two lift whose two central comparison coordinates in (A.40.4) agree with the local points at $2$ and $3$. Formula (A.40.5) is the exact test for that distinguished lift to agree with the point sections at all finite places.
notes: Exactly 24 global class-two lifts; explicit local matching test and at most one locally geometric lift.

statement: An odd prime-power neighbour is recognized. Let $\lambda_0>1$ be an integer. Suppose that the odd integer among $\lambda_0,\lambda_0-1$ is a power of one odd prime, and that the $2$-adic valuation of the even integer is odd. Every noncuspidal Selmer section in A.14 with labeled integral realization $E_{\lambda_0}$ is a rational point section. In particular, this recognizes the parameters $10,11,14,18,19,23, 24,25,26,27,30,31$ as well as further parameters covered by the stated arithmetic test.
depends_on: A.16; A.37; saturated T2 line; local logarithm
notes: Recognition family with odd neighbour an odd prime power and odd 2-adic valuation of the even neighbour.

statement: The rational unit-equation graph is closed and discrete. Give $\widehat{\Q^\times}$ the inverse-limit topology of A.10, and put \[ \mathcal R= \{(\kappa(t),\kappa(1-t)):t\in\Q\setminus\{0,1\}\} \subset\widehat{\Q^\times}^{\,2}. \] This subset is closed and discrete. Every Cauchy net in $\mathcal R$ is eventually constant. For a pair $(A,B)\notin\mathcal R$, there is a positive integer $N$ such that no rational $t\ne0,1$ has both $[t]_N=A_N$ and $[1-t]_N=B_N$ in $\Q^\times/(\Q^\times)^N$.

statement: The weight-three test on the twenty-four integral lifts. Put $E_3=E_U/\Gamma_4\Pi$, where $\Gamma_4\Pi=\overline{[\Pi,\Gamma_3\Pi]}$. With the generators and tangent of A.38, set \[ C=[x,y],\qquad D=[C,x],\qquad F=[C,y]. \] The kernel of $E_3\to E_2$ is $\widehat\Z(3)D\oplus\widehat\Z(3)F$. For a class-two section $s(g)=(a(g),b(g),h(g);g)$ as in A.38, write $\mathbf o_3(s)=(o_D(s),o_F(s))$ for its actual lifting obstruction in $H^2_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,\widehat\Z(3))^2$. Set $\varepsilon=(\chi-1)/2$ and $\eta=(\chi^2-1)/24$. Its components are represented by the continuous two-cocycles \[ \begin{split} W_D&=-(a+\varepsilon)\cup h-\binom a2\cup b,\\ W_F&=(b+\varepsilon)\cup(ab-h)+\binom b2\cup a-\eta\cup b. \end{split} \tag{A.43.1} \] Here $ab$ and $\binom a2$ are pointwise one-cochains with coefficient weight two. In particular all the expressions are integral, including at two. The twenty-four classes in A.40 have the exact obstruction values \[ \mathbf o_3(s+k\eta)=\mathbf o_3(s) -k\bigl((A+\kappa(-1))\cup[\eta], (B+\kappa(-1))\cup[\eta]\bigr), \qquad k\in\Z/24. \tag{A.43.2} \] Let $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$, with ordinary coordinates $x_q$, and let $\delta_q$ be its comparison class from (A.40.16). For $q\ne\ell$ denote the Frobenius coordinate of its $\ell$-part by \[ d_{q,\ell}\in\Z_\ell/(q^2-1)\Z_\ell =H^1(G_{\Q_q},\Z_\ell(2)). \] Under the standard tame-residue isomorphism \[ \rho_{q,\ell}:H^2(G_{\Q_q},\Z_\ell(3)) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Z_\ell/(q^2-1)\Z_\ell, \tag{A.43.3} \] the two localized weight-three obstructions are exactly \[ \rho_{q,\ell}\bigl(\mathbf o_3(s)|_{G_{\Q_q}}\bigr) =\bigl(-v_q(x_q)d_{q,\ell}, -v_q(1-x_q)d_{q,\ell}\bigr). \tag{A.43.4} \] Thus their common zero locus at this place is the annihilator of the two indicated valuation integers in the displayed finite cyclic module. Write $\mathscr L_i(A,B)$ for the geometric conjugacy classes of $E_i$-sections with abelian image $(A,B)$, and $s_*$ for the distinguished class of A.40. On the ordinary locus with \[ (v_2(x_2),v_2(1-x_2))=(0,1),\qquad (v_3(x_3),v_3(1-x_3))=(1,0), \tag{A.43.5} \] the actual projection of section sets satisfies \[ \operatorname{im}\bigl(\mathscr L_3(A,B)\longrightarrow \mathscr L_2(A,B)\bigr)\subseteq\{s_*\}. \tag{A.43.6} \] For the rational pair $(A,B)=(\kappa(3),\kappa(-2))$, this image is exactly the class-two point-section class at $3$.

statement: Infinitely supported ordinary-local solutions of the completed unit equation. There are recursively specified pairwise distinct primes $q_j,r_j>3$, for $j\ge0$, such that, with $n_j=(j+4)!$, the completed products \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{n_j}, \qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}r_j^{n_j} \quad\text{in }\widehat{\Q^\times} \tag{A.44.1} \] have the following properties. At every finite prime $p$ their localizations are the Kummer classes of ordinary nonzero numbers $x_p,y_p\in\Z_p$ with $x_p+y_p=1$. Thus $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$. Their valuation vectors are \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} p&v_p(A)&v_p(B)\\\hline 3&1&0\\ 2&0&1\\ q_j&n_j&0\\ r_j&0&n_j\\ \text{all other primes}&0&0. \end{array} \tag{A.44.2} \] Both coordinates have infinite support, so neither is the Kummer class of a rational number. The construction uses no local section theorem.

Let $4\mid m$, let $d_1,\ldots,d_s$ be positive rational numbers, and suppose there are distinct primes $P_i$ with $v_{P_i}(d_i)\in\{1,-1\}$ and $v_{P_i}(d_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$. statement: No fixed finite puncture set forces rationality. For every finite set $S\subset\Q$ with at least two elements there is a tuple \[ (x_v)_v\in \prod_v\bigl(\Q_v\setminus S\bigr) \] and classes $U_c\in\widehat{\Q^\times}$, one for each $c\in S$, such that \[ (U_c)_p=\kappa(x_p-c) \quad\text{at every finite prime }p, \tag{A.48.1} \] with the corresponding equality of completed Kummer classes at the real place. Every $U_c$ has infinitely many nonzero ordinary integer valuation coordinates. The tuple is not one rational number. In particular, there is no finite $S\supset\{0,1\}$ for which the finite form of (G) in A12 has only rational solutions, even when every finite local coordinate is ordinary and differs from every puncture.

statement: Every ordinary finite-puncture ghost lifts to full profinite class two. Let $S=\{c_1,\ldots,c_r\}\subset\Q$ have distinct elements, with $r\ge2$, and put \[ V_S=\mathbb A^1_\Q\setminus S,\qquad E_S=\pi_1(V_S),\qquad \Pi_S=\pi_1(V_{S,\bar\Q}). \] Let $U_i\in\widehat{\Q^\times}$ and, for every finite prime $p$, let $x_p\in\Q_p\setminus S$ satisfy \[ (U_i)_p=\kappa_p(x_p-c_i)\quad(1\le i\le r). \tag{A.50.1} \] There is a continuous section of \[ E_S/\Gamma_3\Pi_S\longrightarrow G_\Q \tag{A.50.2} \] whose pullbacks of the unit classes $\kappa(t-c_i)$ are the specified $U_i$. This is the actual full profinite class-two quotient, with all coefficient primes retained. No local section theorem is used. For the classes of A.48, none of these sections is the image of a rational point section or of a cuspidal section. Thus ordinary infinite-support abelian data survive to this quotient for every fixed finite rational puncture set. statement: Infinite-support ghosts survive every fixed finite geometric quotient with full abelianization. Let $N$ be a closed normal subgroup of $E_U$ contained in $\Pi$, and suppose $Q=\Pi/N$ is finite. Write \[ E_Q=E_U/N,\quad E_{Q^{\rm ab}}=E_Q/[Q,Q],\quad E_1=E_U/\Gamma_2\Pi. \] The natural map is an isomorphism of profinite extensions of $G_\Q$, \[ E_U/(N\cap\Gamma_2\Pi) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } E_Q\mathop{\times}_{E_{Q^{\rm ab}}}E_1. \tag{A.51.1} \] For every such $Q$, the extension on the left has a continuous section whose full abelian Kummer coordinates form an ordinary infinite-support ghost of the form A.44. Its image in $E_Q$ is the image of the rational point section at $3$. For perfect $Q$, every ordinary ghost admits a section of this extension with that prescribed $E_Q$ image. These sections are excluded from the rational-point and cuspidal images by their full abelian coordinates. Thus no single finite geometric quotient, adjoined to the full abelianization in the exact sense (A.51.1), eliminates all ordinary infinite-support ghosts. This includes any fixed finite modular quotient with geometric group $A_4,(\Z/2)^2,A_5$ or $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_7)$. The assertion prescribes a global quotient section; matching its finite-quotient localizations to the points $x_p$ is an additional requirement.

statement: Exact level-three, four, five and seven maps. Put $k=\bar\Q$. The projective geometric quotients of the Legendre monodromy at levels $N=3,4,5,7$, and the smooth compactifications of their connected covers of $U_k$, are as follows: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} N&\text{linear image}&\text{projective image }Q_N &\text{compactification}&\text{genus}\\ \hline 3&\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf F_3)&A_4&X(6)_k&1\\ 4& (\Z/2)^2&(\Z/2)^2&X(4)_k&0\\ 5&\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf F_5)&A_5&X(10)_k&13\\ 7&\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf F_7)& \operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_7)&X(14)_k&49. \end{array} \tag{A.53.1} \] Here $X(N)$ has its usual symplectic modular meaning over a field containing the relevant roots of unity. The geometric assertions in the table do not assert that every arithmetic twist has a rational point or is isomorphic over $\Q$ to that chosen modular model. The group $S_4\simeq\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z/4)/\{\pm I\}$ belongs to $X(4)\to X(1)$ over the $j$-line. The component obtained after pullback along $X(2)\to X(1)$ has group \[ \ker\bigl(S_4\longrightarrow S_3\bigr)=(\Z/2)^2. \tag{A.53.2} \] At odd $N$ in the table the connected pullback is $X(2N)$. In particular, the genus-zero curves $X(3),X(5)$ and the genus-three curve $X(7)$ in L10 are the curves before this pullback. For each $N$ let \[ N_N=\ker\bigl(\Pi\xrightarrow{\rho_{\rm Leg,N}} \operatorname{GL}_2(\Z/N)\longrightarrow \operatorname{PGL}_2(\Z/N)\bigr). \tag{A.53.3} \] This is a closed normal subgroup of $E_U$, and the section in the question has the actual quotient section \[ G_\Q\xrightarrow{s}E_U\longrightarrow E_U/N_N, \qquad \Pi/N_N=Q_N. \tag{A.53.4} \] Thus A.51 applies with precisely the four groups in (A.53.1). For $N=5,7$ these groups are perfect. For $N=4$ the quotient already factors through the full geometric abelianization; adjoining it to that abelianization adds no further quotient information.

statement: A general recognition criterion with one coordinate supported at two. Let $m\ge5$ be odd, and let \[ \lambda_0=2^m\quad\hbox{or}\quad\lambda_0=1+2^m. \] Write $M=2^m-1$ in the first case and $M=2^m+1$ in the second. Let $s$ be a noncuspidal Selmer section whose full integral Legendre representation is conjugate to that of the point $\lambda_0$ by an element of the geometric closure $H$ in A.17. Every prime $p\mid M$ at which $s_p$ is cuspidal satisfies \[ p\nmid(m-4),\qquad \left(\frac{4-m}{p}\right)=1. \tag{A.54.1} \] Consequently, when no prime divisor of $M$ satisfies (A.54.1), $s$ is precisely the point section $s_{\lambda_0}$. In particular, the conclusion holds for $\lambda_0=33$: $M=33=3\cdot11$ and $4-m=-1$ is a nonsquare modulo both prime divisors. This example settles its exact A7 recognition question. The proof uses the determinant-one hypothesis on the conjugator; it does not assert this conclusion for every unrestricted integral $\operatorname{GL}_2$-intertwiner.

statement: The dual obstruction to correction using completely split auxiliary primes. Let $N\ge2$, let $M_N=\Z/N(2)$, and identify its Cartier dual by the evaluation pairing \[ M_N^D=\operatorname{Hom}(M_N,\mu_N)=\Z/N(-1),\qquad M_N\otimes M_N^D\longrightarrow\mu_N. \tag{A.55.1} \] Let $K/\Q$ be finite Galois containing $\mu_N$, let $S$ contain the infinite place, the primes dividing $N$, and the primes ramified in $K$, and let $T$ be the set of finite primes outside $S$ which split completely in $K$. Write $H^1_{S\cup T}(\Q,M_N)$ for the union of $H^1(G_{\Q,S\cup T_0},M_N)$ over finite $T_0\subset T$. Then \[ \begin{aligned} &\operatorname{im}\left(H^1_{S\cup T}(\Q,M_N) \longrightarrow\prod_{v\in S}H^1(\Q_v,M_N)\right) \\ &\qquad=\left(\operatorname{res}_S H^1(\operatorname{Gal}(K/\Q),M_N^D)\right)^\perp. \end{aligned} \tag{A.55.2} \] Here the annihilator is taken under the actual pairing \[ ((z_v),\xi)\longmapsto \sum_{v\in S}\operatorname{inv}_v (z_v\cup\operatorname{res}_v\xi) \quad\hbox{in }\Q/\Z. \tag{A.55.3} \] There is a concrete order-sixteen character in this dual group. Suppose $N=2^r$ with $r\ge4$, take $c=2v^{24}\in\Q^\times$, and use compatible Kummer coordinates $b=\kappa_N(c)\in Z^1(G_\Q,\Z/N(1))$. For $g\in G_\Q$ write \[ \chi(g)\bmod16=(-1)^{e(g)}5^{L(g)},\quad L(g)\in\Z/4, \qquad \beta(g)=\frac{\chi(g)^2-1}{8}\bmod2. \tag{A.55.4} \] The function $\binom{L}{2}\bmod2$ is well defined on $\Z/4$. Then \[ \zeta_N(g)=\frac N{16}b(g)+\frac N2\binom{L(g)}2 \quad\hbox{in }\Z/N(-1) \tag{A.55.5} \] is a continuous one-cocycle. Its cohomology class has exact order $16$ and factors through \[ K_c=\Q(\mu_N,c^{1/N}). \tag{A.55.6} \] Moreover, \[ 2\zeta_N=\frac N8\kappa_N(c),\qquad 8\zeta_N=\frac N2\beta \quad\hbox{as actual cocycles}. \tag{A.55.7} \] The first expression on the right is viewed in weight $-1$ by the equivariant coefficient map $\Z/N(1)\to\Z/N(-1)$, $u\mapsto(N/8)u$. For an explicit failed correction problem, take \[ c=2\cdot73^{24},\qquad S=\{2,73,\infty\}, \qquad K=K_c. \tag{A.55.8} \] At $73$ let $z_{73}$ be the unramified class in $H^1(\Q_{73},M_N)$ with arithmetic Frobenius value $1$, and prescribe $z_2=z_\infty=0$. This tuple is not in the image in (A.55.2), for every $r\ge4$. There is also an exact constraint on retaining the integral class-two section. For every prime $\ell$ and $a\ge1$, the coefficient connecting map gives the exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow \frac{H^1_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,\Z_\ell(2))}{\ell^a} \longrightarrow H^1(G_\Q,\Z/\ell^a(2)) \xrightarrow{\ \partial\ } H^2_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,\Z_\ell(2))[\ell^a] \longrightarrow0. \tag{A.55.9} \] A finite central correction $z$ of a fixed integral class-two lift is the reduction of an integral central correction exactly when $\partial z=0$. This is equivalent to $z$ being unramified outside $\ell$, with the additional condition $\operatorname{res}_\infty z=0$ when $\ell=2$. Thus the allowable integral corrections are precisely the reductions of the groups computed in A.40. Once its two cross-prime normalizations are imposed, none of their nonzero classes survives at modulus divisible by $24$.

statement: Exact abelian image of the full congruence kernel. Let $H$ be the full geometric Legendre image in A.17, and put \[ C=\ker(\Pi\longrightarrow H),\qquad T=\Pi^{\rm ab}=\widehat\Z(1)^2. \] All derived subgroups in this statement are closed derived subgroups. There is an isomorphism of finite $G_\Q$-modules \[ H^{\rm ab}\simeq (\Z/8(1))^2\oplus\Z/3(1), \tag{A.56.1} \] under which the map induced by the two Kummer coordinates is \[ T\longrightarrow H^{\rm ab},\qquad (a,b)\longmapsto(a\bmod8, b\bmod8, a+b\bmod3). \tag{A.56.2} \] In particular, the image of $C$ in $T$ is exactly the open subgroup \[ K=\{(a,b):a\equiv b\equiv0\pmod8,\quad a+b\equiv0\pmod3\}. \tag{A.56.3} \] Set $E_H=E_U/C$, $E_{H^{\rm ab}}=E_H/[H,H]$, and $E_1=E_U/\Gamma_2\Pi$. The natural map is an isomorphism of profinite extensions, \[ E_U/(C\cap\Gamma_2\Pi) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } E_H\mathop{\times}_{E_{H^{\rm ab}}}E_1. \tag{A.56.4} \] Fix a rational point $b_0\in U(\Q)$. The ordinary infinite-support ghosts of A.44 satisfy (A.56.5) for $b_0=3$. statement: Joint fibre characters and their two-primary bound. Let $4\mid n$, let $D_1,\ldots,D_k\in\Q^\times$, and let \[ \mathcal E=\Q[Z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,Z_k^{\pm1}] /(Z_i^n-D_i:1\le i\le k). \tag{A.57.1} \] This is a finite etale algebra. The finite-order abelian characters of $G_\Q$ that vanish on the absolute Galois group of every field factor of $\mathcal E$ have the following exact finite description. Write \[ D_i=(-1)^{\delta_i}\prod_{P\in\mathcal P}P^{w_{iP}}, \quad \delta_i\in\{0,1\},\qquad F=\Q(\mu_{2n},\sqrt P:P\in\mathcal P),\qquad \Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(F/\Q). \tag{A.57.2} \] For $\sigma\in\Gamma$ define $u_\sigma\in(\Z/2n)^\times$ and $\epsilon_P(\sigma)\in\Z/2$ by \[ \sigma(\zeta_{2n})=\zeta_{2n}^{u_\sigma}, \qquad \sigma(\sqrt P)=(-1)^{\epsilon_P(\sigma)}\sqrt P. \] Let $\mathcal A\subset\Gamma$ consist of the $\sigma$ for which there are $k_P\in\Z/n$ and $e_i\in\Z/n$ satisfying \[ \begin{split} k_P&\equiv\epsilon_P(\sigma)\pmod2,\\ (u_\sigma-1)(\delta_i+2e_i) +2\sum_Pw_{iP}k_P&\equiv0\pmod {2n} \quad(1\le i\le k). \end{split} \tag{A.57.3} \] Put $H=\langle\mathcal A\rangle\subset\Gamma$. Then the required character group is exactly \[ \operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma/H,\Q/\Z). \tag{A.57.4} \] Equivalently, the largest abelian field contained in every field factor of (A.57.1) is $B=F^H$. Writing $n=2^r v$ with $v$ odd, one has the sharper bound \[ B\subset \Q(\sqrt P:P\in\mathcal P)\,\Q(\mu_{2^{r+1}}). \tag{A.57.5} \] In particular every character in (A.57.4) has order a power of two. Formula (A.57.3), or the equivalent divisibility test below, determines the remaining cyclotomic and quadratic relations; complete splitting in the whole radical splitting field imposes more conditions than (A.57.4).

statement: An integral valuation locus in the image of the full class-three section map. statement: Ordinary infinite-support pairs with any fixed product of tame denominators. Fix integers $d\ge2$ and $C>0$ with $24\mid C$. statement: Ordinary ghosts retaining a prescribed finite quotient locally. Let $N\triangleleft\Pi$ be an open subgroup normal in $E_U$, put $Q=\Pi/N$, and fix the point-$3$ section $s_0$. Write $A=\Pi^{\rm ab}$ and \[ E_{Q,A}=E_U/(N\cap[\Pi,\Pi]),\qquad E_Q=E_U/N,\qquad E_A=E_U/[\Pi,\Pi]. \tag{A.72.1} \] There is an actual continuous section $\tau:G_\Q\to E_{Q,A}$ with ordinary infinite-support Kummer coordinates $(A_\tau,B_\tau)$ such that its projection to $E_Q$ is $s_0$ and, at every finite prime $p$, its restriction is geometrically conjugate to the image of a point $x_p\in U(\Q_p)$. Let \(\rho_r:C_r\to C_1\) be multiplication by \(3^{r-1}\), and let \(\iota_r:\mu_3\hookrightarrow\mu_{3^r}\) be inclusion. Every equivariant bilinear form is alternating, and the map \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Hom}_{G_\Q}(\textstyle\bigwedge^2 C_1,\mu_3) &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{Hom}_{G_\Q}(C_r\otimes_{R_r}C_r,\mu_{3^r}),\\ B&\longmapsto\iota_r\circ B\circ(\rho_r,\rho_r) \end{split} \tag{A.129.2} \] is an isomorphism of abelian groups. In particular the group on the right is \((\Z/3\Z)^n\), and every form has values in the literal order-three subgroup of \(\mu_{3^r}\). Here is the integral operator calculation giving the map. Put \[ \mathcal O_n=\Z_3[x]/(\Phi_N(x)),\qquad \Phi_N(x)=1+x^d+x^{2d},\qquad \sigma_u(x)=x^u. \tag{A.129.3} \] Let \(\omega(u)\in\{1,-1\}\) lift \(u\bmod3\), and let \(\chi_r(u)=u\bmod3^r\). Under the perfect underlying block pairing of A.115, the group of forms in (A.129.2) is exactly \[ \begin{split} \{P\in\mathcal O_n/3^r:\ \sigma_u(P)=\omega(u)\chi_r(u)P\text{ for all }u\in U_m\} &=\ker(\sigma_2+2:\mathcal O_n/3^r\to\mathcal O_n/3^r)\\ &=3^{r-1}\ker(\sigma_2-1:\mathcal O_n/3\to\mathcal O_n/3). \end{split} \tag{A.129.4} \] The last notation means the image of the kernel under \(\mathcal O_n/3\to\mathcal O_n/3^r\), \(P\mapsto3^{r-1}\widetilde P\). It is independent of the chosen lift. The coefficient transitions retain their literal maps. For \(r\ge2\), reducing the value of any such form by \(\mu_{3^r}\xrightarrow{z\mapsto z^3}\mu_{3^{r-1}}\) gives zero. Restricting its two arguments to the subgroup \(C_{r-1}\hookrightarrow C_r\) also gives zero. For an actual continuous class \(\gamma\in H^1(\Q_v,C_r)\), the associated quadratic class is \[ \tfrac12\bigl(\iota_r B(\rho_r,\rho_r)\bigr)_* (\gamma\cup\gamma) =(\iota_r)_*\!\left( \tfrac12 B_*((\rho_r)_*\gamma\cup(\rho_r)_*\gamma)\right). \tag{A.129.5} \] Consequently these higher-precision bilinear reciprocity tests are exactly the mod-three tests under the displayed maps. Write \(b_{p,N}\) for its image in \(\Q_p^\times/(\Q_p^\times)^N\), and use the analogous real image of \(\epsilon\). The following actual diagonal maps are injective: \[ \begin{aligned} \lambda_N:\Q^\times/(\Q^\times)^N &\longrightarrow\prod_{p<\infty} \Q_p^\times/(\Q_p^\times)^N,\\ \widehat\lambda:\widehat{\Q^\times} &\longrightarrow\prod_{p<\infty}\widehat{\Q_p^\times}. \end{aligned} \tag{A.132.1} \] There is an exact equality of images \[ \begin{aligned} &\operatorname{im}\bigl(\widehat{\Q^\times} \longrightarrow\{\pm1\}\times \prod_{p<\infty}\widehat{\Q_p^\times}\bigr)\\ &\quad=\bigl\{(\epsilon,(b_p)):\ \forall N\ge1\ \exists a_N\in\Q^\times,\\ &\hspace{30mm}[a_N]_p=b_{p,N}\ (p<\infty),\quad [a_N]_\infty=[\epsilon]_\infty\bigr\}. \end{aligned} \tag{A.132.2} \] On the right, the \emph{same fixed} \(b_p\) is used at every exponent and every place. Every finite class \([a_N]\) is unique, and their reductions are automatically compatible. Thus there is no further inverse-limit obstruction after the all-place finite matching in (A.132.2). If no real sign is prescribed, project the equality to the finite places; all-place finite matching then determines the one possible global sign. There is also the exact character description of the same image. At every \(N\) the local tuple must lie in the restricted product \[ {\mathbb P}^1_N= \prod_v' H^1(\Q_v,\mu_N) \quad\text{with respect to }H^1_{\rm nr}(\Q_p,\mu_N) \text{ at }p\nmid N, \tag{A.132.3} \] and it must satisfy \[ \sum_v\operatorname{inv}_v(b_{v,N}\cup\chi_v)=0 \quad\text{for every }\chi\in H^1(\Q,\Z/N). \tag{A.132.4} \] The real component in this formula is the chosen sign. These two conditions, for all \(N\), are equivalent to (A.132.2), not only necessary conditions. For ordinary \(b_p\in\Q_p^\times\), put \(e_p=v_p(b_p)\in\Z\). statement: The precise local and adelic consequences of a birational lift. Let $k$ be a number field and $X/k$ a hyperbolic curve with smooth completion $\overline X$. A section in $\Sec^{\mathrm{bir}}(X/k)$ is locally a point or cusp section. At finite places this supplies centers $x_v\in\overline X(k_v)$; at real places the section specifies a connected component. Such a section is either globally cuspidal or is integral on $X$ at a set of finite places of Dirichlet density one. A birationally adelic section means one admitting a single birational lift whose image on every nonempty open $V\subseteq X$ is adelic on $V$ or cuspidal. Here adelic requires ordinary local sections everywhere and integrality at all but finitely many finite places. Over a totally real or imaginary quadratic number field, every noncuspidal birationally adelic section is a rational point section. In particular, every adelic section of the tripod over $\Q$ is a rational point section.
