statement: The covering-germ criterion with its exact quantifiers. For a continuous homomorphism $i:H\to G$ of profinite groups the following are equivalent: $i$ is injective; every finite transitive continuous $H$-set is an orbit in the restriction of a finite continuous $G$-set; every such $H$-set is a quotient of such an orbit.
depends_on: finite etale lifting at a henselian valuation
notes: Covering-germ criterion with one chosen prolongation and quantified finite covers.

statement: Distinct rational-residue valuations need not have distinct nonzero inertia images. Let $C/\Q$ be the smooth projective curve $y^2=x^5-x$, and put \[ V=(\Pj^1_\Q\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})\times C. \] This is a strict hyperbolic polycurve. There are distinct rank-two valuation rings of $\Q(V)$ with residue field $\Q$ whose inertia images in $\pi_1(V_{\bar\Q})$ are the same nontrivial subgroup, after compatible choices of paths. Intrinsically their conjugacy classes of subgroups are equal.
depends_on: explicit product hyperbolic polycurve and rank-two flags
notes: Distinct rational-residue valuations have the same nonzero inertia image in an elementary polycurve.

statement: The unrestricted converse to the center criterion. There is a smooth geometrically connected surface $W/\Q$ and a rank-two valuation $v$ of $\Q(W)$ with residue field $\Q$, with no center on $W$, whose full inertia image in $\pi_1(W)$ is trivial.
notes: Unrestricted centre converse is refuted; elementary-polycurve margin retained.

statement: Explicit blowup and minimal-surface inertia maps. For the strict polycurve $V$ of B.10, a blowup of the standard compactification $X=\Pj^1\times C$ at $(0,c_1)$ has a boundary crossing with local-to-global map \[ \widehat\Z(1)^2\longrightarrow I_0\times1, (r,s)\longmapsto r+s. \tag{B.12.1} \] The standard compactification itself has injective boundary inertia and has no exceptional curve of the first kind. For arbitrary smooth opens, even this last surface minimality condition does not ensure injectivity: on $\Pj^2$ with boundary $xy=0$ the map at $[0:0:1]$ is \[ \widehat\Z(1)^2\longrightarrow\widehat\Z(1), (r,s)\longmapsto r-s. \tag{B.12.2} \]
notes: Minimal-surface and blowup examples have their exact scopes; no hyperbolic-polycurve injectivity claim added.

statement: The actual comparison from a birational section to Kummer local data. A continuous birational section $\tau:G_\Q\to G_{\Q(t)}$ gives classes $u_c\in\widehat{\Q^\times}$ for every $c\in\Q$ and compatible local centers $x_v\in\Pj^1(\Q_v)$, with a choice of real representative, such that \[ u_c|_v=\kappa_v(x_v-c) \quad\text{whenever }x_v\ne c,\infty. \tag{B.13.1} \] This is a well-defined comparison on geometric conjugacy classes, apart from the stated choice of real representative. For $r\in\Pj^1(\Q)$, its inverse image over the tuple with all finite centers equal to $r$ consists exactly of the birational lifts whose model section on $U$ is $s_r$ when $r\in U(\Q)$, or lies in the cusp packet at $r$ when $r\in\{0,1,\infty\}$. At the real place only the corresponding component is intrinsic.
notes: Birational section to literal G-data comparison; the real infinity counterexample is outside this image.

statement: A full lift over a genuinely bad marked base cusp. For $F=M_{0,5}=(U\times U)\setminus\Delta\to U_t$, there is a section whose projected section is cuspidal at $t=0$, whose marked generic fibre there has no potentially good marked reduction, and which has a full birational lift. The lift has a compatible invariant valuation above every one-variable subfield of $\Q(t,z)$.
depends_on: Puiseux splitting of a rank-two valuation
notes: An actual M0,5 bad-marked example and compatible one-variable restrictions.

statement: The remaining birational and valuative assertions. For an arbitrary continuous section $s$ of the tripod over $\Q$, we have not split \[ 1\longrightarrow\ker q_U\longrightarrow G_{\Q(t)}\times_{\pi_1(U),s}G_\Q \longrightarrow G_\Q\longrightarrow1. \] For an arbitrary section of $G_{\Q(t)}\to G_\Q$, we have not proved that its image lies in a rational-place decomposition group (B1, cote 149 scans 120--130). B.1 gives local centers and density-one integrality, not the missing global rational valuation. For an arbitrary section of a hyperbolic curve fibration over a hyperbolic curve with cuspidal base projection and genuinely bad marked reduction, we have not constructed a birational lift, or a single invariant valuation restricting compatibly to every one-variable subfield (B2). B.14 proves these properties only for its displayed section. B.10 refutes universal distinctness of the inertia images in scan 128. B.11 refutes the unrestricted center converse in scan 120; the added elementary-hyperbolic scope in its margin remains undecided here. B.12 refutes an unrestricted minimal-surface injectivity assertion in the stated sense, while the existence assertion for appropriately minimal strict hyperbolic compactifications remains undecided.
notes: Remaining full classification, all bad-cusp lifts and stated elementary-model cases.

statement: An infinitely ramified pair with common integral local elliptic curves. There are continuous representations \[ \rho_7:G_\Q\longrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_2(\Z_7),\qquad \rho_{11}:G_\Q\longrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_2(\Z_{11}) \tag{B.16.1} \] with determinants $\chi_7,\chi_{11}$ and surjective residual representations, and elliptic curves $E_q/\Q_q$ for every finite prime $q$, with integral Galois-module isomorphisms \[ \rho_\ell|_{G_{\Q_q}}\simeq T_\ell(E_q) \qquad(\ell=7,11). \tag{B.16.2} \] The same curve $E_q$ occurs on both sides of the coefficient choice. The two ramification sets agree away from $\{7,11\}$ and are infinite, each of density zero. At every common unramified prime $q\ne7,11$ their common Frobenius polynomial is $X^2-a_qX+q$, with $a_q\in\Z$ and $|a_q|\le2\sqrt q$. For $q\in\{2,3,7,11\}$ one can take $E_q:y^2=x(x-1)(x-3)$. At every newly introduced ramified prime one can take the literal split Tate curve with parameter $q^{M_q}$, where $M_q$ is a positive integer specified during the construction.
depends_on: B.8; Khare-Larsen-Ramakrishna Fact6,Lemmas7-9,Propositions10-11; Khare-Rajan Theorem1; Tate uniformization; Waterhouse and simultaneous integral lattice isogenies
his_places: cote149; scans48,54–58,63,66,79–85,120–130; exact item and lead scope in answers column
notes: Constructs actual7-adic and11-adic representations with one common local elliptic curve at every prime, integral local comparisons and infinitely many common ramified primes. The ramification sets agree away from7,11, whose cyclotomic exceptions are retained. Exact field disjointness, split-sign element and alternating finite-level construction are proved. No full all-coefficient family or tripod

statement: Projectivity over the full cyclotomic field. The profinite group $G_F$ is projective in the category of profinite groups and continuous homomorphisms. Every continuous surjection of a profinite group onto $G_F$ has a continuous section.
depends_on: global Brauer invariants; cyclotomic killing; Serre projectivity criterion
notes: Absolute Galois group of Q(mu_infinity) is projective; comparison via all finite subextensions.

statement: A degree-nine cover with no rational compactification point. The smooth plane cubic \[ D:\quad X^3+2Y^3+4Z^3=0 \] has $D(F)=\varnothing$. The morphism $t=-4Z^3/X^3$ to $\Pj^1_F$ restricts to a geometrically connected finite \'etale degree-nine cover $V\to U_F$. Its affine equations are \[ t=-4a^3,\qquad 1-t=-2b^3,\qquad a=Z/X,\quad b=Y/X. \]
notes: A degree-nine finite etale cover of the tripod has no compactification point over the cyclotomic field.

statement: Conjecture A for the tripod over $F$. There exists a continuous section of $\pi_1(U_F)\to G_F$ that is neither the section of an $F$-point nor cuspidal. Its mod-3 Kummer coordinates are \[ (A,B)=(2k,k),\qquad k=\kappa_3(2)\ne0\quad\hbox{in }H^1(G_F,\mu_3). \]
notes: Full continuous noncuspidal nonpoint section over Q(mu_infinity).

statement: Birational lifting over the same field. Every continuous section of $\pi_1(U_F)\to G_F$, including the section of C.3, lifts to a continuous section of $G_{F(t)}\to G_F$.
notes: Every prescribed model section over this field has a birational lift.

statement: Descent of the unique point-section conjugator. Let $F=\Q(\mu_\infty)$, let $K/F$ be finitely generated, and let $X/K$ be a hyperbolic curve. If $x,y\in X(K)$ have geometrically conjugate point sections on the cyclotomic kernel of $G_K$, then $x=y$. The conjugator is unique. No local section theorem is used.
depends_on: R15 unique centralizer; finite-type descent; Kummer separation
notes: Points over fields finitely generated over Q(mu_infinity) are separated by cyclotomic-kernel sections.

statement: A degree-$27$ Heisenberg cover. Put $\xi=\zeta_6$ and $\eta=\xi^{-1}$ in $F$. The point sections at $\xi,\eta\in U(F)$ coincide after geometric abelianization and differ after quotienting by $\Gamma_3\Pi=\overline{[\Pi,\overline{[\Pi,\Pi]}]}$. An explicit geometrically connected finite \'etale Galois cover of degree $27$, with constant group $\operatorname{UT}_3(\mathbf F_3)$, distinguishes them. Thus class two is the first separating stage of the lower-central filtration. No local theorem is used.
depends_on: explicit Fermat elliptic cover; CM Frobenius commutator
notes: The two sixth-root points agree abelianly and are separated first in class two by a degree-27 cover.

statement: A continuous B-prime action acquires a finite quotient. Every action just defined normalizes the deck group of a finite hyperbolic covering level descended over $K$. It is the action of a continuous section for that quotient. The level can be chosen to cover any specified initial level. Consequently B$'$ and B over finite extensions have the same fixed-point existence assertion, including the cyclotomic-kernel version supplied by R15.
depends_on: open function stabilizers; finite etale descent
notes: The specified topology and finite-quotient comparison for continuous B-prime actions.

statement: The local cyclotomic Kummer kernel. Let $L/\Q_p$ be finite and $H=\ker(\chi:G_L\to\widehat\Z^{\times})$. If $b\in L^\times$ satisfies $\kappa_p(b)|_H=0$ in $H^1(H,\Z_p(1))$, then $b$ is a root of unity. No local section theorem is used.
depends_on: local Kummer extensions; local cyclotomic group
notes: The kernel for ordinary local multiplicative elements consists of roots of unity.

statement: An explicit ultralimit with a continuous local restriction. There is an abstract, discontinuous section $s:G_\Q\to E_U$ whose restriction to a fixed decomposition subgroup $G_{\Q_3}$ is geometrically conjugate to the point section at \[ a=1+\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}3^{r!}\in U(\Q_3). \tag{C.9.1} \] It induces a semilinear action on the original universal pro-cover, normalizing its original geometric deck group. The stabilizer of $\sqrt t$ is nonopen.
depends_on: C.8; full section ultralimit; transcendental Q3 limit
notes: An abstract section has a specified continuous local restriction and an explicitly nonopen function stabilizer.

statement: The universal fixed-point assertion for abstract actions. The abstract action of C.9 has no completed geometric closed pro-point fixed by $G_{\Q(\mu_\infty)}$. In particular, the unique-fixed-point assertion fails for unrestricted abstract semilinear actions even when the original deck group is normalized. This statement uses no local section theorem.
depends_on: C.8; C.9; local ordinary pro-point uniqueness
notes: An abstract semilinear action has no fixed point; the continuity qualification remains explicit.

statement: The exact finite-descent localization map. Let $C/K$ be smooth, proper and geometrically connected, of genus at least two, over a number field. There is a bijection \[ \operatorname{loc}:\Sec(C/K)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } C(\mathbb A_K)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}cov}}. \tag{D.1.1} \] Here the right side uses all finite-group-scheme torsors, twists by global $H^1$, and connected components at the real places. If $K$ contains no CM subfield, its image in each individual $C(K_v)$, for $v$ finite, is finite. The construction gives no uniform bound as $v$ varies.
depends_on: local theorem; Harari–Stix; Porowski local conjugacy; Betts–Stix
notes: Exact finite-descent localization bijection; finiteness of each localization does not bound global cardinality.

statement: The strong-density criterion and the failed intersection. Put $\mathcal S=\operatorname{Sel}(C/K)$ and $r(v)=\#\operatorname{red}_v\mathcal S$ at the good finite places. For $d\geq1$, \[ \#\mathcal S\leq d \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \text{there exists a strongly positive set $\Omega$ with $r(v)\leq d$ for all $v\in\Omega$}. \tag{D.2.1} \] Strongly positive means positive upper density after pullback to every finite extension. A positive-density set can have empty intersection with a potentially-density-one set, even over $\Q$.
depends_on: strong upper density algebra; inspected attribution
notes: Repairs the density-intersection criterion and separates it from the actual Selmer corollary.

statement: Actual Jacobians with equal positive-density traces and different potential toric ranks. The genus-two curves \[ C_4:y^2=x^6+8x^4+16x^2+8, \qquad C_0:y^2=x^6+8 \tag{D.3.1} \] have Jacobians of potential toric ranks $2$ and $0$ at $5$. Their Frobenius traces agree at every good prime inert in $\Q(\sqrt2)$, a density-$1/2$ set. Hence positive-density trace equality does not force potential isogeny even for weight-one Jacobian representations distinguished by potential toric rank. There are also elliptic curves with full Frobenius-polynomial equality on a density-$1/4$ set and no potential isogeny.
depends_on: explicit genus-two maps; toric ranks; Frobenius counts
notes: Actual Jacobian countermodels for the arithmetic density inference; no infinite-section curve claimed.

statement: A Tate tower split at all closed points with no generic section. For a finite extension $k/\Q_p$ there is a smooth hyperbolic $k$-curve $B$ and a compatible tower of nontrivial connected finite \'etale cyclic covers of $B$ split at every closed point. Each nontrivial cover has no $k(B)$-point above the generic point. More precisely, there is a continuous epimorphism \[ \theta:\pi_1(B)\longrightarrow\widehat\Z \tag{D.4.1} \] which is surjective on the geometric group and trivial on every closed-point decomposition group. The tower does not construct a nonpoint section of a non-isotrivial proper hyperbolic curve.
depends_on: Tate uniformization; map to an elliptic curve
notes: Closed-fibre splitting and absence of a generic section of the specified tower.

statement: Power-separatedness for finitely generated fields. For every field $F$ finitely generated over $\Q$, \[ \bigcap_{n\ge1}(F^\times)^n=\{1\}. \tag{D.5.1} \]
depends_on: proper-model valuations and elementary bounded conjugates
notes: All finitely generated fields over Q; no section conjecture input.

statement: The arithmetic fundamental-group functor is faithful on these spectra. Two morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ inducing the same relative outer homomorphism (D.5.0) are equal. No dominance assumption is required for this assertion.
depends_on: D.5; Kummer pullback with explicit basepoint transporter
notes: Faithfulness for regular local rings, retaining nontrivial algebraic constant fields.

statement: An actual morphism has open image exactly when it is dominant. For a morphism $f:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, the image of $f_*:\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(B)$ is open if and only if the ring map $B\to A$ is injective. Consequently there is an injective map \[ \operatorname{Hom}^{\mathrm{dom}}_\Q (\operatorname{Spec}A,\operatorname{Spec}B) \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}^{\mathrm{out,open}}_{/G_\Q} (\pi_1(A),\pi_1(B)). \tag{D.7.1} \]
notes: Dominance is exactly openness for actual morphisms; gives injectivity, not fullness.

statement: The exact fullness assertion for D5. For these regular local rings, it remains to construct a dominant morphism from an arbitrary relative outer homomorphism $(\phi,\gamma)$ of (D.5.0) whose continuous homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(B)$ has open image. D.5--D.7 prove faithfulness and the exact openness test for actual morphisms; they do not prove surjectivity of (D.7.1).
notes: Reconstruction of arbitrary open relative outer maps remains undecided.

statement: Nilpotent obstructions and the real case For the actual Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of the tripod, the first obstruction is the integral cup product \(\delta_2(A,B)=A\cup B\). The next obstruction is a pair of triple Massey expressions with cyclotomic and action corrections, evaluated using compatible defining systems belonging to one chosen class-two lift. These are \citet[\S12.3.1, Proposition 7, author p.~14; Theorem 19 and Remark 20(ii), author pp.~21--22]{CohWickelgren2012}. There are non-point, noncuspidal rational abelian pairs with class-two sections already over \(\mathbb Q\), for example \((3,4)\) \citep[Propositions 24--25, author pp.~26--27]{CohWickelgren2012}. For arbitrary depth, the Massey-product necessary conditions in \citet[\S3.11 and Corollary 3.12, arXiv author pp.~16--17]{LitWickelgrenN2012} are stated with the coefficient primes dividing \(n!\) omitted. They are not an unrestricted integral all-depth converse at 2 and 3. The lower-central obstruction framework also appears in the opened \citet[pp.~1--2]{LitEllenberg2007} lecture notes. Those notes are a 2007 source, not the unpublished 2000 manuscript cited by later authors. Over \(\mathbb R\), the full profinite section classes of a hyperbolic curve are its real connected components \citep[Corollary 3.13, pp.~142--143]{LitMochizuki2003}. For a based real curve whose normalization components have real points, the abelian classes lifting to class two already identify these components \citep[Theorem 1.1, author p.~2]{LitWickelgrenReal2014}.

statement: The hypotheses of the nongeometric pro-prime results \citet[Theorem A, author pp.~3--4; Lemma 3.2, author p.~14]{LitHoshi2010} constructs nongeometric geometrically pro-\(p\) sections, for odd regular \(p\), on suitable geometric \(p\)-power covers of the tripod and their proper genus-at-least-two compactifications, after a finite extension inside the extension unramified outside \(p\) that is pro-\(p\) over \(\mathbb Q(\mu_p)\). The hypotheses include rational points and good reduction away from \(p\). This theorem does not assert the claimed construction simultaneously at every coefficient prime over \(\mathbb Q\). \citet[Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 2.5(i), article pp.~9--11]{LitHoshiTsujimura2021} gives a more explicit lifting statement for the tripod itself: let \(p\) be odd regular, let \(F\) be a finite extension of \(\mathbb Q\) or \(\mathbb Q_p\) containing \(\mu_p\), and let \(x_1,x_2\) be \(p\)-units in \(F\cap\Omega_{p\text{-unr}}\). Then their abelian pro-\(p\) Kummer section lifts to a full geometrically pro-\(p\) section. The infinity-cusp qualification in P.3 is needed before using that preprint's asserted nongeometricity criterion. \citet[condition $(*)$ and Theorem A, \S0, pp.~573--575]{LitSaidi2023} constructs nongeometric sections of certain geometrically pronilpotent-by-abelian quotients of proper curves over \(p\)-adic fields, after finite base extension. This is not a theorem about the full pronilpotent quotient over \(\mathbb Q\).

statement: The infinity cusp must be included in the 2021 criterion The implication from condition (3) to ``(2) or (4)'' in \citet[Proposition 1.4(ii), article p.~6]{LitHoshiTsujimura2021} omits the cusp at infinity and is false as printed. Consequently Theorem A(iii) and Corollary 2.5(iii) cannot be used without that qualification. The definition invoked there is \citet[Definition 1.1(iii), author p.~7]{LitHoshi2010}: geometricity means containment in a decomposition group of a rational point of the smooth compactification. The 2021 Theorem A(iii), article p.~3, repeats this definition explicitly; it includes the point at infinity. Here is the corrected tripod statement. For a number field or a finite extension \(F/\mathbb Q_p\), write \(D_p\subset F^\times\) for the kernel of the pro-\(p\) Kummer map; it consists of the roots of unity of order prime to \(p\). A pair of actual elements \((x_1,x_2)\in(F^\times)^2\) is the abelian image of at least one geometric geometrically pro-\(p\) section, where geometric includes cusps, if and only if at least one of the following holds: \[ \begin{array}{ll} \text{ordinary:}&\zeta_1x_1+\zeta_2x_2=1 \quad\text{for some }\zeta_1,\zeta_2\in D_p;\\ \text{cusp }0:&x_2\in D_p;\\ \text{cusp }1:&x_1\in D_p;\\ \text{cusp }\infty:&-x_2/x_1\in D_p. \end{array} \] Thus the lift in P.2 is certainly nongeometric if all four conditions fail.

statement: Full pro-prime counterexamples over \(\mathbb Q\), including 2 Let \(p\) be 2 or an odd regular prime. There is a section of the full geometrically pro-\(p\) fundamental extension of the tripod over \(\mathbb Q\) with abelian pair \((\kappa_p(p),\kappa_p(p^2))\). Every such section is nongeometric, even allowing cusps. Its abelian pair is not ordinary at \(p\), so it is not a counterexample to either limit assertion for ordinary completed pairs. For odd regular \(p\), the same construction lifts every pair \((a\kappa_p(p),b\kappa_p(p))\), \(a,b\in\mathbb Z_p\). This is a derivation from the cited lifting and Galois-group theorems, not a claim that the quoted papers state this precise \(\mathbb Q\)-form.

statement: Unipotent Selmer results and the missing hypotheses Kim's theorem for the tripod proves finiteness of \(U(\mathbb Z[S^{-1}])\) for a fixed finite set \(S\), using rational unipotent fundamental groups and Selmer varieties \citep[\S3, concluding proof of Siegel's theorem, author pp.~17--18]{LitKim2005}. The conjecture of \citet[\S1.3 and Conjecture 3.1, author pp.~2--3 and 12; finite-$S$ variant in \S8]{LitBDCKW2018} asserts eventual equality of the associated local Chabauty--Kim locus with the integral points of the chosen model. These Selmer classes have fixed ramification and the stated local geometric and crystalline conditions. The strengthened comparison in \citet[Theorem A; Definition 2.1; \S2.2.1 and Lemma 2.19]{LitBKL2026} still concerns a fixed finite \(S\) and adelic, locally geometric sections. Its Theorem B and Corollary 5.17 establish the refined Chabauty--Kim conjecture for the tripod over \(\mathbb Z[1/2]\), for every odd coefficient prime. Its Remark 1.8 explicitly records that the corresponding full Selmer section assertion over \(\mathbb Q\), for the tripod and any finite \(S\), was already a consequence of \citet[Corollary 6, author p.~6]{Stix2015}. For the tripod there is a useful stronger local comparison: \citet[Lemma 4.2 and Corollary 4.3, author pp.~31--32]{LitBKL2026} shows that away from the coefficient prime \(p\), rational unipotent local cohomology is already determined by abelianization.

statement: Continuous cohomology and the scope of a derived-limit obstruction For \(T=\varprojlim_m T_m\), with finite discrete coefficient modules and surjective transition maps, continuous cohomology satisfies \[ 0\longrightarrow\varprojlim{}^1_m H^{i-1}(G,T_m) \longrightarrow H^i_{\rm cts}(G,T) \longrightarrow\varprojlim_m H^i(G,T_m)\longrightarrow0. \] This is \citet[equation (2.1) and Theorem (2.2), p.~215; Proposition (1.6), p.~211]{CohJannsen1988}. Finite cohomology groups at a local field, or with a fixed finite set of global ramification primes, make the relevant tower Mittag--Leffler and kill its \(\varprojlim^1\). Finiteness of the modules \(T_m\) alone does not imply finiteness of \(H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},T_m)\). In particular the unrestricted weight-two and weight-twelve computations in Part A require their separate arithmetic inputs and do not follow from Jannsen's formalism alone.

statement: Stronger full-section theorems do not remove the quotient gap For a hyperbolic curve over \(\mathbb Q\) with a nonconstant unit, \citet[Corollary 6, author p.~6]{Stix2015} identifies its full adelic section classes with rational points; Corollary 5, author p.~5, also handles noncuspidal Selmer sections having finite geometric support. For a smooth proper genus-at-least-two curve over a number field containing no CM subfield, \citet[Theorem A and Definition 1.1, author p.~1]{LitBettsStix2025} proves finiteness of the image at every finite place of the full Selmer section set. Neither statement is a theorem about arbitrary pronilpotent sections whose abelian localizations are ordinary.

statement: What this literature comparison says about R1--R7 The cup-product and Massey descriptions, the formal lower-central obstruction tower, real component detection, the fixed-finite-\(S\) unipotent framework, and the derived-limit exact sequence are established inputs and are not new results of the earlier runs. The specific factorial-prime ordinary-pair constructions in R1 and R3, their finite-prefix exclusions in R5, the pointed Heisenberg-cover arithmetic in R6, and the uniform exclusion assertion in R7 are not statements proved in the sources opened here. Their validity is determined by the independent audits in Parts A--E, not by attribution to those sources. No priority claim for the earlier constructions is inferred from this bounded literature search.
notes: Status applies only to the exact numbered statement.

statement: The precise local Hodge bridge for the tripod Let \(U_{p,n}\) be the depth-\(n\) rational \(\mathbb Q_p\)-unipotent geometric fundamental group of the tripod, based at \(0+1\), with its continuous \(G_{\mathbb Q_p}\)-action. Every class of \(H^1(G_{\mathbb Q_p},U_{p,n}(\mathbb Q_p))\) is semistable and hence de Rham. Moreover it is crystalline if and only if its abelian image is crystalline. Consequently, if a pro-\(p\) section has ordinary abelian image represented by \(x_p\), its rational unipotent image is semistable at every depth, and is crystalline when \(x_p,1-x_p\in\mathbb Z_p^\times\). These conclusions do not assert equality with the entire path torsor of \(x_p\).

statement: Brauer--Manin and descent comparisons \citet[Theorem 1.2, corrected author pp.~2--3; Remark 2.4, p.~7]{LitHarariSzamuely2009} characterizes the splitting of the Albanese quotient of the geometric abelian fundamental extension by membership of the Albanese torsor in the maximal divisible subgroup of \(H^1(k,\operatorname{Alb}_X)\). For curves the geometric abelianization itself is the relevant Tate module. The quasi-projective version uses the generalized Albanese. For a torsor under a semiabelian variety, finite Tate--Shafarevich group of its abelian quotient makes the indicated Brauer--Manin obstruction complete for existence of a rational point \citep[Theorem 1.1, author p.~2; Corollary 4.8 and Lemma 4.9, author p.~16]{LitHarariSzamuely2008}. For a geometrically connected variety over a number field and a continuous quotient of its geometric fundamental group whose kernel is normal in the arithmetic fundamental group, \citet[Theorem 2.1 and Remark (3), author pp.~11--12]{LitHarariStix2012} equates interpolation of a tuple of local point sections in that quotient with survival of the corresponding finite descent obstructions. This includes the full pronilpotent quotient and does not require an adelic tuple when formulated as that interpolation statement. Their Corollary 3.1, author p.~13, gives Brauer--Manin orthogonality on a proper curve from a section of its full geometric abelianization whose local sections come from points.

statement: Completed reciprocity complexes and their point domain \citet[Definitions 3.1--3.3, p.~728; Definition 3.10, p.~733]{LitPridham2020} defines adelic cohomology for profinite coefficients by a derived inverse limit of finite-coefficient restricted products, and compactly supported cohomology by the cocone of global restriction. These constructions allow an infinite set of finite places. The nilpotent reciprocity tower in Example 3.16, pp.~734--735, nevertheless starts from actual adelic points and requires a global quotient section matching their local path classes. Example 3.18, pp.~735--736, gives the rational unipotent variant.

statement: Density-zero reduction is weaker than finite prime support For a noncuspidal Selmer section of the \emph{full} arithmetic fundamental group of a hyperbolic curve over a number field, the primes where its local point reduces to a cusp have density zero after a suitable finite field extension. Two such sections with the same reductions on a set of density one are conjugate. These are \citet[Theorems~1.1--1.2, pp.1--2; Theorem~5.4 and Corollary~5.7, pp.14--15]{RootPorowski2025}. They supply neither a finite-support conclusion nor a theorem for an arbitrary geometrically pronilpotent section.

statement: An infinite-ramification deformation theorem does not supply the required cusp constraints \citet[Theorem~1, p.794; local deformation calculation and Proposition~1, pp.796--798]{RootRamakrishna2000} constructs infinitely ramified representations into \(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb Z_p)\) for a density-one set of primes \(p\ge5\), starting from the stated semistable elliptic-curve residual representations. The method has an additional permitted ramified local deformation direction at each chosen auxiliary prime. It is not a theorem about sections of \(E_U^{(p)}\), and does not assert an ordinary completed pair.

statement: The available Massey vanishing theorems do not supply the required compatible section Let $k$ be a number field and $p$ a prime. Every defined $n$-fold Massey product of classes in $H^1(k,\mathbb F_p(1))$, for $n\ge3$, contains zero, with the successive products interpreted in their appropriate Tate twists. This is the rank-one coefficient case of \citet[Theorem 7.4, author p.27]{RootHarpazWittenberg2023}. For trivial coefficients and odd $p$, if $\zeta_p\notin k$, the stronger condition that adjacent cups vanish suffices; it also suffices over the maximal tame Galois quotient \citep[Theorem 1.1]{RootMaireMinacRamakrishnaTan2026}. These are finite-coefficient conclusions with an existential choice of defining system. They do not assert liftability of every specified preceding section, simultaneous compatibility of all the obstruction coordinates for the actual tripod action, or compatible integral sections with one fixed ordinary pair. In particular they do not decide A.2, A.3, or the remainder in B.1.

statement: Comparison of the three survival assertions For an ordinary completed pair \(a=(A,B)\), write \(S_\ell(a)\) for existence of a section of the geometrically pro-\(\ell\) quotient \(E_U^{(\ell)}\) whose abelian class is \(a_\ell\). Write \(S_{r,\ell}(a)\) for its class-\(r\) version, \(S_r(a)\) for existence in \(E_U/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi\), and \(S_{\rm nil}(a)\) for existence in \(E_U^{\rm nil}\). Then \[ S_{\rm nil}(a)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl(\forall\ell\;S_\ell(a)\bigr) \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl(\forall r\;S_r(a)\bigr). \] The pair is the same in every quantifier. Define \[ \begin{split} (\mathrm{FS})_{\rm nil}:\quad& \forall a\in\mathcal G_{\rm ord},\quad S_{\rm nil}(a)\Longrightarrow |\operatorname{supp}(a)|<\infty,\\ (\mathrm{FS})_\ell:\quad& \forall a\in\mathcal G_{\rm ord},\quad S_\ell(a)\Longrightarrow |\operatorname{supp}(a)|<\infty. \end{split} \] For any one prime \(\ell\), \((\mathrm{FS})_\ell\) implies \((\mathrm{FS})_{\rm nil}\). A counterexample to the latter would be a counterexample to every \((\mathrm{FS})_\ell\), with the same pair. Counterexamples chosen separately for the different primes do not furnish that simultaneous counterexample.

statement: The main question and its single-prime versions We have neither proved \((\mathrm{FS})_{\rm nil}\) nor constructed an ordinary infinite-support pair with a section of \(E_U^{\rm nil}\). We have also not decided \((\mathrm{FS})_2\), \((\mathrm{FS})_3\), or the assertion for arbitrary \(\ell\ge5\). These are the exact remaining assertions in tasks A2 and A3 and Lead L1. The fixed-pair equivalence in A.1 is a reduction to an integral class obstruction for each ghost; it is not an obstruction itself. At coefficient three, E.146--E.148 give an exact finite extension criterion: the old-support plus-character Frobenius equations, with every aligning frame retained. E.151 preserves an ordinary pair in the full power completion along any actually chosen infinite path through these systems. The missing assertion is existence or impossibility of such a compatible path. E.149 shows that individual frozen predecessors can fail, so an induction asserting that every node extends is false. This conditional construction concerns one specified support pattern; failure of that entire pattern would not by itself prove the general finite-support assertion. At coefficient two, E.155--E.159 remove the real obstruction for an actually boundary-matched ordinary predecessor and give an exact finite-parameter test for preserving every off-diagonal support match in the stated support pattern. Its passing infinite branch is not constructed. E.171--E.174 do construct one ordinary infinite-support pair with a single integral class-two section matching every support point away from its coefficient prime, simultaneously for all coefficient primes; that section has an unrestricted global class-three lift. These assertions establish nonemptiness of the necessary class-two matching locus. They neither preserve point matching at class three nor supply any all-depth section, and they concern a different family from the original A.44 recursion.

statement: Why finite-ramification pro-prime constructions cannot be ghosts For an ordinary pair, its valuations are actual integers. If its \(\ell\)-primary abelian cocycle is unramified outside a finite set, then the pair has finite prime support and is a rational unit-equation pair. In particular, equality of its \(\ell\)-primary pair with that of a rational point, even at one coefficient prime, implies finite support. For a ghost, the ordinary valuation vectors outside every finite set span a rank-two subgroup of \(\mathbb Z^2\), and generate an open \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-submodule of \(\mathbb Z_\ell^2\). Its pro-\(\ell\) abelian pair is not cuspidal. This confirms these assertions of GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.1.2.

statement: Rational abelian pair and ordinary local full sections determine the full section Let \(s:G\to E_U\) be a section of the full profinite arithmetic fundamental group, whose restriction at every finite place is the section of an ordinary point \(x_q\in U(\mathbb Q_q)\). If its completed abelian pair is \((\kappa(t),\kappa(1-t))\) for \(t\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0,1\}\), then \([s]=[s_t]\). The derivation uses \citet[Corollary 5, p.~5]{Stix2015}, or equivalently his Corollary 6, p.~6, after checking adelicity; it does not use the attached unrefereed local theorem.

statement: The exact conditional implication of a positive or negative limit answer If \((\mathrm{FS})_{\rm nil}\) holds, every section of \(E_U\to G\) whose local sections at finite primes are ordinary is a rational-point section. Thus a positive answer would prove the locally ordinary case of Conjecture A, not merely reduce it to an unresolved rational-abelian-pair case. The twenty-four unrestricted class-two lifts are not a remaining ambiguity under these hypotheses. A negative answer to \((\mathrm{FS})_{\rm nil}\) alone would give a non-point section of \(E_U^{\rm nil}\); to contradict the full section conjecture one would still have to lift it to \(E_U\).

statement: The obstruction at an arbitrary integral class is a class of a specified lift Fix \(\ell\), a literal class-\(r\) cocycle \(c\), and the actual arithmetic action. A continuous Hall-coordinate section of \(N_{r+1,\ell}\twoheadrightarrow N_{r,\ell}\) gives a lift \(\widetilde c\) as a map of spaces. The formula \[ o_c(g,h)=\widetilde c(g)\,g\widetilde c(h)\, \widetilde c(gh)^{-1} \] defines a continuous two-cocycle in \(L_{r+1,\ell}=\mathbb Z_\ell(r+1)^{b_{r+1}}\). Its class vanishes precisely when \(c\) lifts. It depends on the class-\(r\) section as well as on the abelian pair. Its projections to finite coefficients need not determine whether this continuous class vanishes.

statement: The unsolved evaluation problem in A4 and L4 No theorem here identifies a first nonzero higher obstruction for every ordinary ghost. In particular, the existence of nonzero locally trivial continuous cohomology classes does not prove that an obstruction of a given ghost is one of them. The exact class-three residue test below separates local vanishing from the additional convergence of primitives. This supplies a precise gate, but neither proves the nonvanishing claimed in L4 nor constructs an all-depth survivor.

statement: Compatibility, prescribed symmetries, and the ambiguity of a lift Let \(X\) be a compact space of candidates, and let \(X_i\subseteq X\) be closed subsets expressing specified finite conditions. If every finite collection of these conditions has a simultaneous solution in \(X\), they have a common solution. Consequently any purported example in which all finite cofinal tests of one fixed closed lifting-and-symmetry problem succeed, but the problem has no solution, must fail one of these hypotheses. For sections, a chosen lift through a central kernel \(T\), if it exists, leaves the torsor under \(H^1(G,T)\) undetermined. This is the relevant test of the comparisons proposed in R9.

statement: All-depth survival alone does not bound ramification Choose distinct rational primes \(q_j\), and put \(A=\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{(j+4)!}\) in the power completion. There is an actual full profinite cuspidal section of the tripod with abelian pair \((A,1)\). It has infinite support and ramifies at infinitely many primes in every coefficient component. Its pair is not ordinary. Thus finite ramification cannot follow from all-depth lifting alone; any proof of A2 must use the ordinary local unit equation.

statement: Compactness with the abelian cocycle fixed For $r\geq2$, $Z^1_{\rm cts}(G,\mathbb Z_\ell(r))$ is a finite free $\mathbb Z_\ell$-module, compact for the compact-open topology. Fix a literal cocycle $a\in Z^1_{\rm cts}(G,N_{1,\ell})$. Then the space \[ \mathscr S_{r,\ell}(a)= \{c\in Z^1_{\rm cts}(G,N_{r,\ell}):c_{\rm ab}=a\} \] is compact Hausdorff. More precisely, it is parametrized continuously by a closed subset of a finite power of $\mathbb Z_\ell$, with Hall coordinates polynomial over $\mathbb Q_\ell$ in the parameters and continuous cochains as coefficients. This confirms GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.1.3--C.1.6. No compactness is asserted when $a$ varies.

statement: The exact limit equivalence and its quantifiers Fix $(A,B)\in(\widehat{\mathbb Q^{\times}})^2$. For the tripod over $\mathbb Q$, the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item the pair is the abelianization of a continuous section of $E_U^{\rm nil}\to G_{\mathbb Q}$; \item for every prime $\ell$, its $\ell$-component is the abelianization of a continuous section of the full geometrically pro-$\ell$ quotient; \item for every positive integer $r$, the same pair is the abelianization of a continuous section of the integral class-$r$ quotient; \item for every $\ell$ and every $r$, the same $\ell$-component survives the pro-$\ell$ class-$r$ quotient. \end{enumerate} The corresponding fixed-$\ell$ equivalence holds. It continues to hold after imposing geometric conjugacy to one prescribed compatible family of local point sections, or local cuspidal sections, at every level. This confirms GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.1.7. The assertion does not permit the pair to change with $r$ or $\ell$.

statement: Strict integral localization Let $r\geq2$, let $T=\mathbb Z_\ell(r)$, and put $S=\{\ell,\infty\}$. After compatible Tate coordinates are chosen, define \[ R_\ell=\{(z_q)_{q\ne\ell}\in\prod_{q\ne\ell}\mathbb Z_\ell: z_q\longrightarrow0\}, \qquad (d_rz)_q=(q^{r-1}-1)z_q. \] There is a natural exact sequence of abelian groups \[ 0\longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q,S},T) \longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cts}(G,T) \xrightarrow{\Psi_{\ell,r}}R_\ell/d_rR_\ell \longrightarrow0. \] The denominator is the actual image, without closure. At $r=3$, the first group is zero for every $\ell$, so $\Psi_{\ell,3}$ is an isomorphism. This confirms GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.1.13.

statement: A projective quotient retaining the cyclotomic character kills off-diagonal tame inertia Let \(K\) be a number field, \(\ell\) a prime, and \(\psi:G_K\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma\) a continuous quotient. Assume that \(\Gamma\) has an open pro-\(\ell\) subgroup, that \(\operatorname{cd}_\ell\Gamma\leq1\), and that the \(\ell\)-adic cyclotomic character factors continuously through \(\psi\). Then, at each finite place \(v\nmid\ell\), the \(\ell\)-primary tame inertia has trivial image in \(\Gamma\) after passage to any finite extension making the local image pro-\(\ell\). In particular, suppose that the actual tangential action on \(F_\ell\), and a continuous section cocycle \(G_{\mathbb Q}\to F_\ell\), factor through such a quotient of \(G_{\mathbb Q}\). Its abelian pair is unramified away from \(\ell\). If that pair is the \(\ell\)-primary component of an ordinary completed pair, the latter has finite support and is a rational unit-equation pair. This holds without a finite-ramification assumption on \(\Gamma\).

statement: Every ordinary completed pair has support of upper relative prime density zero Let \((A,B)\in\mathcal G_{\rm ord}\) be an ordinary completed pair over \(\mathbb Q\). No nonabelian section is assumed. If \(S\) is its support, then \[ \limsup_{X\longrightarrow\infty} \frac{\#\{p\in S:p\le X\}}{\pi(X)}=0, \tag{A.33.1} \] where \(\pi(X)\) counts all rational primes up to \(X\). Thus the density is relative to the primes, not the ordinary integer density shared by every set of primes. More precisely, partition the support into the three disjoint sets \[ \begin{split} S_0&=\{p:v_p(A)>0\},\qquad S_1=\{p:v_p(B)>0\},\\ S_\infty&=\{p:v_p(A)=v_p(B)<0\}, \end{split} \tag{A.33.2} \] and put \(C_0=B\), \(C_1=A\), \(C_\infty=-A/B\). If \(v_{p_i}(C_i)=m_i\ne0\), then for every squarefree positive integer \(N\) coprime to \(p_i m_i\), \[ \limsup_{X\longrightarrow\infty} \frac{\#\{p\in S_i:p\le X\}}{\pi(X)} \le \frac{\varphi(N)}{N}. \tag{A.33.3} \] If any of these three \(C_i\) has no nonzero valuation, the pair is one of the rational pairs treated explicitly in the proof. In particular the density conclusion cannot distinguish an ordinary ghost from a full-tower survivor: it holds before any survival test.

statement: Varying ghost families are not compact; correction to Lead L2 The original A.44 family is noncompact in $\mathcal K^2$. statement: Finite-prefix control includes two and three Fix a coefficient prime $\ell$ and an integer $N\geq1$. Put $M=N+1$ if $\ell=2$, and $M=N$ otherwise. Let $J_M$ be the least index with $v_\ell(n_{J_M})\geq M$, and define \[ S_{\ell,M}=(\{2,3\}\cup\{q_i,r_i:i<J_M\})\setminus\{\ell\}, \qquad D=M+\max_{p\in S_{\ell,M}}v_\ell(p-1). \] The maximum over the empty set is zero. Choose $L\geq J_M$ with $v_\ell(n_L)\geq D$, and fix the prime prefix through $L-1$. Then every ordinary continuation has the same set of geometric-conjugacy classes of reductions of its integral pro-$\ell$ class-two sections modulo $\ell^N$, after using the common abelian cocycle representatives. At $\ell\geq5$ this set is a singleton. At two and three the assertion concerns the entire finite set, and does not attach consistent labels to its individual members. This confirms and extends GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.1.21.

statement: Closedness of the correctly quantified local remainder Let $\mathscr A$ have the legal-prefix topology. statement: The continuous class-three criterion for a specified lift Write a specified global integral class-two section as $s(g)=y^{b(g)}x^{a(g)}C^{h(g)}s_0(g)$, with $C=[x,y]$ and $\delta h=-a\cup b$. Set $D=[C,x]$, $F_3=[C,y]$, $\epsilon=(\chi-1)/2$, and $\eta=(\chi^2-1)/24$. Its two actual class-three obstruction classes are represented by \[ W_D=-(a+\epsilon)\cup h-\binom a2\cup b,\qquad W_F=(b+\epsilon)\cup(ab-h)+\binom b2\cup a-\eta\cup b. \] Here products and binomial expressions denote continuous cochains with the indicated weight, rather than assertions that they are one-cocycles. At $q\ne\ell$ put \[ \begin{gathered} (m,n,t)=(a(T_q),b(T_q),h(T_q)),\quad (\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=(a(F_q),b(F_q),h(F_q)),\\ e=(q-1)/2,\qquad e_2=(q^2-1)/24, \end{gathered} \] and set $B_q(z)=q^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{q-1}\binom{jz}{2} =(q-1)((2q-1)z^2-3z)/12$. Their images under $\Psi_{\ell,3}$ are the classes of the actual $R_\ell$-sequences \begin{align*} Z_{D,q}={}&m\gamma-q(\alpha+e)t-n\binom\alpha2 +q^{-1}\beta\binom{qm}{2}+emt+nB_q(m),\\ Z_{F,q}={}&n(\gamma-\alpha\beta)+q(\beta+e)(mn-t) +m\binom\beta2-e_2n-q^{-1}\alpha\binom{qn}{2}\\ &{}-e(mn^2-nt)-mB_q(n). \end{align*} The section lifts to the integral class-three quotient if and only if, for every $\ell$, both sequences $Z_{D,q}/(q^2-1)$ and $Z_{F,q}/(q^2-1)$ are integral and tend to zero $\ell$-adically. This confirms GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.1.15.

statement:
Boundary matching forces the global third convergence condition For an ordinary A.44 output, let $s_*$ be the unique global integral class-two section class which agrees with its actual local point section in the pro-two quotient at $q=3$ and in the pro-three quotient at $q=2$. This class exists. Every full pronilpotent section above the pair has class-two image $s_*$. Fix $\ell$ and normalize $s_*$ to literal abelian cocycles $a,b$. At an $A$-support prime $q
e\ell$, write $b=\delta u_q$, so $ eta=(q-1)u_q$, and put \[ R_{A,q}= rac{\gamma-q\alpha u_q}{q^2-1}. \] At a $B$-support prime $q
e\ell$, write $a=\delta v_q$, so $\alpha=(q-1)v_q$, and put \[ R_{B,q}= rac{\gamma+ eta v_q-\eta(F_q)}{q^2-1} = rac{\gamma+ eta v_q}{q^2-1}- rac1{24}. \] Then $s_*|_{G_q}$ is the actual local point class if and only if the corresponding $R_{A,q}$ or $R_{B,q}$ is in $\mathbb Z_\ell$. These conditions, at every support $q
e\ell$ and every $\ell$, are necessary for a full pronilpotent survivor. If they all hold, $s_*$ lifts to the global integral class-three quotient: the strict convergence condition in B.23 follows automatically. This is a necessary all-depth gate and a sufficient class-three test; it is not asserted sufficient at every depth.

statement: Boundary matching leaves a fixed-ramification obstruction Let $r\geq2$, fix $\ell$, and let $s_r$ be a continuous section of the actual pro-$\ell$ class-$r$ quotient with an ordinary completed abelian pair. Assume that, at every support prime $q\ne\ell$, its local class equals the class-$r$ image of the corresponding ordinary point section. Then its next obstruction has the form \[ o_{r+1}(s_r)=\operatorname{inf}(\omega_{r+1}),\qquad \omega_{r+1}\in H^2(G_{\mathbb Q,\{\ell,\infty\}}, \mathbb Z_\ell(r+1))^{b_{r+1}}, \] with a unique $\omega_{r+1}$. In particular it lifts if and only if this fixed-ramification class is zero. The latter group is finite. For $r=2$ it is zero, so the local boundary-matching hypothesis alone implies a global class-three lift for every ordinary pair, including negative-valuation support patterns. This removes the strict tame residue contribution under the stated matching hypothesis. It does not remove the entire absolute derived-limit kernel: a fixed-ramification class can inflate to a nonzero class invisible at every finite absolute coefficient level, as in A.23.

statement: The separate obstruction to preserving boundary matching Retain the hypotheses and notation of B.25, and suppose $\omega_{r+1}=0$. Put $T=\mathbb Z_\ell(r+1)^{b_{r+1}}$ and let $\Sigma$ be the support primes different from $\ell$. Choose one global class-$(r+1)$ lift $t$ of $s_r$. There is a well-defined tuple of local discrepancy classes \[ d(t)=(d_q(t))_{q\in\Sigma}\in \prod_{q\in\Sigma}H^1(G_q,T) \] such that a global lift matching the actual point class at every $q\in\Sigma$ exists if and only if \[ d(t)\in\operatorname{im}\left( H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},T)\longrightarrow \prod_{q\in\Sigma}H^1(G_q,T)\right). \] The image is compact and closed. If this condition fails, some finite set of support primes and some finite coefficient exponents already exclude every integral global twist of $t$. If it holds, the matching lifts form a torsor under the kernel of the displayed localization map. This is an additional condition after the finite second-cohomology obstruction in B.25 has vanished.

statement: Two exceptional-prime tests select a unique class-two class Let $(A,B)\in\mathcal G_{\rm ord}$ satisfy \[ (v_3(A),v_3(B))=(1,0),\qquad (v_2(A),v_2(B))=(0,1). \] Use the actual integral class-two arithmetic quotient of the tripod, the tangential splitting at zero, and geometric conjugacy of continuous sections. There is exactly one class-two section class above $(A,B)$ whose third obstruction vanishes at both of the following pairs of rational place and coefficient prime: \[ (q,\ell)=(3,2),\qquad(q,\ell)=(2,3). \] Consequently at most one class-two section class above this pair can be the projection of an integral class-three section. In particular the twenty-four alternatives in the original A.44 family reduce to one canonical candidate before the other local or continuous tests are imposed. The assertion does not say that this candidate lifts.

statement: The remaining fresh-support test in two scalar sequences For an original A.44 pair let $s$ be the canonical class-two candidate of B.101 and put $n_j=(j+4)!$. Fix a coefficient prime $\ell$. At each positive $A$-support prime $q_j\ne\ell$, write $b=\delta u_j$ locally, and use Frobenius coordinates $\alpha_j=a(F_{q_j})$, $\gamma_j=h(F_{q_j})$. At each positive $B$-support prime $r_j\ne\ell$, write $a=\delta v_j$ and put $\beta_j=b(F_{r_j})$, $\widetilde\gamma_j=h(F_{r_j})$. The two potentially nonintegral normalized residues are \[ T_{A,j}=\frac{n_j(\gamma_j-q_j\alpha_j u_j)}{q_j^2-1}, \qquad T_{B,j}=\frac{n_j(\widetilde\gamma_j+\beta_jv_j)}{r_j^2-1}. \] The fresh-support local class-three obstructions all vanish if and only if these numbers belong to $\mathbb Z_\ell$ for every indicated index and every $\ell$. After the finitely many old-place residues have also been tested, the global continuous class-three obstruction vanishes if and only if, in addition, $T_{A,j}\to0$ and $T_{B,j}\to0$ in $\mathbb Z_\ell$ for every $\ell$. The quotient formulas are exact, including coefficient primes two and three. This is a reduction of B1 to explicit arithmetic conditions on one section class, not a construction of a prime sequence satisfying them.

statement: Geometry of every odd-prime Heisenberg cover Let \(\ell\) be odd and \(t_0\in U(\mathbb Q)\). Let \(H_\ell\) be the universal two-generator quotient of class at most two and exponent dividing \(\ell\). It is the group of upper unitriangular \(3\times3\) matrices over \(\mathbb F_\ell\), of order \(\ell^3\). The inverse image of the point section at \(t_0\) in the arithmetic \(H_\ell\)-quotient defines a connected finite etale cover \(Y_{\ell,t_0}\to U\) of degree \(\ell^3\), with a specified rational point above \(t_0\). Its compactification has \[ g(\overline Y_{\ell,t_0})=1+\frac{\ell^2(\ell-3)}2, \qquad |\overline Y_{\ell,t_0}\setminus Y_{\ell,t_0}|=3\ell^2. \] Its central quotient is the pointed diagonal curve \[ C_{\ell,t_0}:\quad t_0 u^\ell+(1-t_0)v^\ell=1, \qquad (u,v)=(1,1), \] and \(\overline Y_{\ell,t_0}\to\overline C_{\ell,t_0}\) is an unramified cover of degree \(\ell\). Thus the genus-one case \(\ell=3\) is exceptional; the genera at \(\ell=5,7\) are already \(26,99\).

statement: The exponent-prime degree formula cannot include two unchanged There is no nonabelian group of exponent two. In particular the universal rank-two class-two exponent-two quotient has order four, not eight. If ``Heisenberg at two'' instead means \(\mathrm U_3(\mathbb F_2)\), that group has exponent four and is dihedral of order eight. A cover with branch generators its two standard involutions has branch orders \((2,2,4)\), genus zero, and ten boundary points. These are two different conventions, and neither is obtained by substituting two into the odd-prime exponent-\(\ell\) assertion. The exponent-two quotient instead has genus zero and six boundary points. A pointed degree-eight dihedral model above \(t_0=3\) is explicit: \[ \begin{gathered} a(s)=\frac{1+6s^2}{1-6s^2},\qquad b(s)=\frac{2s}{1-6s^2},\\ u(s)=a(s)^2+6b(s)^2+4a(s)b(s),\qquad v(s)=a(s)^2+6b(s)^2+6a(s)b(s),\\ t(s)=3u(s)^2,\qquad 1-t(s)=-2v(s)^2. \end{gathered} \] The point \(s=0\) lies over \(t=3\). The open source is \(\mathbb P^1_s\) with the ten points above \(0,1,\infty\) removed.

statement: Passing to a cover preserves the appropriate prime, not every prime Let \(Y\to U\) be a connected geometrically Galois cover whose geometric group is a nontrivial \(p\)-group of order \(d\). If a geometrically pro-\(p\) section factors through its associated open arithmetic subgroup, that subgroup is the full geometrically pro-\(p\) arithmetic fundamental group of \(Y\). For the full pronilpotent group of \(U\), the induced geometric open subgroup is instead \[ K_p\times\prod_{\ell\ne p}F_\ell, \qquad [F_p:K_p]=d. \] It is not the full pronilpotent geometric fundamental group of \(Y\). For \(\ell\ne p\), the latter has free pro-\(\ell\) rank \(d+1\), whereas the inherited factor has rank two.

statement: Compact finite separation and the limit of the pentagon analogy Let \(X\) be a compact space, \(H\) a profinite group, and \(f:X\to H\) continuous. If \(1\notin f(X)\), there is an open normal subgroup \(V\triangleleft H\) with \(f(X)\cap V=\varnothing\). Thus an exclusion proved on an actual compact family is detected in one finite quotient. This general fact proves the topological inference used in GT\_TOWER\_CHECK A.4.1 conditional on that work's arithmetic vanishing input; it does not verify A.7 or the explicit compiler A.4.57.

statement: Why the modular Fermat theorem does not descend to this quotient \citet[Theorem A and Theorem 5.14]{Steklov2026} proves a cuspidality theorem for full Selmer sections of affine Fermat curves of prime exponent at least seven. The residual Legendre representations used there do not factor geometrically through the pronilpotent quotient of the tripod at an odd coefficient prime \(\ell\ge5\). Thus this theorem is not a proof of the present main assertion.

statement: Fixed-coordinate reciprocity does not exclude the constructed ghosts Let \(A\in\widehat{\mathbb Q^\times}\), and let \(\theta:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\) be a finite character of order dividing \(n\). The local reciprocity sum for the local Kummer coordinates of \(A\), paired with \(\theta\), is zero. It is well defined even when the ordinary local coordinates of \(A\) do not form an idele. The same holds for \(B\) and for every fixed monomial in \(A,B\). Hence reciprocity on these base unit coordinates alone cannot distinguish a ghost from a global completed pair.

statement: The missing pointwise hypothesis in an all-prime pointed-cover test Fix \(t_0\in U(\mathbb Q)\). Suppose an ordinary completed pair \((A,B)\) has, for every prime \(\ell\), the same reduction modulo \(\ell\)-th powers as \((t_0,1-t_0)\). Then \((A,B)=(\kappa(t_0),\kappa(1-t_0))\). In particular, factorization of a single section through the point-\(t_0\) Heisenberg cover at every prime would already force its ordinary abelian pair to be rational. Such factorization is not an automatic property of a full section: the rational-point section at two does not factor through the point-three Heisenberg cover at five.

statement: Finite support; SECTIONS_OVER_Q A.32 and GT_TOWER_CHECK C.1.1 confirmed Put $\mathcal K=\varprojlim_n\mathbb Q^\times/(\mathbb Q^\times)^n$, with discrete power quotients and their inverse-limit topology. We have a continuous group isomorphism, with continuous inverse, \[ \mathcal K\simeq\{\pm1\}\times \left\{(a_q)_q\in\prod_q\widehat{\mathbb Z}: \text{for every }n,\ a_q=0\pmod n\text{ for almost all }q\right\}. \] The topology on the right is defined by simultaneous reduction of all coordinates modulo $n$, with the resulting direct sum given the discrete topology. If $(A,B)$ is ordinary at every finite prime, every valuation $v_q(A),v_q(B)$ is an ordinary integer. If any one of $A,B,A/B$ has finite valuation support, there is a unique $t\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0,1\}$ with $(A,B)=(\kappa(t),\kappa(1-t))$; all its ordinary local points equal $t$. No local section theorem is used.

statement: SECTIONS_OVER_Q A.44 confirmed: ordinary infinite-support pairs There are pairwise distinct primes $q_j,r_j>3$, for $j\ge0$, such that \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{(j+4)!},\qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}r_j^{(j+4)!} \] converge in $\mathcal K$. At every finite prime $p$ they are the Kummer classes of nonzero $x_p,y_p\in\mathbb Z_p$ satisfying $x_p+y_p=1$. Their nonzero valuation vectors are $(1,0)$ at three, $(0,1)$ at two, $((j+4)!,0)$ at $q_j$, and $(0,(j+4)!)$ at $r_j$. The first prime $q_0$ can take infinitely many values. The result concerns the abelian completed pair only; it does not assert a section of any nonabelian quotient. No local section theorem is used.

statement: SECTIONS_OVER_Q A.42 confirmed from rational-point finiteness The rational unit-equation graph $\mathcal R=\{(\kappa(t),\kappa(1-t)):t\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0,1\}\}$ is closed and discrete in $\mathcal K^2$. Every Cauchy net in it is eventually constant. Thus a nonrational completed pair is separated from all rational pairs in some simultaneous finite power quotient.

statement: SECTIONS_OVER_Q A.72 and GT_TOWER_CHECK C.2.17 confirmed Let \(N\subset\Pi\) be open and normal in \(E_U\), and put \(Q=\Pi/N\). There is an integer \(N_0>0\) and an ordinary ghost \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{N_0(j+4)!},\qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}r_j^{N_0(j+4)!} \] whose section in \[ E_U/(N\cap\overline{[\Pi,\Pi]}) \simeq E_Q\mathbin{\times}_{E_{Q^{\rm ab}}}E_{\rm ab} \] has \(Q\)-component the specified point-three section. At every finite place this entire section is geometrically conjugate to the image of the ordinary local point of the pair. The pair and the section depend on \(N\). Consequently no one fixed finite geometric quotient excludes every A.72 output. This last assertion confirms R7, with its varying-pair quantifier.

statement: Exact local images for the variable exponent Let $d\ge2$, let $24\mid C$, and choose $h\ge2d^2$ at least every prime divisor of $C$. Set \[ n=h!,\qquad E(Z)=Cn\prod_{r=2}^d(Z^r-1),\qquad D=Cd!n^d. \] For $p\mid n$, put $v=v_p(n)$, $e=v_p(d)$, and $a_p=1$ for odd $p$, $a_2=2$. Then the map \[ F_p(z)=\exp(E(z)\log z) \] is a bijection \[ 1+p^v+p^{v+a_p}\mathbb Z_p \xrightarrow{\sim} F_p(1+p^v)(1+p^{W_p}\mathbb Z_p),\qquad W_p=v_p(C)+(d+1)v+v_p(d!)+a_p+e. \tag{E.30.1} \] It preserves congruences, agrees with $z^{E(z)}$ on positive integer inputs, and throughout this shell \[ v_p(z-1)=v,\qquad v_p(E(z))=v_p(D),\qquad W_p\le2v_p(D). \tag{E.30.2} \] For $p\nmid n$, let $\omega\in\mu_{p-1}(\mathbb Z_p)$ satisfy $\omega^r\not\equiv1\pmod p$ for $2\le r\le d$. For a fixed integer $e_0$ modulo $p-1$, the map \[ z\longmapsto \omega^{e_0} \exp(E(z)\log(z/\omega)) \tag{E.30.3} \] is a congruence-preserving bijection from $\omega(1+p\mathbb Z_p)$ to $\omega^{e_0}(1+p\mathbb Z_p)$. It equals the ordinary variable power on those positive integer inputs for which $E(z)\equiv e_0$ modulo $p-1$.

statement: The simultaneous variable-exponent arithmetic recursion Fix $d\ge2$, $24\mid C$, and $J\ge2d^2$ at least every prime divisor of $C$. Write \[ n_j=(j+J)!,\quad D_j=Cd!n_j^d,\quad E_j(Q)=Cn_j\prod_{r=2}^d(Q^r-1). \tag{E.31.1} \] There are pairwise disjoint sequences of distinct primes $q_j,r_j,s_j>3$ for which \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}\frac{q_j^{E_j(q_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}},\qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}\frac{r_j^{E_j(r_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}} \tag{E.31.2} \] form an ordinary completed unit-equation pair. Both coordinates have infinite support, their quotients by $3,-2$ are global $C$-th powers, and their nonzero valuation patterns are exactly \[ \begin{array}{c|c} 2&(0,1)\\3&(1,0)\\ q_j&(E_j(q_j),0)\\r_j&(0,E_j(r_j))\\ s_j&(-E_j(s_j),-E_j(s_j)). \end{array} \tag{E.31.3} \] Every prime choice is specified by finitely many congruences and complete splitting in one explicitly given radical field; those conditions have an actual simultaneous Galois element.

statement: Uniform Hall, inertia, and arithmetic-kernel bounds Fix $R\ge3$. Let $N_r=\Pi/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi$ and $L_r=\Gamma_r\Pi/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi=\widehat{\mathbb Z}(r)^{b_r}$. Use the actual point-three section $s_3$ to identify $E_r=N_r\rtimes_{\rho_3}G_{\mathbb Q}$. Define \[ K_r(m)=\ker\left(N_r\longrightarrow (1+I)((\mathbb Z/m)\langle X,Y\rangle/I^{r+1})\right), \qquad I=(X,Y), \tag{E.32.1} \] using the integral Magnus images $x\mapsto1+X$, $y\mapsto1+Y$. If $h_R$ is the number of Hall basis elements through weight $R$, put \[ D_H=(R!)^{h_R+1},\quad T=2(R!)^R,\quad B_r=2|K_{2r-2}(\mathbb Z)|\quad(2\le r\le R). \tag{E.32.2} \] Then $K_r(m)$ is characteristic, the continuous Hall set section $\sigma_r:N_{r-1}\to N_r$ with zero new coordinates satisfies \[ \sigma_r(K_{r-1}(D_Hm))\subset K_r(m), \tag{E.32.3} \] and the finite integer $B_r$ annihilates $H^2(G_{\mathbb Q,\{\ell,\infty\}},\mathbb Z_\ell(r))$ for every coefficient prime $\ell$. At a fresh prime $q>3$, $q\ne\ell$, suppose an ordinary local abelian pair has valuation pattern $(E,0)$, $(0,E)$, or $(-E,-E)$. For any actual class-$(r-1)$ section with this pair, the central defect $c$ of its canonical Hall set lift satisfies the strict tame-residue bound \[ \frac{z_q(c)}{q^{r-1}-1} \in \frac{E}{T\prod_{k=2}^{r-1}(q^k-1)} \mathbb Z_\ell^{b_r}. \tag{E.32.4} \] The product is empty for $r=2$. We use this assertion when all the displayed ideals are integral. At a prime $q>3$, $q\ne\ell$, where both ordinary valuations are zero, the defect residue is zero.

The pair and the section may depend on $R,N$. This proves the fixed-depth content of GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.2.12 and SECTIONS\_OVER\_Q A.65, with C.2.10--11/A.66 reconstructed above.

statement: Why the denominator-clearing recursion does not diagonalize For a fixed prime $q$, put \[ P_R(q)=\prod_{k=2}^{R-1}(q^k-1)\qquad(R\ge3). \] For every coefficient prime $\ell\ne q$, $v_\ell(P_R(q))\to\infty$. Consequently \[ \bigcap_{R\ge3}P_R(q)\mathbb Z=\{0\},\qquad \bigcap_{R\ge3}P_R(q)\widehat{\mathbb Z} =\{z\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}:z_\ell=0\text{ for all }\ell\ne q\}. \tag{E.34.1} \] Thus the sufficient exponent divisibilities imposed in E.33 cannot be maintained at a fixed nonzero ordinary valuation through unbounded nilpotent depth. Moreover, the abelian outputs of the displayed E.33 construction converge in the global power completion to $(3,-2)$ as $R\to\infty$, for arbitrary choices of its finite moduli $N_R$. This also verifies the exact convergence assertion GT C.2.1 about the displayed SECTIONS A.65 parameters. Neither statement says that the exponent divisibilities are necessary for actual nilpotent survival.

statement: Selected fixed-depth examples have a bounded later first failure For every $R\ge1$ and $N\ge1$, the construction in E.33 can be chosen to give an ordinary infinite-support pair that survives full integral class $R$ with the specified finite Magnus congruence, but whose first empty unrestricted integral section fibre is a finite class $r>R$. For $p\mid n$, put $v=v_p(n)$ and \[ F_p(z)=\exp(E(z)\log z). \] On the shell $z\in1+p^v+p^{v+1}\mathbb Z_p$, its image is exactly \[ F_p(1+p^v)(1+p^{W_p}\mathbb Z_p),\qquad W_p= \begin{cases} 3v+v_p(48)+1,&p\text{ odd},\\ 3v+7,&p=2. \end{cases} \tag{E.64.1} \] For odd $p$ the map is bijective on that shell. At two it is two-to-one; restricting to $z\in1+2^v+2^{v+2}\mathbb Z_2$ makes it bijective onto the same image. Throughout these shells $v_p(E(z))=v_p(D)$. For $p\nmid n$, hence $p\geq5$, on any residue ball with $z\not\equiv0,\pm1\pmod p$, the frozen-Teichmuller map \[ F_{e,p}(z)=\omega^e \exp(24n(z^2-1)\log(z/\omega)) \tag{E.64.2} \] is a bijection onto $\omega^e(1+p\mathbb Z_p)$, where $\omega$ is the fixed Teichmuller lift of that residue. These maps preserve congruences within their input balls. For integer inputs whose exponent is $e$ modulo $p-1$, (E.64.2) is the ordinary integer power $z^{E(z)}$.

statement: The exact full-class-three valuation criterion and original three-prime recursion Suppose an ordinary completed pair has valuation patterns $(0,1)$ at two, $(1,0)$ at three, and at every prime $q>3$ either $(0,0)$ or one of \[ (E_q,0),\quad(0,E_q),\quad(-E_q,-E_q), \qquad E_q=24e_q(q^2-1), \tag{E.65.1} \] where $e_q\geq0$ is an integer and $e_q\to0$ in $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$. Then its distinguished integral class-two class from B.101 lifts to the actual global integral class-three quotient. It is the only class-two class which does. This proves the valuation-locus assertion SECTIONS A.58. Such ordinary infinite-support pairs exist with exactly the original parameters of SECTIONS A.59: \[ n_j=(j+4)!,\quad D_j=48n_j^2,\quad E_j(Q)=24n_j(Q^2-1), \tag{E.65.2} \] \[ A=3\prod_{j\geq0} \frac{q_j^{E_j(q_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}}, \qquad B=-2\prod_{j\geq0} \frac{r_j^{E_j(r_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}}. \tag{E.65.3} \] The three sets of primes are pairwise disjoint and consist of primes greater than three. The resulting class-three section is neither a rational-point image nor a cuspidal image.

statement: The exact four-place weight-three matching map The continuous restriction map \[ \begin{split} H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},\widehat{\mathbb Z}(3))\longrightarrow{}& H^1(G_{\mathbb Q_2},\mathbb Z_7(3)) \oplus H^1(G_{\mathbb Q_3},\mathbb Z_{13}(3))\\ &\oplus H^1(G_{\mathbb Q_3},\mathbb Z_2(3)) \oplus H^1(G_{\mathbb R},\mathbb Z_2(3)) \end{split} \tag{E.80.1} \] is surjective. The four targets have orders $7,13,2,2$. This independently confirms SECTIONS\_OVER\_Q A.60. Consequently, above the distinguished integral class-two section of an ordinary pair whose valuations at two and three are $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$, respectively, any global integral class-three lift can be changed to match the ordinary local point classes at these four indicated places and coefficients. Both central weight-three coordinates can be prescribed independently. No local section theorem is used.

statement: The original exact class-four valuation bound Suppose an ordinary completed pair has valuation patterns $(0,1)$ at two and $(1,0)$ at three, and at every prime $q>3$ either $(0,0)$ or one of \[ (M_q,0),\quad(0,M_q),\quad(-M_q,-M_q),\qquad M_q=24e_q(q^2-1)(q^3-1), \tag{E.81.1} \] where the $e_q$ are nonnegative integers tending to zero in $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$. Its distinguished integral class-two section has a lift to the actual integral class-four arithmetic quotient. This independently confirms the precise constant and assertion of SECTIONS\_OVER\_Q A.61. It does not assert ordinary local matching of this class-four lift at the new support primes.

statement: The exact cubic-exponent ordinary recursion, including initial factorial six Let $24\mid C$, and let $J\geq6$ be at least every prime divisor of $C$. With exactly the parameters \[ n_j=(j+J)!,\qquad D_j=6Cn_j^3,\qquad E_j(Q)=Cn_j(Q^2-1)(Q^3-1), \tag{E.82.1} \] there are disjoint sequences of distinct primes $q_j,r_j,s_j>3$ for which \[ A=3\prod_{j\geq0}\frac{q_j^{E_j(q_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}}, \qquad B=-2\prod_{j\geq0}\frac{r_j^{E_j(r_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}} \tag{E.82.2} \] is ordinary at every finite prime and has infinite support. Its valuation patterns are $(0,1)$ at two, $(1,0)$ at three, and respectively $(E_j(q_j),0),(0,E_j(r_j))$ and $(-E_j(s_j),-E_j(s_j))$ at the new primes. This independently confirms SECTIONS\_OVER\_Q A.62 with its literal $J=6$ option. With $C=24,J=6$, E.81 gives an actual integral class-four section above this pair.

statement: The same ordinary ghost has a global class-four section and no locally matching class-two section There is an output of the exact recursion E.82 with $C=24,J=6$ satisfying \[ (A,B)\bmod8=([3],[-2]),\qquad x_{1129}\equiv828\pmod{1129}. \tag{E.83.1} \] It admits an actual continuous global integral class-four section, and its everywhere locally point-or-cusp-matching integral class-two fibre is empty. In particular its everywhere locally point-or-cusp-matching class-four fibre is empty as well. This confirms the full assertions of SECTIONS\_OVER\_Q A.207 and A.209 for the same completed pair. The exclusion is already seen in the actual geometric order-$32$ quotient of E.70; its order-$128$ predecessor gives the stated class-four exclusion. No assertion that the unrestricted class-two or class-four fibres are empty is made.

statement: Vanishing of the finite-ramification second group at three in every weight Put $G_S=G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}}$. For every integer $w$ and every $n\geq1$, \[ H^2(G_S,\mathbb Z/3^n(w))=0, \qquad H^2_{\rm cts}(G_S,\mathbb Z_3(w))=0. \] In particular, for every $w\geq2$, A.22 specializes to an isomorphism \[ H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_3(w)) \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \frac{c_0(\{q:q\ne3\},\mathbb Z_3)} {\{((q^{w-1}-1)y_q)_q:(y_q)_q\in c_0(\mathbb Z_3)\}}. \] The denominator is the actual image. This absolute group need not vanish; the conclusion concerns its finite-ramification kernel. Consequently, for the ordinary pairs and boundary matching specified in B.25, every boundary-matched pro-$3$ class-$r$ section, $r\geq2$, has a global integral class-$(r+1)$ lift. Such a lift can be chosen boundary matched if and only if the discrepancy tuple satisfies the $H^1$ localization-image condition of B.26. Thus at coefficient three that matching condition is the sole remaining step at every depth.

statement: The exact integral first-cohomology parameters at three For every $w\geq2$, inflation identifies $H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_3(w))$ with $H^1(G_S,\mathbb Z_3(w))$, and as compact $\mathbb Z_3$-modules \[ H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_3(w))\simeq \begin{cases} \mathbb Z/3^{\,1+v_3(w)},&w\text{ even},\\ \mathbb Z_3,&w\text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] For even $w$, put $s_w=1+v_3(w)$. A generator is the integral cyclotomic cocycle \[ \eta_w(g)=\frac{\chi_3(g)^w-1}{3^{s_w}}. \] At each $q\ne3$, its localization is the class of $(q^w-1)/3^{s_w}$ in $\mathbb Z_3/(q^w-1)\mathbb Z_3$ and has exact order $3^{s_w}$. In particular, localization of this global group at any one prime $q\ne3$ is injective. At a weight-$w$ step in B.26, the global matching parameters are therefore exactly $(\mathbb Z/3^{s_w})^{b_w}$ when $w$ is even, and a compact free module $\mathbb Z_3^{b_w}$ when $w$ is odd. At an even step, if there is a support prime different from three, there is at most one boundary-matched global lift class above a given preceding class.

statement: Matching at the coefficient prime three For $w\geq2$, put $H_{3,w}=H^1(G_{\mathbb Q_3},\mathbb Z_3(w))$. This is a compact module of rank one. Its torsion is zero for odd $w$, and is a cyclic group of order $3^{s_w}$, $s_w=1+v_3(w)$, for even $w$. The localization map from the global group in E.67 is an isomorphism onto $H_{3,w}$ for odd $w$, and an isomorphism onto its torsion subgroup for even $w$. Suppose that a global class-$(w-1)$ section agrees, up to geometric conjugacy, with a prescribed local point section at three, and that a global class-$w$ lift exists. For odd $w\geq3$, precisely one global lift class above that preceding class matches this local point at class $w$. For even $w$, such a matching lift exists precisely when the local discrepancy maps to zero in $H_{3,w}^{b_w}/(H_{3,w}^{\rm tors})^{b_w}$; if it exists, it is unique. These assertions concern matching at three. The conditions at the other support primes remain to be checked for that uniquely specified lift.

statement: A finite linear gate across each odd--even pair of layers Let an ordinary pair have support $\Sigma$ containing two and satisfying \[ q\equiv-1\pmod3,\qquad v_3(q^2-1)=1 \quad(q\in\Sigma). \] The pairs of E.125 satisfy these hypotheses. Fix an even integer $w\geq4$ and a global integral pro-three class-$(w-2)$ section $s$ which is boundary matched at every $q\in\Sigma$. Put \[ b=b_{w-1},\qquad c=b_w,\qquad s_w=1+v_3(w),\qquad R_w=\mathbb Z/3^{s_w}, \qquad C_w=R_w^c . \] Once a reference lift and cocycle bases are chosen, there are defined matrices $A_q\in\operatorname{Mat}_{c\times b}(R_w)$ and vectors $v_q\in C_w$, for $q\in\Sigma$, such that a boundary-matched class-$w$ section above $s$ exists if and only if the simultaneous system \[ A_q\lambda=v_q \quad(q\in\Sigma\setminus\{2\}) \tag{E.69.1} \] has a solution $\lambda\in R_w^b$. For a fixed integral choice of the intervening odd-layer parameters, matching at two fixes the unique even-layer global twist. Some set of at most $b+2$ support places, including two, determines this entire matching condition. Thus failure has a witness of that bounded size. For $w=4$ there are exactly nine possible odd-layer parameter classes to test, namely $\lambda\in\mathbb F_3^2$, and at most four support places suffice. The statement does not assert consistency of (E.69.1), an effective stopping rule for locating the controlling places, or that higher digits of the odd parameters are irrelevant to subsequent pairs of layers.

notes: Fixes a matched even predecessor. No consistency assertion, no effective controlling-place finder, and no claim that higher odd digits are irrelevant at later layers.

statement: The complete projected Selmer group and the actual order-thirty-two quotient Put \[ C:y^2=x^5-54x,\quad J=\operatorname{Jac}(C),\quad K=\Q(\theta),\quad\theta^4=54,\quad L=\Q(r),\quad r^2=6,\quad\theta^2=3r. \] The cyclic-eight cover \[ W:\ z^8=-t(1-t)^3/24\longrightarrow U \tag{E.70.1} \] has proper compactification $C$. Its proper mod-two homology produces an actual arithmetic quotient of $E_U$ with geometric group $J[2]\rtimes C_8$, of order $128$ and nilpotency class four. Writing $v$ for the cyclic deck generator and $\delta=v-1$, the characteristic quotient by $\delta^2J[2]$ has geometric group \[ \overline Q=\overline M\rtimes C_8,\qquad \overline M=J[2]/\delta^2J[2] \simeq\operatorname{Res}_{L/\Q}\mu_2, \qquad |\overline Q|=32,\quad\operatorname{cl}(\overline Q)=2. \tag{E.70.2} \] Its continuous cohomology map is the quadratic norm $K^\times/K^{\times2}\to L^\times/L^{\times2}$. If $\mathcal S\subset H^1(G_\Q,\overline M)$ consists of the classes whose localization at every place belongs to the projected Kummer image of $J(\Q_w)/2J(\Q_w)$, then \[ \mathcal S=\langle[-(2+r)],[3+r]\rangle\simeq(\Z/2)^2. \tag{E.70.3} \] These four classes are the images of rational divisor classes. In combined eighth-power class $[-24]$ for $t(1-t)^3$, the everywhere locally point-or-cusp-matching section locus of this order-$32$ arithmetic quotient with ordinary centre in $828+1129\Z_{1129}$ is empty. This independently confirms the finite quotient, projected Selmer calculation, and exclusion in SECTIONS\_OVER\_Q A.209, without assuming its earlier full two-Selmer computation A.186.
check_types: independent re-proof:1; computation or formal certificate:1
notes: Excludes everywhere specified local point matching. Does not assert an empty unrestricted class-two fibre.

statement: An original factorial ghost first fails local matching at class two There is an output of the literal recursion E.102, \[ A=3\prod_j q_j^{(j+4)!},\qquad B=-2\prod_j r_j^{(j+4)!}, \tag{E.71.1} \] whose ordinary localization at $1129$ has centre in $828+1129\Z_{1129}$. Its abelian section is locally a point section everywhere, including the real place. Its everywhere locally point-or-cusp-matching integral class-two fibre is empty, while its unrestricted global class-two fibre has the twenty-four classes of A.27. Thus its first local-matching failure is exactly class two. This confirms GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.2.2 in its stated local-matching scope and does not assign this pair a first unrestricted nilpotent failure.
notes: First local-matching failure is class two; unrestricted class-two sections still exist.

statement: The separating prime gives no local third obstruction For every unrestricted global class-two section above the pair of E.71, its local class-three obstruction at $q=1129$ is zero for every coefficient prime. For each $\ell\ne1129$, that specified local class-two section lifts to a continuous section of the entire geometrically pro-$\ell$ local extension over $\Q_{1129}$. This confirms GT\_TOWER\_CHECK C.2.4. In particular the finite global Selmer exclusion in E.70 is not an unrestricted local third obstruction.
notes: No local third obstruction at1129 for any coefficient prime; full local pro-prime lifting away coefficient1129.

statement: R6 C.3.1: the pointed elliptic cover and the necessary factorization Let $Y\to U$ be the pointed degree-$27$ cover defined by the exponent-three Heisenberg quotient and the section of $t=3$. Its compactification, with the distinguished point above $3$ as origin, is $E':y^2=x^3+9$. Put $E:y^2=x^3-243$, $P_0=(6,15)$, and $T=(0,3)$ on $E'$. The map is \[ E'\xrightarrow{\phi}E\xrightarrow{\iota^{-1}} C:\ 3u^3-2v^3=1\xrightarrow{3u^3}\mathbb P^1, \] where, for $d=3u(u-1)-2v(v-1)$, \[ \phi(x,y)=\left(\frac{x^3+36}{x^2}, \frac{y(x^3-72)}{x^3}\right),\qquad \iota(u,v)=\left(\frac{18(uv-1)}d, -\frac{27(3u(u+1)+2v(v+1))}d\right). \] There are nine punctures above each of $0,1,\infty$. Every full geometrically pro-three section above an original A.44 pair factors, after geometric conjugacy, through the actual geometrically pro-three arithmetic group of this $Y$.
depends_on: A.25–A.27; B.101; isogeny factorization; explicit polynomial identities
notes: The cover comparison preserves the prime three; no full section inferred from a truncated section.

statement: R6 C.3.2: a complete three-isogeny descent With the domain curve in the Selmer notation, \[ \operatorname{Sel}^{\phi}(E'/\mathbb Q)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Sel}^{\psi}(E/\mathbb Q) =\langle6,12\rangle\simeq(\mathbb Z/3)^2. \] Both curves have zero three-primary Tate--Shafarevich group, and \[ E'(\mathbb Q)^{\wedge3} =\mathbb Z_3P_0\oplus(\mathbb Z/3)T. \] In particular, the rank is one. This does not assert that $P_0$ is an integral generator of the entire Mordell--Weil group; it is a generator of its free three-adic completion.

notes: P0 is only asserted to generate the free three-adic completion, not the full integral Mordell-Weil group.

statement: R6 C.3.3 and a stronger localization statement at three The natural maps are isomorphisms \[ E'(\mathbb Q)^{\wedge3} \xrightarrow{\sim}H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},T_3E'), \qquad E'(\mathbb Q)^{\wedge3} \xrightarrow{\sim}E'(\mathbb Q_3)^{\wedge3}. \] The first assertion is absolute continuous cohomology, without a fixed ramification set. The second strengthens the previous audit: the compact global class is detected exactly at the coefficient prime three. Moreover $\phi:E'(\mathbb Q_3)\to E(\mathbb Q_3)$ is surjective.
depends_on: E.111; continuous Kummer sequence; local and global duality
