statement: R6 C.3.4: exact necessary support tests For every original A.44 pair admitting a full geometrically pro-three section, each fresh $A$-support prime $q_j$ and $B$-support prime $r_j$ satisfies \[ 3\nmid\operatorname{ord}_{E'(\mathbb F_{q_j})}(-2,1),\qquad 3\nmid\operatorname{ord}_{E'(\mathbb F_{r_j})}(3,-6). \] These are necessary conditions for all original outputs. They do not assert the existence of a section when the tests pass.
notes: Necessary tests only.

statement: R6 C.3.5: infinitely supported pairs passing the compact tests The original A.44 recursion can be carried out with the additional conditions that $3$ is a noncube modulo every $q_j$ and $2$ is a noncube modulo every $r_j$. Every resulting pair passes all tests of E.113. This confirms the stated compact-test survival theorem; the statement that this proves full pro-three survival is unsupported.

statement: R6 C.3.6--C.3.7: the exact generalized-Jacobian image Write $D=D_0\sqcup D_1\sqcup D_\infty=E'\setminus Y$, $K_i=\Gamma(D_i,\mathcal O)$, and $J=\operatorname{Jac}(E',D)$. The geometric abelianization of $\pi_1(Y)$ is $TJ$, with torus \[ \mathcal T=(\operatorname{Res}_{D/\mathbb Q}\mathbb G_m)/\mathbb G_m, \qquad 1\longrightarrow\mathcal T\longrightarrow J \longrightarrow E'\longrightarrow1. \] The exact image on the original three-primary abelian coordinates is \[ \begin{split} A&=3\left(u_0^a\, \frac{N_{K_0/\mathbb Q}\alpha_0} {N_{K_\infty/\mathbb Q}\alpha_\infty}\right)^3,\\ B&=-2\left(v_0^a\, \frac{N_{K_1/\mathbb Q}\alpha_1} {N_{K_\infty/\mathbb Q}\alpha_\infty}\right)^3, \end{split} \] where $a\in\mathbb Z_3$, $\alpha_i\in(K_i^\times)^{\wedge3}$, $u_0=253/655$, and $v_0=-488/655$. The full profinite affine abelian image contains $(3C^{27},-2D^{27})$ for arbitrary completed $C,D$. At the rational prime two the proper three-primary class has no additional restriction: the three rational sheets over any ordinary point with the required cube classes realize all classes of $E'(\mathbb Q_2)^{\wedge3}=\langle T\rangle$.
depends_on: E.110–E.112; generalized Albanese; rigidified Picard sequence; continuous torus Kummer cohomology
notes: Absolute cohomology and full profinite block-constant torus map retain continuity.

statement: R6 C.3.8 and C.3.10: the boundary norms have no obstruction Each $K_i$ is a field of degree nine. Its normal closure has group $G=H_3\rtimes C_2$, where the involution inverts the two generators of $H_3$ and fixes its center; the point stabilizer is $H\simeq S_3$. For $X=\operatorname{coker}(\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z[G/H])$, \[ H^1(G,X)=H^2(G,X)=0. \] Each boundary field satisfies the Hasse norm principle, its norm-one torus satisfies weak approximation, and \[ N:(K_i\otimes\mathbb Q_3)^\times\longrightarrow\mathbb Q_3^\times \quad\hbox{is surjective}. \] In particular, no additional congruence modulo $27$ is required in the norm-lifting construction.
depends_on: Full H3 semidirect C2 action; four-relator cohomology; local torus duality; Macedo-Newton norm comparison
notes: No extra modulus27 condition is needed; dual weak-approximation quotient wording is explicit.

statement: R6 C.3.9--C.3.10: all compact-test-passing pairs lift to the affine abelian quotient Every original A.44 output satisfying the support tests in E.113 has a full profinite section of $\pi_1(Y)/\overline{[K,K]}$, where $K=\pi_1(Y_{\overline{\mathbb Q}})$, with the prescribed original abelian pair. The proper elliptic component of the constructed section is zero. This includes every pair constructed in E.114. It does not construct a full pro-three section of $Y$.

notes: No nonabelian lift inferred.

statement: R6 C.3.11 and its existential premise C.2.7 There is a recursively specified original A.44 pair in the compact-test-passing family of E.114 whose unrestricted integral class-three section fibre is empty. Every integral class-two section has a nonzero third obstruction at the second $A$-support prime $q_1$, for coefficient prime five, detected modulo $25$. The full profinite affine abelian fibre over this pair is nonempty, whereas the fibre for $\pi_1(Y)/\overline{[[K,K],[K,K]]}$ is empty. This is an exclusion at coefficient prime five; it does not decide whether the same pair has a full pro-three section.

notes: The obstruction is five-primary and cannot itself exclude a pro3 section.

statement: The selected local-fibre exclusion in R6 C.3.1 and C.2.6 Original A.44 primes can also be chosen so that the ordinary local point at $q_0$ has no $\mathbb Q_{q_0}$-rational lift to $Y$. For these selected outputs the unrestricted integral class-three fibre is empty, with the obstruction at coefficient prime three. Consequently no full geometrically pro-three section exists over these outputs. These selected outputs are outside the compact-passing family of E.114.

statement: The exact pro-three question left by the elliptic audit It remains undetermined whether any original A.44 pair constructed in E.114 admits a continuous section of the full geometrically pro-three arithmetic fundamental group of $U$. Equivalently, after E.110, the question is whether some affine abelian class in the exact image of E.115 lifts through every compatible nonabelian quotient of the actual pro-three group of $Y$.
notes: A fixed proper class at Q3 does not imply an ordinary point section of the punctured curve at coefficient prime3.

statement: A new three-primary exclusion inside the compact-passing family Let $\mathscr P$ be the original A.44 family with $3$ a noncube at every $A$-support prime and $2$ a noncube at every $B$-support prime. Let $\mathscr A$ be the entire original A.44 family and $\mathscr A_c$ its compact-test-passing subspace. Every legal finite prefix in any of $\mathscr A,\mathscr A_c,\mathscr P$ has an extension whose geometrically pro-three class-three section fibre is empty. For prefixes in $\mathscr A_c$ or $\mathscr P$, the extension still passes all compact elliptic tests and has the full profinite affine abelian section of E.117. A prefix in $\mathscr P$ extends within $\mathscr P$. More precisely, at a new stage $j$ put $n=n_j$ and $f=v_3(n)$. One can choose its $A$-support prime $q=q_j$ with $e=v_3(q-1)>f$. Among three explicitly related choices for the local $n$th root specifying the subsequent $r_j$ CRT condition, at least two force a nonzero third obstruction modulo $3^{f+1}$ for the unique class-two reduction that can pass the test at two. The other two global pro-three class-two classes already fail at two. Thus examples with a local three-primary obstruction are dense in each of these three spaces. The locally excluded set is also open in the legal-prefix topology; in each space its complement is a closed nowhere dense necessary remainder for full pro-three survival. This proves the density conclusions of R6 C.2.8--C.2.9 by a three-primary argument, without certifying their distinct claim that a coefficient prime at least five may always be used.
depends_on: E.110; E.114; B.20–B.23; original A44 root freedom; local Kummer unit group
notes: Root steering gives residue valuation v3(n_j)<v3(q_j-1), detected modulo3^{v3(n_j)+1}. Remaining closed nowhere dense set is not shown empty.

statement: Exact local matching at three in the affine abelian quotient does not force finite support There are ordinary original A.44 ghosts in $\mathscr P$ with \[ A_{\mathbb Q_3}=\kappa(3),\qquad B_{\mathbb Q_3}=\kappa(-2), \] whose full profinite affine abelian cover fibre has a continuous section with zero proper elliptic class and whose restriction to $G_{\mathbb Q_3}$ is the actual origin point section of $Y\subset E'$, up to geometric conjugacy. Thus exact local matching at the coefficient prime three, even in this full affine abelian quotient, together with the proper rigidity of E.112 and all compact support tests does not imply finite support. Such examples may simultaneously be chosen to have empty pro-three class-three fibre by E.121. This is a counterexample to that proposed rigidity inference, not a full nonabelian ghost section.
depends_on: E.102; E.114–E.117; E.121; three-adic logarithmic root estimate; explicit compatible approximation in norm-one tori
notes: Full profinite affine abelian local matching is proved, not full nonabelian local matching. E123 constructs coefficient-three support matching by a different recursion; original A44 all-support matching remains open.

statement: Ordinary ghosts with all support boundary matches in class two There are pairwise distinct primes $q_j,r_j>3$ and integers $n_j=(j+7)!$ such that \[ A=3\prod_{j\geq0}q_j^{n_j},\qquad B=-2\prod_{j\geq0}r_j^{n_j} \] are an ordinary-local completed unit pair with both coordinates of infinite support, and \[ v_3(q_j^2-1)=1,\qquad v_3(r_j^2-1)=2 \quad(j\geq0). \] The pair has a global integral pro-three class-two section which, at every support place different from three, is the class-two image of the actual local point section. This includes the old support place two. Consequently it has a global integral pro-three class-three section. This is a new recursion, with fixed-root conditions in place of complete radical splitting. It is not an output of the original A.44 recursion, and it does not assert a section at every depth. It proves that the coefficient-three boundary-matching gate of B.24 has a nonempty infinitely supported remainder.
depends_on: E.102; A.27; B.23-B.24; E.66; exact H9 image and cyclic radical intersections; Chebotarev
notes: Uses (j+7)! in both coordinates and fixed-root radical conditions. Fresh support denominators have three-adic valuations1 and2. Parent and cohomology agent independently checked the proof.

statement: Only the even matching layers remain for the modified support pattern Let an ordinary pair have the support pattern constructed in E.123. For $w\geq3$, fix a global integral pro-three class-$(w-1)$ section which agrees with the actual local point section at every support place $q\ne3$, and let $b_w$ be the rank of the weight-$w$ lower central graded piece. A global class-$w$ lift exists by E.66. For its possible local boundary matches the following statements hold. If $w\geq3$ is odd, every such lift is automatically boundary matched at all those support places. If $w=2k$ is even, put $s=1+v_3(k)$. The global twisting group is $(\mathbb Z/3^s)^{b_w}$, and the local twisting groups are \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{support place}&\text{local group}& \text{image of the global group}\\ \hline 2\text{ or }q_j&(\mathbb Z/3^s)^{b_w}& \text{the full group}\\ r_j&(\mathbb Z/3^{s+1})^{b_w}& 3(\mathbb Z/3^{s+1})^{b_w}. \end{array} \] The actual localization homomorphisms include the indicated unit factors. Matching at two fixes the unique possible global twist. It matches everywhere if and only if the discrepancy tuple at every fresh support agrees with that pinned twist. Thus an $A$-support still imposes a compatibility condition; a $B$-support additionally has one local digit outside the global twisting image in each Hall coordinate. In particular, the ghosts of E.123 have boundary-matched class-three sections and global class-four sections. Every odd matched layer can be crossed automatically once its predecessor has been matched. This does not solve the simultaneous even-layer compatibility conditions.
depends_on: E.123; E.66-E.67; B.25-B.26; local tame H1 calculation; lifting-the-exponent identity
notes: Even A places require compatibility with the pinned twist; B places have an additional index-three local image condition. No all-depth section is claimed.

statement: A ghost family with equal global and local even-weight parameters There are pairwise distinct primes $q_j,r_j\notin\{2,3,5,11\}$ and integers $n_j=(j+11)!$ for which \[ A=\frac5{16}\prod_{j\geq0}q_j^{n_j},\qquad B=\frac{11}{16}\prod_{j\geq0}r_j^{n_j} \tag{E.125.1} \] are an ordinary-local completed unit pair with both coordinates of infinite support. Every support prime $p$ satisfies \[ p\equiv-1\pmod3,\qquad v_3(p^2-1)=1. \tag{E.125.2} \] The pair has a boundary-matched integral pro-three class-two section, boundary-matched class-three sections, and global class-four sections. Boundary matching here concerns every nonzero-valuation place; three is not a support place. At every subsequent even layer $w=2k$, above a fixed matched predecessor, the global twisting group and every support-place twisting group are $(\mathbb Z/3^{1+v_3(k)})^{b_w}$, and every localization map is an isomorphism. A global matched lift exists if and only if the local discrepancy vectors, pulled back by these isomorphisms, are all equal. Failure is witnessed by two support places, one of which may always be taken to be two. At every odd layer matching is automatic once the predecessor is matched. No compatible all-depth family is asserted.
depends_on: E.102; E.123-E.124; E.66-E.67; exact rational-coefficient Hensel and fixed-root field compatibility; A.31
notes: Both exponents (j+11)!; supports2,5,11 and fresh primes all -1 mod3 with v3(p^2-1)=1. Simultaneous even discrepancy equality remains unproved.

statement: Full geometric image with the actual higher Galois action Let $\Pi$ be the free geometric pro-three fundamental group of $\mathbb P^1-\{0,1,\infty\}$ at the integral tangential base point $\overrightarrow{01}$. Let \[ \rho:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\Pi) \] be its actual Galois action, put $\mathcal A=\rho(G_{\mathbb Q})$, and let $z_t:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\Pi$ be the point cocycle of $t=5/16$, after choosing a geometric path. Then \[ z_t(\ker\rho)=\Pi, \qquad \{(z_t(g),\rho(g)):g\in G_{\mathbb Q}\} =\Pi\rtimes\mathcal A. \tag{E.126.1} \] In particular every finite quotient retaining the actual arithmetic action has the full geometric image. Prescribing finite geometric Frobenius coordinates is therefore possible above every arithmetic element which occurs, before any additional radical-field intersection conditions are imposed. This statement does not replace the higher arithmetic action by its cyclotomic character. The same finite-quotient conclusion holds for any global integral class-$r$ section whose abelian valuation vectors at five and eleven are $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$, respectively. In particular it applies to every such section above the rational pair $(5/16,11/16)$ or an E.125 ghost. It also holds after adjoining any finite arithmetic data unramified outside three, including the cusp path values.
depends_on: Wojtkowiak2007 Definition2.0 and Theorem2.1; point Kummer inertia at5 and11; compact image and pro3 Frattini argument
notes: Actual based action unramified away3 verified from primary source. The finite-class conclusion also holds for any integral section with independent inertia vectors at5 and11, retaining any actual finite arithmetic cusp data. No infinite prime choice follows.

statement: Finite Frobenius prescriptions and fixed radical roots are compatible Let $L/\mathbb Q$ be a finite Galois extension containing $\mu_3$ such that $L/\mathbb Q(\mu_3)$ is a three-extension and $L^{\rm ab}$ is contained in a cyclotomic field of three-power conductor. Let $h$ and $c$ be radical data from E.123 or E.125, so $24\mid h$, \[ [\mathbb Q(\mu_h,c^{1/h}):\mathbb Q(\mu_h)]=h/2, \qquad \mathbb Q(\mu_h,c^{1/h})^{\rm ab}=\mathbb Q(\mu_h). \] Let $F$ be a cyclotomic field containing $\mu_h$ and $L^{\rm ab}$. Suppose $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(F/\mathbb Q)$ and $g\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q)$ agree on $L\cap F$, and \[ \chi_3(\sigma)\not\equiv1\pmod3, \qquad \sigma(\sqrt c)=\sqrt c. \tag{E.128.1} \] Then there are arbitrarily large primes in the prescribed cyclotomic CRT class whose Frobenius on $L$ is conjugate to $g$ and for which $c$ is an $h$th power in the residue field. Any prescribed finite set of primes can be omitted. In the family of E.125 this applies to arbitrary finite point-section Frobenius conditions supplied by E.126, including the actual finite cusp-one path cocycle as part of the arithmetic data. Thus any fixed finite cusp-zero or cusp-one matching condition can be imposed at the corresponding new prime without losing the radical-root or CRT requirements. This is a finite extension lemma; it asserts no prime satisfying infinitely many conditions.
depends_on: E.123; E.125-E.126; cyclotomic maximal-abelian radical calculation; affine fixed root in cyclic3-power intersection; Chebotarev; Wojtkowiak2007 Prop2.3
notes: Works for finite-class representatives with the rational base pair, not only point sections. It does not impose infinitely many Frobenius conditions. Independently checked by cohomology agent.

statement: Selected boundary-matched ghosts still fail the compact pro-three gate There are ordinary infinite-support pairs with every property of E.123--E.124, including boundary-matched integral pro-three class-two and class-three sections and global class-four sections, which have no full pro-three section. They are obtained by varying the first old root at three within the same valuation shells and prescribing one extra finite Frobenius class at the first $B$-support prime. The extra condition makes \[ P_0-T=(3,-6)\in E'(\mathbb F_{r_0}), \qquad E':Y^2=X^3+9, \] have three-primary order three, while $E'(\mathbb F_{r_0})\{3\}$ has order nine. An exact auxiliary witness for the simultaneous finite conditions is the prime $6551$. This is a witness for a Frobenius class, not a proposed actual recursive support prime. The constructed $r_0$ satisfies all the much larger CRT and radical requirements and may be arbitrarily large. The result excludes selected pairs, not the whole family of E.123 and not the family of E.125.

statement: A dense fourth-layer matching exclusion after every finite prefix Every legal finite prefix of the E.125 recursion has an infinite legal continuation whose distinguished class-two section admits no global integral class-four lift matched to the ordinary local point sections at every support prime. In fact, after imposing the match at two, all nine possible odd-layer parameter classes are excluded at one new $A$-support prime. Every such output still has boundary-matched class-two and class-three sections and global class-four sections, as proved in E.125. It has no full pro-three section. The failure occurs at two support places different from the coefficient prime three; no local point-section condition at three is used. In the topology of legal finite prefixes, the locus with no support-matched fourth-layer lift is open and dense. Its complement is a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, by E.132. More precisely, the consistent prefixes of E.132 have both a matched fourth-layer continuation and a continuation with the failure described here. This describes one matching layer, not an all-depth survival theorem.
notes: Retains matched classes2/3 and globalclass4. Does not impose a point condition at coefficient3. Full independent cohomology-agent second read recorded; no all-depth counterexample claimed.

statement: The compact gate of E.123 is already necessary at the fourth matching layer For an E.123 pair, the existence of a global integral pro-three class-four section matched to the ordinary local point sections at every support prime implies all compact support tests of E.113. More precisely, the $A$-support tests already follow from its class-two matching. If a $B$-support prime $r$ fails its compact test, no global integral class-four lift of the distinguished class-two section can match at both two and $r$. The detecting geometric quotient is the actual marked triangle quotient of order $243$ and nilpotent class four. Its kernel over the pointed $H_3$ quotient is the Galois module $E'[3]$. Consequently the selected outputs of E.129 fail the fourth matching layer, although they possess global class-four sections. No local point-section condition at three is imposed. Passing these compact tests is not asserted to be sufficient for fourth-layer matching.
notes: Does not exclude global class4 lifts. Uses one finite Eprime[3] class and reciprocity, not an assumed Tate-module lift; no local point condition at3.

statement: The finite-field point--cusp question is an integral Frobenius-path test Let $k=\mathbb F_q$, with $q$ prime to three, let $t\in\mathbb P^1(k)\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, and fix a rational tangential section at one of the three cusps. Write $\Pi_3$ for the free geometric pro-three group, $N_r=\Pi_3/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi_3$, and $U_r$ for its rational unipotent completion over $\mathbb Q_3$. Use arithmetic Frobenius $F$, acting relative to the tangential section, and let $z_t$ be the point-section cocycle evaluated at $F$. There is a unique compatible sequence $g_r\in U_r(\mathbb Q_3)$ satisfying \[ z_t=g_r^{-1}F(g_r)\quad\text{in }U_r(\mathbb Q_3). \tag{E.135.1} \] The point and tangential section classes in the full geometrically pro-three arithmetic fundamental group coincide if and only if $g_r\in N_r$ for every $r$. If $q\equiv-1\pmod3$ and all earlier coordinates are integral, a first failure of integrality can only occur at an even weight $2k$. Its exact correction denominator has valuation \[ v_3(q^{2k}-1)=v_3(q^2-1)+v_3(k). \tag{E.135.2} \] The elliptic detector E.192 now proves that this integrality test always fails. If $N$ is the least integer with $3^N>2q+1$, the first failure has weight at most $3N-2$. For $q\equiv-1\pmod3$ it is even, and is therefore at most the largest even integer not exceeding $3N-2$. This local separation does not resolve the main global ghost problem.
depends_on: Integral Hall lattices; central induction; compactness; Saidi–Tamagawa2009 and Wakabayashi2012 scope checks; E.192 for the later quantitative separation

statement: Unbounded degree and genus do not separate the finite-field point and cusp Let $q\equiv-1\pmod3$, and put $m_n=3^n$. The Fermat covers of the tripod with compactifications \[ C_n:\quad X^{m_n}+Y^{m_n}=Z^{m_n}, \qquad C_n\longrightarrow\mathbb P^1, \qquad t=(X/Z)^{m_n} \] have geometric degree $3^{2n}$ and genus $(3^n-1)(3^n-2)/2$. Nevertheless \[ \#C_n(\mathbb F_q)=q+1 \quad\text{for every }n. \] Every interior $t\in U(\mathbb F_q)$ has exactly one compatible rational lift throughout this tower, and each cusp also has one compatible rational lift in the compactifications. Thus increasing the degree and genus of a tower of three-covers while retaining rational lifts of a point and cusp does not itself contradict the Hasse--Weil bounds. This particular tower is the geometric abelian pro-three tower; no nonabelian point--cusp equality is asserted.
depends_on: Power-map bijection on Fq; smooth plane genus formula; finite-field Kummer cohomology
notes: The Fermat tower is geometrically abelian and not cofinal in the full pro3 tower. No full point–cusp section equality claimed.

statement:
The all-prime class-two support gate has a two-place failure witness Let $(A,B)$ be an ordinary completed pair and let \[ \Sigma=\{q:(v_q(A),v_q(B))
e(0,0)\}. \] Fix one global integral class-two section class $s$ above the pair. For each $q\in\Sigma$, let $D_q$ be the difference between its local class and the prescribed ordinary point class, with the sign chosen so that $s+k\eta$ matches precisely when $k\eta|_{G_q}=D_q$. Only coefficient components $\ell
e q$ are included in this comparison. After compatible Tate coordinates are fixed, \[ D_q\in\prod_{\ell
e q}H^1(G_{\mathbb Q_q},\mathbb Z_\ell(2)) \simeq \mathbb Z/(q^2-1). 	ag{E.137.1} \] In particular, only the finitely many primes dividing $q^2-1$ can contribute a local difference. For $q\ge5$, localization of the global twist group is the injection \[ \mathbb Z/24\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/(q^2-1),\qquad k\longmapsto k rac{q^2-1}{24}. 	ag{E.137.2} \] Thus matching at a single support prime $q_0\ge5$ determines at most one of the twenty-four global classes. If $\Sigma$ contains such a prime, the set of global class-two classes matched at every support prime in every off-diagonal coefficient component has at most one member. If this set is empty, at most two support primes already witness its emptiness. No effective bound on the sizes of those primes is asserted. Equivalently, each $D_q$ for $q\ge5$ must lie in the order-$24$ subgroup in (E.137.2), its unique preimages must all agree, and any support conditions at $q=2,3$ must agree with their reductions modulo three and eight, respectively. If these conditions hold, B.25 gives a global integral class-three lift of the unique matched class-two section. This does not assert that the class-three lift remains matched, or that any higher lift exists. Every ordinary full pronilpotent survivor satisfies this gate by A.31. The gate concerns support primes with $q
e\ell$ only. Matching at the coefficient prime and at zero-valuation places has not been deduced from full pronilpotent survival. The existence of an infinite-support ordinary pair passing this all-prime gate remains unresolved in this work.
depends_on: A.25–A.27; A.31; B.25; tame local cohomology
notes: Dq lies in Z/(q²−1); eta maps to (q²−1)/24 for q≥5. No coefficient-prime or zero-support local matching conclusion.

statement: Matching at the support prime five imposes no abelian rigidity Every ordinary completed pair whose support contains five has exactly one global integral class-two section class which matches its prescribed ordinary point at five in every coefficient component different from five. This condition imposes no additional restriction on the abelian pair. In particular there are infinite-support ordinary examples satisfying it, furnished by E.125.
notes: The map Z24→Z/(5²−1) is the identity. No coefficient5 or other-place matching asserted.

statement: The relative Bloch component, its harmonic cancellation, and a nonzero ghost example Let $q\ge5$ be a support prime of an ordinary pair, and let $\ell$ be an odd prime dividing $q+1$. The $\ell$-component of the local difference in E.137 has a natural interpretation \[ D_{q,\ell}\in H^1(G_{\mathbb F_q},\mathbb Z_\ell(2)) \simeq K_3(\mathbb F_q)\{\ell\} \simeq \mathcal B(\mathbb F_q)\{\ell\}, \tag{E.139.1} \] where $\mathcal B$ is Suslin's Bloch group. For $\ell\ge5$ there is no global twist ambiguity. For $\ell=3$, the ambiguity is exactly the order-three subgroup generated by the localization of $\eta$. The resulting quotient class is therefore an invariant of the ordinary completed pair. This is a relative class defined by its global central primitive and the local point comparison; it has not been identified with the single symbol of the point's reduction at a cusp. There are infinite-support ordinary pairs for which this relative Bloch quotient is nonzero. More precisely, a modification of the E.123 recursion has a $B$-support prime $r$ with $v_3(r^2-1)=2$ at which $D_{r,3}$ has order nine for every global integral class-two section. Thus none of the twenty-four global classes matches there, although the prescribed ordinary point reduces to the cusp one. There is also an exact harmonic cancellation for the rational reference point $t=1/2$: for every $\ell\ge5$ and every $q\ne2,\ell$ with $\ell\nmid q-1$, its integral class-two local section equals the unit tangential section at zero. In particular its $q+1$ Bloch component vanishes. This reference point calculation does not assert the same cancellation after its two global Kummer coordinates have been changed to a ghost.
depends_on: E.123; E.128; E.137; A.26; finite-field Chern/Suslin comparison

notes: The Bloch class is relative to the global primitive, not the residue-cusp symbol. New central+1 preserves radical intersections. Harmonic cross-term cancellation is not transferred to a changed pair.

statement: The exact joint image of the point $5/16$ and all actual tangential actions Use the integral unit tangent $\overrightarrow{01}$, and write \[ \rho_\ell:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(F_\ell), \qquad \rho_{\rm all}=\prod_\ell\rho_\ell, \qquad D=\rho_{\rm all}(G_{\mathbb Q}),\quad K=\ker\rho_{\rm all}. \] Let $t=5/16$, and let $z_t:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\prod_\ell F_\ell$ be the point cocycle obtained from any one geometric path. Then \[ \prod_{\ell\ \mathrm{odd}}F_\ell \ \subseteq\ z_t(K)\ \subseteq\ \prod_\ell F_\ell, \tag{E.127.1} \] where the left-hand group has identity two-primary coordinate. Consequently the actual joint homomorphism \[ G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{\ell\ \mathrm{odd}}F_\ell\right)\rtimes D, \qquad g\longmapsto\bigl(z_{t,\mathrm{odd}}(g),\rho_{\rm all}(g)\bigr) \tag{E.127.2} \] is surjective. More precisely, if $H_2=z_t(K)\cap F_2$, then \[ H_2=\Phi(F_2),\qquad z_t(K)=\Phi(F_2)\times\prod_{\ell\ \mathrm{odd}}F_\ell. \tag{E.127.3} \] Here $\Phi(F_2)=\overline{F_2^2[F_2,F_2]}$ is its Frattini subgroup. The two quadratic Kummer characters of $5$ and $11$ descend to a continuous homomorphism $\nu:D\to\mathbb F_2^2$. The image of the full joint map $g\mapsto(z_t(g),\rho_{\rm all}(g))$ is exactly \[ \left\{(w,d)\in\left(\prod_\ell F_\ell\right)\rtimes D: w_2\bmod\Phi(F_2)=\nu(d)\right\}. \tag{E.127.4} \] It has index four in this semidirect product.
notes: Status applies only to the exact numbered statement.

statement: Integral fourth-layer normalization to a fixed rational-point quotient Put \(N_i=\Pi^{(3)}/\Gamma_{i+1}\Pi^{(3)}\), let \(t_0=5/16\), and fix its actual point section \(s_0\). There is a characteristic finite quotient \[ Q=N_4/\overline{N_4^9(\Gamma_3N_4)^3} \quad\text{with}\quad 1\longrightarrow M/3M\longrightarrow Q \longrightarrow H_9\longrightarrow1, \qquad M=\Gamma_3N_4, \tag{E.130.1} \] where \(M\simeq\mathbb Z_3^5\) and \(|Q|=3^{11}\). Here \(N_4^9\) means the closed subgroup generated by ninth powers, and \(H_9\) is the class-two Heisenberg quotient with its three Hall coordinates reduced modulo nine. For every pair in E.125, let \(s_2\) be its distinguished support-matched pro-three class-two section, with the literal reduction \(s_2\bmod9=s_0\bmod9\) supplied there. There is a global integral class-four lift \(t\) of \(s_2\) whose section in \(Q\) equals that of \(s_0\), after geometric conjugacy. This allows the intervening class-three lift to vary; it does not prescribe an arbitrary fixed class-three lift. More precisely, the two global \(M\)-valued cocycles lifting a basis of the odd weight-three parameters can be chosen so that their reductions modulo three are the reductions of two fixed cocycles for the rational point \(s_0\). The finite comparison is therefore uniform over the whole family of E.125.

notes: The intervening class3 lift may vary. The residual finite central cocycle is treated only after literal odd alignment; no arbitrary finite lift or absolute H2 vanishing. Uses only boundary rigidity A.31 proved in this audit, not the attached unrefereed full local theorem.

statement: One fixed finite Galois extension encodes every fourth-layer matching equation There is a fixed finite Galois extension \(L/\mathbb Q\), unramified outside \(\{2,3,5,11\}\), which encodes the complete weight-four system of E.69 for every pair of E.125. It can be defined by the actual rational-point representation in \(Q\), the finite cusp-zero and cusp-one path representations, the two reductions \(j_{0,i}\bmod3\) from E.130, and \(\mu_9\). At two, five, and eleven the constant vectors are zero and the matrices are fixed. At a fresh support prime the matrix and constant vector are functions of these finite Frobenius data. They do not depend on later prime choices or on the remaining ordinary local unit coordinates. Here are exact formulas in the integral Lie coordinates of E.130. Write \(Z_i(g)\in\mathbb F_3^3\) for the central component of \(j_{0,i}(g)\bmod3\), put \[ k_q=\frac{q^4-1}{3}\bmod3\in\mathbb F_3^\times , \qquad Z(g)=\bigl(Z_1(g)\ Z_2(g)\bigr), \tag{E.131.1} \] and use the \(H_9\)-aligned Frobenius representative already prescribed in E.125. At a fresh \(A\)-support use the cusp-zero section; at a fresh \(B\)-support use the cusp-one section. The quotient of the rational-point Frobenius by that cusp Frobenius belongs to \(M/3M\); denote its weight-four component by \(P_{q,4}\). Then the local data in E.69 can be chosen as \[ B_q=k_q^{-1}Z(F_q),\qquad d_q=-k_q^{-1}P_{q,4} \quad(q\text{ fresh}),\qquad d_2=d_5=d_{11}=0 . \tag{E.131.2} \] The exact global matching condition is \[ (B_q-B_2)\lambda=d_q,\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb F_3^2,\quad q\in\Sigma\setminus\{2\}. \tag{E.131.3} \] This is an exact finite-representation description, not an assertion that an explicit defining polynomial for \(L\) or numerical values for all its Frobenius classes have been computed.

statement: A support-matched fourth-layer subfamily and an exact extension criterion for finite prefixes The family of E.125 has an infinite subfamily whose distinguished class-two section lifts to a global integral pro-three class-four section matched to the ordinary local points at every support prime. Every such section has a support-matched class-five lift and a global integral class-six lift. More generally, a legal finite E.125 prefix extends to such a fourth-layer matched pair if and only if the finite system (E.131.3) for its already specified support, including two, five, and eleven, is soluble. Every solubility witness can be retained while all later primes and local roots are chosen. Thus an inconsistent prefix cannot be repaired by a later tail, and every consistent prefix has an infinite continuation satisfying the entire fourth-layer matching condition. Matching here concerns the support primes, all different from the coefficient prime three. It does not assert local matching at three, class-six matching, or a full pro-three section.

statement: The finite odd-Tate embedding theorem and its exact scope Let \(\ell\) be odd and let a finite embedding problem over \(\mathbb Q\) have abelian kernel \[ A=(\mathbb Z/\ell^n(w))^b \] with the indicated actual Galois action. If it is soluble at every completion, it has a global weak solution. Given a global weak solution, any prescribed local solutions at a finite set \(S\) can be attained while retaining that solution at a disjoint finite set \(T\). A proper solution can also be obtained with these prescriptions. Here solutions are considered up to conjugation by the kernel. The theorem fixes the finite lower homomorphism. It supplies neither a specified ramification set outside \(S\cup T\), nor integral Tate-module lifts, nor ordinary point-section behaviour at the newly ramified primes.

statement: An explicit finite correction which has no integral lift Let \(\phi_7\) be the cubic character of \(\mathbb Q(\zeta_7)^+/\mathbb Q\), normalized by \([2]\mapsto1\) in \((\mathbb Z/7)^\times/\{\pm1\}\simeq\mathbb F_3\). Regard it as a class in \(H^1(\mathbb Q,\mathbb F_3(4))\). Its local Frobenius values at two and five are \[ (1,1). \tag{E.141.1} \] No integral class in \(H^1(\mathbb Q,\mathbb Z_3(4))\) has these two reductions. In particular \(\phi_7\) has a nonzero integral coefficient Bockstein, already visible locally at seven.

statement: Which auxiliary primes can change finite and integral central parameters Let \(S\) contain three and infinity. For even \(w\) and \(A=\mathbb Z/3^n(w)\), allowing any additional set \(T\) of primes \(q\equiv-1\pmod3\) changes neither finite first nor finite second cohomology: \[ H^i(G_{\mathbb Q,S},A) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^i(G_{\mathbb Q,S\cup T},A), \qquad i=1,2. \tag{E.142.1} \] For integral coefficients and \(w\ge2\), first cohomology is unchanged by allowing \emph{any} new primes different from three: \[ H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},\mathbb Z_3(w)) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S\cup T},\mathbb Z_3(w)) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^1(\mathbb Q,\mathbb Z_3(w)). \tag{E.142.2} \] The second assertion does not extend to integral second cohomology. In particular auxiliary primes congruent to one modulo three can supply finite corrections such as E.141, without supplying any new integral central parameter.

statement: Ordinary inertia forbids the usual new central ramification at fixed exponent Let \(Q\) be a finite geometric pro-three quotient of exponent \(3^a\), whose abelianization is \((\mathbb Z/3^a)^2\) with the marked peripheral generators. At \(q\ne3\), an ordinary local point section whose abelian inertia is zero has trivial geometric inertia in \(Q\). Consequently a new nontrivial central inertia introduced by a finite embedding solution, while its abelian inertia remains zero, cannot be absorbed by choosing nonzero ordinary integer valuations divisible by \(3^a\). This obstruction occurs already in the marked Heisenberg quotient \(H_3\).

statement: A necessary frozen-support gate for the changing-pair embedding route Let \(F=\Pi^{(3)}\) and use its lower exponent-three central series \[ P_1=F,\qquad P_{n+1}=\overline{P_n^3[P_n,F]} . \] For \(n\ge2\) put \[ Q_{n-1}=F/P_n,\qquad Q_n=F/P_{n+1},\qquad W_n=P_n/P_{n+1},\qquad B_n=\langle x^{3^{n-1}},y^{3^{n-1}}\rangle \ \subset W_n . \tag{E.144.1} \] Then \(B_n\simeq\mathbb F_3(1)^2\). The actual action on \(W_n\) factors through \(\chi_3\bmod3\), and hence \[ W_n/B_n=C_n^+\oplus C_n^-, \qquad C_n^+\simeq\mathbb F_3^{\,a_n},\quad C_n^-\simeq\mathbb F_3(1)^{\,d_n}. \tag{E.144.2} \] Retain the actual action on \(Q_n\) in a finite arithmetic quotient \(D\), unramified outside three. Fix a lower homomorphism \[ \rho:G_{\mathbb Q,S}\longrightarrow Q_{n-1}\rtimes D \] with its prescribed arithmetic projection. Suppose it matches specified ordinary point sections at every old place in \(S\). Any extension of \(\rho\) to \(Q_n\rtimes D\) which retains these old local point conditions, and whose local class at each newly ramified prime is the image of an ordinary point section, must induce a solution \[ \bar\rho:G_{\mathbb Q,S}\longrightarrow (Q_n/B_n)\rtimes D \tag{E.144.3} \] which retains all these old local point conditions. This necessity is unchanged if arbitrarily many new primes are allowed, including primes congruent to one modulo three. For \(S=\{3,\infty,q_1,\ldots,q_t\}\), with all \(q_i\equiv-1\pmod3\), the quotient embedding in (E.144.3) has an unramified global weak solution. Its old local matching is an exact finite first-cohomology localization problem for \(C_n^+\oplus C_n^-\). More explicitly, \[ \begin{split} H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S},\mathbb F_3) &=\mathbb F_3\cdot\bar\eta_4,\\ H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S},\mathbb F_3(1)) &=\langle\kappa(3),\kappa(q_1),\ldots, \kappa(q_t)\rangle . \end{split} \tag{E.144.4} \] For each choice of old local aligning frames, comparison with one global weak solution gives a finite linear system in these stated parameters. Allowing all finite aligning frames gives the precise quotient matching condition. No sufficiency for a full ordinary \(Q_n\)-extension, or for an infinite tower, is asserted.

statement: The free three-adic Galois group and the relations created by frozen support Put \(K=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3)\). The maximal pro-three quotient of \(G_{K,\{3\}}\) is free pro-three of rank two. If \(t\) rational primes \(q_i\) with \[ q_i\equiv-1\pmod3,\qquad v_3(q_i^2-1)=1 \] are added to the ramification set, its maximal pro-three quotient \(P_S\) instead satisfies \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_3}H^1(P_S,\mathbb F_3)=t+2, \qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_3}H^2(P_S,\mathbb F_3)=t . \tag{E.145.1} \] In particular it is not free when any such ordinary support prime has been frozen. The new second-cohomology classes are detected by the explicit cups \(\kappa(\zeta_3)\cup\kappa(q_i)\). Thus projectivity at the coefficient prime alone cannot be applied to the Galois group which retains this old support.

statement: The quotient gate is sufficient for one finite step Use the groups \(Q_{n-1},Q_n,B_n\) of E.144, with \(n\ge2\). Let \[ S=\{3,\infty,q_1,\ldots,q_t\},\qquad q_i\equiv-1\pmod3, \] and include five and eleven among the \(q_i\). Fix a lower homomorphism \(\rho\) and actual ordinary point classes at all the old places, as in E.144. Assume its inertias at five and eleven are, respectively, nonzero multiples of the two marked generators in the Frattini quotient \(F/P_2\). Keep the actual arithmetic projection fixed. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item There is a lift to \((Q_n/B_n)\rtimes D\), unramified outside \(S\), matching all the specified old point classes. \item There is a lift to \(Q_n\rtimes D\), unramified outside \(S\) and a finite set of new primes, which matches those same old point classes and is the image of an ordinary point at every new prime. \end{enumerate} When (i) holds, at most two new primes are needed. They can be chosen outside any prescribed finite set and satisfy \[ q\equiv2\pmod9. \tag{E.146.1} \] At each new prime the point may be taken to be \(q^m\) or \(1-q^m\), with \[ m\in\{3^{\,n-1},\,2\cdot3^{\,n-1}\}. \tag{E.146.2} \] Arbitrarily many additional pairs of such new primes may also be introduced without changing any old point class. Thus the actual ordinary integer valuations at old support remain frozen as externally specified point data, and every new valuation can be fixed as a positive ordinary integer when it is introduced. The finite quotient itself detects those valuations only modulo \(3^n\). Matching the specified actual point at three is an additional requirement of this construction; it is not forced by boundary rigidity A.31 or by ordinary pro-three abelianization. The statement is one finite step. It does not assert that a choice satisfying the next quotient gate can always be retained at every later level, or that the resulting finite abelianization is the reduction of one completed pair ordinary at every zero-support place. There is also a version with no point condition at three. In that version the quotient gate remains equivalent to the next-step condition, and no new prime is needed to lift while matching the old support. Moreover the minus-character part of the quotient matching gate is automatically soluble. Only its plus-character Frobenius conditions remain: in each plus coordinate the old local discrepancies must be restrictions of one global cubic character. New support can still be introduced if desired.

statement: An exact finite everywhere-ordinary extension criterion Use \(Q_{n-1},Q_n,B_n\) and the Frattini hypothesis at five and eleven from E.146. Suppose the old set \(S\) contains \(2,3,5,11,\infty\), with every finite prime other than three congruent to minus one modulo three. Fix actual point targets at the old places other than three. At three fix an ordinary point \(t_3\), and assume that its abelianization modulo \(3^{n-1}\) agrees with the given lower homomorphism. Put \[ M=|Q_n|,\qquad H=(4M+3)^2,\qquad T=\{p\notin S:p\text{ prime},\ p\le H\}. \tag{E.147.1} \] At each \(p\in T\), choose a good-reduction point target, or allow a choice among such targets. Only its reduction in \(\mathbb F_p\setminus\{0,1\}\) matters. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item The fixed lower homomorphism has a lift to \((Q_n/B_n)\rtimes D\), unramified outside \(S\), matching the old point targets away from three and the chosen good-reduction targets at \(T\). \item It has a lift to \(Q_n\rtimes D\), with the same old and \(T\)-point matches, whose abelianization at three equals that of \(t_3\) modulo \(3^n\), and whose local class is an actual point image at every prime different from three. The lift is unramified outside \(S\) and at most three new primes, all greater than \(H\), all congruent to two modulo nine. \end{enumerate} The new primes may avoid any additional prescribed finite set. Their valuation patterns can be chosen among \[ (m,0),\qquad (0,m),\qquad (-m,-m), \qquad m\in\{3^{n-1},2\cdot3^{n-1}\}. \tag{E.147.2} \] In particular the finite abelianization is locally the reduction of an ordinary pair at every place. If a full point match at three is required instead, the same equivalence holds after adding that point condition to (i). As in E.146, actual integer valuations are prescribed external data; the finite quotient detects them only modulo \(3^n\). No compatible infinite choice of the quotient lifts, or one completed global ordinary pair, is asserted.

statement: Only the old-support plus equations remain in the finite ordinary extension route Let \(n\ge2\), and retain the hypotheses on \(S\), the actual arithmetic action, and the five/eleven Frattini inertia vectors from E.147. Call the following data admissible at level \(n-1\): \begin{itemize} \item a literal global homomorphism in \(Q_{n-1}\), unramified outside \(S\); \item specified actual point matches at every old place other than three, and the ordinary abelian class of a fixed point \(t_3\) at three; \item at every finite \(p\notin S\), a lower abelian class represented by an ordinary good-reduction point, so both ordinary valuations are zero. \end{itemize} All abelian classes in these data are taken modulo \(3^{n-1}\). The last requirement is a finite test at each fixed level, by the bound below. For such data, there is an admissible extension at level \(n\), with the same literal predecessor and the same old point data, if and only if the quotient \(Q_n/B_n\) has a global lift unramified outside \(S\) matching the old point classes away from three. When this condition holds, the extension can introduce two or three fresh primes, all congruent to two modulo nine and outside any prescribed finite set. It freezes at each new prime one of the ordinary integer patterns in (E.147.2). The new primes may all be taken greater than \[ H_{\rm ab}(n)=(3^{2n}+3)^2 . \tag{E.148.1} \] At every remaining zero-support prime, the new abelian class still has a good-reduction ordinary representative. No actual higher point match at those zero-support places or at three is required. The quotient condition itself has only the following finite obstruction. Write \[ W_n/B_n=C_n^+\oplus C_n^-, \qquad C_n^+\simeq\mathbb F_3^{a_n}. \] Choose any global weak quotient lift and, at each old place, an aligning element in the finite lower geometric group. Let \(\Delta_q^+\in\mathbb F_3^{a_n}\) be the plus part of the aligned local point discrepancy, evaluated on Frobenius. For at least one of the finitely many aligning-frame choices, there must exist \(z\in\mathbb F_3^{a_n}\) such that \[ \Delta_q^+=k_qz\quad(q\in S,\ q\ne3,\infty), \qquad k_q=\frac{q^4-1}{3}\pmod3. \tag{E.148.2} \] This is necessary and sufficient. Since \(k_5=1\), it can equivalently be written \[ \Delta_q^+=k_q\Delta_5^+. \tag{E.148.3} \] The minus-character equations, coefficient-three ordinary abelian digits, and all zero-support ordinary abelian conditions impose no additional obstruction to this one step. If these finite systems can be passed indefinitely, the construction gives one continuous full pro-three section with an infinite-support three-primary Kummer pair whose local class at every place comes from an ordinary point. This implication is conditional: no assertion is made that the successive systems have a compatible infinite solution. Nor does a three-primary construction by itself supply compatibility with the other coefficient primes in the ordinary pair. E.151 supplies a separate arithmetic refinement retaining that full ordinary compatibility, still conditional on an actual infinite path. Neither result constructs sections at the other coefficient primes required by the full pronilpotent question.

statement: The finite ordinary extension gate can genuinely fail There are admissible level-one data of E.148 with lower homomorphism equal to the actual point-\(5/16\) section in \[ Q_1=F/P_2\simeq\mathbb F_3(1)^2 \] for which no next-level ordinary extension exists, even if arbitrarily many additional primes of any congruence class are allowed. One may take the old finite support to be \(\{2,5,11,q\}\), where \[ q\equiv2\pmod9, \] so all old support primes have \(v_3(p^2-1)=1\). At two, five, and eleven the point target is the original \(5/16\); at \(q\) it is \(1-q^m\), with any specified positive integer \(m\) divisible by three. The point at three may be fixed to \(5/16\) at the abelian level. The obstruction is already the plus Frobenius equation at the two old places five and \(q\). The same failed finite data can be realized by an actual ordinary completed pair of infinite support, by changing one central Frobenius prescription in E.125. This proves failure for specific frozen predecessors; it does not prove that every possible infinite extension path must eventually fail.

statement: Distinct finite-field points with the same full pro-\(3\) section Let \(U=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\) over \(K=\mathbb F_q\), where \(3\nmid q\), and let \(F=\pi_1(U_{\overline K})^{(3)}\). Set \(e=\operatorname{ord}_{\mathbb F_3^\times}(q)\in\{1,2\}\). If \(L=\mathbb F_{q^d}\) and \(\gcd(d,3e)=1\), then the full geometrically pro-\(3\) sections associated to any two points in one \(\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\)-orbit in \(U(L)\) are conjugate by an element of \(F\). The geometric group \(F\) is fixed; only the arithmetic base field is extended. In particular, both of the following are explicit failures of injectivity: \begin{enumerate} \item Let \(K=\mathbb F_{25}\) and \(L=\mathbb F_5[\alpha]/(\alpha^4+2)=\mathbb F_{625}\). The distinct points \(\alpha,-\alpha\in U(L)\) have the same full pro-\(3\) section class. \item Let \(K=\mathbb F_5\) and \(L=\mathbb F_5[\beta]/(\beta^5-\beta-1)=\mathbb F_{3125}\). The five distinct points \(\beta+i\), \(i\in\mathbb F_5\), have the same full pro-\(3\) section class. Here \(\#L\equiv-1\pmod3\). \end{enumerate} These examples disprove a general fixed-pro-\(3\) interior-point separation assertion, including one restricted to finite fields of cardinality \(-1\pmod3\). They do not identify an interior point section with a tangential section, give an example over a prime field, or settle the gate in E.135 or the ordinary completed-pair question over \(\mathbb Q\).

statement: The finite plus gate can retain ordinary compatibility at every coefficient prime We strengthen the conditional construction in E.148; the existence of an infinite path through its finite plus equations remains undecided. Put \[ T_n=\frac{(n+11)!}{3^{v_3((n+11)!)}},\qquad M_n=3^{n-1}T_n,\qquad B(m)=(m+1)^4\quad(n\ge2). \tag{E.151.1} \] Thus \(M_n\mid M_{n+1}\), \(v_3(M_n)=n-1\), and \(M_n\) tends to zero in \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}\). At level \(n-1\) retain a literal section in \(Q_{n-1}\), unramified outside \(S\), and positive, pairwise coprime integers \[ a=5U^8,\qquad b=11V^8,\qquad c=16W^8, \qquad (UVW,2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot11)=1. \tag{E.151.2} \] The prime factors of \(UVW\) are distinct support primes congruent to two modulo nine; the three supports are disjoint. We require the following finite-stage invariants: \begin{enumerate} \item the abelianization of the section is \((\kappa(a/c),\kappa(b/c))\) modulo \(3^{n-1}\); \item at each support prime it agrees with the actual ordinary point class having the prescribed integer valuation pattern, and at three its abelianization agrees with the fixed point \(t_3=5/16\); \item the curve \(aX^{M_n}+bY^{M_n}=cZ^{M_n}\) has a unit-coordinate point over every finite \(\mathbb Q_p\); \item with \(H_n(p)=2v_p(M_{n+1})+n+3\), \[ v_p(a+b-c)\ge H_n(p)\qquad(p\le B(M_n)). \tag{E.151.3} \] \end{enumerate} Here \(S\) consists of three, infinity, and the support primes; in particular two, five, and eleven belong to \(S\). The rational-point section and \((a,b,c)=(5,11,16)\) initialize these invariants at \(n=2\). For these data the next stage exists if and only if the quotient \(Q_n/B_n\) has a global lift over \(G_{\mathbb Q,S}\) matching the old support point classes. Equivalently, for one of the finite aligning-frame choices it satisfies the plus equations (E.148.2). If it exists, we can obtain it by introducing between nine and twenty-one new primes, all two modulo nine and arbitrarily large, and by multiplying each of \(a,b,c\) by a product of their \(M_n\)-th powers. The ordinary integer valuation at each newly introduced prime is frozen thereafter. If this construction has an infinite path, its limits give one ordinary completed pair in \(\widehat{\mathbb Q^\times}^{,2}\) of infinite support, together with one continuous full geometrically pro-three section above its three-primary projection. Thus the remaining condition for this construction is the compatible infinite solution of the old-support plus equations; compatibility with the other coefficient primes in the ordinary pair introduces no extra finite-step condition. This is not a construction of an infinite path, nor of sections in the other pro-prime components.

statement: Finite relative class-two approximation using only ordinary new inertia Retain E.152. Given arbitrary local classes in \(H^1(\mathbb Q_v,V_b)\) for \(v\in S\), they are the restrictions of a global class in \(H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S\cup T},V_b)\) for some finite set \(T\) of arbitrarily large primes \(q\not\equiv\pm1\pmod\ell\). Under (E.152.3), require in addition that every prime of \(T\) have Frobenius class \([\sigma]\) in \(D\). This remains possible whenever the first coordinates of the prescribed local classes are the localizations of one global class \[ a_0\in H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S},R(1)). \tag{E.153.1} \] More generally the exact obstruction is the sum of local Tate pairings with the characters in (E.152.4). In symmetric Heisenberg coordinates, these global classes are actual finite class-two sections with the fixed second Kummer cocycle \(b\). At each newly ramified prime \(q\in T\), their local section class is the image of an ordinary point \(t_q=q^{m_q}\), for some positive integer \(m_q\). Thus no new coefficient-\(\ell\) support-matching condition is introduced at these primes. This is a finite-coefficient relative approximation result; it does not by itself produce integral class-two lifts, a compatible coefficient sequence, or an ordinary completed pair.

statement: Arithmetic compatibility criterion and removal of the special coefficient-five collision In the prescribed-arithmetic version of E.153, condition \(D\cap K_b=K\) is automatic whenever \(D\) contains \(K\) and the commutator subgroup of \(\operatorname{Gal}(D/\mathbb Q)\) has order prime to \(\ell\). Thus one can retain finite arithmetic data with geometric groups at coefficient primes other than \(\ell\), together with cyclotomic congruences, provided an arithmetic element \(\sigma\) satisfying all those data and \(\chi_\ell(\sigma)\not\equiv\pm1\pmod\ell\) actually exists. The assertion is a compatibility criterion; it does not discard this last existence requirement. For the reference pair \((5/16,11/16)\), preserving its quadratic first coordinate at a fresh \(B\)-support prime forces \((5/q)=1\), and hence \(q\equiv\pm1\pmod5\). Thus this particular reference pair cannot use the nonexceptional coefficient-five auxiliary primes of E.153 under that preservation condition. The rational base \[ t=23/64,\qquad 1-t=41/64 \tag{E.154.1} \] removes this specific collision. Its support primes \(2,23,41\) are all minus one modulo three; inertia at the last two primes gives a Frattini basis at coefficient three. The ordinary recursion of E.151 applies, replacing its factorial offset eleven by forty-one, with coefficient forms \[ a=23U^8, \qquad b=41V^8, \qquad c=64W^8. \tag{E.154.2} \] Its complementary squareclasses are \(41,23,-943\). These quadratic characters impose no restriction on \(q\bmod5\). At coefficients \(23\) and \(41\), a required square residue class can still be chosen different from \(\pm1\). Therefore the identified coefficient-five quadratic obstruction is not intrinsic to the ordinary-pair problem. Neither this replacement nor E.153 establishes a simultaneous all-coefficient class-two matched construction.

statement: All dyadic weights and the exact real obstruction Put \(S_2=\{2,\infty\}\). For every integer \(w\) and every \(n\geq1\), restriction is an isomorphism \[ H^2(G_{\mathbb Q,S_2},\mathbb Z/2^n(w)) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^2(G_{\mathbb R},\mathbb Z/2^n(w)). \tag{E.155.1} \] Both finite groups have order two. With continuous integral coefficients, \[ H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q,S_2},\mathbb Z_2(w)) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^2(G_{\mathbb R},\mathbb Z_2(w)) = \begin{cases} \mathbb Z/2,&w\text{ even},\\ 0,&w\text{ odd}. \end{cases} \tag{E.155.2} \] For \(w\geq2\) and any finite \(S\supset S_2\), real restriction and the actual tame residues give an isomorphism \[ H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q,S},\mathbb Z_2(w)) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^2(G_{\mathbb R},\mathbb Z_2(w)) \oplus\! \bigoplus_{q\in S\setminus S_2} \mathbb Z_2/(q^{w-1}-1). \tag{E.155.3} \] In particular A.22 gives the canonical absolute description \[ \begin{split} H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_2(w)) &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^2(G_{\mathbb R},\mathbb Z_2(w))\oplus R_2/d_wR_2,\\ R_2&=c_0(\{q:q\ne2\},\mathbb Z_2),\qquad d_w(y)_q=(q^{w-1}-1)y_q . \end{split} \tag{E.155.4} \] The denominator is the actual image, so (E.155.4) retains the possible non-Hausdorff and derived-limit contribution. Consequently a pro-two class-\(r\) section satisfying the ordinary boundary matching hypothesis of B.25 has a global integral class-\((r+1)\) lift if and only if its real restriction has such a lift. statement: The actual real pro-two section classes of the tripod The geometrically pro-two arithmetic fundamental group of \(U_{\mathbb R}=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb R}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\) is \[ E^{(2)}_{U_{\mathbb R}}\simeq C_2\amalg_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2} C_2\amalg_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2}C_2. \tag{E.157.1} \] Its geometric kernel is free pro-two of rank two, and its three geometric-conjugacy classes of sections are precisely the ordinary real point classes of the intervals \((-\infty,0)\), \((0,1)\), and \((1,\infty)\). statement: The dyadic localization map on the ordinary support pattern Put \[ \Sigma=\{2,23,41\}\cup\mathcal T,\qquad \mathcal T\subset\{q\text{ prime}:q\equiv5\pmod8\}. \tag{E.158.1} \] Fix compatible Tate bases. statement: An exact finite parameter test for every dyadic matching step Let a fixed ordinary completed pair have support E.158.1. Suppose an integral global \(N_{w-1}\)-section is matched to its ordinary boundary point at every odd support place and to its ordinary real class. It has an integral global \(N_w\)-lift \(s_w\). Fix such a lift. At each odd support place let \(\delta_q\in H^1(\mathbb Q_q,L_w)\) be the correction needed to match the ordinary point lift. These classes are independent of the lower aligning frame. At the real place choose one aligning frame and let \(\xi_\infty\in H^1(\mathbb R,L_w)\) be its correction. statement: An ordinary arithmetic advance avoiding every previously treated residue Fix the point \(t_*=23/64\), its actual class-two quotient with Hall coordinates modulo \(2^8\), and its actual class-two quotient modulo nine. Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of primes at least five. Suppose \[ a=23U^8,\quad b=41V^8,\quad c=64W^8 \tag{E.172.1} \] are positive and pairwise coprime, with disjoint new supports, all of whose primes are five modulo eight and two modulo nine. The private primes and three are excluded from \(UVW\). Let \(M\) be divisible by \(43!\) and every prime in \(\mathcal P\). Assume the exponent-\(M\) diagonal curve has unit-coordinate points over every finite completion, and \[ v_p(a+b-c)\ge2v_p(M)+R \quad(p\le B(M)),\qquad B(m)=(m+1)^4,\quad R\ge10. \tag{E.172.2} \] Suppose the two fixed finite sections have the global abelian reductions of \((a/c,b/c)\) and match its support point classes away from their coefficient primes. These classes are independent of the unit-coordinate point chosen on the curve: the integer valuations are fixed, and \(M\) kills the relevant two- and three-primary local unit groups. For any multiple \(h\) of \(M\), any \(R'\ge10\), and any additional prime \(\lambda\ge5\), there is an advance \[ a'=aP_a^M,\qquad b'=bP_b^M,\qquad c'=cP_c^M \tag{E.172.3} \] using between eighteen and thirty distinct new primes. They may avoid any finite set and may all satisfy \[ q\equiv5\pmod8,\qquad q\equiv2\pmod9, \qquad q\not\equiv\pm1\pmod r \quad(r\in\mathcal P\cup\{\lambda\}). \tag{E.172.4} \] The new exponent-\(h\) curve has unit-coordinate points everywhere, and (E.172.2) holds for \((a',b',c',h,R')\). The same two finite global sections still match every support place, including the newly introduced ones. All retained finite abelian reductions whose moduli divide \(M\) are unchanged.

statement: A coefficient can be installed once without disturbing the ordinary prefix Retain an arithmetic prefix of E.172, and let \(\ell\ge5\) be a prime not yet in \(\mathcal P\). Let \(\Sigma_0\) be its finite support. Set \(e,u\) as in (E.171.1) for \(\Sigma_0\), excluding \(q=\ell\), and choose \[ N\ge\max(1,e+u),\qquad v_\ell(M)\ge N. \tag{E.173.1} \] There is an \(A\)-only update \[ a'=a\prod_{q\in T}q^{m_q},\qquad b'=b,\quad c'=c, \tag{E.173.2} \] with finite new support \(T\), positive integer exponents, and a finite class-two section \(s_\ell\) modulo \(\ell^N\) with the following properties. It has abelianization \((a'/c,b/c)\), is unramified outside \(\{\ell,\infty\}\cup\Sigma_0\cup T\), and matches the ordinary support points away from \(\ell\). Every new prime satisfies (E.172.4) with \(\lambda=\ell\). The exponent-\(M\) unit curves, the sum-error bound, and both fixed small-coefficient sections remain valid. Every \(m_q\) may be required to be divisible by any prescribed integer prime to \(\ell\), in particular the prime-to-\(\ell\) part of \(M\) and all previously retained coefficient moduli. No retained \(\ell\)-section is being refined: this operation is used only once for a previously untreated coefficient. Its new exponents need not be globally divisible by \(\ell^N\). The diagonal-curve invariant is preserved by local power conditions at old places and a complementary root at new places.

statement: An infinite-support ordinary pair with all-prime class-two support matching There exists an ordinary completed pair \[ (A,B)\in\widehat{\mathbb Q^\times}^{\,2} \tag{E.174.1} \] with infinite support and one integral all-prime class-two section whose restriction, at every support prime \(q\), is the actual ordinary local point class in every coefficient \(\ell\ne q\). In particular this pair has a global integral class-three lift. The support can be required to contain \(2,23,41\), with their valuation pairs respectively \[ (-6,-6),\qquad(1,0),\qquad(0,1), \tag{E.174.2} \] and every other support prime is five modulo eight and two modulo nine. At every support prime the two valuations are fixed ordinary integers, never subsequently changed. The pair is not the image of a rational point, because its support is infinite. This theorem supplies no point matching at coefficient-prime places or at zero-support places, and supplies no class-three point matching or full pronilpotent lift. It establishes nonemptiness of the earlier all-coefficient support-matched class-two gate E.137.
notes: Every ordinary integer valuation freezes; each coefficient is repaired once; full-completion tail divisibility and actual p-adic sum convergence are proved. No coefficient-prime, zero-support, or class-three matching asserted.

statement: Finite fixed-component recognition and finite fusion Let \(X\) be a connected aspherical smooth manifold of real dimension \(d\), with a smooth action of a finite group \(C\). Suppose that \(P=\pi_1(X,x)\) is finitely generated and is an iterated extension of finitely generated free groups of rank at least two. Let \(H=C_2^2\leq C\), and choose \(x\in X^H\). Let \[ 1\longrightarrow P\longrightarrow E =\pi_1^{\rm orb}([X/C],x)\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow1 \tag{E.176.1} \] be the actual path extension; the fixed point gives its named subgroup \(H\). For every finite quotient \(q:E\to Q\), after joining the label map to \(C\), there is a finite-index subgroup \(V\leq P\), characteristic in \(P\) and contained in \(\ker q\), such that \[ \operatorname{im}\bigl(C_{E/V}(H)\longrightarrow Q\bigr) =q(C_E(H)). \tag{E.176.2} \] There is such a refinement with the following additional property. Choose one point \(x_j\) in each component of \(X^H\), and paths \(\gamma_j:x\to x_j\). They give actual subgroups \[ s_j(h)=\bigl(h,\gamma_j*(h\gamma_j)^{-1}\bigr)\in E. \tag{E.176.3} \] Every homomorphism \(\iota:H\to E/V\) whose composite to \(C\) is the named inclusion has, in \(Q\), the form \[ \operatorname{pr}_Q\iota(h) =q(p)\,q(s_j(h))\,q(p)^{-1} \qquad(h\in H) \tag{E.176.4} \] for some \(p\in P\) and some component \(j\). The same refinement works for every such \(\iota\). Only finitely many components will be used in E.177.

statement: Conditional irreducibility and infinite ramification of the three cusp-specific detectors Let \((A,B)\) be an ordinary completed pair of infinite valuation support. Suppose that a full geometrically pro-three section over \(\mathbb Q\) has its three-primary abelianization. The three pullbacks of the elliptic family E.192.2 described below give continuous representations \[ \rho_c:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow \operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb Z_3), \qquad c\in\{0,1,\infty\}. \tag{E.200.1} \] Each \(\rho_c\) is ramified at infinitely many finite primes. At least two of these representations are absolutely irreducible. More precisely, \(\rho_c\) is absolutely irreducible whenever the ordinary support contains, away from three, both a prime in direction \(c\) and a prime in one of the other two directions. These are necessary conditions on a putative full section. They do not assert that such a section exists, and they do not exclude it. In particular the detector does not turn the global problem into a finite-ramification problem.

statement: The pro-two comparison and the one-prime free product Let \(S=\{2,\infty,q_1,\ldots,q_t\}\), where the \(q_i\) are distinct odd primes. Write \(G_S\) for the full Galois group unramified outside \(S\), and \(G_S(2)\) for its maximal pro-two quotient. Inflation and local restriction give isomorphisms \[ H^2(G_S(2),\mathbb F_2) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^2(G_S,\mathbb F_2) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^2(\mathbb R,\mathbb F_2) \oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^t H^2(\mathbb Q_{q_i},\mathbb F_2). \tag{E.185.1} \] Each summand on the right has order two. There is a minimal pro-two presentation with generators \(c,a,x_1,\ldots,x_t\) and defining relations \[ c^2=1,\qquad y_i x_i y_i^{-1}=x_i^{q_i}\quad(1\leq i\leq t). \tag{E.185.2} \] Here \(c\) maps to complex conjugation, \(x_i\) to a chosen generator of tame inertia at \(q_i\), and \(y_i\) is a word mapping to an actual arithmetic Frobenius at that same prime. The generator \(a\) can be chosen dual modulo the Frattini subgroup to \(\kappa_2(2)\), with its other Kummer coordinates zero. The words \(y_i\) are not independent generators. For \(t=0\), the group is \(C_2\amalg_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2}\mathbb Z_2\). For \(t=1\) and \(q_1\equiv3\) or \(5\pmod8\), one may replace \(a\) by the actual Frobenius at \(q_1\), obtaining \[ G_{\{2,q_1,\infty\}}(2) \simeq C_2\amalg_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2} \bigl(\mathbb Z_2\rtimes_{q_1}\mathbb Z_2\bigr) = C_2\amalg_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2}G_{\mathbb Q_{q_1}}(2). \tag{E.185.3} \] The two indicated factors are the actual real and chosen local decomposition groups. This result is an arithmetic presentation, not a simultaneous local section approximation theorem.

statement: The sharp one-prime limit on an untwisted arithmetic splitting Let \[ G=G_{\mathbb Q}(2),\qquad \Gamma=G_{\mathbb Q,\{2,\infty\}}(2),\qquad \pi:G\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma. \] Fix an actual complex conjugation \(c\in G\), and write \(\bar c=\pi(c)\). Suppose \(s:\Gamma\to G\) is a continuous splitting with \(s(\bar c)=c\). For an odd prime \(q\), let \(f_q\) be an arithmetic Frobenius in the unramified local decomposition group of \(\Gamma\). Call \(q\) compatible with \(s\) if \(s(f_q)\), up to conjugacy in \(G\), is an actual local Frobenius lift at \(q\). At most one odd prime is compatible with \(s\), and any such prime satisfies \(q\equiv3\) or \(5\pmod8\). Conversely, for any one prime in those two residue classes, there exists such a splitting compatible with it. Thus the bound is sharp. In particular no single real-preserving splitting of \(\pi\) simultaneously identifies two odd local Frobenius subgroups with their actual arithmetic lifts. This excludes that way of removing the path twists in an arithmetic free-inertia construction. It does not exclude an equivariant map that retains those twists, and is not a finite-support theorem for ordinary section pairs.

notes: Exact obstruction to simultaneously removing arithmetic path twists by a single real-preserving splitting. Does not exclude twisted equivariant maps or prove ordinary finite support.

statement: The exact compact-catalog criterion, and its missing nonemptiness input For every rational prime \(p\), fix a nonempty finite set \[ \mathcal V_p\subset \{(0,0)\}\cup \{(e,0),(0,e),(-e,-e):e\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\}. \tag{E.187.1} \] Assume the following uniform divisibility condition: for every positive integer \(d\), all entries of every pair in \(\mathcal V_p\) are divisible by \(d\) for all but finitely many \(p\). Also choose finitely many allowed real sign pairs from \((+,+),(+,-),(-,+)\). These data define a compact catalog of completed Kummer pairs \[ A=\epsilon_A\prod_p p^{m_p},\qquad B=\epsilon_B\prod_p p^{n_p},\qquad (m_p,n_p)\in\mathcal V_p. \tag{E.187.2} \] Its everywhere ordinary locus is closed and compact. One may additionally prescribe any finite set of valuations, and choose pairwise disjoint finite prime blocks \(\mathcal B_1,\mathcal B_2,\ldots\), imposing that each block contain a prime with nonzero valuation pair. These are closed conditions, and their simultaneous satisfaction forces infinite support. There is a compact space parametrizing, up to geometric conjugation, every full pro-two section whose abelian pair belongs to this ordinary catalog. It retains the actual arithmetic Frobenius words, including their path twists. The existence of such a section satisfying all the block conditions is equivalent to nonemptiness of every finite test in one nested sequence of finite tests described below. Each test uses finitely many catalog choices, one finite pro-two target, finitely many actual arithmetic relations, and finitely many ordinary local Kummer tests. The quantifier is one common catalog followed by every finite test. Neither one frozen nonzero valuation, nor separately chosen catalogs at arbitrarily large depths, supplies this hypothesis. No catalog with all these tests nonempty is established here. The section conclusion is at coefficient two; a full pronilpotent conclusion would also require the other coefficient sections for the same pair.

statement: Minimal five-adic prime shells in the original A.44 recursion The original recursion E.102, with its unchanged exponents \(n_j=(j+4)!\), has an infinite legal ordinary subfamily in which \[ \begin{gathered} s_j=v_5(n_{j+1}),\\ q_j\equiv1+5^{s_j}\pmod{5^{s_j+1}},\qquad r_j\equiv1-5^{s_j}\pmod{5^{s_j+1}}. \end{gathered} \tag{E.199.1} \] In particular \(v_5(q_j^2-1)=v_5(r_j^2-1)=s_j\). This changes only permitted old-prime unit-root choices, and does not scale the factorials or alter the radical splitting requirements. For such an output take the unique possible global integral class-two predecessor of B.101, with the literal coordinates of B.102, and put \[ \begin{aligned} D_{A,j}&=\gamma_j-q_j\alpha_j u_j,& d_{A,j}&=(q_j^2-1)/n_{j+1},\\ D_{B,j}&=\widetilde\gamma_j+\beta_jv_j,& d_{B,j}&=(r_j^2-1)/n_{j+1}. \end{aligned} \tag{E.199.2} \] Here the coefficient prime is five and both \(d_{A,j},d_{B,j}\) are five-adic units. The complete local coefficient-five third tests are \[ v_5(D_{A,j})\geq v_5(j+5),\qquad v_5(D_{B,j})\geq v_5(j+5)\quad(j\geq0). \tag{E.199.3} \] Thus these local tests are automatic at every index not divisible by five, including the second pair \(q_1,r_1\). The first possible nonautomatic tests are the two finite equations \[ \gamma_0-\alpha_0u_0=0\pmod5,\qquad \widetilde\gamma_0+\beta_0v_0=0\pmod5. \tag{E.199.4} \] They are determined by a fixed legal prefix through index five. No assertion that either equation is forced, or that they can always be satisfied simultaneously, is made. After E.199.3, the continuous coefficient-five third obstruction vanishes if and only if \[ \frac{D_{A,j}}{j+5}\longrightarrow0,\qquad \frac{D_{B,j}}{j+5}\longrightarrow0 \quad\hbox{in }\mathbb Z_5. \tag{E.199.5} \] The minimal shells therefore do not remove the continuous convergence gate. This statement isolates an exact subfamily of the original problem; it neither constructs a class-three survivor nor excludes all original A.44 outputs.

statement: An exact affine system for the first two original factorial support primes Fix a legal first pair $q=q_0,r=r_0$ in the minimal-five-shell subfamily of E.199, so $v_5(q-1)=v_5(r-1)=1$. Every parameter occurs by changing only the fifth-root-of-unity factors in the two old local roots at stage one, followed by legal choices in the original recursion. The first two coefficient-five obstruction values depend only on that parameter, not on the later prime choices in this subfamily. Moreover these twenty-five parameters exhaust the possible first-gate values of all original-recursion continuations with the fixed $q,r$. Here is their exact system. Fix the local tame generators and arithmetic Frobenius lifts at $q,r$, and use the resulting common Tate coordinate. Put $m=24\in\mathbb F_5^\times$. There are unique classes \[ z_q,z_r\in H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{5,q,r,\infty\}},\mathbb F_5(2)) \] whose tame residue vectors are $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$. Choose any one branch as reference. statement: We use the following form of Grothendieck's three axioms. A class $W$ of functors in $\Cat$ is a fundamental localizer if it satisfies LF1--LF3. LF1 means that identities belong to $W$, that $W$ has the two-out-of-three property, and that whenever $i:X\to Y$ and $r:Y\to X$ satisfy $ri=\id_X$ and $ir\in W$, then $r\in W$. LF2 says that $A\to e$ belongs to $W$ whenever $A$ has a terminal object. LF3 says that for a commutative triangle $A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}C$, if every functor $u/c:A/c\to B/c$ belongs to $W$, then $u\in W$. Here both slices use the indicated functors to $C$. A category is $W$-aspherical when its unique functor to $e$ belongs to $W$.

statement: For a presheaf $H:U^{\op}\to\Set$, write $U/H$ for its category of elements: its objects are $(u,h)$, and a morphism $(u,h)\to(v,k)$ is an arrow $a:u\to v$ with $H(a)k=h$. Given $p:U\to U'$, the functor $p_!:\Set^{U^{\op}}\to\Set^{U'^{\op}}$ is ordinary left Kan extension along $p^{\op}$. The presheaf $H$ is totally $W$-aspherical if $U'/p_!H$ is $W$-aspherical for every small $U'$ and every $p$. A category $A$ is totally $W$-aspherical if its terminal presheaf $1_A$ is so. We denote this property by $T_W(A)$. For $f:X\to Y$, put $H_y(x)=\Hom_Y(fx,y)$. The functor $f$ is \emph{strictly} $W$-aspherical if every presheaf $H_y$ is totally $W$-aspherical, and \emph{totally} $W$-aspherical if every category $X/y=X/H_y$ satisfies $T_W$. For a sieve $i:U\hookrightarrow X$, let $\overline U$ be the full cosieve on the objects $x$ for which some arrow $u\to x$, $u\in U$, exists. The sieve is $W$-dwy\'erienne, respectively totally $W$-dwy\'erienne, if $U\to\overline U$ is strictly, respectively totally, $W$-aspherical. A cosieve has either property when its opposite sieve has that property.

statement: For $f:A\to B$, define the presheaf $P_f:B^{\op}\to\Set$ by \[ P_f(b)=\pi_0(b\backslash A). \] There is a canonical factorization in $\Cat$ \[ A\xrightarrow{q_f}D_f:=B/P_f\xrightarrow{\rho_f}B, \qquad q_f(a)=(fa,[a,\id_{fa}]), \] where $q_f$ is final and $\rho_f$ is a discrete fibration. It is the factorization into a final functor followed by a discrete fibration, unique up to a unique isomorphism over $B$ compatible with the map from $A$. Moreover $P_f\cong f_!1_A$ naturally in $b$.

statement: For a fundamental localizer $W$, the axiom called W(7 bis) at XII ms.~75--76 asserts the following biconditional for every small category $X$ covered by two full sieves $U,V$ \citep{GrothendieckDerivateursXIIb}: \[ (U\cap V\longrightarrow V)\in W \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (U\longrightarrow X)\in W. \] The symmetric biconditional is included. W(7), at ms.~76--77, concerns a morphism of two such cover squares. Of the three conditions that the map on the intersection belongs to $W$, that both maps on the pieces belong to $W$, and that the map on the union belongs to $W$, any two must imply the third. statement: Let $U$ be a small category, $H:U^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$ a presheaf, and $E=U/H$ with projection $\alpha:E\to U$. statement: Let $W$ be a fundamental localizer satisfying the full W(7 bis), and let $U\subseteq X$ be a full sieve. Write $T=X\setminus U$, and let $\overline U$ be the full cosieve generated by $U$. For a one-point complement, the corollary at XII ms.~85 is likewise valid under full W(7 bis): $U\to X$ belongs to $W$ if and only if $U/t$ is $W$-aspherical.

statement: There is a category $A$ with $35$ objects and $159$ arrows, including identities, such that $BA$ is connected and integrally acyclic but has nontrivial fundamental group. We specify its complete finite presentation through face operators. Start with the two words \[ w_0=aaaaaBBB,\qquad w_1=bbbBABA, \] where capital letters denote inverses, with lengths $n_0=8,n_1=7$. A finite semisimplicial set $K$ has vertices $v,c_0,c_1$, edges $a,b$ with both endpoints $v$, and edges $r_{k,i}:c_k\to v$ for $k\in\{0,1\}$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/n_k$. It has triangles $t_{k,i}$ with ordered vertices $(c_k,v,v)$. If the $i$th letter of $w_k$ is the positive letter $\ell$, define \[ (d_0t_{k,i},d_1t_{k,i},d_2t_{k,i}) =(\ell,r_{k,i+1},r_{k,i}); \] if that letter is $\ell^{-1}$, define this triple to be $(\ell,r_{k,i},r_{k,i+1})$. The endpoint faces of every $r_{k,i}$ are $(v,c_k)$, and those of $a,b$ are $(v,v)$. These prescriptions satisfy the semisimplicial identities. There are no simplices above dimension two. The objects of $A$ are the simplices just listed. A morphism $\sigma\to\tau$ is an increasing injection $\theta:[\dim\sigma]\hookrightarrow[\dim\tau]$ for which $\theta^*\tau=\sigma$; composition is composition of the injections. In particular, distinct occurrences of the same face give distinct arrows. These definitions specify every object, arrow and composite of $A$.

statement: Let $A$ be small and $K:A\to\Set$ covariant. Form the category $A_K$ by adjoining an object $x$, with $A_K(x,a)=K(a)$, $A_K(a,x)=\varnothing$, and $A_K(x,x)=\{\id_x\}$. statement: Suppose $BA$ is weakly contractible and $E=\El_A(K)$ is nonempty and connected. statement: Let $a,b:p\to q$ be a parallel pair in any small category $A$. statement: Let $M=\{1,e,f\}$, with $1$ a unit and $uv=v$ for $u,v\in\{e,f\}$. Regard $M$ as a one-object category with multiplication $uv=u\circ v$. Let $K:M\to\Set$ have underlying set $\{h,i\}$, with $1$ acting identically and both $e,f$ acting constantly with value $i$. Then \[ B\El_M(K)\simeq S^1, \qquad B(M_K)\simeq S^2. \] The inclusion $M\to M_K$ is final. In particular $M$ is not totally $\Winfty$-aspherical and is not totally $W_R$-aspherical for any nonzero commutative ring $R$.

statement: Let $I,J$ be nonempty small sets, let $R_{I,J}=I\times J$ with $(i,j)(k,l)=(i,l)$, and let $M_{I,J}=R_{I,J}^{1}$ have a new identity adjoined. statement: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with identity.
