More generally, if every $b\backslash A$ is nonempty and its reduced $R$-homology vanishes in degrees $0,\ldots,d-1$, for an integer $d\geq1$, then $Bf$ induces isomorphisms in degrees less than $d$ and an epimorphism in degree $d$.
notes: Proved: homological Theorem A in the final variance source_label=C:homology-A Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Bisimplicial-chain proof

statement: If $A$ satisfies $\mathcal P_R$, then every connected component $E$ of $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$, for every $H:A\to\Set$, also satisfies $\mathcal P_R$. The corresponding assertion holds for $\mathcal P_\infty$.
notes: Proved: inheritance by categories of elements source_label=C:inherit-elements Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Explicit coproduct-over-fibres comparison isomorphism

statement: Suppose that a connected, nonempty small category $E$ satisfies $\mathcal P_{\mathbb Z}$. Then $BE$ is weakly contractible. Consequently $\mathcal P_{\mathbb Z}(A)$ and $\mathcal P_\infty(A)$ are equivalent for every small category $A$.
notes: Proved: integral acyclicity detects every cyclic subgroup source_label=C:cyclic-covers Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Cyclic-subgroup covering test and Hurewicz

statement: For every small category $A$, the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical in the sense of XII, Definition~1. \item $A$ is totally $W_{\mathbb Z}$-aspherical. \item $A$ is nonempty and connected, and satisfies $\mathcal P_{\mathbb Z}$. \item $A$ is nonempty and connected, and satisfies $\mathcal P_\infty$. \end{enumerate} In particular, this is a criterion in terms of all covariant set-valued diagrams on $A$, involving no quantification over target categories or final functors. Moreover every connected component of every $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$ is itself totally $\Winfty$-aspherical whenever $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical.
notes: Proved: characterization of total asphericity source_label=C:classification Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Complete characterization with covariant set-valued tests

statement: Let $A$ be nonempty and connected. If $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$ is exact, then $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical.
notes: Proved: exact integral colimits are sufficient source_label=C:exact-sufficient Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Direct sums over element fibres preserve exactness

statement: Let $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ have objects $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ for $n\geq0$, and all strictly increasing functions as arrows, with ordinary composition of functions. This is a countable small category. In the next construction $\mathbb Z[S]$ denotes the free abelian group on a set $S$, and the augmentation of a finite linear combination of arrows is the sum of its coefficients.
notes: Proved: the category of injective ordinals source_label=C:delta-definition Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Countable small category

statement: Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be polynomials in $\mathbb Z[x_0,\ldots,x_n,u]$ such that $F_i-F_j\in(x_i,x_j)$ for every pair $i,j$. There exists $C$ in this polynomial ring with $C-F_i\in(x_i)$ for every $i$. If all $F_i$ are homogeneous of the same degree, $C$ can be chosen homogeneous of that degree.
notes: Proved: interpolation on coordinate hyperplanes source_label=C:interpolation Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Explicit inclusion-exclusion formula

statement: For every $n\geq0$ there are an integer $M\geq n$ and \[ t\in\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}}([n],[M])] \] of augmentation $1$ such that $th=th'$ whenever $h,h':[m]\to[n]$ are parallel arrows. Here composition is extended bilinearly in the free preadditive category. For $n\geq1$ one can take $M=2^{n+1}-2$.
notes: Proved: normalized affine cones source_label=C:affine-cones Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Explicit polynomial construction; exact computational checks through dimension 3

statement: The category $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical and has exact colimits of abelian-group-valued diagrams, but is not filtered. Consequently Lead~4 for $\Winfty$ and manuscript row II-C-003 have a negative answer for arbitrary small categories.
notes: Refuted: total asphericity need not imply filteredness source_label=C:counterexample Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Counterexample Delta_inj completely specified and verified

statement: A totally $\Winfty$-aspherical category $A$ is nonempty, its objects have common successors, and for every parallel pair $a,b:p\to q$ there exist an object $r$ and an integral arrow combination $t\in\mathbb Z[A(q,r)]$ of augmentation $1$ satisfying $ta=tb$.
notes: Proved: directedness and affine equalizers source_label=C:directed-affine Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Finite target consolidation proved

statement: Let $M$ be any small monoid, with multiplication $yx$ denoting composition of $x$ followed by $y$. Suppose that for every $x,a\in M$ there is $t\in\mathbb Z[M]$ with augmentation $1$ such that $tx=txa$. Then $M$, viewed as a one-object category, is filtered.
notes: Proved: a signed-measure criterion for monoids source_label=C:monoid-lemma Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Finite invariant signed measures and minimal period descent

statement: Let $A$ have a weakly terminal object $q$, meaning that $A(a,q)\ne\varnothing$ for every object $a$. Then $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical if and only if it is filtered. In particular the equivalence holds for every monoid and every category with finitely many objects, and hence for every category with finitely many arrows.
notes: Proved: monoids and categories with a weakly terminal object source_label=C:weak-terminal Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Includes all finite-arrow categories; does not extend by an unsupported infinite-limit argument

statement: The category $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ is not sifted. In the category of cospans from $[0],[0]$ to a common ordinal, a cospan is an ordinal with two distinguished points. Their comparison, $<$, $=$, or $>$, is invariant under every morphism of cospans, since all transition functions are injective and increasing. Each comparison class is connected: it receives the canonical cospan on $[1]$, $[0]$, or $[1]$ respectively, by the injection selecting the distinguished points. Thus this cospan category has exactly three connected components, and the diagonal is not final. This prevents an attempted proof of the open implication in Remark~D.7 by first asserting that totality forces siftedness.
notes: Proved: the counterexample is not sifted source_label=C:not-sifted Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Its two-point cospan category has exactly three components

statement: For every nonzero commutative ring $R$ with identity, let $W_R$ be the functors whose nerves induce isomorphisms on $H_j(-;R)$ for every $j\geq0$. Then $W_R$ is a fundamental localizer with the precise relative Theorem~A axiom fixed in Part~A.
notes: Proved: the homology localizer source_label=D:homology-localizer Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Relative Theorem A established by the slice Grothendieck constructions

statement: A small category $A$ is totally $W_R$-aspherical if and only if it is nonempty and connected and satisfies $\mathcal P_R(A)$ of Definition~C.1. In particular \[ \{A:A\text{ is totally }W_{\mathbb Z}\text{-aspherical}\} =\{A:A\text{ is totally }\Winfty\text{-aspherical}\}. \]
notes: Proved: total $R$-asphericity source_label=D:R-action Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Exact coefficient-ring scope

statement: For a small category $A$ and a nonzero commutative ring $R$, define $\operatorname{Aff}_R(A)$ to have the objects of $A$ and the morphisms \[ \operatorname{Aff}_R(A)(a,b)= \left\{\sum_{f\in A(a,b)}r_ff\in R[A(a,b)]: \text{finite support},\ \sum_fr_f=1_R\right\}. \] Composition is the bilinear extension of composition in $A$; augmentations multiply, so composition preserves augmentation $1$. Each identity is the original identity with coefficient $1_R$. This is an ordinary small category, generally not an additive category. Its connected components are those of $A$.
notes: Proved: affine linearization source_label=D:aff-definition Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Ordinary category; commutative unital nonzero coefficient ring

statement: For every small category $A$, including the empty category, and every nonzero commutative ring $R$, the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $\colim_A:(R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})^A\to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is exact. \item Every connected component of $\operatorname{Aff}_R(A)$ is filtered. \end{enumerate} In explicit terms, condition (2) requires common successors within each component and an augmentation-one affine equalizer for every pair of parallel \emph{affine} arrows. It is not merely the condition in Lead~2 for one pair of original arrows. For $R=\mathbb Z$ this is the Isbell--Mitchell affine criterion \citep{IsbellMitchell1973Exact,IsbellMitchell1976Fixed}; a related finite-family formulation is verified in \citet[Section~1, unnumbered theorem]{Isbell1968Exact}. We supply the proof rather than relying on an unavailable theorem number from the original AMS papers.
notes: Proved: the affine exact-colimit criterion source_label=D:affine-exactness Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Self-contained proof of the precise affine condition

statement: If $A$ is nonempty and connected and $\colim_A:(R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})^A\to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is exact, then $A$ is totally $W_R$-aspherical. For $R=\mathbb Z$ the conclusion strengthens to total $\Winfty$-asphericity.
notes: Proved: exact module colimits imply total homology asphericity source_label=D:exact-R-sufficient Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Integral conclusion strengthens to W_infinity

statement: Let $D$ have two objects $0,1$ and only their identity arrows. Its colimit functor on abelian groups is $(M_0,M_1)\mapsto M_0\oplus M_1$, which is exact. Nevertheless $D$ is not totally $W_{\mathbb Z}$-aspherical: the identity is final and $H_0(BD;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^2\ne\mathbb Z$. The empty category provides another counterexample, with exact zero colimit. Thus the literal equivalence stated in Lead~4 is false; nonemptiness and connectedness cannot be suppressed. The finite category and its composition law are checked in \texttt{cd\_finite\_checks.py}.
notes: Refuted: the literal homology half of Lead 4 source_label=D:disconnected-counterexample Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Discrete two-object and empty categories; finite check attached

statement: The remaining implication is the precise statement \[ \left. \begin{array}{c} A\text{ small, nonempty, connected},\\ A\text{ totally }\Winfty\text{-aspherical} \end{array}\right\} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab\text{ exact}. \] Equivalently, by Theorems~C.5 and D.4, does $\mathcal P_\infty(A)$ force $\operatorname{Aff}_{\mathbb Z}(A)$ to be filtered? We have not proved this implication or produced a counterexample. This is an unresolved implication of the present work, not an assertion of a currently open problem in the literature. The attempted reduction through the acyclicity of $\mathbb Z[H]$ fails because these diagrams are not generally projective and their acyclicity does not supply acyclicity of arbitrary module diagrams. Lead~2 supplies affine equalizers of original parallel arrows, but exactness requires equalizers of all affine pairs. The proof in Lemma~C.12 bridges this gap for monoids and, by Theorem~C.13, for categories with a weakly terminal object. It also holds for $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ by its explicit affine cones. The first size not covered by the finite-object theorem is the case of countably infinitely many objects with no weakly terminal object; no particular smallest counterexample is claimed. For general nonzero $R$, the corresponding unproved necessity is $\mathcal P_R(A)$, with $A$ connected and nonempty, implying filteredness of $\operatorname{Aff}_R(A)$. Neither assertion is replaced here by its sufficient direction.
where_proved: TOTASPH_paper.pdf p.22; Remark D.7; sections/D.tex:100; exact unresolved claim and obstruction, not a proof
notes: Open: the corrected connected converse source_label=D:exact-converse-open Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Unresolved in this work; no claim of literature-open status; gap and first unhandled size stated

statement: Let $G$ be a small group, regarded as a one-object category. It is totally $W_R$-aspherical if and only if every subgroup $K\leq G$ is $R$-acyclic. If $G$ is finite, this is equivalent to $|G|\in R^\times$. In particular a nontrivial finite group is totally $W_{\mathbb Q}$-aspherical but is not totally $\Winfty$-aspherical.
notes: Proved: a subgroup criterion for groups source_label=D:group-criterion Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. C2 separates W_Q from W_infinity; code attached

statement: For an integer $n\geq0$, $W_n$ denotes functors inducing bijections on connected components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups in degrees $1,\ldots,n$, at every basepoint. Thus $W_0$ tests only components. A category is $W_n$-aspherical precisely when its classifying space is nonempty and $n$-connected. These are fundamental localizers: weak saturation and the terminal-object axiom are immediate, and the relative axiom follows by applying $n$-truncation to the two bisimplicial comparisons used in Proposition~D.1. The functor to $n$-types is left adjoint to inclusion \citep[Proposition~5.5.6.18]{Lurie2009HTT} and consequently preserves homotopy colimits in the category of $n$-types, so an objectwise $W_n$-equivalence induces a $W_n$-equivalence on those comparisons.
notes: Proved: truncation convention source_label=D:n-convention Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Truncation adjunction cited at exact proposition

statement: An ordinary final functor $f:A\to B$ induces a bijection on components and, on each component with a chosen object $a_0$, an epimorphism \[ \pi_1(BA,a_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(BB,f(a_0)). \]
notes: Proved: final functors and fundamental groups source_label=D:final-pi1 Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Explicit edge-path lift

statement: A small category is totally $W_0$-aspherical if and only if it is nonempty and connected. It is totally $W_1$-aspherical if and only if its classifying space is nonempty and simply connected.
notes: Proved: the cases $W_0$ and $W_1$ source_label=D:zero-one Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Identity proves necessity

statement: For $n\geq2$, a small category $A$ is totally $W_n$-aspherical if and only if $BA$ is $n$-connected and every connected component of every $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$, for covariant $H:A\to\Set$, is $(n-1)$-connected.
notes: Proved: the cases $W_n$, $n\geq2$ source_label=D:truncated-classification Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Truncated collage test, covers, and Hurewicz

statement: For every $n\geq2$, a small category with a weakly terminal object is totally $W_n$-aspherical if and only if it is filtered. The same equivalence holds for every category with finitely many objects, including the empty category by separate inspection. It fails for $n=1$: the contractible nonfiltered right-zero monoid of Part~B is totally $W_1$-aspherical.
notes: Proved: truncated totality with a weakly terminal object source_label=D:truncated-finite Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. W1 exception supplied by right-zero monoid

statement: If $W\subseteq V$ are fundamental localizers, every totally $W$-aspherical category is totally $V$-aspherical. In particular every totally $\Winfty$-aspherical category is totally $W$-aspherical for every fundamental localizer satisfying exactly the axioms fixed in Part~A. Total $\Winfty$-asphericity is not invariant under a weak homotopy equivalence of categories.
notes: Proved: dependence on the localizer and on the category source_label=D:general-localizer Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Uses fundamental-localizer minimality and explicit right-zero monoid

statement: If the zero ring is allowed, every homology group with its coefficients is zero, so $W_R$ is the class of all functors and every small category, including the empty category, is totally $W_R$-aspherical. Its module category is the zero category, and every colimit functor is exact. The nonzero hypothesis in the preceding affine and connectedness criteria is therefore necessary. The ring-theoretic statements above have been stated for commutative unital rings; no unannounced extension of their affine-linearization proof to noncommutative coefficients is being used.
notes: Proved: the zero coefficient ring source_label=D:zero-ring Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Explains the nonzero hypothesis

statement: If $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical, then $\colim_A:\Set^A\to\Set$ preserves monomorphisms. Moreover every span $a\xrightarrow{f}b$, $a\xrightarrow{g}c$ in $A$ has a commuting completion: there are $u:b\to d$, $v:c\to d$ with $uf=vg$.
notes: Proved: preservation of monomorphisms of set diagrams source_label=D:set-monos Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Complete proof using directed element categories

statement: Let $A$ be totally $\Winfty$-aspherical, and let $H:A\to\Set$ have a nonempty connected category of elements. Every natural endomorphism $\tau:H\to H$ fixes an element: there are $a\in A$ and $h\in H(a)$ with $\tau_a(h)=h$.
notes: Proved: fixed points in connected representations source_label=D:fixed-points Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Classifying-space obstruction first for N then for cyclic groups

statement: The fixed-point condition of Proposition~D.17, for all connected representations, is strictly weaker than exactness of abelian colimits. A small connected counterexample is constructed in \citet[Part~C, Construction~C.1 and Theorem~C.2, pp.~384--389]{AdamekKoubekReiterman1981Embeddings}. Their Section~A.4, p.~370, explicitly corrects the earlier identification of these conditions. In particular, the statement in \citet[Section~II.3, p.~100]{AdamekReiterman1976SetColim} cannot be used as an exactness criterion. The 1981 counterexample has the fixed-point property but fails simultaneous affine equalization of three specified parallel arrows. This source correction does not resolve Remark~D.7: we have not proved that the published counterexample satisfies $\mathcal P_\infty$. The distinction between pairwise and simultaneous affine equalization remains essential.
notes: Known: the fixed-point condition does not imply exactness source_label=D:fpp-not-exact Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Verified primary theorem C.2 pp385–389; totality of its counterexample is not established here

statement: Let $W$ be a fundamental localizer with $W_1\subseteq W$. For every small category $A$, including the empty category, \[ T_W(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\to e\in W. \] Equivalently, every ordinary final functor whose source is $W$-aspherical has a $W$-aspherical target. By Proposition~F.28, the assumption on $W$ is precisely that $S^2$ be $W$-aspherical; it imposes no accessibility condition.
notes: Proved: totality above the one-type localizer source_label=D:sphere-totality Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Includes the empty category; no accessibility hypothesis

statement: Under the same hypothesis on $W$, for every small $U$ and every presheaf $H:U^{\op}\to\Set$, the following are equivalent: \[ H\text{ is totally }W\text{-aspherical},\qquad U/H\text{ is }W\text{-aspherical},\qquad T_W(U/H). \] These equivalences include the empty presheaf. Strictly and totally $W$-aspherical functors coincide, and the $W$-dwy\'erienne and totally $W$-dwy\'erienne sieve classes coincide.
notes: Proved: presheaf and element-category totality above the one-type localizer source_label=D:sphere-presheaves Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Includes empty presheaves; strict and total functor and sieve classes coincide

statement: Fix a fundamental localizer $W$ with $W_1\subseteq W$. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item The $W$-dwy\'erienne sieves are closed under composition. \item The totally $W$-dwy\'erienne sieves are closed under composition. \item Every nonempty small category is $W$-aspherical. \end{enumerate} When these conditions hold, every full sieve belongs to both classes. If condition~3 fails, the failure of composition can be witnessed by a classical Dwyer first factor and a second factor obtained by adjoining one terminal object, as in Theorem~F.9.
notes: Proved: sieve composition above the one-type localizer source_label=D:sphere-sieve-composition Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Failure has a classical first factor and a terminal-object extension second factor

statement: For any fundamental localizer $W$ and any presheaf $H:U^{\op}\to\Set$, total $W$-asphericity of $U/H$ implies total $W$-asphericity of $H$. If $H$ is subterminal, the converse also holds.
notes: Proved: forward implication and the subterminal converse source_label=E:forward-subterminal Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $C$ be small, let $c\in C$, and let $d:c\to c$ satisfy $d^2=d$. Define \[ Q_d(v)=\{\alpha:v\to c\mid d\alpha=\alpha\}. \] This is a split subpresheaf of $C(-,c)$, with retraction $\alpha\mapsto d\alpha$. Its category of elements $C/Q_d$ is filtered and has contractible classifying space.
notes: Proved: fixed-arrow presheaves of an idempotent source_label=E:idempotent Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $U$ be the one-object category with endomorphism monoid $\{1,e\}$, $e^2=e$. Let $R=U(-,*)$, let $Q=\{e\}\subset R$, and form the pushout of presheaves \[ H=R\amalg_QR. \] Explicitly $H(*)=\{i,h_1,h_2\}$, and $H(e)$ is the constant function with value $i$. Then $H$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical, and consequently totally $W$-aspherical for every fundamental localizer $W$. The category $E=U/H$ is not totally $\Winfty$-aspherical, is not totally $W_R$-aspherical for any nonzero commutative ring $R$, and is not filtered. Thus the converse of manuscript Proposition~8 is false, even for a finite category with two arrows and a three-element presheaf.
notes: Refuted: row B035 and the first biconditional in Lead 5 source_label=E:counterexample Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: For the fixed base $U=\{1,e\}$ of Theorem~E.3, a finite presheaf $H$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical if and only if $H(*)$ is nonempty and $H(e)$ has exactly one fixed point. Such a presheaf has a totally $\Winfty$-aspherical category of elements if and only if $|H(*)|\leq2$. Thus three elements are the smallest counterexample on this base.
notes: Proved: minimality within the two-element idempotent base source_label=E:finite-idempotent-classification Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: For a fundamental localizer $W$, the implication ``every totally $W$-aspherical presheaf $H$ has totally $W$-aspherical category of elements holds for all small bases and presheaves if and only if $S^2$ is $W$-aspherical. For every fundamental localizer in which the displayed sphere category $C$ is not aspherical, Theorem~E.3 gives a totally $W$-aspherical presheaf whose category of elements is not totally $W$-aspherical. In particular this holds for $\Winfty$, every nonzero homology localizer $W_R$, and every truncation localizer $W_n$ with $n\geq2$. For $W_0$ the two notions are equivalent to $U/H$ being nonempty and connected. For $W_1$ they are equivalent to $B(U/H)$ being nonempty, connected, and simply connected.
notes: Proved: the exact localizer range of the presheaf converse source_label=E:localizers Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: For a small $U$ and a presheaf $H$, the category $U/H$ is filtered if and only if $H$ is a small filtered colimit of representable presheaves. Hence this condition is sufficient for total $W$-asphericity of $H$ for every fundamental localizer. It is not necessary, by Theorem~E.3.
notes: Proved: the genuine filtered-presentation criterion source_label=E:flat Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $i:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a sieve, and let $i_0:U\to\overline U$ have the codomain of Definition~A.2. There is an ind-right adjoint precisely when every $U/x$, $x\in\overline U$, is filtered. Here an ind-right adjoint means a functor $r:\overline U\to\Ind(U)$ and bijections \[ \Hom_{\Ind(U)}(y_U(u),r(x))\cong\Hom_X(u,x) \] natural in $u\in U$ and $x\in\overline U$, where $y_U$ is Yoneda and $\Ind(U)$ is the full subcategory of presheaves given by small filtered colimits of representables. Such a sieve is totally $W$-dwy\'erienne for every fundamental localizer. The converse for $\Winfty$-dwy\'erienne sieves is false, even for a finite sieve, and the converse for totally $\Winfty$-dwy\'erienne sieves is also false in general.
notes: Refuted: the ind-right-adjoint biconditional in Lead 5 source_label=E:ind-adjoint Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $E=U/H$ and $\pi:E\to U$. For a nonzero commutative ring $R$, $H$ is totally $W_R$-aspherical if and only if $BE$ is $R$-acyclic and every connected component of \[ \El_E(L\pi),\qquad L:U\to\Set, \] is $R$-acyclic. For $\Winfty$, the corresponding criterion is that $BE$ is weakly contractible and these same components are integrally acyclic. The restriction that the action factors through $\pi$ is essential; Theorem~E.3 disproves removing it.
his_places: XIIb-a-B035; XIIba-C045; Part F discrete-flatness comparison
notes: Proved: what the presheaf quantifier actually tests source_label=E:restricted-actions Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $i:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a full sieve of small categories, let $T=X\setminus U$, and let $\overline U$ be the full cosieve generated by $U$. For $t\in T$ put \[ H_t:U^{\op}\longrightarrow\Set,\qquad H_t(u)=\Hom_X(u,t). \] The immersion is $W$-dwy\'erienne if every nonempty $H_t$ is a totally $W$-aspherical presheaf. It is totally $W$-dwy\'erienne if every nonempty $U/t$ is a totally $W$-aspherical category. These are precisely the conditions that $U\to\overline U$ be strictly, respectively totally, $W$-aspherical in XII ms.~109. A classical Dwyer map additionally requires that $U\to\overline U$ have a right adjoint. A $W$-cofibration is a functor $i:U\to X$ such that \[ i_!:U\backslash\Cat\longrightarrow X\backslash\Cat, \qquad (U\to C)\longmapsto(X\to X\amalg_U C), \] preserves morphisms whose underlying functors belong to $W$.
notes: Known: the manuscript's variance source_label=F:definitions Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. The presheaf is contravariant; empty boundary weights are excluded from totality tests. Classical Dwyer and pseudo-Dwyer conditions are distinguished.

statement: Let $W$ be a fundamental localizer. Both classes of dwy\'erienne sieves in Definition~F.1 are stable under arbitrary cobase change in $\Cat$. Every $W$-dwy\'erienne sieve is a $W$-cofibration. In a pushout square \[ \begin{tikzcd} U\arrow[r,"i",hook]\arrow[d,"p"']&X\arrow[d,"q"]\\ C\arrow[r,"i'",hook]&X\amalg_U C, \end{tikzcd} \] the implications $p\in W\Rightarrow q\in W$ and $i\in W\Rightarrow i'\in W$ hold. The assertions apply to arbitrary small $C$ and arbitrary $p$, with no injectivity or fullness assumption on $p$.
notes: Proved: cobase change and the forward part of Th\'eor\`eme~3 source_label=F:pushout Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. All categories are small; p is arbitrary, without fullness or object-injectivity assumptions. Uses only forward gluing, not full W(7) or W(7 bis).

statement: For every fundamental localizer $W$, a functor is a couniversal $W$-equivalence if and only if it is both a $W$-cofibration and a member of $W$. The class of $W$-cofibrations is closed under composition, cobase change, and retracts in the arrow category.
notes: Proved: couniversality in the fundamental-localizer setting source_label=F:couniversal Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. The general-W proof uses Thomason factorization and Cisinski’s corrected retract statement. The equivalence is not asserted for an arbitrary weakly saturated class lacking the localizer axioms.

statement: In the square of Proposition~F.2, suppose that $i$ is $W$-dwy\'erienne. Under the full axiom W(7 bis) of XII ms.~76, the following conditions are equivalent: \[ i\in W,\qquad i'\in W,\qquad (\dot T\hookrightarrow T)\in W,\qquad i\text{ is a couniversal }W\text{-equivalence}. \] Under the full axiom W(7) of XII ms.~77 one also has $p\in W\Longleftrightarrow q\in W$. The equivalence between the first and last conditions requires neither additional axiom.
notes: Proved: the conditional equivalences and the boundary corollary source_label=F:conditional-theorem3 Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. These are conditional reflection statements. Full W(7 bis) and W(7) must not be assumed for W∞; the boundary is dot(T)=bar(U)∩(X∖U).

statement: For $W=W_\infty$, or $W=W_R$ for a nonzero commutative unital ring $R$, connected components of discrete opfibrations over a totally $W$-aspherical category are totally $W$-aspherical. Every nonempty cosieve in such a category is totally $W$-aspherical. If $B$ and every value of a small covariant functor $D:B\to\Cat$ are totally $W$-aspherical, then $\int_BD$ is totally $W$-aspherical.
notes: Proved: operations on totally aspherical categories source_label=F:total-operations Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. The Grothendieck construction uses actual transition functors. The variance is discrete opfibration; no corresponding assertion for arbitrary discrete fibrations is made. statement: Let $Y$ be a small category and $y_0$ an object of $Y$. A type $\tau$ is a finite word in the signs $+$ and $-$. Its interval $I_\tau$ has objects $0,\ldots,n$, where $n$ is the length of $\tau$, and is the free category on the oriented line whose $i$th edge has the indicated sign. A morphism of types is an endpoint-preserving functor $\varphi:I_\tau\to I_\rho$ whose object function is nondecreasing in the numerical ordering of the vertices. This numerical ordering is distinct from the ordering defined by the arrows of the interval. An object of $P(Y,y_0)=\operatorname{Ch}(Y;y_0,-)$ is a pair $(\tau,c)$ with $c:I_\tau\to Y$ and $c(0)=y_0$. A morphism \[ (\tau,c)\longrightarrow(\rho,d) \] is a pair $(\varphi,\eta)$ consisting of such a type morphism and a natural transformation $\eta:c\Rightarrow d\varphi$ whose component at $0$ is $\mathrm{id}_{y_0}$. The composite of $(\varphi,\eta)$ and $(\psi,\theta)$ is $(\psi\varphi,(\theta\varphi)\eta)$. The endpoint functor \[ q:P(Y,y_0)\longrightarrow Y \] sends $(\tau,c)$ to $c(n)$ and $(\varphi,\eta)$ to $\eta_n$. The category $\operatorname{Ch}(Y;a,b)$ has fixed source $a$, fixed endpoint $b$, and requires the natural-transformation components at both endpoints to be identities.

statement: With common successors, a triple has a simultaneous affine equalizer iff aug(K1∩K2)=Z. For C=P_q/(K1+K2), there is a canonical surjection L_1 colim_A C→(aug(K1)∩aug(K2))/aug(K1∩K2), with numerator Z when both pairs have affine equalizers.

statement: For H3=A(p,−)/(ca0∼ca1∼ca2) and K=ker(P_q²→P_p), H1(BEl H3)=Z²/im(colim K→Z²), H2(BEl H3)=ker(colim K→Z²), and H_j(BEl H3)=L_{j−2} colim K for j≥3.

statement: For quasi-filtered A, every component of every El_A(H) is simply connected. Hence degree two is the first possible further homological obstruction to totality.

statement: Adjoining one terminal object gives a full extension A→A^▷ that is filtered and total, has exact abelian colimits, and supplies an ordinary simultaneous equalizer for every old finite parallel family. One added object is minimal among proper full extensions obtained by adding objects.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Proposition C.7, p. 12; TOTEX_paper.tex, label C:terminal-repair

statement: For arbitrary small A, the comparison ∫_A D→colim_A^Cat D is a weak equivalence for every Cat-valued D iff A is componentwise filtered, allowing the empty category. On nonempty connected A, the four conditions of R8 are equivalent as stated.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Proposition D.1, p. 13; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:R8-scope

The first error is inferring nonempty connectedness from the constant-point test; it gives BA≃π0A. The repair is componentwise filteredness, or the explicit nonempty-connected hypothesis.

statement: If every component of every action category El_A(S) is simply connected, this property descends to all such components. Every nonempty connected one of those components has common successors for pairs of objects.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Lemma D.2, p. 13; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:inherit-common

notes: Label D:inherit-common. Prompt coverage: D.1, D.2, D.3. If two objects have no common successor, the union of two disjoint principal cosieves yields a connected doubled action category with H1=Z. This is the contradiction used in the truncation arguments.

statement: For nonempty connected A, filteredness is equivalent to totality plus preservation of 1-truncation for all diagrams of groups, and to the categorical Grothendieck-construction comparison for all Cat-valued diagrams. Explicit bipartite Artin-group diagrams attached to parallel pairs suffice for the group test.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Proposition D.3, p. 13; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:RAAG

The proof checks natural H2 orientations under color-preserving graph maps, transport-generator computation of π1(hocolim), and collapse of the permutation-coefficient spectral sequence. The opened sources supply Salvetti/comparison ingredients, not the full shape theorem.

statement: Every sifted totally W∞-aspherical category is filtered. It suffices that all components of all its action categories are simply connected.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Theorem D.4, p. 14; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:sifted-total

notes: Label D:sifted-total. Prompt coverage: D.2, R8, F. A common successor of (q;u,id_q) and (q;v,id_q) in the connected cospan action category forces a single postmap equalizing u and v. In particular a total/nonexact separator could not be sifted.

statement: If A is nonempty connected and total, preservation of 1-truncation for all abelian diagrams B M forces filteredness. Without an initial shape hypothesis, all canonical maps hocolim_A B M→B colim_A^Ab M are weak equivalences iff A is filtered.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Theorem D.5, p. 15; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:abelian-one

notes: Label D:abelian-one. Prompt coverage: D.1, D.2, R8. The omitted common-successor argument is supplied. The H2 edge filtration gives L1 colim M=0; its exterior-square cross summand gives the tensor comparison and siftedness. This settles the abelian form of R8.

statement: For an abelian group M and n≥2, K(M,n) is (n−1)-connected with H_n=M and H_{n+1}=0. Its pointed self-equivalence space is homotopically discrete with components Aut(M).
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Lemma D.6, p. 15; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:EM-low

notes: Label D:EM-low. Prompt coverage: D.3. The proof permits arbitrary abelian groups. Reduced cohomology in degree zero is included in the vanishing of the positive homotopy groups of the pointed mapping space.

statement: For total A and any one fixed finite n≥1, if hocolim_A K(M(a),n) is n-truncated for every abelian diagram M, then A is filtered. Filtered categories satisfy the condition for every n.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Theorem D.7, p. 16; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:fixed-n
depends_on: D.5 (D:abelian-one); D.6 (D:EM-low); D.8 (D:connectivity); D.4 (D:sifted-total); Reduced bar spectral sequence; Integral Künneth theorem
his_places: II ms. 36–36ter (fixed positive abelian Eilenberg–MacLane strengthening)
notes: Label D:fixed-n. Prompt coverage: D.3, F. Degree n+1 first proves exactness; the degree-2n cross summand M⊗M′ then proves siftedness. Filtered homotopy colimits preserve n-types by finite simplicial data.

statement: If every map in a diagram of spaces has (n−1)-connected homotopy fibres, the induced map on homotopy colimits has (n−1)-connected homotopy fibres.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Lemma D.8, p. 16; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:connectivity
notes: Label D:connectivity. Prompt coverage: D.3. The proof takes limits of the actual lifting-space equivalences against arbitrary (n−1)-truncated maps over the colimit base, then reapplies the connective-map criterion.

statement: If C is nonempty, BC is simply connected, and homotopy colimits over C preserve n-truncated spaces for one finite n≥1, then C is filtered.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Lemma D.9, p. 16; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:simply-connected-shape
depends_on: D.2 (D:inherit-common); D.5 (D:abelian-one); D.8 (D:connectivity); D.6 (D:EM-low); D.7 (D:fixed-n); Classification of pointed K(L,n)-families by BAut(L); Relative Künneth theorem and reduced bar spectral sequence
notes: Label D:simply-connected-shape. Prompt coverage: D.3. For n=1 a doubled action yields a surviving H2 term while π1=Z, forcing common successors. For n≥2 the zero section gives a pointed K(L,n)-family trivial on the simply connected base; relative degree-(n+1) homology forces exactness, then the fixed-n theorem applies.

statement: For every finite n≥1, A belongs to T_n iff each universal-cover category C_a=El_A Hom_{ΠA}(a,ℓ(−)) is filtered. Thus T1=T2=⋯; T0 consists of categories with total nonempty components, and T0∩T_n is the componentwise filtered class. Empty categories are included.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Theorem D.10, p. 17; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:Tn-classification
depends_on: D.9 (D:simply-connected-shape); A.1 (A:R1); Groupoid completion and universal covering; Filtered-colimit preservation of n-types
notes: Label D:Tn-classification. Prompt coverage: D.3. The proof specifies the dependent-sum action comparison and the pullback of the universal cover on bar constructions. Coverings preserve homotopy groups in degrees ≥2, proving sufficiency for positive levels. Nontrivial groups lie in every positive class but not T0; the trivial group lies in all classes.

statement: The positive-level classification reduces to ordinary finite zigzag data: common successors in C_a of pairs (x,γ), and actual post-equalizers of parallel arrows with the same image in ΠA. For the one-object monoid N, C_* is the ordered set Z, so N lies in every positive T_n but is not total.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Remark D.11, p. 18; TOTEX_paper.tex, label D:Tn-finite-data
notes: Label D:Tn-finite-data. Prompt coverage: D.3. This expresses the universal-cover criterion without quantifying over arbitrary space-valued diagrams and supplies a non-group positive-level example.

statement: For any commutative R and M:A→R-Mod, π_i(hocolim_A HM)=L_i colim_A M for i≥0, with negative groups zero. Such homotopy colimits are Eilenberg–MacLane for all M iff R-module colimits are exact. Exact integral colimits imply exactness for every R, including Q and F_p.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Proposition D.12, p. 19; TOTEX_paper.tex, label main:stable
depends_on: Two-sided bar complex and projective-diagram double complex; Eilenberg–MacLane realization spectral sequence
notes: Label main:stable. Prompt coverage: D.4. The argument allows nonprojective objectwise R-modules. Forgetting HR-module spectra preserves the displayed colimit, and ordinary R-module colimits have the same underlying abelian group.

statement: For total A and every commutative R, L_i colim_A R[H]=0 for every set-valued H and i>0. The same vanishing holds for sums, direct summands, and filtered colimits of these coefficient diagrams.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Proposition D.13, p. 19; TOTEX_paper.tex, label main:tested
depends_on: A.1 (A:R1); D.12 (main:stable); Additivity and filtered-colimit exactness of the coefficient bar complex
notes: Label main:tested. Prompt coverage: D.4. This records exactly the coefficient classes controlled by the action criterion. It does not assert that arbitrary abelian or field-valued diagrams are built from them in a way preserving the needed vanishing.

statement: For nonzero commutative R and A with common successors for finite object sets, exact R-module colimits, simultaneous R-affine equalizers for every finite ordinary parallel family, and filteredness of Aff_R(A) are equivalent.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Proposition D.14, p. 20; TOTEX_paper.tex, label main:ring-affine
depends_on: Kernel of P_q→P_p^k; Explicit affine extension and universal colimit cocones; Isbell–Mitchell (1973), Theorem 1 and Lemma 1 for the integral instance (opened)
notes: Label main:ring-affine. Prompt coverage: D.4. Necessity moves a colimit preimage of 1 in the kernel to a common successor. Sufficiency extends module diagrams affinely and verifies that their ordinary colimit cocones are unchanged. This supplies the field criterion without an unproved coefficient substitution.

statement: A finite parallel family has a rational affine equalizer iff some integral simultaneous annihilator has nonzero augmentation. It has an F_p-affine equalizer iff an integral combination annihilates every difference modulo p and has augmentation nonzero modulo p.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Proposition D.15, p. 20; TOTEX_paper.tex, label main:field-tests
depends_on: Clearing finite denominators and lifting finite field coefficients
notes: Label main:field-tests. Prompt coverage: D.4. These are separate finite-support tests. The modular kernel is formed after reduction; it need not be the tensor product of the integral kernel.

statement: Total⇒exact remains undecided separately for integral abelian, Q-vector-space, and F_p-vector-space colimits. Pairs are settled in every coefficient case, and the first unhandled case is a triple satisfying the corresponding simultaneous affine equations.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Obstruction D.16, p. 20; TOTEX_paper.tex, label main:stable-open

The free-resolution attempt fails at replacing colim_Set U Z[S] by U Z[colim_Set S]; those sets need not coincide. No arbitrary modules are silently substituted for permutation coefficients.

statement: For total A and F:A→Ab, the set presheaf G_F(P)=colim_Set Hom(P,F(a)) satisfies LG_F≃colim_A^{D(Z)≥0}F(a), hence π_i(LG_F)=L_i colim_A F. In particular G_F(Z^n)=colim_Set (UF)^n.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Theorem D.17, p. 21; TOTEX_paper.tex, label main:reflection
depends_on: A.1 (A:R1); D.12 (main:stable); Badzioch (2002), Theorems 1.3 and 6.4 (opened); Lurie, Higher Algebra, Theorem 1.2.3.7 (opened)
notes: Label main:reflection. Prompt coverage: D.5. R1 is applied only to the actual set functors Hom(P,F(−)). Naturality in P gives the presheaf comparison; the reflection preserves colimits. Rigidification and Dold–Kan identify the target with connective animated abelian groups.

statement: For any set presheaf G on finite-rank free abelian groups, define E_G with arrows f:(P,x)→(Q,y) satisfying G(f)y=x. Then π_i(LG) is the homology of C_n(G)=⊕_{(P0,x0)→⋯→(Pn,xn)}P0 with bar faces. Thus LG is discrete iff every positive finite-support cycle is a finite-support boundary.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Proposition D.18, p. 21; TOTEX_paper.tex, label main:reflection-criterion
depends_on: D.12 (main:stable); Homotopy-colimit density of representables with explicit initial factorization objects; Badzioch (2002), Theorems 1.3 and 6.4, and Lurie, Higher Algebra, Theorem 1.2.3.7 (opened)
notes: Label main:reflection-criterion. Prompt coverage: D.5. This is an intrinsic necessary-and-sufficient chain criterion in G's values, restriction maps, and integer matrices; it does not refer back to the reflection operation. It uses the general rigidification/Dold–Kan setup, not the totality hypothesis of the preceding theorem.

statement: The set presheaf G(P)=Hom(P,Z)/{±1} has π_{2j}(LG)=Z/2 for every j≥0 and π_{2j+1}(LG)=0. Therefore a set-valued presheaf, even a two-element orbit quotient of one representable, need not have discrete reflection.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Example D.19, p. 22; TOTEX_paper.tex, label main:sign

notes: Label main:sign. Prompt coverage: D.5. This refutes the unrestricted assertion for all set presheaves. The fixed zero orbit is replaced by a point before reflection; L sends its representable to zero. The program checks degrees through ten, while the periodic proof establishes all degrees. It is not a counterexample for G_F over a total A.

statement: Whether every presheaf G_F arising from a total shape has discrete reflection remains exactly the integral main question. No such total-shape presentation of the sign-orbit counterexample is obtained.
where_proved: TOTEX_paper.pdf, Obstruction D.20, p. 23; TOTEX_paper.tex, label main:special-presheaves
notes: Label main:special-presheaves. Prompt coverage: D.5, A, R6. The sign presheaf's natural element category has a weakly terminal object and unequalizable endomorphisms id and −id, so R5 excludes its totality. The smallest unhandled affine test remains the triple.

statement: Totality and exactness of abelian colimits are both preserved by finite products, Grothendieck opfibrations with the corresponding property on base and fibres, and passage to nonempty connected components of categories of elements; final images also preserve both.

statement: If u:A→B is an ordinary final functor, totality of A implies totality of B, and exactness of Ab-valued colimits over A implies exactness over B.

statement: A nonempty full cosieve V in a total A is total; if abelian colimits over A are exact, so are those over V.

statement: Ordinary localization A→A[S^{-1}] preserves totality and exact abelian colimits. Both properties are invariant under idempotent completion A→Kar(A).

statement: For a nonempty filtered diagram of small categories whose transition functors are final, every structural functor A_i→colim_I A_i is final. If one stage is total, or has exact abelian colimits, the colimit has the corresponding property.

statement: Nonempty full cosieves, ordinary localizations, idempotent completion, and filtered colimits along final transitions all preserve both totality and Aff_Z-filteredness. None of the four operations separates their preservation behavior.

statement: For every finite m≥1, Aff_Z(W_m) is filtered and W_m is total with exact abelian colimits, but W_m is neither filtered nor sifted. W2,W3,W4 are pairwise nonequivalent.

statement: Let $\mathcal C_\delta$ have as objects all pairs $([n],E)$, where $n\geq1$, $[n]=\{1<\cdots<n\}$, $E\subseteq\binom{[n]}3$, and \[ \delta_X(U)=2|U|-3|\{e\in E:e\subseteq U\}|>0 \quad(\varnothing\ne U\subseteq[n]). \] An arrow $f:X\to Y$ is a strictly increasing injection which is an induced hypergraph embedding and satisfies \[ \delta_Y(U)>\delta_Y(fX) \quad(fX\subsetneq U\subseteq Y). \] Identities and composition are those of functions. This is a small, nonempty connected total category. Let $V$ be the one-point object, let $W$ be the ordered three-point object with its unique triple as an edge, and let $v_i:V\to W$ select its $i$th vertex. The three arrows $v_1,v_2,v_3$ have no integral affine post-equalizer. Consequently $\colim_{\mathcal C_\delta}:\Ab^{\mathcal C_\delta}\to\Ab$ is not exact.
his_places: II ms. 36-36ter; XII ms. 88-89 (totality does not imply exactness)
notes: Explicit small category of positive ordered 3-uniform hypergraphs and strict closed embeddings. All covariant set actions are covered; the named triple has no affine equalizer. Stable label: A:main

statement: For every small category $A$, including the empty category and categories with several components, the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$ is exact; \item $\colim_A:(\Q\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})^A\to\Q\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is exact and, for every prime $p$, the functor $\colim_A:(\F_p\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})^A\to\F_p\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is exact. \end{enumerate} No totality hypothesis is needed. Consequently, Parts A.1 and A.2 taken together ask equivalent universal questions. A negative answer to A.1 necessarily gives a failure over $\Q$ or over at least one prime field, although the obstructing diagram need not remain the same after reduction.
notes: All small categories; no totality assumption. Reduction, not a decision of the main question. Stable label: A:fieldwise

statement: The same category $\mathcal C_\delta$ has nonexact colimits over every nonzero unital coefficient ring $R$. In particular the implication from totality to exactness is false over $\Q$ and over $\F_p$ for each prime $p$, with one category and one triple working simultaneously for all these coefficients. Explicitly, put \[ D_R:R[\mathcal C_\delta(W,-)]\longrightarrow R[\mathcal C_\delta(V,-)]^2, \qquad g\longmapsto(gv_2-gv_1,gv_3-gv_1). \] Then $D_R$ is injective, $Q_R=\operatorname{coker}D_R$ has projective dimension exactly one, and $T_1(Q_R)\cong R$.
notes: One total category and one triple work over every nonzero unital ring, in particular Q and every F_p. The column cokernel has projective dimension exactly one and T1=R. Stable label: A:coefficients

statement: For a small category $A$, let $\mathcal R_A$ be the smallest class of covariant integral modules containing every $\mathbb Z[H]$, for $H:A\to\mathrm{Set}$, and closed under extensions, kernels of epimorphisms between members, arbitrary direct sums, direct summands, filtered colimits, and $F\mapsto F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z[H]$. Every member of $\mathcal R_A$ is objectwise torsion-free. There is a finite filtered category $A$ and three parallel arrows $a_0,a_1,a_2:p\to q$ for which \[ Q_a=\operatorname{coker}\bigl(P_q\longrightarrow P_p^2, \ t\longmapsto(t(a_1-a_0),t(a_2-a_0))\bigr) \notin\mathcal R_A. \] Thus the first proposed target of approach P1 cannot work uniformly, even for filtered categories. This does not refute P1's alternative of finding a different module with the same $T_1$, and it is not a separator between totality and exactness.
notes: Four objects and seventeen arrows with a terminal object. Q_a(x)=Z^2 plus Z/3. Alternative modules with the same T1 are not excluded. Stable label: A:P1-torsion

statement: There is a small filtered category $A$ and a triple $a_0,a_1,a_2:p\to q$ such that its rational column module \[ Q_a=\operatorname{coker}\bigl( \mathbb Q[A(q,-)]\longrightarrow\mathbb Q[A(p,-)]^2,\quad t\longmapsto(t(a_1-a_0),t(a_2-a_0))\bigr) \] does not belong to the smallest class of rational diagrams containing all permutation modules and closed under extensions, kernels of epimorphisms, arbitrary direct sums, direct summands, filtered colimits, and tensoring with permutation modules. This strengthens the integral torsion obstruction: all values of this example are rational vector spaces. It does not refute the alternative in P1 of using another module with the same $T_1$. Moreover, the same category and triple give an integral column module with torsion-free values which lies outside the original integral resolving class.
notes: Four-object category with terminal object and one infinite-cyclic automorphism group. Rational obstruction and integral torsion-free strengthening; the even-power invariant includes tensor-permutation closure. Not a separator. Stable label: B:P1-rational

statement: Let $A$ be a small category with finite hom-sets. Suppose that any two objects have a common successor. Suppose also that $A$ has the following morphism Ramsey property: for any objects $p,q$ and positive integer $c$ there is an object $r$ such that every coloring \[ \chi:A(p,r)\longrightarrow\{1,\ldots,c\} \] admits $g:q\to r$ for which $\chi$ is constant on $g\circ A(p,q)$. Then $A$ has exact colimits in abelian groups. More precisely, if $a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$ and $k\geq1$, every target $r$ with the stated Ramsey property for $p,q,c=(3k+1)^k$ admits an integral affine combination $t\in\mathbb Z[A(q,r)]$ satisfying $ta_0=\cdots=ta_k$.
notes: Proved: a Ramsey criterion for integral exactness Stable label: OG:Ramsey-exact

statement: It is used above only to give an elementary Smith normal form proof of extension to the circle. Divisibility makes $\mathbb T$ an injective abelian group, so the same argument works without finite hom-sets if one invokes that standard injectivity theorem. The finite version already covers the ordered-graph application below.
notes: Proved: scope of the finite-hom-set hypothesis Stable label: OG:finite-hom-scope

statement: Let $\mathcal G$ have one representative of each finite linearly ordered simple graph as objects and increasing induced graph embeddings as arrows, composed as functions. Then $\mathcal G$ has exact colimits in abelian groups. In particular it is not a counterexample to totality implying exactness.
notes: Proved: ordered finite graphs are exact Stable label: OG:exact

statement: For the three embeddings $v_0,v_1,v_2$ of the one-vertex graph into $q$, an integral affine equalizer exists in the ordered graph $r_6$ on $\{0<\cdots<5\}$ with edge set \[ \{01,12,13,15,23,24,34,35\}. \] It is \[ t=(012)-(015)+(124)-(134)+(235). \]

statement: For the embeddings $e_0,e_1$ of the ordered edge into the two edges of $q$, an integral affine equalizer exists in the ordered graph $r_7$ on $\{0<\cdots<6\}$ with edge set \[ \{01,12,23,35,56,14,45\}. \] It is \[ t=(012)+(123)+(235)+(356)-(014)-(145)-(456). \]
