statement: Let $C$ be a skeleton of the category of nonempty finite sets with an independent linear order and cyclic order, whose arrows are injections preserving both orders. Cyclic orders on one or two points are taken to be unique. This small category is neither total nor exact. More precisely, $BC$ is simply connected and $H_2(BC;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$, and there is a five-arrow parallel family with no affine equalizer over any nonzero commutative ring. No assertion that $C$ is quasi-filtered is made.
notes: Refuted: the linear--cyclic order candidate Stable label: A:cyclic-linear

statement: A small category $A$ has the finite-pattern morphism Ramsey property if, for every $p,q\in A$, finite subset $S\subset A(p,q)$, and positive integer $c$, there is $r\in A$ such that every coloring \[ \chi:A(p,r)\longrightarrow\{1,\ldots,c\} \] admits $g:q\to r$ for which $\chi$ is constant on $gS$. When all hom-sets are finite, this is equivalent to the morphism Ramsey property in Theorem~\ref{OG:Ramsey-exact}: take $S=A(p,q)$.
notes: Proved: agreement of the two Ramsey formulations for finite hom-sets Stable label: CD:FPR

statement: Let $A$ be a small nonempty category with common successors. The following are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item Every contravariant diagram $X:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathrm{CompHaus}$ of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces has a nonempty strict inverse limit. \item $A$ has the finite-pattern morphism Ramsey property. \end{enumerate} No bound on the hom-sets is assumed.
notes: Proved: compact inverse limits and finite-pattern Ramsey Stable label: CD:compact-Ramsey

statement: A nonempty small category with common successors satisfying either condition of Theorem~\ref{CD:compact-Ramsey} has exact abelian colimits.
notes: Proved: the compact assertion implies integral exactness Stable label: CD:compact-exact

statement: Let $A$ be nonempty, connected, and quasi-filtered. Every contravariant diagram $X:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Set$ of nonempty finite sets with $|X(a)|\leq N$ for one finite integer $N$ has a nonempty inverse limit.
notes: One uniform finite size bound; unbounded fibres not covered. Stable label: CD:bounded-fibres

statement: Let $A=\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$, which is exact and total, and let $B(n)$ be the free Boolean algebra on the generators $x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}$, also regarded as its associated Boolean ring with addition given by symmetric difference. An increasing injection $f:n\to m$ acts by $x_i\mapsto x_{f(i)}$. These are injective unital Boolean-algebra homomorphisms: the corresponding restriction maps on the sets of Boolean valuations are surjective. In $B(2)$ the elements $x_0,x_1$ have the same class in $\colim_A^{\Set}UB$, since the two maps $1\to2$ carry the sole generator to them. Nevertheless, with $c=x_0$, the pairs $(c,x_0)$ and $(c,x_1)$ lie in different components of $\El_A(UB\times UB)$. Equality of the two coordinates is preserved and reflected by every structure map; it holds for the first pair and fails for the second. The failure persists for the abelian colimit after pinning $c$. Consider the component $E$ of $\El_A UB$ containing $(2,x_0)$. Its objects are exactly the pairs $(n,x_j)$. Indeed renaming variables sends a Boolean expression to a generator only if that expression was itself a generator, as can be checked on valuations. On $E$, evaluation at the valuation which sends $x_j$ to $1$ and all other generators to $0$ defines a natural homomorphism of additive groups \[ B(n)\longrightarrow\F_2. \] For an arrow $f:(n,x_j)\to(m,x_{f(j)})$, the target valuation restricts to the specified source valuation, proving naturality. At $(2,x_0)$ this map takes $x_0$ to $1$ and $x_1$ to $0$. Consequently $x_0$ and $x_1$ remain distinct in the abelian colimit over $E$. Thus moving to a category of elements in order to hold a multiplicative coefficient fixed need not preserve even a set-colimit relation available before that move. In a proposed Boolean-algebra argument, one must prove the needed lifted tuple relations; totality alone cannot be cited for their existence. This example does not rule out a different homological argument exploiting the full Boolean identity.
notes: An exact total category can lose an original set-colimit relation after passage to a component of elements that fixes a coefficient. Stable label: CD:pinning-counterexample

statement: Totality does not imply either equivalent compact-limit or finite-pattern Ramsey condition of Theorem~\ref{CD:compact-Ramsey}. In particular there is a countable total category with common successors admitting a contravariant diagram of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces whose inverse limit is empty.
notes: The former missing implication is false: total C_delta is nonexact and therefore cannot satisfy the equivalent compact/Ramsey conditions. Stable label: CD:unresolved

statement: Let $A$ be either a repaired AKR category $K^*$ covered by Proposition~\ref{C:akr-all-rings}, or the ordered predimension category $\mathcal C_\delta$. For every object $X$ and every finitely supported family of nonnegative real coefficients $(t_g)_{g:W\to X}$ with $\sum_g t_g=1$, put \[ \mu_i(v)=\sum_{g:\,gv_i=v}t_g\quad (v\in A(V,X),\ i=1,2,3). \] Then \[ \|\mu_2-\mu_1\|_1+\|\mu_3-\mu_1\|_1\geq1. \] In particular the initial triple has no arbitrarily accurate simultaneous equalizers obtained from probability combinations of ordinary arrows, even as the target varies.
notes: All admissible repaired AKR categories and the total predimension category; probability combinations have total marginal discrepancy at least one. Stable label: CC:positive-gap

statement: There is a nonempty connected quasi-filtered small category $A$ and a contravariant diagram of nonempty finite-dimensional compact convex sets, with continuous affine transition maps, whose strict inverse limit is empty. One may take $A=K^*$ as above, or the countable category $A=\mathcal C_\delta$, which is total by Theorem~\ref{A:predimension-total}. Thus the proposed implication fails even under totality.
notes: The predimension example is total. Nonempty finite-dimensional compact convex potential sets can have empty strict inverse limit even under totality. Stable label: CC:convex-counterexample

statement: Let $A$ be a nonempty connected small quasi-filtered category, and let $M:A\to\Ab$ satisfy $|M(a)|\leq N$ for every object $a$, for one finite integer $N$. Then $T_1^A(M)=0$. If $A$ is total, then $T_i^A(M)=0$ for every $i>0$. Consequently, a prime-field column module $Q_a$ with nonzero first derived colimit over a quasi-filtered category must have unbounded dimensions as the object varies.
notes: A single uniform bound on the cardinalities is essential. Quasi-filteredness gives T1 vanishing; totality gives all positive degrees. Unbounded finite-valued diagrams are not covered. Stable label: A:uniform-finite-coefficients

statement: The relation $\leq_d$ is preserved by restriction to subsets, is transitive, and is closed under finite intersections inside an ambient object. Free amalgams of $d$-closed embeddings are positive-predimension hypergraphs, and both factors are $d$-closed in the amalgam. The orders can be amalgamated. In particular, $\mathcal C_\delta$ satisfies condition I and has common successors.
notes: Finite ordered simple 3-uniform hypergraphs, delta=2|V|-3|E|, strict d-closed induced embeddings. Closure, composition and free amalgamation proved directly. Stable label: A:predimension-amalgam

statement: Let $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ be arrows of $\mathcal C_\delta$. Choose $n\geq2$ bounding the vertex lengths of the nonfixed paths of the partial bijection $f(x)\mapsto g(x)$, and put $w=2n-2$. For $k\geq n$, let $Z$ be the covered, actual-length repaired point necklace of Lemma~\ref{C:necklace-set-colimit}, of length $s=4k+1$, with copies $\alpha_i:T\to Z$. Give $Z$ precisely the hyperedges that occur in those copies. If \[ s>w\bigl(\delta(T)+2|S|\bigr), \tag{PD} \] then $Z$ is a positive-predimension hypergraph and every $\alpha_i$ is an induced embedding with $d$-closed image.
notes: Explicit bound s>(2n-2)(delta(T)+2|S|); proof counts first-appearance indices, and proves inducedness and strict relative positivity for every subset. Stable label: A:predimension-necklace

statement: The category $\mathcal C_\delta$ is quasi-filtered. The same is true of its full subcategory consisting of objects in which every point and every hyperedge is $d$-closed.
notes: Both the full positive-predimension category and its full point-and-edge-closed subcategory; all parallel pairs. Stable label: A:predimension-quasi

statement: Let $V$ be one point, let $W$ be the ordered three-point single-edge hypergraph, and let $v_1,v_2,v_3:V\to W$ be its three point arrows. In either category of Proposition~\ref{A:predimension-quasi}, this triple has no affine post-equalizer over any nonzero unital ring $R$. For \[ D:R[A(W,-)]\longrightarrow R[A(V,-)]^2, \qquad D(g)=(gv_2-gv_1,gv_3-gv_1), \qquad Q=\operatorname{coker}D, \] one has $T_1^A(Q)\cong R$. In particular neither category is exact.
notes: Actual representable arrows only, arbitrary nonzero unital coefficient rings. The column is injective and T1 of its cokernel equals the coefficient ring. Stable label: A:predimension-triple

statement: Let $B$ be a positive-predimension hypergraph and let $x,c$ be two distinct vertices of $B$. Adjoin five distinct new vertices $r,s,a,b,d$ and precisely the three new hyperedges \[ \{x,r,a\},\qquad \{r,s,b\},\qquad \{s,c,d\}. \tag{LP} \] Then $B$ is $d$-closed in the resulting positive-predimension hypergraph. No assumption that $\{x,c\}$ is $d$-closed is needed.
notes: Proved: adjoining a loose path of length three Stable label: A:predimension-three-path

statement: Let $C$ be a loose hypergraph cycle of length $\ell\geq4$: it has binary vertices $b_0,\ldots,b_{\ell-1}$, distinct private vertices $p_0,\ldots,p_{\ell-1}$, and edges $\{b_i,b_{i+1},p_i\}$ with cyclic indices. Then $C$ has positive predimension, and every point and every hyperedge is $d$-closed.
notes: Proved: atoms in a loose cycle Stable label: A:predimension-loose-cycle

statement: For either category $A$ of Proposition~\ref{A:predimension-quasi}, augmentation induces an isomorphism \[ \operatorname{colim}_A K\xrightarrow{\ \epsilon\ }\Z. \] Consequently, for $H=A(V,-)/(ev_1\sim ev_2)$, \[ H_2(B\operatorname{El}_A H;\Z)=0. \] In particular, the binary class used to prove nontotality for the selected generated AKR category vanishes upon passage to this full predimension category.
notes: Proved: the binary cycle colimit is exactly its augmentation Stable label: A:predimension-binary-colimit

statement: For either category $A$ of Proposition~\ref{A:predimension-quasi}, there is an endofunctor $F:A\to A$ with natural transformations \[ \eta:\operatorname{id}_A\longrightarrow F, \qquad \gamma:\operatorname{const}_V\longrightarrow F. \] The map $\eta_X$ includes $X$, and $\gamma_X$ selects a new centre $c_X$. For every $V$-arrow $x:V\to X$, the two vertices $\eta_Xx$ and $\gamma_X$ are joined by a directed binary path of three actual $W$-arrows in $F(X)$.
notes: Proved: the path cone is a functor Stable label: A:predimension-cone-functor

statement: Let $A$ be either category of Proposition~\ref{A:predimension-quasi}. The categories of elements of each of the two actions \[ H_{12}=A(V,-)/(ev_1\sim ev_2), \qquad H_{123}=A(V,-)/(ev_1\sim ev_2\sim ev_3) \] have contractible classifying spaces. More generally this holds for every pointwise quotient $H$ of $H_{12}$. In particular all their positive-degree integral homology groups vanish. For the binary cycle functor $K$ of Proposition~\ref{A:predimension-binary-colimit}, \[ T_i^A(K)=0\qquad(i>0). \]
notes: Proved: contractibility of the binary and triple element categories Stable label: A:predimension-cone-contracts

statement: In either category $A$ of Proposition~\ref{A:predimension-quasi}, let $B,C\leq_d D$ and put $F=B\cap C$. Empty subsets are permitted as formal amalgamation bases. Suppose $d_0,d_1:D\to E$ are arrows agreeing on $F$. There is an arrow $E\to Z$ and a finite sequence of arrows \[ a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{2N}:D\longrightarrow Z, \] whose endpoints are the given $d_0,d_1$ followed by $E\to Z$, such that \[ a_{2j}|_B=a_{2j+1}|_B, \qquad a_{2j+1}|_C=a_{2j+2}|_C \quad(0\leq j<N). \]
notes: Finite explicit bridge for arbitrary closed endpoint embeddings agreeing on B intersection C; all-subset predimension and order bounds proved, including degenerate bases. Stable label: A:predimension-alternating-bridge

statement: Let $\mathbb M$ be a countable strong Fra\"iss\'e limit for either category $A$ of Proposition~\ref{A:predimension-quasi}, and let $G=\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb M)$, preserving the order. For a finite $d$-closed subset $B$, write $G_B$ for its pointwise stabilizer. Then for all finite closed $B,C$, \[ \langle G_B,G_C\rangle=G_{B\cap C}. \] The equality is algebraic and in particular implies the corresponding topological-generation assertion.
notes: The generated subgroup of pointwise stabilizers of B and C equals the pointwise stabilizer of their intersection. Stable label: A:predimension-stabilizers

statement: Every open subgroup of $G$ is the pointwise stabilizer of a finite $d$-closed subset of $\mathbb M$, possibly the empty subset. Such a subset can be chosen contained in every finite closed subset whose pointwise stabilizer is contained in the given group.
notes: Every open subgroup is the pointwise stabilizer of a finite closed set, possibly empty; finite order eliminates the setwise/pointwise ambiguity. Stable label: A:predimension-open-subgroups

statement: Let $A$ be either ordered predimension category of Proposition~\ref{A:predimension-quasi}. Let $M$ be its countable strongly homogeneous rich limit, let $G=\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ with the topology of pointwise convergence, and for a finite $d$-closed substructure $B\subseteq M$ put \[ G_B=\{g\in G:g|_B=\id_B\}. \] Assume that every open subgroup of $G$ equals $G_F$ for some finite $d$-closed $F\subseteq M$, allowing $F=\varnothing$. Then $A$ is total. This conclusion concerns every covariant $H:A\to\Set$, with no finiteness or injectivity assumption on $H$.
depends_on: A.21 [A:predimension-amalgam]; A.23 [A:predimension-quasi]; Source: EvansHubickaNesetril2019; Source: GoerssJardine2009
notes: Arbitrary set actions: eventual-equality quotient and smooth-action saturation are homotopy final. No finiteness or injectivity restriction remains. Stable label: A:predimension-stabilizer-criterion

statement: Both $\mathcal C_\delta$ and its full subcategory whose raw points and hyperedges are all $d$-closed are total. For each of these categories and every covariant $H:A\to\Set$, every component of $\El_AH$ is weakly contractible. In each category the three point arrows $V\rightrightarrows W$ of Proposition~\ref{A:predimension-triple} have no affine equalizer over any nonzero unital ring $R$, and the displayed column cokernel $Q_R$ satisfies $T_1(Q_R)\cong R$. Thus both categories are separators, simultaneously for integral, rational and every prime-field coefficient system.
notes: Both full ordered positive-predimension categories are total and nonexact over every nonzero unital ring. Complete separator theorem; independently audited. Stable label: A:predimension-total

statement: In the total category $\mathcal C_\delta$ of Theorem~\ref{A:main}, the three ordinary point arrows $v_1,v_2,v_3:V\to W$ have no affine equalizer over any nonzero unital ring. In particular, for integral coefficients, \[ T_1\!\left(\operatorname{coker} \left(P_W\longrightarrow P_V^2,\quad t\longmapsto(t(v_2-v_1),t(v_3-v_1))\right)\right)\cong\Z. \] Three is the smallest possible obstructing ordinary family size in a total category.
notes: Refuted by the same total category and its three closed point arrows. Three is the smallest possible obstructing ordinary family size. Stable label: B:triple-question

statement: Let $a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$ be a finite family of ordinary arrows in an arbitrary small category, and let $z_i=a_i-a_0$ for $1\leq i\leq k$. Put \[ d:P_q^k\longrightarrow P_p,\qquad (t_i)\longmapsto\sum_i t_i z_i,\qquad K=\ker d, \] and let $H$ be $A(p,-)$ modulo all relations $ca_i\sim ca_0$. Then $\mathbb Z[H]=\operatorname{coker}d$ canonically, and \begin{align*} T_1(\mathbb Z[H])&\cong \operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{colim}K\xrightarrow{\epsilon^k}\mathbb Z^k),\\ T_2(\mathbb Z[H])&\cong \ker(\operatorname{colim}K\xrightarrow{\epsilon^k}\mathbb Z^k),\\ T_j(\mathbb Z[H])&\cong T_{j-2}(K)\quad(j\geq3). \end{align*} Consequently, for total $A$, $\epsilon^k$ is an isomorphism and $K$ is colimit-acyclic. For $k=1$ the module $J_i=P_qz_i\subseteq P_p$ is colimit-acyclic and has zero colimit.
notes: Proved: the row calculation used below Stable label: B:row-audit

statement: Let $A$ be total and $a_0,a_1,a_2:p\to q$. Put $K_i=\ker(P_q\xrightarrow{z_i}P_p)$ and $L=K_1\cap K_2$. Then the surjection in TOTEX B.1 is a canonical isomorphism \[ T_1\bigl(P_q/(K_1+K_2)\bigr)\ \cong\ \mathbb Z/\epsilon(L). \]
notes: Both derivations checked, including the sign between their explicit maps. Stable label: B:lead1

statement: Let $A$ satisfy I; neither connectedness nor nonemptiness is required in this proposition. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $\operatorname{colim}_A:\mathrm{Ab}^A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is exact; \item for every $p,r\in A$ and every $z\in\mathbb Z[A(p,r)]$ with $\operatorname{aug}z=0$, some affine $t:r\to s$ satisfies $tz=0$. \end{enumerate} For every small $A$, every such $p,r,z$, and $L_z=\ker(P_r\xrightarrow{t\mapsto tz}P_p)$, one has canonically \[ T_1(P_p/P_rz)\cong\mathbb Z/\epsilon(L_z). \]
notes: The Tor formula requires augmentation zero; I is required for the criterion, connectedness is not. Stable label: B:lead2

statement: For every small category $A$, every integer $k\geq0$ and every family $a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$, put \[ d^{\mathrm t}:P_q\longrightarrow P_p^k, \quad t\longmapsto(tz_i)_{i=1}^k, \qquad Q_a=\operatorname{coker}d^{\mathrm t}, \quad L=\ker d^{\mathrm t}. \] Then canonically \begin{align*} T_1(Q_a)&\cong\mathbb Z/\epsilon(L),\\ T_2(Q_a)&\cong\ker(\operatorname{colim}L\to\mathbb Z),\\ T_i(Q_a)&\cong T_{i-2}(L)\qquad(i\geq3). \end{align*} If objects in the component of $q$ have common successors, the family has an affine equalizer if and only if $T_1(Q_a)=0$. In the covariant-module presentation, $Q_a$ has $k$ generators $x_i$ at $p$ and one relation $\sum_i(a_i-a_0)x_i=0$ at $q$.
notes: No category hypothesis for the formulas; common successors for the equalizer criterion; k=0 included. Stable label: B:lead3

statement: Suppose $A$ is nonempty and connected and satisfies I and IV. For $M:A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ and $\alpha,\beta\in M(q)$, equality of their classes in $\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{Set}}_A UM$ implies that an affine $t:q\to s$ satisfies $t\alpha=t\beta$ in $M(s)$. Moreover $A$ is exact if and only if, for every such $M,q,\alpha,\beta$, equality in $\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{Ab}}_A M$ implies the same affine equalizability.
notes: Proved: the precise assertions of Lead 4 Stable label: B:lead4

statement: The comparison map \[ \operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{Set}}_A UM\longrightarrow U\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{Ab}}_A M \] is surjective under the common-successor hypothesis: transport the finite sum representing an abelian colimit element to one object and add there. The two assertions above precisely locate the distinction in its fibres: set equality is already sufficient, while abelian equality may identify additional components. This does not identify exactness with finite-product preservation of the set-colimit functor. For example, for $A=\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$, $p=[0]$, and $M=P_p$, the elements $2[a]-[b]$ for distinct $a,b:p\to q$ and $[a]$ have the same abelian-colimit class. Ordinary increasing injections preserve the number and coefficients of nonzero basis terms, so these two elements lie in different set-colimit components. Nevertheless $A$ is exact, by the already audited Isbell example. Thus the final phrase of Lead 4 is valid as motivation for the difference between the two colimits, and would be false if read as the asserted equivalence with siftedness or with injectivity of this comparison.
notes: Exactness is not equivalent to siftedness or injectivity of the set-to-abelian comparison. Stable label: B:lead4-scope

statement: Let $A$ be a nonempty category in which every pair of objects has a common successor, and let $F:A\to\mathrm{Ab}$. For $\kappa\in F(s)$, its colimit class is zero if and only if there are an ordinary arrow $u:s\to y$, finitely many ordinary parallel pairs $e_j,e'_j:x_j\rightrightarrows y$, and $k_j\in F(x_j)$, such that \[ F(u)\kappa=\sum_j\bigl(F(e_j)-F(e'_j)\bigr)k_j\quad\hbox{in }F(y). \] In particular Lead 5(ii) holds; its condition I can be weakened to common successors.
notes: Common successors suffice. Stable label: B:zero-normal-form

statement: Let $A$ be total and let $a_0,a_1,a_2:p\to q$. Use $z_i,K_i,K,L$ as in Lemma~\ref{B:row-audit} and Proposition~\ref{B:lead1}, and put $K_3=\ker(P_q\xrightarrow{a_2-a_1}P_p)$. Choose affine pair equalizers $\rho_1\in K_1(s)$, $\rho_2\in K_2(s)$ and $\rho_3\in K_3(s)$ at a common object $s$. Then \[ \kappa=(\rho_1-\rho_3,\rho_3-\rho_2)\in K(s) \] has zero class in $\operatorname{colim}K$. If an affine $t:s\to r$ kills $\kappa$, then $t\rho_1=t\rho_2=t\rho_3$ is an affine equalizer of the triple. Such a $t$ exists whenever the finitely many pairs in a normal form of Lemma~\ref{B:zero-normal-form} have a common affine equalizer. In particular, a normal form with at most one summand implies the existence of such a $t$. Finally the natural morphism \[ \psi:K_1\oplus K_2\oplus K_3\longrightarrow K, \qquad(k_1,k_2,k_3)\longmapsto(k_1-k_3,k_2+k_3) \] has kernel canonically isomorphic to $L$, and \[ T_1(K/\operatorname{im}\psi)\cong\mathbb Z/\epsilon(L). \]
notes: Proved: Lead 5(i), (iii), and (iv) Stable label: B:lead5

statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{B:lead5}, suppose the triple has no affine equalizer. Its class $[\kappa]$ in $\operatorname{colim}I$ is the nonzero generator of $\ker(\operatorname{colim}I\to\operatorname{colim}K) \cong\mathbb Z/\epsilon(L)$. It cannot have a normal form in which every $k_j$ belongs to $I(x_j)$, and it cannot have a normal form whose pairs have a common affine equalizer. In particular every one-term normal form is impossible.
notes: A bar chain with module coefficients is intended, not nonzero H1 of BA. Stable label: B:mixed-cycle-obstruction

statement: For the repaired AKR construction and every admissible choice of its parameters and targets, \[ H_2\!\left(\El_{K^*} \bigl(K^*(V,-)/(cv_1\sim cv_2)\bigr);\Z\right)\ne0. \] Every attachment preserves the whole old colimit of the binary cycle functor. In particular, the first-stage class $\kappa_+-\kappa_-$ survives the infinite union, and every such category $K^*$ is not total.
notes: Every admissible repaired C.1 construction. Every attachment preserves the old binary cycle colimit; the first-stage H2 generator survives the infinite union. Stable label: C:survival-question

statement: Let $A$ and $D$ be small categories, let $u:D\to A$ be a functor, and let \[ R=\mathop{\rm colim}_{d\in D}A(-,u(d)):A^{\rm op}\longrightarrow\mathrm{Set}. \] Assume that every connected component of every comma category $x\downarrow u$ is weakly contractible. Form $A'$ by adjoining one object $Z$, by setting $A'(x,Z)=R(x)$ for $x\in A$, by allowing no arrows from $Z$ to $A$, and by setting $A'(Z,Z)=\{1_Z\}$; composition with arrows of $A$ is the presheaf action of $R$. Let $H':A'\to\mathrm{Set}$ be any covariant functor, and put $H=H'|_A$. Define the two-sided category $E(R,H)$ to have objects $(x,r,k)$ with $x\in A$, $r\in R(x)$ and $k\in H(x)$. An arrow $(x,r,k)\to(y,s,l)$ is an arrow $b:x\to y$ of $A$ satisfying $R(b)s=r$ and $H(b)k=l$. Then the functor \[ F:\operatorname{El}_D(u^*H)\longrightarrow E(R,H),\qquad (d,k)\longmapsto(u(d),[d,1_{u(d)}],k) \] which sends an arrow $\delta:d\to d'$ to $u(\delta)$ is a weak equivalence on nerves. For every $h\in H'(Z)$ the old comma link \[ L_h=(\operatorname{El}_A H)\downarrow (Z,h) \] is a full union of connected components of $E(R,H)$. If $e=\dim ND<\infty$, then $H_j(BL_h;\mathbb Z)=0$ for $j>e$ and the inclusion induces an injection \[ H_j(B\operatorname{El}_A H;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H_j(B\operatorname{El}_{A'}H';\mathbb Z) \quad(j>e). \] The assertion also holds with arbitrary constant coefficients. If $D$ is empty, $R$ and all links are empty and adjoining $Z$ adds only isolated objects to the category of elements.
notes: Proved: the link comparison, with its necessary hypothesis Stable label: C:link-comparison

statement: Consider a cyclic quasi-filter indexing graph with copies of $S$ at its vertices and copies of $T$ on its edges, the two maps on each edge being chosen from a parallel pair $f,g:T\rightrightarrows S$. If an arrow $c:x\to T$ satisfies $fc=gc$, the component of $x\downarrow u$ containing these lifts has nonzero first integral homology. If $f$ and $g$ are monomorphisms, this component is precisely a subdivided circle. Consequently the comma hypothesis in Proposition~\ref{C:link-comparison} fails. In the repaired first-stage AKR quasi-filter for $v_1,v_2$, the last and first maps satisfy $\alpha_{4k}v_1=\alpha_0v_1$, so this obstruction occurs when quasi-filtering $(\alpha_0,\alpha_{4k})$ at the next stage.
notes: Proved: the equalizing-precomposition obstruction Stable label: C:link-obstruction

statement: For every admissible choice in the repaired AKR Construction C.1, for every nonzero unital commutative ring $R$, and for every object $X$ of $K^*$, the $R$-linear map \[ R[K^*(W,X)]\longrightarrow R[K^*(V,X)]^2,\qquad t\longmapsto\bigl(t(v_2-v_1),t(v_3-v_1)\bigr) \] is injective. In particular, the three initial point maps have no $R$-affine equalizer. The same injectivity holds for finitely supported coefficients in an arbitrary abelian group, with the evident meaning of the two differences.
notes: Every admissible repaired construction, arbitrary abelian-group coefficients. Stable label: C:akr-all-rings

statement: Let $A'$ be obtained from $A$ by adjoining one new maximal object $Z$ with identity endomorphism only. Suppose a family $\alpha_i:T_i\to Z$ ($i\in I$, possibly infinite) generates all incoming arrows: every $b:X\to Z$, $X\in A$, can be written $\alpha_i c$ with $c:X\to T_i$ in $A$. For any covariant functor $F':A'\to\mathrm{Ab}$, write $F=F'|_A$ and $Q=\operatorname{colim}_A F$. Define homomorphisms \[ a:\bigoplus_{i\in I}F(T_i)\longrightarrow F'(Z),\quad (x_i)\longmapsto\sum_i F'(\alpha_i)x_i, \qquad b:\bigoplus_{i\in I}F(T_i)\longrightarrow Q,\quad (x_i)\longmapsto\sum_i[x_i]. \] Then, canonically, \[ \operatorname{colim}_{A'}F' \cong (Q\oplus F'(Z))/\{(b(x),-a(x)):x\in\bigoplus_iF(T_i)\}, \] \[ \ker(Q\to\operatorname{colim}_{A'}F')=b(\ker a). \] For the AKR action $H=h_V/(cv_1\sim cv_2)$, put $K(X)=\ker(\mathbb Z[A(W,X)]\xrightarrow{,v_2-v_1,} \mathbb Z[A(V,X)])$. Thus $K(X)$ is the integral cycle group of the graph whose vertices are $V$-arrows and whose edges are $W$-arrows, with edge $c$ directed from $cv_1$ to $cv_2$. For a quasi-filter attachment all $T_i=T$. Its old-to-new map on $H_2(B\operatorname{El}H)$ is injective if and only if \[ \sum_i\alpha_i\kappa_i=0\ \text{in }K(Z) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \left[\sum_i\kappa_i\right]=0\ \text{in }\operatorname{colim}_A K \] for every finitely supported family $\kappa_i\in K(T)$.
notes: Proved: an exact cycle-space test for one attachment Stable label: C:attachment-cycle-test

statement: The unqualified phrase ``the component is a circle'' in Lead~7 is false if it is read without the monomorphism hypothesis of the AKR application. Let $A$ have objects $x,T,S$, arrows \[ A(x,T)=\{c,d\},\qquad A(T,S)=\{f,g\},\qquad A(x,S)=\{h\}, \] identity endomorphisms only, no other arrows, and the four compositions $fc=fd=gc=gd=h$. Composition with identities is prescribed in the usual way. This is a complete finite category: there are no three composable nonidentity arrows, and the identity laws settle every remaining associativity equation. Take the five-vertex cyclic quasi-filter indexing graph ($k=1$). It has copies $S_i$ of $S$ and copies $T_i$ of $T$, with two arrows from $T_i$ to $S_i,S_{i+1}$ (cyclic indices), mapped by $u$ to $(g,f)$ for $i=0,1$, to $(g,g)$ for $i=2$, to $(f,g)$ for $i=3$, and to $(f,f)$ for $i=4$. The comma category $x\downarrow u$ has five $S$-vertices $(S_i,h)$ and ten $T$-vertices $(T_i,c),(T_i,d)$, and twenty nonidentity arrows. It is connected. Its nerve is a graph, with $H_1\cong\mathbb Z^{20-15+1} =\mathbb Z^6$; each $S$-vertex has valence four. Thus its component is neither isomorphic nor homotopy equivalent to a circle, although $fc=gc$ and its noncontractibility is exactly as asserted in the corrected proposition. The complete composition table, all typed composable triples, and these graph counts are checked by \texttt{akr\_nonmonic\_comma\_circle.py} and its supplied output.
notes: Three objects, eight arrows; comma graph H1=Z^6. Stable label: C:nonmonic-circle-counterexample

statement: There exists a small nonempty connected quasi-filtered category $A$ and a covariant functor $Q:A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ such that every $Q(X)$ is finitely generated free abelian, every $Q(g)$ is split injective with free abelian cokernel, and nevertheless \[ T_1(Q)\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad T_i(Q)=0\quad(i\geq2). \] One may take any repaired AKR category $A=K^*$ and \[ Q=\operatorname{coker}\bigl(D:P_W\longrightarrow P_V^2\bigr), \qquad D(t)=\bigl(t(v_2-v_1),t(v_3-v_1)\bigr). \] Thus pointwise freeness and split injectivity do not by themselves close the cycle-module colimit obstruction.
notes: Quasi-filtered AKR, finite free values, split injections, T1=Z; totality not asserted. Stable label: C:split-monic-counterexample

statement: For the same quasi-filtered category $A=K^*$ there is a covariant functor $\Gamma:A\to\mathrm{Grp}$ such that every $\Gamma(X)$ is a finitely generated free group and every transition map identifies its source with a free factor of its target, but the abelianization functor $\Gamma_{\rm ab}:A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ has $T_1(\Gamma_{\rm ab})\cong\mathbb Z$.
notes: Proved: the same obstruction with free groups and free-factor maps Stable label: C:free-group-counterexample

statement: There is a diagram of finitely generated free groups, with every transition a free-factor inclusion and with free group colimit, whose ordinary simplicial-set colimit of nerves has second integral homology $\mathbb Z$.
notes: Finite parallel-pair index, not quasi-filtered. Free values and free-factor transitions do not make the ordinary nerve colimit aspherical. Stable label: C:freefactor-nerve

statement: Let $A$ be a finite stage, or a full finite substage containing $V,W$ and every prescribed incoming generator and factorization for its retained targets, of the repaired AKR construction. Adjoin a single quasi-filter target $Z$ for $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ and write $A'$ for the resulting category. Put $s=4k+1$, where $k\geq n$, and write $\alpha_i:T\to Z$, $i\in\mathbb Z/s$, for its generating maps. All old objects and arrows remain unchanged. For an object $X$ let $G_X$ have vertices $A(V,X)$ and one directed edge $b$ from $bv_1$ to $bv_2$ for each $b\in A(W,X)$, using $A'$ when $X=Z$. Let $K(X)=H_1(G_X;\mathbb Z)$ and $Q=\operatorname{colim}_A K$. Let $F\subseteq G_S$ be the equalizer subgraph: its vertices are those $c:V\to S$ with $fc=gc$, and its edges are those $b:W\to S$ with $fb=gb$. Then \[ \ker\bigl(Q\longrightarrow\operatorname{colim}_{A'}K\bigr) =\left\langle [(g_\#-f_\#)\sigma]\ :\ \sigma\in C_1(G_S;\mathbb Z),\quad \partial\sigma=w-v,\quad v,w\in F_0\right\rangle. \tag{FP} \] Only pairs $v,w$ lying in the same component of $G_S$ occur. A path may be chosen for $\sigma$; reversing edges is represented by negative coefficients. The displayed difference is a cycle in $G_T$, and its class in $Q$ is independent of the chosen path. It is enough to choose one vertex from each component of $F$ and paths joining those representatives which lie in a common component of $G_S$. Consequently this attachment preserves $Q$, and hence the old second homology of the binary category of elements, if \[ \pi_0(F)\longrightarrow\pi_0(G_S) \quad\hbox{is injective}. \tag{FC} \] More generally, preservation holds if and only if all classes in \eqref{eq:akr-fixed-path-kernel} are zero in $Q$; injectivity in \eqref{eq:akr-fixed-components} is sufficient but is not asserted to be necessary.
notes: Every repaired attachment with prescribed covered target. Exact kernel formula; no all-stage vanishing inferred. Stable label: C:fixed-path-kernel
Exact prefix/suffix classification for every actual point path size and k at least the common bound; at most 2L-1 subsets. Stable label: C:beta-fixed-subsets

statement: Assume that $f$ and $g$ induce injections on binary graph components and that their underlying point images meet in at most one point. Then every equalizer subgraph of a pair of copy maps $\alpha_i,\alpha_j:T\to Z$ is connected in each component of $G_T$. Thus the fixed-path criterion applies to a subsequent attachment for any such copy pair, even when $K(T)/F(T)$ is nonzero.
notes: Component injections and point-image overlap at most one imply the stated next-copy fixed-set criterion. Stable label: C:beta-small-overlap

statement: In any repaired AKR Construction C.1, let $P_+$ and $P_-$ be the fresh first-stage quasi-filter targets for $(v_1,v_2)$ and $(v_2,v_1)$. Write $s_+,s_-$ for their respective numbers of quasi-filter maps. In the binary graph $G_{P_\pm}$, let $S_\pm$ be the $s_\pm$ vertices of its unique circular component, and choose its integral cycle $\kappa_\pm$ with augmentation one. For $X\in K^*$ define \[ F(X)=\mathbb Z[K^*(P_+,X)]\oplus\mathbb Z[K^*(P_-,X)], \qquad \iota_X(b)=b\kappa_\pm\in K(X) \quad(b:P_\pm\to X). \] Then $\iota:F\to K$ is a natural monomorphism. Its quotient $M=K/F$ is pointwise a finitely generated free abelian group, and every arrow of $K^*$ induces a split injection on $M$ with free abelian cokernel. The splitting is an existence statement for each individual arrow; no compatible family of splittings is asserted. More precisely, if $X\in K_m$, $m\geq1$, $g:Y\to X$ is any arrow, and $h_i:P_{\epsilon_i}\to X$ is a finite family of distinct typed arrows, then: \begin{enumerate} \item $|h_i(S_{\epsilon_i})\cap g(Y)|\geq3$ implies that $h_i$ factors through $g$; \item if every displayed intersection has at most two points, then \[ \left|\bigcup_i h_i(S_{\epsilon_i})\setminus g(Y)\right| \geq\frac{a_m}{a_1}\sum_i(s_{\epsilon_i}-2). \] \end{enumerate} These assertions hold for mixed families with either source $P_+$ or $P_-$.
notes: All-stage pointwise and relative result; not injectivity after taking colimit. Stable label: C:protected-cycles

statement: Use the protected objects $P_+,P_-$, their marked circles $S_+,S_-$, and their cycle generators from Theorem~\ref{C:protected-cycles}. For every object $X$ of the repaired construction, every protected arrow $h:P_\epsilon\to X$, and every arrow $g:Y\to X$, the following stronger routing assertion holds. If $h(S_\epsilon)\cap g(Y)$ contains the images of two vertices which are not adjacent in $S_\epsilon$, then $h$ factors through $g$. Consequently, if $h$ does not factor through $g$, that intersection is empty, a single vertex, or two adjacent vertices. The boundary graphs of two distinct protected cells in $G_X$ meet in an empty set, one vertex, or one edge.
notes: All admissible stages: a proper protected-circle overlap is empty, a vertex, or one edge. Stable label: C:protected-nonadjacent

statement: Let $P(X)\subseteq K(X)\subseteq C_1(G_X;\mathbb Z)$ be the subgroup freely generated by the protected cycles in Theorem~\ref{C:protected-cycles}. For any two arrows $f:Y\to X$ and $g:Z\to X$, let $U\subseteq G_X$ be the union of their image subgraphs. Then \[ P(X)\cap C_1(U;\mathbb Z) = f_\#P(Y)+g_\#P(Z). \tag{PI} \] The same assertion holds with coefficients in an arbitrary abelian group. Thus a protected-cycle combination whose edge support lies in the union uses only protected cells factoring through one of those two arrows.
notes: Objectwise two-image saturation over every abelian coefficient group; no colimit saturation inferred. Stable label: C:protected-two-images

statement: Let $X\in K_m$, let $h:Y\to X$ be an arrow of the repaired C.1 construction, and let $J=h_\#G_Y\subseteq G_X$. If a simple graph path has distinct endpoints in $J$, all its internal vertices outside $J$, and all its edges outside $J$, its length $r$ satisfies \[ (2-a_m)r\geq1. \] For $m\geq1$ put \[ R_m=\left\lceil\frac1{2-a_m}\right\rceil-1. \] Every simple path of length at most $R_m$ with endpoints in $J$ is contained in $J$. In particular every arrow image is \emph{two-convex}: every geodesic of length at most two whose endpoints lie in that image stays in the image. This holds at all stages and for every admissible numerical choice.
notes: All actual C.1 arrows, all admissible choices. An outside simple excursion of length r satisfies (2-a_m)r>=1; in particular all images are two-convex. Stable label: C:local-convexity

statement: Let $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ be parallel arrows at an old stage $K_m$, where $m\geq1$. If each component of $G_S$ has diameter at most $R_m$, then its equalizer subgraph $F$ is connected in every component of $G_S$ that it meets. A repaired quasi-filter attachment for this pair therefore preserves the whole old colimit of $K$, and in particular the whole old binary second homology. The same conclusion holds at any later stage whenever every component of the fixed source $G_S$ has diameter at most two. It does not require prior component injectivity of $f$ or $g$.
notes: Source component diameters at most the explicit local radius suffice; no component-injectivity hypothesis is used. Stable label: C:small-diameter-source

statement: In any repaired C.1 construction, let $S$ be an object already in $K_1$. At any later finite stage, every repaired quasi-filter attachment for any pair $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ preserves the whole old colimit of the binary cycle functor $K$. It therefore preserves every old binary second-homology class, independently of the target $T$, the chosen pair, and all admissible numerical parameters. Consequently an attachment with a nonzero fixed-path kernel, if one occurs, must have a source object born at stage two or later.
notes: Every later attachment from a source already in K1 preserves the old binary cycle colimit. The separate universal component theorem extends preservation to all later-born sources. Stable label: C:first-stage-safe-sources

statement: Let $P\ne V$ be an object with its generating cover at birth, and let $p,q\in P$ be a forbidden pair. At every later stage, if $h:P\to X$ and $g:Y\to X$ satisfy \[ h(p),h(q)\in g(Y), \] then $h$ factors through $g$ by an arrow of the constructed category.
notes: Proved: routing a forbidden pair Stable label: C:birth-forbidden-pair

statement: Let $P\ne V$ have its generating cover at birth. A nonempty subset $U\subseteq P$ with no forbidden pair is contained in one member of that generating cover.
notes: Proved: pairwise visibility has a common copy Stable label: C:birth-cover-helly

statement: For any two arrows $h:P\to X$ and $g:Q\to X$ of a repaired C.1 stage, their nonempty point-image intersection is the image of a commuting span already in that stage: there are an object $R$ and arrows $u:R\to P$, $v:R\to Q$ such that \[ hu=gv,\qquad (hu)(R)=h(P)\cap g(Q). \] Consequently every nonempty finite intersection of arrow images in one object is itself an existing arrow image. This statement asserts equality of point sets and the existence of the displayed factorization span. It does not assert the categorical pullback universal property.
notes: Proved: intersections are existing arrow images Stable label: C:arrow-image-intersections

statement: For every parallel pair $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ in a repaired C.1 stage, its pointwise fixed subset is empty or is exactly the image of a single arrow $e:R\to S$ already in that stage: \[ \{x\in S:f(x)=g(x)\}=e(R),\qquad fe=ge. \] No categorical equalizer universal property is claimed.
notes: Proved: pointwise equalizers descend to one arrow Stable label: C:point-equalizer-image

statement: Fix an object $S$ of a repaired C.1 construction. Suppose every arrow $e:R\to S$ is injective on binary graph components. Then every parallel pair $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ at every later stage has a fixed subgraph connected in each component of $G_S$. Every later quasi-filter attachment whose source is this $S$ therefore preserves the whole old cycle colimit and the whole old binary second homology. The hypothesis is a finite condition which can be checked at the birth of $S$, provided the retained finite substage contains all its incoming generators and their ancestors. No subsequent stage adds an object with an arrow into $S$, or adds an arrow between its old objects.
notes: Proved: a finite certificate for all future targets Stable label: C:certified-safe-source

statement: Suppose every arrow of an old repaired C.1 stage induces an injection on binary graph components. Then every quasi-filter attachment for a pair in that stage has zero old cycle-colimit kernel. If this component-injectivity assertion holds at every stage, the first-stage binary second-homology class survives the whole infinite construction.
notes: Proved: the separate component-injectivity obligation Stable label: C:equalizer-component-reduction

statement: Consider a finite generated stage in which: \begin{enumerate} \item every arrow is injective on $H$; \item each source's generating cover at birth, interpreted on $H$, has the Helly property of Lemma~\ref{C:birth-cover-helly}; \item the forbidden-pair routing assertion of Lemma~\ref{C:birth-forbidden-pair} holds for pairs of source \emph{components}, and yields factorizations of actual arrows. \end{enumerate} If $h:P\to X$, $g:Q\to X$ have at least two components in the intersection of their $H$-images, there are actual arrows $u:R\to P$, $v:R\to Q$ with \[ hu=gv,\qquad H(hu)(H(R))=H(h)(H(P))\cap H(g)(H(Q)). \tag{CI} \] If $h$ does not factor through $g$, $R$ is strictly earlier than $P$ in its generation history, allowing the step $W\to V$ at stage zero.
notes: The intersection is represented by an actual commuting span; at least two components are essential to avoid the singleton point-lifting defect. Stable label: C:component-two-intersection

statement: Under the three hypotheses of the preceding lemma, every actual parallel pair $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ has an acyclic component transition relation and \[ L_H(f,g)\leq L_U(f,g)+1. \tag{PB} \] Here the absence of nontrivial point-transition cycles for actual arrows is the established AKR property (4).
notes: Simultaneous source induction: no component cycles and L_H(f,g) <= L_U(f,g)+1, with exact path vertex counts. Stable label: C:component-path-inflation

statement: Every arrow in every repaired AKR C.1 construction is injective on the component sets $H(X)=\pi_0G_X$. At every finite stage the component transition relation of every actual parallel pair is acyclic and satisfies $L_H(f,g)\leq L_U(f,g)+1$.
notes: Every admissible C.1 choice; s>=15n and k>=n+1 suffice. No selected size, convexity or ordering bound is added. Stable label: C:universal-components

statement: In every repaired C.1 construction, every attachment preserves the old colimit of the binary cycle functor $K$. The first-stage class $\kappa_+-\kappa_-$ consequently survives to a nonzero element of \[ H_2\!\left(B\operatorname{El}_{K^*} \bigl(h_V/(cv_1\sim cv_2)\bigr);\mathbb Z\right). \] Thus every such repaired C.1 category is not total.
notes: Nonzero binary H2 in the infinite union for every admissible repaired construction. Three independent mathematical audits passed. Stable label: C:universal-nontotal

statement: Let $S,T$ be finite simple graphs and let $f,g:S\to T$ be induced graph embeddings. Suppose each connected component of each image is geodesically convex in $T$, and that both embeddings induce injections on connected components. Suppose also that the directed graph with edges $f(x)\to g(x)$ whenever $f(x)\ne g(x)$ has no directed cycle. Then the induced subgraph on \[ F=\{x\in S:f(x)=g(x)\} \] is geodesically convex within each connected component of $S$. In particular its intersection with every component of $S$ is empty or connected.
notes: Proved: fixed sets of convex partial isometries Stable label: C:convex-fixed

statement: For arbitrary finite graphs, convex image components, injectivity on connected components, and bounded point-transition paths do not suffice to ensure that the repaired beta gluing is injective on connected components of each old copy. This assertion concerns a generic graph construction; the displayed arrow configuration is not asserted to occur in the category generated by C.1.
notes: Generic repaired graph gluing only; not shown to occur in C.1. Stable label: C:generic-component-warning

statement: For a generic pair of induced graph embeddings with connected source and target, strong convexity of both source images, injectivity on components, and bounded nontrivial point paths do not guarantee convexity of the old copies in the repaired beta target. This failure can occur at $n=3$, $s=45$, $k=11$, even though these numbers satisfy the numerical C.1 condition for $a_0=2$, $a_1=8/5$. The graph configuration below is not asserted to arise among the arrows of the prescribed C.1 construction.
notes: Connected source and target, all old images strongly convex, point paths of size two, and numerically admissible s=45. A 46-edge path shortens to 45; no realization as actual C.1 arrows is claimed. Stable label: C:connected-convex-warning

statement: Let $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ be injections of finite sets. Suppose the nonidentity part of the relation $f(x)\mapsto g(x)$ has only directed paths. Let $n\geq2$ bound their numbers of vertices, choose $k\geq n$, and put $s=4k+1$. Let \[ \alpha_i:T\longrightarrow Z_k,\qquad i\in\mathbb Z/s, \] be the actual-path-length repaired beta maps. Define \[ (\lambda_i,\mu_i)= \begin{cases} (g,f),&0\leq i<2k,\\ (g,g),&i=2k,\\ (f,g),&2k<i<4k,\\ (f,f),&i=4k. \end{cases} \] Then $Z_k$ is the coequalizer in sets of \[ \coprod_{i\in\mathbb Z/s}S \rightrightarrows \coprod_{i\in\mathbb Z/s}T, \qquad (i,x)\longmapsto(i,\lambda_i x),\quad (i,x)\longmapsto(i+1,\mu_i x). \tag{NC} \] In particular, compatible maps from the displayed copies of $T$ to any set induce a unique map from $Z_k$.
notes: Proved: the repaired target is the strict necklace colimit Stable label: C:necklace-set-colimit

statement: Let $S,T$ be finite linearly ordered sets and let $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ be increasing injections. Fix $n\geq2$ at least the number of vertices in every nontrivial path of the relation $f(x)\mapsto g(x)$. There is an integer $K\geq n$ such that, for every $k\geq K$, the covered repaired target $Z_k$ admits a linear order making every generating map $\alpha_i:T\to Z_k$ increasing. The prescribed order on $T$ is unchanged. The assertion permits any additional lower bounds on $k$.
notes: All sufficiently large k, with a terminating finite choice procedure; no assertion at every smaller admissible k. Stable label: C:ordered-necklace

statement: The proposition asserts existence for all sufficiently large $k$; it does not assert orderability at every minimally admissible value. Its proof is a strict set-colimit argument and uses no conversion of a homotopy-coherent cocone into a strict one. The choice can be made effectively. Place $T$ at integer coordinates and choose the piecewise-linear $h$ just described, with rational coefficients. Its fixed intervals and the endpoints of the other components are determined by finitely many affine equations. Iterate the finitely many rational points $g(x)$ and increase $k$ until \eqref{eq:akr-order-separation} holds, together with all additional numerical lower bounds. The convergence argument proves termination. The subsequent prescriptions for $w$ and $\rho$ are finite and rational. Thus arbitrary tie-breaking in the last step may also be replaced by a fixed deterministic ordering rule.
notes: Proved scope and effective parameter selection Stable label: C:ordered-necklace-scope

statement: The sufficiently-large-$k$ hypothesis in Proposition~\ref{C:ordered-necklace} cannot be replaced, for arbitrary increasing maps of finite linear orders, by the condition that $k$ bounds the sizes of their nontrivial point paths. The failure can occur at $n=3$, $s=45$, $k=11$, satisfying the numerical C.1 condition for $a_0=2$, $a_1=8/5$. The pair below is not asserted to occur among the actual generated arrows of C.1, so this does not refute the universal statement of Part C.1 or the selected construction already proved.
notes: Increasing maps with point paths of size two can force an order cycle at numerically admissible n=3, k=11. The pair is not shown to occur among actual generated C.1 arrows. Stable label: C:ordered-necklace-short-warning

statement: Let $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ be a parallel pair at a finite stage of the repaired AKR construction. Suppose that each of the induced graph embeddings $G_S\to G_T$ is injective on connected components and that the image of each component is geodesically convex. Here geodesically convex means that every shortest graph path between two of its vertices lies in that image. Let $D$ be the largest diameter of a component of the finite graph $G_T$, taking the diameter of a singleton to be zero. Choose the repaired path bound $n\geq2$ and a parameter $s=4k+1$, $k\geq n$, such that \[ s>(2n-2)(D+1). \tag{LC} \] Then every generating map $\alpha_i:T\to Z$ of the repaired target has geodesically convex image on each component of $G_T$. This lemma alone does not assert injectivity on components of $G_T\to G_Z$.
notes: Strong geodesic convexity follows from the explicit strict diameter/visibility bound; component injection is proved separately. Stable label: C:large-target-convexity

statement: For every sequence $(a_m)$ satisfying the numerical requirements of the repaired AKR Construction C.1, one can choose its finite targets so that all of the following hold at every stage: \begin{enumerate} \item the underlying point sets $X$, and separately the sets $H(X)=\pi_0G_X$, admit linear orders for which every arrow induces an increasing injection on each of these two sets; \item every arrow image component in $G_X$ is geodesically convex; \item every attachment induces an injection on the second integral homology of the binary category of elements. \end{enumerate} For the resulting countable union $A=\bigcup_mK_m$, the action \[ H=h_V/(bv_1\sim bv_2) \] satisfies \[ H_2(B\operatorname{El}_A H;\mathbb Z)\ne0. \] In particular there exists a quasi-filtered category which is not total. This is an existence theorem about selected sufficiently large targets; it does not assert the universal choice statement of Part C.1.
depends_on: C.5 [C:attachment-cycle-test]; C.29 [C:convex-fixed]; C.10 [C:fixed-path-kernel]; C.36 [C:large-target-convexity]; C.32 [C:necklace-set-colimit]; C.33 [C:ordered-necklace]
uses: TOTEX2:C.10, TOTEX2:C.29, TOTEX2:C.32, TOTEX2:C.33, TOTEX2:C.36, TOTEX2:C.5
notes: Every admissible a-sequence admits selected large targets with persistent binary H2. A deterministic countable example is specified. This earlier geometric proof is retained separately from the universal component proof. Stable label: C:selected-nontotal

statement: Let $C$ be a small category and let $n\geq1$. Every free homotopy class of maps $S^n\to |NC|$ has a representative $|Nv|:|ND|\to |NC|$, after a homeomorphism $|ND|\cong S^n$, where $D$ is the poset of nonempty faces of a finite triangulation of $S^n$ and $v:D\to C$ is a functor.
notes: Known, with the reduction proved: finite-poset representatives Stable label: FT:sphere-representatives

statement: Let $A$ be a small nonempty connected category. For a functor $u:D\to A$, define the covariant $A$-set \[ H_u(a)=\pi_0(u\downarrow a),\qquad H_u(b)([d,f])=[d,bf] \] for $b:a\to a'$. Here $(d,f)$ has $f:u(d)\to a$, and an arrow $(d,f)\to(d',f')$ is $\delta:d\to d'$ with $f'u(\delta)=f$. Define a functor \[ j_u:D\longrightarrow\operatorname{El}_A(H_u),\qquad d\longmapsto(u(d),[d,1_{u(d)}]), \] whose value on an arrow is its image under $u$. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item Every component of every $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$, for every covariant $H:A\to\mathsf{Set}$, is weakly contractible. \item For every finite poset $D$ and every $u:D\to A$, $Bj_u$ is null-homotopic on every connected component of $BD$. \item The same conclusion holds when $D$ is the face poset of a finite triangulation of $S^n$, for every integer $n\geq1$. \end{enumerate} In particular the tests in (3) suffice; no bound on the dimension of the spheres is being imposed.
notes: Proved: Lead 6 Stable label: FT:finite-test

statement: Let $\mathsf{Ty}$ be the category in PRETOT Definition E.1: its objects are finite words $\tau$ in $+,-$, including the empty word, and a morphism $\tau\to\rho$ is an endpoint-preserving functor $I_\tau\to I_\rho$ whose function on vertices is nondecreasing. Here $I_\tau$ is the free category on the oriented line prescribed by $\tau$. Then $\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is isomorphic to the category of these words and nondecreasing sign-preserving maps of their letter sets. Under this isomorphism, the colored-word category $W_2$ is its wide subcategory of injective letter maps, after identifying its two colors with $+$ and $-$. Put $p=(++)$, $q=(+-+)$, and use one-based letter indices. The arrows \[ e=(1,3),\quad c=(1,1):p\rightrightarrows q \] have no completion to a commutative square. For every nonzero unital ring $R$ they have no affine equalizer in $\operatorname{Aff}_R(\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}})$. In fact, for the covariant set quotient \[ H=\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}(p,-)/(ge\sim gc) \] we have $H_1(B\operatorname{El}_{\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}}(H);\mathbb Z) \cong\mathbb Z$. Thus $\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is neither total nor exact. The phrase ``over any ring'' in Lead 8 must exclude the zero ring; with that qualification the lead is true.
notes: Every nonzero unital ring; zero ring refutes literal any-ring wording. Stable label: FT:ty

statement: Suppose $A$ is a small total category that is not exact, and let $a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$ be a family without an integral affine equalizer. Assume $k$ is least among all such families in $A$. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item $A(q,p)=\varnothing$. \item The finite cardinalities $|A(p,x)|$ have no uniform finite bound; in symbols, $\sup_x|A(p,x)|=\infty$ in the sense of unboundedness in the natural numbers, allowing infinite values. \item The full cosieve $V_p=\{x\in A:A(p,x)\ne\varnothing\}$ is again a separator, with the same exhibited family. Its object $p$ is weakly initial, and the minimal integer $k$ remains the same after restriction. \item For every arrow $g:q\to x$, the arrows $ga_0,\ldots,ga_k:p\to x$ are pairwise distinct. \end{enumerate}
notes: Proved: Lead 9 Stable label: FT:minimal-family

statement: Among nonempty connected small categories, \[ \{\text{filtered}\}\subsetneq\{\text{exact}\} \subsetneq\{\text{total}\}\subsetneq\{\text{quasi-filtered}\}. \] The ordinal-injection category witnesses the first strict inclusion. The ordered predimension category $\mathcal C_\delta$ of Theorem~\ref{A:predimension-total} witnesses the middle strict inclusion. The selected repaired AKR category of Theorem~\ref{C:selected-nontotal} witnesses the last strict inclusion.

his_places: II ms. 36-36ter; all three inclusions strict
notes: Proved: every inclusion in the class diagram is strict Stable label: D:known-diagram

statement: The implication \emph{totalement $W_\infty$-asph\'erique $\Longrightarrow$ filtrante} at II manuscript page 36ter is false. For nonempty connected small $A$, \[ A\text{ filtered}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\text{ total and sifted}. \] For every fixed integer $n\geq1$, \[ \begin{split} A\text{ filtered}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad& A\text{ total and } \hocolim_A K(M(a),n)\text{ is }n\text{-truncated}\\ &\text{for every covariant }M:A\to\Ab. \end{split} \] The implication from siftedness alone to totality in Proposition 2.19 at II manuscript page 36 is false. Replacing ``filtered'' by ``exact'' in the conjectured implication does not repair it: totality does not imply exact abelian colimits.
his_places: II ms. 36-36ter; XII ms. 88-89 (stated corrected implications)
notes: Refuted conjecture; known corrected implications Stable label: D:manuscript

statement: For every small category $A$, including empty and disconnected categories, let $\ell:A\to\Pi A$ be groupoid completion. For every fixed finite $n\geq1$, homotopy colimits over $A$ preserve $n$-types if and only if \[ C_a=a\downarrow\ell =\El_A\bigl(\Hom_{\Pi A}(a,\ell(-))\bigr) \] is filtered for every $a$. This is supplied TOTEX D.10.
notes: Known, with the comparison maps audited: positive truncations Stable label: D:truncation

statement: At II manuscript page 36, for $f:X\to Y$, finality must use $y\backslash X$ rather than the printed $y\backslash Y$. The latter always has initial object $\id_y$ and would make the condition vacuous. At XII manuscript page 88, $H'\in(U')^\wedge$, so the correctly typed isomorphism is \[ U'/t'\simeq U'/H', \] not $U'/t'\simeq U/H'$. A presheaf on $U$ is a covariant set-valued functor on $U^{\mathrm{op}}$; its usual element category is opposite to the corresponding covariant element category. Opposition preserves the classifying-space homotopy type. Definition 1 at XII manuscript pages 88--89 quantifies over all left Kan extensions and equivalently over ordinary final images. It is the notion used here, distinct from the test-category diagonal condition in \emph{Pursuing Stacks}. We inspected the supplied transcription, not an independent copy of the authoritative edition. These are mathematical typing corrections, not a new editorial collation.
